t: Socialist ideology as an enabler of "value alignment" in large AI models
zh: 论社会主义意识形态赋能人工智能大模型“价值对齐”
paras: Gao An'an takes up the "value alignment" problem in large AI models, first formulated by Stuart Russell in 2014. The article argues that Western states, led by the United States, have turned alignment into a political project for technological hegemony and for exporting their ideology as "universal values". Gao contends that China urgently needs its own alignment scheme with socialist ideology at its core, and that existing Chinese research, which the author describes as mostly defensive (engineering control, legal sanction, moral restraint), has not shown how socialist ideology can actively empower alignment.

The article has three parts. The first sets out why socialist ideology is the right "alignment target", the second proposes three practical principles, and the third sets out four paths for embedding socialist ideology in models. A short conclusion looks ahead to further research. Gao draws on Marx and Engels, on speeches by Xi Jinping, and on Chinese regulations and standards on generative AI. The author also uses cases such as ChatGPT, Amazon's recruitment algorithm, Anthropic's "constitutional AI" and DeepSeek.

Gao argues that capitalist ideology, with its priority on profit maximisation, tends to make AI a tool of exploitation. Socialist ideology, in the author's account, supplies basic value resources (the core socialist values and the "common values of all mankind" across individual, group, national and global levels), steers both the training and the post-deployment stages of alignment, and points toward the final aim of "machines for people" and human liberation. The three principles are balancing innovation with safety and control, combining positive incentives with negative sanctions, and combining industry self-governance with social co-governance, the last aimed at easing the "alignment tax". The four paths aim to make models "virtuous", "emotional", "refined" and "orderly": ethical training and review, emotion computing, cultural-meme extraction and generation, and institutional design, support and criticism.

Gao concludes that alignment is becoming a permanent and demanding undertaking. It faces unresolved technical and ethical difficulties and a persistent mismatch between machine rationality and human value systems. The author calls for research to move from theory to technical practice, and for sustained effort toward human–AI coexistence and the digital-intelligent advance of civilisation. Read the original if you want to see how Chinese Marxist scholarship links AI governance, ideological security and concrete technical proposals for alignment.
quoteEn: Socialist ideology concentrates the people-centred development philosophy and the pursuit of a community with a shared future for mankind. It holds rich foundational value resources, process-steering resources and outcome-securing resources, and is the best choice for the "value alignment" of China's large AI models.
quoteZh: 社会主义意识形态集中反映了以人民为中心的发展理念与人类命运共同体的价值追求，具备丰富的基础性价值资源、过程性驾驭资源以及结果性保障资源，是中国人工智能大模型“价值对齐”的最优选择。

glossary.explanation: A set of 24 characters in twelve values, promoted officially since the 18th Party Congress (2012). They cover the national level (prosperity, democracy, civility, harmony), the social level (freedom, equality, justice, rule of law) and the individual level (patriotism, dedication, integrity, friendship).
A formulation Xi Jinping introduced in 2015: peace, development, fairness, justice, democracy and freedom. Official discourse presents it as an alternative to Western "universal values".
The effort to make AI systems act in line with human values. Stuart Russell named it the "value alignment problem" in 2014; the article treats it as a political and ideological question.

t: The cultural self-awareness behind the formation and continuation of the Chinese Communists' spiritual lineage
zh: 中国共产党人精神谱系生成与赓续的文化自觉
source: Studies on Marxism (马克思主义研究), 2026 no. 2
paras: Xu Yan asks why and how the "spiritual lineage of Chinese Communists" (a series of named "spirits" such as the Long March spirit and the Yan'an spirit) came into being, and how it can be continued. The article argues that earlier studies describe individual spirits or their functions but do not explain the internal cultural driver. Drawing on Fei Xiaotong's concept of "cultural self-awareness", Xu holds that the lineage is the product of the Communist Party's conscious cultural creation as a historical subject.

The article adopts a three-part framework of awareness of formation, awareness of value and awareness of practice. It opens with a review of case studies and holistic studies of the lineage, then moves through the historical genesis of the lineage, its value structure and contributions, and finally the paths for its continuation in the new era. Examples run from the Long March, the "Two Bombs, One Satellite" spirit and the reform and opening-up spirit to the poverty-alleviation spirit.

On formation, Xu argues that the Party achieved a "double transcendence": a practical overcoming of hard realities and a sublating critique of dogma, such as the "encircling the cities from the countryside" strategy and the debate on the criterion of truth. The Party also drew on two sources, Marxism and fine traditional Chinese culture, through the Two Integrations. On value, Xu identifies three layers: ideals and convictions, a people-first stance, and seeking truth from facts together with hard struggle. Xu claims the lineage builds national cohesion and offers a spiritual reference beyond Western modernity and the logic of capital.

On continuation, Xu proposes four paths. These are upholding the Party's cultural leadership and the Party's self-reform; deepening the Two Integrations for innovative transmission; embedding the lineage in Chinese modernization through high-quality development, common prosperity and the modernization of people; and building new narratives and digital communication. Xu concludes that the cultural self-awareness lens moves research from historical narrative toward analysis of mechanisms and supports building China's independent knowledge system. Read the original if you study Party spirit-building, ideological education or the Party's account of cultural subjectivity and want a detailed example of how these are framed.
quoteEn: The spiritual lineage of Chinese Communists is the result of the Party, as a highly self-aware political subject, actively creating and constructing culture in great historical struggles, and is a product of its cultural self-awareness.
quoteZh: 中国共产党人精神谱系，是中国共产党作为高度自觉的政治主体，在伟大历史斗争中主动进行文化创造与建构的成果，是其文化自觉的产物。

t: Examining the practical dimension of ideological and political theory courses in schools in the new era
zh: 新时代学校思政课教学的实践维度审视
paras: Xu Yanguo takes up the place of practice in the teaching of school ideological and political theory courses (sizheng ke), whose core content is now Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. Starting from the practical character of the Party's innovative theory, the article argues that these courses are at root the teaching of truth, and that truth must withstand the test of practice. Teaching should therefore be organised around a practical logic rather than treating practice as a supplement to theory.

The article has three parts. The first traces course construction from the early People's Republic to the present, through the teaching of Mao Zedong Thought, Deng Xiaoping Theory, the Three Represents and the Scientific Outlook on Development, to the introductory course on Xi Jinping Thought. The second looks at practice as teaching content in the first classroom (textbooks, lesson plans, assignments, assessment) and in the second classroom (off-campus practice teaching). The third examines method, teachers, organisation and assessment.

Xu reads the history of the curriculum as showing that the courses have always taught Marxism and its latest Chinese adaptations, so that the Party's theory persuades students through its demonstrated strength in practice. The goal is for students to internalise ideals and convictions and then act on them. Xu proposes practice bases tied to first-classroom content, with front-line practitioners joining teachers, and a teaching logic that runs from practice to theory and back. Theory teaching is likened to the skeleton and practice teaching to the muscle, the bridge from the abstract to the concrete. Xu notes that many teachers go from school to school with little social experience, and urges field research for them. Xu also wants practice written into course standards and assessed for courses, teachers and students, not just exam scores.

Xu concludes that traditional teaching treated practice as a supplement, and that, with the 15th Five-Year Plan period under way, a practice-based "big ideological and political course" matters for Party governance. Mastering and truly believing theory both depend on practice, which Xu compares to travelling ten thousand miles alongside reading ten thousand books. Xu calls for active exploration of organising these courses around practice. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese academic frames the practice dimension of ideological and political courses, including a historical survey of curriculum documents and concrete proposals on teaching content, teacher training and assessment.
quoteEn: Both mastering theory and truly believing in it are inseparable from practice.
quoteZh: 掌握理论与真信理论都离不开实践。

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses in Marxism, Party history and political education taught from primary school through university in China. They are meant to build students' worldview and political convictions.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party constitution in 2017 and the state constitution in 2018. It is now the core content of the political theory curriculum.
Hu Jintao-era guiding concept, adopted by the Party in 2007 and 2012, stressing people-centred, coordinated and sustainable development.

Jiang Zemin's theory, made a guiding ideology at the 16th Party Congress (2002). It holds that the Party represents advanced productive forces, advanced culture and the fundamental interests of the people.

t: The red gene as the spiritual foundation for young people's achievements in the new era
zh: 红色基因是新时代青年建功立业的精神根基
paras: This commentary, published in the People's Daily in July 2026, asks how young people can make their mark in the new era. Bi Mingyang argues that the "red gene", which the author calls the spiritual lifeblood of Chinese communists, is the spiritual foundation of that effort. The piece opens with Xi Jinping's remarks to youth at the Party's 105th anniversary and in a reply to youth award winners.

Bi first defines the red gene by three features: firm ideals and convictions, a deep sense of responsibility to family and country, and a practical character that unites knowing and doing. The commentary then sets out the opportunities of the first year of the 15th Five-Year Plan period, and offers three tasks, each paired with a quotation from Xi.

The first task is to forge the soul through the red gene and so consolidate young people's ideals. Bi proposes making Party history education routine, building red education into the national education system, and using memorials and immersive technology. The second is to draw energy from the opportunities of the era. Here Bi points to the plan's support for young people as vanguard and main force, to new quality productive forces and to regional development, and calls for closer links between universities and industry and for better talent policies. The third is to build a style of solid, responsible action by training young people at grassroots posts and in major projects, with incentives, tolerance of error and role models.

Bi concludes that inheriting the red gene must be joined to seizing the opportunities of the era, so that young people gather strength for the 15th Five-Year Plan period. Read the original if you want an example of how official commentary links Party history education to youth policy and the 15th Five-Year Plan.
quoteEn: The red gene is a practical tradition that is continually reactivated and enriched through the hard work of successive generations, and inheriting it depends above all on the unity of knowing and doing.
quoteZh: 红色基因是在一代代人的实干奋斗中被持续激活、不断丰富的实践传统，传承红色基因贵在知行合一。

glossary.explanation: A metaphor in Party discourse for the revolutionary ideals, values and traditions of the Communist Party, said to be passed down across generations.
A concept Xi Jinping introduced in 2023, referring to productivity driven by technological innovation and emerging industries.
China's national development plan for 2026–2030, the fifth-year-plan cycle following the 14th.

t: Integration and symbiosis: advancing university–enterprise collaborative education
zh: 融合共生 推动校企协同育人
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily on 24 March 2026, Bi Tianshu, president of North China Electric Power University, argues that industry-oriented universities should deepen collaboration with enterprises in training talent. Starting from the proposal in the outline of the 15th Five-Year Plan to integrate scientific and industrial innovation, Bi holds that such collaboration can link the education, talent, industry and innovation chains and support the building of a leading education country.
The commentary has three parts. It first sets out the value of collaborative education, then proposes three changes of mindset, and finally outlines three directions for practice.

On value, Bi presents collaboration as the link joining national strategy, industrial upgrading and the university 'Double First-Class' initiative, through shared mission, aligned responsibility and common development. On ideas, Bi urges universities and firms to move from short-term 'project-based' or 'order-based' cooperation to long-term strategic coordination, to treat each other as interdependent partners sharing teachers, resources and results, and to replace 'adaptive' training with innovation-led training aimed at 'bottleneck' technologies. On practice, Bi calls for three shifts: from a discipline-driven to a strategy-driven training system, from single-point cooperation to an ecosystem covering the whole industrial chain, and from serving industry to enhancing national competitiveness, including exporting technologies and standards through the Belt and Road Initiative.

Bi concludes that collaborative education should become a vehicle for national competitiveness and a foundation of educational strength. Read the original if you want a concise statement, by a university head, of how Chinese industry-oriented universities frame cooperation with enterprises under the 15th Five-Year Plan.
quoteEn: Abandon short-term practices such as 'project-based cooperation' and 'order-based recruitment', and build deep cooperation founded on a long-term strategic consensus.
quoteZh: 摒弃“项目式合作”“订单式招工”等短期行为，构建基于长期战略共识的深度合作关系。

glossary.explanation: A Chinese international infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative launched in 2013.
A government programme, launched in 2015, to build world-class universities and disciplines in China.
An official goal of making China a global leader in education, set out in national plans for the period to 2035.

t: Using a "broad view of employment" to connect the whole cycle of educating students
zh: 以“大就业观”贯通育人全周期
paras: This commentary, first published in Guangming Daily on 24 March 2026, asks how universities should respond to a record graduating cohort, which the author gives as 12.7 million, 480,000 more than the previous year. Ning Depeng argues that employment work must stop being treated as a graduation-season task and must be built into the whole cycle of educating students through a "broad view of employment". The author ties this to the demand of new quality productive forces for composite and innovative talent.

The piece is organised under four headings: running through the whole process, breaking down barriers, balancing hard and soft skills, and precise services without interruption. It addresses university administrators and employment offices, with concrete measures on admissions, curriculum, assessment and career guidance.

Ning's central move is to bring employment quality forward to the start of training. This means linking admissions plans to national strategy, judging institutions by employer feedback, salary growth and social contribution rather than first-job rates, and fostering lifelong learning. The author then calls for dismantling disciplinary boundaries through new interdisciplinary fields, micro-majors, AI and digital literacy for all students, and university–enterprise cooperation. Ning also proposes a two-wheel approach: hard skills through project-based learning and simulation, and soft skills through a "second-classroom transcript" and ideological and political education that encourages graduates to work in areas of national need and in remote or grassroots posts.

On services, the author recommends career education from freshman year, differentiated guidance for students seeking stable posts, new sectors or start-ups, regulated support for platform and flexible work, and big-data matching with a "one student, one policy" ledger for those facing difficulty. Ning concludes that these measures would raise talent-training quality and so support high-quality and full employment. Read the original if you want a concise example of how a Chinese education scholar translates national employment and industrial policy into university practice.
quoteEn: The essence of this idea is to bring consideration of employment quality forward to the starting point of talent training and make it a core link in that process.
quoteZh: 这一理念的实质，在于将就业质量的考量前置至人才培养的起点，成为其核心环节。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping since 2023, referring to advanced productivity driven by technological innovation, emerging industries and higher-quality labour.
A policy goal in recent government work reports that stresses both the number of jobs and their quality.
The author's term for treating employment as a concern across the whole cycle of admissions, training, further study and career, not only the graduation season.
A record of a student's activities outside formal teaching, such as volunteering and social practice, used in evaluating overall quality.

t: Innovative paths for integrating red cultural resources into university ideological and political theory courses
zh: 红色文化资源融入高校思政课教学的创新路径
paras: Zhang Xiaozhi, an associate professor at a school of Marxism, asks how "red cultural resources" (the heritage of the Chinese revolution) can be built into university ideological and political theory courses. The article argues that this should rest on the fundamental task of fostering virtue and cultivating talent, and proceed on four levels: content, teaching model, carriers and mechanisms. In Zhang's view, doing so helps train a new generation able to shoulder the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

The piece is a short practical commentary organised around four proposals. Each is given a three-part formula: a "history–theory–reality" curriculum, an "immersive–interactive–research-based" teaching paradigm, a "digital–networked–social" set of communication platforms, and a "process-based–comprehensive–developmental" evaluation system. It closes with a brief statement of the results Zhang says such integration has achieved.

On content, Zhang calls for going beyond simply telling stories, by linking the Jinggangshan and Yan'an spirits to Marxist views of practice and the masses. Content should be tiered by discipline and year of study, for example the "two bombs, one satellite" spirit for science and engineering students, and drawn from local resources such as Gannan, Shanghai and Jiaxing. On method, Zhang proposes VR/AR simulation labs, practice bases at memorials and former revolutionary areas, debates, historical dramas, flipped classrooms and student research projects. Platforms would include a national open digital archive, short videos, WeChat columns, live lectures, and cooperation among universities, government and enterprises.

For evaluation, Zhang proposes that process-based assessment make up at least 50 per cent of the final grade, with indicators covering knowledge, ability and values. Long-term tracking of graduates through surveys and interviews would feed back into course reform. Zhang concludes that the integration has already made abstract theory more vivid, raised classroom participation and strengthened students' patriotism and ideals. Read the original if you want a concise inventory of the teaching methods and assessment schemes currently promoted for Party-directed ideological courses in Chinese universities.
quoteEn: Integrating red cultural resources into university ideological and political courses must rest on the fundamental mission of fostering virtue and cultivating talent, working at four levels (content, model, carrier and mechanism) to bring red culture and these courses into deep fusion.
quoteZh: 将红色文化资源融入高校思政课教学，要立足立德树人根本使命，从内容、模式、载体、机制四个层面着力，推动红色文化与思政课深度交融。

glossary.explanation: The sites, documents, stories and spirit associated with the Chinese Communist Party's revolutionary history, used in patriotic and political education.
Compulsory Marxism and Party-theory courses taught in Chinese schools and universities.
A principle in Chinese education policy that moral and political formation is the basic task of schooling.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal of restoring China's national strength and international standing, prominent in official discourse since the 2010s.

t: Passing on the red gene to build a shared spiritual home for the Chinese nation
zh: 传承红色基因构筑中华民族共有精神家园
paras: Ma Xingyu asks how state-owned enterprises can pass on the "red gene" and so help build a shared spiritual home for the Chinese nation. This short commentary, published in China Social Sciences Today in March 2026, argues that corporate culture is a key force for carrying on red heritage and strengthening national spirit. It takes Baotou Iron and Steel (Group), known as Baogang, as its single case.

The piece has three parts. The first traces how Baogang's history became a "red resource". The second shows how that resource became identification with the company's culture. The third explains how Baogang's culture helps build the shared spiritual home. Ma draws on Halbwachs's account of how historical memory is activated through narration and commemoration.

Ma argues that the story "All pulling together to build Baogang" rose through four levels: individual builders' oral histories, artistic representations, internalisation in company histories, exhibition halls and ceremonies, and finally recognition in national narrative as a "historical tale" and red resource. Baogang then joined this inheritance of dedication and hard struggle to the new development philosophy. In Ma's account, "pulling together" now means collaborative research, industrial-chain coordination and company–locality co-prosperity. The author claims this gives a multi-ethnic workforce a "community" in practice, ties national and company identity together, and strengthens the sense of the Chinese nation as one family.

Ma concludes that Baogang has both grounded and elevated the shared spiritual home by turning historical memory into an ideological resource within present-day corporate culture. Read the original if you want a brief case study of how Chinese state-enterprise culture is linked to ethnic unity and red heritage.
quoteEn: Red resources are no longer static commemoration but an endogenous driving force for the enterprise's strategic transformation and for fulfilling its social responsibility.
quoteZh: 红色资源不再是静态的纪念，而是驱动企业战略转型、履行社会责任的内生动力。

glossary.explanation: A Party-discourse metaphor for the revolutionary values, spirit and traditions of the Communist Party that are meant to be inherited across generations.
Sites, relics, stories and spirit linked to the Party's revolutionary and socialist history, used in education and cultural work.

glossary.zh: 中华民族共有精神家园
glossary.en: shared spiritual home for the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: common spiritual homeland of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A Party formulation for the common culture and values meant to unite all ethnic groups in China, linked to building a sense of community of the Chinese nation.
Official concept introduced in 2015 stressing innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development.

t: Enhancing the value appeal of socialist culture in the new era
zh: 提升新时代社会主义文化的价值感召力
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 24 March 2026
paras: This newspaper commentary asks how the value appeal (jiazhi ganzhaoli) of socialist culture can be raised in the new era. Feng argues that this appeal is the core measure of a culture's vitality and influence, and that raising it is essential to building a strong socialist cultural nation and to steady progress of Chinese modernization. The piece takes its cue from the recommendations for the 15th Five-Year Plan adopted at the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee.
The article is organised in three parts: the theoretical source of the appeal, its core task, and the practical paths to strengthen it. It ends with a short summary of the whole project.

Feng locates the source of value appeal in the Two Integrations, especially the integration of Marxism with fine traditional Chinese culture. In the author's account, this produces a "new cultural organism" with firm cultural subjectivity, free of cultural "apprenticeship" and dependence, and it contributes to a new form of human civilization that goes beyond the Western path of capital logic and materialism. The core task is to internalise the core socialist values as national consensus and to turn them into people's civility. The paths are stimulating cultural creativity, including through AI and digital technology, deepening reform of cultural institutions under Marxism's guiding role in the ideological sphere, and building Chinese discourse and narratives to solve the problem of being unable to be heard abroad.

Feng concludes that raising value appeal is a major undertaking tied to the future of the nation and its spirit. It calls for cultural consciousness and confidence, institutional reform and a modern communication system. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official Chinese commentary links cultural confidence, core socialist values and international communication.
quoteEn: The "integration" is not a "platter of assorted dishes" or a simple "physical reaction" but a profound "chemical reaction", and through it a "new cultural organism" has been created.
quoteZh: “结合”不是“拼盘”，不是简单的“物理反应”，而是深刻的“化学反应”，经由“结合”造就了一个“新的文化生命体”。

glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's formula for integrating the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities (the first) and with fine traditional Chinese culture (the second).
The official term for China's path of modernization, presented as distinct from the Western model.
A twelve-word set of values promoted by the Party since 2012: prosperity, democracy, civility, harmony, freedom, equality, justice, rule of law, patriotism, dedication, integrity and friendship.

glossary.en: a new form of human civilization
glossary.explanation: An official phrase describing Chinese modernization as creating a civilization form different from Western modernization.

t: Empowering ideals-and-convictions education for young people through red venues
zh: 以红色场馆赋能青少年理想信念教育
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 24 March 2026
paras: This short newspaper commentary asks how red venues (museums, memorial halls and similar sites of Party history) can strengthen ideals-and-convictions education for young people. Li Nan argues that these venues are a core base for patriotic education and a "second classroom" for ideological and political education. The piece opens from Xi Jinping's call to use red resources and from the recommendations for the 15th Five-Year Plan.

The article first sets out the educational value of red venues on three levels: cognition, value guidance and practice. It then turns to two sets of measures, one on venue design and one on new educational forms and routes.

Li contends that red venues convey historical understanding, offer moral exemplars and let young people turn patriotic feeling into action. Because young people now want personalised, interactive and immersive experiences, Li says venues must be a two-way space. Proposed measures include digital reconstruction of historical scenes, VR/AR and 3D rendering, and symbolic rituals such as oath-taking. They also include big-data analysis to tailor content, and tasks, debates and short-video creation to spread red culture through "buzz" dissemination among peers.

Li concludes that red venues should pursue high-quality development by innovating on a foundation of fidelity to tradition. They should become places where the red gene is passed on and ideals are nurtured, supplying spiritual motivation for a new generation to take on national rejuvenation. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Chinese ideological-education writing links museum design, digital technology and youth engagement.
quoteEn: Red venues are not merely passive historical records and educational vehicles, but stand in a two-way, dialogic and interactive relationship with their audiences.
quoteZh: 红色场馆并非单纯被动的历史记录和教育载体，而是有着与受众双向的对话互动关系。

glossary.explanation: Museums, memorial halls, former revolutionary sites and similar places that preserve and present the history of the Communist Party and the revolution, used for patriotic education.
A Party metaphor for the revolutionary ideals, spirit and traditions that are said to be inherited across generations.
Ideological education aimed at instilling commitment to communism and socialism with Chinese characteristics, especially among young people.

glossary.literal: great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: Official goal of restoring China's strength and international standing, central to Party discourse since the early 2010s.
Official term for a development model stressing quality, innovation and efficiency over scale; here applied to the running of red venues.

t: Cultivating a high-spirited and striving ethos across the whole nation
zh: 涵养全民族昂扬奋发的精神气质
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 24 March 2026
paras: This commentary, first published in China Social Sciences Today, takes up a phrase from the Party Central Committee's recommendations for the 15th Five-Year Plan: the call to cultivate a high-spirited, striving ethos across the whole nation. Wang Weiguo argues that national rejuvenation needs spiritual as well as material strength. In Wang's account, this ethos reflects the character of an era and shapes a nation's future. The call is presented as guidance for advancing Chinese modernization, in which material and cultural-ethical progress are coordinated.

The article has three parts. The first sets out the theoretical foundations of the call. The second names its core requirements. The third proposes practical paths for putting it into effect. Wang draws on Marx, on Xi Jinping's remarks on Chinese civilization, and on classical Chinese sayings about self-improvement, renewal and the people as the foundation of the state.

Wang grounds the call in three sources. It puts into practice the Marxist view that the masses make history, by stirring the people's historical initiative. It is a contemporary expression of the vitality and continuity of Chinese civilization. It is also a requirement of common prosperity in spiritual life. The core requirements are three qualities: resolve (zhiqi), meaning unity and the will to overcome difficulties; backbone (guqi), meaning self-reliance, rejection of dependence and fearlessness under external pressure; and confidence (diqi), which Wang says rests on long cultural accumulation, economic strength and a solid scientific and technological base.

For practice, Wang calls for three steps. First, study the Party's innovative theory and master the Marxist standpoint, viewpoint and method. Second, build a healthy social atmosphere by coordinating urban and rural cultural-ethical development and weaving core socialist values into all areas of social life. Third, encourage people to strive in the economy, society and people's livelihood, through high-quality development, deeper reform and opening up, and shared social governance. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated scholars link the 15th Five-Year Plan's cultural goals to Marxist theory, traditional culture and policy practice.
quoteEn: Cultivating a high-spirited and striving ethos across the whole nation is a contemporary expression of the inner vitality and continuity of Chinese civilization.
quoteZh: 涵养全民族昂扬奋发的精神气质是中华文明内在生命力与赓续力的当代表达。

glossary.explanation: The official Party concept of China's own path to modernization. It stresses coordination of material and cultural-ethical progress, among other features.
A long-term official goal of shared prosperity for all. Here it is extended to the sphere of spiritual and cultural life.
The official economic strategy that puts quality, innovation and efficiency ahead of speed of growth.
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world, begun in 1978.
A set of 24 characters in twelve values, promoted officially since 2012 at the national, social and individual levels.

t: Three paths to strengthening the reach and influence of Chinese civilization
zh: 提升中华文明传播力影响力的三条路径
paras: Writing in China Social Sciences Today (20 March 2026), Han asks how Chinese civilization can be communicated abroad more effectively during the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026–2030). Han argues that the declining discursive dominance of the West and the rise of the Global South create an opening, but that the task now is to move from breaking through to building a lasting position, and from broad coverage to deep recognition. The answer is three mutually supporting paths, framed by the Plan's call for a Chinese discourse and narrative system.

The commentary is a short policy-oriented piece. It takes each path in turn: regional and country studies, culture–technology integration, and a plural ecosystem of narrators. Han draws on phrases from the Outline of the Plan and on public figures for online-game, micro-drama and web-literature revenue.

The first path uses area studies to overcome the "cognitive discount" that cultural products suffer abroad. Han calls for in-depth country research, country-specific or region-specific strategies, and measuring recognition and goodwill rather than output volume. The second path treats technology as a core variable. Han points to AI-driven content generation, immersive experiences such as digital museums, and online games, citing 2025 overseas revenue of US$20.455 billion for self-developed games. The third path draws on enterprises, local and grassroots actors, and outside voices such as foreign influencers and scholars. Han holds that the mainstream media's "solo" can no longer cover the whole field.

Han concludes that the paths answer three questions: precise communication addresses whom to speak to, technology-driven innovation addresses how, and ecosystem communication addresses who speaks. Together they would form a more effective international communication system and support a community with a shared future for mankind. Read the original if you want a concise statement of current Chinese thinking on international cultural communication under the 15th Five-Year Plan.
quoteEn: To make the "listeners" accept China's story, one must tell it well in a way the "listeners" find easy to accept.
quoteZh: 要让“听故事者”接受中国故事，则要用“听故事者”易于接受的方式讲好中国故事。

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy and global-governance concept promoted by Xi Jinping since the early 2010s. It presents the world's countries as sharing common interests and responsibilities.
A term for developing and emerging countries, used in Chinese official discourse to denote a group China seeks to engage and lead in international affairs.
China's national economic and social development plan for 2026–2030, setting priorities in areas including culture and international communication.

t: Using new types of cultural business to raise national cultural soft power across the board
zh: 以新型文化业态全面提升国家文化软实力
paras: Writing in the Chinese Social Sciences Today (20 March 2026), Li Fengliang asks how China's cultural industries can strengthen national cultural soft power during the 15th Five-Year Plan period. The commentary argues that fostering new types of cultural business (xinxing wenhua yetai) is the key breakthrough. It presents this as an economic question and also a political and cultural one, tied to the new cultural mission and to Xi Jinping's cultural thought.

Li begins by assessing where the sector stands. Citing official statistics, the article reports 2025 operating revenue of 15.2135 trillion yuan for cultural enterprises above designated size, up 7.4%, with sixteen new-format sub-sectors growing 14.3%. It also lists weaknesses: regional imbalance, with the eastern region producing about 80% of value added, a shortage of internationally influential IP, weak derivative and copyright operations, and low international market share. The rest is organised around new directions and new paths.

The core argument names three directions. First, technology empowerment should move from "culture plus technology" to "culture times technology", a chemical rather than physical reaction, illustrated by Henan TV's festival programmes and the Digital Palace Museum. Second, integration should build a "culture plus" ecosystem across tourism, sport, education and commerce, with the "Su Super" football league as an example. Third, value transmission should create globally influential cultural IP, with Ne Zha 2 and online literature, games and drama as examples. Li then proposes three paths: nurture new formats such as digital animation, immersive shows and micro-dramas; build large flagship "cultural aircraft carrier" firms, modelled on Disney and Shueisha, that work with smaller content makers; and release new momentum through institutional reform and support for new popular literature and art.

Li concludes that the 15th Five-Year Plan period is a critical stage for building a modernised socialist country and for upgrading the cultural industries. The author calls for guidance from Xi Jinping's cultural thought, high-quality development, and a cultural industry system that matches China's standing as a major country, so that Chinese culture can reach the world. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated scholars link the 15th Five-Year Plan's cultural policy to new cultural formats, technology and cultural exports.
quoteEn: Re-evaluating the value of new types of cultural business is not only an economic question but also a political and cultural one, and an inevitable requirement for fulfilling the new cultural mission of the new era.
quoteZh: 重新认识新型文化业态的价值，不仅是经济命题，更是政治命题、文化命题，是实现新时代新的文化使命的必然要求。

glossary.explanation: The influence a country gains through culture and values rather than coercion. In Chinese policy discourse it is treated as part of comprehensive national strength.
A body of ideas on cultural work attributed to Xi Jinping and formally set out in 2023. It guides Party policy on ideology, culture and the cultural industries.
An official policy goal, prominent since 2017, that favours innovation and quality over scale-driven growth.
China's national plan for economic and social development for 2026–2030, whose outline was adopted in March 2026.

t: Integration and symbiosis: advancing university–enterprise collaboration in education
zh: 融合共生 推动校企协同育人
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily on 24 March 2026, Bi Tianshu, president of North China Electric Power University, takes up how industry-oriented universities can deepen collaboration with enterprises in training talent. Starting from the 15th Five-Year Plan outline's call to integrate scientific and industrial innovation, Bi argues that such collaboration is the key link joining national strategy, industrial upgrading and university development, and so supports the building of a leading country in education.
The commentary has three parts. It first sets out the value of university–enterprise collaboration, then proposes rethinking the underlying ideas, and finally outlines three practical directions.

On value, Bi presents shared mission, aligned responsibility and common development as the three links between higher education, industry and the Double First-Class initiative. On ideas, Bi calls for a strategic partnership in place of short-term project or order-based cooperation, and for 'integration and symbiosis', in which teachers, platforms and research results are shared and the two sides form a '1+1>2' effect. Bi also calls for innovation-driven, 'leading' rather than merely adaptive training, focused on bottleneck technologies.

For practice, Bi proposes shifting from discipline-oriented to strategy-oriented training, from single-point cooperation to an ecosystem covering the whole industrial chain, and from serving the industry to strengthening national competitiveness. The last includes exporting technologies and standards through the Belt and Road Initiative and training globally minded professionals. Read the original if you want a university leader's official-style outline of how industry-oriented universities are expected to link talent training to national strategy.
quoteEn: Collaborative education should be upgraded from project cooperation to joint construction of an industry ecosystem, so that the integration of industry and education becomes an important ecological support for building a leading country in education.
quoteZh: 推动协同育人从项目合作升级为行业生态共建，让产教融合成为教育强国建设的重要生态支撑。

glossary.explanation: A national goal of building a world-leading education system, set out in official planning documents and linked to national development strategy.
China's national development plan for 2026–2030, whose outline sets economic and social priorities.
A government programme launched in 2015 to build world-class universities and disciplines.
China's international infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative, launched in 2013.

t: Practical paths to improving the effectiveness of the international communication of China's discourse
zh: 提升中国话语国际传播效能的实践路径
paras: This commentary, published in Guangming Daily on 20 March 2026, asks how China can raise the effectiveness of its international communication. Ni Mingsheng starts from the 15th Five-Year Plan outline's call to speed up China's discourse and narrative system. The author argues that digital-intelligent technology and media change are reshaping international communication, and that China needs a multi-channel, three-dimensional outward communication pattern to build a favourable external climate for Chinese modernization.

The piece is organised under four headings: building signature concepts and a discourse system that connects China and the world; using digital-intelligent technology to build a multi-channel communication pattern; coordinating platforms and cross-screen dissemination; and adopting effective strategies in the struggle over international opinion. Each section opens with a quotation from Xi Jinping and then sets out measures.

Ni's core claim is that China must shift its image from being shaped by others to self-shaping. The author proposes original concepts, story-based and differentiated messaging for different regional audiences, and big-data "user profiles" with AI-generated content and immersive technologies. Mainstream media should "borrow boats to go out to sea" by studying overseas platforms' recommendation mechanisms, while domestic platforms expand abroad. Ni describes the opinion landscape as still "strong West, weak China" and calls for rapid rebuttal of false information and for setting new agendas.

The author concludes by calling for a politically reliable, professionally skilled and technically literate international communication workforce. It would combine official, academic, popular and international voices, and be backed by a standardised system for evaluating effects by country, language and medium. Ni presents this as creating a favourable external environment for national rejuvenation. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official Chinese commentary frames international communication strategy under the 15th Five-Year Plan.
quoteEn: Efforts should focus on resolving the "contrast" between China's real image and Western subjective impressions, and the "gap" between self-shaping and being shaped by others.
quoteZh: 着力解决好中国真实形象与西方主观印象的“反差”、“自塑”与“他塑”之间的“落差”

glossary.explanation: The official Party formulation of China's own path to modernization, promoted since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
A contrast used in Chinese communication discourse between China presenting its own image and having it defined by foreign media.
China's national development plan outline for 2026–2030.

t: From "coping with virtual shocks" to "mastering the symbiosis of the virtual and the real": the social quasi-reality turn in ideological and political education
zh: 从“应对虚拟冲击”到“驾驭虚实共生”:思想政治教育之社会拟现实转向探究
source: Teaching and Research (教学与研究), 2025 no. 11
paras: Lu Lan asks how ideological and political education should respond as digital-intelligent technologies reshape human interaction and draw learners from physical into virtual space, a drift the article calls "spatial escape". The author proposes a "social quasi-reality turn" as a new concept and analytical framework. It would move the field from merely coping with virtual shocks to mastering a symbiosis of the virtual and the real.

The article defines social quasi-reality, sets out why the turn is needed, and describes what it changes in practice. It places the concept against policy documents, including the national education digitalisation strategy launched in 2022 and the State Council's August 2025 opinions on the "AI Plus" initiative. Its sections cover the concept's structure and theoretical roots, the technological and disciplinary drivers of the turn, and the new educational scenes it makes possible. The author also lists the risks.

Lu holds that social quasi-reality is a new reality nested inside existing society, not a copy of it. It is distinct from VR/AR "simulated reality", which reproduces the world as a digital scene. The author grounds it in Marxist practice theory and historical materialism and rejects Baudrillard-style "hyperreal" nihilism. The author argues that educators can neither intervene directly in real society nor in virtual society, so the quasi-reality layer is the interface where values become symbols, experience becomes narrative and contradictions become spectacle. Intervening at this layer would turn educators from passive responders into active architects. The author describes the resulting changes as multiple and virtual educational subjects, fragmented and customised content, a shift from authority-led transmission to intersubjective "meaning negotiation", and "liquid narrative" anchored by core socialist values. The author also names risks: algorithmic black boxes, the dilution of educators' discourse power, and the loss of critical reflection.

Lu concludes that the aim is to strengthen the real with the virtual, not to replace it. Embodied presence and face-to-face emotional exchange remain irreplaceable, and moral education must stay at the centre of technological innovation. The author calls for embodied scenes, personalised AI-assisted provision, cross-disciplinary tools for tracking value shifts in virtual communities, and an autonomous knowledge system for ideological and political education. Read the original if you study how Chinese scholars theorise digital technology, AI and ideological work, or how the field is being repositioned around the "AI Plus" policy.
quoteEn: Whether one speaks of quasi-reality, physicality or presence in ideological and political education, the core is to strengthen the "real" through the "virtual" rather than replace the "real" with the "virtual", thereby extending the educational function of physical space.
quoteZh: 无论是思想政治教育的拟现实或者实体性,还是在场性,其核心在于以“虚”强“实”,而非以“虚”代“实”,进而延伸物理空间的育人功能。

glossary.explanation: A Chinese Party-state educational field and discipline that cultivates political beliefs, values and morality, taught in schools and universities and in wider social settings.

The author's term for a new social reality in which virtual and physical spaces interweave in everyday life and social relations. The author distinguishes it from deliberately built VR/AR simulations.
A twelve-word set of national, social and individual values promoted officially since the 18th Party Congress (2012).
A State Council policy programme for integrating artificial intelligence into economic and social sectors, set out in opinions issued in August 2025.

t: The civilizational narrative and political-cultural logic of building the Chinese national community
zh: 华民族共同体建设的文明叙事与政治文化逻辑
paras: An Beijiang asks what historical and cultural foundations, and what practical logic, underlie the current policy of building the Chinese national community (Zhonghua minzu gongtongti jianshe). The author notes that existing research approaches the topic from many angles but rarely addresses its historical-cultural meaning. The article's thesis is that this project rests on the idea of grand unification, takes cultural identity as its core, uses exchanges, interaction and integration among ethnic groups as its practical path, and draws on cultural empowerment as its source of innovation.

The article opens with the Confucian-era "all under heaven" outlook and its development into the doctrine of grand unification (da yitong), traced from the Zhou, the Spring and Autumn and Warring States periods through the Qin-Han, Tang, Yuan and Qing dynasties. It then treats cultural identity, citing non-Han dynasties' claims to legitimacy and their adoption of Confucianism. A third section sets out Marxist theories of the nation, from Marx, Engels, Lenin and Stalin, and reviews the history of ethnic interaction, including migration, frontier settlement and trade. The last section turns to present-day measures.

An argues that grand unification was never simply territorial expansion. In the author's account it combined institutional innovation (commanderies and counties, the examination system, flexible frontier arrangements) with ideological integration. Because rulers of non-Han origin also claimed the mantle of "China", political consensus formed around shared cultural standards rather than lineage. The author presents the community as the product of long interaction that produced a "pluralistic yet unified" pattern. They also present the current term "exchanges, interaction and integration" as the Marxist theory of ethnic fusion combined with the Chinese idea of harmony, and as distinct from assimilation.

For the present, An proposes a socialist core values-led consensus, the retelling of historical narratives around the pluralistic-unified pattern, the exploration of shared cultural resources, and the building of mutually embedded social structures and communities. The author also calls for a move from "physical superposition" to "chemical reaction", and for opposing narrow nationalism. The author concludes that the approach offers a Chinese solution for governing multi-ethnic states and for the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want a Chinese scholarly account that links imperial-era unification thought, Marxist nation theory and current ethnic policy.
quoteEn: The consciousness of the Chinese national community is in essence the result of historical and cultural identification, and cultural identity is the deepest level of identity.
quoteZh: 中华民族共同体意识本质上就是历史文化认同的结果，文化认同是最深层次的认同

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal, prominent since Xi Jinping's leadership began in 2012, of restoring China's strength and international standing by the mid-twenty-first century.

The Party's current ethnic policy line, which stresses the shared identity of all of China's ethnic groups as one nation and places it above group-specific identities. Related slogans include forging a strong sense of community for the Chinese nation.

A traditional Chinese political idea, found in the Gongyang commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals, valuing a politically and culturally unified realm. The article treats it as the ideological basis of the national community.
A formula in current ethnic policy for broad contact among ethnic groups. Official discourse presents it as distinct from forced assimilation.

t: Building a strong cultural self for contemporary China
zh: 构建当代中国强大的文化自我
source: Marxist Studies (马克思主义研究), 2025 no. 12
paras: Shen Xiangping takes up a concept he reads out of Xi Jinping's thought on culture: the "cultural self", meaning a nation's firm self in the cultural sense. He argues that the new cultural mission of the new era, namely promoting cultural prosperity and building a strong cultural nation, amounts to building a strong cultural self for contemporary China. In his view this is the fundamental task of cultural construction today.

The article treats Xi's remarks as an implicit system of five "identity questions" about the cultural self: who it is (subjectivity), where it comes from (historicity), where it is going (direction), what its essence is, and how it is confirmed in practice. It first draws on the philosophical question "who am I" to trace a sequence from self-knowledge through self-awareness and self-confidence to self-reliance and self-strengthening. It then takes each of the five questions in turn, relating them to the Two Integrations and to Xi's wider strategic framework.

Shen's central claim is that cultural subjectivity is the foundation of the cultural self. In his account, the Communist Party rebuilt it in modern form after it had nearly been lost, and consolidated it through the Two Integrations, above all the second. Contemporary Chinese culture, he says, is a "new cultural life-form" whose lifeblood is Marxism as its soul, excellent traditional Chinese culture as its root, and present-day practice as its vitality. Its essence is socialism with Chinese characteristics under Party leadership. Its core is Chinese values: core socialist values, common values of all humanity, and the primacy of the people. Shen presents it as a culture at "the height of principle", citing Marx, with the free and all-round development of the person as its aim, in contrast to a Western modernity he characterises as capital-centred.

Shen proposes that confirming the cultural self in practice follows the "7+1" requirements Xi set out. He highlights four tasks: strengthening cultural identity across ethnic groups, stimulating cultural creativity through information technology and AI, raising soft power through opening up while insisting on China's own discourse, and keeping the person at the centre of cultural work. He ends by calling for long-term mechanisms in institutions, policy, talent and evaluation. Read the original if you want a detailed look at how Chinese philosophers systematise Xi Jinping's cultural thought around the concepts of cultural subjectivity and the cultural self.
quoteEn: In essence, the cultural self of contemporary China is a deep fusion of Marxism and Chinese civilization.
quoteZh: 当代中国文化自我本质上是马克思主义与中华文明的深度融合。

glossary.explanation: Formula for combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture. The second integration was added to official discourse by Xi Jinping in 2021–2023.
The cultural component of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, formally put forward in October 2023.
Xi's term, used since 2023, for a culture's capacity to stand on its own, develop itself and respond to challenges. Official texts treat it as the basis of cultural confidence.
A set of twelve values promoted by the Party since 2012, covering the national, social and individual levels.

t: Artificial intelligence and the transformation of teaching paradigms in ideological and political education
zh: 人工智能赋能思想政治教育教学范式变革
paras: This newspaper commentary, published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in March 2026, asks how artificial intelligence (AI) can drive a systematic change in the teaching paradigm of ideological and political education. Yuan and Huang argue that deep integration of AI and such teaching is an important route for carrying out the fundamental task of fostering virtue through education, and that it requires a coordinated framework rather than scattered tools.

The authors begin with policy background: Xi Jinping's remarks on AI and education, the proposal for the 15th Five-Year Plan period to implement an "AI Plus" action, and the 2024–2035 plan for building a leading education nation. They then review existing practice, set out the risks of the coming period, and discuss three measures: a three-in-one system, a school-wide ecosystem, and new human–machine teaching models.

In Yuan and Huang's account, platforms, virtual simulations and case libraries have eased the limits of time, space and uniform supply in traditional teaching, but problems remain: fragmented applications, content that does not match needs, and weak institutional links. They call for a system of technology, content and mechanisms, with the leading role of value guidance combined with students' and teachers' actual needs. They also call for strict tiered data management and prior review and dynamic calibration of algorithms to prevent bias, data leaks and non-compliant content. Using the national smart education platform, university systems and social resources, they propose tiered resource pools and unified data platforms. They cite Tsinghua, Huazhong and UESTC AI agents as examples of the shift from one-way lecturing to human–machine guidance.

The authors conclude that teachers should become designers of integrated teaching, supported by a dedicated corpus for ideological and political education, cross-university sharing and AI training for teachers, so that technology and value guidance move together. Read the original if you want a concise view of how official policy language frames AI in Chinese university ideological and political courses.
quoteEn: We must uphold the principle of "technology for good", focus on the difficulties of putting technology into practice, improve the design of smart platforms, break down data barriers between teaching settings and management departments, and make the analysis of learning conditions, resource delivery and evaluative feedback intelligent.
quoteZh: 要坚持“科技向善”原则，聚焦技术落地难点，优化智慧平台功能设计，打通不同教学场景、管理部门数据壁垒，实现学情分析、资源推送、评价反馈的智能化。

glossary.explanation: The system of teaching in Chinese schools and universities, including "ideological and political theory courses", meant to convey Party-endorsed values and theory.
A stated fundamental task of Chinese education: shaping students' moral character alongside knowledge, in line with Party policy.
A national initiative, set out in a 2025 State Council opinion, to integrate AI into the economy, society and public services, including education.
China's national development plan for 2026–2030.

t: Promoting the effective integration of the ideological and political classroom and the social classroom
zh: 促进思政课堂和社会课堂有效融合
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 17 March 2026
paras: This newspaper commentary takes up a call in the proposals for the 15th Five-Year Plan, adopted at the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2025), to integrate the ideological and political classroom with the social classroom. Wang argues that such integration is the fundamental route for universities to carry out the task of fostering virtue through education.

The piece has three parts: the theoretical rationale, the practical obstacles, and proposed remedies. It draws on the Marxist theory of practice and on Marx's Theses on Feuerbach, and it discusses higher-education ideological and political courses.

Wang holds that "effective integration" is not a spatial overlay but a deep mutual embedding of theory teaching and social practice. In this account it moves students from knowledge to identification to action and counters the weakness of one-way lecturing amid contested currents of thought. The author names three problems: fragmented mechanisms and uncoordinated resources, with practice reduced to visits; practice that is formalistic, driven by "check-in" tasks and lacking evaluation; and uneven coverage, with teachers who are poorly prepared to guide practice.

Wang proposes a systematic understanding of each classroom's function and stronger top-level design, with resource sharing and integrated primary-to-university courses. The author also proposes two-way feedback between practice and theory, and a professional support system with evaluation and cross-sector instructors. The aim is to train a new generation able to shoulder national rejuvenation and serve Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-line ideological education policy is justified and operationalised in universities.
quoteEn: "Effective integration" is by no means a simple spatial overlay or formal patchwork.
quoteZh: “有效融合”绝非简单的空间叠加或形式拼凑

glossary.explanation: A long-standing educational formula, made the 'fundamental task' of Chinese education in Party documents since the 18th Party Congress (2012). It stresses moral and political formation alongside knowledge.
The compulsory courses in Marxism and Party ideology taught at Chinese schools and universities.
The official term for the Party's path of national development, prominent since the 20th Party Congress (2022).

t: Strengthening the scholarly foundations to release the educational vitality of ideological and political courses
zh: 厚植学理根基，释放思政课育人活力
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily, Feng Xiujun, dean of the School of Marxism at Renmin University of China, asks how ideological and political theory courses (sizheng ke) in schools and universities can meet the new demand for "connotative development". Feng argues that this development depends on winning by quality and persuading through reasoning, and that both rest on deeper theoretical and teaching research. The piece opens with Xi Jinping's 2019 remarks on these courses and with the 15th Five-Year Plan outline, which calls for implementing the new-era curriculum plan for university courses of this kind.

The commentary is organised under three headings, each proposing a base of research. The first concerns ideas and theory, the second course and textbook research, and the third research on teaching methods and on students. Feng presents the courses as combining politics, ideology, scholarship and professional skill, and as requiring a unity of "the way", "learning" and "technique".

On theory, Feng calls for systematic, scholarly interpretation of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. This means turning concrete experience into general laws and political discourse into academic expression. Feng also urges teachers to read the Marxist classics and traditional Chinese texts closely, in line with the Two Integrations. On textbooks, the author distinguishes the academic system, driven by the unknown and valuing originality, from the textbook system, built on consensus and certainty. The textbook system in turn differs from the teaching system, which is organised around specific problems. Feng wants each to be converted into the next, and research on how the Introduction to Xi Jinping Thought course relates to other courses, and across undergraduate, master's and doctoral stages. On teaching, Feng says the notion that pedagogical research is not scholarship must be overcome. The author proposes studying students' thinking, using AI-based learning data, and mastering the shift from knowing to believing to acting, so that abstract theory becomes concrete narrative in youth-friendly language.

Feng concludes that the courses' persuasive power comes from rigorous research at all three levels, and that this is what will move teaching from supplying content to shaping values. The author also calls for the courses to adopt digital and intelligent technologies, combining case-based, inquiry-based and experiential teaching. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how a leading Marxist-studies administrator links theory, textbook and pedagogical research in ideological and political education.
quoteEn: The \"connotation\" in connotative development lies, at its core, in winning by quality, at root in persuading through reasoning, and, crucially, in in-depth theoretical and teaching research.
quoteZh: 内涵式发展之“内涵”，核心在于以质取胜，根本在于以理服人，关键在于深入的理论和教学研究。

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses in Chinese schools and universities that teach Marxism, Party theory, history and morality. They are treated as central to the task of fostering virtue and cultivating people.
A development path that stresses quality, depth and internal substance rather than expansion in scale.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018. It is now the core content of ideological and political courses.
The formula that Marxism's basic tenets should be combined with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture.

t: How to better explain theory to young people
zh: 如何更好地把理论讲给青年听
authors: Yanhe Lecturers' Group, Renmin University of China
paras: This commentary, published in Guangming Daily on 17 March 2026, is written by Renmin University of China's "Yanhe Lecturers' Group", a student-led theory outreach team. It asks how the Party's innovative theory can be presented in ways that suit young people's habits of thought and reception. The authors argue that youth, as a generation that grew up with the internet, resist rigid preaching but want vivid ideas, and that young lecturers have a distinct advantage in speaking to their peers.

Written while the Party is studying the spirit of the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2025), the piece draws on the group's own practice in schools, communities, villages and enterprises. It is organised around three problems the group says it has tried to solve: the gap between theoretical discourse and young people's lives, the competition for attention in the modern media environment, and the mismatch between uniform supply and varied audiences.

On the first, the authors say that abstract, document-style language fails young listeners. The group therefore links the plenum's decisions to real issues and uses a chain of theory point, real-life scene, case and action implication, with everyday phrasing such as ecological civilization being a "grand chorus" rather than the government's "solo". On the second, it combines online booking platforms with on-site lectures, and ties talks to grassroots Party and Youth League meetings so that a single talk becomes regular study. On the third, it profiles each audience before preparing, swaps cases and adjusts expression under the same theme, and assembles modular "lecture packs".

The authors conclude that accuracy and depth must be combined with lively expression, flexible organisation and precise targeting if the popularisation of theory is to persuade and take root. Read the original if you want a short, practice-based example of how Party-sponsored student lecture teams describe their methods for youth theory outreach.
quoteEn: By having theory undergo a "re-translation" for the masses in concrete situations, the popularisation of theory can achieve more persuasive and compelling innovation while preserving its scientific character and truth.
quoteZh: 通过推动理论在具体情境中完成一次面向群众的“再转译”，使理论大众化在保持科学性、真理性的前提下实现更具说服力感染力的创新创造。

glossary.explanation: Official phrase for the Party's latest theoretical achievements, centred today on Xi Jinping Thought. Study and propagation of it is a standing task of Party education.

glossary.pinyin: dǎng de èrshí jiè sì zhōngquánhuì
glossary.en: the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee
glossary.explanation: A plenary session of the Party's 20th Central Committee, held in 2025, whose decisions are being studied nationwide according to the article.

t: Optimising and strengthening the discursive power of the Communist Party of China in the all-media era
zh: 全媒体时代中国共产党话语权优化与提升分析
paras: Wu Yangsong asks how the Communist Party of China can consolidate and raise its discursive power (huayuquan, the capacity of its language to shape public understanding) now that the "all-media" environment has changed how information is produced and spread. The article argues that this environment has reset discourse production, interaction and power relations, and that the Party must therefore strengthen its discursive consciousness, discourse system and discursive capabilities together.

The article is built in three steps. It first describes how the all-media era, driven by network, digital and intelligent technologies, has transformed the Party's discursive environment. It then sets out four new features of the discourse field and four resulting challenges. Finally it proposes remedies under three headings: discursive consciousness, the discourse system (theme, content, form) and discursive capability (production, communication, struggle, governance).

Wu holds that, unlike in the era of newspapers, radio and television, discourse production is no longer one-directional, and communication has shifted from top-down "one-to-many" to networked "many-to-many". In this setting the public's sense of itself as a speaker has grown, and attention has turned to everyday life, entertainment and emotion. In the author's account, this tests the consensus-building quality of Party discourse, weakens its dominance, and exposes its cohesion and practical effect to deconstruction, rumour, commercial traffic logic and what the article calls hostile forces. The remedies include overcoming the habit of doing rather than speaking, balancing lofty ideals with livelihood concerns, making content fact-based and problem-oriented, and using popular, vivid forms. Wu also calls for original concepts, agenda-setting, segmented and dialogic communication, a readiness to confront erroneous trends, and law-based content review and governance of online discourse.

Wu concludes that building discursive power in the all-media era is a complex systemic project requiring simultaneous change in how the Party thinks about, structures and conducts its speech. The proposals are presented as the Party's task of leading the production, spread and governance of discourse, not merely reacting to it. Read the original if you study Chinese Party communication, ideological work or online public opinion management and want a detailed statement of how a Chinese Marxist scholar frames the Party's discursive challenges and responses.
quoteEn: Discursive power is a power that expresses certain ideas and value orientations through the control and use of discursive resources, and thereby gains the authority to interpret, regulate and guide social life.
quoteZh: 话语权是一种通过对话语资源的控制与运用来表达某种思想观念、价值取向并获得解释、规范和指导社会生活的权力

glossary.explanation: The capacity to shape how issues are framed and understood in public communication. Widely used in Chinese scholarship and official language on ideology and international communication.
A term for the converged media environment of integrated traditional and digital media, in which, as Xi Jinping has put it, media is omnipresent and everyone can take part in producing information.
The organised set of concepts, themes, expressions and narratives through which a party or state presents its ideas.

t: Practical paths and significance of carrying forward the Long March spirit in the new era
zh: 新时代传承长征精神的实践路径与意义探析
source: Journal of the China Executive Leadership Academy Jinggangshan, 2025 no. 6
paras: Zhu Hong and Li Wenjia ask how the Long March spirit, long treated mainly through historical study and commemoration, can be turned into a working resource under socialism with Chinese characteristics in the new era. They argue that the spirit is a dynamic structure that has moved from political mobilisation to governance guidance. In their account it is now embedded in institutions, culture and communication, and supports Chinese modernization.

The article first traces the spirit through four stages: its original formation during the Long March of the 1930s, its deepening in socialist construction, its extension in the reform and opening up period through the idea of a "new Long March", and its dual institutional and cultural embedding since the 18th Party Congress (2012). It then sets out a five-part structure of belief, organisation, action, communication and cohesion. Finally it examines four fields of value (political, social, cultural and international) and illustrates them with cases such as Ninghua's "Long March College", Ruijin volunteer teams, Guangxi's Xiang River memorial sites and the Guizhou Long March National Cultural Park.

The core argument is that each dimension of the structure has its own route of transmission. Belief is cultivated through renewed ideological and political education, including integrated courses, case banks and experiential or digital "memory communities". Organisational capacity is carried by turning red resources into institutions through legislation, cadre-training academies and grassroots Party building. Action appears in social collaboration, for example volunteers invoking the spirit during the 2021 Zhengzhou floods. Communication and cohesion rely on digital re-creation, immersive red culture-and-tourism, and international outreach such as the "Long March" rockets and the Belt and Road Initiative. The authors also note a tension between authoritative narratives and user-generated reinterpretation online.

The authors conclude that the Long March spirit has moved beyond static commemoration to become a cultural gene of institutional design and a support for the national narrative. They call for it to move past ritualised and symbolic communication and be integrated more fully into the systems of governance, cultural innovation and international communication. In their view this would turn it from red memory into a civilisational resource and from national spirit into a global value. Read the original if you want a survey of how Chinese scholars and local institutions describe the practical institutionalisation of Party spirit, with many regional examples.
quoteEn: From "revolutionary mobilisation" to "development governance", its core function has shifted from political mobilisation to guidance of governance.
quoteZh: 从“革命动员”到“发展治理”，其核心功能实现了由政治动员向治理引领的转型。

glossary.explanation: The set of values attributed to the Red Army's Long March of 1934–36, such as firm belief, endurance, self-reliance and reliance on the masses. The Party treats it as part of its spiritual lineage.
The official term for China's path of modernisation under Party leadership, prominent in Party discourse since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
A metaphor used since the late 1970s for the tasks of modernisation and reform. Later leaders applied it to national rejuvenation.
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world, launched in 1978.
China's international infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative, launched in 2013.

t: The spiritual force for achieving the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation: structure, roots and driving mechanisms
zh: 实现中华民族伟大复兴的精神力量：结构、根源与动力机制
paras: Wang Yongyou and Wei Mingyong take up the call in the 20th Party Congress report (2022) to strengthen the spiritual force for achieving the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. They note that existing scholarship deals mainly with its meaning, how it arises, its sources and ways of promoting it, but has not analysed its structure, roots and driving mechanisms. Their thesis is that this force is a complex system that can be understood through three analytical lenses, and that such an analysis is a precondition for strengthening it in the drive to build a modern socialist country.

The article is organised in three parts. The first analyses the internal structure of the spiritual force along three dimensions: its agents (individual, group and nation), its sources of motivation (material, psychological and spiritual needs) and its functions. The second traces four roots: material, ideological, institutional and cultural. The third sets out three driving mechanisms, namely guidance, incentive and publicity. The argument draws throughout on Marx, Engels, Lenin and Xi Jinping.

On structure, the authors argue that individual, group and national strength relate quantitatively, as accumulation, and qualitatively, as consolidation. Human needs, rising with the productive forces, are the source of the force, which performs four functions: spiritual guidance, cohesion, creativity and fighting capacity. These are described as subjective in content but objective in essence, and as mutually reinforcing. On roots, the authors rely on the claim that social being determines social consciousness. They hold that economic achievements since reform and opening up, the Party's innovative theory, the institutions of socialism with Chinese characteristics, and Chinese traditional, revolutionary and socialist culture together generate the force. The institutional argument contrasts Chinese institutions with what the authors call Western capitalist systems, which they describe as unable to overcome the contradiction between private ownership and socialised production.

The three mechanisms are presented as working together. Guidance turns people's interests and needs into action under the leadership of the Communist Party of China. Incentive uses the Chinese Dream, phased goals and the link between the ultimate communist ideal and the common ideal of socialism with Chinese characteristics. Publicity builds public understanding of the Party and a supportive climate of opinion. The authors conclude that strengthening the force requires adherence to Marxism, cultural confidence and Party leadership.
