In the first section, Li presents the Second Integration, the combination of Marxism with fine traditional Chinese culture, as an expression of cultural and spiritual subjectivity. Without it, Li says, a nation cannot treat its own or other cultures correctly. In the second, Li holds that Marxism and traditional culture suit each other and enrich each other, so that the Party must neither abandon Marxism nor forget its cultural roots. Li contends that this approach goes beyond the old "ti-yong" (substance–function) relationship and resolves the long dispute between ancient and modern, Chinese and Western, which Li sees in both wholesale Westernisation and cultural restorationism. In the third section, Li describes the cultural achievements since the 18th Party Congress (2012), lists remaining challenges, and says culture must be built for and by the people.

Li concludes that cultural strength depends on self-reliant spiritual independence, a people-centred orientation and a large body of cultural talent. Li holds that this is compatible with openness and mutual learning among civilisations, and rejects what the author calls Western theories of a "clash of civilisations" and "civilisational superiority". The task, in Li's account, is to cultivate socialist culture with Chinese characteristics for a new era. Read the original if you want a senior Central Party School official's account of how the Second Integration and cultural subjectivity are framed in Party discourse on building a culturally strong country.
quoteEn: Holding fast to this soul and these roots is the foundation and precondition of theoretical innovation.
quoteZh: 坚守好这个魂和根，是理论创新的基础和前提。

glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's formula for combining the basic tenets of Marxism with fine traditional Chinese culture. It is the second of the Two Integrations, the first being the combination of Marxism with China's concrete realities.
The cultural component of Xi Jinping Thought, formally put forward in 2023. It covers Party leadership of ideology and culture, cultural confidence and the building of a culturally strong country.
The idea that Chinese culture has its own independent standing, self-awareness and initiative. Xi Jinping has linked it to the Second Integration.
The official term for the Party's path of modernisation with Chinese characteristics, stressed since the 20th Party Congress (2022).

t: The spirit of the Northeast Anti-Japanese United Army as an enduring monument forged by the Communist Party of China
zh: 东北抗联精神是中国共产党熔铸的不朽丰碑
paras: This short commentary, published in China Social Sciences Today in October 2025, asks where the spirit of the Northeast Anti-Japanese United Army (Kang Lian) came from. Li Xiaoyu argues that it was not an isolated or spontaneous product. In the author's account, its roots and its guiding thread lie in the leadership of the Communist Party of China.

The article first sets out the historical background: the Japanese occupation after the September 18th Incident of 1931, early volunteer forces, the Party-led guerrilla units of 1932, and the formal founding of the United Army in February 1936. It then examines three foundations of the spirit, namely its historical setting, its ideological base and its organisational guarantee.

On ideology, Li holds that Party cadres sent to the northeast, such as Yang Jingyu and Zhao Yiman, used Marxism to raise soldiers' understanding from simple patriotism to a grasp of national independence and the world anti-fascist cause. The author points to the journal Lenin's Banner and study classes as channels for this. On politics, Li stresses the Party's early calls for resistance and the anti-Japanese national united front line. On organisation, Li cites political departments, commissars and the principle of building Party branches at company level. Li quotes the commander Feng Zhongyun to argue that units without Communists at their core collapsed or surrendered.

Li concludes that Party leadership ran through the whole formation of the spirit. The article calls on readers to understand this inner link, carry on the "red genes" and work for the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want a brief example of how current Party-education writing links a wartime resistance narrative to the principle of Party leadership.
quoteEn: The spirit of the Northeast Anti-Japanese United Army is a precious spiritual legacy forged in blood and lives by the Communist Party of China leading the people of the Northeast through 14 years of arduous anti-Japanese struggle, and Party leadership ran through the whole process of its formation.
quoteZh: 东北抗联精神是中国共产党领导东北人民在14年艰苦卓绝的抗日斗争中，用鲜血和生命浇灌铸就的宝贵精神财富，党的领导贯穿于这一精神形成的全过程。

glossary.en: the spirit of the Northeast Anti-Japanese United Army
glossary.explanation: A Party-defined body of values drawn from the Communist-led guerrilla resistance to Japan in Manchuria, 1931–45. It is one of the officially recognised spirits of the Party's revolutionary history.
The Communist Party's policy from the mid-1930s of uniting all classes and factions against Japanese aggression. The article ties it to the 1935 August 1st Declaration and the Wayaobu meeting.

glossary.en: building Party branches at company level
glossary.explanation: A principle of Party control over the army, put forward in the late 1920s. Party branches are set up in each company so that Party leadership reaches the lowest units.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: An official goal of Chinese national revival, strongly associated with Xi Jinping's leadership.

t: The Asiatic conception of society in Marx's theory of world history
zh: 马克思世界历史理论中的亚细亚社会观
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 13 October 2025
paras: This short commentary asks how Marx's view of "Asiatic" society changed and why it came to be included in his scheme of world history. Wang argues that around 1853 Marx shared the Europe-wide image of Asia as a stagnant society, but that in the Grundrisse he built a new framework and so moved Asiatic society from a regional particularity to a universal stage of history.

The article first outlines the Asiatic conception current in Europe in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries. It then turns to Marx's 1853 articles on India in the New-York Daily Tribune, the Grundrisse chapter on pre-capitalist forms, his 1881 draft replies to Vera Zasulich, and the 1859 Preface to A Contribution to the Critique of Political Economy.

Wang says the European conception moved from state ownership of land under despotism (eighteenth century), to the absence of a bourgeoisie and civil society (early nineteenth), to the despotic state resting on patriarchal communities (late nineteenth). In 1853 Marx described India as stagnant, without private landownership or history, and as able to change only through British capitalism's \"double mission\". In the Grundrisse, Wang argues, Marx instead identified three features of Asiatic ownership: the individual's dependence on the community, communal landownership, and the union of agriculture and handicrafts within the community. His focus shifted from the despotic state to the community and its land tenure. Wang links this to Marx's effort to escape Eurocentrism by studying Asia on its own terms, which allowed the \"Asiatic mode of production\" to open the sequence of stages in the 1859 Preface.

Wang concludes that the Grundrisse framework guided Marx's later work on Asiatic society, including the \"agricultural commune\" of 1881, and that the text made Asiatic society part of world history. Read the original if you want a compact account of how Marx's treatment of the Asiatic mode of production developed from the 1853 India writings to the Grundrisse and the 1859 Preface.
quoteEn: To escape Eurocentrism, Marx no longer examined Asiatic society through European historical experience but returned to Asiatic society itself, seeking to bring its trajectory of development into the scheme of world history.
quoteZh: 马克思为了摆脱欧洲中心论，不再依据欧洲历史经验审视亚细亚社会，而是回到亚细亚社会本身，试图将亚细亚社会发展轨迹纳入世界历史图示。

t: Accelerating the construction of an independent knowledge system for Chinese ecological economics
zh: 加快构建中国生态经济学自主知识体系
paras: This short commentary, published in China Social Sciences Today in October 2025, asks how China should build an independent knowledge system for ecological economics. Liu Yaobin takes Xi Jinping's call to build an independent Chinese system of knowledge as the starting point. Liu argues that such a system is a mission of the era for a modernization in which humanity and nature live in harmony, and that it also serves China's voice in global environmental governance.

The article is organised in three parts. The first sets out the mission and the need for original concepts and theories drawn from China's own conditions. The second treats China's ecological civilization practice as the "roots" of the system. The third treats the "two mountains" idea as its "soul".

Liu holds that practical results confirm the theory: the article cites a 57 per cent fall in PM2.5 in key cities, more than thirty years of simultaneous growth in forest area and stock, and energy consumption growth of 3.34 per cent a year supporting 6.11 per cent economic growth over 2013–2024. In Liu's account, institutional innovations such as the "1+N+4" legal framework, central environmental inspections and the river and lake chief system turn the principle of internalising externalities into governance practice. The "two mountains" idea, which Liu describes as a Sinicised development of Marxist ecological thought, treats nature as "natural capital" and a source of value. Liu presents this as a shift from Western environmental economics' externality theory to an "endogenisation" theory, supported by mechanisms such as GEP accounting, ecological compensation and carbon trading.

Liu concludes that the system is needed for Chinese modernization and for global environmental governance. The author calls for deeper summing-up of local experience, definition of signature concepts, extraction of original theory and Chinese discourse, guided by the Two Integrations. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Chinese academic leadership frames ecological economics as part of building independent knowledge systems.
quoteEn: The \"two mountains\" idea has given the independent knowledge system of Chinese ecological economics its soul, achieving a paradigm revolution from Western environmental economics' \"externality\" theory to a \"ecological endogenisation\" theory with Chinese characteristics.
quoteZh: “两山”理念为构建中国生态经济学自主知识体系注入了灵魂，实现了从西方环境经济学“外部性”理论到中国特色“生态内生化”理论的范式革命。

glossary.explanation: Formula associated with Xi Jinping: combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's specific realities and with its fine traditional culture.
The official term for China's path of modernization, presented since the 20th Party Congress (2022) as distinct from Western models.

glossary.literal: the 'two mountains' concept: lucid waters and lush mountains are invaluable assets
glossary.explanation: Slogan put forward by Xi Jinping in 2005 that "lucid waters and lush mountains are invaluable assets", holding that environmental protection and economic development can reinforce each other.
Official concept of a development model that integrates environmental protection into economic, political and social development, written into Party and state documents.

t: Actively building China's autonomous knowledge classification system
zh: 积极构建中国自主知识分类体系
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 27 October 2025
paras: Sun Guozhu asks how Chinese scholarship can move beyond building discipline-by-discipline autonomous knowledge systems towards a deeper layer: an autonomous knowledge classification system and a 'public framework of principles' (gongong xueli kuangjia). Writing in a newspaper commentary, Sun argues that mutual understanding between civilizations depends on aligning modes of thinking, which are embodied in the knowledge systems each civilization produces. The classification system is presented as the 'chip' or underlying logic of knowledge production.

The piece first distinguishes the autonomous knowledge system from the classification system. The latter is a framework for classifying knowledge, and Sun borrows Yan Fu's phrase 'the method of all methods, the learning of all learning' to describe it. The public framework is the set of universal principles on which classification rests, so that realising one amounts to completing the other. Sun then proposes three dimensions of work: rethinking how disciplines divide and recombine, overcoming the split between the sciences and the humanities, and drawing on Chinese civilization's own intellectual resources.

On the first dimension, Sun notes that existing human knowledge is built mainly on Western disciplinary frameworks and calls for integrating the classification schemes of other civilizations, since the social sciences and humanities often lack a single optimal answer. On the second, Sun treats the sciences–humanities divide, citing C. P. Snow's 'two cultures' and Marx's remark that natural science and the science of man will become one science. Sun adds that science is ultimately a 'technique' (shu) and cannot be the shared foundation of society, which should rest on a 'way' (dao). Sun adds that AI and the problem of value alignment give the humanities a practical role. On the third, Sun contends that Chinese learning historically stressed scholarship and method, producing a synthesising, 'comprehensive' character. Sun argues that this should help dispel the 'China had no science' view, which Sun attributes to civilizational misunderstanding and narrow Western disciplinary definitions.

Sun concludes that forming a new form of human civilization requires an autonomous knowledge system, and that exploring classification and the public framework is an important breakthrough for reform. The system should not become a fixed standard but a living, open scheme that can be adjusted as humanity comes to know and change the world. Sun presents this as significant for reconciliation among civilizations and for a fresh arrangement of 'the sum of human knowledge'. Read the original if you want a short statement of one scholar's agenda for rethinking disciplinary classification within the Chinese debate on autonomous knowledge systems.
quoteEn: The autonomous knowledge classification system is like the 'chip' of knowledge production, able to organically optimise and recombine 'the sum of human knowledge'.
quoteZh: 自主知识分类体系犹如知识生产的“芯片”，能够对“人类知识的总和”进行有机的优化组合。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted in Chinese official and academic discourse, especially since Xi Jinping's 2022 remarks, calling for Chinese philosophy and social sciences to develop their own concepts and theories rather than depend on Western ones.
The author's proposed underlying framework for classifying all knowledge, treated as a deeper layer beneath individual disciplines' knowledge systems.
The author's term for a system of universal principles and rules underlying knowledge classification, meant to be shared across civilizations.
An official formulation associated with Chinese modernization, used to describe a civilizational path China presents as distinct from the Western model.

t: The internal mechanism by which culture supports high-quality economic development
zh: 文化支撑经济高质量发展的内在机理
paras: This commentary in Guangming Daily asks how culture sustains economic development. Zhu Hongjun builds on Xi Jinping's remarks in Zhijiang xinyu (Xi's collected Zhejiang-era essays) and argues that culture gives economic development three things: deep humanistic value, high organisational efficiency and stronger competitiveness.

The piece follows that three-part structure, one section for each. It draws on contrasts between Western mainstream economics and Marxist political economy, on traditional Chinese ethics, on the Party's record of economic work, and on the example of Zhejiang's regional economy. It ends with proposals for the new era.

On value, Zhu contrasts the "rational economic man" of Western economics, which the author ties to the logic of capital, with a Marxist stance that puts people first. Traditional ideas such as enriching the people and balancing righteousness with profit are presented as cultural resources, and the call to cultivate a financial culture with Chinese characteristics is read as an application of the Two Integrations. On organisation, Zhu credits cultural traditions of honesty, contract and cooperation with lowering transaction costs. Zhejiang's tailoring, footwear and small-commodity trades are offered as cases, as is corporate culture's role in cohesion. On competitiveness, advanced culture is said to raise workers' quality and digital skills, and the digitalisation of culture is said to raise the whole economy.

Zhu calls for firm cultural confidence, for building a strong socialist cultural nation, and for balancing material and spiritual civilisation. Zhu also urges using core socialist values to build consensus, promoting entrepreneurial spirit, and cultivating new quality productive forces. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated commentary links culture to high-quality development.
quoteEn: Advanced culture can not only stimulate workers' enthusiasm and initiative but also raise their level of knowledge and capacity for innovation.
quoteZh: 先进文化不仅能激发劳动者的积极性、主动性，而且能提升其知识水平和创新能力。

glossary.explanation: Official formula for combining Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities (the first integration) and with its fine traditional culture (the second). Xi Jinping stressed the second integration in 2023.
A concept Xi Jinping put forward in 2023. It refers to advanced productivity driven by technological breakthroughs, emerging industries and higher-quality labour.
Official goal of a shift from fast growth to growth that is efficient, innovative, balanced and sustainable. It has been the central economic line since 2017.

t: Carry forward the Yan'an style of work and cultivate a good Party conduct
zh: 弘扬延安作风 培塑优良党风
paras: This short commentary, published in the Party journal Dangjian in June 2025, asks how the Party's wartime Yan'an style of work can serve present-day Party conduct. Zhao and Zhang argue that the Yan'an style, the outward expression of the Yan'an spirit, offers nourishment and strength for the current study and education campaign on the central Party's eight-point regulation, and that good conduct will in turn support Chinese modernization and national rejuvenation.

The authors open with Xi Jinping's remark that the Yan'an style defeated the 'Xi'an style', and recall that in the Yan'an period the Party stressed discipline education and fostered ties between theory and practice, close links with the masses, and criticism and self-criticism. The body is organised under four headings: firm ideological foundations, a deep commitment to the people, strict discipline, and a spirit of hard struggle.

Each section pairs historical examples with a task for today. Mao Zedong's plain meal for Chen Jiageng, Zhou Enlai learning to spin during the production campaign, the 1944 speech 'Serve the People', Yan'an-era disciplinary regulations and the corruption case of Xiao Yubi, and the labour models of the production campaign all serve this purpose. The authors treat these as models for officials: to hold their position on matters of principle, to stay clean, to keep close to the people, to respect discipline and to oppose formalism and bureaucracy.

The authors conclude that Party members and cadres should turn the Yan'an style into personal conviction and practical action, so that Party conduct draws together popular support and shapes social customs. Their stated aim is concrete results in serving the people and promoting development. Read the original if you want a compact example of how current Party-building writing draws on Yan'an history to support the eight-point regulation campaign.
quoteEn: The Yan'an style of work is the outward expression of the Yan'an spirit, and a concentrated embodiment of the revolutionary spirit and fine traditions the Party formed during the Yan'an period.
quoteZh: 延安作风是延安精神的外在表现，是党在延安时期形成的革命精神和优良传统的集中体现。

glossary.explanation: The working style attributed to the Party in its wartime base at Yan'an (1935–1948): frugality, closeness to the masses, discipline and practical effort. It is invoked in current Party-building discourse as a model.
A set of rules adopted by the Central Committee in December 2012 to curb extravagance, formalism and bureaucracy among officials. Study and education campaigns on it were launched in 2025.
The official term for the Party's path of modernization under its leadership, presented as distinct from Western models.

t: Leadership of the Communist Party of China as the fundamental feature of China's new type of party system
zh: 中国共产党领导是中国新型政党制度的根本特征
paras: Taking its cue from Xi Jinping's remarks to non-Party figures at the Spring Festival gathering on 20 January 2025, Zuo Peng argues that leadership of the Communist Party of China is the fundamental feature of China's new type of party system. The system of multi-party cooperation and political consultation under Party leadership is presented as a political creation that grew from Chinese soil. Zuo sees it as the product of integrating Marxist party theory with China's realities and with its fine traditional culture, and as the conclusion of comparison with Western party politics.

The article is organised around three claims about what Party leadership secures. First, it ensures the system represents the fundamental interests of the broadest people in a genuine, broad and lasting way. Second, it unites the parties and non-Party figures around shared goals. Third, it enables institutionalised, standardised and procedural arrangements that gather opinions and make decisions more scientific and democratic. Zuo traces the system's history from the united front of the revolutionary period through the founding of the People's Republic, the reform era and the period since the 18th Party Congress (2012).

On representation, Zuo argues that the Party has no special interests apart from those of the nation and people, and that it integrates the specific interests of the groups the democratic parties connect with into the people's fundamental interests. Zuo describes the system as uniting governing and participating, leadership and cooperation, consultation and oversight. In this account it avoids the defects of one-party rule without supervision and of multi-party rotation with vicious competition. On decision-making, Zuo says Party leadership has built party consultation, democratic oversight and participation in the discussion of state affairs into standard procedures, so that the democratic parties are consulted before and during policy implementation.

Zuo concludes that upholding and improving the system bears on the Party's long-term governance and the country's lasting stability. The article describes the system as having historical inevitability, great creativity, superiority and vitality. It also holds that the system embodies the essence of fine traditional culture and the requirements of the socialist system, and that it contributes to modernizing national governance and to human political civilization. Read the original if you want a concise statement of the official Party-line case for the primacy of Party leadership within China's multi-party cooperation system.
quoteEn: Apart from the interests of the nation, the Chinese people and the people, the Communist Party of China has no special interests of its own, and has never represented any interest group, powerful clique or privileged stratum.
quoteZh: 中国共产党除了国家、民族、人民的利益，没有任何自己的特殊利益，从来不代表任何利益集团、任何权势团体、任何特权阶层的利益

glossary.explanation: The official description of China's system of multi-party cooperation and political consultation under the leadership of the Communist Party, in which the eight democratic parties act as participating parties rather than opposition. It has been promoted as distinct from both Western multi-party competition and one-party rule.
The eight non-Communist parties legally recognised in China, most founded before 1949. They accept Party leadership and take part in consultation and in the discussion of state affairs.
A formal channel through which the Communist Party consults the democratic parties and non-Party figures on major policies before decisions are made.
The Party's long-standing strategy of building broad alliances with non-Party groups and individuals to pursue its political goals.

t: Nurturing university students in the new era with the Chinese Communist Party's spirit of struggle: value dimensions and cultivation paths
zh: 以中国共产党奋斗精神涵养新时代大学生的价值向度与培育路径
source: School Party Building and Ideological Education (学校党建与思想教育), 2025 no. 8
paras: Zhao Yimo and Gong Weijia ask how the Chinese Communist Party's spirit of struggle can be built into the ideological and political education of university students. They treat this spirit as a core part of the Party's spiritual lineage and as a driving force of historical development. Their thesis is that integrating it into university education helps train a new generation able to carry the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, and supports both social progress and the all-round development of the individual.

The article has three parts. The first sets out the theoretical content of the spirit of struggle along three dimensions. The second identifies three value orientations for students. The third proposes cultivation paths across five areas of education: moral, intellectual, physical, aesthetic and labour. The authors draw on Marx, Mao Zedong's On Contradiction and episodes from revolution, construction and reform.

The authors read the spirit of struggle through three lines. Practical rationality means seeking truth from facts, grounded in the Marxist view of labour and the cycle of practice, knowledge and renewed practice. Dialectical thinking means turning contradictions and pressure into momentum, with targeted poverty alleviation as their example. Innovation means keeping to fundamental principles while innovating. For students, they argue, this spirit consolidates historical understanding and guards against historical nihilism. It also calibrates values by reconnecting the individual with the collective, a task they say capital logic has made harder. And it strengthens political identification through cognition, emotion and practice. For education, they propose concrete steps. History and current cases would serve moral education. Course-embedded problem chains would serve intellectual education, such as the 'two bombs, one satellite' spirit in artificial intelligence courses and the Xiaogang village contract in entrepreneurship teaching. Red-themed fitness training would serve physical education. Revolutionary aesthetic resources would serve art education. Model workers such as Wang Jinxi and Jiao Yulu, plus service and production work, would serve labour education.

The authors conclude that weaving the spirit of struggle through all five strands of education offers value guidance and practical routes for training socialist builders and successors. The article is largely conceptual and prescriptive, with illustrative examples rather than empirical evaluation of outcomes. Read the original if you want an example of how Party-spirit themes are translated into course design and teaching activities in Chinese higher education.
quoteEn: The Chinese Communist Party's spirit of struggle is a political character tempered through more than a century of practical exploration in revolution, construction and reform.
quoteZh: 中国共产党的奋斗精神是在百余年革命、建设和改革的实践探索中淬炼形成的政治品格

glossary.zh: 中国共产党的奋斗精神
glossary.literal: the Chinese Communist Party's spirit of struggle
glossary.explanation: A component of the Party's 'spiritual lineage' (党的精神谱系), a canon of named spirits such as the Long March spirit. It stresses perseverance, hard work and pursuit of national goals.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The official national goal, associated with the Chinese Dream and emphasised under Xi Jinping. It refers to restoring China's strength and international standing.

The article uses the problem-chain design as a way to embed ideological and political content in ordinary subject courses. This is part of the wider 'curriculum ideology and politics' policy, which integrates political education into all disciplines.
In official Chinese usage, a term for views that question or negate the Party's historical narrative, especially of the revolution and socialist construction.
An official phrase for young people of the new era expected to shoulder national rejuvenation. Here it is rendered as a new generation able to carry that goal.

t: On the innovative spirit of Chinese modernization
zh: 论中国式现代化创新精神
paras: This article, published in Ideological and Theoretical Education (2025, no. 8), asks what the innovative spirit generated by Chinese modernization is, why it matters and how it can be fostered. Sun Tingting argues that Chinese modernization has produced an innovative spirit of 'daring to climb the heights and be the first', which is also a major spiritual driving force for advancing Chinese modernization itself and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

The article is organised in three parts. The first sets out the spirit's value for the present era. The second analyses its inner meaning. The third proposes ways of cultivating it. Sun draws throughout on Xi Jinping's statements, on the history of the People's Republic from the Mao period through reform and opening up to the new era, and on US think-tank reports and statistics on China's research capacity.

Sun gives three reasons for the spirit's present value: it is needed to speed up scientific and technological innovation and the development of new quality productive forces; it is needed for building a strong country, since the article presents national competition as ultimately competition in innovative spirit and capacity; and it is needed to break what Sun calls the 'extreme pressure' of US and Western technology containment. Sun contends that such pressure strengthens China's drive for self-reliance. The spirit itself has four aspects: pioneering, independent, collaborative and sustained innovation. Sun contrasts the sustained innovation of Chinese modernization, supported by Party-led strategic planning and institutional innovation, with Western modernization. Western modernization is described as capital-led, short-termist because of party rotation, and prone to Schumpeter's 'creative destruction'.

For cultivation, Sun calls for nurturing innovative young people through innovation education, and for creating a social atmosphere that respects innovation and tolerates failure. Sun also calls for long-term mechanisms covering demand orientation, innovation leadership, competition and policy support, and for stronger collaboration among government, enterprises, universities and research institutes. Sun presents the new-type whole-nation system as the framework for this collaboration. Read the original if you want a Party-school-style account of how innovation is framed as a spiritual resource of Chinese modernization and of the policy measures attached to it.
quoteEn: Competition between countries is competition in comprehensive national strength, which is competition in core competitiveness, and core competitiveness is, in the final analysis, competition in innovative spirit and innovative capacity.
quoteZh: 国家之间的竞争是综合国力的竞争，综合国力的竞争是核心竞争力的竞争，核心竞争力的竞争归根到底是创新精神和创新能力的竞争。

glossary.explanation: The official concept of China's path to modernization under Communist Party leadership, promoted since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as sharing features common to all modernization while having distinctive Chinese characteristics.
A concept introduced by Xi Jinping in 2023 for advanced productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs, innovation and upgraded industries.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's central national goal, often dated to the 18th Party Congress (2012) and the Chinese Dream, of restoring China to a leading global position by mid-century.
A model of mobilising state, enterprise and research resources nationwide for major strategic goals, especially key technologies, adapted to a socialist market economy.

t: The value of building a discourse system for ideological and political education across university, secondary and primary schools
zh: 大中小学思政教育话语体系建设的价值意蕴
paras: This short commentary, published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in October 2025, asks why a discourse system for integrated ideological and political education across universities, secondary schools and primary schools is worth building. Long and Liu argue that, with the institutional framework for integration largely in place, discourse building has deep value in three respects.

The authors start from the 20th Party Congress (2022) call to promote integrated ideological and political education across all school levels, usually pursued through integrated ideological and political theory courses. They note progress on textbooks, practice bases, teaching staff, steering committees and policy documents, while acknowledging problems still to be solved.

First, Long and Liu say, discourse building is a matter of theory: practice of integration has run ahead of its knowledge system, so experience must be raised into systematic, autonomous knowledge. Second, they link it to the Chinese discourse and narrative system called for by the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024). They describe international discourse power as a contest between Chinese and Western ideologies, in which Western discourse is dominant, and call for guarding mainstream ideological security. Third, they present it as a basis for the strong ideological and political guidance that Xi Jinping places first among the traits of a leading education power.

The authors conclude that the discourse must explain integration requirements, evaluation standards and students' mechanisms of reception, and must absorb the Party's latest theoretical innovations. They call for drawing on Marxist theory and traditional Chinese culture, innovating in both content and form, and telling the story of Chinese ideological and political education to the world. Read the original if you want a brief statement of how official Chinese education discourse justifies discourse building in this field.
quoteEn: The primary issue in discourse building is in fact the issue of theory building.
quoteZh: 话语建设的首要问题其实就是理论建设问题

glossary.explanation: A policy aim of coordinating moral, political and ideological education across primary, secondary and university stages, mainly through ideological and political theory courses (思政课).

glossary.zh: 中国话语和中国叙事体系
glossary.pinyin: Zhōngguó huàyǔ hé Zhōngguó xùshì tǐxì
glossary.literal: China discourse and China narrative system
glossary.explanation: A goal in Xi Jinping's thinking on culture of building Chinese concepts and storytelling to improve China's international communication.
A national goal of building a world-leading education system, with strong ideological and political guidance listed first among its defining traits.

t: Methodological self-awareness in advancing the systematisation and academic grounding of the Party's innovative theory in the new era
zh: 新时代推进党的创新理论体系化学理化研究的方法论自觉
source: Ideological and Theoretical Education (Sixiang lilun jiaoyu), 2025 no. 8
paras: Duan Yan takes up Xi Jinping's statement that advancing the systematisation (tixihua) and academic grounding (xueli hua) of theory is an inherent requirement and important route of theoretical innovation. The article asks why this work matters for the Party's innovative theory since the 18th Party Congress (2012) and what methodology should govern it. Duan argues that the research should be guided consciously by the Two Integrations and the "Six Musts" of the 20th Party Congress report (2022), and carried out across three systems: disciplines, scholarship and discourse.

The article has three parts. The first sets out the significance of the work, the second the methodological principles to follow, and the third the practical paths. Duan defines systematisation as turning concepts, principles and methods into a coherent, layered organic whole, and academic grounding as revealing the determinate content of theory through induction, deduction, analysis and abstraction. The two are described as mutually reinforcing.

On significance, Duan argues that the work helps build China's autonomous knowledge system and strengthens the standing of Chinese philosophy and social science. In this account, Western countries now exercise hegemony through knowledge production, with Western modernization theory as the main example. The work also converts political and academic discourse into popular and external discourse, raising the theory's appeal and international reach. On method, the Two Integrations are said to guide the study of original and signature concepts such as Chinese modernization, the new-type party system and the Party's self-reform institutions, which are derived from practice and tested against it. The Six Musts (putting the people first, self-confidence and self-reliance, upholding fundamental principles while breaking new ground, a problem-oriented approach, a systems approach, and a worldwide perspective) are treated as a layered whole that shapes how the theory is built.

For practice, Duan calls for coordinated disciplines, with interdisciplinary study of new quality productive forces as an example. Duan also proposes links between textbooks and ideological and political courses, training for the "five armies" of theoretical talent, academic platforms and think tanks, and a discourse system that connects political, academic and popular language at home and uses targeted narratives abroad to counter what the article calls Western discourse traps. The article concludes that the whole Party should consciously adopt this methodology so that the theory is rooted in China and recognised worldwide. Read the original if you want a Party-theory view of how Chinese scholars are directed to organise research on Xi Jinping Thought and the construction of an autonomous knowledge system.
quoteEn: Advancing research on the systematisation and academic grounding of the Party's innovative theory is, in the end, about forming a scientific theoretical system that can explain reality and guide practice.
quoteZh: 推进党的创新理论体系化学理化研究，归根到底是要形成能够解释现实、引领实践的科学理论体系。

glossary.explanation: The formula of combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities (the first) and with its fine traditional culture (the second, added in 2021–23). It is presented as the core method of adapting Marxism in China.

Six principles in the 20th Party Congress report (2022): put the people first, self-confidence and self-reliance, uphold fundamental principles while breaking new ground, a problem-oriented approach, a systems approach, and a worldwide perspective. They are described as the worldview and methodology of Xi Jinping Thought.
The official name for China's path to modernization under Party leadership, presented as distinct from the Western model. It was formally elaborated at the 20th Party Congress (2022).
A concept put forward by Xi Jinping in 2023 for productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs and innovation, as a basis for high-quality development.
The official idea that the Party can keep itself pure and vigorous through its own rigorous self-governance and discipline.

t: The historical evolution and reflective construction of Chinese cultural subjectivity
zh: 中华文化主体性的历史嬗变与省思建构
source: Ideological and Theoretical Education (思想理论教育), 2025 no. 8
paras: How did Chinese culture lose, and then regain, its cultural subjectivity? Chen Hongjuan treats cultural subjectivity as a culture's capacity to absorb and integrate the "other" and to innovate consciously, and as the basis of cultural confidence. The article argues that this subjectivity was strong before the Opium War, collapsed in modern times, and was rebuilt, consolidated and then raised up under the leadership of the Communist Party of China.

The article is organised chronologically in three parts. It first covers the display and loss of subjectivity, from the ancient "all under heaven" order to the post-1840 crisis. It then examines the Party's rebuilding of subjectivity in the New Democratic Revolution, socialist revolution and construction, and reform and opening up. The third part addresses the new era since the 18th Party Congress (2012).

Chen's core argument rests on three tasks that the Party is said to have handled dialectically in each period. The first is to identify the "subject" of cultural innovation: the Party rejected both wholesale Westernization and restorationist cultural conservatism, sifting the "essence" of tradition from its "dross". The second is to assimilate foreign culture on the principle of "China as the main body, foreign things serving China". The third is to create new culture by combining Marxism with Chinese culture. For the new era, Chen adds that cultural subjectivity has moved from defence to assertion. The author describes the Two Integrations as ending older confusions over Marxism and tradition and turning an implicit method into a conscious one. Chen also holds that Chinese culture can offer "Chinese wisdom" for problems of Western modernity, and contrasts this with a declining Western-centrism.

Chen concludes that Chinese cultural subjectivity is not nostalgia for tradition. In the author's account it is a living cultural organism, shaped by adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times and confirmed through Chinese modernization. Clarifying this history, the author suggests, offers a guide for strengthening cultural subjectivity further. Read the original if you want a periodised Party-historical account of how official discourse links cultural subjectivity, the Two Integrations and Chinese modernization, with many citations of Party leaders and Republican-era debates.
quoteEn: Chinese cultural subjectivity is not simple nostalgia for traditional Chinese culture, but refers to a living cultural organism of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times.
quoteZh: 中华文化主体性并非是对中华传统文化的简单怀旧，而是指涉马克思主义中国化时代化的文化生命体

glossary.explanation: Formula in Xi Jinping-era Party theory: integrating the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities (the first) and with China's fine traditional culture (the second).
The official name for China's path of modernization, presented as distinct from Western models and rooted in Chinese conditions and civilization.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for the Party's ongoing project of fitting Marxism to China's conditions and to the present era.

A concept Xi Jinping stressed in 2023: a culture's capacity to act as an autonomous agent, absorbing outside influences and innovating from its own base. The article treats it as the foundation of cultural confidence.
The traditional Chinese worldview of a culturally centred order in which the civilised centre transforms peripheral peoples through moral and ritual education.

t: Virtual simulation experiments empowering ideological and political theory courses: an innovative exploration
zh: 虚拟仿真实验赋能思政课教学的创新探索
source: Ideological and Theoretical Education (Sixiang lilun jiaoyu), 2025 no. 8
paras: Zhang Yu and Wang Qingqing ask how virtual simulation experiments (VR-based teaching) can be built into university ideological and political theory courses so that they raise the courses' relevance and appeal. They note that current use is mostly for demonstration, for extracurricular activities and by a minority of teachers, which leaves it superficial and formalistic. Their answer, drawn from the Tsinghua University course "Ideological and Moral Cultivation and the Rule of Law", is that the technology works only when it is embedded in the classroom as a regular part of teaching, under the teacher's guidance.

The article has four parts. It first sets out why such experiments are needed: the digital age, the generational traits of students described as "digital natives", and the "big ideological and political course" initiative. It then describes the Tsinghua teaching model. Next it identifies the regularities by which the experiments work, namely knowledge transmission, emotional cultivation and value guidance. Finally it proposes innovation paths. The case material is VR experiences built around the lives of Deng Jiaxian and Nan Rendong.

The core of the argument is a small-class blended model. About 15 students, in five groups, choose one of six themes, such as life values, ideals and convictions, or the spirit of scientists. Each session moves from a teacher's lecture to an immersive VR experience, then group discussion, presentations, peer review and a teacher's summary. The authors insist that technology must not weaken the teacher's leading role, and they cite classroom questionnaires in which most students said the method improved engagement and sense of gain. They argue that VR supplies intuitive, multimodal knowledge, that immersion creates the emotional identification on which value formation rests, and that discussion of real-world issues turns experience into reflection and action. Values guidance is presented as the ultimate aim.

The authors propose three paths. The first is a new teaching model that unites teacher leadership with student agency. The second is to integrate the experiments into the "big ideological and political course" framework as low-cost practical education, with suitable themes and carefully designed processes. The third is to build platforms and shared resources across universities and school levels, to research teaching methods, and to strengthen teachers' ability to educate online. Read the original if you want a detailed, practice-based account of how a Chinese university integrates VR into Party-led ideological education, including its course design and the officially stated rationale.
quoteEn: Carrying out virtual simulation experiment teaching in ideological and political courses is not meant to weaken the teacher's leading role, but to raise teachers' capacity to lead by broadening teaching vehicles, enriching content and innovating teaching scenarios, thereby improving teacher–student interaction and exchange of ideas.
quoteZh: 开展思政课虚拟仿真实验教学，不是要削弱教师的主导作用，而是要通过拓展教学载体、丰富教学内容、创新教学场景来提升教师的主导能力，进一步提升师生教学互动和思想交流的效果。

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses in Marxism, Party theory, morality and law taught at all Chinese schools and universities to shape students' political outlook and values.
A concept promoted by Xi Jinping in 2021 that extends ideological and political education beyond the classroom into society and practice, drawing on social resources.

t: Consolidating and developing the subjectivity of Chinese culture and the principles it requires
zh: 中华文化主体性的巩固发展及其原则遵循
source: Ideological and Theoretical Education (思想理论教育), 2025 no. 8
paras: Xu Guomin and Shi Yutong take up the question of how the subjectivity of Chinese culture (中华文化主体性) can be consolidated and developed. They start from Xi Jinping's 2023 remark that cultural confidence comes from cultural subjectivity. The authors argue that many scholars treat subjectivity as a static essence and remain trapped in oppositional thinking. In their view it is a dynamic "cultural complex" formed through the practice of national rejuvenation, and its philosophical basis is the theory of integration and of comprehensive innovation.

The article has three parts. The first traces the century-long dispute over "ancient and modern, China and the West", from Wei Yuan, the Self-Strengthening Movement's "Chinese learning as substance, Western learning for application" and the Reformers Kang Youwei and Yan Fu, through Sun Yat-sen and the New Culture Movement, to Li Zehou's "Western substance, Chinese application". It then reviews Zhang Dainian's "comprehensive innovation" and Fang Keli's "Marxism as soul, Chinese learning as substance, Western learning for application". The second part follows how the Party consolidated cultural subjectivity in four periods. The third derives guiding principles.

The authors contend that Chinese cultural subjectivity has a Marxist "soul vein" and a traditional-culture "root vein", and that it is a product of the Two Integrations. They say this complex unifies dialectical and analytical thinking, collectivism and individualism, and "one guiding principle" with "diverse development". In their account, Marxism's guiding position is the fundamental principle. They hold that the creative transformation of fine traditional culture, above all through the second integration, is the most basic one. They add that absorbing the rational elements of Western culture, after rejecting Western-centrism, is an important third principle.

The article concludes that handling the relations among Marxism, fine traditional Chinese culture and Western culture, and so building a pattern of "one dominant, many diverse", lies at the core of consolidating cultural subjectivity. All of this, the authors say, must serve Chinese modernization and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. They also hold that comprehensive-innovation theory still leaves the relative status of the three components unclear. Read the original if you want a Party-theory account of how debates on Chinese versus Western learning are recast around Marxism and the Two Integrations.
quoteEn: In fact, the subjectivity of Chinese culture has both a Marxist "soul vein" and a "root vein" of fine traditional Chinese culture, and is the cultural crystallisation of continually advancing the Two Integrations.
quoteZh: 事实上，中华文化主体性既有马克思主义“魂脉”，也有中华优秀传统文化“根脉”，是不断推进“两个结合”的文化结晶

glossary.explanation: A concept Xi Jinping formally put forward in 2023, meaning that Chinese culture must have its own distinct identity and agency. It is presented as the basis of cultural confidence.

The formula of integrating Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture. The "second integration" is the link with traditional culture, stressed since 2021–23.
The authors' term for the composite formed by Marxism, fine traditional Chinese culture and absorbed Western elements. They present it as dynamic and evolving.
The official name for China's path to modernity, said to differ from Western models. It is a central slogan since the 20th Party Congress (2022).

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A long-term national goal in official discourse, associated with Xi Jinping's "Chinese Dream", of restoring China's strength and standing.

t: On the comparative research method in ideological and political education
zh: 论思想政治教育比较研究方法
source: Ideological and Theoretical Education (思想理论教育), 2025 no. 8
paras: Comparative research has been part of the discipline of ideological and political education since the 1980s. Gao and Tang ask what the comparative method is, why it is justified and how it should be used. Their thesis is that, as the discipline builds an autonomous knowledge system, the method must be clarified and made more scientific. In their account it rests on Marxist premises and must be anchored in China's own standpoint and needs.

The article has three parts. The first gives a theoretical account of the method and its value. The second builds a typology of methods. The third sets out principles for applying it. The authors survey five existing ways of classifying comparative methods, such as by social-science levels, by descriptive, analytical and explanatory comparison, or by research steps. They then propose their own scheme, organised by research purpose.

Gao and Tang describe the method as a fusion of qualitative and quantitative work, combining synchronic and diachronic comparison. It holds a necessary tension between objectivity and subjectivity. They ground it in the dialectic of the universal and the particular, in Marx's theory of world history and in Marx's idea of the "other", which they read as critical borrowing measured by China's own yardstick. Their four types are comparison-description, comparison-attribution, comparison-prediction and comparison-mutual construction, and these can be combined. Three principles follow. First, Marxist views of comparison require that like be compared with like, that all the relevant facts be grasped and that the underlying essence be revealed. Second, comparison should proceed from Chinese standpoint and needs, strengthening the Four-sphere Confidence, solving practical problems and offering "Chinese wisdom" and "Chinese solutions". Third, it should serve the autonomous knowledge system through greater methodological rigour, a clearer logical architecture and more self-conscious innovation.

The authors conclude that the comparative method has long borrowed tools from other disciplines, and these carry the "other's" ways of seeing. They call for methods that express the discipline's own nature and for a consistent "I"-centred perspective when judging forms of ideological and political education elsewhere. Read the original if you study the methodology of ideological and political education in China, or want to see how Chinese scholars link Marxist theory, national standpoint and the building of an autonomous knowledge system in discussing comparative research.
quoteEn: Ideological and political education in different times and places should be understood and assessed from the perspective of "the self", so that the discipline's defining character and its research standpoint remain consistent throughout.
quoteZh: 以“我”之视角认识鉴别不同时空下的思想政治教育，使学科规定性和研究立场一以贯之。

glossary.explanation: A Chinese academic discipline and educational practice concerned with shaping the ideas, political outlook and values of students and citizens in line with the dominant ideology. It is taught in universities and schools and studied as a Marxist-theory subfield.
A slogan in Chinese social-science policy, calling for concepts, theories and methods developed on China's own basis rather than imported from the West.
Official formula for confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics.

t: Innovating the scenario methods of ideological and political education in the era of large models
zh: 大模型时代思想政治教育场景方法创新
paras: Zhao Jianchao and Wen Yanfei ask how large AI models are changing the "scenes" (changjing) in which ideological and political education is carried out, and what methods should follow. They define an educational scenario as the deep fusion of a "field" (the web of connections mediated by educational technology) and a "scene" (the values conveyed through it). Their thesis is that large models bring a "scenario revolution": the field becomes interconnected, cross-boundary and co-created, and the educational scene becomes more personalised, integrated and emergent.

Published in Ideological and Theoretical Education (2025, no. 8), the article follows a three-step line of inquiry: scenario narrative, scenario analysis and scenario evolution. Narrative is examined through four dimensions: subject, time, space and ideology. Analysis is examined through four techniques: data mining, network analysis, modelling and simulation, and computational experiments. Evolution is examined through four system properties: self-adaptation, self-organisation, self-replication and self-creation.

On narrative, the authors argue that large models move subject narrative from informational to node-based forms, time narrative from real-time to user-defined, and space narrative from mass communication to "pan-audience" communication centred on each individual and to social integration. In ideological narrative, they say the models supply fuller content that meets learners' need for mainstream ideology, and use "filtering" and "selection" strategies to prompt recognition, so that concrete individuals become identified subjects of the mainstream ideological field. On analysis, they claim models can automatically extract the meaning of scenarios, assess their value, build digital twins and run parallel virtual and real experiments that complement each other. On evolution, they hold that models activate the scenario's capacity to adapt, self-organise, replicate through "genetic information" and create, ending in whole-system emergence.

The authors conclude that innovating scenario methods through this narrative–analysis–evolution logic can raise the efficiency, benefit and effect of scenario-based education, and that intelligent transformation opens a new path for the field. The argument is conceptual and framework-building, with no empirical case studies and no discussion of risks. Read the original if you study how Chinese scholars of ideological and political education conceptualise AI, digital scenarios and ideological recognition, and want the detailed taxonomy of methods.
quoteEn: An ideological and political education scenario is in essence the deep fusion of a "field" and a "scene" mediated by educational technology, a way of educating people in which the "field" of connections carries the "scene" of value transmission.
quoteZh: 思想政治教育场景本质上是教育技术中介下“场”与“景”的深度融合，是以连接关系之“场”承载价值传播之“景”的育人方式。

glossary.explanation: A field and practice in Chinese education and Party work that aims to cultivate political convictions, values and morality, and is an academic discipline in its own right within Marxist theory studies.
Here a technical concept borrowed from media and internet studies, combining a relational 'field' (场) with a 'scene' (景). The authors treat it as the basic unit through which education is delivered.
A term for personalised communication that is centred on each individual yet reaches everyone, presented as the step beyond mass and niche-audience communication.

t: Synchronous advancement of ideological and political course construction and arming minds with the Party's innovative theory: its integrative meaning and practical path
zh: 坚持思政课建设与党的创新理论武装同步推进的一体化意蕴及其实践进路
source: Ideological and Theoretical Education (思想理论教育), 2025 no. 8
paras: In May 2024 Xi Jinping instructed that the construction of ideological and political courses in schools should proceed in step with arming minds with the Party's innovative theory. Luo Hongjie takes up this instruction, abbreviated as 'synchronous advancement', and asks what logic lies behind it, what problems it addresses and what goal it serves. The article argues that the formula is best read through the lens of 'integration' (yitihua), meaning orderly connection across space and effective sequencing across time, and that this reading clarifies both its theoretical basis and its practice.

The article is built in three parts. The first sets out the integrative meaning of the formula along three aspects: course construction, theoretical arming, and the combination of the two, including coordination across primary, secondary and tertiary schooling. The second offers a theoretical account drawing on Marx, Lenin and Engels, and on the notions of 'ideological reality' and 'theoretical reality'. The third proposes a practical path and ends with three relationships to be handled.

Luo's core argument has two moves. First, drawing on Marx's remark that theory becomes a material force once it grips the masses, Lenin's theory of 'inculcation' from outside, and the gap between students' 'ideological reality' (their actual thinking) and the 'theoretical reality' of an evolving theory, Luo contends that synchronisation must be continuous and integrated. Second, the practical path follows a 'point–plane–body' sequence. The 'point' identifies problems: fragmented and passive theoretical arming, partial and delayed integration of theory into teaching, and low enthusiasm for theoretical interpretation, with teachers and Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era as key subject and content. The 'plane' calls for horizontal integration through textbooks, teaching methods and content. The 'body' calls for vertical sequencing across school stages through coordinated actors, graded content and institutional mechanisms.

Luo concludes that synchronisation should keep students' ideological reality, theoretical reality and practical reality consistent. The author proposes that time and space, leading and receiving subjects, and the three 'realities' be handled as paired relationships. Luo also distinguishes this formula from integration of ideological education across school stages: the former concerns bringing the Party's theory into every stage's courses, the latter concerns repetition and gaps between stages. Read the original if you study Chinese ideological and political education and want a detailed Chinese-language account of how the 2024 instruction is being theorised and operationalised.
quoteEn: Synchronous advancement aims to make the 'lightning of thought' strike the spiritual home of young students thoroughly and precisely, so that they become people who possess truth and strength.
quoteZh: “同步推进”就是为了将“思想的闪电”彻底、精准地击中青少年学生的精神家园，让其成为拥有真理且有力量的人。

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses in Marxism and Party theory taught at all school levels in China. They are officially regarded as the main channel of ideological education.

glossary.en: arming minds with the Party's innovative theory
glossary.literal: theoretical arming with the Party's innovative theory
glossary.explanation: The Party's practice of systematically educating cadres, teachers and students in its latest theoretical achievements, currently centred on Xi Jinping Thought.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.
Shorthand for Xi Jinping's 2024 instruction to advance ideological and political course construction in step with arming minds with the Party's innovative theory.
A term in Chinese ideological education for people's actual state of thought, attitudes and values, which educators are expected to understand and shape.

t: Grasping the "six dimensions" to advance new development of socialist culture
zh: 把握好“六个维度”推进社会主义文化新发展
paras: This newspaper commentary sets out how Xi Jinping Thought on Culture can guide the further development of socialist culture. Wang Hai describes it as the cultural chapter of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, enriching Marxist cultural theory. Wang argues that explaining it well supports propaganda and ideological work, continuity of Chinese civilisation, a strong socialist cultural nation and cultural confidence.

The piece is organised around six dimensions: Party leadership of cultural work, the Second Integration, cultural confidence and traditional culture, culture for the people, the goal of a cultural nation, and cultural communication abroad.

On leadership, Wang holds that culture reflects politics and economics and has a clear ideological character, so its direction requires the Party's comprehensive leadership. The longest section treats the Second Integration, the combination of Marxism with excellent traditional Chinese culture. Wang says it frees thought from cultural blind imitation of the West and rests on five points: the two sides are compatible, they enrich each other, they firm up the path's foundations, they open space for innovation and they consolidate cultural subjectivity. The remaining sections call for protecting heritage, producing high-quality cultural products for the people, raising citizens' moral standards and soft power, and telling China's story well internationally.

Wang concludes that culture is a driver of economic development, a tool of governance and a spiritual force for the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Through communication, the author says, the world will see China as committed to peaceful development. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how Party-aligned scholars present the main themes of Xi Jinping Thought on Culture.
quoteEn: The result of "integration" is mutual fulfilment.
quoteZh: “结合”的结果是互相成就。

glossary.explanation: The body of Xi Jinping's statements on culture, presented officially as the cultural part of his broader thought, and formally articulated at a national work conference in 2023.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology since 2017, written into the Party and state constitutions.

The formula of combining the basic principles of Marxism with China's excellent traditional culture, stressed by Xi Jinping in 2023 as a complement to the First Integration with China's concrete realities.
An official concept stressing confidence in China's traditional, revolutionary and socialist culture, one of the Four-sphere Confidence.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's central national goal, referring to restoring China's strength and international standing by the mid-twenty-first century.

t: Marx's view of labour justice and its bearing on labour happiness
st: With a discussion of the basic content of labour-concept education in universities in the new era
zh: 马克思劳动正义观及其对劳动幸福的现实观照——兼论新时代高校劳动观教育的基本内容
paras: He and Lai start from Marx's claim that labour is the species-essence of human beings and ask whether the proposition of 'labour happiness' can stand, given how often labour makes workers unhappy. They answer that it holds as a normative ('ought') judgement, and that the labour which produces happiness must be just labour. On this basis they argue that Marx's theory of labour justice explains what labour happiness is and what conditions it requires, and that it fixes the content of labour education in universities.

The article has three main sections and a closing discussion. The first presents labour justice as the ground of labour happiness. The second treats justice of the labour subject and of the labour object (means of production) as the fundamental precondition. The third treats just motives and the protection of labour rights as basic conditions. The closing section turns to labour-concept education in universities since the 18th Party Congress (2012), citing Xi Jinping's 2018 call for an education system combining moral, intellectual, physical, aesthetic and labour education, and the 2020 central guidelines on labour education.

The authors define just labour as labour whose usefulness exceeds its harmfulness, so that people share in happiness. They draw on Marx to argue that the labour subject must be capable and must do labour as a duty, within physical and mental limits set by age and sex. For the object, they hold that ownership of the means of production must be just, citing Marx's idea of re-establishing individual ownership on the basis of common possession. In their reading, public ownership addresses the defects of large-scale private ownership, though the authors say China's uneven development still requires unwaveringly encouraging the non-public sector. They also distinguish slave labour, labour for a living, decent labour and free associated labour, and contend that capitalist profit motives and wage labour undermine happiness for workers and for society as a whole.

The authors propose that university labour education rest on Marx's view of labour as making the person, aim at labour happiness, and make labour-justice education its core task. They set out five strands: labour as moral formation, labour happiness, labour duty and the labour subject, labour process, and labour rights. These include rejecting consumerism and 'lying flat', and respecting labour models and the craftsman spirit. They also include learning to comply with labour law. Read the original if you want a Marxist ethical reading of labour, happiness and ownership linked directly to current Chinese ideological education policy.
quoteEn: Just labour that realises labour happiness is labour whose usefulness exceeds its harmfulness, so that people share in happiness.
quoteZh: 实现劳动幸福的正义劳动就是劳动的有用性大于有害性，从而使人们共享幸福的劳动。

glossary.explanation: A concept developed by the authors from Marx's view of labour as human species-essence. It denotes the deep satisfaction people gain when labour confirms their essence.
The article uses the phrase 'unwaveringly encourage, support and guide' the non-public sector. It echoes the official Two Unwaverings formula on the public and non-public sectors.

glossary.pinyin: dé zhì tǐ měi láo wǔ yù bìngjǔ
glossary.en: moral, intellectual, physical, aesthetic and labour education
glossary.literal: five educations pursued together: moral, intellectual, physical, aesthetic, labour
glossary.explanation: An education policy line stated by Xi Jinping at the 2018 National Education Conference. It adds labour education to the four earlier components of Chinese schooling.
A colloquial term for deliberately minimising work and ambition. The authors cite it as an attitude that university labour education should counter.

t: Giving full play to culture's role in nurturing aspirations and cultivating sentiments
zh: 充分发挥文化养心志、育情操重要作用
paras: This short commentary, published in the People's Daily on 23 October 2025, takes up Xi Jinping's call at a Political Bureau study session to use culture to nurture aspirations (xin zhi) and cultivate sentiments (qing cao). Lian Ziqiang argues that the strength of a culturally strong socialist country shows above all in people's ideological outlook, spirit and cultural refinement. Promoting cultural education is presented as both an internal requirement of building a culturally strong country and a practical need for steadiness amid what the author calls a century of great change.

The piece first defines the two functions, then gives historical examples, then turns to the sources of cultural resources and to practical measures. It draws on Party history from the revolutionary and socialist construction periods to the present era.

Lian contends that healthy culture internalises values as cultural and value identification, binds people through shared symbols, rituals and beliefs, and fosters social cohesion and a positive social ethos. The author cites slogans from successive periods as examples of how culture has inspired people. The sources named are advanced socialist culture, revolutionary culture and fine traditional Chinese culture, guided by core socialist values. On the supply side, Lian says the main cultural contradiction has shifted from "whether there is" to "whether it is good", which calls for better public cultural services and products, a large and well-structured pool of cultural talent, and the use of artificial intelligence, big data and virtual reality for precise, immersive delivery.

The author concludes that culture-building must start and end with people, and that stronger cultural influence will give spiritual support to Chinese modernization and national rejuvenation. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official commentary links cultural policy, core socialist values and new technology to moral and ideological education.
quoteEn: People are both the enjoyers and the creators of culture, and the number and quality of talent bear directly on the degree of development and depth of influence of socialist culture with Chinese characteristics.
quoteZh: 人是文化的享有者，也是文化的创造者，人才的数量与质量直接关系中国特色社会主义文化的发展程度和影响深度。

glossary.explanation: The official name for the Party's model of national development, promoted since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western paths of modernization.

A set of twenty-four characters in twelve values, formally promoted since the 18th Party Congress (2012), at national, social and individual levels. It is used as the guiding framework for cultural and moral education.

glossary.literal: great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The official goal of restoring China's national strength and international standing, central to Party discourse since the 2010s.

t: Making good use of the "Big Ideological and Political Course" to strengthen the leading force of ideological and political education
zh: 善用“大思政课” 增强思政引领力
paras: Wu Qiantao's commentary, first published in Guangming Daily on 9 October 2025, takes up the idea of "leading force of ideological and political education" (sizheng yinlingli), a phrase Xi Jinping introduced at the National Education Conference in September 2024. Wu argues that a key way to strengthen this force is to make good use of the "Big Ideological and Political Course" (da sizheng ke), a approach to teaching ideology and politics that goes beyond the classroom.

Wu first defines "sizheng" as shorthand for the worldview, outlook on life and values a society or party promotes. In his account, it covers ideological and political education, ideological and political work, socialist ideological education and the ideological and political courses themselves. The article then sets out three "bigs": a big sense of responsibility, a big content system and a big space for extension. Each is tied to one function: giving direction, supplying driving force, and building an education pattern involving all personnel, the whole process and every dimension.

On responsibility, Wu holds that the course serves the fundamental task of fostering virtue through education and cultivating "new-era people" loyal to the Party. He calls for Party leadership over its construction, better top-level design and a place for it as the highest form of school ideological work. On content, he stresses three strands: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, traditional, revolutionary and advanced socialist culture, and the histories of the Party, the PRC, reform and opening up, socialism and the Chinese nation. Wu says these turn theory into a teaching system and a system of belief.

On extension, Wu proposes practice bases and "walking" courses in rural revitalization and grassroots governance, AI, big data and VR for teaching, and new-media matrices. He also proposes cross-department coordination, "curriculum ideology and politics" across all subjects, and integrated courses from primary school to university and between family, school and society. He concludes that this would make the leading force a systemic effect that builds the socialist direction of a strong education nation. Read the original if you want a concise statement of the official framework for ideological and political education under Xi Jinping's "education powerhouse" agenda.
quoteEn: The leading force of ideological and political education is not a simple force released by a single actor in a single link; it is a systemic joint force formed by many actors inside and outside schools, across moral education, cultural and knowledge education, social practice and other links.
quoteZh: 思政引领力作为一种“力”，不是在单一环节中、由单一主体释放的简单力量，而是涉及思想道德教育、文化知识教育、社会实践等各环节，由校内校外等多元主体形成的系统合力。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted since 2021 under Xi Jinping that extends ideological and political teaching beyond the classroom into social practice, online spaces and the wider society.

glossary.en: leading force of ideological and political education
glossary.explanation: A term Xi Jinping used at the National Education Conference in September 2024. It refers to the capacity of ideological and political education to steer the direction, development and talent training of education.
An official formulation of the fundamental task of education in China: cultivating moral character alongside knowledge and skills.
A policy of embedding ideological and political content in all subjects, not only in dedicated ideological and political courses.
A national goal of building China into a leading country in education, set out in official plans and stressed at the 2024 National Education Conference.

t: Providing institutional support for building a strong cultural nation
zh: 为文化强国建设提供制度支撑
paras: Wang Zengfu, writing in Guangming Daily in October 2025, asks how institution-building can support the drive to turn China from a large cultural country into a strong cultural nation. Taking up the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) principle of making institution-building the main thread of deepening reform, Wang argues that cultural institutions regulate cultural order, guide cultural governance and coordinate the elements of cultural development. Strengthening the cultural system of socialism with Chinese characteristics is presented as both a guarantee of cultural soft power and a necessary choice for national rejuvenation.

The article is organised in four parts, each pairing a goal with a set of institutional measures. These are: using the strengths of the cultural system to strengthen ideological leadership; stimulating institutional vitality; improving the cultural system to raise governance capacity; and consolidating institutional safeguards to widen the paths to cultural prosperity. It is a policy-oriented commentary that draws mainly on Xi Jinping's statements and Party documents rather than on empirical cases.

Wang's central claim is that Party leadership and Marxism's guiding position are the foundation of the cultural system. In Wang's account, public ownership, the people's democratic dictatorship and the Party's governing status determine Marxism's guiding role in ideology. The practical agenda that follows includes a public cultural service system that moves from "having" to "excellent", and top-level design guided by Xi Jinping Thought on Culture. It also covers reform that keeps social benefits first while managing the dual ideological and market character of cultural products. Wang then lists specific systems: heritage protection with scientific and technological support, comprehensive online governance including protection of minors, cultural security against what the author calls hostile Western ideological infiltration, and an international communication system with new concepts and expressions.

Wang concludes that cultural legislation, market supervision and technological support must be strengthened so that China can keep its cultural subjectivity amid global cultural competition. Proposals include multi-level cultural law and judicial protection of intellectual property, restructuring state-owned cultural enterprises, a fair and unified cultural market, and secure management of cultural data.
