Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated scholars frame cultural institution-building, ideological security and international communication in the context of building a cultural powerhouse.
quoteEn: Cultural security is an important component of national security.
quoteZh: 文化安全是国家安全的重要组成部分。

glossary.explanation: A Party goal, set out in 2035 targets, of raising China's cultural influence, public cultural services and cultural industries to a leading level.
A body of ideas on cultural work attributed to Xi Jinping and formally articulated in 2023, used as the guide for cultural policy.
The idea that a country's cultural identity, values and ideology are part of national security and must be protected from outside influence.
In cultural policy, the principle that the social and ideological effects of cultural products take priority over economic returns.

t: Building on our own strengths: teaching the "Great Ideological and Political Course" well in information-technology universities
zh: 立足自身优势，上好信息科技特色高校“大思政课”
paras: Xu Mei, Party secretary of Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications, asks how universities that specialise in information technology can use their own traditions and disciplinary strengths to run the "Great Ideological and Political Course" well. Writing in Guangming Daily in October 2025, Xu argues that such universities should turn their distinctive profile into an advantage in moral education, in line with the fundamental task of fostering virtue through education.

The commentary has three parts. It first sets out the value of the course for these universities, then names four relationships to be handled, and finally proposes practical paths. These are organised around four "big" elements: classroom, platform, teaching staff and overall framework.

Xu's core claim is that disciplinary and technological resources should be fused with value guidance rather than used on their own. The four relationships are disciplinary distinctiveness and the laws of education, instrumental rationality and value rationality, multiple actors and university leadership, and on-campus and off-campus resources. Xu warns against the idea that technology is all-powerful and insists that university Party committees steer the work. The practical measures include using the university's revolutionary history in teaching and ceremonies, and building AI-based student development platforms, citing Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications' "You AI" platform. Others are dual mentors from the university and industry, and a closed loop in which industry sets problems, students and teachers solve them and firms evaluate the results.

Xu concludes that this approach would produce talent who combine technical skill with patriotism and a sense of mission for the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, and who contribute to Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want a concrete example of how a Party-led technical university describes the integration of AI and industry partnerships into ideological and political education.
quoteEn: The use of information technology should always revolve around the fundamental task of fostering virtue through education: its positive role in expanding the boundaries of education should be fully used, and above all technology application must be organically united with value guidance.
quoteZh: 信息技术的运用应当始终围绕“立德树人”的根本任务，既要充分发挥其在拓展教育边界方面的积极作用，更要确保技术应用与价值引领的有机统一。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping that extends ideological and political education beyond the classroom by linking it to social reality and practice. It involves schools, society, and online and offline resources.
Official term for the fundamental task of education in China: moral and ideological formation of students alongside knowledge and skills.
The official Party formulation of China's path of development, prominent since the 20th Party Congress (2022).

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's central national goal, associated with the Chinese Dream, of restoring China's strength and international standing.

keywords: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

t: The significance and pathways of raising the effectiveness of the global communication of Chinese culture
zh: 提升中华文化全球传播效能的意义和路径
paras: This commentary, published in Guangming Daily on 14 October 2025, asks why the global communication of Chinese culture needs to become more effective and how that can be done. Zeng Xiangmin and two co-authors take as their starting point the 20th Party Congress report (2022) and the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), which call for stronger international communication capacity. They argue that raising communication effectiveness is both strategically necessary and practically feasible, and that it requires coordinated work on four fronts.

The piece has two parts. The first sets out the significance of the task, and the second proposes four practical routes: drawing on cultural resources, innovating the discourse system, training versatile communication talent and building a plural set of communicators, and creating self-controlled platforms and new carriers of communication. Each route is broken into short sub-measures.

On significance, the authors say that competition in cultural soft power has become a key dimension of overall national strength. They hold that ideas such as harmony in diversity and "all under heaven is for the public" match global demands for peace, development and cooperation. They also point to three conditions: the depth of Chinese civilisation, state support for international communication, and new technologies such as artificial intelligence and immersive media. On method, they urge strengthening cultural confidence and cultural subjectivity, distilling spiritual symbols, and presenting both historical and contemporary China. They also call for shifting from "display and promotion" to "interaction and participation", combining grand and micro narratives, and diversifying language, channels and settings. Communication should be a "chorus" of official bodies, think tanks, cultural enterprises, young people and overseas Chinese rather than a "solo".

The authors conclude that, in the international opinion arena, "platform is channel, and channel is influence". They call for digital cultural products, everyday objects that carry cultural elements, and multilingual, algorithm-supported communication matrices that match the needs of different audiences. They also want universities to build interdisciplinary programmes in language, culture, journalism and digital technology. Read the original if you want a concise statement of the official policy framework for the international communication of Chinese culture, as set out in a Party newspaper in late 2025.
quoteEn: Cultural communication is not a "solo" by a single actor but should be a "chorus" of many actors.
quoteZh: 文化传播不是单一主体的“独奏”，而应是多元主体的“合唱”。

glossary.explanation: The capacity of a country to gain influence through culture and values rather than coercion. Chinese official texts treat it as a component of comprehensive national strength.
A term in recent Party discourse for the idea that Chinese culture should keep its own independent standpoint and character in dealings with other cultures.
Confidence in the value and vitality of Chinese culture, promoted in official discourse since the 2010s as part of the Four-sphere Confidence.

t: Strengthening the idea of using culture to engage in dialogue with the world
zh: 强化用文化同世界对话的理念
paras: This Guangming Daily commentary takes up Xi Jinping's call, in his article on accelerating the building of a cultural powerhouse, to use culture in dialogue with the world. Lian presents the call as a strategic arrangement for raising China's cultural soft power and the influence of Chinese culture amid what the article calls changes unseen in a century. The thesis is that such dialogue must rest on the subjectivity of Chinese culture and on more effective cross-cultural communication.

The piece first defines dialogue as interaction between subjects aimed at reducing differences and building mutual understanding. It then develops two requirements: holding to the subjectivity of Chinese culture, and improving the effectiveness of cross-cultural communication. It closes with a short statement of the vision behind both.

On the first requirement, Lian argues that the subjectivity of Chinese culture was built under Communist Party leadership through the combination of Marxism with China's realities and its fine traditional culture. Holding to it is said to guard against self-doubt and external steering, and against both uncritical worship of foreign culture and conservatism, closed-mindedness, and national and historical nihilism. The guiding formula is to put one's own culture first while drawing on others. On the second, Lian urges softer communication in place of indoctrination, shared themes and emotions, use of digital media, tailoring to each country, and long-term strategic patience. The aim is for audiences abroad to understand and love Chinese culture, not merely see or hear it.

Lian concludes that dialogue means mutual learning on the basis of cultural self-reliance. The envisioned result is a plural, harmonious world culture, and Chinese culture's lasting development within a community with a shared future for mankind. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official discourse links cultural subjectivity, international communication and the cultural powerhouse goal.
quoteEn: To use culture in dialogue with the world, we must hold to the subjectivity of Chinese culture and strengthen cultural confidence.
quoteZh: 用文化同世界对话，必须坚守中华文化主体性，坚定文化自信。

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy and theoretical concept promoted by Xi Jinping since the early 2010s. It envisions countries sharing interests and responsibilities in global governance.
A concept stressed in official discourse since 2023. It refers to Chinese culture's distinctive core and independent character, which the Party presents as the basis for absorbing foreign influences.
An official goal of building China into a country with strong cultural influence and soft power, set for 2035 in Party documents.

t: Seizing the key links to make ideological and political work in universities more targeted
zh: 抓住关键环节，提高学校思政工作针对性
paras: Following the Central Committee's recent issuing of the Regulations on Ideological and Political Work of the Communist Party of China, this Guangming Daily commentary asks how universities can make their ideological and political work more targeted and effective. Yin Zhaohua argues that universities, charged with training builders and successors of socialism, should concentrate on four key links: Party leadership, a student-centred approach, the main teaching and support forces, and campus culture.
The piece is a short, practical outline written by a university Party official. It moves through four headed sections, each setting out measures for university Party organizations and staff.

On leadership, Yin holds that Party committees must exercise overall leadership and bear primary responsibility for running the university, while grassroots branches serve as fortresses and Party members as vanguards. Universities should arm teachers and students with Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era and strengthen the role of Marxism schools. On students, Yin says the key is to understand them, especially the post-2000 generation, and calls for heuristic and experiential teaching rather than cramming, history education, new-media platforms and help with practical difficulties. Yin also names three key forces: full-time teachers, student counsellors, and administrative and support staff, who should integrate education into daily work.

On culture, Yin urges each university to build a distinctive brand drawing on its history, disciplines and regional setting, and to run cultural projects, practice activities and volunteer service. The aim is to strengthen students' sense of belonging and social responsibility, and to make ideological and political work more approachable. Read the original if you want a concise example of how a university Party official translates the new Party regulations into campus-level practice.
quoteEn: Students' status as the main body must be fully respected, their inner drive for self-education stimulated, and platforms and conditions created to guide them from being 'the educated' to being 'self-educators'.
quoteZh: 要充分尊重学生主体地位，激发其自我教育的内生动力，搭建平台、创造条件，引导学生从“被教育者”转变为“自我教育者”。

glossary.explanation: The Party's work of shaping the beliefs, values and political outlook of its members and the public. In universities it covers political theory courses, counsellors and campus culture.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The official guiding ideology of the Communist Party of China, written into the Party constitution in 2017.

keywords: Regulations on Ideological and Political Work

t: Making red culture a "living source" that nourishes students' minds
zh: 让红色文化成为滋养心灵的“源头活水”
paras: This commentary, published in Guangming Daily on 21 October 2025, asks how universities can make red culture a lasting source of moral and ideological nourishment for students. Dong argues that red cultural resources, including the "great spirit of resistance against Japanese aggression", should be built into ideological and political education. In Dong's view this is both a way of passing on red genes and a means of carrying out the fundamental task of fostering virtue through education.

The piece has two parts. The first, "from 'moment-based inspiration' to 'routine education'", deals with teaching in classrooms and practice. The second, "from active exploration to conscious practice", deals with campus culture and student initiative.

Dong says university red-culture education is too often tied to particular anniversaries and lacks continuity and system. The author proposes extending it into everyday life through the main classroom, the "second classroom", AI and virtual-simulation tools for "cloud visits" to revolutionary sites, and "dual-qualified" teaching teams that include red-culture experts and site guides. Practice should be linked to values through research-study bases, "ideological and political classes on the move", and student-chosen projects such as short videos, historical dramas and oral-history interviews. Students should then move from passive reception to self-directed practice, through exhibitions, performances, reading activities, student-made creative work, and campus symbols such as display windows and sculptures.

Dong concludes that red culture should move from "moment-based inspiration" to "routine education" and then to "gene-like transmission". The author expects this to strengthen students' cultural confidence and sense of national purpose, and to turn them toward science and technology work that serves national strategic needs. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Chinese university practice and policy language frame red-culture education.
quoteEn: Universities should use red culture to firm up young people's ideals and convictions, moving red culture from "moment-based inspiration" to "routine education" and then to "gene-like transmission".
quoteZh: 高校要用红色文化筑牢广大青年理想信念，推动红色文化从“节点化感动”到“常态化育人”，再到“基因化传承”。

glossary.explanation: The heritage of the Chinese revolution under the Communist Party, including sites, documents and the spirit associated with them. It is used in patriotic and ideological education.
An official formulation of education's fundamental task: cultivating moral character alongside knowledge. It is widely used in Chinese education policy.
Extracurricular activities such as social practice, volunteering and campus events. They are meant to complement formal classroom teaching (the first classroom).
A metaphor for the revolutionary ideals, spirit and traditions that the Party says must be inherited across generations.
A concept in official discourse stressing confidence in China's own cultural tradition, revolutionary culture and socialist culture.

t: Bringing ideological and political elements to life in stage performance
st: The gala "Justice Will Prevail" as a model for the "Great Ideological and Political Course"
zh: 让思政元素在文艺演出中“活起来”
paras: This commentary takes the gala "Justice Will Prevail", staged for the 80th anniversary of victory in the War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression and the World Anti-Fascist War, as a case for ideological and political education. Ren and Wu argue that the show gave concrete form to the "Great Ideological and Political Course" and offers a living sample for reforming such education in the new era.
The piece has two parts. The first explains how the performance builds historical confidence among Chinese youth. The second proposes turning a one-off show into a lasting educational mechanism.

In the first part, the authors say the music and staging build collective memory across generations, present red classics in contemporary form to strengthen cultural confidence, and make clear the responsibility of young people in the new era. In the second part they propose three pairings. History and present-day experience would be joined in "immersive" classrooms, for example at revolutionary sites. Professional guidance would be combined with mass participation, including crowdsourced topics and modular creation. Emotional resonance would be combined with value guidance and assessed through a "whole-chain" evaluation covering process, outcomes and participation.

The authors conclude that such performances can move from a single artistic display to a long-term project of moral education and cultivating people through culture. Read the original if you want to see how Chinese educators frame mass cultural events as vehicles for patriotic and ideological education.
quoteEn: This ideological and political lesson, which moves from "entering the ear" to "entering the heart", must ultimately come down to forming value identification and turning it into action.
quoteZh: 文艺演出这堂由“入耳”到“入心”的思政课，最终必须落脚于价值认同的形成与行为转化的实现。

glossary.explanation: A policy concept promoted in recent years that extends ideological and political education beyond the classroom into society, practice and cultural life.
The stated fundamental task of education in China: cultivating morally grounded citizens who support the socialist cause.

t: Advancing military course development and raising university students' national defence literacy
zh: 推进军事课建设 提升大学生国防素养
paras: This short commentary, published in Guangming Daily on 28 September 2025, takes up the reform of the compulsory military course (junshi ke) in Chinese universities. Li Ke argues that the course is the main channel of national defence education for students and a key means of implementing the 2022 opinions on strengthening national defence education and the revised 2024 National Defence Education Law. The article contends that the course should combine political, ideological, contemporary and innovative qualities.

The piece sets out eight directions for reform: content, ideological security, teaching staff, core military elements, frontier developments, new technology, a combined first- and second-classroom system, and assessment. It is a practical programme addressed to university teachers and administrators rather than a theoretical study.

Li's core proposals are that Party, army and revolutionary history be built into chapters such as national defence and war, and that teaching strengthen students' political awareness and their commitment to national security, including political, institutional and ideological security under the holistic view of national security. Li also calls for joint teaching by serving soldiers, military experts and civilian staff, and for study of Xi Jinping's thought on strengthening the military, the Art of War and On War. The author wants teaching to address emerging security domains such as the deep sea, space and polar regions, and to use AI, big data, virtual simulation, war-gaming and VR battlefield training.

Li proposes making national defence literacy the central goal, moving students through knowing, feeling, intending and acting, supported by field study, volunteer work, competitions and commemorations. Assessment should combine summative and process evaluation, with defence practice reports, reading reflections and a "national defence literacy growth file". Read the original if you want a concise sample of how a university military instructor presents the official agenda for defence education and its proposed teaching methods.
quoteEn: The cultivation of university students' national defence literacy should be made the core goal of the military course.
quoteZh: 应将大学生国防素养培养作为军事课的核心目标

glossary.explanation: A framework introduced by Xi Jinping in 2014 that treats security as covering political, military, economic, cultural, technological and other domains together.

glossary.en: Xi Jinping's thought on strengthening the military
glossary.literal: Xi Jinping thought on a strong military
glossary.explanation: The part of Xi Jinping's thinking dealing with Party leadership of the armed forces and military modernisation, summarised in official texts by "eleven clarifications" and "five adherences".
The knowledge, attitudes and skills regarding national defence that official education policy aims to cultivate in citizens.
A compulsory course on military theory and training for Chinese university students, the main vehicle of national defence education in higher education.

t: Upholding fundamental principles and innovating to improve the quality and effectiveness of ideological and political education
zh: 守正创新提升思政教育质效
paras: This commentary, published in the People's Daily on 25 September 2025, asks how ideological and political education can reach young students more effectively and make the Party's innovative theory take root in their minds and hearts. Ge Jihong, head of a cultural creativity institute at Zhejiang University of Media and Communications, argues that the answer lies in upholding fundamental principles while innovating. The article begins from Xi Jinping's instructions on school ideological and political courses and the fundamental task of fostering virtue through education.

Ge acknowledges that the overall environment for these courses has improved and that students' Four-sphere Confidence has grown. The author nonetheless lists persisting problems: spoon-fed instruction, dry language and empty content that ignores current concerns, and teaching geared to exams rather than to value identification. The body has three sections, on strengthening political guidance, on making the courses more targeted and appealing, and on combining theory with practice. Each draws on Zhejiang examples, mainly short videos on Xi's Zhijiang Xinyu and a portrait project for martyrs.

Ge's core claim is that political guidance is the basic function of the courses, and that this does not mean simple propaganda. Theoretical rigour and political orientation must go together, and ideals should rest on rational acceptance of scientific theory. The author calls for a shift from one-way instruction to two-way interaction and from the closed classroom to society. Examples include students making short videos in the "short, fast, new, lively" style, students using their professional skills to portray martyrs, and young people lecturing peers in their own idiom. Ge also proposes a closed loop of "what is needed, taught, understood and used", with "walking" courses that move from "book-based reasoning" to "narratives of the land". A 2022 programme bringing Hong Kong students to Zhejiang is cited as moving participants from knowing to believing.

Ge concludes that joining theory and practice returns ideological and political education to its essence and implements the fundamental task of fostering virtue through education. In this view, a "society as classroom" approach lets students move from cognitive agreement to putting belief into practice. The goal is a new generation that the Party can rely on to take up national rejuvenation. Read the original if you want a representative example of how official commentary describes current methods of ideological and political education in universities, with concrete Zhejiang cases.
quoteEn: Only by taking deep root in the land of China and resonating with the times can ideological and political education steadily strengthen its ideological and theoretical character, its affinity and its relevance, and achieve connotative development.
quoteZh: 思政教育只有深深扎根中国大地，与时代同频共振，才能不断增强思想性、理论性和亲和力、针对性，实现内涵式发展

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses in Chinese schools and universities that teach Marxism, Party theory and national values. The Party treats them as a key vehicle for moral and political education.
A slogan defining the fundamental task of Chinese education as moral cultivation alongside learning. It has been stressed in Party documents since the 18th Party Congress (2012).
Confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics. The formulation is associated with Xi Jinping's leadership.

glossary.literal: great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The official goal of restoring China's strength and international standing by the mid-twenty-first century. It is a central theme in Party discourse.
A collection of short commentaries written by Xi Jinping while Party secretary of Zhejiang (2002–2007). The article treats it as an important source for studying his thought.

t: Feelings for family and country: a distinctive spiritual hallmark of Chinese civilization
zh: 家国情怀：中华文明的鲜明精神标识
paras: Chen Yanbin and Zhang Jinqiu take up the question of where Chinese 'family-and-country feelings' (jiaguo qinghuai) come from and why they persist. The article, a newspaper essay in Guangming Daily, defines them as a deep emotional bond that ties individual and family fate to the destiny of the nation. The authors argue that this bond is a distinctive spiritual hallmark and cultural gene of Chinese civilization, formed over several thousand years.

The essay is organised in five parts. It traces the sentiment to the agrarian roots of Chinese civilization, then to the 'family–state isomorphism' of the traditional social order, and then to the transmission of family traditions. It goes on to examine how the idea worked in moments of national crisis, from Yue Fei and Wen Tianxiang to Lin Zexu, the anti-Japanese war and the nuclear-submarine engineer Huang Xuhua. It ends with the contemporary value of the idea.

The authors' central move is a chain of explanation. Attachment to the land, which they contrast with nomadic and maritime civilizations, was lifted into family-and-country feeling through a social order in which family and state were built on the same pattern. They point to the Western Zhou feudal-patriarchal system, the Qin-Han unification and the Confucian sequence from self-cultivation to 'bringing peace to all under heaven'. Family traditions and family instructions, such as Yan Zhitui's Family Instructions for the Yan Clan, then carried these values across generations. In crises, the authors say, filial duty was converted into loyalty to the nation. They present this as the reason Chinese civilization is the only one to have continued unbroken in the form of a state.

The authors conclude that family-and-country feeling remains a source of spiritual strength for the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. They call for it to be passed on, especially to young people, so that individuals tie their fate to the nation's, in a period of what they call changes unseen in a century. They also propose drawing on the traditional experience of family instruction to build good family traditions, which they say would support clean Party conduct, honest government and sound social customs. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official-academic writing presents family culture and patriotism as a continuous civilizational inheritance.)
quoteEn: Family-and-country symbiosis is a distinctive value of Chinese civilization. Built on the historical base of 'family–state isomorphism', it lifts the filial duty of kinship ethics into the duty to serve the nation in political ethics, and finally unites the values of individual and collective.
quoteZh: 家国共生是中华文明鲜明的价值观念，它以“家国同构”为历史基底，将血缘伦理中的孝亲义务升华为政治伦理中的报国担当，最终实现个体与集体的价值同构。

glossary.explanation: A sentiment that links personal and family fate to the fate of the nation. Chinese official discourse presents it as a core trait of traditional Chinese culture.

glossary.literal: family and state sharing one structure
glossary.explanation: The idea that traditional Chinese state and family were organised on the same hierarchical, kinship-based pattern. The ruler stands to subjects as a father to his household.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central official goal of the Communist Party, referring to restoring China's national strength and international standing.

t: Using the Party's innovative theory to transform the subjective and objective worlds
zh: 用党的创新理论改造主观世界和客观世界
paras: Writing in the People's Daily (24 September 2025), Zang Anmin takes up the question of how Party members should put the Party's innovative theory to work. The author's answer is that Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era should be treated as a weapon for changing both the objective world and one's own subjective world. Zang presents this as a long-standing Party tradition and as a requirement for advancing Chinese modernization.

The piece has two main parts. The first sets out six principles for studying, grasping and applying the theory: putting the people first, self-confidence and self-reliance, upholding fundamental principles while breaking new ground, a problem-oriented approach, systems thinking, and a global outlook. The second part turns to Party members and especially leading cadres, and sets out practical requirements for political ability, discipline, competence and work style. It draws on Marx, Engels, Mao Zedong's On Practice, Xi's speeches and examples from Party history and Chinese tradition.

Zang's central move is to treat transformation of the subjective and objective worlds as one unified process. Citing Marx's Theses on Feuerbach, the author holds that the proletariat changes itself while changing circumstances. Cadres are therefore urged to raise their political judgement, comprehension and execution, and to remain loyal to the Party in line with the Two Establishes and the Two Upholds. They are also urged to follow the Party Constitution, think in terms of the whole country, and build the "eight skills" and "seven abilities". Work style is summarised as being both clean and bold in action. Cadres are to avoid corruption, dare to act within Party discipline, act promptly and do investigative research. They are also asked to hold a correct view of performance, citing Zhejiang's "Eight-Eight Strategy" and the Saihanba afforestation effort as examples.

Zang concludes that the two kinds of transformation reinforce each other, and that only by grasping this can one understand the dialectical unity of the Party's self-reform and social revolution. The Party is to keep reshaping its members' ideals and Party spirit while changing the objective world, so that the whole Party keeps unified thinking, firm will and coordinated action. Read the original if you want a representative example of how official Party commentary links theoretical study, cadre conduct and the goals of Chinese modernization.
quoteEn: Using the Party's innovative theory to transform the subjective world and the objective world is always an inherently unified process.
quoteZh: 用党的创新理论改造主观世界和客观世界始终是内在统一的

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018. It is presented as the latest stage of adapting Marxism to China.
The official name for China's path to modernization, promoted since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.
A formula adopted in 2022 that affirms Xi Jinping's position as the core of the Party Central Committee and of the whole Party, and the guiding role of Xi's thought.
The Party requirement to uphold Xi Jinping's core position and the authority and centralised leadership of the Central Committee.
The Party's term for its newly developed theory, in this article chiefly Xi Jinping Thought. It is presented as Marxism adapted to China's conditions.

t: Carrying forward the great spirit of resistance against Japanese aggression: from great victory to great rejuvenation
zh: 传承和弘扬伟大抗战精神 从伟大胜利走向伟大复兴
paras: Published in the People's Daily after Xi Jinping's speech of 3 September 2025 marking the 80th anniversary of victory in the War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression and the World Anti-Fascist War, this commentary sets out how the Party should read that war's spirit. Wang Qiang argues that without grasping how the great spirit of resistance grew, and why victory was won, the war's meaning cannot become a lasting source of strength. The author's thesis is that this spirit should be carried forward to advance national strength and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

The article has four sections. The first traces the origins of the resistance spirit. The second describes the force it released in the war itself. The third assesses its lasting significance, for the Party, for China and for the wider world. The fourth lists four ways to carry it forward today. Wang draws throughout on Xi's speech and other statements, and briefly cites Engels on the lessons of history.

In Wang's account, the spirit has three roots: the long-standing spirit of the Chinese nation, the modern history of national struggle against aggression, and the Communist Party's sense of mission. The Party, the author says, rallied a divided people while other political forces wavered or capitulated. Wang presents the war as three kinds of battle. It was a turning point for the nation, a forging of the Party, and a life-and-death test in which the people's army relied on people's war. The spirit is then said to have enriched the Party's spiritual lineage, to have underpinned the nation's path from 'standing up' to 'becoming strong', and to have encouraged oppressed peoples. Wang adds that the Global South is now changing the world's map.

Wang calls for four applications of the spirit. These are unity and struggle toward rejuvenation; confidence and strategic resolve during the 15th Five-Year Plan period, answered with high-quality development; resolute struggle against external pressure and containment; and win-win cooperation against Cold War thinking, hegemonism and protectionism, moving toward a community with a shared future for mankind. Wang treats the spirit as living and not as a thing of the past. Read the original if you want to see how a National Defence University researcher links wartime memory to current Party themes in the official press.
quoteEn: The great spirit of resistance is not something in the past tense, but in the present continuous.
quoteZh: 伟大抗战精神不是“过去式”，而是“进行时”。

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal, promoted especially under Xi Jinping. It means restoring China's strength and international standing after the 'century of humiliation'.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's formula for international relations based on cooperation and shared interests. It is presented as an alternative to bloc politics and hegemony.
A term for developing countries, used in Chinese official discourse to refer to a growing collective voice in world affairs.
An official economic goal, adopted by the Party in 2017. It stresses quality, innovation and sustainability over speed of growth.

glossary.zh: 中国共产党人的精神谱系
glossary.literal: the spiritual genealogy of Chinese Communists
glossary.explanation: An official series of named 'spirits' (such as the Jinggangshan, Long March and Yan'an spirits) traced back to the 'founding spirit' of the Party. Xi Jinping highlighted it in 2021.

t: Vigorously promoting the educator spirit distinctive to China
zh: 大力弘扬中国特有的教育家精神
paras: Published in China Social Sciences Today in September 2025, this commentary takes up how the "educator spirit distinctive to China" can move from an inspiring ideal to conscious action among teachers. Mei opens with Xi Jinping's reply to representatives of the Special-Post Teachers programme, who work in rural schools, and treats these teachers as a living example of that spirit. The author argues that promotion needs a systematic mechanism built on research, cultural inheritance, dissemination and practice.

The article is organised around four headings: systematic research and interpretation as the foundation, highlighting the distinctive features of Chinese civilization as the core, a comprehensive communication system as the safeguard, and improved paths of practice as the key. Each section lists specific measures. They range from research frameworks and digital databases to selecting model teachers, media campaigns, teacher training and evaluation reform.

Mei argues that the educator spirit continues the Party's teacher-building line since the 18th Party Congress (2012), which the author calls both a creative transformation of Marxist educational theory and an innovative development of traditional Chinese educational wisdom. The author calls for research across history, theory and reality, and for comparison with Western educational theories in order to break the habit of "interpreting China through the West" and build an autonomous Chinese pedagogical discourse. The spirit is traced to figures such as Confucius, Wang Yangming and Cai Yuanpei, and presented as a source of cultural confidence and a link for exchange between civilizations. On practice, Mei proposes a three-part path of training, evaluation and coordination. This includes a growth ladder from special-post teacher to backbone teacher to educator-type teacher, and a shift from quantitative metrics to a developmental evaluation system.

Mei concludes that the educator spirit should become part of teachers' professional makeup and improve educational governance, supporting the building of a leading education nation. The author calls on Party committees and governments to take political responsibility, and on society to give teachers priority and support. Read the original if you want to see how a university Party secretary links teacher-development policy, cultural confidence and Party leadership of education in the official discourse of 2025.
quoteEn: To promote and implement the educator spirit vigorously, research and interpretation must be the foundation, cultural inheritance the vein, promotion and dissemination the axis, and practice the guiding thread.
quoteZh: 大力弘扬落实教育家精神，要以研究阐释为基、以文化传承为脉、以弘扬传播为轴、以践行实践为纲

glossary.explanation: A formulation Xi Jinping put forward in 2023, set out as six attributes, including ideals and convictions, moral integrity, teaching wisdom and a caring heart. It is promoted as a standard for China's teachers.
A national programme, begun about 20 years before 2025, that recruits teachers for rural schools in central and western China.
A concept in Party discourse, associated with the Four-sphere Confidence, which stresses confidence in China's own cultural traditions and socialist culture.
A national goal set out in an official plan for 2024–2035, which aims to make China a global leader in education.

t: Injecting innovative momentum into the dissemination of the Northeast Anti-Japanese United Army spirit
zh: 为东北抗联精神传播注入创新动能
paras: This short commentary in China Social Sciences Today (11 September 2025) asks how new media can strengthen the spread of the spirit of the Northeast Anti-Japanese United Army. Gao Shiying, an associate professor at a university school of Marxism, argues that content innovation, technological empowerment, platform linkage and audience interaction can raise the reach and influence of this spirit today. Gao treats this as a new task for passing on red culture.

The article begins with the Party Central Committee's April 2022 formulation of the spirit: firm conviction of loyalty to the Party, national righteousness in going to the aid of the country, and heroic resolve to fight to the end. It then describes the technical and audience base provided by new media, citing internet penetration of 78% in China by June 2024. It goes on to the new forms and channels this offers, and ends with the mechanisms that Gao says give the spirit lasting vitality.

Gao's central claim is that new media change both presentation and participation. Short video, animation, livestreaming and VR/AR make the history of the fighters vivid, while likes, reposts, comments and re-creation on platforms such as Bilibili and Douyin bring young people closer to revolutionary history. Content production shifts from professional institutions to ordinary users, as in Weibo topics where people share family stories of anti-Japanese forebears. Gao also points to big-data recommendation and AI image restoration as tools for reaching target audiences and for restoring the faces of heroes. Gao cautions that historical authenticity must be kept and that shallow or entertainment-driven content must be avoided.

Gao concludes that the digital, interactive and fragmented features of new media open broad space for innovative dissemination and let the spirit take on new life in the digital age. Read the original if you want a brief example of how Chinese ideological-education writers link red culture and digital communication strategy.
quoteEn: The interactive character of new media has completely changed the traditional one-way model of communication.
quoteZh: 新媒体的互动性特征彻底改变传统单向传播的模式。

glossary.en: the spirit of the Northeast Anti-Japanese United Army
glossary.explanation: A Party-defined body of values drawn from the communist-led anti-Japanese guerrilla forces in Northeast China in the 1930s–40s. Its core content was officially set in April 2022.
Official term for the culture, memory and heritage associated with the Chinese revolution and the Communist Party, used in patriotic and ideological education.

t: How the "Second Integration" resolves the "dispute between ancient and modern, Chinese and Western": its ideological implications
zh: “第二个结合”破解“古今中西之争”的思想蕴涵
source: Ideological and Theoretical Education (思想理论教育), 2025 no. 6
paras: Since the Opium War, Chinese thought has been caught between "tradition" and "modernity" and between the "native" and the "foreign". Yang Zengdong and Dang Jiamei take up Xi Jinping's 2023 claim that China is now better placed than ever to resolve this "dispute between ancient and modern, Chinese and Western". They argue that the Second Integration, the combination of Marxism with fine traditional Chinese culture, supplies the resolution, because it overcomes both the opposition of tradition to modernity and the tension between native and foreign cultures.

The article is organised in three parts. The first addresses the temporal dimension, the "ancient–modern" question, and treats the Second Integration's handling of tradition under four heads. The second addresses the spatial dimension, the "Chinese–Western" question, and the third draws practical implications for civilizational development and for Chinese modernization. The authors draw on Gadamer, Husserl, Habermas, Huntington and Marx's and Engels's remarks on tradition and history.

In the first part, Yang and Dang contend that tradition and modernity are not absolute opposites, since modernity grew out of pre-modern roots and traditions are constantly dissolved and created anew. They say the Second Integration works in three steps: it sifts out negative elements by making "fine" traditional culture, not tradition in general, one party to the integration; it safeguards cultural subjectivity; and it "discovers" tradition through creative transformation and innovative development, with Marxism as the "soul". In the second part, they argue that Chinese intellectuals who either rejected tradition or opposed modernity both fell into Eurocentrism by equating modernization with Westernization. Using the notion of "inter-culturality", they claim that Marxism and Chinese culture share compatible values and that each chooses the other. The Second Integration therefore recognises difference and achieves a "heterogeneous fit" (yigou qihe), so Marxism can no longer be regarded as foreign.

The authors conclude that the dispute has been genuinely resolved. They present this as showing that openness, mutual learning among civilizations and cultural confidence are the way forward. They add that Chinese modernization, rooted in both Marxism and Chinese culture, has the universal character to offer other countries Chinese wisdom and experience, whereas they describe Western modernization as claiming civilizational superiority and prizing material over human development. Read the original if you want to see how a Party-theory scholar draws on Gadamer, Habermas and Huntington to argue that the Second Integration overcomes the "ancient–modern, Chinese–Western" divide.
quoteEn: In moving step by step from dissolving tradition to safeguarding it and then discovering it, the Second Integration repeatedly confirms its transcendence of the opposition between tradition and modernity.
quoteZh: “第二个结合”在消解传统、维护传统和发现传统的层层递进中，反复印证其对于传统和现代对立的超越。

glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's 2023 formulation of the combination of the basic tenets of Marxism with fine traditional Chinese culture, presented as following the 'First Integration' of Marxism with China's concrete realities.
The Party's term for the parts of China's cultural heritage judged worth inheriting, as distinct from traditional culture in general.
Official formula for the approach to traditional culture: transforming it creatively and developing it innovatively to fit contemporary needs.
A concept in recent Party discourse for a nation's self-awareness and self-confidence in its own culture, treated as the basis of cultural identity.
The official term for China's own path of modernization, said to differ from Western models.

keywords: ancient and modern, Chinese and Western

t: The Two Integrations as a "chemical reaction": the meaning of a metaphor
zh: “两个结合”作为“化学反应”的思想喻义
source: Journal of Ideological and Theoretical Education (思想理论教育导刊), 2025 no. 5
paras: Xi Jinping has said that "integration" is not a "platter" or a simple "physical reaction" but a "chemical reaction" that produces a new, organically unified cultural life-form. Wu and Zhang take up the question of what this metaphor means for the Two Integrations (combining Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture). They argue that reading it correctly is the key to the core meaning of the concept, which they call original and emblematic of Xi Jinping's thought on culture.

The article is organised in three parts, each drawing out one implication of the metaphor. The first treats the Two Integrations as life activity, tracing the idea from the historical blending of Confucian, Daoist and Buddhist thought through the founding of the Communist Party to successive stages of Sinicised Marxism. The second treats them as creative innovation that depends on cultural subjectivity. The third holds that the "reaction" must yield something new, and it surveys theories, paths and institutions said to result.

Wu and Zhang's central move is an analogy with biology. Just as chemical reactions drive an organism's metabolism and produce new cells, the Two Integrations drive the "cultural life-form" of the Chinese nation and produce new ideas, theories and culture. From this the authors draw a contrast between creative combination and mechanical juxtaposition. Applying theory to reality by "cutting" or "fitting" it is, in their reading, the dogmatism seen in Wang Ming. The second integration likewise cannot stop at comparing points of agreement between Marxism and tradition. It must reinterpret classical sources in the context of the new era.

The authors then list what they say the reaction has generated: Mao Zedong Thought, the theoretical system of socialism with Chinese characteristics, and Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. They also point to the primary stage of socialism and the coexistence of multiple forms of ownership with public ownership. In their account, the "Chinese characteristics" of socialism come from traditional culture, for example the "great unity" idea, which they say was transformed into democratic centralism. They conclude that grasping the metaphor helps open new horizons for adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times and supports Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want to see how Chinese theorists interpret Xi's metaphor philosophically and use it to define the creative character of the Two Integrations.
quoteEn: "Integration" is not an external adding-together of ready-made ideas and theories or of concrete realities. It is an integration accomplished through innovation and creation.
quoteZh: “结合”并非一个停留在对“现成”思想理论或具体实际的外在相加过程，而是在创新创造中完成的“结合”

glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's formula for combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture. The second integration was added to the older first one in Xi's 2021–2023 statements.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official description of the Party's ongoing project of fitting Marxism to Chinese conditions and to each new era.
The official term for China's own path of modernisation, promoted in Party documents especially since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
A thesis developed by Deng Xiaoping and the Party in the 1980s. It holds that China remains in a long early phase of socialism because its productive forces are underdeveloped.

The capacity of a nation to inherit its own culture, resist foreign cultural dominance and independently create its own ideas and theories. The term features prominently in Xi's 2023 remarks on culture.
The organisational principle of Leninist parties and the Chinese state, combining discussion with binding unified decisions.

t: Studying and implementing General Secretary Xi Jinping's statements on upholding the dominant position of Marxist political economy
zh: 学习贯彻习近平总书记关于坚持马克思主义政治经济学主体地位的论述
source: Studies in Political Economy (政治经济学研究), 2025 no. 1
paras: Wu Qingjun and Gu Zhengyun ask why Western economics came to dominate Chinese economics after reform and opening up, and what should be done about it. They argue that this dominance resulted from uncritically learning Western market-economy theory while building the socialist market economy. In their view it should be corrected, so that Marxist political economy for the new era becomes the mainstream of Chinese economics teaching and research, with useful elements of Western economics absorbed in a subordinate role.

The article first reviews how the standing of Western economics changed from 1979 to the present. It then sets out the harms of Western economics occupying the mainstream, relying heavily on quotations from Xi Jinping and one from Deng Xiaoping. A third section explains why Marxist political economy should hold that place. The last and longest section makes five proposals on scholarship, curriculum, journals, doctoral training and course design.

The authors describe a shift from critical study of Western economics in the early 1980s to wholesale acceptance from the mid-1990s. They cite the predominance of Western economics in course numbers, teaching hours, postgraduate entrance exams and journal articles. Drawing on Xi, they claim that Western mainstream economics ignores social relations and class and cannot explain crises under capitalist private ownership. They also hold that copying it undermines the public-ownership base of the economy. They present hostile foreign forces as using economic theory to promote privatisation, a 'colour revolution' and 'peaceful evolution'. Marxist political economy, they say, offers a scientific and dialectical method and serves the socialist system, so socialist market-economy theory must be built on it.

The authors propose that the Party and government interact constructively with Marxist scholars to build new-era Marxist political economy, which they define as Xi Jinping's economic thought plus innovative work by Marxist economists. They call for total teaching hours in Marxist political economy to slightly exceed those in Western economics. They also want at least half of the articles in a journal's special columns on Xi's economic thought and Marxist political economy, and one-third in general journals and university journals. Further proposals are to prioritise doctoral training in Marxist political economy, as in the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences programme, and to integrate Xi's economic thought into Western economics courses. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese scholar translates this ideological position into concrete institutional proposals for universities and journals.
quoteEn: In the new era, Marxist political economy should be the main body, drawing on and absorbing the useful elements of Western economics to develop Marxist political economy for the new era, and using its theory to study and answer the real problems facing China.
quoteZh: 新时代应以马克思主义政治经济学为主体，借鉴、吸收西方经济学的有益成分来发展新时代马克思主义政治经济学，用新时代马克思主义政治经济学的理论来研究和回答中国面临的现实问题。

glossary.explanation: The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched in China in 1978 under Deng Xiaoping.
The economic system adopted as China's reform goal at the 14th Party Congress (1992), combining market mechanisms with socialist public ownership and Party leadership.
The body of economic ideas attributed to Xi Jinping, which official sources present as the latest development of Marxist political economy in contemporary China.
A term used in Chinese official discourse for externally encouraged popular movements that overthrow governments. It is presented as a threat to the Party's rule.

t: Lenin's late view of culture and its implications for the inheritance and development of culture
zh: 列宁晚年文化观及其对文化传承发展的启示
paras: Wang and Xu ask what Lenin's late writings on culture contribute to socialist cultural construction, and what they offer China today. They argue that Lenin treated culture as a multidimensional category and gave the "cultural revolution" a central place in building socialism. In their view this approach, read alongside Xi Jinping's call for a "cultural mission" and for building a strong socialist culture, supplies a useful reference for China's own cultural work.

The article has three parts. The first sets out Lenin's multidimensional account of culture: its broad and narrow senses, its class character, its economic role, and his critique of Narodism (populism). The second reconstructs the logic of his late cultural thinking in the New Economic Policy period, covering its methods, practical grounding, theoretical depth and overall framework. The third draws lessons for China under three headings: independence and self-reliance, openness and inclusiveness, and upholding fundamental principles while innovating.

The authors argue that Lenin used historical materialism and the idea of society as a living organism to place culture within the whole of socialist construction. They report his claims that illiteracy rules out communism and that cooperatives and industrialisation require a cultural revolution. They also report his warnings that changing peasant habits takes generations and that haste in cultural matters is most harmful. On this reading, Lenin's "two cultures within each national culture" thesis ties culture to class, and he held that the proletariat, through its vanguard party, must lead cultural work.

The authors turn these points into proposals for China. They call for Party leadership of cultural work and for cultural subjectivity, for reform of cultural institutions in the spirit of the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), and for socialist core values. They also propose spreading traditional culture abroad and using AI and digital technology for innovation, with the Two Integrations as the guide to "upholding fundamental principles". Read the original if you want a Chinese academic reading of Lenin's late cultural writings, or an example of how they are linked to current Chinese cultural policy.
quoteEn: In cultural matters, haste and rash advance are the most harmful.
quoteZh: 在文化问题上，急躁冒进是最有害的

glossary.explanation: A formula in Xi Jinping-era Party theory: integrating the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities, and with China's fine traditional culture.
A Party goal of making China a country with strong cultural influence and creativity. The article links it to Xi Jinping's 2023 remarks on the new cultural mission.
Lenin's term, used in the early 1920s, for raising literacy and general cultural level in Soviet Russia as a precondition of socialism. It is not the Chinese Cultural Revolution of 1966–76.
The policy adopted in Soviet Russia from 1921 that allowed limited market exchange and private trade after War Communism.
A twelve-word set of national, social and individual values promoted by the Party since the 18th Party Congress (2012).

t: Reflections on promoting the intensive (connotative) development of ideological and political theory courses
zh: 关于推动思想政治理论课建设内涵式发展的思考
source: Journal of Ideological and Theoretical Education (思想理论教育导刊), 2025 no. 5
paras: Zhang Leisheng and Long Xiaofei ask how the university ideological and political theory courses (sizheng ke) can move from expansion to quality-focused, internally driven development. Taking Xi Jinping's call to promote the courses' development "in a way that upholds fundamental principles and breaks new ground", the authors argue that such development rests on the dialectical unity of adhering to orthodoxy and innovating. They add three supports: a better-integrated curriculum, a well-run "Big Ideological and Political Course", and a stronger teaching force.

The article treats course development as a systemic project and is organised in four parts. It first sets out what adhering to fundamental principles and innovating mean, then turns to the curriculum system, the "Big Ideological and Political Course", and the quality of teachers. It draws on the history of the course schemes since 1949 (the 1952, 1961, 1985, 1998 and 2005 schemes) and on specific textbook and curriculum examples from senior secondary and undergraduate levels.

On the first point, the authors say that adhering to fundamental principles means keeping the courses Marxist in theory, socialist in politics, focused on cultivating people in thought, and rule-bound as courses. Innovation is presented as an attitude, a cultural trait, an accumulated experience and a way of thinking. On the curriculum, they call for integration across six stages from primary school to doctorate, with national course standards "one for each stage, one for each textbook". They identify repetition, disconnection, gaps and inverted sequencing in current content, such as the order in which basic Marxist concepts appear. The "Big Ideological and Political Course", which extends teaching into society, must stay ideologically consistent with the classroom courses. The authors want its resources improved, Schools of Marxism to coordinate it, and entertainment-style or superficial formats avoided. For teachers, they stress the "six requirements" set by Xi and the need to pass tests of politics, professional competence and professional ethics.

The authors propose reforms to selecting, training, refreshing, evaluating and rewarding teachers. These include an integrated bachelor-to-doctorate training route in Marxist theory, lifelong retraining, evaluation that does not favour research over teaching, and better pay and status. They conclude that integration, unity of principle with innovation, and a stable teaching force are the keys to higher course quality. Read the original if you want a detailed Chinese-language account of current policy thinking on how ideological and political courses are structured, taught and staffed, including the problems the authors identify in curriculum design and teacher evaluation.
quoteEn: Adhering to fundamental principles is not clinging to convention or never changing, but respecting objective laws and keeping to the right path; innovation is not a tree without roots or a stream without a source, but breaking through the status quo and keeping pace with the times.
quoteZh: “守正”不是墨守成规、一成不变，而是尊重客观规律、坚守正道；“创新”不是无本之木、无源之水，而是突破现状、与时俱进。

glossary.explanation: Compulsory Marxist theory and political education courses taught at all levels of Chinese schooling, abbreviated sizheng ke. They are treated as the main channel for teaching Marxism and the Party's theories.
A concept promoted by Xi Jinping that extends ideological and political education beyond the classroom into society, through practice bases, community partners and wider resources.
University units responsible for teaching the ideological and political theory courses and for the Marxist theory discipline.

t: Paths to making practical teaching in university ideological and political theory courses more precise
zh: 增强高校思政课实践教学精准性的进路探究
source: Journal of Party Building and Ideological Education in Schools (Xuexiao dangjian yu sixiang jiaoyu), 2025 no. 8
paras: Yang Yuan takes up a problem in Chinese higher education: practical teaching in university ideological and political theory courses has grown in importance, yet the author says it still suffers from formalism, entertainment-style activities and superficiality. Yang argues that moving from "formal coverage" to "real effectiveness" requires a "precision mindset" (jingzhun siwei) and proposes three routes to it. The article opens by citing the January 2025 outline on building China into a leading education power (2024–2035), which calls for a larger share of practical teaching.

The article is organised in three parts, each following the same pattern of a practical requirement, a diagnosed shortcoming and a proposed remedy. The parts deal with precise positioning of teaching philosophy, precise matching of teaching methods, and precise layout of teaching space. Yang draws on Marx's remark that social life is essentially practical, on speeches by Xi Jinping on students' subjectivity and on precision in online ideological education, and on the 2025 education outline.

On teaching philosophy, Yang criticises uniform syllabi, standardised content and rigid schedules that leave students little room for independent learning. The author calls for a shift from teacher-centred "teaching" to student-centred "learning", likening precise "drip irrigation" to indiscriminate "flood irrigation". Content would be tailored to students' majors and to year-by-year concerns, such as adaptation in the first year and life choices in the fourth. On methods, Yang urges that traditional formats such as surveys, visits and volunteering be adjusted through inquiry-based, project-based and task-driven teaching. New formats would use big data and AI to reach differentiated audiences, so that students move from "being made to practise" to "wanting to practise". On space, Yang observes that practice is too often confined to offline venues and neglects online settings. The author proposes a "reality plus virtual" field that combines local practice bases (communities, villages, factories, museums) with 5G, VR, AI and 3D simulations and "smart classrooms".

Yang concludes that precision in philosophy, methods and space together can convert the knowledge system of ideological and political courses into students' system of belief. The author presents this as a way to strengthen students' faith in Marxism, their confidence in socialism with Chinese characteristics and their confidence in the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. The discussion stays at the level of principles and examples, with no empirical data or case studies. Read the original if you want to see how Chinese education researchers currently frame practical teaching in ideological and political courses, using the language of precision, student-centredness and virtual-reality technology.
quoteEn: To strengthen the appeal and effectiveness of practical teaching in ideological and political courses, young students must be guided from "passive acceptance" to "active exploration".
quoteZh: 要增强思政课实践教学的吸引力和实效性，引导青年学生从“被动接受”转向“主动探索”

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses in Marxism, Party theory, morality and law taught in Chinese schools and universities. They are meant to carry out the fundamental task of fostering virtue through education.
The out-of-classroom component of ideological and political courses, including social surveys, site visits, volunteering and online activities.
An approach, borrowed from the language of targeted policy, that matches educational content and methods to specific groups or individuals rather than applying uniform measures.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The official national goal of restoring China's strength and standing, closely associated with Xi Jinping and the Chinese Dream.

t: On the difficulty of ideological and political education and its innovative development
zh: 论思想政治教育的艰难性及创新发展
paras: Xi Houjun takes up a question the author says has been neglected in the field of ideological and political education: why the work is so hard. After more than 40 years of disciplinary development, Xi argues, research has produced rich findings on its value, regularity and effectiveness, but not on its distinctive difficulty (jiannanxing). The article holds that this difficulty can be treated as an independent research topic, and that naming it is meant to sharpen the work's targeting and guiding power, not to excuse it.

The article is built in three parts. The first explains why the difficulty deserves attention. It draws on scholars' remarks and on Xi Jinping's comments that students' sharp questions are hard to answer thoroughly. The second sets out four dimensions of difficulty: political, theoretical, practical and the audience. The third offers a development path through three capacities, and a short conclusion places the problem in the context of social transition.

In Xi Houjun's account, the difficulty follows from the nature of the discipline. Politically, the work is openly political, so overcoming prejudice such as the label of "brainwashing" is hard. Theoretically, content that is abstract and systematic must be turned into vivid, connected reasoning and tied to reality, which taxes both teachers and students. Practically, education works as a "weapon of criticism" and cannot by itself abolish the social relations that produce mistaken ideas, a point supported by quotations from Marx and Engels. As for the audience, learners look for tangible interests, which ideological education supplies mainly as knowledge and spiritual guidance. To address these, Xi proposes strengthening scholarly capacity (sizheng xueshuli), the capacity to lead (yinlingli) and attractiveness (xiyinli). These are to be pursued through better argument, a more rigorous theoretical basis, attention to learners' circumstances, new media, team confidence and institutional support under the "big ideological and political education" concept.

Xi concludes that today's difficulty is a composite product of social transformation and the rebuilding of value order. The article names globalised cultural currents, the expansion of capital logic, great-power contests over ideological discourse, reification consciousness and the erosion of educators' authority as pressures. It stresses that the four dimensions and three strategies are not exhaustive. It also calls for sustained Party and state support, public understanding and better practitioner skills. Read the original if you want a Chinese-language account of how scholars in the field frame the obstacles facing ideological and political education, and how they link them to current policy language.
quoteEn: Raising the question of the difficulty of ideological and political education is not a matter of retreating in the face of hardship or consoling ourselves, but of analysing and answering why it is difficult and where the difficulty lies.
quoteZh: 把思想政治教育的艰难性之问提出来，并非知难而退、自宽自解，而是要分析和解答思想政治教育究竟为何难、难在哪

glossary.explanation: A Chinese academic discipline and educational practice through which the Party and state convey their ideology and political values, notably through compulsory political theory courses in schools and universities.
A concept that treats ideological and political education as a task for all schools, society and Party committees, not only for political theory courses.

t: Integrating Xi Jinping Thought on Culture into the teaching of the course "Ideology, Morality and the Rule of Law"
st: Principles, content and implementation paths
zh: 习近平文化思想融入“思想道德与法治”课教学探究
source: Journal of Party Building and Ideological Education in Schools, 2025 no. 8
paras: This article, from the field of ideological and political education, asks how Xi Jinping Thought on Culture can be brought into the first ideological and political theory course that university students take, "Ideology, Morality and the Rule of Law". Wang Shijing argues that the integration must not be a simple "stacking" of content. It should follow set principles, be tied to specific teaching content, and use new implementation methods suited to the digital era.

The article has three parts. The first sets out three general principles. The second maps the content of Xi's cultural thought onto the chapters of the 2023 edition of the textbook. The third proposes implementation paths organised around three dimensions: learning, belief and teaching. It is aimed at Generation Z university students and at the teachers who instruct them.

Wang's first move is to state the principles as three paired relationships: political guidance with scholarly inquiry, knowledge transmission with value formation, and theoretical indoctrination with practical enlightenment. Each pair is described as dialectically unified and not to be separated. The second move divides Xi's cultural thought into three theories, of spiritual independence, of value pursuit and of moral cultivation. Wang assigns these to chapters one and two, chapters three and four, and chapter five respectively. The Two Integrations, especially the second, are to be explained so that students grasp cultural confidence and the Party's theoretical creativity. Socialist core values and a view of civilisations based on equality and mutual learning are to be linked to a community with a shared future for mankind. The third move concerns method. Wang calls for case comparison, historical tracing, situational teaching, flipped classrooms, online platforms and volunteer service activities. Teachers are also to offer a scholarly critique of Western social trends and of what the article calls the "de-" tendencies (de-mainstreaming, de-historicising, de-Sinicising, de-ideologising and de-valuing).

Wang concludes that the integration is both knowledge transmission and the shaping of belief, and that teachers must themselves hold firm convictions in order to pass them on. The goal is for students to move from theoretical recognition to firm belief in Marxism, socialism with Chinese characteristics and national rejuvenation. Read the original if you want a concrete example of how Party theory is turned into chapter-by-chapter curriculum design and teaching method in Chinese university ideological courses.
quoteEn: Integrating Xi Jinping Thought on Culture into the teaching of "Ideology, Morality and the Rule of Law" is both the transmission of knowledge and, even more, the shaping of belief.
quoteZh: 习近平文化思想融入“思想道德与法治”课的教学过程，既是知识传授，更是信仰塑造。

glossary.explanation: A body of theory on cultural work attributed to Xi Jinping and formally presented in 2023. It is treated in official discourse as part of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era.

glossary.en: Ideology, Morality and the Rule of Law
glossary.literal: Thought, morality and the rule of law
glossary.explanation: A compulsory ideological and political theory course, usually the first one taken by Chinese university students. It covers outlook on life, values, morality and the rule of law from a Marxist standpoint.

The formula of combining Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities (the first) and with China's fine traditional culture (the second). The second was added in 2021–2023 and is stressed in official cultural theory.
A set of twelve values promoted officially since 2012. They cover the national, social and individual levels, and include prosperity, democracy, equality, rule of law and patriotism.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's official concept for international relations, stressing common interests and cooperation among states.

keywords: Ideology, Morality and the Rule of Law

t: The Communist Party of China's escape from the historical cycle of rise and fall: an interpretation from the mass-line view of history
zh: 中国共产党跳出历史周期率的群众史观阐释
source: Journal of Ideological and Theoretical Education (思想理论教育导刊), 2025 no. 5
paras: The article asks how the Communist Party of China can escape the 'historical cycle' of rise and fall, the question Huang Yanpei put to Mao Zedong in Yan'an. It starts from Xi Jinping's formulation of two answers: popular supervision of government, and the Party's self-reform. Ma and Yang argue that existing research has not applied historical materialism consistently here. They propose to read the problem through the 'mass view of history', which treats the people as the creators of history. On this basis they claim that the Party can escape the cycle by combining popular supervision with self-reform.

The article has three parts: why the cycle arises, why the Party must escape it, and how it can. The first part covers exploitative-class states and then relatively backward socialist states, using Marx, Engels, Lenin, Chinese classical sayings and the example of the Soviet Communist Party. The second part ties escaping the cycle to the Party's historical mission. The third part reviews popular supervision and self-reform from the Central Soviet Area to the period after the 18th Party Congress (2012).

In the authors' account, the cycle is a recurring overthrow of regimes. Its root cause is a ruling group whose rule seriously diverges from the people's interests. Exploiting classes, backed by the ruling group, keep intensifying exploitation. The ruling group's own corruption also erodes popular interests, so overthrow cannot be avoided. In backward socialist countries, Ma and Yang say, material motives and the need to govern through a vanguard stratum create room for Party members to degenerate. Market economy and long years in power add further tests, and they cite a Siberian newspaper poll in which 85 per cent said the Soviet party represented its apparatus. The Party can avoid this, they argue, because as a proletarian party its interests match the people's. Popular supervision is said to be authentic, broad, targeted, self-motivated and useful for governance. Self-reform is said to be thorough, conscious and guided by Marxism.

The authors conclude that the Party must stay in power for a long time, to develop the productive forces, suppress reactionary forces and carry out the long process of reaching communism. They call for continued popular supervision and self-reform. Specific measures are developing whole-process people's democracy, innovating forms of mass supervision, improving the Party's rules for self-reform and maintaining full and rigorous self-governance of the Party. Read the original if you want a detailed example of how Chinese Party theorists use classical Marxist texts to ground Xi Jinping's 'two answers' in historical materialism.
quoteEn: From the standpoint of the mass view of history, uncovering the deep causes of the periodic overthrow of regimes amounts to examining why a serious divergence between the ruling group's rule and the people's interests has always been so hard to avoid.
quoteZh: 在群众史观视域下，揭示政权周期性倾覆的深层原因实质是考察统治集团的统治与人民群众利益的严重背离为何总是难以避免。

glossary.explanation: The pattern in which regimes rise, decay and collapse in repeated cycles. Huang Yanpei raised it with Mao Zedong in Yan'an in 1945, in the exchange known as the 'cave dialogue'.

glossary.literal: view of history of the masses
glossary.explanation: The Marxist-Leninist claim that the people are the creators of history and decide its course. Chinese authors use it as part of historical materialism.
Xi Jinping's term for the Party's continuing internal self-correction and discipline. He presents it as the second answer to the historical cycle.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: The policy of strict Party discipline and anti-corruption work that has been stressed since the 18th Party Congress in 2012.
Official term for the Chinese model of democracy, which stresses popular participation at every stage of decision-making, not only elections.

t: Key focal points for advancing Party building in emerging fields
zh: 推进新兴领域党的建设的着力点
paras: Tang Yalin takes up the question of how the Party should build its organisation in the new economic, social and online spaces created by private-sector growth, the socialist market economy and new technology. Tang argues that new economic organisations, new social organisations and new forms of employment are both a key platform for Chinese modernization and a focal point for Party building in the new era. Strengthening Party building there is presented as the key to keeping the private economy on the right course, and as an indicator of the modernization of national governance capacity.

The article opens with the policy trajectory: the Constitution's treatment of the non-public economy, the 2012 Central Committee General Office opinion on Party building in non-public enterprises, the 18th, 19th and 20th Party Congress reports, and the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024).
