It also cites Xi Jinping's February 2025 remarks to private entrepreneurs and the Private Economy Promotion Law of April 2025. Tang then describes four features of emerging fields, and ends with three sets of measures.

In Tang's analysis, workers in emerging fields such as delivery riders, ride-hailing drivers and couriers are mobile, dispersed and atomised, work intensively under platform algorithms, and generate labour tensions and social spillover effects in communities. Citing a national workforce survey, Tang notes that 84 million platform-type workers make up 21 per cent of a 402 million workforce. Tang calls for fusing community-based, regional and grid-based Party building, and for an organisational system that joins offline and online. Examples include online Party-building and consultation platforms and 24-hour service channels. Tang also proposes moving from comprehensive coverage to effective coverage of Party organisations and strengthening the Party-building responsibility system, with annual agenda-setting and evaluation.

Tang concludes that Party organisations should combine "organisational work" with "work on people", attending to the material, cultural and emotional needs of new workers and the financing and development needs of new organisations. Online channels would build emotional connection with this aim. The stated goal is a pattern in which the Party, government and emerging-field actors move in the same direction. Read the original if you want a concise statement of current Party-building priorities for platform workers and private-sector organisations, with its policy references.
quoteEn: Shift the focus of Party-building work from the earlier emphasis on comprehensive coverage of Party organisations in emerging fields to an emphasis on their effective coverage.
quoteZh: 将党建工作重点从过去的重视新兴领域党组织的全面覆盖，向重视新兴领域党组织的有效覆盖转变

glossary.explanation: The official concept for China's own path of modernization, promoted by the Party leadership since the 20th Party Congress (2022).

glossary.zh: 新经济组织、新社会组织、新就业群体
glossary.pinyin: xīn jīngjì zǔzhī, xīn shèhuì zǔzhī, xīn jiùyè qúntǐ
glossary.en: new economic organisations, new social organisations and new forms of employment
glossary.literal: new economic organisations, new social organisations, new employment groups
glossary.explanation: Official shorthand for emerging private firms, non-state social bodies and platform or flexible workers. The 20th Party Congress report called for strengthening Party building among them.
A system that makes Party committees and officials accountable for Party-building tasks. It is assessed through annual agenda-setting and evaluation.
The official name for China's economic system after reform and opening up, which combines market mechanisms with public ownership as the main body and Party leadership.

t: Achievements and experience of "Chinese governance" in the new era
zh: 新时代“中国之治”的成就及经验
paras: Against what the author describes as a world of turbulence and accelerating change, in which "Chinese governance" contrasts sharply with "Western disorder", this article sets out the achievements and lessons of China's governance in the new era. Tian argues that "Chinese governance" is a concentrated summary of results achieved under Communist Party leadership in modernizing the national governance system and capacity. In the author's view it answers that question for China and offers Chinese wisdom and a Chinese approach to reforming global governance.

The article has three parts. The first reviews achievements since the 18th Party Congress (2012): institutional strengths, economic and social stability, national security, defence, emergency management, social governance, and the fusion of high-quality development with governance innovation. The second draws out main lessons. The third sets out directions for further modernizing governance. Tian supports the first part with figures, including a 2024 economy of 134.9 trillion yuan, R&D spending rising from 1 trillion yuan in 2012 to 3.6 trillion in 2024, and trade with Belt and Road Initiative partners above half of China's total.

Tian's core claim is that institutional advantages are being converted into governance effectiveness, with "Chinese governance" resting on "Chinese institutions" and being in essence governance by the people. The lessons offered are: Party leadership as the fundamental political guarantee; a people-centred approach, including whole-process people's democracy and grassroots governance; balancing reform and governance; renewing the Party's mass line, for example through the "Fengqiao experience"; technology and digital platforms as an engine of governance; and combining independent innovation with mutual learning among civilizations. The author presents Chinese modernization as breaking the myth that modernization equals Westernization and as a new path for developing countries.

For the future, Tian calls for upholding centralised Party leadership and balancing development with security. Other proposals are consolidating the domestic economy, relying on the people to build resilience against risk, fostering new growth drivers alongside the green transition, and pursuing high-standard opening up under the new development paradigm. The author also calls for greater influence in global governance, contributing public goods and a Chinese approach to improving the global system. Read the original if you want a compact, officially aligned overview of how the Chinese state presents its governance record and the lessons it draws from it, with the supporting statistics.
quoteEn: The foundation of "Chinese governance" lies in "Chinese institutions".
quoteZh: “中国之治”的基础在于“中国之制”。

glossary.literal: China's governance / the governance of China
glossary.explanation: An official slogan, prominent since the 2019 Fourth Plenum, summarising China's record in governing under Party leadership. It is paired with "Chinese institutions" (中国之制) as its basis.

glossary.zh: 国家治理体系和治理能力现代化
glossary.pinyin: guójiā zhìlǐ tǐxì hé zhìlǐ nénglì xiàndàihuà
glossary.en: modernizing the national governance system and capacity
glossary.explanation: A formula first put forward at the Third Plenum of the 18th Central Committee (2013) and made part of the overall goal of comprehensively deepening reform. It covers institutional improvement and the ability to implement institutions.
An official concept promoted by Xi Jinping since 2019, describing China's democracy as covering every stage of political and social life, not only elections.
The official term for China's own path of modernization, set out at the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as an alternative to Western models.
A grassroots dispute-resolution model from Fengqiao, Zhejiang, dating from the 1960s. It stresses settling conflicts locally and is promoted in the "new era" as a governance method.
An official economic goal since 2017, emphasising innovation, efficiency, coordination and sustainability over speed of growth.

t: Understanding Xi Jinping Thought on Ecological Civilization through the "six musts"
zh: 从“六个必须坚持”深刻把握习近平生态文明思想
paras: This short commentary, published in the Party journal Dangjian in 2025, sets out how to grasp Xi Jinping Thought on Ecological Civilization through the "six musts" (six principles to be upheld). Liu presents the thought as an important part of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era and as the fundamental guide for ecological civilization building. Understanding it through the six principles, Liu argues, strengthens theoretical and practical commitment to that work.

The article takes the six principles in turn: a people-first value stance, self-confidence and self-reliance, adherence to fundamental principles while innovating, a problem-oriented approach, a systems perspective, and a global outlook. Each section pairs the principle with examples from policy and from China's international role.

On the people-first principle, Liu argues that a good ecological environment is described as the most inclusive public benefit and that the thought enriches the Marxist view of people's livelihood. On self-reliance, the article contends that green development goes beyond the Western path of polluting first and cleaning up later, and that China's carbon peaking and carbon neutrality goals are firm while their pace and methods are for China to decide. On innovation, Liu holds that the idea that lucid waters and lush mountains are invaluable assets is a creative development of Marxist productive-forces theory, combined with traditional Chinese ecological wisdom. The systems principle is illustrated by the idea of mountains, rivers, forests, farmland, lakes, grasslands and deserts as a community of life.

Liu concludes that the thought is widely recognised internationally and that China has become an important participant, contributor and leader in global ecological civilization building, citing the Kunming-Montreal biodiversity framework and implementation of the Paris Agreement. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned overview of how Party-affiliated scholars frame the core principles of Xi's ecological thought.
quoteEn: Xi Jinping Thought on Ecological Civilization creatively put forward "lucid waters and lush mountains are invaluable assets", revealing the principle that protecting the ecological environment is protecting productive forces and improving it is developing productive forces.
quoteZh: 习近平生态文明思想创造性提出“绿水青山就是金山银山”，揭示了保护生态环境就是保护生产力、改善生态环境就是发展生产力的道理

glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Ecological Civilization
glossary.explanation: The body of ideas on environmental protection and green development attributed to Xi Jinping and formally systematised by the Party in 2018. It is treated as part of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.

glossary.zh: 绿水青山就是金山银山
glossary.en: lucid waters and lush mountains are invaluable assets
glossary.literal: green waters and green mountains are mountains of gold and silver
glossary.explanation: A slogan associated with Xi Jinping since 2005, holding that environmental protection and economic development are mutually reinforcing.
China's announced goals of peaking carbon dioxide emissions before 2030 and reaching carbon neutrality before 2060, often called the "dual carbon" goals.

t: Raising the capacity to govern the cultural sphere under conditions of informatization
zh: 提升信息化条件下文化领域治理能力
paras: Ouyang Xuemei's commentary takes up a remark by Xi Jinping at the 17th collective study session of the Politburo of the 20th Central Committee. Xi called for raising the capacity to govern the cultural sphere under conditions of informatization, so as to consolidate the Party's governing foundation and mass base ideologically, spiritually and culturally. Ouyang presents this as guidance for propaganda, ideological and cultural work in an age of digital, networked and intelligent technology, and argues that cultural governance capacity must be raised comprehensively.

The piece has three parts. The first sets out why the task matters. The second identifies four key areas of cultural governance online and cites a figure of 1.108 billion Chinese internet users by December 2024, an internet penetration rate of 78.6%. The third lists the measures needed, framed as study and implementation of Xi Jinping's thought on culture.

Ouyang gives three reasons for the task: it is required to modernize the national governance system and capacity; it is needed to consolidate the Party's governing and mass base amid more diverse and contested ideas; and it is needed to counter what the author calls Western digital hegemony, in which Western states use algorithms and big data to manipulate public opinion. The four areas are holding the leading role in online public opinion, building an online spiritual home around core socialist values and mainstream culture, using digital and intelligent tools to widen access to cultural services, and strengthening cultural soft power and international discourse power. The measures proposed are Party leadership over propaganda, ideology, media and the internet; an online mass line; multi-party governance; stronger cultural legislation; new technology for content management; and training of talent who combine cultural and technical skills.

Ouyang concludes that Party leadership is the most fundamental guarantee of cultural governance, and that technology, law, market actors and ordinary internet users must be combined in one system. The author points to gaps in current law on data security, privacy, technology ethics and algorithmic fairness, and calls for faster legislation. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how Party-affiliated scholarship frames internet and cultural governance in 2025, together with the specific policy measures it lists.
quoteEn: Raising the capacity to govern the cultural sphere under conditions of informatization is an inevitable requirement for effectively countering Western digital hegemony, deepening exchanges and mutual learning among civilizations, and further strengthening national cultural soft power and China's international discourse power.
quoteZh: 提升信息化条件下文化领域治理能力，是有效应对西方数字霸权，深化文明交流互鉴，进一步提高国家文化软实力、提升我国国际话语权的必然要求。

glossary.explanation: A phrase in Chinese official discourse for the alleged dominance of Western states and firms over digital technology and online information flows. The article says this dominance is used to manipulate public opinion.
A set of twenty-four characters in twelve values, promoted by the Party since the 18th Party Congress (2012), covering national, social and individual levels.
An extension of the Party's traditional 'mass line' (going among the people and responding to their needs) to digital platforms. It is used to justify user-oriented services and online participation.
The body of Xi Jinping's statements on culture, formally presented in 2023 as part of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era.
The influence a country gains through culture and values rather than coercion. Chinese leaders have made raising it an explicit policy aim.
A country's ability to shape agendas, narratives and norms in international communication. Chinese official writing treats it as something to raise in line with national strength.

t: The dialectical wisdom of advancing exchange and mutual learning among human civilizations
zh: 推进人类文明交流互鉴的辩证法智慧
source: Journal of Ideological and Theoretical Education (Sixiang lilun jiaoyu daokan), 2025 no. 5
paras: Pang Lisheng and Gong Yifei ask how different civilizations can coexist and develop in the modern world, taking as their starting point Xi Jinping's Global Civilization Initiative and its call for exchange and mutual learning among civilizations. They argue that this idea goes beyond the West-centred view of civilization and embodies a "practical dialectics" of civilizational exchange. In their account, it overcomes the understanding-bound (intellectual, non-dialectical) thinking behind Western civilizational theories.

The article has three parts. The first argues that the age of world history requires a new view of civilization and criticises three Western positions: hegemonism, isolationism and the clash-of-civilizations thesis. The second analyses three dialectical relations in civilizational development. The third sets out four practical paths for promoting exchange and mutual learning.

The authors read Fukuyama's "end of history" and Daniel Bell's "end of ideology" as hegemonist, Franz Boas's historical particularism as isolationist, and Samuel Huntington's thesis as a one-sided view that treats difference as inevitable conflict. They say all three rest on a metaphysical subject–object dualism. Against this they set three dialectical pairs: universality and particularity, individuality and worldliness (self and other), and necessity and contingency. Universality, they hold, appears only through particular civilizations, and the Western "universal values" are a particularity posing as universality. Cultural subjectivity, in their view, means autonomy of path and originality of theory, and is compatible with openness to other civilizations. Exchange and mutual learning are presented as a necessary tendency that works through contingent factors.

For practice, the authors propose four steps: recognise the plurality of civilizations and respect their diversity; build a community with a shared future for mankind and foster understanding between peoples; promote the common values of all humanity (peace, development, fairness, justice, democracy and freedom); and take mutual learning as the path to shared progress. They acknowledge that exchange will meet ideological prejudice and narrow national interests. They conclude that it requires rejecting both dogmatic absolutism and the "bad infinity" of relativism. Read the original if you want a Marxist-philosophical, dialectics-based reading of Xi Jinping's civilizational thought and its critique of Fukuyama, Boas and Huntington.
quoteEn: The universality of civilization is not detached from particularity; it is embodied in particular forms of civilization and is expressed through the particularity of different civilizations.
quoteZh: 文明的普遍性并不是脱离特殊性，而是体现于特殊性的文明样态中，并通过不同文明的特殊性得以表现出来

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A concept Xi Jinping has promoted since 2012–13 as a framework for global governance and international relations, stressing interdependence and shared interests among states.
A proposal announced by Xi Jinping in 2023 calling for respect for civilizational diversity, common human values, the value of heritage and international cultural exchange.

glossary.literal: common values of the whole of humankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's formulation of peace, development, fairness, justice, democracy and freedom as shared values. Official discourse contrasts it with Western "universal values".

t: Writing a new chapter for the times in Party conduct building on the new journey
zh: 书写好新征程党的作风建设的时代新篇
paras: Writing in Red Flag Manuscript in 2025, Sun Mingzeng asks how Party members and cadres should carry forward the Party's work on conduct (zuofeng jianshe) at a critical point between the 14th and 15th Five-Year Plans. The article takes as its occasion the Politburo meeting of 25 April 2025 and Xi Jinping's May 2025 remarks in Henan on the study and education campaign on implementing the eight-point regulation. Sun's thesis is that conduct building is a permanent task that bears on the Party's survival and that it should provide strong support for Chinese modernization.

The commentary has three parts. The first explains why conduct matters, drawing on theoretical, historical and practical logics. The second reviews what the author presents as achievements in conduct building since the 18th Party Congress (2012). The third sets out five practical directions for the new journey. Sun draws on statements by Mao Zedong and Xi Jinping and on the Party's historical record from the revolutionary years through reform and opening up.

In the first part, Sun argues that conduct is the concrete expression of a party's nature, purpose and line, so a ruling party that tolerates unhealthy tendencies risks losing popular support and power. In the author's account, the Party's history shows that the further it keeps from such tendencies, the closer it stays to the masses. The second part credits Xi Jinping's discourse with deepening understanding of conduct as a question of Party spirit and of the Party's relationship with the people. It also credits the Party Central Committee with improving political ecology, issuing Party regulations on discipline, supervision and frugality, and curbing hedonism, extravagance, formalism and bureaucratism. The final part calls for strengthening ideological foundations, targeted rectification combined with positive example-setting, leading cadres setting an example, investigating and handling unhealthy conduct and corruption together, and consistently strict management.

Sun concludes that conduct building has no end point and must become regular and long-term, with responsibility assigned at every level of the Party. Big-data tools should be used to trace leads on misconduct. The aim, in Sun's words, is to ensure the Party never changes in nature, colour or flavour. Read the original if you want a representative example of how a Party-school scholar frames the 2025 campaign on the eight-point regulation within the official discourse on full and rigorous self-governance of the Party.
quoteEn: Conduct building is not an expedient or a one-off measure; it has no final note.
quoteZh: 作风建设，不是权宜之计、一时之举，没有休止符。

glossary.explanation: A set of rules adopted by the Politburo in December 2012 to curb extravagance, formalism and bureaucratism among officials, covering matters such as official receptions, meetings and travel. It is widely treated as the starting point of Xi Jinping's conduct campaign.
The official name for the Party's path of national development, set out as a concept after the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western modernization.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.literal: comprehensively and strictly governing the Party
glossary.explanation: The official term for the Party's disciplinary and anti-corruption programme, prominent since the 18th Party Congress (2012).

keywords: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party

t: Raising the quality and effectiveness of universities' service to the integrated development of scientific and technological innovation and industrial innovation
zh: 提升高校服务科技创新和产业创新融合发展的质效
paras: Ma Xiaojie, writing in Red Flag Manuscripts in 2025, asks how Chinese universities can better serve the fusion of scientific and technological innovation with industrial innovation. Citing Xi Jinping, the article treats this fusion as the basic path to developing new quality productive forces. Ma argues that universities should build a mutually supporting system of talent cultivation, scientific innovation and the transfer of research results into practice, and should use their particular strengths to deepen that fusion.

The piece has three parts. The first explains why the two kinds of innovation matter for new quality productive forces and high-quality development, and why universities are a key link, citing the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024). The second sets out the "three-legged" system in detail. The third offers five sets of practical measures: talent training, discipline layout, research supply, transfer of results, and Party building together with innovation culture.

In Ma's account, each leg of the system is being reshaped. Talent training moves from supply-driven knowledge transmission to demand-driven innovation, cross-disciplinary study and open, ecosystem-style training. Research moves from the linear laboratory model to networked, "organised research" that links basic research, technology transfer and industrial conversion. Transfer of results should be both "reaching for the sky" (world-class work) and "standing on the ground" (real productive use), supported by proof-of-concept, pilot-scale testing, benefit-sharing and financing, and by collaboration among government, industry, universities, research institutes and users.

Ma's concrete proposals include dual mentors from academia and industry, disciplines aligned with industrial clusters, joint laboratories with leading firms, university science parks, evaluation systems that reward technology transfer, and international scientific cooperation. Ma also calls for Party branches to be set up within disciplines, major platforms and transfer projects, for "AI+" curricula, and for promotion of the spirit of scientists and educators. The aim, Ma says, is to contribute momentum to new quality productive forces and Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want a detailed picture of how a university Party leader frames higher education's role in national innovation policy and which institutional measures are recommended.
quoteEn: In promoting scientific and technological innovation, universities must both "reach for the sky" and "stand on the ground".
quoteZh: 高校推动科技创新，既要“顶天”，也要“立地”。

glossary.explanation: A concept introduced by Xi Jinping in 2023 for advanced productive forces driven by innovation, high technology, high efficiency and high quality. It is now central to official economic policy.
An official goal, stressed since 2017, of shifting from rapid growth to growth that is efficient, innovative, green and balanced.
The official name for China's own path to modernization, set out by the Party after the 20th Party Congress (2022).
A policy approach in which universities direct research towards national strategic needs through coordinated teams and platforms, rather than relying mainly on individual free exploration.

t: Continuing to stimulate strong momentum for economic recovery and improvement
zh: 《求是》杂志评论员：持续激发经济回升向好的强劲动能
paras: This commentary, issued under the byline of Qiushi magazine's commentator (issue 17, 2025), asks how China can sustain its economic recovery as traditional growth drivers weaken. Its answer is that science and technology innovation should lead the development of new quality productive forces, so that new drivers of growth can take over from the old.

The piece opens with figures for 2024 and the first half of 2025. It cites 5.3% growth in the first half, a "three new" economy contributing over 24 trillion yuan (18.01% of GDP) in 2024, and services contributing 60.2% of growth. It then takes four areas in turn: strategic emerging industries, the digital economy, the upgrading of traditional industries, and services.

The commentary argues that the economy is at a critical stage of transition between old and new drivers. Property and infrastructure booms are fading, while the "new three" (new-energy vehicles, lithium batteries, solar products) are growing, but the new drivers cannot yet fully offset the old ones. For each area it names problems: core technologies controlled by others, weak investment mechanisms and talent shortages in emerging industries; data silos, algorithmic discrimination and infrastructure gaps in the digital economy; and firms that are unwilling, afraid or unable to transform among traditional industries, which make up over 80% of manufacturing. It stresses that new drivers should not be equated with new industries, and that traditional ones must not be discarded.

The remedies it proposes include the new whole-nation system, long-term and "patient" capital, the "AI+" initiative, large-scale equipment renewal and support for digital transformation of small and medium firms. It also proposes better policies for healthcare, elderly care and education services. It concludes that China stands at a new starting point for high-quality development and will create fresh achievements. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official Party commentary framed the 2025 economic outlook and policy priorities.
quoteEn: New drivers of growth cannot simply be equated with emerging industries; traditional industries can also nurture new drivers.
quoteZh: 新动能不能简单等同于新兴产业，传统产业也能孕育新动能。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping since 2023, referring to advanced productivity driven by technological breakthroughs, emerging industries and innovation.
An official goal since the late 2010s that shifts emphasis from high-speed growth to efficiency, innovation, sustainability and balance.
An official term for mobilising state, market and research resources nationwide to achieve breakthroughs in key technologies.
A national policy to integrate artificial intelligence into sectors of the economy and society, announced in official documents in 2024–2025.

t: Integrating the great spirit of resistance against Japanese aggression into the building of the "Great Ideological and Political Course"
zh: 将伟大抗战精神融入“大思政课”建设
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in September 2025, Peng Qinghong asks how the great spirit of resistance against Japanese aggression can be built into the "Great Ideological and Political Course" (da sizheng ke), the effort to extend ideological and political education beyond the classroom. Peng argues that doing so is both a requirement of passing on the "red gene" and a way to strengthen the ideological content, theoretical depth, appeal and relevance of that education. The piece is a short commentary on university teaching practice.

The article is organised in three parts: clear goals, open channels, and long-term mechanisms. It begins from Xi Jinping's summary of the spirit of resistance, which comprises patriotism, national integrity, heroism and conviction of victory. It then moves from aims to practical delivery routes and finally to institutional safeguards, drawing mainly on examples from university settings.

On goals, Peng says the fundamental aim is to cultivate new-era youth, through ideals and convictions, love of family and country, a spirit of struggle, and a sense of mission. Using historical facts, students are to be guided to see the Chinese Communist Party's role in the war and the historical inevitability of the socialist path. On channels, Peng lists course design and textbooks, classroom teaching (including professional courses, which could use stories such as Mao Yisheng's bridge-building, Fan Xudong's soda-ash manufacture and Mei Lanfang's refusal to perform, plus VR/AR and role-play), campus culture and Party and Youth League activities, visits to museums and memorial sites, and online platforms and student-made short videos.

For lasting effect, Peng proposes cooperation between Party committees, publicity departments, ideological and political teachers and subject teachers. Other proposals are partnerships with memorial halls and cemeteries, a supply of content covering sources, teaching resources and research, incentives for teachers and students, and guarantees of organisation, funding and staffing. The aim is to make integration institutionalised, standardised and long-term. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Chinese university leaders are told to turn wartime commemoration into concrete ideological and political education practice.
quoteEn: Integrating the great spirit of resistance into the "Great Ideological and Political Course" is a systematic project that requires coordination among the university's internal departments and between the university and all sectors of society.
quoteZh: 伟大抗战精神融入“大思政课”是一项系统工程，需要学校内部各部门之间，学校与社会各界之间的协同配合。

glossary.explanation: A policy concept promoted from around 2021 that extends ideological and political education from the classroom into society, practice and online spaces.

glossary.en: great spirit of resistance against Japanese aggression
glossary.explanation: A formulation, set out by Xi Jinping, for the values said to have emerged during the War of Resistance against Japan (1931–45): patriotism, national integrity, heroism and conviction of victory.
A Party term for the revolutionary traditions and values said to be inherited by later generations.
An official term for the young generation that education is meant to shape to take on national rejuvenation tasks.

t: Advancing high-quality development and high-efficacy governance in universities in tandem
zh: 协同推进高校高质量发展与高效能治理
paras: This commentary in Guangming Daily asks how Chinese universities should handle two tasks together: high-quality development and high-efficacy governance. He argues that the two are mutually reinforcing, like the two wheels of a cart or two wings of a bird. Pursuing them jointly, in He's view, is both an internal requirement of comprehensive reform of higher education in the new era and a driving force for building a strong education nation.

The piece has four sections. It first sets out what high-quality development means for universities, then the basic logic of effective governance, then the interaction between the two, and finally practical steps to promote that interaction. Throughout, He draws on Xi Jinping's statements on talent cultivation, first-class universities, systems thinking and education digitalisation.

In He's account, high-quality development is a combined leap in talent training, disciplinary innovation, international competitiveness and social service, not one indicator. Talent training must join moral education with innovation. Disciplines should be built around basic, applied and interdisciplinary strengths, linked to industry and to key technologies. Governance, for He, must shift from fragmentation to integration, with cross-disciplinary platforms, joint goals for knowledge creation and training, and digital tools for decision-making. The two reinforce each other: development goals set the direction of governance, while governance supplies institutional foundations and resources. This forms what the author calls a virtuous circle.

He proposes three measures. The first is to build consensus on public values through digital democratic consultation, outside advisory bodies and cultural education. The second is to improve coordinated governance by devolving some powers to second-tier colleges, setting up cross-departmental platforms and holding joint meetings. The third is to deepen digital applications through unified data platforms, digital skills training and rules on data security, privacy and algorithmic transparency. He says these should keep technology serving moral education and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official discourse links Xi Jinping's high-quality development agenda to university management and digitalisation.
quoteEn: High-quality development is the goal orientation and value expression of high-efficacy governance, while high-efficacy governance lays the institutional foundation for high-quality development and provides operational guarantees.
quoteZh: 高质量发展是高效能治理的目标导向和价值体现，高效能治理则为高质量发展筑牢制度根基、提供运行保障。

glossary.explanation: A slogan adopted by the Party leadership around 2017 for shifting from rapid growth to quality, innovation and efficiency. Here it is applied to universities.
A term from recent Party documents on improving the performance of state and institutional governance. The article applies it to university management.
A national goal, set out in a 2024 plan, of making China a leading country in education by 2035.
The stated fundamental task of Chinese education: cultivating students' moral character and political orientation alongside knowledge.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's central national goal, stressed under Xi Jinping: restoring China's strength and international standing by the mid-twenty-first century.

t: Shaping a new pattern of fostering virtue and cultivating people through the "Big Ideological and Political Course"
zh: 以“大思政课”塑造立德树人新格局
paras: Lü Chao, writing in Red Flag Manuscript in 2025, asks how the "Big Ideological and Political Course" can be used to give new shape to the fundamental task of fostering virtue and cultivating people. The article takes its cue from Xi Jinping's remarks to education-sector political advisers during the 2025 "Two Sessions", which called for joining the ideological and political "small classroom" with the "big classroom" of society. Lü's thesis is that this model is the main channel for strengthening ideological guidance and for supplying talent for Chinese modernization.

The piece has three parts. The first sets out why the "Big Ideological and Political Course" matters. The second discusses regularities that should be understood more deeply: focusing on moulding minds, emphasising practical education, and strengthening systems thinking. The third proposes new paths for building the course, covering problem-solving, methods and evaluation. Lü cites the 453 national practice-teaching bases and examples from Peking University, Renmin University of China and the National University of Defense Technology.

Lü argues that the course is needed for three reasons. It carries out the fundamental task of fostering virtue and cultivating people amid complex ideological struggle, rapid advances in the internet and artificial intelligence, and young people who prefer personalised and diverse experiences. It also advances the content-based development of ideological and political courses, which the author says currently suffer from weak links between theory and reality and from narrow methods. Finally, it consolidates the ideological and political foundations of young students. In practice, Lü calls for knowledge teaching to be joined to value guidance, explicit to implicit education, and scientific to humanistic training. Lü also wants more practical teaching, online and offline integration, and overall planning of classrooms, teaching staff and platforms.

Lü proposes integrating ideological and political education across primary, secondary and tertiary levels, which the author says now repeat content and work in isolation. Schools, families and society should be linked in one system. Teaching should use case-based, inquiry-based and experiential methods, practice bases and digital platforms such as "Study Power" (Xuexi Qiangguo). Lü also wants a "community of evaluation" of teachers, students and parents, with indicators of knowing, believing and acting, and with AI used to support assessment. Read the original if you want a Party-school-style account of how current policy on university ideological and political education is being operationalised, including its AI and practice-base elements.
quoteEn: The "Big Ideological and Political Course" focuses on the fundamental questions of what kind of people to cultivate, how to cultivate them and for whom, and is an important way of carrying out the fundamental task of fostering virtue and cultivating people in the new era.
quoteZh: “大思政课”聚焦解决好培养什么人、怎样培养人、为谁培养人这个根本问题，是贯彻落实新时代立德树人根本任务的重要途径。

glossary.explanation: A policy concept promoted since 2021 that links classroom ideological and political courses with social practice, using society as a 'big classroom'. It is meant to involve many actors and venues, not only formal courses.

Official term for the fundamental task of education in China, stressing moral formation alongside intellectual, physical, aesthetic and labour education. It is prominent in Xi Jinping-era education policy.
Compulsory courses in Chinese schools and universities that teach Marxism, Party theory, history and morality. Their content and delivery are set by national policy.
The official name for the Party's path of national development, set out in 2021–22 as a distinctive route to modernization with Chinese characteristics.
The annual plenary meetings of the National People's Congress and the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference, held together each March.

t: High-quality ideological and political education leading the cultivation of top-notch innovative talent in universities: a practical path
zh: 高质量思想政治教育引领高校拔尖创新人才培养的实践进路
source: Journal of Party Building and Ideological Education in Schools, 2025 no. 8
paras: Qiu Yanghai asks how universities can use high-quality ideological and political education to guide the cultivation of top-notch innovative talent. Starting from the 20th Party Congress (2022) call to raise the quality of home-grown talent training, the article argues that such talent is strategically vital: it is, in Qiu's account, the fundamental way to answer the "Needham question" and the "Qian Xuesen question", and it underpins breakthroughs in core technologies and the development of new quality productive forces. Qiu's thesis is that political and ideological quality is a cornerstone of such talent's success, so universities need a dedicated, well-resourced ideological and political education system for them.

The article is a policy-oriented piece organised in three parts. The first concerns top-level design, the second the construction of an education system, and the third the safeguarding institutions. Each part sets out numbered measures, with examples such as leadership groups, joint training with schools and enterprises, differentiated curricula and individualised evaluation. Qiu cites a 2020 Ministry of Education guideline on integrating ideological and political content into courses and one survey figure on student stress.

On top-level design, Qiu proposes a "special zone" for these students built on three mechanisms: a special plan embedded in the university's medium- and long-term and five-year plans, a coordination mechanism, and a feedback mechanism. The coordination mechanism includes a leadership group headed by senior university leaders, a community of universities, local governments, research bodies, enterprises and families, and integration across primary, secondary and tertiary stages. The feedback mechanism uses big data and generative AI to track students and graduates. On the system itself, Qiu calls for high-grade ideological and political theory courses with leading teachers, for ideological and political content woven into specialist courses and research training, and for daily education led by well-qualified counsellors. On safeguards, Qiu stresses resource orientation (small classes, eminent research supervisors, Party branches in research platforms led by "dual leaders"), targeted environmental and psychological support, and inclusive evaluation. That evaluation would place more weight on political assessment, process and the long term, for instance by extending review cycles from one year to two.

Qiu concludes that these measures would help such students form correct political views, a sense of the larger picture and clear judgement of right and wrong, so that universities can supply strategic talent for Chinese modernization. Political evaluation is presented as the safeguard of direction, while process-based and long-cycle assessment protects exploratory research. Read the original if you want a concrete example of how Chinese higher-education policy writing proposes to combine ideological and political education with elite talent training.
quoteEn: Evaluation is the baton that directs the ideological and political education of top-notch innovative talent.
quoteZh: 评价是拔尖创新人才思想政治教育的指挥棒。

glossary.explanation: A policy term for exceptionally gifted students and researchers expected to drive scientific and technological breakthroughs. It features in national talent and education strategies.
The system of Party-guided teaching in schools and universities that aims to shape students' political outlook, values and ideals. It includes dedicated courses and daily guidance.
A concept introduced by Xi Jinping in 2023 for advanced productivity driven by technological innovation and emerging industries.
The official name for China's path of modernization under Party leadership, prominent in Party documents since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
The question, associated with Joseph Needham, of why modern science did not originate in China despite its earlier technological advances.
A question attributed to the scientist Qian Xuesen asking why Chinese universities do not produce more outstanding, innovative talent.

t: Digital-intelligence empowerment of Party governance modernization through the lens of complex adaptive systems theory
st: Systemic logic and practical path
zh: 复杂适应系统理论视阈下数智赋能政党治理现代化的系统逻辑与实践进路
paras: Writing in a Party-affiliated journal, Tang Qingpeng asks how digital-intelligence technologies (big data, cloud computing, AI) can enable the modernization of the Communist Party's own governance, which the article treats as a precondition of Chinese modernization. Tang argues that existing research, especially abroad, concentrates on party competition and elections and misses the organisational and systemic side. The article proposes complex adaptive systems (CAS) theory as a remedy: the Party is a complex system that adapts non-linearly to its technological environment, so empowerment is neither automatic nor always beneficial.

The article has four parts. It first states the problem and reviews the literature, then derives a logic of digital-intelligence empowerment from the three CAS properties of adaptability, openness and emergence. Next it identifies three practical difficulties, each tied to one property, and finally sets out four paths of response. Tang draws on Marx's remark that new productive forces change modes of production and social relations, and cites figures such as 99.185 million Party members and 5.176 million primary organisations at the end of 2023.

In the first half, Tang reads empowerment as a process in which the Party actively uses technology, not merely receives it. It operates on Party governance methods, the governance system and governance capacity. Its emergent values are stronger governing capacity, a technical means of tackling the "unique problems of a large party", and greater ability to lead the modernization of national governance. The second half turns to risks, described as "empowerment" turning into "binding". Tang names a rejection effect (skills gaps, uneven digitalisation, "information islands", copycat platforms), security risks (cyberattacks, data leaks) and digital formalism, such as rigid quantitative indicators and points rankings on the Xuexi Qiangguo platform.

Tang proposes four paths: an internet-minded, forward-looking outlook; digital channels that serve the Party–masses relationship under the mass line; institutional arrangements for data integration and data security; and digital literacy and talent training for Party members and cadres. The article presents CAS theory as moving beyond technological determinism toward active, systemic practice. Read the original if you want an example of how Party-school scholarship applies systems theory to Party building, including its frank list of implementation problems such as formalism.
quoteEn: Digital-intelligence empowerment of Party governance has a "double-edged sword" effect: "empowering" can also turn into "binding".
quoteZh: 数智赋能政党治理存在着“双刃剑”效应，数智“赋能”也可能变成数智“缚能”。

glossary.explanation: A recent term combining digitalisation and intelligent (AI) technologies. It refers to organisations using these technologies to strengthen their own capacity.

glossary.en: unique problems of a large party
glossary.literal: problems unique to a large party
glossary.explanation: A phrase in Party discourse for the governance difficulties that arise from the Party's very large membership and organisational scale.
The official term for China's path of modernization under Party leadership, prominent since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
A Party principle, associated with Mao Zedong, that officials should gather views from the people and turn them into policy and service.
In Party usage, an emphasis on outward show, paperwork and indicators over real results. The Party has repeatedly campaigned against it.
A theory from the life sciences that treats systems as interacting agents adapting non-linearly to an open environment. It is applied here to the Party.

t: The core of the problem of work style is the relationship between the Party and the people
zh: 作风问题核心是党同人民群众的关系问题
paras: Huang Xianghuai, a deputy director and researcher at the Central Party School, offers a study commentary on Xi Jinping's statement that "the core of the problem of work style is the relationship between the Party and the people". The author argues that this relationship is the fundamental question for a Marxist proletarian party. Serving the people wholeheartedly, in Huang's reading, must show itself in the Party's governance, its line and policies, and also in its work style. The piece appeared in the journal Dangjian (Party Building) in 2025.

The article has three parts. The first looks at Party work-style building through the Party–people relationship. The second argues that building a good work style means keeping flesh-and-blood ties with the people. The third proposes that the ability to do mass work be used as a yardstick of how effective work-style building has been.

In the first part, Huang says work-style building must start from and return to serving the people. The people should take part in it and judge it, and its results must be tangible to them. The Party is urged to combine "establishing" good practices with "breaking" bad ones, citing Xi's line that the people are the "examiners". In the second part Huang sets out three requirements for cadres: shed bureaucratic airs, stay grounded by going to the grass roots, and cultivate moral rectitude through Party-spirit training. Huang warns that dropping official airs without getting close to the people can leave hidden or mutated formalism and bureaucratism.

In the third part, Huang calls on Party members and cadres to improve three abilities. These are investigation and research, which Huang says must not become formalistic; guiding public opinion in the internet age, where "Four Dimensions of Misconduct" problems can be amplified online; and innovation in work methods, given the more diverse interests of different social groups. Huang concludes that cadres should be seen by the public to have both a good style and strong capability. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party Building presents Xi Jinping's work-style discourse to cadres and links it to the mass line.
quoteEn: Whether work-style building is done well is best seen by the people's sharp eyes, and their feelings are the most genuine.
quoteZh: 作风建设好不好，群众的眼睛最雪亮，群众的感受最真实。

glossary.explanation: A long-standing Party term for efforts to improve the conduct and habits of Party members and cadres, such as campaigns against formalism, bureaucratism and extravagance.
The four undesirable work styles targeted since 2012: formalism, bureaucratism, hedonism and extravagance.
A Party method of governance and work associated with Mao Zedong: gathering the views of the masses, concentrating them into policy, and returning to the masses to test it.

glossary.literal: serve the people with one heart and one mind
glossary.explanation: The Party's stated fundamental purpose, a slogan associated with Mao Zedong and written into the Party constitution.
Two work-style faults the Party campaigns against: going through the motions without substantive results, and detached, hierarchical behaviour by officials.

t: The concepts, interrelations and integrity of Party spirit, Party style and Party discipline
zh: 党性党风党纪的概念内涵、相互关系及整体性探析
paras: Ding and Zhang take up a formula from Xi Jinping: Party spirit (dangxing), Party style (dangfeng) and Party discipline (dangji) form an organic whole, in which Party spirit is the foundation, Party style the manifestation and Party discipline the safeguard. The authors argue that existing scholarship either treats only two of the three concepts or studies all three without tracing their historical evolution. They also find that the "trinity" has not been explained systematically in theoretical terms. They aim to fill both gaps and to support the requirement to "grasp all three together".

The article has three parts. The first defines each concept, drawing on Marx, Lenin, Mao Zedong, Liu Shaoqi, Deng Xiaoping and later leaders, and on the main scholarly positions. The second traces how the Chinese Communist Party's understanding of the three evolved, from the Red Army's disciplinary rules and the Yan'an rectification campaign through reform and opening up to the period since the 18th Party Congress (2012). It then gives a theoretical account of their relationship. The third part explains why the three form a whole.

The core argument is that each element has its own role. Party spirit is the "inner basis" that determines the nature of style and discipline, and the driving force of the Party's self-reform. Party style is a "barometer" and "window" through which otherwise hard-to-measure Party spirit and the strictness of discipline become visible. It also has relative independence: good style nourishes Party spirit and discipline, while bad style erodes them. Party discipline is the "anchor" that supplies institutional constraint and educational guidance, yet it depends in turn on strong Party spirit and sound style. The authors say the whole is shown in four features: coordinated governing subjects, complementary functions, shared goals and a common method. The shared goals include solving the problems unique to a large party and keeping the Party advanced and pure. The common method rests on putting the people first, problem orientation and systems thinking.

The authors conclude that the three must be tackled together, and that implementing this still faces difficulties. They name three open questions: how to coordinate the governing subjects effectively, how to cover all elements and avoid a "barrel effect", and how to build workable mechanisms. They propose integrating the three across organisation, mechanisms, process and institutions, so that the whole exceeds the sum of its parts. They also call for breakthroughs on prominent problems in each area, including strengthening the spirit of the Central Committee's eight-point regulation. Read the original if you want a systematic account of how Party-building theory in China defines and links these three concepts, with a historical survey of leaders' statements.
quoteEn: Party spirit is the inner basis of Party style and discipline, Party style is the outward manifestation of Party spirit and discipline, and Party discipline provides an important safeguard for Party spirit and style.
quoteZh: 党性是党风党纪的内在根据，党风是党性党纪的外在表现，党纪为党性党风提供重要保障。

glossary.explanation: The class stance, ideals and organisational loyalty expected of a Communist Party and its members. The authors discuss it at the level of the organisation and of the individual member.
The Party's conduct and image in thought, work and life, as seen by the public. The term is traced to Mao Zedong's 1942 essay on rectifying the Party's style.

The binding code of conduct for Party organisations and members. It includes political, organisational, integrity, mass-line, work and lifestyle discipline, set out in the Regulations on Disciplinary Actions.
A term in Xi Jinping-era discourse for the Party's continual correction of its own faults, presented as its answer to the question of how to escape the "historical cycle" of rise and decline.

keywords: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party

t: Re-examining the Marxist view of the masses: from the dissolution of fetishism to the generation of intersubjectivity
zh: 重审马克思主义群众观：从拜物教消解到主体间性的生成
paras: Historical materialism holds that the people are the true subject of history, yet Ma Youru argues that under capitalism this truth is deeply obscured by commodity fetishism. The article proposes that re-examining the Marxist view of the masses requires criticising and dissolving fetishism, then reconstructing the masses' subjectivity as a process of intersubjectivity that is generated through practice.

The short commentary first describes how fetishism turns social relations between people into relations between things, then identifies the material route to overcoming it, and finally sets out the dimensions of intersubjectivity. It ends by summarising a three-step dialectical path.

Ma contends that fetishism works at the levels of production, exchange and consumption. Workers come to see themselves as commodities, social ties are reified, and history appears to have no subject, only the self-unfolding of capital. Because fetishism is rooted in private ownership and generalised commodity production, Ma argues that criticism of ideas is insufficient. Only the revolutionary practice of the masses, aimed at abolishing private ownership and founding an "association of free individuals", can pierce the illusion. In such an association Ma identifies three dimensions of intersubjectivity: mutual recognition as equals, symbiotic practice, and co-generation of the community's form and goals. Ma presents this as overcoming the opposition between collectivism and individualism.

Ma concludes that the Marxist view of the masses follows a path from dissolving fetishism, through the practical formation of subjectivity, to the internal construction of intersubjectivity. The "masses" are therefore a historical force that is continually generated, not a fixed concept, and Ma holds that this theoretical legacy retains critical and emancipatory force today. Read the original if you want a brief, philosophically oriented restatement of the Marxist theory of the masses through fetishism critique and intersubjectivity.
quoteEn: The \"masses\" are not a fixed, static concept; they are a historical force that is continually generated and developed in confronting oppressive structures, overcoming their own alienation and building relations of equal cooperation.
quoteZh: “群众”并非一个凝固的静止的概念，它是在对抗压迫性结构、克服自身异化、建构平等协作关系中不断生成、发展的历史性力量。

t: Universities should serve as the vanguard of education reform
zh: 高校要当好教育改革排头兵
paras: This short commentary, published in China Social Sciences Today in August 2025, takes up Xi Jinping's call for Chinese universities to lead education reform. Wang argues that universities should act as the vanguard of that reform, anchored in the fundamental task of fostering virtue through education (立德树人), and should help build a strong education nation.

The article is organised around three reasons. First, reform is an inherent requirement of the fundamental task of fostering virtue through education. Second, universities have particular strengths that qualify them to lead. Third, reform is necessary for high-quality development of higher education.

On the second point, Wang lists talent, teaching and research capacity, cultural exchange and multi-party cooperation as the sources of universities' leading role. On the third, the author calls for systemic innovation in three areas. Evaluation should move away from overemphasis on research, test scores and credentials, and should add weight to practice, innovation and moral conduct, with ideological and political content in courses counted in staff assessment. Training models should be adjusted to national strategy and industry needs through interdisciplinary courses and project-based learning. Management should give departments more autonomy, tilt resources to frontline teaching and set up a tolerance-for-error mechanism.

Wang concludes that the Party's leadership must run through the whole reform process. Universities should train people for the Party and the country, and should use Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era to shape students' values. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-line language on university reform and moral education is presented in a Chinese academic commentary.
quoteEn: Universities must ensure that the Party's leadership runs through the entire process of education reform.
quoteZh: 高校必须把党的领导贯穿教育改革全过程。

glossary.explanation: A guiding principle of Chinese education policy, stressed in Party documents since the 18th Party Congress (2012). It makes moral and ideological formation the core task of schooling.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The official Party ideology associated with Xi Jinping, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017 and 2018. It is taught throughout the Chinese education system.
A national goal of building a world-leading education system, set out in a Party and State plan in early 2025.

glossary.en: ideological and political content in courses
glossary.explanation: A policy of integrating ideological and political education into all subject courses, not only dedicated political classes.

t: The fourfold logic behind the emergence of "ideological and political leadership capacity"
zh: 论思政引领力的四重出场逻辑
source: Ideological and Theoretical Education (思想理论教育), 2025 no. 6
paras: In September 2024 Xi Jinping told the National Education Conference that a leading education country with Chinese characteristics must have, first of all, strong "ideological and political leadership capacity" (sizheng yinlingli). Bai and Wang ask why this concept appeared and why it was ranked as the first trait of such a country. They argue that its emergence is scientific, reasonable and necessary, and that this can be shown through four logics: disciplinary, theoretical, historical and practical.

The article is a conceptual and historical study in ideological and political education. It first places the concept within the discipline's forty years of development and traces its precursors in Party documents. It then turns to its Marxist foundations, surveys the Party's ideological and political work from the New Democratic Revolution to the post-2012 period, and finally links the concept to current strategic tasks.

The authors first present the concept as a "signature concept" for building an autonomous body of knowledge in the discipline. They trace it through phrases such as "ideological leadership capacity" in the 19th Party Congress report (2017) and earlier scholarly work on the leading force of ideological and political education. Second, they ground it in three Marxist principles: the dialectic of social being and social consciousness, the doctrine of "inculcation" (read as combining instilling with enlightening, not rote cramming), and the theories of human essence and free, all-round development. Third, they argue that the Party's record shows ideological work uniting revolutionary forces, building consensus for construction, and promoting the liberation of thinking after reform and opening up.

On the practical side, Bai and Wang contend that the concept answers the needs of building a leading education country. They name the Party's overall leadership of education, the fundamental task of fostering virtue and cultivating talent, and education modernization by 2035. They also see it as required for socialist ideological work, which includes ideological security, leading online public opinion, and combining constructive and critical work against erroneous trends. They add that it drives Chinese modernization and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation through spiritual motivation, direction and consensus. Read the original if you want a detailed account of how Chinese scholars justify and theorise this new official concept, with its Party-document genealogy.
quoteEn: Ideological and political leadership capacity is neither a concrete expression of empirical description nor a simple translation of policy discourse, but a theoretical expression of the essential attributes of the discipline of ideological and political education.
quoteZh: 思政引领力既非经验描述的具象化表达，也非政策话语的简单转译，而是对思想政治教育学科本质属性的理论表达

glossary.explanation: A concept Xi Jinping put forward at the National Education Conference in September 2024, listed first among the traits of a leading education country. It refers to the capacity of ideological and political education and work to guide values, direction and consensus.
The Chinese academic discipline and practice of teaching political theory, values and morality in schools and through Party work. "Sizheng" is its common short form.
The stated fundamental task of Chinese education: building moral character while training people, with the aim of producing builders and successors of socialism.
A strategic goal set out in official documents, including the 2024–2035 plan, to make China a global leader in education by 2035.
The official term for China's path to modernization under Party leadership, presented as distinct from Western models.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal of restoring China's national strength and international standing, closely associated with Xi Jinping's "Chinese Dream".

t: The meaning and key points of strengthening ideals and convictions in building a leading country in education
zh: 教育强国建设背景下坚定理想信念的内涵意蕴与着力要点
source: Ideological and Theoretical Education (思想理论教育), 2025 no. 6
paras: Taking its cue from Xi Jinping's September 2024 speech at the National Education Conference, this article asks why young students' ideals and convictions must be strengthened in building a leading country in education, what those ideals and convictions contain, and how to strengthen them. Liao Xiaoqin argues that firm ideals and convictions are the core of ideological and political guidance in this project and a source of strength for building a strong country and achieving the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

The article has three parts. The first sets out the strategic value of strengthening ideals and convictions. The second traces how their content has been formulated in Party discourse, from "two" and "three" beliefs to "four". The third proposes four key working points. It draws mainly on Xi Jinping's speeches and Party documents, including the resolution on the Party's century of struggle and the decision of the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024).

Liao identifies three kinds of strategic value: guarding national ideological security in a setting of "two overall situations", training builders and successors of socialism with Chinese characteristics, and providing spiritual support for national rejuvenation. On content, the author says that since the 18th Party Congress (2012) the formula has grown into four elements: faith in Marxism and communism, conviction in socialism with Chinese characteristics, trust in the Communist Party of China, and confidence in the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. In Liao's reading, trust in the Party is the core that binds these into a composite spiritual system. The proposed working points are to ground the effort in Chinese modernization, to make fostering patriotism the first task, to teach differently by age group and audience while coordinating family, school and society, and to build regular institutional mechanisms, including online education and measures against online ideological risks.

Liao concludes that ideals and convictions must be anchored in the practice of Chinese modernization and in daily life, and must be matched to students' stages of development, if they are to take firm hold. Education is presented as the means of ensuring that each generation of young people takes up the task of national rejuvenation. Read the original if you want a detailed account of how current Party discourse frames ideals-and-convictions education for students, including the "four beliefs" formula and the proposed institutional measures.
quoteEn: The primary task of strengthening ideals and convictions is to cultivate deep patriotic feeling.
quoteZh: 坚定理想信念的首要任务是厚植爱国主义情怀

glossary.explanation: A goal set out in official documents of building a country with a strong education system, which the article reads as both a country strong in education and one made strong through education.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal of restoring China's national strength and international standing, linked to the centenary targets of 2021 and 2049.
The official term for China's own path to modernization, set out in Party documents since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
An official formulation referring to the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation and to profound changes in the world unseen in a century.

t: A cultural interpretation of making ideals-and-convictions education regular and institutionalised
zh: 理想信念教育常态化制度化的文化阐释
source: Ideological and Theoretical Education (Sixiang lilun jiaoyu), 2025 no. 6
paras: The Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) called for making education in ideals and convictions regular and institutionalised. Han Liying asks what this means when read through culture rather than administration. The article argues that the aim is to turn faith in Marxism, the lofty ideal of communism and the common ideal of socialism with Chinese characteristics into a "spiritual atmosphere" present everywhere, and into values people hold without consciously noticing them.

The article is organised in three parts. The first sets out the cultural context: the "great changes unseen in a century", Chinese modernization and the Two Integrations, and the Party's century of struggle. The second analyses the cultural meaning of "regularisation" and of "institutionalisation" separately. The third proposes cultural strategies, built on traditional culture, everyday life and institutional mechanisms.

Han's central move is to place regularisation in three "normal states": the historical normal of reform and opening to the outside world, daily life, and the course of a human life. Ideals should be forged through history and national-condition education, applied "at all times, in all places, in all matters", and kept up through life stages, with the limited individual life given meaning by service to society. Institutionalisation is treated as a value-bearing process: citing Marx and Engels, Han argues that institutions serve and free people rather than restrict them, raise the efficiency and quality of education through supervision and accountability, and work through an institutional culture that follows the Confucian tradition of moral guidance over coercion.

The strategies proposed are threefold. First, deepen the foundation of belief with fine traditional Chinese culture, revolutionary culture and advanced socialist culture, through cultural cognition, innovation, ritual experience and environment. Second, root the work in daily life, so that people's material and spiritual needs are met and their sense of happiness and of gain grows. Third, build three mechanisms: education and guidance (theory, history and national-condition education), practice-based cultivation, and cultural influence. Read the original if you study ideological and political education in China and want to see how Party educational policy is justified through cultural, Confucian and Marxist references.)
quoteEn: The overall value of institutions lies in serving people rather than restricting them, and in fulfilling people's freedom rather than limiting it.
quoteZh: 制度的整体价值在于服务人而非限制人，在于成就人的自由而非限制人的自由。

glossary.explanation: The official term for China's path of modernization under Party leadership, presented as distinct from Western models.
Xi Jinping's formula of combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture.

glossary.zh: 世界百年未有之大变局
glossary.pinyin: shìjiè bǎinián wèi yǒu zhī dà biànjú
glossary.en: great changes unseen in a century
glossary.explanation: An official phrase for the current shifts in the global balance of power, technology and order.

t: Ideological and political education large models: generative logic, core meaning and practical application
zh: 思政大模型：生成逻辑、内核要义与实践运用
source: Ideological and Theoretical Education (思想理论教育), 2025 no. 6
paras: Following the global spread of ChatGPT from 2022 and the release of the Chinese model DeepSeek in January 2025, Cui and Chen ask how large-model AI can be built for, and used in, ideological and political education. They propose a specialised "ideological and political large model" (sizheng damoxing) and argue that clarifying how it is generated, what it is and how it can be applied would help move it from theoretical idea to practice.

The article has three parts. The first sets out how such a model is generated, through four components: ideological and political education big data, suitable algorithms, strong computing power and a performance orientation. The second defines the model, its characteristics and its functions. The third turns to practical use in data integration, interaction and teaching methods. The authors draw on examples of educational models in other fields and on Marx's remarks on machines.

A central move is that data and algorithms are not neutral. The authors argue that data carry the ideology of those who produce them, so training material must be screened to remove content at odds with the educational value orientation. Algorithms are likewise an extension of human will, so they should be designed under Marxist guidance and keep the model within the value bounds of ideological and political education. The model is defined as a specialised tool combining general and professional intelligence. Its stated characteristics are ideological character, human-like intelligence, tool character and progressive learning, and it remains dependent on people and cannot replace educators. Three functions follow: integrating data into one model-based resource base, sustained dialogue, and giving educators technical skills.

For practice, the authors propose merging separate databases into an integrated intelligent resource base. They suggest discursive, heuristic, simulated and scene-based interaction, with each learner in effect having a personal tutor. They also propose three teaching methods: an "intelligent learning companion", a "virtual expert" system and multimodal teaching that converts between text, audio, video and images. The authors present these as ways to overcome the technical barriers educators face with new technologies and to advance the digital-intelligent transformation of ideological and political education. Read the original if you want a detailed conceptual framework for AI in Chinese ideological and political education, including how its ideological requirements are built into the technical design.
quoteEn: The ideological and political large model always needs human drive as its \"switch\"; it is not an autonomous, active individual, and still less can it fully replace the role of the educator.
quoteZh: 思政大模型始终需要人的驱动作为“开关”，并非是一个自主能动的个体，更不能完全替代教育者的角色。

glossary.explanation: The system of teaching in schools, universities and other institutions that conveys the Party's ideology, political stance and moral values. It is a discipline and a practical field in China.
The authors' term for a large AI model built specifically for ideological and political education, trained on that field's data and aligned with mainstream ideology.

t: The connotation, essence and enhancement path of the ideological and political guiding force of education
zh: 论思政引领力的内涵、实质与提升路径
source: Journal of Ideological and Theoretical Education (思想理论教育导刊), 2025 no. 5
paras: Xi Jinping's speech at the National Education Conference in September 2024 listed six defining features of a strong education nation, with ideological and political guiding force (sizheng yinlingli) placed first. Cao Jinlong takes up what this concept means, what it is in essence, and how it can be strengthened. The article argues that it is a systemic, collective force generated across all links of education, and that it is in essence the guiding force of socialist ideology realised in education.

The article is organised in three parts. The first clarifies the concept through a linguistic and conceptual analysis of "ideology and politics" and of "guiding force", borrowing the idea of force from physics. The second sets out its spiritual essence, tracing the Party's tradition of treating political work as a "lifeline", the political character of education, and the question of ideological security. The third proposes a path of improvement built on three questions: who exerts the force, on whom, and how.

Cao contends that the concept should not be reduced to the force of ideological and political theory courses, or to the discipline of ideological and political education, since other courses and disciplines, and even support staff, also convey the Party's values. Drawing on the idea that force requires a source, a target and conditions, Cao defines it as the combined capacity of educators to lead learners to accept Marxist guidance and socialist institutions. In Cao's account, the proletariat openly acknowledges education's political nature, unlike the bourgeoisie, which is said to conceal it. The article describes schools as a front line of ideological work, where hostile forces compete for young people, so that winning youth requires strong guiding force.

For the path forward, Cao calls for collective action by theory-course teachers (the core) and other teachers, counsellors and staff (an indispensable supporting group). Guidance should be precise, responding to students' individual intellectual puzzles and practical difficulties. Cao also calls for coordination within schools, between school, family and society, and between offline and online spaces, aiming to turn the internet from the "biggest variable" into the "biggest increment". Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese scholar of ideological and political education conceptualises this new official term and translates it into concrete educational practice.
quoteEn: Ideological and political guiding force is not the isolated strength of any one aspect of education, but a combined educational force formed by the systemic linkage of all of education's stages and agents.
quoteZh: 思政引领力不是教育工作中某个方面单独的力量，而是教育各个环节和各个主体之间系统联动形成的教育合力。

glossary.explanation: One of the six features of a strong education nation named by Xi Jinping in September 2024. It refers to the capacity of education to guide students' values and political orientation in line with Marxism and the Party's line.
A national goal of building a leading education system, set out at the 2024 National Education Conference as a support for national strength and rejuvenation.

t: Integrating the ideological and political "small classroom" with the social "big classroom"
zh: 融合思政教育“小课堂”和“大课堂”
paras: This newspaper commentary asks how ideological and political theory courses in schools can become more persuasive. Qiu argues that, following Xi Jinping's call to join the classroom "small classroom" with the social "big classroom", such courses must tie theory to social reality and practice rather than rely on explanation and logic alone.

The piece has two parts. The first sets out why the integration matters. The second proposes four practical links for carrying it out, and draws on the "Great Ideological and Political Course" (da sizheng ke) initiative.

In the first part, Qiu holds that integration helps teachers explain principles in a deeper, more thorough and livelier way, because students experience and reflect on them themselves. Qiu also says the achievements of socialism with Chinese characteristics, especially since the 18th Party Congress (2012), supply content, and that local examples make courses more credible. Integration is further said to help students understand national and popular conditions, so that they become capable successors to the cause of national rejuvenation.
