The four links are: widening teachers' horizons, for instance through visits to archives, Party history museums and achievement exhibitions; expanding practical teaching through fieldwork and patriotic education sites; coordinating schools and society under Party committee leadership; and using information technology, such as VR tours of Party memorial halls and virtual battlefields.

Qiu concludes that a course delivered across the country, and not only in lecture halls, will build firmer convictions, deepen national identity and foster patriotic feeling in students. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official guidance on the "Great Ideological and Political Course" is translated into teaching methods.
quoteEn: The "Great Ideological and Political Course" is great in that it is a major social course and a systematic project; schools alone are not enough, and all sectors of society must take part.
quoteZh: “大思政课”，大就大在是一门社会大课，是一项系统工程，光靠学校还不够，需要社会各方面共同参与。

glossary.explanation: A policy concept promoted by Xi Jinping that extends ideological and political education beyond the classroom into society and practice, involving multiple social actors.
Compulsory courses in Chinese schools and universities that teach Marxism, Party history and official political theory.
The official name for China's current political and economic system and its guiding theory.

t: Laying a solid cultural foundation for ideological and political education
zh: 筑牢思想政治教育的文化之基
paras: This short commentary, published in the China Social Sciences Today in August 2025, asks how ideological and political education can be given a firmer cultural footing. Feng and Sun argue that it must be guided by Xi Jinping's cultural thought, so as to deepen its theoretical depth, cultural thickness and practical effectiveness and cultivate a new generation able to carry the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

The article is organised around three requirements: upholding the fundamental task of fostering virtue through education (立德树人), adhering to the Two Integrations, and cultivating the core socialist values. Each is treated as a way of linking Party ideology with Chinese cultural tradition.

On the first point, the authors say that Xi's cultural thought answers the questions of whom to train, how and for whom. They call for a shift from 'propaganda and indoctrination' towards 'value guidance' and 'cultural initiative', and for an educational system that unites political, cultural and contemporary dimensions. On the second, they hold that combining Marxism with China's concrete realities and with fine traditional culture makes the teaching more relevant, humane and persuasive. On the third, they see the core socialist values as drawing on traditional ethics, revolutionary culture and socialist culture, and want them to run through the whole teaching process, from understanding to habitual conduct.

The authors conclude that, on the new journey, schools should build a 'big ideological and political course' pattern. It would integrate Marxist principles, traditional culture and the spirit of the Communist Party, strengthen the sense of community of the Chinese nation, and supply ideological and cultural support for building a modern socialist country. Read the original if you want a concise example of how current Chinese ideological education is justified in terms of Xi Jinping's cultural thought.
quoteEn: Ideological and political education is the front line of the Party's ideological work; it must be guided by Xi Jinping's cultural thought and strengthen its theoretical depth, cultural thickness and practical effectiveness.
quoteZh: 思想政治教育是党的意识形态工作的前沿阵地，必须坚持以习近平文化思想为指导，增强思想政治教育的理论深度、文化厚度和实践效度

glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's formula for combining the basic principles of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture.
A body of Xi Jinping's statements on culture, publicly articulated in 2023, covering cultural confidence, socialist culture and the combination of Marxism with traditional culture.
The stated fundamental task of Chinese education: moral cultivation alongside the training of knowledge and skills.
A set of twelve values promoted officially since the 18th Party Congress (2012), at national, social and individual levels.
An official concept that extends ideological and political teaching beyond the classroom into society and practice.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's overarching national goal of restoring China's strength and international standing.

t: Promoting the connotative development of ideological and political theory courses in universities
zh: 推动高校思政课建设内涵式发展
paras: This short commentary, published in China Social Sciences Today in August 2025, asks how university ideological and political theory courses (sizheng ke) can improve in quality rather than simply expand. Wu Lili takes Xi Jinping's instruction to explain principles "deeply, thoroughly and vividly" as methodological guidance. The author argues that each of the three requirements corresponds to a distinct goal: theoretical depth, thoroughness and liveliness.

The article is organised in three parts, one for each requirement. It links them in sequence: depth is the basis of thoroughness, and both underpin liveliness. Wu draws on the integration of ideological and political education across university, secondary and primary schooling, on Marx, Lenin and Xi, and on examples from the first-year course on ideology, morality and the rule of law.

On "depth", Wu argues that university teachers should go beyond the secondary-school emphasis on memorising "what" something is. They should explain "why" through the unity of the historical and the logical, and "how it is possible" through practice, drawing on Marxist theory and on other disciplines. On "thoroughness", the author calls for teaching that responds to events, to the times and to current trends, so that students come to accept that the Party's success rests on Marxism adapted to China. On "liveliness", Wu proposes taking case material from students' everyday lives, replacing textbook and academic language with ordinary speech, and integrating mainstream discourse with the online language of students born after 2000.

Wu concludes that these three steps together raise the pertinence, appeal and sense of benefit of the courses and help students grow into well-rounded people. Teachers are urged to keep up with Party theory, with students' characteristics and with technological change. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Chinese university teaching of Marxist theory is framed methodologically.
quoteEn: To explain principles "vividly" means promoting the popularisation of Marxist theory and bringing it into everyday life.
quoteZh: 把道理“讲活”就是要推动马克思主义理论的通俗化与生活化

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses on Marxism, Party theory, morality and law taught at all levels of Chinese education. At universities they are run by schools of Marxism.

t: The ideological and political education functions of red literature and art
zh: 红色文艺的思想政治教育功能
paras: This short commentary from the Chinese Social Sciences Today (11 August 2025) asks what role red literature and art play in ideological and political education. Hong argues that, in the strategic context of the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation and a world undergoing changes unseen in a century, stressing these functions is a necessary requirement for developing socialism with Chinese characteristics.

The piece is organised around four functions: political guidance, the transmission of spirit, character formation and spiritual motivation. Each section is built on quotations from Xi Jinping on culture and the arts, supported by examples of novels, songs and films from different periods.

Hong contends that red literature and art, as part of Party propaganda and ideological work, strengthen political identification and help guide social thinking, showing in works why the Party and socialism with Chinese characteristics succeed. They are also presented as the vehicle for "red genes", letting younger people experience revolutionary history directly. On character, Hong cites works from the early People's Republic and the early reform and opening up period, such as the novel The Builders and the film Lushan Romance, as shaping patriotism and hard work. On motivation, the author points to the films Taking Tiger Mountain by Strategy (2014) and the Battle at Lake Changjin series (2021), which reworked earlier classics and drew audiences across generations.

Hong concludes that red literature and art give the era its backbone and take its temperature, and that they inspire the people to strive for the Chinese Dream. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated scholars currently justify the educational role of revolutionary-themed culture.
quoteEn: Red literature and art forge the backbone of the era and take its temperature; through art they celebrate and shape the era, inspiring the broad masses to strive for the realisation of the Chinese Dream.
quoteZh: 红色文艺铸就时代筋骨、把脉时代温度，用艺术讴歌和塑造了时代，激励广大人民群众为实现中国梦而奋斗。

glossary.explanation: Literary and artistic works that depict the revolutionary history, spirit and achievements of the Communist Party and the People's Republic. The category includes films, songs, novels and operas.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central official goal of the Party, in which China is to regain strength and international standing, usually linked to the Chinese Dream.
An official metaphor for the revolutionary ideals, spirit and traditions of the Party, which are meant to be handed down to later generations.
A slogan associated with Xi Jinping since 2012, describing national rejuvenation and the people's prosperity.
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world, begun in China in 1978.

t: Advancing the reform and innovation of ideological and political courses across universities, secondary and primary schools
zh: 推进大中小学思政课改革创新
paras: Published in the China Social Sciences Today in August 2025, this commentary by Yang Tianmei and Cao Sheng takes up how ideological and political courses (sizheng ke) can be reformed as a single integrated system running from primary school to university. The authors argue that such integrated reform and innovation is a key step in carrying out the fundamental task of fostering virtue through education. They rely throughout on Xi Jinping's statements on the subject.

The piece has two parts. The first sets out the theoretical significance of integrated reform, divided into an epistemological and an axiological dimension. The second proposes seven practical paths: leadership and communication mechanisms, cooperative working mechanisms, integrated curriculum building, integrated teaching staff development, integrated teaching and research, resource sharing, and a leading role for university schools of Marxism.

On the theoretical side, the authors say integration must follow Marxist epistemology and the dialectic of practice and cognition, matching course content to students' cognitive development at each stage. They describe the sequence as moral feeling in primary school, ideological foundations in middle school, political literacy in high school and a sense of mission at university. On the value side, they link integration to answering whom education trains, how and for whom, and to producing new-era people who can shoulder national rejuvenation. They also tie it to the strong ideological and political guidance expected of a Chinese-style education powerhouse. In practice, the authors call for joint planning by education authorities, university Marxism schools and primary and secondary schools. They propose a research direction on integration within the Marxist theory discipline, and the recruitment of senior school teachers as postgraduate supervisors. They also want training from multidisciplinary university staff for schools short of teachers in areas such as law and mental health. Other proposals include collective lesson preparation, use of local red-culture resources, links between teacher promotion and participation, varied teaching methods, and shared courses and practice bases.

The authors conclude that universities, with their talent, theoretical, disciplinary, curricular, teaching and resource advantages, should lead integrated construction. In their view this would make the courses more targeted and effective, and would help train people who are reliable for the Party, patriotic and ready for national rejuvenation. Read the original if you want a concise statement of the institutional measures currently proposed for linking Party-line ideological education across school levels.
quoteEn: Integrated reform and innovation of ideological and political courses across universities, secondary and primary schools is an inevitable requirement for achieving the fundamental task of fostering virtue through education.
quoteZh: 大中小学思政课一体化改革创新是实现立德树人根本任务的必然要求。

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses in Marxist theory, Party policy, morality and law taught at all levels of Chinese education. They are treated as the main channel of ideological education.
A long-standing educational goal that the Party has presented since the 18th Party Congress (2012) as the fundamental task of education: moral formation alongside knowledge.
A phrase in Party discourse for young people expected to be politically loyal, patriotic and capable of taking part in national rejuvenation.

glossary.literal: great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The official goal of restoring China's strength and international standing, central to Party narratives since the 2010s.

t: Strengthening ideological and political guidance to empower university education
zh: 以强大思政引领力赋能高校育人工作
paras: This newspaper commentary, published in Guangming Daily on 30 July 2025, asks how universities can build what Xi Jinping at the 2024 National Education Conference listed first among the six attributes of a strong education nation: the capacity for ideological and political guidance. Wang Yin argues that universities should develop an ideological and political work system that keeps pace with the times, resonates with young people and connects with practice.

The piece has three parts. It first sets out the meaning of this guiding capacity, then its role in the university education system, and finally concrete measures for running socialist universities with Chinese characteristics.

Wang presents the capacity as continuing the Party's tradition of treating ideological and political work as a "lifeline", as expressing the political, popular and strategic attributes of education, and as answering the challenges of a world undergoing changes unseen in a century. In Wang's account it supports the fundamental task of fostering virtue through education, secures the Party's overall leadership of universities, and widens channels of value guidance through ideological and political theory courses, "curriculum ideology and politics" and a second classroom of practice.

Wang calls for university Party committees to take political responsibility and improve the "big ideological and political" pattern of work, advancing the reform of whole-staff, whole-process and all-round education. Wang also proposes teaching Party theory in depth, training teachers jointly, using student organisations and Party activities, and expanding social practice. Read the original if you want a concise example of how a university Party official frames ideological and political education within the drive to build a strong education nation.
quoteEn: Ideological and political courses should use a grand historical perspective and grand logic to explain the Party's innovative theory in depth, thoroughly and vividly, and, through unified teaching standards, joint teaching-research design and integration with specialist subjects, bring specialist courses and ideological and political education into resonance.
quoteZh: 思政课应坚持用大历史、大逻辑讲深讲透讲活党的创新理论，通过统一教学标准、协同教研设计、专业融合渗透等路径，实现专业课程与思政教育的同频共振。

glossary.explanation: A phrase presented in Party documents as the fundamental task of education: cultivating moral character alongside knowledge and skills.
An approach that embeds ideological and political content in specialist, non-political courses so that they work in step with dedicated political theory courses.

glossary.literal: education by all staff, throughout the whole process, in all respects
glossary.explanation: A reform framework requiring all university staff to take part in educating students throughout their studies and across all areas of campus life.

t: Building a high-calibre corps of ideological and political theory teachers for the new era
zh: 建设新时代高素质思政课教师队伍
paras: This commentary, published in the People's Daily on 30 July 2025, asks how to build a high-quality teaching force for ideological and political theory courses in schools and universities. Li argues that such teachers are central to the fundamental task of fostering virtue through education. The author calls the work systematic and strategic, to be pursued through four tasks: strengthening political development, raising professional ability, promoting collaborative education and improving evaluation.

The piece opens by placing teachers within the three questions of education: whom to cultivate, how, and for whom. It then sets out four requirements, each framed as a "checkpoint": belief, training, the educational ecosystem and orientation. Li draws throughout on Xi Jinping's statements on these courses and on his stated qualities for their teachers.

Li contends that these teachers must train socialist builders and successors who support Party leadership and the socialist system, joining theoretical teaching with value guidance and conveying belief and ideals as well as knowledge. In practice, Li calls for putting political criteria first in selecting, training and employing teachers and for study of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. The author also proposes full-cycle training from entry to career growth, research projects and teaching platforms, and clearer duties and career paths inside schools, together with school-local and inter-school cooperation. Evaluation should abandon the fixation on papers and titles, stress classroom quality and students' ideological growth, and make teachers' ethics the first criterion.

Li concludes that a corps of teachers strong in politics, theory and teaching craft is the way to ensure the fundamental task of fostering virtue is carried out, and that it should lead students to align personal development with national strength and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want a concise, official-style statement of current Party expectations for ideological and political theory teachers in China.
quoteEn: In the classroom, ideological and political theory teachers spread not only knowledge but also belief and ideals, using their own political stance, moral conduct and personal charisma to lead young students to a deep grasp of the decisive significance of the "Two Establishes".
quoteZh: 思政课教师在课堂中不仅传播知识，更传播信仰、传递理想，用自己的政治立场、道德风范和人格魅力，引导青年学生深刻领悟“两个确立”的决定性意义

glossary.explanation: A long-standing educational concept that Party documents since the 18th Party Congress (2012) present as the fundamental task of education: moral and political formation alongside knowledge.
Compulsory courses in Marxism, Party theory and moral and political education taught in Chinese schools and universities, often abbreviated as sizheng ke.

glossary.explanation: A central Party goal of restoring China's national strength and international standing, associated with the Chinese Dream.

t: Expanding ideological and political courses through walking
st: On "walking" ideological and political courses as a route to educating new-era youth
zh: 用行走扩容思政课
paras: Writing in the 80th anniversary year of victory in the War of Resistance against Japan (2025), Zhang Yanqing presents the "walking" ideological and political course as an important way of forging new-era youth. In this commentary, "reading ten thousand books" meets "travelling ten thousand miles": students learn at sites such as Yan'an, the Nanjing Massacre memorial and the Marco Polo Bridge. Zhang, citing Xi Jinping, argues that such courses link the small classroom of theory to the big classroom of society.

The piece is short and organised around three tasks. It first discusses red resources, then excellent traditional Chinese culture, and finally the teaching design and support structures that make these courses effective. Examples include Jinggangshan, Zunyi and Xibaipo, and Renmin University of China's course along Beijing's Central Axis.

Zhang's core argument is that red sites turn patriotic education from slogans into lasting spiritual imprints, and that cultural sites and intangible heritage make tradition a living skill rather than a museum exhibit. The author insists that these visits must not be superficial sightseeing. Instead, a loop from the first classroom to the second and back should join theory, teaching topics and practice. Zhang proposes three supports: joint "big classroom" bases such as laboratories and university history museums, digital platforms, and a "big teaching force" including specialists from various fields and local experts.

Zhang concludes that growing Party and social support for ideological and political courses gives this model a strong basis. In the author's view it extends knowledge and cultivates a lifelong commitment to the cause of socialism with Chinese characteristics. Read the original if you want a brief, official-style example of how practice-based ideological and political education is promoted in Chinese schools.
quoteEn: The essence of ideological and political courses is to reason things through.
quoteZh: 思政课的本质是讲道理。

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses in Chinese schools and universities that teach Marxism, Party theory, history and socialist values. The Party treats them as central to moral and political education.
A teaching format that takes students out of the classroom to visit historical, cultural and other sites. It combines lectures, social practice and open discussion.
Sites, relics, stories and memories linked to the Chinese revolution and the Communist Party's history, used in patriotic and political education.

t: Teachers of ideological and political courses should practise the spirit of educators
zh: 思政课教师要做教育家精神的践行者
paras: Chen Juan, writing in Guangming Daily on 25 July 2025, asks how teachers of ideological and political courses can turn the "spirit of educators" into daily practice. Chen argues that the six dimensions of that spirit set out by Xi Jinping closely match his "six requirements" for such teachers. Because the teaching staff is the key to these courses, Chen calls for building the teacher corps as a foundational task in the new era.

The short commentary has two parts. The first proposes institutional measures to strengthen teachers' conscious commitment to the spirit of educators. The second sets out how teachers should apply it in teaching, research and social service.

On institutions, Chen calls for making the spirit of educators a required part of teacher training, in a regular and institutionalised way. Chen also wants it written into evaluation, including qualification, hiring, promotion and awards, with teaching outcomes and professional ethics as the main standards. Chen would end the fixation on scores, diplomas, papers and titles, and would give more weight to teaching and teaching research. Resources should include priority development of the Marxist theory discipline, policy support for teachers and publicity for model teachers. For practice, Chen urges more inspiring and interactive teaching methods, including new technologies. Research should address major problems of national rejuvenation and feed into the classroom. Teachers should also take part in whole-staff moral education, policy research and public theory outreach.

Chen concludes that teachers should uphold virtue in conduct, scholarship and teaching, and become firm believers in and practitioners of the spirit of educators. Chen presents this as essential to cultivating people for the Party and the country. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official discourse links Xi Jinping's remarks on educators to concrete training, evaluation and teaching measures for ideological and political course teachers.
quoteEn: The key to running ideological and political courses well lies in the teachers.
quoteZh: 办好思政课的关键在教师。

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses in Marxist theory, Party doctrine and moral education taught at all levels of Chinese schools and universities.

A formulation Xi Jinping put forward in 2023, describing the ideal qualities of teachers: ideals and convictions, moral sentiment, wisdom in teaching, dedication, benevolence and the pursuit of promoting the Way.

t: Strengthening the guiding power of the "Great Ideological and Political Course" through a more complete system
st: Practice at Wuhan University of Technology
zh: 以体系完善增强 “大思政课”引领力
paras: This short commentary, published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today on 24 July 2025, asks how a university can build out the "Great Ideological and Political Course" (da sizheng ke) so that ideological and political education becomes more persuasive and influential. Sun and Shen, both from the School of Marxism at Wuhan University of Technology, present their own institution's practice as an answer. They argue that the course should be run with an open door, mobilising resources beyond the classroom, and that this serves the fundamental task of fostering virtue and nurturing talent.

The article is organised around three areas of work at the university, followed by a section on teaching staff. These are holding the classroom as the main front, building distinctive ideological-education brands, and using society as a large classroom. A short closing passage commits the university to continued development under the same headings.

On classroom teaching, the authors describe ties between national policy and students' daily lives, rural revitalisation cases, virtual-simulation reproductions of red memorials, and classroom debates on topics such as the key to common prosperity and Chinese modernization. They also report that courses in all disciplines are being aligned with ideological education, citing a physics-based project approved by the Ministry of Education in 2023. On brands and practice, they list the "one course, one brand" activities, cultural programmes, platforms combining innovation, volunteering or the arts with ideological education, a practice base with a hospital, and a WeChat column. On society as classroom, they cite student volunteer teams, visits to factories, bridges and tunnels tied to the university's industry strengths, and the "three goings, three learnings" red-themed projects. Training sessions, collective lesson preparation and ethics lectures for teachers are also described.

The authors conclude that building a high-quality "Great Ideological and Political Course" is now unavoidable for the university's reform of ideological teaching and a key means of raising a new generation able to carry the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. The university plans to keep the campus as the main front, extend education into society and strengthen its brands. Read the original if you want a concrete, institution-level example of how a Chinese university reports implementing the "Great Ideological and Political Course" in classrooms, practice activities and community settings.
quoteEn: Building a high-quality "Great Ideological and Political Course" has become the necessary path for innovative change in the university's ideological and political teaching, and also an important lever for cultivating new-era people who can shoulder the great task of national rejuvenation.
quoteZh: 高质量构建“大思政课”已经成为学校思政教学创新变革的必经之路，也是培育新时代能够担当民族复兴大任新人的重要抓手。

glossary.explanation: A policy concept promoted since 2021 that extends ideological and political education beyond the classroom into society, practice and online spaces, drawing on social resources.
The officially stated fundamental task of Chinese education, combining moral and ideological formation with the cultivation of knowledge and skills.
The Party's official term for China's own path of modernization, set out prominently since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
An official goal of socialism with Chinese characteristics, meaning prosperity shared by all, which has been emphasised in policy since the early 2020s.

t: Making ideological and political theory courses more appealing and engaging
st: A review of Professor Li Xia's "Research on Innovating the Teaching Discourse System of University Ideological and Political Theory Courses"
zh: 让思政课教学更有吸引力感染力
zhSub: 评李霞教授《高校思政课教学话语体系创新研究》
paras: This is a book review by Zhang Yanguo of Li Xia's Research on Innovating the Teaching Discourse System of University Ideological and Political Theory Courses (China Social Sciences Press, April 2024). Zhang holds that ideological and political theory courses touch students only if their teaching discourse is innovative and carries intellectual force. In Zhang's view, the book makes a new and useful contribution to that task.

Zhang reports that the book is organised around the questions of who teaches these courses, what kind of course to teach and how to teach it well. It sets four goals for discourse innovation: ideological quality, theoretical quality, affinity and relevance. It draws on a survey of university students' expectations and on analysis of the teaching language in prize-winning demonstration lessons.

According to the review, Li defines each goal and pairs it with a unifying principle. Ideological quality is the soul of teaching, theoretical quality its foundation, affinity its precondition and relevance its focus on students' real concerns. From the survey and case analysis Li distils "six musts and six haves" for teaching language, and names problems such as the pull of diverse social trends, fragmented online information, uniform discourse and over-abstraction. Li's proposed remedy is student-centred teaching, with a model of "theory + problems + cases + classroom participation" and a dialogic dual-subject classroom. The model is illustrated with the course on the basic principles of Marxism. Zhang sees the book's novelty in its clear goals, its classroom design, its student-centred stance and its systematic method.

Zhang concludes that the book offers useful reference for improving the effectiveness of teaching discourse and for reform of both these courses and "course-embedded" ideological education. Zhang adds that some topics need deeper treatment, including how to realise the Two Integrations in class, how to use fine traditional Chinese culture, and how to make teaching more artful. Read the original if you want a brief overview of current Chinese thinking on teaching discourse in university ideological and political courses.
quoteEn: The book strives to explore the laws of teaching in university ideological and political courses and focuses on models for innovating their teaching discourse system, offering useful reference and inspiration for making that discourse more effective and for reforming both these courses and course-embedded ideological education.
quoteZh: 该书努力探索高校思政课教学规律，聚焦高校思政课教学话语体系创新模式，对提高高校思政课教学话语效力，以及思政课改革和课程思政改革提供了有益的借鉴和启示。

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses in Chinese universities that teach Marxism, Party history and official ideology. They are a central part of political education in higher education.
Xi Jinping's formula for combining Marxism's basic principles with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture.

glossary.literal: ideology and politics in the curriculum
glossary.explanation: A policy of building ideological and moral education into all university subjects, not only dedicated political courses.

t: Empowering the integrated development of ideological and political courses across university, secondary and primary schools with generative AI
zh: 以生成式人工智能赋能大中小学思政课一体化建设
paras: This short commentary from People's Daily asks how generative artificial intelligence can support the integrated development of ideological and political courses (sizheng ke) across university, secondary and primary schools. Wang and Long argue that, amid rapid AI progress and educational digitalisation, the technology can strengthen resource integration, practice settings and evaluation, and so raise the quality and effectiveness of ideological and political education.

The article opens by citing Xi Jinping's call to treat integrated course development as an important project. It then takes three areas in turn, each following the same pattern: current difficulties, followed by AI-based remedies. These are a resource base covering all school stages, a blended virtual-and-physical space for practical education, and a whole-process evaluation system.

On resources, the authors identify repetition and weak sequencing between stages' textbooks, cases that lag behind current events, and uneven regional provision. They propose AI that analyses textbook logic, flags gaps, turns political events into stage-appropriate cases and supplies layered materials for each level. On practice, they note the lack of a stepped path from primary to university, limits of time and space for offline activities, and weak feedback. They propose simulated historical scenes and AR, VR and MR technologies, plus large-model analysis of student work. On evaluation, they criticise reliance on exam scores, the lack of tools to measure values and attitudes, and inconsistent standards across stages. They propose multimodal learning analytics, personalised diagnostic reports, a cross-stage standards converter and digital portraits of each student's development.

The authors conclude that such a data-driven, intelligent, continuously improving system would support personalised and differentiated teaching and help realise the educational goals of integrated courses. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official commentary frames AI applications in Chinese ideological and political education.
quoteEn: The deep development and efficient use of course resources that cut across school stages and integrate disciplines is the foundation for the continued deepening of integrated ideological and political course development across university, secondary and primary schools.
quoteZh: 跨学段、融学科的课程资源深度开发与高效利用，是大中小学思政课一体化建设得以持续深化的基础。

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses in Marxist theory, Party ideology, morality and law taught at all school levels in China, intended to shape students' values.

t: Methods and pathways for strengthening the guiding power of ideological and political education
zh: 增强思政引领力的方法路径
paras: Xie Ruijin, a researcher at a provincial theory research centre and Party secretary of Anhui University of Chinese Medicine, asks how universities can strengthen their "guiding power" in ideological and political education. The commentary, published in Guangming Daily in July 2025, starts from Xi Jinping's statement at the National Education Conference (2024) that a leading education power must have six strengths, of which ideological and political guiding power comes first. Xie argues that universities should work on several fronts at once to raise this power and to lay an ideological foundation for educating a new generation able to carry the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

The piece sets the context as a period of accelerating global change, continuing struggle in the ideological sphere and increasingly diverse thinking among young students. It then proposes four pathways: strengthening Party leadership as an organisational guarantee, promoting the spirit of educators, making good use of the "great ideological and political course", and strengthening digital empowerment. Each is given a short section with concrete measures.

On leadership, Xie calls for Party committees to oversee all school work, for the president responsibility system under Party committee leadership to be improved, and for the ideological work responsibility system to be strictly applied so that the Party holds leadership, management and discourse power over campus ideology. Xie also proposes collaboration among school, family and society. On teachers, Xie urges that political identification with Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era be deepened, that professional ethics become the first criterion in evaluation, and that results in moral education carry more weight in promotion and awards.

For the "great ideological and political course", Xie advocates taking classes out into society through Red education bases and rural revitalisation sites, integrating the Party's innovative theory into all ideological and political courses, and promoting "curriculum ideology and politics" across subject courses. On digital tools, Xie calls for online courses, virtual simulation and big-data platforms, while stressing that technology should raise quality and not replace teachers, and that educators should use technology without being ruled by it. Read the original if you want a concise example of how a university Party secretary presents the practical measures linked to the "education power" agenda in ideological and political work.
quoteEn: The aim of digital empowerment is to improve quality and efficiency, not simply to replace; its core lies in the intellectual resonance and value identification of teachers and students.
quoteZh: 数字赋能的目标是提质增效，而非简单替代，其核心在于师生的思想共鸣与价值认同

glossary.explanation: The first of six strengths that Xi Jinping said in 2024 a leading education power should have. It refers to the capacity of ideological and political education to steer students' values and beliefs.
A concept promoted by Xi Jinping that extends ideological and political teaching beyond the classroom into society, practice and online platforms, drawing on wider teaching resources.

glossary.literal: ideology and politics in the curriculum
glossary.explanation: The practice of integrating ideological and political content into non-political subject courses, so that all teaching contributes to value formation.
A set of six qualities for teachers set out by Xi Jinping, including patriotic ideals, moral example, teaching wisdom and a vocation to serve.

t: Focusing on the cultivation of innovative talent and strengthening science–education collaboration in nurturing people
zh: 聚焦创新型人才培养 强化科教协同育人
paras: Xi Yinglun, writing in Red Flag Manuscripts in 2025, takes up the question of how universities can train a large, well-structured and high-quality corps of innovative talent. Starting from Xi Jinping's remarks that science and technology innovation depends on talent, talent on education, and the three are mutually supporting, the author argues that universities should build a mechanism of science–education collaboration in nurturing people. The stated aim is to provide talent support for Chinese modernization.

The commentary is organised in three parts. The first concerns ideological guidance as the foundation of collaborative education. The second concerns improving the system of cultivation by strengthening students' capabilities. The third concerns practice-oriented paths: institutional innovation, platform building and resource integration. Each part opens with quotations from Xi Jinping and then sets out measures for universities.

In the first part, Xi Yinglun contends that universities must put serving the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation first. They should use Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era to shape students' convictions. They should also link education to national needs such as breakthroughs on 'choke-point' technologies and the carbon peaking and neutrality goals. The second part proposes a progressive curriculum framework running from required courses to project practice to commercialisation of results. It also proposes industry-supplied problem banks, project-based training with real enterprise tasks, and multidimensional assessment of students' teamwork and sense of social responsibility. The third part calls for greater autonomy for research teams, counting students' innovation results in teachers' performance appraisal, platforms co-built with enterprises, an 'innovation resource list' for shared equipment and data, and 'open competition' pilots with third-party evaluation.

The author concludes that integrating education, science and technology, and talent development, and clearing the 'last mile' of training innovative talent, requires reform of science and technology management and better coordination of innovation resources. The piece is a practical policy proposal from a university administrator, written in the Party's official vocabulary. Read the original if you want a concrete example of how Party-school and university administrators translate Xi Jinping's statements on education, science and talent into institutional measures.
quoteEn: Universities should integrate successful cases of the great transformations of the new era and the vivid practice of high-level scientific and technological self-reliance into ideological and political education, tell the innovation stories of the new era well, and stir young students' enthusiasm for striving and their sense of responsibility.
quoteZh: 高校应将新时代伟大变革成功案例与高水平科技自立自强生动实践融入学校思想政治教育，讲好新时代的创新故事，激发青年学生的奋斗热情与担当精神。

glossary.explanation: The official concept of China's path to modernization, promoted by the Party leadership since 2021 as distinct from Western models.

t: Opening a new chapter in ideological and political education for the new era
zh: 开创新时代思政教育新局面
paras: Wang Chengbin, writing in the China Social Sciences Today in July 2025, asks how universities can open a new chapter in ideological and political education in the new era. The commentary takes its cue from Xi Jinping's May 2024 instruction on school ideological and political courses and his remarks at the 2025 Two Sessions. Wang argues that the "Big Ideological and Political Course" is the answer. It joins the ideological and political "small classroom" to the "big classroom" of society, and Wang presents it as a new form of university ideological and political education.

The article builds its account of "Big Ideological and Political Course" construction around four components. Ideological and political courses are the core and foundation, social practice is the extension, innovation and entrepreneurship is the upgrade, and the "second classroom" transcript is the support and guarantee. Each component gets its own section, and Xi Jinping's statements are quoted throughout as the basis for the argument. A short closing section sets out three requirements for future work.

On the core courses, Wang calls on teachers to move away from one-way indoctrination towards respect for students' agency. They should match what students need with what is supplied, tie content to Party theory and national strategy, and use AI, big data and virtual reality to create immersive teaching settings. On practice, Wang grounds the case in the Marxist view that practice is the basis of knowledge, and calls for students to learn in society and then turn what they learn into courses for others. Nanjing Normal University's practice-results transformation centre is given as an example. On innovation and entrepreneurship, Wang proposes a "reaching the sky and standing on the ground" principle. Programmes should serve national strategy and high-quality development, and should also build on each university's own disciplinary strengths. The "second classroom" transcript quantifies student performance in ideological and political activities, and Wang assigns it evaluation, resource-integration and collaborative functions.

Wang concludes that "Big Ideological and Political Course" construction must achieve "three fits": with national development strategy, with the university's overall plan, and with students' growth needs. It should be built into disciplinary development, talent training and social service, and delivered in a tailored, lifelong and close-at-hand way. The stated aim is to nurture a new generation who are reliable for the Party, patriotic and equal to the task of the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want a concise, practice-oriented example of how a university Party leader frames ideological and political education reform under Xi Jinping's guidance.
quoteEn: The content-based development of the "Big Ideological and Political Course" will certainly continue, constantly opening up a new chapter for university ideological and political education in the new era.
quoteZh: “大思政课”内涵式建设必将持续发展，不断开创新时代高校思政教育新局面

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted since 2021 that extends ideological and political teaching beyond the classroom into social practice and real-world settings.
Compulsory courses in Chinese schools and universities on Marxism, Party theory and socialist values.
A university record that logs and scores students' extracurricular activities, such as social practice and volunteering, alongside their academic grades.
The official goal, stressed since 2017, of growth driven by innovation and efficiency rather than scale alone.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's long-term national goal of restoring China's strength and international standing.

t: Strategic outlook on AI empowering the transformation of higher education
zh: 人工智能赋能高等教育转型的战略前瞻
paras: Zhang Fuqing, writing as a university Party secretary in a newspaper commentary first published in China Social Sciences Today on 9 July 2025, asks how artificial intelligence can drive the transformation of Chinese higher education. Zhang argues that AI, the core driver of what the article calls the Fourth Industrial Revolution, is reshaping educational concepts and models. In this reading, AI-enabled higher education has become a source of competitive advantage and a key variable in moving China from a large education country to a strong one.

The piece opens with Xi Jinping's statements on education and AI, then proceeds through four headed sections: leading the digital transformation of higher education; reconstructing the higher education ecosystem; fostering a distinctive 'Chinese paradigm'; and steering the strategy of building China into a leading education power. It closes with role-specific recommendations for education administrators, universities, teachers and students.

Zhang's central claim is that AI changes higher education at every level, and that this change should be directed by national strategy. On the ecosystem, the author points to new teaching models built on platforms such as the National Smart Education Platform for Higher Education, personalised learning, multi-dimensional and data-driven evaluation, and more refined university management. On the 'Chinese paradigm', Zhang holds that AI must serve national strategic goals, uphold the socialist orientation of education and the fundamental task of fostering virtue through education, and promote educational equity. The Ministry of Education's 'MOOCs in the West' programme is offered as an example of digital technology serving equity and of the advantages of the new type of whole-nation system.

Zhang concludes with proposals for each actor. Administrators should draw up strategic plans, set goals and rules for research, talent training and ethical governance, and create dedicated funds. Universities should adopt an 'AI+' education system. Teachers should treat AI as a 'cognitive enhancement partner' rather than a replacement, forming an 'education triangle' with students and AI. Students should build AI literacy and data-security awareness and become 'high-level AI masters'. Read the original if you want a concise example of how a Chinese university leader links AI in education to national strategy and the 2035 goal of becoming a leading education power.
quoteEn: AI-enabled higher education has become an advantage in future competition among higher education systems, and an important variable in China's drive to move from a large education country to a strong one.
quoteZh: 人工智能赋能高等教育已成为未来高等教育竞争的优势，是我国加快从教育大国向教育强国迈进的重要变量。

glossary.explanation: An official formulation of the fundamental task of education: moral and ideological formation alongside knowledge. It is stressed in Party education policy since the 18th Party Congress (2012).
A national goal set out in the 2025 Outline for Building a Leading Education Power (2024–2035), which aims to achieve this status by 2035.
A model that mobilises state and national resources behind strategic goals, usually in science, technology and major projects, combined with market mechanisms.

t: Making red resources the spiritual engine of the "great ideological and political course"
zh: 让红色资源成为“大思政课”的精神引擎
paras: Zhang asks how "red resources" (the material and spiritual legacy of the Communist Party's history) can be built into university ideological and political education. Citing the 20th Party Congress report (2022) and Xi Jinping's speech at the National Education Conference in September 2024, the author argues that doing so serves the university mission of training people for the Party and the country. It is also presented as necessary for cultivating a new generation suited to the new era.

The short commentary has three parts: the logic of integrating red culture into the "great ideological and political course", the features that make the fit possible, and practical paths for universities. It is aimed at university administrators and Party committees rather than at theorists.

On logic, Zhang describes four pairings: material with spiritual, theory with practice, historical moment with present events, and inner with outer. On features, the author finds that red resources and the course share a common basis in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, a common cultural root in traditional Chinese culture, and similar educational functions. The practical section proposes a sound institutional system with unified Party committee leadership, better coordination across stages of schooling and between school, family and society, fresh narratives that bring in the "four histories", and richer carriers such as ceremonies, campus-history materials and local red-culture tours.

Zhang concludes that red resources, used through these institutional and educational mechanisms, can strengthen students' political sensitivity and ideological commitment and help guard against major security risks. Read the original if you want a compact example of how a university Party official frames red-resource education and its practical implementation.
quoteEn: Red resources carry the emergence, development and innovation of the integration of the basic tenets of Marxism with China's specific realities.
quoteZh: 红色资源承载着马克思主义基本原理同中国具体实际相结合的发生、发展以及创新

glossary.explanation: The people, events, sites, objects and ideals associated with the history of the Communist Party and the Chinese revolution, used as material for patriotic and political education.
An approach promoted since 2021 that extends ideological and political education beyond the classroom into society, practice and online spaces.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for applying Marxism to China's conditions and updating it for the present era.
A Party education theme covering the history of the Party, of New China, of reform and opening up, and of socialist development.

t: Building a new pattern of collaborative education between ideological-political courses and curriculum-based ideological-political education
zh: 构建思政课程与课程思政协同育人新格局
paras: This short commentary, published in Guangming Daily in July 2025, asks how university ideological-political theory courses and the ideological-political content of other subjects can work together as one education effort. Hu Xihua argues that the two are close in task and aligned in goal, and that coordinating them is both a requirement of the fundamental task of fostering virtue through education and a practical response to current problems in ideological and political education.

The piece first defines the terms. Ideological-political courses are the main channel of ideological and political education in universities. Curriculum-based ideological-political education means weaving such elements into specialist courses so that knowledge transmission and value guidance coincide. It then sets out four lines of action, quoting Xi Jinping repeatedly in support.

First, Hu calls for the Party's overall leadership: university Party committees should take principal responsibility, with Party secretaries and presidents leading in the classroom, and should link departments and institutions to share resources. Second, teachers should form diverse collaborative teams of theory teachers, specialist teachers, industry experts and model workers. Such teams would map each specialist topic to ideological elements and draw a "concentric circle" of shared goals. Third, Hu proposes a new discourse system that moves from "embedding" to "internal growth". It would translate political language into academic and everyday language and use short video and livestreaming. Fourth, Hu proposes joint platforms with industry, such as enterprise laboratories and industry colleges, working through courses, cooperation and practice.

Hu concludes that this pattern would tie ideological education to regional economic and social development and form a mutually beneficial education ecosystem. The author presents it as meeting the needs of the new era and of training well-rounded talent. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official guidance on ideological-political education is turned into institutional measures for universities.
quoteEn: The key to building ideological-political courses lies in the Party.
quoteZh: 思政课建设，关键在党。

glossary.explanation: Dedicated ideological and political theory courses that all Chinese university students take, such as courses on Marxism and Party doctrine. They are treated as the main channel of ideological education.
The practice of integrating ideological and political content into ordinary specialist courses such as engineering or business. It has been promoted in Chinese higher education since the mid-2010s.
Officially the fundamental task of education in China, stressing moral and political formation alongside knowledge and skills.
The principle that the Communist Party leads all sectors of work, including education. In universities it is exercised through Party committees.

t: Building an ideological and political education system that consolidates the foundation and forges the soul
zh: 构建固本铸魂的思想政治教育体系
paras: Writing in a Party journal in 2025, Chen Diming takes up the call in the Outline for Building a Strong Education Nation (2024–2035), issued in January by the Central Committee and the State Council, to build an ideological and political education system that "consolidates the foundation and forges the soul". Chen argues that universities, as frontline positions of socialist ideological work, must make moral education the central task. They must also run ideological and political work through the whole of teaching, in order to train a new generation able to carry the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

The article has three parts. The first explains why such a system matters, the second sets out what it means, and the third proposes practical measures. It draws throughout on Xi Jinping's statements, including his speech at the 2024 National Education Conference, and on a Ministry of Education document on university ideological and political work.

Chen gives four reasons for the system's importance. It follows from the political requirement of Party leadership over universities and from the need to raise the quality of ideological and political education amid global change and the pressure of AI and network technology. It is also needed to put moral education into practice among students who are still forming their values. On meaning, Chen describes a system that has political, popular and strategic attributes. It consists of seven linked sub-systems: theoretical armament, discipline teaching, daily education, management and services, security and stability, staffing, and evaluation and supervision. It also balances high-quality development with high-level security, so that graduates are firm supporters of the Party and the socialist system. For implementation, Chen calls for stronger top-level design under Party committees, using Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. Chen also calls for better teacher training and ethics, and for following the laws governing ideological work, teaching and student growth. The proposals include making classrooms the main channel, encouraging student self-education and building converged-media platforms.

Chen concludes that such a system will realise education that involves all staff, covers the whole process and reaches every dimension, and will open a new stage for higher education. In this account, it will also ensure that young people "listen to the Party and follow the Party". Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated university leaders present the policy framework and priorities of ideological and political education in the drive to build a strong education nation.
quoteEn: Building an ideological and political education system that consolidates the foundation and forges the soul means keeping moral education as the central task, running ideological and political work through the whole teaching process, achieving education by all staff, throughout the process and in every respect, and striving to open a new chapter for higher education in China.
quoteZh: 构建固本铸魂的思想政治教育体系，就是要坚持把立德树人作为中心环节，把思想政治工作贯穿教育教学全过程，实现全员、全程、全方位育人，努力开创我国高等教育事业发展新局面。

glossary.en: consolidates the foundation and forges the soul
glossary.literal: consolidate the root, cast the soul
glossary.explanation: A slogan from the 2025 education-strengthening outline describing the aim of ideological and political education: securing the political and ideological base of education and shaping students' convictions.
A long-standing official formula that makes moral and ideological cultivation the fundamental task of education.
The system of teaching and activities, in and outside the classroom, through which the Party seeks to instil Marxist theory, political loyalty and socialist values in students.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017 and 2018.
An official goal of making China a leading country in education by 2035, set out in the 2024–2035 outline.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's central national goal, presented as restoring China's strength and international standing by mid-century.

t: The strategic role of universities in integrating scientific and technological innovation with industrial innovation
zh: 发挥高校在科技创新与产业创新融合发展中的战略作用
paras: Ren Shaobo, Party Secretary of Zhejiang University, asks how universities can help integrate scientific and technological innovation with industrial innovation. Ren argues that technological innovation is the endogenous driving force of industrial innovation, while industrial innovation is where technological innovation realises its value. Universities, in this account, are the key link between science and technology, talent and innovation. They should build a mutually reinforcing system of talent training, technological innovation and the commercialisation of results, in support of high-level scientific and technological self-reliance.

The piece, published in Red Flag Manuscripts in 2025, is organised in four parts, each opening with Xi Jinping's statements and Party documents, including the 20th Party Congress report (2022) and the Third Plenum decision (2024). Each part names shortcomings in current university practice and then proposes remedies. The four parts cover raising innovation capacity and the supply of original research, recruiting and developing talent, connecting the innovation chain through commercialisation and start-up incubation, and building an innovation and entrepreneurship ecosystem.

Ren first holds that universities have too little strategic weight in the national innovation system, supply too little original research and lack well-organised, goal-oriented research. Remedies include strengthening basic and interdisciplinary research, building high-level platforms such as national key laboratories, and reforming collaborative mechanisms so that the innovation, industrial, talent and funding chains are joined up. On talent, Ren calls for strategic talent maps, easier flows of personnel among universities, institutes and firms, "talent special zones" and evaluation reform. The third and fourth parts propose entrepreneurship education, incubation through university science parks and proof-of-concept centres, university-run venture funds offering "patient capital", and shared-benefit arrangements with firms and alumni.

Ren concludes that universities should act as the source of innovation and as drivers of industry, and so cultivate new quality productive forces. The article presents this as a way to support Chinese modernization and the building of China as a leading country in education. It treats alumni networks, regional culture and flexible intellectual-property arrangements with firms as parts of one ecosystem centred on universities. Read the original if you want a university Party leader's detailed, policy-oriented account of how Chinese universities are being steered towards technology transfer, talent mobility and industry partnership.
quoteEn: The innovation and entrepreneurship ecosystem is in essence a kind of "soft power", and it matters greatly for energising innovating actors, drawing innovation factors together and raising overall innovation efficiency.
quoteZh: 创新创业生态本质上是一种“软实力”，对于激发创新主体活力、促进创新要素汇聚、提升创新整体效能具有重要意义。

glossary.explanation: Official Party term for China's own path to modernization, prominent since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.
A concept promoted by Xi Jinping since 2023. It refers to advanced productivity driven by technological breakthroughs and emerging industries.

glossary.literal: science and technology standing on its own and strengthening itself
glossary.explanation: An official goal of reducing dependence on foreign technology and building indigenous innovation capacity. The 19th Party Central Committee's Fifth Plenum (2020) made it a strategic pillar of national development.

t: Strengthening ecological civilization education in universities
zh: 加强高校生态文明教育
paras: This commentary, published in Guangming Daily in June 2025, asks how universities should carry out ecological civilization education. Guo and Zhang argue that it must be built into the national education system under the guidance of Xi Jinping Thought on Ecological Civilization. They present this as part of training a new generation committed to a socialist ecological civilization outlook and to the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

The authors begin from the Party's policy documents on building a Beautiful China. They then describe the content of Xi's ecological thought and set out proposals in four areas: teaching and curriculum, scientific research, international exchange, and institutional design.

Guo and Zhang claim that Western models of ecological governance have achieved little against global problems such as climate change and species loss. In their account, Xi Jinping Thought on Ecological Civilization brings a revolution in discourse at the ontological, axiological and methodological levels. They therefore call for it to guide classroom teaching, textbooks, student activities and school management. They propose strengthening ideological and political courses, compiling new textbooks, and using Marxism to revive fine traditional ecological culture. They also call for a research chain running from green projects to green products, and for university think tanks.

The authors conclude that universities should add ecological education to international exchange, telling China's story abroad. They also propose school-level planning, regulation and an evaluation system, so that students adopt green, low-carbon lifestyles and take part in building a Beautiful China. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official Party discourse sets out the tasks of ecological education in higher education.
quoteEn: Universities should carry ecological civilization education through the whole process of talent cultivation, deepening curriculum reform, strengthening organisational coordination, building up the teaching staff and promoting inter-university cooperation, so as to build a "big ideological and political education" pattern.
quoteZh: 高校要将生态文明教育贯穿人才培养全过程，深化课程改革、强化组织协同、建强教师队伍、推动校际合作，构建“大思政”育人格局。

glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Ecological Civilization
glossary.explanation: The body of ideas on environmental protection and development attributed to Xi Jinping, formalised after the 18th Party Congress (2012). It is presented officially as a guide for building a Beautiful China.
An official concept that makes environmental protection a core part of national development, alongside economic, political, cultural and social development.
An official goal of building a country with a good ecological environment, tied to the idea of harmony between humans and nature.

keywords: Xi Jinping Thought on Ecological Civilization

t: Innovating student work models to raise the level of Party building in universities
zh: 创新学生工作模式 提升高校党建水平
paras: Cui Zhigang and Wen Qin argue that student Party members are the 'key minority' in universities' 'all-round education' arrangement, and that raising their quality answers the basic question of whom to train, how and for whom. Their short commentary, from the Chinese Social Sciences Today, presents the '1234' model of Party member education and training introduced at Nanchang Normal University.

The article describes the model as four sets of measures: a 'Youth Candle Vanguard Corps', a 'dual-mentor linkage' mechanism, a 'three services' practice platform and training in 'four abilities'. It reports that the model addresses weak continuity and weak practical grounding in training student Party members. It is presented as the result of a Jiangxi provincial university Party-building research project.

The authors describe a four-tier structure running from the university to colleges, Party branches and student residence service stations. In it, each college sends 12 student Party members a year to central training. Party-affairs staff act as one-to-one mentors, and corps members serve as class leaders in Party school courses, so that 'educators are educated first'. Practice runs through serving teachers and students, the branch and society, including rural revitalization research. Training targets political, professional, practical and employment abilities.

As evidence the authors cite results over three years: 8 corps members won national scholarships, 16 entered master's programmes, one joined the Western Programme and over 20 went to basic education posts in Jiangxi. They conclude that the model moves student Party members from 'theoretically qualified' to 'fully competent'. Read the original if you want a concrete example of how a Chinese teacher-training college organises student Party member training.
quoteEn: The 'dual-mentor linkage' mechanism deeply fuses 'teacher guidance' with 'student agency', forming a closed training loop of 'guidance, practice, reflection and improvement', so that Party-spirit education has both theoretical height and emotional warmth.
quoteZh: “双导联动”机制将“教师主导”与“学生主体”深度融合，形成“指导—实践—反思—提升”的培养闭环，使党性教育既有理论高度又有情感温度。

glossary.literal: education by all personnel, throughout the whole process, in all respects
glossary.explanation: A policy concept in Chinese higher education that calls for all staff to take part in moral and political education of students at every stage and in every aspect of campus life.
The name of the selected group of student Party members at Nanchang Normal University who receive intensive training and lead activities.

t: Seizing the historic opportunity of AI development to build a new pattern of higher education
zh: 抢抓人工智能发展历史机遇构建高等教育发展新格局
paras: Zhang Guangjun, writing in Red Flag Manuscripts in 2025, asks how universities should respond to artificial intelligence (AI) as a driver of the new round of scientific and technological revolution. The author argues that universities must grasp this historic opportunity with a higher political standpoint and more systematic strategy, build a new pattern of higher education, and so help a strong education nation support Chinese modernization. The piece is a Party-journal commentary that draws heavily on Xi Jinping's statements.

The article has four parts. It first sets out three ways AI is changing higher education: the education system, the paradigm of scientific research, and global talent competition. It then turns to reshaping how top-notch innovative talent is trained, through new educational concepts, teachers' roles and student assessment. The third part covers disciplinary crossover and industry–education integration. The last part deals with university governance, Party leadership and ideological education.

Zhang's central claim is that AI's effect is a reshaping of educational paradigms, not a simple addition of technology. In teaching, the stress shifts from transmitting knowledge to higher-order thinking, personalised and precisely matched learning, and blended virtual–physical spaces. Teachers become designers of learning, and assessment moves beyond exam scores to a three-in-one system of knowledge, ability and value formation. In research, the author expects AI-driven science to become a new paradigm, citing the 2024 Nobel prizes in physics and chemistry as evidence of disciplinary convergence. Universities are urged to strengthen basic research on data, algorithms and computing power, build "AI+" crossover with the humanities as well as the sciences, and link education, talent, innovation and industry chains.

Zhang concludes that higher education must combine "upholding fundamental principles" with innovation. In this account, Party leadership must steer the direction of universities in the AI era, drawing on the Two Establishes, the Two Upholds and the Four-sphere Confidence. Ideological and political education must run through AI-enabled teaching to counter risks such as algorithmic bias, "information cocoons", hidden academic misconduct and emotional alienation. The author also proposes embedding socialist core values in recommendation algorithms. Read the original if you want an example of how a senior Party-affiliated university leader frames AI and higher-education reform in official terms.
quoteEn: This change is by no means a simple superimposition of AI technology onto the field of education, but a profound reshaping of the educational paradigm.
quoteZh: 这种变革绝不只是人工智能技术在教育领域的简单叠加，而是对教育范式的深刻重塑。

glossary.explanation: Official concept of a distinctively Chinese path to modernization, promoted by the Party leadership since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
Party formula, adopted in 2022, affirming Xi Jinping's position as the Party's core and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought.
Party requirement to uphold Xi Jinping's core position in the Party and the Central Committee's authority and unified leadership.
Official slogan calling for confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics.
Policy of tying universities and vocational education closely to industry, including joint labs, research institutes and technology transfer.

t: The connotation, characteristics and contemporary value of "life-based ideological and political education"
zh: 论“生活思政”的内涵特征和时代价值
source: Journal of Party Building and Ideological Education in Schools, 2025 no. 8
paras: The article takes up "life-based ideological and political education" (shenghuo sizheng), a concept put forward in 2018 by the Party committee of the Zhejiang Wanli Education Group and developed at Zhejiang Wanli University. Wang and Cao argue that, although the idea is not strictly new, it opens a research space and deserves systematic theoretical treatment. Their thesis is that it is best understood as an educational philosophy that roots ideological and political education in students' everyday lives.

The piece has three parts. It first reviews existing definitions and then analyses the two components, "life" and "ideological and political" work or education, to reach a working definition. It then sets out three defining features, and finally assesses the concept's value for theory, for university practice and for building a strong education nation.

On definition, the authors hold that life-based ideological and political education is not simply a subset of everyday ideological education, nor an all-encompassing "unified field". It is a concept that stresses the importance of "life" for such work, covering both real and online life, and combining explicit and implicit education. They identify three features: it is grounded in life and focused on nurturing people, working across individual and dormitory "small spaces" and wider "large spaces" such as classes and clubs; it draws on culture to shape people, with culture as the key to fusing life and ideological education; and it uses digital means, linking precision and digital ideological education to bridge virtual and real life. Its value, they say, lies in new research topics, including empirical research, in a model of whole-staff, "all-round" nurturing built on the "three-all" approach and the "seven nurturing" mechanisms, and in supporting the "leading force of ideological and political education" that Xi Jinping introduced at the National Education Conference in September 2024.

The authors conclude that the concept gives theory a new field, gives universities a fresh way to innovate, and supplies the everyday ground on which the leading force of ideological and political education can operate. They present Zhejiang Wanli University's experience as a model of this. Read the original if you study Chinese university ideological education, or want to see how a locally coined practice concept is given theoretical form and tied to current Party discourse.
quoteEn: "Life-based ideological and political education" is an ideological and political education concept that takes students' everyday life as its basic field and seeks to integrate ideological and political courses, ideological and political education across the curriculum, and everyday ideological education organically with students' daily lives.
quoteZh: “生活思政”是一种以学生日常生活为基本场域，尝试将思政课程、课程思政、日常思想政治教育与学生日常生活有机融合的思想政治教育理念。

glossary.explanation: A concept proposed in 2018 by the Party committee of the Zhejiang Wanli Education Group. It aims to embed ideological and political education in students' daily lives on and off campus.

An official approach to university education in which all staff, across the whole process and in all settings, take part in nurturing students. The article treats it as a framework that life-based education advances.

glossary.en: leading force of ideological and political education
glossary.explanation: A concept Xi Jinping introduced at the National Education Conference in September 2024. It treats ideological and political work as a defining strength of China's education system.
An official goal of building China into a leading country in education, which the article links to the role of ideological and political education.

t: Forging the heart and soul: opening a new phase in cultural education in universities
zh: 立心铸魂 开创高校文化育人工作新局面
paras: Writing in the Chinese Social Sciences Today (23 June 2025), Yan Longzhong asks how universities can carry out cultural education in line with Xi Jinping's thought on culture. The author argues that cultural education and moral cultivation are integral to ideological and political work in higher education and to ensuring the Party's cause is passed on. Universities, Yan holds, should draw on excellent traditional Chinese culture, revolutionary culture and advanced socialist culture to "forge the heart and soul" of a "new generation for the new era".

The commentary opens by describing Xi Jinping's thought on culture as the cultural part of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era and as a result of the Two Integrations. It then sets out three tasks: forging the soul through culture, educating people through culture, and nourishing the mind through culture. Each task is tied to a metaphor (the "steering wheel" of values, the "backbone" of commitment, and the "spirit" of striving) and broken into practical measures.

On soul-forging, Yan says students should be guided to hold firm faith in Marxism, conviction in socialism with Chinese characteristics, and confidence in the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. The author proposes using the "four histories" and comparisons between China and the West to counter what is described as denigration of socialism and erroneous trends of thought. On educating through culture, Yan argues that each of the three cultural strands has a distinct role: traditional culture lays the spiritual foundation, revolutionary culture strengthens the spiritual lifeline through Party, revolutionary and martyr stories, and advanced socialist culture, centred on core socialist values, enriches students' inner world. On nourishing the mind, the author proposes three channels: campus environments that carry cultural elements, locally distinctive cultural courses, and themed activities such as reading campaigns combining online and offline formats.

Yan concludes that universities should combine explicit and implicit education so that culture works quietly and continuously on students, and should build a cultural space that is deep-rooted, harmonious and inclusive. The piece is a practice-oriented statement of how Xi Jinping's cultural thought is to be applied in university student work. Read the original if you want an example of how a university student-affairs official frames cultural education and the tasks of ideological and political work in Chinese higher education in 2025.
