quoteEn: Universities should take excellent traditional Chinese culture, revolutionary culture and advanced socialist culture as their foundation of strength, and work to forge the heart and soul of the "new generation for the new era".
quoteZh: 高校要以中华优秀传统文化、革命文化和社会主义先进文化为力量根基，着力为“时代新人”立心铸魂

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018. It is presented as the current stage of adapting Marxism to China.
The cultural component of Xi Jinping Thought, formally put forward in October 2023. It covers cultural construction, cultural confidence and the Party's cultural mission.
Official formula for combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture. The second integration was added in 2021–2023.
A long-standing educational principle, made the fundamental task of education in Party documents, that schools should cultivate virtue as well as knowledge.
An official study programme covering the history of the Party, of the People's Republic, of reform and opening up, and of the development of socialism.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's central national goal, often linked to the Chinese Dream, of restoring China to national strength and prosperity.
A twelve-word official value set promoted since 2012, covering national, social and individual levels (e.g. prosperity, democracy, patriotism, integrity).

t: Making the "walking ideological and political course" take root in minds and hearts
zh: 让“行走的思政课”入心入脑
paras: This short commentary, published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in June 2025, asks how the "walking ideological and political course" (practice-based teaching outside the classroom) can truly persuade university students. The authors argue that the "big ideological and political course" initiative is not mere expansion in scale. In their view it restructures the elements of teaching through a dialectic of "seeing the large in the small".

Taking the 2025 work plan issued by the Ministry of Education and nine other departments as its starting point, the piece is organised around three "bigs": a "big teaching force", a "big classroom" and a "big platform". Each section pairs a broad aim with concrete, small-scale methods.

On teachers, the authors call for "great teachers" who combine disciplinary mastery with moral example, and for student-centred design. This includes menu-style activity choices, a "compulsory core plus elective" practice chain, problem-based guidance and mixed evaluation. On the classroom, they propose drawing on local revolutionary sites, traditional culture and the Party's founding spirit. They also propose immersive settings, including AR, visits to families, factories and fields, and ritual activities on meaningful dates. On the platform, they propose online-offline systems for showcasing student work, flipped classrooms, and cooperation among family, school, government and society. Volunteering and the "three going to the countryside" campaigns would serve as practice. The authors frame all this as the Marxist cycle of practice, knowledge and renewed practice.

The authors conclude that the "big teaching force" is realised in each teacher's classroom craft, the "big classroom" in small observations in the field, and the "big platform" in cooperation among many actors. They present this unity of broad vision and fine detail as the basic guide for making the course reach minds and hearts. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Chinese university ideological and political education is framed and what practical measures are proposed for it.
quoteEn: This dialectical unity of "taking the broad view" and "starting from small details" vividly reflects, in ideological and political education, the governing wisdom of "reaching breadth while mastering subtlety", and is the fundamental guide for making the "walking ideological and political course" enter minds and hearts.
quoteZh: 这种“大处着眼”与“小处着手”的辩证统一，正是“致广大而尽精微”治理智慧在思想政治教育中的生动映照，也是“行走的思政课”入脑入心的根本遵循。

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses in Marxist theory, Party ideology and moral education taught at Chinese schools and universities.
An initiative to extend ideological and political teaching beyond the classroom by drawing on society-wide resources, with a "big classroom", "big platform" and "big teaching force".
Practice-based teaching in which students learn through site visits, fieldwork and social investigation rather than only in lectures.

t: A new account of the process of ideological and political education from the perspective of social operation
zh: 基于社会运行视角的思想政治教育过程新论
source: Teaching and Research (教学与研究), 2025 no. 4
paras: Dai Yuqi and Yu Xiaochun ask how the process of ideological and political education should be understood once it is placed within the wider operation of society rather than treated as an isolated teaching activity. They argue that the process has a pronounced social character, and that viewing it through 'social operation' (society as a living organic whole in motion and change) gives a fuller grasp of its meaning and logic. The authors present this as both a critique of traditional educational models and an exploration of models suited to the new era.

The article proposes three layers of the process, running from core to periphery: self-organising operation inside the ideological and political education system, interactive operation between that system and other social subsystems, and 'ubiquitous' operation in which such education is embedded in society as a whole. Each layer gets its own section, which sets out the process's elements (educators, educatees, content, methods and context), describes how it unfolds, and proposes ways to optimise it. The self-organisation concept is traced to Kant.

In the authors' account, the three layers differ in how widely the five elements are defined. In self-organising operation, educators are professional theory and propaganda staff, educatees are highly organised groups such as Party members, soldiers and students, and methods are explicit ones such as theoretical indoctrination. In interactive operation, the categories widen to all who work in culture, media and education, and to loosely organised groups such as flexible workers. Methods become implicit ones such as exemplars, motivation and influence, and the system exchanges resources with the political, economic, cultural and technological subsystems. In ubiquitous operation, implicit political, ideological, economic and cultural factors run through the process. The authors distinguish benign, neutral and malign social operation and argue that a well-functioning society itself acts as an 'invisible' form of such education.

For optimisation, the authors call for broadening the field beyond schools and teachers, ensuring all elements are present and linked, and coordinating mechanisms, personnel (full-time and part-time) and resources across social subsystems. They also call for closer ties to practice, responsiveness to social concerns and greater continuity across time and space, including online. They state that Chinese society is currently in a benign, stable and improving state, which they say strengthens the effects of such education. Read the original if you want a systems-theoretical framework for studying ideological and political education as part of society, and how Chinese scholars conceptualise its explicit and implicit forms.
quoteEn: The process of ideological and political education has a distinct social character, and placing it within the broad horizon of social operation helps in grasping as a whole its basic meaning and operating logic.
quoteZh: 思想政治教育过程具有鲜明的社会性，将其置于社会运行的广阔视域之下，有助于整体把握其基本内涵与运行逻辑。

glossary.explanation: A field and practice in China covering the teaching of political ideology, values and morality, in schools and in Party, government, military and community settings. It is also an academic discipline within Marxist studies.
A concept in Chinese sociology and Marxist theory describing society as a living organic whole that moves, changes and develops through interaction among its parts.
The authors' term for the inner layer of the process: explicit, relatively bounded education activities in which the system's own elements interact to form order.
The authors' term for the outer layer, in which ideological and political education is spread throughout society and works largely implicitly through the social environment.

t: Constructing a value-added evaluation system for teaching ideological and political theory courses in universities
zh: 高校思政课教学增值评价体系构建探赜
source: School Party Building and Ideological Education, 2025 no. 8
paras: Chang Qing asks how the teaching effect of university ideological and political theory courses (sizheng courses) can be evaluated effectively as these courses move towards high-quality development. The author borrows the economic notion of "value-added" evaluation, which looks at the "added value" created between input and output and so measures process as well as result. The article argues that such a system goes beyond traditional outcome-based evaluation, records the whole teaching process and separates out the effects of unfair background factors.

The article is published in School Party Building and Ideological Education (2025, no. 8) and has three parts. The first sets out the design orientation of the system around three goals: knowledge, ability and emotional identification. The second builds the indicators, weights them with the analytic hierarchy process (AHP) and describes how the system is applied. The third discusses the difficulties of construction and proposes countermeasures.

Chang derives the indicators from official documents and speeches by Xi Jinping. The three first-level indicators are acquisition of Marxist theoretical knowledge, students' ability to analyse and solve problems, and loyalty to the Party and state. Second-level indicators include knowledge of Marxist theory and of the Party's innovative theory, practical and complex problem-solving ability, and political literacy, moral feeling and self-identification. AHP is used to build a three-tier hierarchy, a 1–9 scale pairwise comparison matrix and a consistency test. Application is to centre on students' learning outcomes and a dynamic feedback mechanism of data collection, analysis, feedback generation and adjustment.

Chang names three difficulties: emotional and political goals resist quantification, teachers of large classes struggle to track students' changing behaviour, and evaluation is affected by uncertain external and individual factors. The proposed responses are to fuse multi-source data (text and behaviour logs, with teachers and supervisors as evaluators), to track students with online platforms, for instance attention curves and interest in theoretical and social issues, and to reduce uncertainty through what the author calls the "common base-point principle", which seeks the core link between students and Marxist theory. Read the original if you are interested in how Chinese scholars try to turn the goals of political-theory teaching into measurable indicators and weighted evaluation models.
quoteEn: The value-added evaluation system for ideological and political courses will examine whether students have progressed and gained value, taking students' acquisition of knowledge, improvement of ability and emotional identification as its starting point.
quoteZh: 思政课增值评价体系将考查学生是否有所进步和增值，并以学生的知识获得、能力提升和情感认同为出发点

glossary.explanation: The compulsory Marxist theory and political education courses taught in Chinese schools and universities. They are treated as the core means of moral and ideological education.
An assessment approach that measures the progress learners make over time, rather than only final results. The article borrows it from economics and applies it to political-theory teaching.
A decision-making method that breaks a goal into a hierarchy of criteria and derives weights from pairwise comparisons. It includes a consistency check on the comparisons.

t: The logic and mechanisms of integrating revolutionary cultural relics into the "Big Ideological and Political Course"
zh: 革命文物融入“大思政课”建设的逻辑与机制
source: Journal of Party Building and Ideological Education in Schools, 2025 no. 8
paras: Wu Xiaowei takes up a practical question in Chinese ideological and political education: how revolutionary cultural relics can be built into the "Big Ideological and Political Course" (da sizheng ke), a concept Xi Jinping stressed in 2021 when he said it must be used well and tied to reality. The article argues that the relics are a high-quality teaching resource and that integration needs a clear rationale, guiding principles and working mechanisms. Wu sets out these three layers in turn.

The article is organised in three parts. The first sets out why integration is possible and valuable. The second lists six principles tied to six elements of the construction work: subjects, objects, purpose, content, method and context. The third describes two forms of integration and the mechanisms each requires. Wu cites figures that China has registered 36,000 immovable revolutionary relics, over one million state-held movable items and more than 1,600 revolutionary museums and memorial halls.

On value, Wu argues that the relics embody revolutionary history and spirit, enrich the content of teaching, and link the classroom with society at large. They also open the way to "inter-subjective" education, in which teachers and students explore the relics together. The six principles are collaborative education, teaching according to aptitude across school stages, moral cultivation (lide shuren), adaptation to local conditions, keeping pace with the times through digital technology, and building immersive settings. In the third part, Wu distinguishes two forms. In the first, relics enter the classroom indirectly, through teachers' retelling, and need a screening mechanism and an embedding mechanism. In the second, museums and memorial sites themselves become courses, and need a collaboration mechanism and a transformation mechanism that turn social actors into participants in a community of educators. Wu says that in each pair the first mechanism is a precondition of the second, and that feedback runs between them.

Wu concludes that integration works only if multiple actors are coordinated, the resources are screened and fitted to specific courses, and sites are converted into learning environments, all in service of the fundamental task of moral education. The relics are presented as helping to strengthen emotional identification with the Party's revolutionary history. Read the original if you are interested in how Chinese education scholars design practical frameworks for using museums and red heritage in ideological and political teaching.
quoteEn: Integrating revolutionary cultural relics into the "Big Ideological and Political Course" follows the distinctive requirement of being "big", but the centre and foundation remain the "course", and the aim is to achieve "educating people".
quoteZh: 革命文物融入“大思政课”建设，遵循的是“大”的特色要求，但重心与根本仍然是“课”，目的是实现“育人”

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2021 that extends ideological and political teaching beyond the classroom into society, practice and community resources.

Objects and sites associated with the Chinese Communist Party's revolutionary history, such as former headquarters, documents and personal items, protected as state heritage and used in patriotic education.
The official fundamental task of Chinese education: fostering moral character and ideological commitment alongside knowledge.
The system of courses and activities in Chinese schools and universities intended to instil the Party's ideology, values and patriotism.

t: Shaping a new pattern of fostering virtue through the "Great Ideological and Political Course"
zh: 以“大思政课”塑造立德树人新格局
paras: Writing in Red Flag Manuscripts (2025, no. 11), Lü Chao takes up Xi Jinping's remarks to education-sector political advisers at the 2025 national "two sessions". Xi called for merging the ideological and political "small classroom" with the social "big classroom". Lü argues that the "Great Ideological and Political Course" is the main channel for fostering virtue and cultivating talent, and for supplying the personnel that Chinese modernization requires.

The commentary has three parts. The first sets out why the Great Course matters. The second sets out the regularities that should guide it. The third proposes new paths for building it. Lü draws on Xi's speeches and on official documents, including the Education Power Construction Plan (2024–2035) and a Ministry of Education opinion on digitalising education. Lü also cites examples: 453 national practice teaching bases, and university brands at Peking University, Renmin University and the National University of Defense Technology.

Lü gives three reasons for the Great Course. It is needed to carry out the fundamental task of fostering virtue and cultivating talent amid ideological struggle, rapid growth in the internet and artificial intelligence, and changes in how young people think. It is needed to develop ideological and political courses in depth. And it is needed to consolidate students' ideological foundations. On method, Lü highlights three principles: focusing on forging souls, emphasising practice-based education, and strengthening systems thinking. Under these principles, knowledge transmission goes with value guidance, explicit teaching with implicit teaching, and scientific literacy with humanistic grounding. Teaching, faculty and platforms are planned as a whole, and schools, families and society are linked.

Lü's proposals concern three areas. The first is problem-solving, through integrated ideological and political education across primary, secondary and tertiary levels, with shared content, rituals and teacher training, plus a school–family–society framework. The second is innovation in method: case-based and interactive teaching, practice bases, and online "smart teaching" via platforms such as Xuexi Qiangguo. The third is results-oriented evaluation, with teachers, students and parents forming an "evaluation community" that assesses students' knowing, believing and acting and uses AI-assisted tools. Read the original if you want a Party-journal account of how ideological and political education is being extended beyond the classroom, including its institutional examples and policy references.
quoteEn: The "Great Ideological and Political Course" focuses on the fundamental questions of what kind of people to cultivate, how to cultivate them and for whom, and is an important route for carrying out the fundamental task of fostering virtue and cultivating talent in the new era.
quoteZh: “大思政课”聚焦解决好培养什么人、怎样培养人、为谁培养人这个根本问题，是贯彻落实新时代立德树人根本任务的重要途径。

glossary.explanation: A policy concept promoted since 2021 that extends ideological and political education beyond the classroom into society, practice bases and online spaces. It is presented as a way to link theory with real-world experience.

The officially defined fundamental task of Chinese education: moral and character formation alongside intellectual training. It is used to justify integrating political and moral education into all teaching.

glossary.literal: ideological-political courses and ideological-political education within courses
glossary.explanation: Refers to dedicated ideological and political courses and to the embedding of ideological content in other subjects. Xi Jinping has called for the two to work in the same direction.
The official term for China's path of modernization, set out in the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.

t: Making good use of the "grand ideological and political course" to cultivate new-era youth
zh: 善用“大思政课”培育时代新人
paras: This short commentary, first published in Guangming Daily on 17 June 2025, asks how schools can make better use of the "grand ideological and political course" (da sizheng ke). Zhou Jing, drawing on Xi Jinping's remarks, argues that it is a necessary part of reforming ideological and political courses in the new era. Zhou contends that coordination mechanisms, a stronger teaching force and use of society as a classroom will raise the courses' guiding power and produce "new-era people" loyal to the Party and committed to national rejuvenation.

The article has three parts. The first deals with top-level design and coordination across school levels and departments. The second concerns teachers. The third concerns taking teaching out of the classroom into society.

On coordination, Zhou calls for stronger Party leadership over the courses, with school Party secretaries and principals personally involved. Zhou also wants Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era built into teaching, and the aim of educating through all staff, all stages and all aspects pursued. Universities should form joint teaching bodies with urban and rural schools, share resources on cloud platforms and send teachers to rural areas, to narrow uneven development. On teachers, Zhou proposes refined full-time staff, a wider pool of part-time lecturers, a social lecturer database, training, and speaking teams drawing on veterans and model figures. On practice, courses should move to red-education sites, fields, factories and volunteer activities, using local resources and formats such as "mobile red classrooms".

Zhou concludes that combining the "small classroom" of the course with the "big classroom" of society will let students understand basic principles in real situations and deepen their belief. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-state educators describe the practical implementation of ideological and political education in schools.
quoteEn: Organically combine the "small ideological and political classroom" with the "big social classroom", take root in China's vast land, face vibrant social practice, keep ideological and political courses open to the world, and continually explore innovation in practical courses.
quoteZh: 把“思政小课堂”与“社会大课堂”有机结合，扎根广袤的中国大地，面向火热的社会实践，坚持开门办思政课，不断探索实践课程创新

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2021 that links ideological and political teaching in schools with real-life social settings and resources, rather than confining it to the classroom.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The official body of ideas associated with Xi Jinping, written into the Party and state constitutions and taught across the education system.
A Party term for the younger generation expected to be politically reliable, patriotic and ready to take on national rejuvenation.
The official goal of restoring China's strength and international standing, usually rendered as the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

t: Doing ideological and political work and united front work well, and keeping absolute loyalty to the Party as a political hallmark
st: The CASS Party Leadership Group's theoretical study centre group studies Xi Jinping's important statements on strengthening and improving ideological and political work and on the Party's united front work in the new era
zh: 认真做好思想政治工作和统战工作 永葆对党绝对忠诚的政治本色
zhSub: 中国社会科学院党组理论学习中心组深入学习领会习近平总书记关于加强和改进思想政治工作的重要论述、关于做好新时代党的统一战线工作的重要思想
paras: This is a news report from China Social Sciences Net on the fifth (enlarged) study session of 2025 held by the theoretical study centre group of the Party Leadership Group of the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (CASS) on 19 June. The session studied Xi Jinping's important statements on strengthening and improving ideological and political work, and his important thinking on the Party's united front work in the new era. Its stated aim was to push CASS units to carry out the responsibility systems for both kinds of work.

CASS President and Party Leadership Group Secretary Gao Xiang chaired the meeting and spoke. Vice-presidents Peng Jinhui, Zhao Rui and Li Xuesong attended, as did Hang Yuanxiang of the Central Commission for Discipline Inspection team stationed at CASS. Zhao Rui gave the keynote speech, and Xin Xiangyang, head of the Institute of Marxism, gave an exchange speech. Heads of Party organisations in CASS units also took part.

According to the report, the meeting described ideological and political work as the Party's fine tradition and political advantage, and as the "lifeline" of all work. It said that Xi's thinking on the united front is part of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. In the meeting's account, this thinking answers why a united front is needed, what kind, and how to consolidate it. The meeting called CASS a political organ centred on research. It said the first task is to study and explain Xi Jinping Thought and to build a disciplinary theoretical system guided by it.

The meeting called on CASS units to strengthen political and ideological guidance, build up their talent teams and improve work style. It also demanded rigorous implementation of the central inspection rectification requirements, with focus on societies, associations, foundations, non-entity research centres and enterprises under CASS. Read the original if you want a short record of how CASS leadership frames its political-work priorities and inspection rectification in mid-2025.
quoteEn: The Chinese Academy of Social Sciences is a political organ whose central work is scientific research, and it must make studying and explaining Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era its primary task.
quoteZh: 中国社会科学院是以科研为中心工作的政治机关，要把研究阐释好习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想作为首要任务

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The official guiding ideology of the Communist Party of China, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.
The Party's strategy of building alliances with non-Party groups and social forces, including other parties, ethnic and religious groups, and overseas Chinese.
Party work of political education and persuasion aimed at shaping the views and conduct of members and the public.
Follow-up action required of an organisation after a Party inspection team has reported problems in it.

t: Giving full play to the key role of the "Situation and Policy" course
zh: 发挥好“形势与政策”课的关键作用
paras: This commentary, published in Guangming Daily in June 2025, asks what role the "Situation and Policy" course should play in the development of ideological and political theory courses in Chinese universities. Hong Bo argues that it is a special and indispensable course because it responds quickly to what the Party, society and students themselves want to know, and that it therefore has an irreplaceable part in the high-quality, content-focused development of such courses.

The piece begins from Xi Jinping's call to improve the relevance and appeal of ideological and political courses. It then organises its case around three features of the course: timeliness, pertinence (targeting) and comprehensiveness. It ends with practical suggestions for teaching resources and practice-based teaching.

On timeliness, Hong holds that the course should use the achievements of Chinese modernization as its vehicle. It should combine the classroom with "the big classroom of society" so that students grasp Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era and develop patriotism and an international outlook. On pertinence, the author describes the course as a front line of ideological struggle. It should explain policy and hot-button issues, strengthen the Four-sphere Confidence and help students resist arguments such as the "China collapse" and "overcapacity" theories. On comprehensiveness, Hong says the course can link topics such as a community with a shared future for mankind or cultural strength to other courses, complementing them rather than duplicating them.

Hong concludes that the course should be linked more effectively with other courses and supported by a combined package of teaching points, dedicated textbooks, lecture materials, collective lesson preparation and research. The author also proposes on-site formats such as "ideological and political classes in museums and venues" and "walking" classes. Read the original if you want a short, official-style statement of how Party-aligned educators define the purposes and teaching methods of the Situation and Policy course.
quoteEn: The pertinence of the "Situation and Policy" course can effectively strengthen the capacity of university ideological and political courses to dispel doubts and resolve real-world questions.
quoteZh: “形势与政策”课的针对性,能够切实增强高校思政课的释疑性和现实解惑作用。

glossary.explanation: A required ideological and political course in Chinese universities that explains current domestic and international developments and Party and state policy to students.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The official guiding ideology of the Communist Party of China, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017 and 2018.
The official term for China's path of development under Party leadership, stressed since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
An official formula calling for confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept for China's vision of international relations and global governance.
The set of compulsory courses on Marxism, Party history and Party theory taught in Chinese schools and universities.

t: The "Great Ideological and Political Course" and the building of a "three-wide education" pattern in universities
zh: “大思政课”助推高校构建“三全育人”格局
paras: Writing in the Study Times (11 June 2025), Wang argues that the "Great Ideological and Political Course" (da sizheng ke) can help universities build and deepen the "three-wide education" pattern. Wang presents this as both a strategic need amid complex international competition and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, and a necessary way to meet the development needs of society and students and to carry out the fundamental task of fostering virtue through education.

The commentary, short and practice-oriented, begins from Xi Jinping's call to use the "Great Ideological and Political Course" and tie it to reality. It then sets out measures in several areas: building a multi-actor education system; linking courses horizontally and school stages vertically; extending education into new settings; and digital transformation.

Wang first calls for stronger ideological and political theory teachers, through recruitment, training, practical placements and teaching innovation. Professional-course teachers, student-affairs staff, administrative and service departments, families and society would also take part. Wang then proposes integrating ideological and political theory courses with ideological and political elements in all courses, using "double-teacher classrooms" and evaluation mechanisms, and joining up university, secondary and primary teaching. Student "one-stop" communities, "walking" ideological and political classes and a "digital ideological and political education" project, with virtual labs and new-media platforms, would extend the work beyond the classroom.

Wang concludes that universities should build on their own strengths, learn from good practice, keep adjusting to new problems and make education more effective and engaging. Through coordination of all staff, the whole process and all dimensions, the course is expected to lay an ideological foundation for a new generation able to shoulder national rejuvenation. Read the original if you want a concise example of how a university Party official describes the practical implementation of ideological and political education policy in 2025.
quoteEn: Through the model of "community as classroom, practice as learning", the in-class and extracurricular, theory and practice, and knowledge and values can be deeply integrated.
quoteZh: 通过“社区即课堂、实践即学习”的模式，实现课内与课外、理论与实践、知识与价值的深度融合。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping that extends ideological and political education beyond the classroom into society and practice. It is meant to link theory teaching with real-world experience.

glossary.literal: education by all staff, through the whole process, in all dimensions
glossary.explanation: A policy principle for Chinese universities requiring that all personnel, the whole course of study and all aspects of campus life contribute to moral and ideological education.
The officially stated fundamental task of Chinese education: cultivating moral character and political orientation alongside knowledge.

glossary.en: ideological and political elements in all courses
glossary.explanation: The practice of embedding ideological and political content in non-political, professional courses, as distinct from the dedicated ideological and political theory courses.
An official goal, associated with the Chinese Dream, of restoring China's national strength and international standing by the middle of the twenty-first century.

t: Generative AI empowering propaganda, ideological and cultural work: transformation, risks and responses
zh: 生成式人工智能赋能宣传思想文化工作：嬗变、风险与应对
paras: Wu Yalin asks how generative AI, represented by ChatGPT and DeepSeek, is changing China's propaganda, ideological and cultural work, and how that work should respond. The article argues that the technology brings new capacities but also risks to ideological security, the information environment, communication effectiveness and cultural content. It holds that the work must adopt digital-intelligence thinking so as to turn these 'variables' into 'increments'.

The article has three parts. The first identifies four new features: richer and faster content supply, more precise and intelligent distribution, a shift from interpersonal to human–machine communication, and the integration of subjects, objects, media and environments. The second sets out four risks, which Wu labels the 'whirlpool', the 'swamp', diluted effectiveness and 'hollowing out'. The third proposes four innovation paths. Wu draws on Kittler, Baudrillard and post-truth theory, and cites regulations from 2023 and 2025 as well as examples such as CGTN's AI-assisted animated series.

On risks, Wu contends that models trained largely on English-language data carry Western bias and 'digital hegemony'. Their conversational, 'zero-distance' style is said to make ideological influence implicit, and young people (Generation Z) are described as especially exposed. Wu also points to hallucinations, deepfakes and 'black box' algorithms that defeat keyword-based filtering. 'Disembedded' human–machine dialogue is said to weaken trust in official media, and Western-led AI is said to squeeze out Chinese traditional culture. Wu's responses are demystifying the technology while strengthening value guidance and political resolve, reducing information noise through AI-literacy education and rule-of-law governance, building a Chinese cultural database and large language models, and upgrading discourse and the work force.

Wu concludes that this work is a systemic undertaking that must move forward in step with the technology, coordinating public opinion, culture, domestic and foreign communication, and online and offline work. The author recommends that propaganda and cultural departments use AI to help traditional Chinese culture 'come alive' and spread abroad, while keeping the Party's leadership over the technology. Read the original if you want a Chinese official-academic view of how AI is framed as both a tool and an ideological risk for propaganda and ideological work.
quoteEn: Generative AI technology is itself neutral, but the intelligently generated content it provides to audiences carries the attributes of public opinion and the capacity for social mobilisation.
quoteZh: 生成式人工智能技术本身是中立的，但面向受众提供的智能生成内容具有舆论属性或社会动员能力。

glossary.explanation: The Party's portfolio covering publicity, ideology, media and cultural affairs. The Chinese term for propaganda (xuānchuán) is used officially and is not pejorative in Chinese.

t: Building an ideological and political education system that consolidates the foundation and forges the soul
zh: 构建固本铸魂的思想政治教育体系
source: Research on Ideological Education (Sixiang jiaoyu yanjiu), 2025 no. 3
paras: The article takes up the first of the "eight systems" listed in the Outline of the Plan for Building a Leading Country in Education (2024–2035), issued by the Central Committee and State Council: an ideological and political education system that "consolidates the foundation and forges the soul" (gùběn zhùhún). Peng and Yuan argue that this system is a necessary requirement for keeping to a socialist orientation in schooling and for carrying out the fundamental task of fostering virtue and cultivating talent. They present it as the direction that building a leading education country must be anchored to.

The text has three parts: the significance of the system, its core meaning, and the paths for building it. It draws mainly on the Outline and on statements by Xi Jinping, and it is a policy-interpretive piece rather than an empirical study. Its target is ideological and political education from primary school to university, together with the families, society and government bodies that surround schools.

On significance, the authors give three grounds. Education has a political attribute, which makes the system a bottom line for socialist education. Ideological and political work is described as the Party's "lifeline" and traditional strength. And the "new generation of the era" who are to shoulder national rejuvenation need guidance amid a varied online information environment. On meaning, the authors read "consolidating the foundation" as upholding the socialist system and Party leadership, and "forging the soul" as internalising Marxism, the Party's innovative theory and traditional culture. They stress four features: unity of goals, plurality of actors, richness of resources, and continuity across stages, including integrated courses for primary, secondary and tertiary levels and the use of artificial intelligence and big data for tailored teaching.

For construction, the authors propose four paths. These are raising political standing under unified Party committee leadership, adopting a systems perspective, concentrating on key tasks, and integrating resources. The key tasks are ideological and political theory courses, with textbooks centred on Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, and teacher training. Resource integration draws on Party and national history, museums, digital platforms and social practice. The authors conclude that this is a long-term systems project requiring forward-looking, innovative research, with the aim of producing successors who are reliable for the Party. Read the original if you want a detailed example of how Chinese academics interpret the 2024 education plan's ideological and political education component.
quoteEn: Building an ideological and political education system that consolidates the foundation and forges the soul is a systematic integration of the present actors, carriers, resources and technologies of such education. It is also a long-term plan, looking ahead to building a leading education country, for the pattern of education and the standards for talent.
quoteZh: 构建固本铸魂的思想政治教育体系既是对当下思想政治教育主体、载体、资源、技术的系统整合，更是面向未来教育强国建设，对育人格局、人才标准的长远规划。

glossary.en: consolidates the foundation and forges the soul
glossary.literal: consolidate the root, cast the soul
glossary.explanation: A phrase used in the 2024 education plan for ideological and political education. The authors read it as upholding the socialist system and Party leadership, and instilling Marxism and traditional culture.
The system of teaching and guidance in schools and society meant to shape students' ideals, values and political outlook in line with Party doctrine.
Officially described as the fundamental task of education in China, combining moral formation with the training of skills.
A term used in Xi Jinping's speeches for young people expected to take on the task of national rejuvenation.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017 and 2018.
A strategic goal set out in the 2024–2035 plan, which aims to make China a leading country in education by 2035.

t: Making education in ideals and convictions regular and institutionalised
zh: 推动理想信念教育常态化制度化
source: Research on Ideological and Political Education, 2025 no. 1
paras: This article takes up the call, in the Decision adopted at the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), to "promote the regularisation and institutionalisation of education in ideals and convictions". Liu and Te argue that this is a complex, strategic and systematic undertaking, essential for leading people to hold the lofty communist ideal and the common ideal of socialism with Chinese characteristics, and for gathering spiritual strength behind further deepening reform and Chinese modernization.

The article has three parts. The first clarifies the core meaning of the formula, moving from the concepts of ideal and conviction to the necessity of such education and then to what regularisation and institutionalisation each involve. The second reviews the history of the demand, citing its repeated appearance in Party documents from 2019 to 2024, and sets out its significance. The third proposes five mechanisms for putting it into practice.

In the authors' conceptual analysis, ideal points to the future and conviction to the present; each depends on the other, and "ideals and convictions" is an integrated concept that goes beyond both. Regularisation means making such education familiar, habitual and part of daily life, in contrast to campaign-style efforts. Institutionalisation means giving it rule-governed, systematic, normative and dynamic safeguards. The authors present the two as mutually reinforcing, in a spiral of regularisation, institutionalisation, new regularisation and new institutionalisation. They hold that it supplies spiritual impetus for modernization and cultural reform, upholds Marxism's guiding position in ideology against what they describe as Western ideological infiltration, supports the Party's self-reform, and shapes young people's worldview and values.

For practice, Liu and Te call for mechanisms for ideals-and-convictions education itself, for cultivating civilisation, for cultural nourishment, for motivating talent, and for education in core socialist values. Their specific proposals include coordinating schools, families and communities, targeting different groups, promoting model figures and new-era civilisation practice centres, drawing on traditional, revolutionary and socialist culture, and supporting educators. Read the original if you want to see how Party-aligned ideological and political education scholarship defines and justifies this official formula and the institutional measures it proposes.
quoteEn: The institutionalisation of education in ideals and convictions is the rigid safeguard by which such education achieves its goals and performs its functions.
quoteZh: 理想信念教育制度化是理想信念教育实现其目标、发挥其功能的刚性保障。

glossary.explanation: A strand of Party ideological and political education that aims to instil Marxist belief, the communist ideal and the common ideal of socialism with Chinese characteristics, especially among Party members and young people.
The official term for China's path of development under Party leadership, presented as distinct from Western models and combining material and cultural-ethical advancement.

glossary.zh: 中国特色社会主义共同理想
glossary.en: the common ideal of socialism with Chinese characteristics
glossary.explanation: The official medium-term shared goal of building a modern socialist country and achieving national rejuvenation, usually paired with the long-term communist ideal.
An official formulation for the Party's continuous efforts to discipline and renew itself, stressed since the 18th Party Congress (2012).
A set of twenty-four characters in twelve values at the national, social and individual levels, promoted officially since the 18th Party Congress (2012).

t: The original contributions of General Secretary Xi Jinping's important statements on ideological and political theory courses
zh: 习近平总书记关于思想政治理论课重要论述的原创性贡献
source: Ideological and Political Education Research, 2025 no. 1
paras: This article from Ideological and Political Education Research (2025, no. 1) asks what is original in Xi Jinping's statements on ideological and political theory courses (sizhengke), the compulsory Marxist theory and moral-education courses taught from primary school to university. Qi and Zhu argue that since the 18th Party Congress (2012) Xi has answered three basic questions: what kind of course this is, why it must be run well, and how to run it well. In their account the result is a body of theory and practice that contributes to Marxist pedagogy and to the courses themselves.

The article is organised in three parts. The first treats Xi's new understanding of the courses' nature, covering their status and their essence. The second covers teaching theory, namely the "eight unifications" as a methodology and the "six requirements" for teachers. The third turns to practice and examines how Xi has reshaped the way the courses are organised. It draws on Xi's speeches, including the 2019 symposium for teachers of these courses, his visit to Renmin University of China, and the National Education Conference of September 2024.

On the courses' nature, the authors argue that Xi defines them as the key course for fulfilling the fundamental task of fostering virtue through education. They are not ordinary knowledge courses but courses in mainstream ideology and values. His formula that their essence is "to explain principles" (jiang daoli) uses reasoning as the link between political and academic content and between knowledge and values. The authors say this corrects the earlier tendency to lean towards either politics or knowledge. They read the eight unifications as eight pairs of contradictions, and the six requirements as a refinement of teacher-quality theory. In practice they credit Xi with three advances. The first is coordination between ideological-political courses and "ideological and political education across the curriculum" (kecheng sizheng). The second is integration of these courses across primary, secondary and tertiary stages. The third is the "great ideological and political course" (da sizhengke), which extends teachers, curricula, classrooms and teaching materials into society.

Qi and Zhu conclude that Xi's statements form a rigorous and wide-ranging system whose value has not been fully drawn out, and that it is still developing. They note that the 2024 National Education Conference listed "ideological and political leadership" first among the qualities of a strong education nation, and they call for continued study of Xi's contributions. Read the original if you want a Party-theory account of how Xi's discourse on Marxist education is framed and how the policy documents and practices behind it are described.
quoteEn: Xi Jinping's thesis on the essence of these courses uses \"principles\" as the mediating link to unify organically their political and academic character and their knowledge and value content, which is of important innovative significance.
quoteZh: 习近平总书记关于思政课本质的论断用“道理”作为中介实现了思政课政治性与学理性、知识性与价值性的有机统一，具有重要的创新意义。

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses in Marxist theory, Party history, morality and the rule of law taught from primary school to university in China. They are designed to instil the official ideology and values.
The stated fundamental task of Chinese education: cultivating moral character as well as knowledge. It has been stressed in official education policy since the 18th Party Congress.

glossary.en: ideological and political education across the curriculum
glossary.explanation: The practice of building ideological and moral education into all subjects, including professional and general courses, not only dedicated political courses. It began in Shanghai school reforms and was later promoted nationally.
A concept in which these courses draw on society as a whole, using outside speakers, practical sites, digital resources and real-life material alongside the classroom.
Xi's 2019 methodological principles for these courses, pairing politics with scholarly rigour, values with knowledge, and so on. They are presented as eight contradictions to be balanced.

keywords: ideological and political education across the curriculum

t: Teaching the "Great Ideological and Political Course" through social practice
st: A summer volunteer teaching project in rural northern Shaanxi
zh: 在社会实践中上好“大思政课”
source: Chinese Social Sciences Today (中国社会科学报), 4 June 2025
paras: This short commentary reports on how a teacher-training college puts the "Great Ideological and Political Course" into practice. Zheng and Wang describe a ten-day "Three Going to the Countryside" summer programme run by Suide Normal College of Yulin University from 21 July 2024 in Changjiagou village, Suide, Shaanxi. Under the theme of shouldering responsibility for Chinese modernization, the authors present it as a way for students to be educated, develop their abilities and contribute to society.

The article is organised as a descriptive account of the volunteers' work. It covers their daily classroom teaching, a set of specialist courses (paper-cutting, dance, calligraphy, origami, music, sport and writing) and two psychological team-building activities held with partner university teams. It closes with a reflection on what the experience means for the student volunteers.

The authors' main claim is that teaching in villages turns practical service into ideological and political education. They describe volunteers drawing on their teacher-training backgrounds, using varied methods and multimedia, and tailoring lessons to individual children. The specialist courses are said to pass on fine traditional Chinese culture, for example the paper-cut "zhuaji doll" and calligraphy. The team-building games are said to raise the children's mental health, teamwork and time management.

Zheng and Wang conclude that the programme helped students understand rural education and their future responsibilities as educators. They express confidence that the students will follow the school motto and grow into "striving youth" in step with the country and the people. Read the original if you want a concrete, institution-level example of how Chinese universities describe summer practice as ideological and political education.
quoteEn: The college's practice team of teachers and students boldly shoulders the burdens of the age, combines theory with practice, contributes the strength of youth on this hot land of northern Shaanxi, and earnestly teaches the "walking ideological and political course", supporting rural education.
quoteZh: 学院实践队师生勇挑时代重担,将理论与实践相结合,在陕北这块热土上贡献青春力量,认真上好“行走的思政课”,助力乡村教育

glossary.explanation: A policy concept promoting ideological and political education beyond the classroom, by linking it with social practice and real-world settings. It is associated with Xi Jinping's remarks on school ideological and political courses.

glossary.literal: three goings down to the countryside
glossary.explanation: A long-running summer programme in which university students take culture, science and technology, and health services to rural areas. Education support teaching is a common form.
The official term for China's path of modernization, promoted by the Party leadership since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.

t: Running high-quality affiliated schools to serve the high-quality and balanced development of basic education
zh: 办好高质量附校 服务基础教育优质均衡发展
paras: This short commentary from Guangming Daily asks how teacher-training universities can use their affiliated primary and secondary schools to serve high-quality, balanced development of basic education. Yan Shuai argues that such schools are the universities' "experimental fields" and a key strategy for building a leading education nation. The author holds that universities should run them in an organised way, since basic education is in a critical period of change.

The piece is built around three requirements for "organised" high-quality schooling: Party leadership and the right direction, an organisational advantage that raises quality and standards, and the effective mobilisation of both universities and schools as models for others. Each is developed in three concrete points.

On leadership, Yan calls for a clear political, popular and strategic orientation, schools sited in regions of national strategic priority, and reform of the leadership system in primary and secondary schools so that Party organisations play their leading role. The author also proposes integrated ideological and political education across university, middle and primary levels, with university Marxism schools guiding teaching and textbooks. On quality, Yan urges group-based, intensive school management; subject and talent support that helps schools interpret curriculum standards and use new textbooks; and teacher training that treats affiliated schools as a "second campus" for student teachers.

Yan concludes that universities should build communities for shared development, such as the university alliance for basic education led by Beijing Normal University. They should also develop products such as artificial intelligence, brain science, assessment and smart-campus tools, and spread the benefits of each good school to its wider region through shared resources, results and teacher training. Read the original if you want a brief official-style statement of how teacher-training universities are expected to link affiliated schools, Party building and regional basic education.
quoteEn: Running basic education affiliated schools well is an important strategy by which teacher-training universities serve the high-quality and balanced development of basic education.
quoteZh: 办好基础教育附属学校是高师院校服务基础教育优质均衡发展的重要战略。

glossary.literal: education great power / strong education country
glossary.explanation: A national goal of building a world-leading education system, promoted in Party documents and speeches in recent years.

t: Inheriting and innovating excellent traditional Chinese culture from the perspective of "education by all, throughout the process and in all respects"
zh: “三全育人”视角下中华优秀传统文化的传承与创新
paras: Zhang Wei and Yang Haiping ask how excellent traditional Chinese culture can be passed on and renewed within higher education. They take as their framework the concept of "education by all, throughout the process and in all respects" (sān quán yùrén). Their thesis is that inheritance should not be a simple replication of historical knowledge: core cultural values must be turned into educational resources that shape young people's values and support social and spiritual development.

The article is organised in three parts: holistic inheritance, innovation suited to the times, and multi-dimensional collaborative education. The first deals with how to build a systematic understanding of cultural roots. The second takes up digital technology, points of contact between tradition and modern society, and new forms of expression. The third sets out how schools, families, society and government can cooperate across the stages of a student's education. A short concluding section draws these together, and the authors note that the work is supported by national and Xinjiang-level research projects.

On inheritance, the authors call for a "whole–part–whole" logic and an attitude of sublation: outdated elements, such as the hierarchy of the culture of ritual (li), should be separated from still-useful ethical norms like respect for others and self-restraint. They warn against reducing tradition to fragmentary labels. On innovation, they argue that digital tools such as virtual scenes, short videos, AI-based learning applications and big-data analysis should reshape how culture is interpreted, but must stay oriented to cultural substance rather than "technology for technology's sake". Ideas like "harmony without uniformity" and "the Way follows nature" are said to speak to alienation and ecological problems. On collaboration, they propose staged teaching (cognition, critical reflection, innovative practice), informal settings such as campus design and student clubs, and pluralistic evaluation through projects and service feedback.

The authors conclude that transmitting this culture amounts to continuing and rebuilding cultural vitality, and to reproducing cultural subjectivity. They call on schools to make traditional culture a core aim of talent cultivation, on families to lead by example, and on society to respect tradition and encourage innovation. They propose a linked mechanism of "core positioning, innovative methods, system rebuilding" to move learners from cultural consciousness to cultural confidence. Read the original if you want an example of how Chinese ideological and political education scholars link traditional culture to the "three-whole" education framework and to practical curriculum and evaluation design.
quoteEn: The vitality of traditional culture lies in its dynamic adaptation to the context of the times.
quoteZh: 传统文化的生命力在于其与时代语境的动态适配。

glossary.en: education by all, throughout the process and in all respects
glossary.explanation: A policy concept in Chinese higher education, calling for all staff, every stage of schooling and all settings to take part in moral and ideological education. It is used to coordinate ideological and political work across the university.
A dialectical term (Hegel's Aufhebung, adopted by Marx) meaning to negate while preserving what is valuable. Chinese authors often use it to describe critically retaining parts of tradition.
A concept stressed in Party discourse since the 2010s, referring to confidence in the value and vitality of Chinese culture, including traditional and socialist culture.
The idea that a nation should hold an independent, self-aware position in its own cultural development rather than depending on outside models.

t: Methodological guidance for ideological and political education of children and teenagers
zh: 做好少年儿童思想政治教育的方法论指引
paras: This commentary asks how ideological and political education for children and teenagers can be done well. Li argues that Xi Jinping's "sixteen-character" requirement, first set out in 2014 at a Children's Day event in Beijing, offers a methodological guide: remember the requirements, have role models in mind, start from an early age, and accept help.

The piece is a short People's Daily article. It reads each of the four phrases against educational principles and links them to Xi Jinping's remarks at the 2025 "two sessions" on coordinating classroom teaching with society as a "big classroom". It ends with a brief assessment of results over the past decade or so and of new challenges.

Li makes three main moves. First, the four phrases embody the unity of knowing and doing: remembering the requirements is the base of knowledge, role models turn knowing into doing, starting small shapes conduct, and help from teachers and parents bridges the two. Second, the phrases follow the cycle of practice, understanding, renewed practice and deeper understanding, and Li says this addresses the gap between theory and practice in traditional education. Third, they call for teaching suited to the pupil, using stories and analogies to explain demanding ideas to young children, and for timely answers to current problems such as competing over possessions or ignoring advice. Li cites Xi's remarks on these.

Li concludes that the education system has made clear progress under this guidance, citing stronger curriculum channels, role-model teachers and practice-based education. Li notes that the information age brings new demands, and calls for the Party's leadership and broad mobilisation of social forces. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official commentary draws a method for moral and political education of the young from Xi Jinping's remarks.
quoteEn: Ideological and political education differs significantly from knowledge education: it is not simply the teaching of theoretical knowledge but takes the unity of knowing and doing as its goal.
quoteZh: 思想政治教育与知识教育有着重要区别，它并非单纯传授理论知识，而是以知行合一为目标

glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's 2014 formulation for children practising core socialist values: 记住要求、心有榜样、从小做起、接受帮助. It is now widely cited in school moral education.
A concept from Chinese philosophical tradition, associated with Wang Yangming, and used in Party education discourse for linking understanding with practice.
A traditional Chinese pedagogical principle of adapting teaching to each learner's abilities and characteristics.

t: Integrating volunteer service education into ideological and political theory courses
zh: 将志愿服务教育融入思政课
paras: This short commentary, published in the People's Daily on 3 June 2025, asks how volunteer service education can be built into the ideological and political theory courses (sizheng ke) taught in Chinese schools and universities. Li Zhishui argues that these courses carry an important mission in guiding students to uphold the volunteer spirit and contribute their youthful strength.

The piece opens with Xi Jinping's May Fourth reply to a volunteer teaching team in the western border region and a April 2024 General Office guideline on improving the volunteer service system for the new era. That guideline calls for volunteer service to be made part of moral education for minors and ideological and political education for university students. Li then sets out three principles.

The first is to combine serving the people with a global outlook. Li proposes drawing on cases such as student volunteers at China Agricultural University's science and technology courtyards and environmental volunteers in the Danjiangkou reservoir area, and encouraging participation in international volunteer projects where feasible. The second is to combine classroom teaching with practice: Marxist principles and Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era should explain volunteering's significance for Chinese modernization, supported by "walking" ideological and political classes in the community. The third is to link focused goals with continuity across school stages.

On the third principle, Li calls for integrated planning from primary school to university: storytelling for primary pupils, responsibility education through practice in middle school, and theoretical explanation at university that turns emotional experience into value conviction. Read the original if you want a brief example of how official guidance on volunteering is being translated into teaching recommendations for ideological and political courses.
quoteEn: Ideological and political theory courses bear the important mission of volunteer service education and are a key venue for guiding students to uphold the volunteer spirit and contribute their youthful strength.
quoteZh: 思政课承担着开展志愿服务教育的重要使命，是引领学生弘扬志愿精神、贡献青春力量的重要阵地。

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses in Marxism and Party ideology taught at all levels of Chinese education, intended to shape students' political and moral outlook.
The official term for China's path of modernization under Party leadership, prominent in Party discourse since the 20th Party Congress (2022).

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017 and 2018.

t: Teaching the deeper logic of upholding and developing socialism with Chinese characteristics
zh: 讲好坚持和发展中国特色社会主义的深层次逻辑
source: Journal of Ideological and Theoretical Education (Sixiang lilun jiaoyu daokan), 2025 no. 2
paras: This teaching-oriented article takes up Chapter 1 of the university textbook Introduction to Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, whose theme is socialism with Chinese characteristics. Li Guoquan argues that the chapter's core and most difficult teaching task is to explain the deeper logic of upholding and developing this socialism. In Li's account, its distinctive features rest on four logics: historical, cultural, theoretical and practical.

The article is organised in four sections, one per logic. Each identifies the key points to be conveyed to students, flags the "difficult" teaching problems, and suggests examples or quotations from Xi Jinping to use in class. It covers the 500-year history of socialism, the relation between the periods before and after reform and opening up, the role of traditional Chinese culture, the doctrine of scientific socialism, and the features of the new era.

On the historical logic, Li says teachers must show socialism with Chinese characteristics as the outcome of world socialism's development and of the Party's long search for its own path. The two historical periods before and after reform and opening up should be presented as continuous, and Li warns that separating them amounts to historical nihilism aimed at discrediting the Party's path. On the cultural logic, Li holds that the continuity of Chinese civilisation determines that China must follow its own path, and that the Two Integrations, especially the "second integration" with traditional culture, supply cultural subjectivity and governance resources. On the theoretical logic, Li argues that this socialism fits scientific socialism through Party leadership, public ownership, distribution according to work and a socialist market economy, and that it accords with Marxist laws of social development and the view that the people make history.

On the practical logic, Li lists five ways in which the new era is new: the changed principal contradiction in society, a new leap in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, new strategic goals, a changed relationship between China and the world, and a renewed Party shaped by the Party's self-reform. Li describes the endeavour as a great social revolution and as the necessary road to national rejuvenation and Chinese modernization. Teachers should reinforce students' confidence in the path through historical and international comparison. Read the original if you want to see how a Party-school-style syllabus for this textbook chapter frames its key arguments, difficult points and teaching examples.
quoteEn: Upholding socialism with Chinese characteristics is an essential requirement of Chinese modernization, and the two are fundamentally consistent.
quoteZh: 坚持中国特色社会主义是中国式现代化的本质要求，两者具有本质上的一致性

glossary.explanation: Formula in Xi Jinping's thought: combining the basic principles of Marxism with China's specific realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture. The 'second integration' with traditional culture was stressed from 2021–23.
Official concept, prominent since the 20th Party Congress (2022), describing China's own path to modernization as socialist and adapted to national conditions.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: Official formula for the continuing process of applying Marxism to China's conditions and updating it for the contemporary era.
Term used since the 18th Party Congress (2012) for the Party's efforts to discipline itself and correct its own problems, linked to full and rigorous self-governance of the Party.
Official label for views seen as denying or discrediting the Party's history and socialist achievements, including by setting the pre- and post-1978 periods against each other.

Concept used to define the stage of China's development. Since the 19th Party Congress (2017) it is defined as the contradiction between people's growing needs for a better life and unbalanced, inadequate development.

t: Conditions for applying artificial intelligence in ideological and political education
zh: 思想政治教育应用人工智能的实现条件
source: Journal of Ideological and Theoretical Education (Sixiang lilun jiaoyu daokan), 2025 no. 2
paras: Chang Yanhui takes up a gap in work on ideological and political education (sixiang zhengzhi jiaoyu) and artificial intelligence. Existing studies, the author says, infer from AI's technical features how it might empower the field, but they seldom consider what conditions are needed for real-world adoption. The article argues that a discussion of prospects should be both imaginative and realistic. It therefore sets out the likely uses of AI and then the technical conditions and the norms that would make those uses possible.

The article has three parts. The first explains the principles of current generative AI (ChatGPT, DeepSeek, Doubao and similar products), which Chang describes as specialised, weak AI built on data, algorithms and computing power, and then lists application scenarios. The second discusses the technical conditions: national policy support, energy and computing costs, the data to be used in training, and the role of educators in development. The third proposes rules for standards, data collection, market access, content review and legal compliance.

Chang argues that AI can support academic research by gathering literature and public-opinion data and generating new forms of presentation. It can also act as a teaching assistant, producing text-to-video scenes for abstract value concepts and supporting differentiated, targeted outreach, as the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) urged. For these uses Chang calls for three kinds of data to be fed into models: published research, the Party's accumulated teaching experience, and longitudinal data on students and teachers. Ideological and political educators, Chang says, should help build industry-specific models by advising on parameters, vetting data quality and giving feedback. Because the field bears on national ideological security and students' wellbeing, the author proposes authoritative third-party assessment of 'intelligent' products, schools keeping control of data collection instead of leaving it to internet firms, and entry rules for products. Chang notes that the opacity of AI results conflicts with the transparency that the field requires, so important decisions must stay with human educators.

Chang further proposes review of AI-generated content under the principle of political standards first, upholding Marxism's guiding position and guiding algorithm design with core socialist values. In Chang's account, domestic AI products tend to hold the correct political stance, while some foreign products conceal liberal values behind a show of neutrality. The article also calls for rules grounded in the Data Security Law and the Personal Information Protection Law, with data classified into four types: ideological security, students' political views, physical and mental health, and diverse lifestyles. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese scholar of ideological and political education sets out the practical, regulatory and ideological conditions for adopting AI in that field.
quoteEn: Scenarios for applying AI in ideological and political education
quoteZh: 思想政治教育应用人工智能的场景

glossary.explanation: The Party-state's system of value and political education in schools, universities and other institutions, and also an academic discipline within Marxist theory studies in China.

t: Bringing into play universities' role as a vanguard force in scientific and technological innovation
zh: 发挥高校科技创新生力军作用
paras: This commentary, published in the China Social Sciences Today in May 2025, asks how Chinese universities can serve as a vanguard force in scientific and technological innovation. Ren Xiaolong, a university Party secretary, argues that Chinese modernization depends on technological modernization and that science and technology support is a defining trait of a socialist education powerhouse with Chinese characteristics. Universities, as the meeting point of education, science and talent, should be guided by the spirit of scientists and oriented to national strategic needs.

The piece is organised in three parts. The first concerns inheriting and promoting the spirit of scientists as a source of motivation. The second concerns improving research systems and mechanisms. The third concerns building a virtuous cycle among education, science and technology, and talent. Ren draws throughout on speeches by Xi Jinping, the 2021 Central Talent Work Conference and the decision of the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) on deepening reform.

On the first point, Ren presents the spirit of scientists as part of the Chinese Communists' spiritual lineage. It should shape the research workforce, stimulate creativity and nurture young people, with teachers serving as models and the spirit written into the task of fostering virtue and cultivating talent. On the second, Ren calls for universities to align basic research with national strategic needs and to target 'bottleneck' technologies. They should also move from 'papers to papers' topic selection towards organised research, use the new type of whole-nation system, and strengthen links with enterprises and local governments so that results are converted into industry applications.

On the third, Ren proposes adjusting disciplines dynamically to national needs, advancing the 'new engineering, new medicine, new agriculture and new liberal arts' initiatives, and combining science education with the humanities. Universities should also build up strategic scientific talent, focus policy on young talent, and continue reforms that end the 'five onlys' in evaluation. They should create management based on trust, respect and tolerance. Ren concludes that these measures would let universities contribute more to building a leading scientific and technological power and advancing Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want an example of how a Chinese university leader translates central policy language on science, talent and education into institutional tasks.
quoteEn: Universities, as the meeting point of education, science and talent, and especially as an important base for basic research and major technological breakthroughs, should give full play to their role as a vanguard force in scientific and technological innovation.
quoteZh: 高校作为教育、科技、人才的集中交汇点，尤其是作为基础研究与重大科技突破的重要阵地，应充分发挥科技创新生力军作用

glossary.explanation: The official Party formulation of China's own path to modernization, prominent in Party documents since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
An officially promoted set of values for scientists, including patriotism, dedication, innovation and seeking truth. It is treated as part of the Chinese Communists' spiritual lineage.
A policy concept for mobilising state, market and institutional resources in a concentrated way on major scientific and technological tasks.
A model in which research is planned and coordinated around national strategic goals and large projects, rather than driven by individual topics.

t: Digital empowerment of integrated reform and innovation in ideological and political courses across university, secondary and primary schools
zh: 数字化赋能大中小学思政课一体化改革创新
paras: Pan Jingang takes up how digital technology can advance the integrated development of ideological and political courses (sizheng ke) across primary, secondary and tertiary education. Pan frames the question with the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), which called for integrated reform of these courses, and with the 2025 National Education Work Conference, which called for continuing the national education digitalization strategy. The article's thesis is that digital technology can break down barriers between school stages, reform teaching models and innovate institutions, producing a pattern of collaborative education that raises teaching quality.

This is a short commentary from the Chinese Social Sciences Today (23 May 2025), and it is a stage result of a National Social Science Fund project on Xi Jinping's statements on school ideological and political courses. It is organised in three parts: building integrated shared platforms, integrating teaching, learning and evaluation, and promoting collaborative education. Each part is supported by quotations from Xi Jinping.

Pan's first argument concerns platforms. Digital resource libraries, unified data standards and a big-data monitoring centre are presented as a remedy for scattered teaching materials and "data islands". Pan adds that natural language processing and knowledge graphs can link moral cultivation in primary school, political understanding in secondary school and theoretical deepening at university into a progressive sequence. The second argument is about teaching and teachers. Big-data analysis and machine learning are said to build individual learning profiles, which allow more precise teaching and richer evaluation than exam scores. Pan also proposes training courses in digital skills for teachers and incentives that count digital teaching results in promotion and appraisal.

Pan concludes that digital empowerment is a complex systemic project needing work on top-level design, institutional mechanisms and platform building. Pan proposes a leadership mechanism of Party committee unified leadership, joint management by Party and government, and divisions of labour among departments. Pan also proposes a unified evaluation system across all stages, digital training platforms and pairing of schools in developed and less developed regions to narrow the digital divide, and links between schools, families and society, so that the classroom and the "big classroom" of society work together. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Chinese education officials and scholars connect digitalization policy with ideological and political education.
