quoteEn: Digital technology has broken the boundaries of school education, providing convenient channels of communication and collaborative platforms for building an ecosystem of ideological and political education in which family, school and society educate together.
quoteZh: 数字技术打破了学校教育的边界，为构建家庭、学校、社会协同育人的思政教育生态提供了便捷的沟通渠道和协作平台。

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses in Marxist theory, Party policy, morality and law taught from primary school to university in China. Their content and teaching are overseen by the Party and education authorities.
Unequal access to, and ability to use, digital technology. Here it refers to gaps among teachers and between schools in different regions.

t: Key points for building a knowledge system of online ideological and political education
zh: 构建网络思想政治教育知识体系的着力点
paras: This short commentary asks how to build an autonomous knowledge system for online ideological and political education, a field that emerged after China's full internet connection in 1994. The authors say the field has produced many studies and trained many specialists. They also say it still fits new conditions imperfectly, lacks completeness and systematic order, and needs greater practical effect. They propose three priorities: grounding the system in Chinese reality, enriching its content, and organising it systematically.

The piece opens by citing the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), whose Decision calls for differentiated and targeted mechanisms for online moral and ideological education. It then takes the three priorities in turn. The first is autonomy, which the authors treat in terms of theory and practice. The second is the breadth of knowledge. The third is systematisation through principles, methods, and evaluation and governance.

On autonomy, the authors argue that the system should be guided by Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era and rooted in China's online practice, citing the scale of China's internet users and digital economy. They describe a basic logic running from network information technology to people's thought and behaviour to online education. Within it they distinguish three kinds of knowledge: preparatory technical knowledge, composite analytical knowledge drawn from several disciplines, and practical professional knowledge. To remedy fragmentation, they call for an integrated system. It would have a principles system that responds to artificial intelligence, a methods system combining adapted classic methods with big-data, algorithmic-push and human–machine approaches, and an evaluation and governance system.

The authors conclude that evaluation and governance let the knowledge system assess, absorb feedback and renew itself. They call for evaluation indicators, behavioural data analysis, intelligent platforms, and ethical, legal and self-regulatory rules. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how Chinese ideological education scholars frame the digital-age agenda of this field.
quoteEn: Online ideological and political education is the product of combining the internet with ideological and political education.
quoteZh: 网络思想政治教育是互联网与思想政治教育相结合的产物。

glossary.explanation: A Chinese academic discipline, founded in 1984, and a field of practice concerned with shaping people's political views, ideals and moral conduct in line with Party-state guidance.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The official guiding ideology of the Communist Party of China, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017 and 2018.
A term in current Chinese scholarship and policy for a body of concepts and theories developed from China's own conditions rather than drawn from foreign frameworks.

t: Comprehensively advancing digital-intelligence technologies to empower educational transformation
zh: 全面推进数智技术赋能教育变革
paras: This short commentary, published in Guangming Daily after the 2025 World Digital Education Conference in Wuhan, asks how digital and AI technologies should be used to transform education. Luo and Tian argue that advancing digital-intelligence empowerment across the whole education system is a shared choice of countries worldwide, and that China must pursue it while keeping a correct value orientation.

The article opens with examples from the conference's exhibition, such as virtual simulation platforms and AI calligraphy analysis. It then sketches how education and technology have shaped each other, from oral-era apprenticeship to print-era classroom teaching. It cites international moves (UNESCO's 2023 guidance on generative AI, South Korea's AI education plans, the UK's 2024 document) and China's policy documents, including the Education Power Construction Plan (2024–2035).

The authors report that, three years into the national education digitalization strategy, China's overall level of education modernization has entered the ranks of upper-middle-income countries. They also cite the world's largest education resource base, more than 60.8 billion views on the national smart education platform, and 590 million person-times of benefit from MOOCs in western regions. They also name remaining gaps: a low share of high-skilled talent, uneven coverage of quality resources, and insufficient digital literacy among teachers and students. Their answer is to hold to fostering virtue through education and a people-centred orientation, to integrate AI into all elements of teaching and talent training, and to deepen international exchange.

Luo and Tian call for lifelong learning, including AI ethics and the ability to judge digital information. They also call for stronger digital leadership among administrators, digital teaching ability among teachers, and higher-order thinking among students. They present this as support for high-quality development, for building China into a leading education country with Chinese characteristics, and for the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want a brief, official-style account of China's education digitalization policy and the figures used to promote it.
quoteEn: Humanity becomes civilized through education, and education develops through technology.
quoteZh: 人类因教育而文明，教育因科技而发展。

glossary.explanation: An official economic and social goal since 2017 that stresses quality, efficiency and innovation over speed of growth. Here it is applied to education.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party slogan describing the goal of restoring China to national strength and prosperity, closely tied to the Chinese Dream.
The official fundamental task of education in China: moral and ideological cultivation alongside knowledge and skills.

t: Enhancing the appeal and relevance of ideological and political education
st: Liaocheng's experience in building a "grand ideological and political course"
zh: 提升思想政治教育亲和力针对性
paras: This short commentary, published in Study Times in May 2025, is a work report by the head of the education authority in Liaocheng, Shandong. Cui Wei describes how the city is raising the appeal and relevance of ideological and political education. The author presents ideological and political courses as the key means of fulfilling the fundamental task of fostering virtue through education, and says Liaocheng is building a "grand" classroom, platform and teaching force.

The text is organised around three areas of work: the teaching force, the reform and innovation of the "grand ideological and political course", and the consolidation of schools as the main sites of this work. It gives local figures and examples, and closes with a pledge to keep studying Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era.

On teachers, Cui reports 10,782 ideological and political teachers in the city, 3,966 of them full-time. The measures listed are training, a mentoring scheme, master-teacher studios, equal treatment with other subjects in promotion and awards, and a municipal expert pool of 103 teachers. On the courses, the author describes combining red and local resources, using digital micro-courses and cloud classrooms, linking primary, secondary and tertiary teaching, and building local brands such as "Two Rivers ideological education". On school leadership, Cui describes Party and government leaders teaching these courses, principals bearing first responsibility, practice bases, three-tier collective lesson preparation, and quantified evaluation of teachers by students, peers and experts.

Cui concludes that the bureau will keep implementing the Party's education policy and contribute to building China into a leading education power. Read the original if you want a concrete example of how a Chinese municipal education bureau reports on implementing national policy for ideological and political courses.
quoteEn: Upholding the principle that ideological and political courses come first, the city integrates the resources of its universities, middle schools and primary schools, and pushes joint construction and joint research to raise the level of integrated development of these courses.
quoteZh: 秉持“思政课是第一课”建设理念，凝聚整合全市高校、中学、小学的思政资源，全力推进共建、共研，提高思政课一体化发展水平

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses in Marxism, Party theory, morality and law taught at all levels of Chinese schooling. They are treated officially as the core channel of political education.
An official formulation of the fundamental task of education in China: moral and political formation alongside knowledge.
A policy concept that extends political education beyond the classroom into society, practice bases and online platforms, linking it with social resources.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The official guiding ideology of the Communist Party of China, written into the Party and state constitutions.
An official goal of making China a world leader in education, promoted in recent national planning.

t: Empowering teaching innovation in university ideological and political courses with digital-intelligence technology
zh: 以数智技术赋能高校思政课教学创新
paras: This short commentary, published in Guangming Daily in May 2025, asks how big data, intelligent algorithms and virtual reality can improve university ideological and political courses (sizheng ke). Ke Meng argues that traditional classes suffer from abstract content, one-way instruction and delayed evaluation, which clash with the differentiated, flexible and scenario-based learning needs of students born after 2000. In Ke's view, digital-intelligence technology can resolve these problems and serve the fundamental task of fostering virtue through education.

The article opens with a statement by Xi Jinping on reform, innovation and online education, then proposes three practical paths: optimising teaching resources for precise instruction, building a teaching model of multidimensional interaction and value resonance, and creating an intelligent system of evaluation and feedback.

On resources, Ke proposes knowledge graphs that link textbook content, cases and videos; multidimensional digital student profiles with algorithmic recommendation, for example sending explanatory videos on surplus-value theory to students who are unclear about it; and large-language-model teaching assistants that answer questions around the clock. On interaction, Ke describes mixed-reality classrooms in which students take part in a simulated land-reform meeting, digital-twin tours of model villages to illustrate common prosperity, on-screen comment streams analysed by AI, and policy decision simulations. On evaluation, Ke suggests multimodal data collection, automated marking with teacher review, multi-source assessment of teachers and instant micro-surveys.

Ke concludes that these tools can shift teaching from "flood irrigation" to "precision drip irrigation", turning abstract theory into emotional identification and giving teachers timely data to refine their work. Read the original if you want a concise, practice-oriented account of how digital technologies are being proposed for Party-line political education in Chinese universities.
quoteEn: [This helps] shift teaching in ideological and political courses from "flood irrigation" to "precision drip irrigation".
quoteZh: 使思政课教学从“大水漫灌”向“精准滴灌”转变。

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses in Chinese universities teaching Marxism, Party history and official political theory, treated as a core channel of political education.
An official formulation describing the fundamental task of education as shaping students' moral and political character as well as their knowledge.
A policy goal stressed under Xi Jinping, referring to prosperity shared by all the people rather than a few.

t: Promoting the deep integration of moral education and running it through the whole process of nurturing students
zh: 推动德育深度融入 有效贯穿育人全过程
paras: This short commentary, published in Guangming Daily in May 2025, responds to Xi Jinping's remarks during the 2025 Two Sessions that moral education should run through intellectual, physical, aesthetic and labour education. Meng and Han argue that moral education must be deeply integrated with the other four strands. They say this requires systems thinking and an all-staff, whole-process, all-round pattern of nurturing students.

The article takes the four pairings in turn: moral and intellectual education, moral and physical education, moral and aesthetic education, and moral and labour education. Each section describes a current shortcoming, traces its cause and proposes remedies. The authors cite the Plan for Building a Strong Education Country (2024–2035) as policy background.

In the authors' account, each pairing is held back by treating moral education as an add-on. Schools favour knowledge over values, rely on slogans in sport, teach art technique without value guidance, and reduce labour education to simple manual tasks. They attribute these problems to exam-oriented habits and to evaluation systems that count fitness scores, competition results or skills but not moral value.

The authors propose dual teaching goals and a two-dimensional evaluation of knowledge mastery and value internalisation. They also call for sport and art courses that embed rule-following, teamwork, resilience and patriotic feeling, and for labour projects with ethical content backed by cooperation among families, schools and society. The aim is to cultivate well-rounded builders and successors of socialism. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official education policy on moral education is explained to teachers and school administrators.
quoteEn: Moral education forges the soul of physical education.
quoteZh: 德育为体育铸魂

glossary.explanation: Education in morals, values and ideology in Chinese schools. It is often tied to the fundamental task of fostering virtue through education (立德树人).
The annual plenary meetings of the National People's Congress and the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference, held each March.

t: Raising the quality and effectiveness of universities' service to the integrated development of scientific and industrial innovation
zh: 提升高校服务科技创新和产业创新融合发展的质效
paras: Ma Xiaojie, Party Secretary of Lanzhou University, asks how universities can better serve the integration of scientific and technological innovation with industrial innovation. Opening with Xi Jinping's statement that the two are the basic path to developing new quality productive forces, Ma argues that universities should build a mutually supporting system of talent training, scientific innovation and the transfer of results into practice.

The article has three parts. The first explains why the integration of the two kinds of innovation matters for new quality productive forces and high-quality development, and why universities are a key link. The second sets out the three-part university system, describing changes in each of its legs. The third offers five practical directions: talent training, discipline layout, the supply of research, the transfer of results, and Party-building and innovation culture. Ma supports the argument throughout with quotations from Xi Jinping and the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024).

Ma's central claim is that the three functions of universities must develop together rather than separately. In talent training, Ma sees a shift from supply-driven to demand-driven education, from disciplinary silos to interdisciplinary work, and from a closed campus to an open ecosystem. In research, Ma calls for organised research, a chain running from knowledge creation through technology transfer to industrial application, and a new national system for pooling major resources. On transfer, Ma urges concept-verification systems, pilot-scale platforms, reformed rights-sharing and evaluation that counts industrial service. The aim is research that is both 'reaching the sky' and 'standing on the ground'.

Ma concludes that universities should use their strengths to co-define problems with firms, train talent jointly, tackle research challenges together and share in turning results into products. Ma calls for ideological and political education in the spirit of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, dual mentors from academia and industry, discipline 'special zones', AI-enabled curricula and Party branches built on research platforms and transfer projects. These steps are said to feed Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want a Party-affiliated university leader's concrete policy agenda for linking higher education, research commercialisation and industrial policy.
quoteEn: In promoting scientific and technological innovation, universities must both 'reach the sky' and 'stand on the ground'.
quoteZh: 高校推动科技创新，既要“顶天”，也要“立地”。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2023 for advanced productive forces driven by innovation, high technology, high efficiency and high quality. It is used to guide industrial upgrading and technology policy.
The official goal of shifting China's economy from rapid growth towards quality, efficiency and innovation-led growth.
The Party's official term for China's own path to modernization, set out prominently at the 20th Party Congress (2022).

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology since 2017, written into the Party and state constitutions.
A policy approach in which universities steer research towards national strategic needs through coordinated teams and platforms, rather than relying only on individual researchers' free exploration.
An official term for mobilising state, enterprise and academic resources nationwide to achieve major scientific and technological breakthroughs under market conditions.

t: Decoding the "One Core, Two Wings, Three Cultures, Four Histories" model of ideological and political education
zh: 解码“一核二翼三文四史”思政育人模式
paras: This short commentary, published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in April 2025, describes the "One Core, Two Wings, Three Cultures, Four Histories" model of ideological and political education that Beijing has piloted. Jiang presents it as a successful local experience that offers lessons for building ideological and political courses in schools and universities nationwide. The model is tied to the "big ideological and political course" and to integrating such education across primary, secondary and tertiary levels.

The article first explains the model's four components. It then reports a May 2024 Beijing call for course-based ideological and political education results, and lists four measures taken to promote integration across school stages.

Jiang defines the "core" as Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. The "two wings" are dedicated ideological and political courses and ideological content built into other subjects. The "three cultures" are fine traditional, revolutionary and advanced socialist culture, and the "four histories" are the histories of the Party, New China, reform and opening up, and socialism. On results, the author reports 261 submissions from the city's 17 districts, about four-fifths of them teaching case designs, for example literature lessons drawing on classical works and physics lessons recounting Chinese scientists' stories. The measures are a provincial-level guideline on integration, five pilot zones, a digital map of over 200 practice-teaching bases, and a 34-member expert committee.

Jiang concludes that the model systematically integrates ideological and political content and brings it closer to students' lives and level of understanding. The author calls it a meaningful attempt and exploration, not a finished solution. Read the original if you want a concise official-style account of how Beijing structures ideological and political education across school stages, and of the policy measures behind it.
quoteEn: The "One Core, Two Wings, Three Cultures, Four Histories" model systematically and organically integrates the content of ideological and political education, bringing it closer to students' real lives and cognitive level, and is undoubtedly a meaningful attempt and exploration.
quoteZh: “一核二翼三文四史”的育人模式，将思政教育的内容进行系统整合和有机融合，使思政教育更加贴近学生的生活实际和认知水平，无疑是一次有意义的尝试和探索。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The official guiding ideology of the Communist Party of China, written into the Party and state constitutions. It is the "core" of the Beijing model.
A policy concept that extends ideological and political education beyond the classroom into society, practice bases and online resources.
The histories of the Party, New China, reform and opening up, and the development of socialism, promoted as core study content in Party education.
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world begun in China in 1978.

t: Raising university teachers' ideological and political leadership through the "four guides"
zh: 以“四个引路人”提升高校教师的思政引领力
source: China Social Sciences Today (中国社会科学报), 24 April 2025
paras: Wang Gang takes up a concept Xi Jinping first used at the National Education Conference in September 2024: "ideological and political leadership" (sizheng yinlingli), placed first among the six strengths of a strong education nation. Wang argues that for university teachers of ideological and political courses, Xi's call to be "guides" in four respects offers the fundamental guideline for raising this capacity. The four are shaping character, acquiring knowledge, innovative thinking and dedication to the motherland.
This short commentary in a newspaper devotes one section to each of the four guides. Each section sets out three tasks for teachers. A closing section treats the four as a single system.

In Wang's account, character is built through teachers' own ethics, value guidance and a sense of rules. Knowledge rests on solid scholarship, effective teaching methods and taking students out into society through "walking" classes. Innovative thinking is cultivated through heuristic teaching, free expression and intelligent technology such as VR and AI. Dedication to the country is nurtured through family-and-country feeling, a sense of mission and digital tools, including a proposed assessment system for students' patriotic sentiment. Wang presents the four as a closed loop of values, knowledge, methodology and attachment to family and country.

Wang concludes that teachers who consistently take the "four guides" as their guideline will raise ideological and political leadership and train a new generation able to carry the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. The piece is a prescriptive statement of Party-line pedagogy, with examples from classroom practice. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Xi's educational directives are being turned into teaching guidance for university ideological and political courses.
quoteEn: The "four guides" do not exist in isolation, but form a closed loop of education running from outlook on values to outlook on knowledge, methodology and views of family and country.
quoteZh: “四个引路人”并非孤立存在，而是一个“价值观—知识观—方法论—家国观”的育人闭环。

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central goal of Party discourse since the early 2010s, referring to restoring China's national strength and international standing by the mid-twenty-first century.

t: Continuously strengthening the targeting of ideological and political theory courses
zh: 不断增强思政课的针对性
paras: This short commentary, published in China Social Sciences Today in April 2025, takes up one of the four qualities Xi Jinping has asked of university ideological and political theory courses (sixiang zheng zhi ke): ideological depth, theoretical rigour, affinity and targeting. Ren Peng argues that targeting (zhenduixing) is the most basic precondition, because depth, rigour and approachable language all depend on it to reach, guide and win over students.

The article first explains why targeting matters and then diagnoses present shortcomings. It ends with practical proposals. Ren defines targeting as a precise fit between what is taught and what students need, with the student at the centre and content and methods adjusted to different learners.

On the case for targeting, Ren offers three reasons: it determines teaching effectiveness, since the courses differ in whether they stress principles, history or values and should not be taught uniformly; it answers students' confusions, such as those over "involution" and "lying flat"; and it serves the fundamental task of cultivating successors to the socialist cause. On the problems, Ren points to three: teachers' limited grasp of students' varied thinking, teachers' own capacity and thin practical experience, and teaching methods that lag behind, including superficial use of AI and VR and a gap between textbook and online language.

Ren proposes that teachers adopt a "user mindset", carry out first-hand research among students and tailor courses to different majors. They should also draw fresh material from reform and development practice. On method, Ren calls for genuine use of big data and AI in "digital integration" of courses, and for recasting academic, policy and textbook language into the idiom of young people. Read the original if you want a concise example of how a Party-school scholar frames the aims and practical problems of ideological and political course reform in 2025.
quoteEn: The essence of ideological and political courses is reasoning; explaining reasons deeply and thoroughly requires targeting, and making them lively requires it even more.
quoteZh: 思政课的本质是讲道理，把道理讲深讲透需要针对性，讲活更需要针对性。

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses on Marxism, Party theory, Party and national history and moral and legal education, taught at all Chinese universities. Usually abbreviated as sizheng ke.

t: Multidimensional innovation in building ideological and political courses in the new era
zh: 新时代思政课建设的多维创新
paras: This short commentary asks how practical teaching in university ideological and political courses (sizheng ke) can overcome the problem of 'stressing theoretical indoctrination while neglecting practical cultivation'. Deng argues that the answer is to build practice teaching around General Secretary Xi Jinping's inspection tours of localities, guided by the principle of unifying theory and practice within the 'Eight Unifications'. The aim is to let students move between the 'small classroom' of the course and the 'big classroom' of society.

The article is organised around one main line, two driving forces, a three-dimensional content system and four types of teaching vehicle. It cites Xi's remarks on the 'great ideological and political course', on teacher guidance and student-centred teaching, and on content drawn from socialism with Chinese characteristics. It closes by linking the model to the Outline for Building a Strong Education Nation (2024–2035).

Deng's central moves are as follows. First, local inspection sites supply concrete cases that tie general policy to familiar places and people, which the author says counters fragmented resources, abstract theory and shallow emotion. Second, teachers' leading role and students' initiative are combined through learning-profile modelling with intelligent technology, interdisciplinary work and government–enterprise–university cooperation. Third, content is organised under four themes: rural revitalisation, cultural heritage, science and technology, and ecology. It is delivered through mobile classrooms, short films, online writing in Gen-Z idiom and think-tank-style reports.

Deng concludes that turning inspection routes into teaching routes is a creative application of the unity of theory and practice and a contemporary practice of the Marxist view of practice. In Deng's account it moves students from 'ideological awakening' to 'awakening to mission'. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Chinese scholars propose to build leader-centred local case studies into university political-course teaching.
quoteEn: Using small entry points to explain big principles, students start from concrete, tangible cases and gradually build a cognitive framework for abstract theory.
quoteZh: 以小切口讲大道理,学生从具体可感的案例切入,逐步搭建对抽象理论的认知框架

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses in Marxism, Party theory and moral education taught in Chinese schools and universities.
Eight principles for teaching ideological and political courses set out by Xi Jinping in 2019, including the unity of theory and practice.
A slogan promoted by Xi Jinping urging that political education be linked with real social life and not confined to classrooms.

t: The current state of ideological and political short videos and paths to improving their reach
zh: 思政短视频传播的现实镜像与优化路径
paras: Short videos have become a new platform for ideological and political education in universities, but Liu argues that their communication effect is held back by weak production teams and distorting platform algorithms. Writing in April 2025, the author links the question to the Education Power Plan Outline (2024–2035), which calls for deeper integration of ideological and political work with information technology. Liu holds that raising the quality of such videos is the best way to build a distinctive online ideological and political education brand.

This short newspaper commentary has two parts. It first describes three problems: formulaic content, weakly professional operating teams, and value drift under recommendation algorithms. It then proposes four remedies covering content, teams, algorithms and an intelligent communication ecosystem.

On content, Liu criticises the "teacher on camera plus slideshow" format and calls for micro-narratives, timely responses to young people's anxieties, and a move from transmitting knowledge to generating meaning. On teams and platforms, the author urges incentives, "ideological and political education plus communication" graduates, regular exchange between ideological and political experts and new-media staff, and algorithms that move from traffic first to value first, with ideological-education weighting, AI content screening and a feedback loop. Liu also proposes shared resource libraries, matrix distribution across platforms and tiered communication for students and the wider public.

Liu concludes that these videos are both an innovation in digital-age education and a strategic need for mainstream ideology to hold online ground. The author calls for balance between technological instrumentality and value-led agency, and for a systemic approach of content first, technology as enabler and mechanisms as safeguard. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how a Chinese university lecturer frames the practical problems and policy options of online ideological and political education.
quoteEn: We must handle correctly the relationship between \"technological instrumentality\" and \"value-led agency\": make good use of algorithms to expand views, while guarding against the traffic logic dissolving the essence of ideological and political education.
quoteZh: 要正确处理“技术工具性”与“价值主体性”的关系：既要善用算法扩大浏览量，又要警惕流量逻辑对思想政治教育本质的消解

glossary.explanation: The system of political and moral instruction in Chinese schools and universities, aimed at instilling Party-endorsed values and Marxist theory. It includes the compulsory ideological and political theory courses (思政课).

glossary.zh: 教育强国建设规划纲要（2024—2035年）
glossary.pinyin: Jiàoyù qiángguó jiànshè guīhuà gāngyào (2024–2035 nián)
glossary.literal: Outline of the Plan for Building a Strong Education Country
glossary.explanation: A planning document issued by the Central Committee of the Communist Party and the State Council in 2025. It sets goals for education development through 2035.

t: Making deepened theoretical armament run through every aspect of university ideological and political courses
zh: 将深化理论武装贯穿高校思政课建设全过程各方面
paras: This commentary, published in Guangming Daily on 23 April 2025, takes up Xi Jinping's instruction that the building of ideological and political courses in schools should advance in step with arming minds with the Party's innovative theory. The instruction is also written into the Outline of the Plan for Building a Strong Education Country (2024–2035). Xu Tao argues that deepening this theoretical armament is of the utmost importance for university ideological and political courses, and that the courses should be used to train a new generation who are reliable for the Party, patriotic and ready to shoulder national rejuvenation.

The piece is organised under three headings: securing the political direction of the courses, consolidating their content, and stimulating innovative thinking in how they are run. Xu writes from the standpoint of a university Party secretary and gives practical measures at each level, from curriculum design and teacher training to student practice and campus culture. Examples are drawn mainly from university practice, such as finance and economics institutions.

On political direction, Xu holds that Marxism must be the fundamental guide and that students should be taught through Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. The author also calls for integrating the courses with course-embedded ideological education across all subjects, and for a stronger sense of universities as ideological front lines that resist erroneous trends of thought and monitor student attitudes. On content, Xu urges rigorous, scholarly exposition of Party theory with critical-thinking training, attention to its historical and traditional-cultural roots, and new modules such as an introductory course on Xi Jinping Thought on economics, developed jointly by Marxism and economics schools. On innovation, Xu proposes organised research platforms across disciplines, stronger teacher training and collective lesson preparation, "micro-innovations" such as a first-day class given by model figures, and practice bases, rural visits and entrepreneurship projects so that students apply theory.

Xu concludes that high-quality development of these courses requires sustained effort and ever more thorough theoretical armament, together with new approaches and plans. The text is a policy-oriented statement of how a university leadership frames the task, and it offers concrete examples of implementation. Read the original if you want a short, official-register account of how university leaders translate the directive on theoretical armament into curriculum, teaching and campus-management measures.
quoteEn: Each time the Party's theoretical innovation advances a step, theoretical armament must follow a step behind.
quoteZh: 党的理论创新每前进一步，理论武装就要跟进一步。

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses in Chinese schools and universities that teach Marxism, Party theory, history and morality. They are treated as the core vehicle of political education.
The Party's term for equipping members and the public with its official theory through study and education.
Official shorthand for the Party's latest theoretical developments, currently centred on Xi Jinping Thought.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017 and 2018.
The practice of weaving ideological and political content into ordinary subject courses, so that it complements the dedicated ideological and political courses.

t: The salient themes, inherent characteristics and construction priorities of the discourse system of ideological and political education in the new era
zh: 新时代思想政治教育话语体系的鲜明主题、内在特质与建构重点
source: Teaching and Research (Jiaoxue yu Yanjiu), 2025 no. 3
paras: Taking up Xi Jinping's call to build disciplinary, academic and discourse systems with Chinese characteristics, Gu Chao and Wang Xuejian ask what the discourse system of ideological and political education should look like in the new era. They argue that it is shaped both by the themes of the age and by the nature of ideological and political education itself. On that basis they set out its themes, its inherent characteristics and the priorities for building it.

The article has three parts. The first identifies four themes: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, moral and political education with answers to students' doubts, contention over discourse power in international communication, and digital-intelligent transformation. The second describes three sets of inherent characteristics: how the discourse is generated, its constituent elements, and the ways it is converted for audiences. The third proposes four construction priorities.

On the characteristics, the authors argue the discourse is generated through realism, subjectivity (anchored in national language, culture and a stance of "putting ourselves first") and knowledge content. It has three layers: political discourse at the core, academic discourse in the middle and everyday discourse on the outside. These layers are linked by conversion: political discourse becomes more scholarly, academic discourse more accessible, and everyday discourse more engaging, through storytelling, metaphor and popular buzzwords. The authors also warn of risks from digital transformation, including digital colonialism, instrumental rationality and algorithmic "echo chambers". On construction, they call for four things. The first is to uphold Marxism and the mainstream ideology and to adopt a people-centred stance. The second is to build an autonomous knowledge system with distinctive concepts, including on Chinese modernization, and to move away from Eurocentric knowledge. The third is to ground the discourse in China's achievements since reform and opening up, explaining the reasoning behind them. The fourth is to draw on Chinese civilisation and cultural confidence.

The authors conclude that the discourse system should combine value guidance with knowledge content, and political stance with accessible expression. They propose that it should convert China's development experience into general concepts and paradigms. They present this as a way both to counter Western discourse hegemony and to extend the influence of Chinese discourse. Read the original if you want a systematic account of how Chinese scholars of ideological and political education conceptualise the layers, themes and tasks of their field's discourse.
quoteEn: It must be able to answer and explain forcefully the confusions that its audience develops, including questions about their own development, their understanding of theory and institutions, and real problems of social development.
quoteZh: 要能对话语对象产生的相关困惑，包括自身的发展问题、对理论和制度的认识问题、对社会发展的现实问题等能够进行有力回答和解释

glossary.explanation: The Chinese term for the Party-state's education in political values, ideology and morality, taught in schools and universities and also practised more widely. It is also an academic discipline in China.

The organised body of concepts, terms and modes of expression through which a field presents its ideas. Xi Jinping has called for building Chinese discourse systems alongside disciplinary and academic systems.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal, associated with the Chinese Dream, of restoring China's national strength and international standing.
The official name for China's path of modernization, presented by the Party as distinct from Western models.
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched in China in 1978.

t: Goals and tasks in constructing a system of methods for ideological and political education
zh: 思想政治教育方法体系建构的目标任务
source: Research on Ideological Education (Sixiang jiaoyu yanjiu), 2025 no. 3
paras: Wang Xisheng takes up a premise question that he says has been neglected in the study of ideological and political education: what goals and tasks a system of methods for the field should serve. Since the first treatise on methods appeared in 1985, the author counts more than 150 related works, over twenty of them systematic. Wang argues that these systems differ so much in aim because their builders look at methods differently, and proposes that the goals and tasks be reset along three lines: theoretical depth and precision, practical validity and reliability, and an inclusive disciplinary identity.

The article has four parts. It first reviews representative systems: Wang Xuanwu's Ideological and Political Education Methodology (1985, revised 1992), Zheng Yongting's work with its historical and contemporary dimensions, and Zu Jiahe's textbook centred on educator and educatee, with brief notes on others. It then sets out four expectations for the new era, followed by a critique of how systems are built, and finally the proposed resetting of goals.

In Wang's account the main existing systems share a narrow scope and mostly follow the process of educational work. The author contends that Marxism, the Marxism of the twenty-first century, and Xi Jinping's writings on ideological work should not be only a "theoretical basis" but the top-level method of the system. Wang ties this to the analysis of people's ideas through productive forces and relations of production, extending it to new quality productive forces and the digital economy. The author also calls for a "strong ideological and political guiding force", the wider "big ideological and political education" pattern, and technology-enabled methods such as large-model teaching. Three terms organise the critique: scope (which methods are included), angle (the dimension of construction) and focal point (where effort concentrates). Wang notes that the field has no consensus on focal point, so additional systems struggle to add up.

Wang concludes that systems should supply an insightful theoretical schema, refined into a genealogy of methods whose internal relations are explained. They should also offer an operational map tested for validity and reliability, and show a distinctive, value-laden disciplinary character that rejects Weberian value neutrality while absorbing methods from pedagogy, psychology, sociology and management. Read the original if you work on the theory of ideological and political education, or want to see how Chinese scholars survey and critique the field's methodology texts and link them to Party priorities.
quoteEn: Only when methods of different kinds and levels are integrated into a closely related genealogy can the theory become more rigorous and standardised, and its guidance of practice more orderly and effective.
quoteZh: 只有将不同种类和层面的方法整合成关系紧密的谱系，理论上才能更严密与规范，对实践的指导才可能更加有序与有力。

glossary.explanation: A Chinese discipline and field of practice that teaches political values, worldview and morality, especially in schools and universities and within Party work.
A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2023 that refers to advanced productive forces driven by technological innovation, such as digital technology and AI.
A policy idea that ideological and political education should draw on the whole of society, including schools, social resources and platforms, rather than only dedicated courses.

t: Making good use of the "Great Ideological and Political Course" to raise the ideological and political leadership of universities
zh: 善用“大思政课”提升高校思政引领力
paras: Writing in April 2025, Jiang Jiaping, Party secretary of Anhui Normal University, takes up the concept of "ideological and political leadership" (sizheng yinlingli). Xi Jinping introduced it at the National Education Conference in September 2024, and the January 2025 Outline for Building a Leading Education Country lists it first among the traits of a strong education system. Jiang argues that universities should use the "Great Ideological and Political Course" as the main lever to strengthen this capacity, together with a broad working philosophy, structure and system of "great" ideological and political work.

This newspaper commentary is organised around four "great" elements. They are "great education of people" (organisational, curricular, practical and cultural education), the "great classroom" of society, the "great front" of ideological positions, and the "great teaching force". Each section turns Xi's statements, including his March 2025 call to merge the ideological and political "small classroom" with the social "great classroom", into measures for university Party committees.

Jiang defines ideological and political leadership as the combined strength of intellectual, moral, spiritual, cultural and practical forces that leads society's members into the effort to build an education powerhouse and achieve national rejuvenation. On this basis, the author calls for Party committees to coordinate the "Three-wide Education" reform and integrate schools, families and society. Courses should be built around Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, and every subject should carry ideological content. Teaching should use museums, memorials, fieldwork and volunteering to show the Party's achievements. Jiang also stresses the ideological struggle in cyberspace, where "if we do not occupy it, others will". The author proposes using big data, blockchain and DeepSeek in online teaching, and building a teaching force from full-time and part-time instructors with four-level training.

Jiang concludes that universities must act proactively on all four fronts so that ideological and political leadership grows through history education, education about national conditions and life education. The author's recommendations are practical: organisational leadership, curriculum reform, practice-based teaching, digital methods and teacher recruitment and training. Read the original if you want a concrete example of how a university Party leader translates current Party education policy into institutional measures.
quoteEn: Universities should take responsibility and act proactively, uphold the "great ideological and political" working philosophy, shape its working pattern, build its working system, and use the "Great Ideological and Political Course" as the lever to raise ideological and political leadership across the board.
quoteZh: 高校要积极担当，主动作为，坚持“大思政”工作理念，塑造“大思政”工作格局，构建“大思政”工作体系，以“大思政课”为抓手全面提升思政引领力。

glossary.explanation: A concept Xi Jinping put forward at the National Education Conference in September 2024. It refers to the capacity of ideological and political work to guide society and is presented as the primary trait of an education powerhouse.
A policy idea promoted by Xi Jinping that extends ideological and political teaching beyond the classroom into society and real-life practice.

glossary.literal: education of all people, throughout the whole process, in all respects
glossary.explanation: A reform framework that calls on all staff to take part in moral and ideological education of students at every stage and in every aspect of university life.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018. It is taught as the core content of ideological and political courses.

t: Advancing the integrated development of ideological and political education across universities, secondary and primary schools through a systems perspective
zh: 以系统观念推进大中小学思想政治教育一体化建设
paras: Chang Qing, a university Party official, takes up how the integration of ideological and political education across universities, secondary schools and primary schools should be advanced. The newspaper commentary argues that this integration must be treated as an organic whole and a systems project, guided by what it calls the systems perspective, a core element of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. In Chang's view, it bears directly on whom education serves, what kind of people it cultivates and how, and is a key step in the fundamental task of fostering virtue through education.

The article is organised in three parts. The first sets out why integration is necessary. The second identifies three dimensions for it: sequence, effectiveness and depth. The third outlines a practical route, covering institutional coordination, continuity of student development and a multi-actor pattern of education. It draws throughout on Xi Jinping's statements and on the decision of the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024).

Chang gives three reasons for integration: it ensures the Party's cause has successors, it reflects the political, popular and strategic attributes of education, and it serves the building of a strong education nation, whose first listed trait is the capacity for ideological guidance. The core argument pairs concepts in three relations. Wholeness and progression concern coordinating courses, course-embedded ideological education and everyday ideological work, while stages from primary school to university move from easy to difficult. Direction and effectiveness require the guidance of Marxism and Party leadership, with results measured first by the cultivation of virtue. Value and knowledge hold that values are conveyed through knowledge, with new Party theory, core socialist values and traditional culture as key content.

On implementation, Chang calls for stronger top-level design and coordination among Party committees, education authorities, research bodies and schools, with support for staff, resources and artificial intelligence. Chang also calls for spiral progression across stages, from goals to textbooks and teacher training, and for cooperation among schools, government, local communities and museums. The article presents this as raising the efficiency of integration. Read the original if you want a concise example of how the official discourse links systems thinking, the 'big ideological and political course' and the building of a strong education nation in Chinese schooling policy.
quoteEn: To advance integrated ideological and political education across universities, secondary and primary schools, we must focus on 'cooperation', strengthen 'joint effort', and twist the 'many threads' into 'a single rope'.
quoteZh: 推进大中小学思想政治教育一体化建设，要聚焦“合作”、增强“合力”，将“多条线”拧成“一股绳”。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Communist Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018. It is presented as the latest stage in adapting Marxism to China.

An official formulation of education's fundamental task: cultivating moral character alongside knowledge and skills. It has been prominent in Party education policy since the 18th Party Congress (2012).
A way of thinking that treats phenomena as interconnected wholes. It is listed as one of the guiding principles for deepening reform in the Third Plenum decision of 2024.
A policy concept that extends ideological and political education beyond the classroom into society, practice bases and all courses. It is promoted by the Ministry of Education.
The practice of integrating ideological and political content into non-ideological subjects such as the sciences and professional courses, alongside dedicated ideological and political courses.
A national goal of building China into a leading education power, set out at the National Education Conference in September 2024 with six listed attributes.

t: Advancing Chinese modernization requires vigorously cultivating an innovation culture
zh: 推进中国式现代化必须大力培育创新文化
paras: Yan Xiaofeng, writing in Red Flag Manuscript in 2025, asks how China can build the cultural conditions for innovation. The article argues that Chinese modernization is an innovation-driven modernization and that an innovation culture, meaning a culture that honours, encourages and dares to innovate, must therefore be placed in a prominent position in developing socialist culture for a new era. Yan frames this as a response to Xi Jinping's call to cultivate innovation culture and to make respect for science and the pursuit of innovation a social norm.

The commentary has three parts. The first treats innovation culture as a driving force for the central tasks of the new era and the new journey. The second sets out how to create a cultural atmosphere that values and encourages innovation. The third places the cultivation of innovation culture within the development of socialist culture with Chinese characteristics for a new era. Yan cites the success of DeepSeek and the animated film Ne Zha 2 during the 2025 Spring Festival as products of long-term cultural cultivation.

Yan's core argument starts from the Marxist claim that culture reflects and is determined by the economic base, yet acts back on it as a soft power. Yan reads Chinese modernization as itself an innovation, achieved through the Two Integrations and without ready-made models. Yan lists obstacles in practice: risk aversion, conformism and evasion of responsibility. The remedy comes in four steps: strengthen innovation confidence and initiative; develop innovative thinking that follows laws and starts from problems; raise innovation capacity and train talent; and build a patient environment with tolerance of failure and talent evaluation based on contribution.

In the third part Yan calls for guidance by Xi Jinping's thought on culture, strengthened Party leadership over cultural work, and a balance of "upholding fundamental principles" and innovation, in which the former secures direction and the latter renews it. The Second Integration, joining Marxism with fine traditional Chinese culture, is presented as a further liberation of thought that supplies the cultural root of innovation. Yan concludes that transforming traditional culture creatively will strengthen the cultural subjectivity of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want an example of how Party-school-style commentary links innovation policy, cultural confidence and Xi Jinping's cultural thought.
quoteEn: Innovation is a process of trial and error; it may fail along the way and is hard to achieve at the first attempt.
quoteZh: 创新是一个试错的过程，会有夭折的可能，难以一次成功。

glossary.explanation: The official term for China's path to modernization, promoted since the 20th Party Congress (2022) as combining universal features with Chinese national conditions.
Xi Jinping's formula for combining Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities (the First) and with fine traditional Chinese culture (the Second).

glossary.literal: upholding what is correct and innovating
glossary.explanation: An official formula holding that adherence to the Party's core principles and orientation must go together with innovation.
A body of ideas on cultural work attributed to Xi Jinping and formally set out in 2023, covering the role of culture, traditional civilisation and ideological leadership.

t: In the new era and on the new journey, the Party's cultural leadership must be upheld
zh: 新时代新征程必须坚持党的文化领导权
paras: Writing in the Party journal Dangjian (2025, no. 2), Zhang Shihai and Wang Tong ask why the Communist Party's cultural leadership must be upheld in the new era and how this should be done. They take as their starting point Xi Jinping's June 2023 remarks at the symposium on cultural inheritance and development, which named the Party's cultural leadership and the Chinese nation's cultural subjectivity as things that must be preserved. The authors argue that, amid accelerating global change and coexisting opportunities and risks, upholding this leadership is needed to build a socialist ideology with strong cohesion and guiding power.

The short commentary has two parts. The first sets out why cultural leadership matters. The second identifies four main points of focus for putting it into practice. The authors draw throughout on Xi Jinping's statements on publicity, ideological and cultural work, and tie the argument to the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, which they say requires a flourishing Chinese culture.

On significance, Zhang and Wang present cultural leadership as an inherent requirement for a Marxist ruling party doing ideological work, and as a safeguard for building a strong country and achieving national rejuvenation. They credit it with strengthening ideological defences, shaping mainstream opinion and uniting the people spiritually. On practice, they call for four things: maintaining Marxism's guiding position in the ideological sphere as a fundamental system; being guided by Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era; innovating in concepts, methods (including artificial intelligence and other digital technologies) and grassroots work; and uniting Party spirit with the people's character. On the last point, they hold that the two are consistent. Party principles must be stated openly and confidently. Party theory must also be made accessible to ordinary people and respond to their concerns.

The authors conclude that upholding the Party's cultural leadership is a systematic project requiring coordinated effort, and that it is the basis for unity of thought, politics and action. They hold that adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, together with innovation grounded in practice, will sustain its force. Read the original if you want a concise example of how the Party's current official line on cultural and ideological leadership is explained in a Party-oriented journal for cadres and academics.
quoteEn: In our country, Party spirit and the people's character are consistent and unified; there is no Party spirit divorced from the people's character, and no people's character divorced from Party spirit.
quoteZh: 在我国，党性和人民性是一致的、统一的，没有脱离人民性的党性，也没有脱离党性的人民性。

glossary.explanation: The Party's authority to direct culture, ideology and public opinion. The term echoes Gramsci's 'hegemony' and is used in official discourse on ideological work.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The official goal of restoring China's national strength and international standing, central to Party discourse since the 18th Party Congress (2012).

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for developing Marxist theory in line with China's conditions and the current era.

t: On the content dimensions of building an autonomous knowledge system for the discipline of ideological and political education
zh: 论思想政治教育学自主知识体系构建的内容向度
source: Ideological and Political Education Research (思想教育研究), 2025 no. 2
paras: Hou Yong and Ke Zengjin take up the call to build an autonomous Chinese knowledge system in philosophy and the social sciences and ask what this means for the discipline of ideological and political education. Their thesis is that the system should be built along the lines of the "three systems" (disciplinary, academic and discourse systems), following a logic of knowledge organisation, knowledge production and knowledge dissemination.

The article opens by clarifying what an autonomous knowledge system is. It reviews views on its function, process, structure and elements, then offers the authors' own definition: a functional, procedural, systemic integration of concepts, categories, laws, methods, discourse and supporting structures. Three sections then treat the disciplinary, academic and discourse systems in turn. A fourth section sets out systems-thinking requirements, and the piece ends with six "must" principles.

The central move is to link each of the three systems to a stage of knowledge work. The disciplinary system (core and branch discipline clusters, cooperation within and across disciplines, talent training and textbooks) organises knowledge. The academic system (Marxist theory and traditional Chinese culture as foundations, basic theory and interdisciplinary borrowing) produces it. The discourse system (a "terminological revolution" around original concepts, narrative and international communication) disseminates it. The authors say the three are interdependent: the disciplinary system is the foundation, the academic system the driving force and the discourse system the key. They also stress that interdisciplinary borrowing must avoid mechanical copying. A second move places the whole project within Chinese modernization, with the aim of the modernization of the human being, and calls for top-level design and methodological innovation at macro, meso and micro levels.

The authors conclude that the project is long-term and systematic. They list principles: the Two Integrations, putting the people first, self-confidence and self-reliance, preserving fundamental principles while innovating, problem orientation, systems thinking and a global outlook. They add that dimensions beyond the three systems still need study. Read the original if you want a detailed map of how Chinese scholars of ideological and political education frame disciplinary construction, its sub-fields, methods and discourse strategy.
quoteEn: The autonomous knowledge system of ideological and political education is not a simple accumulation or mechanical assembly of knowledge. It builds on existing knowledge and organises it in a logically coherent way, so that knowledge becomes systematic and scientific.
quoteZh: 思想政治教育学自主知识体系不是知识的简单累加和机械组装，而是以现有知识作为基础，以逻辑贯通的方式组织起来，实现知识的体系化、科学化。

glossary.explanation: The official Party formulation of China's own path to modernization, prominent since the 20th Party Congress (2022). The article treats it as the field and goal of knowledge construction.
Xi Jinping's formula for combining Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture.
The Party-state's system of ideological, political and moral education, taught in schools and universities. It is also an academic discipline under Marxist theory.

glossary.zh: 学科体系、学术体系、话语体系
glossary.pinyin: xuékē tǐxì, xuéshù tǐxì, huàyǔ tǐxì
glossary.literal: disciplinary system, academic system, discourse system
glossary.explanation: The disciplinary, academic and discourse systems that, according to official statements, make up Chinese philosophy and social sciences with Chinese characteristics.

A concept stressed by Xi Jinping from 2022 and in the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024). It calls for Chinese scholarship to rest on its own concepts and theories instead of Western ones.

t: The value and practical path of empowering university ideological and political theory courses with the "Two Integrations"
zh: “两个结合”赋能高校思政课的价值意蕴与实践理路
source: New Era Marxism Series (Xin shidai Makesizhuyi luncong)
paras: Zhang Rongjun and Zhang Xi ask how the Two Integrations (combining Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture) can be used as an intellectual resource in university ideological and political theory courses. They argue that this is both necessary and feasible, and that it can make the courses more theoretically grounded and persuasive. In their view it also meets the courses' basic tasks of Marxist theoretical education and the transmission of traditional culture.

The article opens with a short review of existing scholarship. The authors note that studies have focused either on integrating traditional culture, or on integrating Marxist principles, into these courses, and that the Two Integrations as a whole have been less examined. The body then has three parts: the value of the Two Integrations for the courses; the scholarly grounds on which the two fit together; and a practical path of implementation.

On value, the authors hold that the Two Integrations supply resources for fostering virtue and cultivating people (lide shuren). They also help to produce a new generation capable of the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, by addressing what the authors call students' lack of faith, wavering conviction and insufficient confidence, and strengthen students' cultural confidence. On fit, they identify three shared features: both rest on Marxism and fine traditional culture, both are guided by Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, and both aim to serve socialist modernization. The practical path has four strands. The Two Integrations should be built into students' overall qualities and into teachers' political and theoretical competence. They should also shape teaching content, covering Marxist theory, the achievements of the Sinification of Marxism, and history and moral education. Finally, they should inform evaluation, where the authors propose assessing teachers' teaching and research and replacing grade-only assessment of students with one based on knowing, feeling, will and action.

The authors conclude that integrating the Two Integrations into students, teachers, content and assessment together can make the courses more targeted and effective. The argument is largely prescriptive and works within official policy documents and Party-congress texts rather than empirical testing. Read the original if you want a detailed example of how Chinese education scholars translate Party theoretical formulations into teaching content, teacher requirements and assessment criteria for university political courses.
quoteEn: Integrating the "Two Integrations" into university ideological and political courses requires highlighting key points and making the integration more targeted.
quoteZh: “两个结合”融入高校思政课，需要突出重点、增强融入的针对性。

glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's formula of combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture. It was prominently stated in his speech at the Party's centenary in 2021.
The fundamental task of education in official policy: moral cultivation together with the training of talent. It is the stated basic task of ideological and political courses.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology since 2017. It is written into the Party constitution and is the core content of the courses discussed.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's long-term national goal of restoring China's strength and standing, closely associated with Xi Jinping's "Chinese Dream".
Compulsory courses in Marxist theory, Party history and official ideology taught in all Chinese universities. They are often abbreviated as sizheng ke.

t: How Mao Zedong told the story of the Long March
zh: 毛泽东如何讲长征故事
source: Mao Zedong Deng Xiaoping Theory Studies (毛泽东邓小平理论研究), 2025 no. 1
paras: Taking its cue from the 20th Party Congress (2022) call to tell China's story well, this article asks how Mao Zedong, a participant in and witness of the Central Red Army's Long March, narrated it. Gao and Gong argue that his storytelling can be explained through three questions: why it was needed (historical context), what it contained (core content) and how it was done (method). They present it as a resource for building a Long March discourse and a Chinese narrative system today.

The study draws on Party documents, memoirs of historical figures and local gazetteers. It follows Mao's Long March narratives across three settings: the New Democratic revolution, Party building, and socialist construction. It then turns to content (experience, theory, spirit) and to method, organised by who tells, to whom, and in what form.

In the authors' account, Mao used the Long March in each setting for a different purpose. In the revolutionary period he declared it a victory against talk of failure and tied it to the anti-Japanese united front. After 1949 he invoked it to warn cadres against complacency, in the "Two Musts" and elsewhere, and to encourage confidence in socialist construction. The authors identify three core themes: Party leadership and the mass line, the integration of Marxism's universal truth with China's concrete conditions (traced to the Zunyi Meeting), and a revolutionary optimism. On method, they stress that Mao combined his own telling with that of others such as Edgar Snow and Red Army soldiers' diaries. He also adapted content to students, officers, ordinary people and foreign audiences, and he blended poetry with theoretical writing, calligraphy, vivid scenes, and the unity of knowing and doing.

Gao and Gong conclude that Mao's main contributions were the political judgement that the Long March was a victory, the summing-up of its lessons to establish the seek-truth-from-facts line, and the affirmation of Party leadership and the strength of the people. They also credit him with explaining the principle of adapting Marxism to China's conditions through Long March examples. They call on everyone in the new era to tell Long March stories, innovate in communication and promote the Long March spirit for building a modern socialist country. Read the original if you want a detailed, source-based account of Mao's Long March rhetoric and its use in later Party narrative-building.
quoteEn: The audience for Mao Zedong's telling of the Long March story was no longer confined to the domestic masses but extended to the world's public.
quoteZh: 毛泽东讲述长征故事的对象不再局限于国内群众，而是面向世界大众。

glossary.explanation: A formula Mao set out in March 1949 at the Second Plenum of the 7th Central Committee. It urged Party members to remain modest, prudent and free of arrogance, and to keep up hard struggle.
The Party's principle of working "from the masses, to the masses". It means relying on ordinary people and staying close to them.
A January 1935 Party leadership meeting during the Long March. Party history treats it as a turning point that corrected the leadership's military line and established Mao's leading role.
The official Party term for the ideals, courage and perseverance attributed to the Red Army on the Long March. It is invoked in political education and Party narratives.

t: Conditions for applying artificial intelligence in ideological and political education
zh: 思想政治教育应用人工智能的实现条件
source: Journal of Ideological and Theoretical Education (思想理论教育导刊), 2025 no. 2
paras: Chang Yanhui takes up a gap in work on ideological and political education and artificial intelligence. In the author's view, existing studies infer from the technical features of AI how it might empower the field, but rarely ask what is needed for it to work in practice. The article argues that prospects for AI in ideological and political education are credible only if three core elements (data, computing power and algorithms) are secured and if usage norms suited to both the discipline and the technology are put in place.

The article has three parts. The first reviews scenarios of use, starting from the principles of generative AI such as ChatGPT, Doubao and DeepSeek, which Chang classes as specialised, weak AI. The second sets out technical conditions: national policy support, data resources and the involvement of educators in development. The third proposes regulatory norms, covering standards for what counts as an intelligent product, data collection rules, admission conditions, content review and legal compliance.

On scenarios, Chang argues that AI can speed up literature searches and empirical analysis of public opinion, act as a teaching assistant, generate video scenes that make abstract values concrete, and support audience-segmented, targeted online education. On conditions, the author says costs in energy and computing power should ease through national plans, and that three kinds of data should enter model training: published research, the Party's accumulated teaching experience, and teacher and student behaviour data. Ideological and political educators, Chang holds, should help tune models, judge training-data quality and feed back on use, so that general models become specialised ones.

On norms, Chang calls for independent third-party evaluation of products, schools that keep control over data collected by internet firms, and a ban on handing important decisions to AI because its opaque "black box" conflicts with the transparency the field requires. The author claims domestic AI products hold the correct political stance, whereas some foreign products hide liberal values in their algorithms. Products must therefore be guided by core socialist values, with training data screened ideologically. Chang proposes four data categories under existing data-security law: national ideological security, students' political views, their physical and mental health, and their varied lifestyles. Read the original if you want a Chinese pedagogical-ideological perspective on AI governance in universities, including its data and content-review proposals.
quoteEn: Ideological and political education is highly ideological in nature, bears on national ideological security and the physical and mental health of those taught, and in many respects leaves no room for error.
quoteZh: 思想政治教育活动的意识形态性很强，涉及国家意识形态安全和教育对象的身心健康，很多地方是不容许出错的。

glossary.explanation: A field and teaching practice in Chinese universities and schools that conveys Marxist theory, Party policy and socialist values, and also a discipline within Marxist theory studies.
A set of twelve values promoted by the Party since 2012, covering the national, social and individual levels, used as a guide in education and public culture.
The idea that a state must protect its dominant ideology from erosion or challenge, treated in Chinese official discourse as part of national security.
A communication approach that divides audiences into groups and tailors content to each; the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) applied it to online moral and ideological education.

t: Retrospect and prospect: thirty years of theory and practice in online ideological and political education
zh: 回顾与展望：网络思想政治教育理论研究与实践推进30年
source: Contemporary Chinese Marxism Studies (当代中国马克思主义研究), 2024 no. 2
paras: Marking thirty years of online ideological and political education (wangluo sixiang zhengzhi jiaoyu) within a discipline that is itself forty years old, Wu Manyi and Yang Rongsuo ask what the field has accumulated and where it is stuck. They present it as the history of technology entering ideological and political education and also of Party and state will being carried out in cyberspace. Their thesis is that the field has matured in practice but still lacks settled concepts, boundaries and paradigms. They argue that both theory and practice must therefore be reorientated.

The article has three parts. The first periodises the field in three stages: the rise of the internet (1994–2002), social media (2003–2012) and the mobile internet (2012–2024). Each stage is tied to technological change, to official documents, and to keyword-co-occurrence analyses of CNKI papers made with CiteSpace. The second part diagnoses theoretical and practical problems. The third sets out prospects for theory and practice.

On theory, the authors identify three unresolved matters. The first is the concept, which scholars have variously defined as a tool, a way of life, a virtual world or an ecology. The second is the boundaries, which are blurred against traditional ideological and political education, offline education and other disciplines, and are eroded by uncritical cross-disciplinary borrowing. The third is the paradigm, since research stays at the level of surface operational issues, neglects ontology and epistemology, and rarely uses empirical or comparative methods. On practice, they report weak and unsustained drivers (formalism in implementing documents, thin funding, unstandardised evaluation, unmaintained platforms), generic and homogeneous content, and a technicist tendency that favours spectacle over substance. In their account, this tendency produces a fetishised appearance that hides the real relations of education.

For theory, the authors call for clarifying the concept from a totalising perspective, drawing firm but open boundaries that balance guarding the discipline's own ground with crossing disciplines, and reconstructing the paradigm so that online ideological and political education is studied as a subject in its own right. For practice, they propose a sounder driving mechanism, guarantees of policy, funding and personnel, and attention to three functions: guiding values, guiding behaviour and building consensus. They conclude that the discipline, as a practical humanities field, must keep reviewing its history to answer the questions of the human–machine era. Read the original if you want a detailed periodisation and critical overview of Chinese scholarship and practice in online ideological and political education.)
quoteEn: Only by establishing a new paradigm can online ideological and political education escape the rut of the traditional research paradigm, make up for its own theoretical shortcomings, and deserve to be called an "emerging discipline".
quoteZh: 网络思想政治教育只有建立一种新范式才能跳出传统思想政治教育研究范式的窠臼，弥补自身理论缺陷，称得上是“新兴学科”。
