glossary.explanation: The application of Party-led ideological and political education, a core activity of Chinese universities, to the internet and digital platforms. It has developed since the mid-1990s as a sub-field of the ideological and political education discipline.

The system of teaching and guidance through which the Party and state seek to shape students' and citizens' political outlook, values and morality. It is also an academic discipline within Marxist theory studies.

t: Basic issues in building the disciplinary subjectivity of ideological and political education over forty years
zh: 论析40年来思想政治教育学科主体性建设的基本议题
source: Contemporary Chinese Marxism Studies (当代中国马克思主义研究), 2024 no. 2
paras: Marking forty years since ideological and political education was set up as an undergraduate programme in 1984, Yu Wenli asks how the field can build its own disciplinary subjectivity (xueke zhutixing), meaning the independent character that makes it a discipline rather than a borrower of other fields' concepts. Yu argues that this subjectivity is the discipline's foundation and source of vitality. It has to be built through five paired relationships, which the article treats in turn.

The article first separates the programme (zhuanye) from the discipline (xueke), noting that the field began as a programme in 1984 and only later became a discipline. It describes how the discipline's classification moved from education to political science and then, in 2006, to the first-level discipline of Marxist theory. It then examines in sequence: cross-disciplinary borrowing and integration; politics and scholarship; knowledge and values; and facts and norms. Yu draws on Kant, Bertrand Russell and Jürgen Habermas for supporting distinctions.

Yu holds that the discipline grew out of the Party's political work in the revolutionary years and out of attempts to make the ideological work of state-enterprise staff more scientific. It has therefore drawn heavily on Marxist philosophy, pedagogy, sociology and psychology. The task now is to turn borrowing into independent knowledge, theory and method. Yu sees politics as the discipline's defining character, since it exists to uphold Marxism as the Party's guiding ideology. Yet research often stops at explaining policy, which leaves its scholarly side weak. The proposed way forward is to move from common sense to theory, to policy reasoning and then to philosophy, without setting politics and scholarship against each other. On knowledge and values, Yu describes the discipline's knowledge as experiential, or "soft", and inseparable from value formation. Yu also says that its conceptual base is still too dependent on Western concepts. The tension is between theory and practice, and between foreign and native concepts. Finally, Yu locates subjectivity in the interplay of facts (practice, problems, solutions) and norms (policies, institutions, plans).

Yu concludes that an autonomous knowledge system should be built on the principle of creating Chinese knowledge from Chinese values, with Chinese knowledge carrying those values. Future efforts should balance facts and norms and avoid both pure factualism and voluntarism. The aim is a modern discipline that combines scientific and revolutionary character, politics and scholarship, and theory and practice. Read the original if you want to see how a leading scholar of the field frames its identity problems, and how it relates the Party's ideological mission to academic discipline-building.
quoteEn: The leading path of theoretical research in ideological and political education is the zone where political practice and academic practice meet and interact: it seeks scholarship and theory in politics and policy, while using scholarship and theory to serve politics and policy.
quoteZh: 思想政治教育学理研究的主导性轨迹是融合政治实践和学术实践的交互区间，从政治和政策中探寻学术和学理，同时以学术和学理服务于政治和政策。

glossary.explanation: A Chinese field of teaching and research that cultivates political conviction and values in line with Marxism and Party ideology. It is taught in universities and has its own degree programmes.

The independent identity and self-grounded character of an academic discipline, as distinct from borrowing from other fields. It is a theme in recent Chinese debates on building autonomous knowledge systems.
A first-level discipline established in China in 2006 under the law category. Ideological and political education is one of its second-level disciplines.

t: Practical pathways for strengthening ideological and political leadership in building a strong education nation
zh: 教育强国建设背景下提升思政引领力的实践理路
source: Research on Ideological Education (Sixiang jiaoyu yanjiu), 2025
paras: Wu Yandong and Yang Siqing take up Xi Jinping's call, made at the National Education Conference, for a socialist education powerhouse with six strengths, the first of which is "ideological and political leadership" (siheng yinlingli). The article asks what value this capacity holds and how it can be raised. Its thesis is that ideological and political work is the "lifeline" of the project, and that stronger leadership requires a systematic, multi-dimensional practical path.

The article has two parts. The first sets out the value of ideological and political leadership in building a strong education nation. The second proposes five ways of strengthening it: political leadership, value leadership, institutional leadership, curriculum leadership and leadership through the ideological and political workforce. Each is broken into three sub-measures, drawing on Xi Jinping's statements on education and ideological work.

In the first part the authors argue that ideological and political leadership shows the political character of education, fixes the direction of talent cultivation, and helps build the strategic layout that integrates education, science and technology, and talent. In the second part, the authors argue that political leadership means upholding the Party's overall leadership of education, guiding it with Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, and strengthening Party ideological work. Value leadership means turning core socialist values into students' aims, countering what the authors call erroneous trends such as historical nihilism, and developing education with a people-centred approach. Institutional leadership means keeping Marxism's guiding position, improving the mechanism of fostering virtue through education, and running ideological work through every part of the talent-training system. Curriculum leadership covers ideological and political courses, "curriculum ideology and politics" in other subjects, and a "big ideological and political course" linking classroom and society.

The authors conclude that a strong education nation needs strong ideological and political leadership. They propose steps for the workforce: building awareness, raising its organising, value-shaping and coordinating abilities, and making use of model examples, publicity and evaluation. Read the original if you want a detailed, policy-oriented account of how ideological and political education is being linked to the education-power agenda in Chinese universities and schools.
quoteEn: Ideological and political leadership not only defines the goals and direction of building a strong education nation but also supplies its spiritual impetus, keeping the project moving in the correct political direction.
quoteZh: 思政引领力不仅规定了教育强国建设的目标方向，并且为教育强国建设提供精神动力，推动教育强国建设始终沿着正确的政治方向前进。

glossary.explanation: The capacity of ideological and political work to guide the direction of education. Xi Jinping listed it first among the six strengths of a strong education nation in 2024.
An official goal of building a leading education system by 2035, described as socialist with Chinese characteristics and as a foundation for national rejuvenation.
The stated fundamental task of Chinese education: shaping students' moral character along with their knowledge and skills.

glossary.literal: ideology and politics in the curriculum
glossary.explanation: The practice of embedding ideological and moral content in all subject courses, so that they work alongside dedicated ideological and political theory courses.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017 and 2018.

t: Understanding in depth how the leading force of ideological and political education works
zh: 深刻把握思政引领力的作用机制
source: Ideological and Political Education Research, 2025 no. 2
paras: Dai Yuqi and Tian Yu take up a concept introduced in September 2024, when Xi Jinping told the National Education Conference that a leading education nation must have strong "leading force of ideological and political education" (sizheng yinlingli), placed first among six capacities. The authors argue that although the term is new, the function it names has run through the Party's history. Their thesis is that this force operates through distinct mechanisms in three fields: education, culture and society.

The article, published in Ideological and Political Education Research (2025, no. 2), notes that most existing work approaches the concept from the angle of building a leading education nation, and says it instead concentrates on mechanisms of action. Each of its three main sections sets out functions of the leading force, then identifies shortcomings in current practice. A short conclusion describes vertical deepening and horizontal interaction across the fields.

In education, the authors identify three functions: forging the soul (political and value guidance, opposing "value neutrality"), stimulating intellect (integrating ideological education with subject knowledge) and cultivating virtue (moral and emotional guidance of young people). In culture, they treat it as upholding cultural leadership, consolidating cultural subjectivity through the Two Integrations, and raising national soft power. They describe Western cultural infiltration, commercial distortion of cultural products and weak overseas communication as challenges. In society, it is said to build consensus, sustain orderly operation through self-restraint and conflict mediation, and support innovative governance. Here Dai and Tian stress balancing unity with plurality, "managing well without managing rigidly".

The conclusion holds that the leading force starts in education, runs through culture and society, and that the three fields reinforce each other through shared values, integrated goals and feedback loops. The authors add that it does not belong automatically to those who do ideological work but sets higher demands on each of them, and that it requires sustained effort. They call for continuously improving ideological and political education, fitting it to mainstream values and to socio-economic development, and combining direct and indirect, explicit and implicit guidance. Read the original if you want a detailed account of how Chinese scholars conceptualise the functions and weak points of ideological and political work in the new "six forces" framework.
quoteEn: The leading force of ideological and political education refers to ideological and political work as a whole. It does not mean that ideological and political workers naturally possess a high degree of leading force; rather, it sets a higher requirement on each of them to strengthen effective guidance.
quoteZh: 思政引领力是就思想政治工作整体而言的，并不意味着思想政治工作者天然具有较高的引领力，而是对每位思想政治工作者提出了加强有效引领的更高要求。

glossary.en: leading force of ideological and political education
glossary.explanation: A concept first put forward by Xi Jinping in September 2024 as the first of six capacities of a leading education nation. It denotes the capacity of ideological and political work to give political, ideological and directional guidance.
A national goal of building China into a country with a strong education system, set out in a 2025 Party-State outline covering 2024–2035.
Formula stating that Marxism should be integrated with China's concrete realities and with China's fine traditional culture.
The ability of the ruling ideology to win acceptance through attraction, persuasion and identification rather than coercion; the article treats it as a form of soft power.
A term in recent Party discourse for a culture's spiritual independence and capacity for self-understanding and development, linked to the Two Integrations.

t: Strengthening Party conduct and discipline to clear obstacles and safeguard reform
zh: 强化正风肃纪为改革清障护航
paras: Writing in the Party journal Dangjian (2025, no. 2), Lü Man argues that sustained efforts to rectify Party conduct and enforce discipline are a necessary guarantee for the further deepening of reform. The article takes as its starting point the decision of the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) and Xi Jinping's call at the Fourth Plenary Session of the 20th Central Commission for Discipline Inspection to link work on conduct, discipline and anti-corruption. Lü's thesis is that, given the unprecedented scope and depth of reform, such work must run through every aspect of Party building to create a healthy political ecology.

The piece is organised in three parts. The first sets out why strengthening conduct and discipline matters, drawing on three grounds: the basic principles of Marxist party-building theory, the Chinese Communist Party's historical experience, and the task of leading social revolution through the Party's self-reform. The second explains how this work protects reform in terms of breadth, depth, and force and effectiveness. The third offers methods for putting it into practice.

In Lü's account, reform is both a profound social revolution and a deep-level self-reform of the Party. Lü reasons that discipline and conduct serve different functions: discipline restrains, educates and motivates throughout Party governance, while conduct displays the Party's image and sets the tone. Lü argues that, as reform tackles its hardest problems, rectifying conduct helps break 'unwritten rules', correct distorted views of power and achievements, and create a fair environment for market actors, while firmness is also needed on what must not be changed. The methods proposed are four: stress the political nature of the work, keep a strict tone, adopt precise thinking by focusing on key tasks, key people (leading officials) and key measures, and promote coordinated action across Party committees, functional departments and discipline bodies.

Lü concludes that officials should act as 'promoters and doers' of reform, balancing personal and collective, local and overall, and short-term and long-term interests. The article calls for combining strict management with care for cadres, handling conduct and corruption problems together, and keeping Party discipline education regular. Read the original if you want an example of how Party-school commentary links the Party's disciplinary campaign to the Third Plenum's reform agenda and to Xi Jinping's thought on Party building.
quoteEn: Comprehensively deepening reform is both a profound social revolution and a deep-level self-reform of the Party.
quoteZh: 全面深化改革既是深刻的社会革命，也是党深层次的自我革命。

glossary.explanation: A concept emphasised under Xi Jinping, holding that the Party must continually purify and improve itself, especially through discipline and anti-corruption work. The Chinese word is literally 'self-revolution'.

t: Strengthening the educational ecology of ideological and political education for university students: several reflections
zh: 加强大学生思想政治教育育人生态建设的几点思考
source: Research on Ideological Education (思想教育研究), 2025 no. 2
paras: Bai and Peng ask how Chinese universities can improve the "educational ecology" of ideological and political education for undergraduates. They argue that, despite visible progress since the 18th Party Congress (2012), the work still suffers from fragmented and superficial practices. Their remedy is to build a coherent "ecological forest" and a "scenic landscape" of ideological and political education, one that carries out the fundamental task of fostering virtue through education.

The article has three parts. The first sets out why strengthening this ecology is necessary: it serves the fundamental task of fostering virtue through education, it is required to build a university system of ideological and political work, and it is needed to raise the effectiveness of education amid a more complex online and ideological environment. The second diagnoses four typical problems. The third proposes four practical strategies. Throughout, the authors draw heavily on Xi Jinping's statements on education and on the 2020 guideline issued by eight central departments on accelerating that system.

The core move is the diagnosis, which uses landscape metaphors. The authors describe a "bonsai" type that polishes a few exemplary showpieces while neglecting the ordinary field. A "stage-set" type arranges scenes and performers to hide real problems. A "framing" type changes packaging and angle while the content stays the same, "old wine in new bottles". A "timely" type chases hot topics for attention without explaining their substance. Against these the authors propose four remedies. The first is systems thinking applied to the whole, the elements and the process, led by the university Party committee. The second is a reform of evaluation that takes fostering virtue as the basic standard, adds humanistic care, and combines process and outcome assessment. The third is innovation that follows the laws of the field and adapts to each institution's circumstances. The fourth is long-term mechanisms.

The authors conclude that effective ideological and political education cannot be quick or campaign-style. It requires routine practice, durable mechanisms and institutionalisation within university governance, so that it can release what they call the "guiding force" of ideological and political work in building a leading country in education. Read the original if you want a detailed example of how Chinese scholars of ideological and political education classify formalistic practice and frame the official policy language on this work in Party-line terms.
quoteEn: Objectively speaking, ideological and political education for university students still shows multiple problematic patterns: the \"bonsai\", \"stage-set\", \"framing\" and \"timely-show\" types.
quoteZh: 但客观来说，大学生思想政治教育目前仍存在着“盆景式”“布景式”“取景式”和“应景式”等多重问题样态

glossary.explanation: The officially stated fundamental task of Chinese education, stressed under Xi Jinping. It means that moral and ideological formation comes first in cultivating students.
The system of courses and activities through which Chinese schools and universities teach Party-endorsed ideology, values and ideals. It is both an academic discipline and an operational field.
A metaphor for the overall environment of people, resources, institutions and atmosphere in which students are educated. The authors use it to stress coordination across all parts of a university.

glossary.en: system of ideological and political work
glossary.explanation: The integrated set of links, elements and institutions through which universities carry out ideological and political work. It was the subject of the 2020 guideline from eight central departments.

t: The implications for values education of consolidating cultural subjectivity
zh: 巩固文化主体性的价值观教育意蕴
source: Ideological and Theoretical Education (思想理论教育), 2025 no. 3
paras: Li Yifei takes up a question raised by Xi Jinping's remark that any culture needs its own subjectivity to have leading, cohesive, shaping and radiating power. The article asks what mission values education carries in consolidating cultural subjectivity, and how it should carry it out. Li argues that, because core values form the hard core of any culture, values education is a central means of strengthening a distinctive, self-determining cultural self in China.

The article has three parts. The first defines culture and cultural subjectivity, drawing on anthropology, psychology (William James, Carl Rogers), Marx and Fei Xiaotong. The second sets out three demands that consolidating cultural subjectivity places on values education. The third proposes three practical paths: the Two Integrations, theoretical innovation under a grand view of history and a new view of civilization, and the cultivation of a public character open to exchange.

Li divides culture into a hard core (core values), a middle layer (emotions, language, institutions, specific cultural forms) and an outer ring (visible forms, emerging cultures and subcultures). Cultural subjectivity is then read in three dimensions: as identity (knowing who 'we' are), as social (confirmed through exchange with others) and as value-based (independent value judgement and choice). From these follow three tasks. Values education should build value confidence and promote the wide practice of socialist core values. It should strengthen emotional identification and love of Chinese civilization. It should also convey public spirit and the common values of all humanity, while keeping a constructive-yet-critical stance towards foreign and emerging cultures.

For the three paths, Li calls on values education to explain the significance of the Two Integrations, which the article says created a new cultural form and resolved the long-running dispute over 'ancient and modern, Chinese and Western'. Li also wants it to build its own knowledge and discourse system from traditional, revolutionary and advanced socialist culture, and to cultivate openness and a public character. The article ties these tasks to upholding the Party's cultural leadership and to Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese ideological-education scholar links a layered theory of culture to concrete tasks for values education.
quoteEn: The core of cultural subjectivity is value subjectivity, which shows in the constant capacity for independent value judgement and value choice in the course of cultural development and cultural exchange.
quoteZh: 文化主体性的核心是价值主体性，体现为在文化发展和文化交流的过程中始终保持独立自主的价值判断和价值选择能力。

glossary.explanation: A concept stressed in Xi Jinping's recent statements on culture. It refers to a culture's autonomy, initiative and creativity, including self-awareness, self-identification and self-determination.
The formula that Marxism must be combined with China's concrete realities and with China's fine traditional culture. The second 'integration' was added in official discourse in 2021–2023.
A twelve-word official value set promoted since the 18th Party Congress (2012), covering national, social and individual levels: prosperity, democracy, freedom, equality, patriotism and others.
The official term for China's own path of modernization, promoted by the Party leadership since 2021–2022 as distinct from Western models.
The Party's claim to guide ideology and culture, echoing Gramsci's idea of hegemony. It is used in official discourse as part of ideological work.

t: On the generative mechanism of the leading force of ideological and political education
zh: 论思政引领力的生成机理
source: Research on Ideological Education (思想教育研究), 2025 no. 2
paras: Ye Fangxing takes up a concept that entered official language only recently: "ideological and political leading force" (sizheng yinlingli), listed in Xi Jinping's September 2024 speech at the National Education Conference, and again in the January 2025 Outline for Building a Strong Education Country (2024–2035), as the first attribute of a strong education country. The article asks how this force is generated. Ye argues that it arises from a practical process with five dimensions: real-world context, value direction, practical foundation, key link and supporting conditions.

The article is organised in five sections that follow these dimensions. It first places the concept in the policy context of building a strong education country, citing documents from 2010, 2019, the 20th Party Congress (2022) and 2024–25. It then discusses moral education as the value direction, the school ideological and political education system as the practical base, students' inner needs as the key link, and a healthy educational ecology as the guarantee.

Ye first distinguishes two senses of the term: a force as outcome, an indicator of how strong an education system is, and a force as means, the effect achieved through guiding practice. In Ye's account the force is directed by the fundamental task of fostering virtue and cultivating talent (lide shuren), with moral education given priority and ideals and convictions at its core. It is realised mainly in schools through a vertical "chain" across school stages and a horizontal "network" of channels. Three parts of this system are stressed: ideological and political theory courses, ideological and political education across all curricula, and everyday ideological and political education. Ye then argues that guidance must meet students' spiritual needs through targeted, differentiated approaches, must include reflection on and criticism of negative ideas rather than simply catering to students, and must draw on students' own initiative.

Ye concludes that the force depends on a good educational ecology at three levels. The macro level is a society-wide pattern of ideological and political work, the meso level is school governance, institutions and campus culture, and the micro level is the classroom as a space of meaning and emotion. Ye holds that these levels are conditional, intermediary and foundational respectively, and that they must interlock. Read the original if you want a systematic, policy-oriented account of how Chinese education scholars conceptualise ideological and political guidance within the drive to build a strong education country.
quoteEn: The leading force of ideological and political education is the practical effectiveness that educational activity displays, and the improvement of the school ideological and political education system bears directly on its effective generation.
quoteZh: 思政引领力是教育实践活动展现出的实践效能，学校思想政治教育体系的完善直接关乎思政引领力的有效生成。

glossary.explanation: A term first used in Xi Jinping's speech at the National Education Conference in September 2024 and repeated in the 2025 education outline. It refers to the effectiveness of education in shaping students' ideals, values and moral character.
A strategic goal of building China into a country with leading education capacity and influence by 2035. Official documents describe it as a precondition for national rejuvenation.
The officially stated fundamental task of education in China, giving priority to moral and political formation alongside knowledge and skills.
The compulsory courses on Marxism, Party theory and related subjects taught in Chinese schools and universities, regarded as the main channel of explicit moral and political education.

glossary.en: ideological and political education across all curricula
glossary.explanation: A policy of building moral and political education content into every subject, not only the dedicated political courses.

t: On the guiding power of ideological and political education
zh: 论思政引领力
paras: Xiang Jiuyu takes up the concept of "guiding power of ideological and political education" (sizheng yinlingli), which Xi Jinping introduced at the National Education Conference in September 2024. The 2025 Outline for Building a Strong Education Nation (2024–2035) repeated that a strong education nation with Chinese characteristics must possess it. Xiang argues that the concept is a theoretical distillation of the Party's historical experience in ideological and political education, and that it can be understood at three connected levels: macro, meso and micro.

The article is organised around these levels. The macro level places the concept within the construction of a strong education nation. The meso level treats it within the ideological and political education system, including ideological and political courses (sizheng ke), the "big ideological and political course" and "ideological and political education across the curriculum". The micro level examines it as a force of mainstream ideology. Xiang also traces the concept's lineage to Xi's earlier notion of "ideological guiding power" in Party building.

At the macro level, Xiang notes that guiding power comes first among the six powers Xi lists for a strong education nation. The others are talent competitiveness, scientific and technological support, livelihood security, social coordination and international influence. In Xiang's account it is the "lifeline" that shapes the other five, and it reflects national will and the value orientation of educational modernization. At the meso level, it is a unity of six forms of guidance: intellectual, political, cultural, value-based, faith-based and moral. These cannot be separated, and together they yield long-cycle, foundation-strengthening and wide-ranging advantages in moulding people. At the micro level, Xiang calls it essentially an ideological force that maintains Marxism's guiding position, orienting students towards history, the present and the future and countering views such as that communism is "remote" or "outdated". Xiang names three supports: the Party's innovative theory, the core socialist values, and the creative transformation of fine traditional Chinese culture.

Xiang concludes that the three levels together give the concept its theoretical content and practical force. At the macro level it answers the questions of whom to train, how and for whom. At the meso level it forms a "matrix" of guidance whose strength determines the effectiveness of ideological and political education. At the micro level it shows the Party's deepening grasp of how mainstream ideology is built. Xiang calls for further scholarly elaboration of the concept and for developing a disciplinary, academic and discourse system for the field with Chinese characteristics. Read the original if you study ideological and political education, Party ideology work or the official discourse on education in China, and want a systematic account of this newly coined concept.
quoteEn: The guiding power of ideological and political education is in essence an ideological force, that is, a real force formed through the dissemination of mainstream ideology.
quoteZh: 思政引领力本质上是一种意识形态力量，亦即主流意识形态传播所形成的现实力量。

glossary.en: guiding power of ideological and political education
glossary.explanation: A concept Xi Jinping put forward at the National Education Conference in September 2024. It refers to the capacity of ideological and political education to steer students' thinking, values and conduct.
A national goal set out in the 2024–2035 outline for building China into a leading country in education, with six listed attributes including this guiding power.
Compulsory courses in Chinese schools and universities that teach Marxism, Party theory and socialist values. The article calls them the main channel of ideological and political education.
The officially promoted Marxist-based body of ideas that guides the Party and the state, which the article treats as the content that guiding power conveys.

t: The content dimensions of building an autonomous knowledge system for the discipline of ideological and political education
zh: 论思想政治教育学自主知识体系构建的内容向度
source: Research on Ideological Education (Sixiang jiaoyu yanjiu), 2025 no. 2
paras: Responding to Xi Jinping's call (2022) to build an "autonomous knowledge system" for Chinese philosophy and social sciences, Hou and Ke ask what such a system should contain for the discipline of ideological and political education. Their thesis is that it should be built through the "three systems" (disciplinary, academic and discourse systems), following a logic of knowledge organisation, knowledge production and knowledge dissemination. They present this as an internal requirement of the discipline and a contribution to Chinese modernization.

The article first clarifies what the autonomous knowledge system is, surveying existing views by function, process, structure and elements, and then offers the authors' own definition: an integrated whole comprising conceptual, categorical, academic, rule-based, discourse, method and supporting systems. Three sections follow, one for each of the three systems. A fourth section turns to systems thinking: strategic orientation, overall planning, structural coupling and methodological innovation.

Hou and Ke argue that the disciplinary system organises knowledge: its core and branch discipline clusters, internal and cross-disciplinary coordination, and talent training and textbooks need strengthening. The academic system produces knowledge. It rests on Marxism as the "soul", excellent traditional Chinese culture as the "roots", and borrowing from related disciplines, together with basic-theory research and interdisciplinary work that avoids "mechanical borrowing". The discourse system disseminates knowledge. The authors call for a "terminological revolution" built around original, identifying concepts and for coordinated political, academic and everyday registers, along with narrative innovation. They also stress overseas communication that resists Western discourse dominance. They hold that the three systems are interdependent: the disciplinary system is the foundation, the academic system the driving force and the discourse system the key.

The authors conclude that the project is long-term and systematic. It requires the Two Integrations, the principle of putting the people first, self-confidence and self-reliance, and innovation within fundamental principles. It also requires problem orientation, systems thinking and a global outlook tied to a community with a shared future for mankind. They add that the content dimensions go beyond the three systems and need further study. Read the original if you want a detailed map of how Chinese scholars of ideological and political education frame disciplinary, academic and discourse construction in the language of Chinese modernization.
quoteEn: The disciplinary system is the foundation, the academic system is the driving force, and the discourse system is the key.
quoteZh: 学科体系是基础，学术体系是推动力，话语体系是关键。

glossary.explanation: A Chinese academic discipline, within the field of Marxist theory, that studies how the Party and state shape the ideas, political views and morals of citizens, especially students. It also covers the related teaching practice.
A concept stressed by Xi Jinping from 2022. It calls for Chinese social science to build its own concepts and theories on China's experience, rather than relying on Western frameworks.
The disciplinary, academic and discourse systems of Chinese philosophy and social sciences. The 20th Party Congress (2022) called for accelerating their construction.
The formula of integrating Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities and with China's fine traditional culture. It is associated with Xi Jinping.
The official name for China's development path, presented by the Party as distinct from Western modernization.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept for international relations and global governance, used officially to frame China's foreign policy and outlook.

t: Exploring the essence and laws of ideological and political theory courses
zh: 探求思想政治理论课的本质和规律
source: Marxist Theory Discipline Studies (马克思主义理论学科研究), 2025 no. 2
paras: How should one understand what China's school courses in ideological and political theory (sizheng courses) fundamentally are, and what regularities govern teaching them well? Tian Xinming takes up this question as an attempt to give the construction of these courses a more systematic, theoretically grounded form, drawing on Xi Jinping's remarks on the subject. The article's thesis is that the essence of the courses is "reasoning" (jiang daoli), that this demands explaining principles in depth, thoroughly and vividly, and that good teaching follows identifiable laws.

The article has four parts. It first defines the essence of the courses; it then explains what "deeply, thoroughly and vividly" means; it then treats the eight "unities" that Xi set out in 2019 as the laws of classroom teaching; and it finally turns to the laws of teacher development. Tian draws throughout on Xi, Mao Zedong, Lenin, Marx and Engels, and uses the method of contradiction analysis.

Tian argues that the "reasoning" in question is theory, and fundamentally Marxist theory. This follows from Marxism's guiding position in the Party and state, from its distinctive character as scientific and people-centred, and from the courses' particular role within the curriculum. Explaining "deeply" means moving from phenomena to essence and answering "why". Explaining "thoroughly" means tracing arguments to two root principles: that the world is unified in matter, and that the people are the creators of history. Tian adds that these principles are finally verified by social practice, not by logic. Explaining "vividly" means teaching a living Marxism, avoiding dogmatism and pragmatism, and presenting it as a system. The eight unities are read as eight contradictions to be handled, for example between political and academic character, values and knowledge, indoctrination and heuristic teaching, and explicit and implicit education.

For teachers, Tian proposes three laws. They should aim at the six qualities Xi listed: strong politics, deep feeling, fresh thinking, broad vision, strict self-discipline and upright character. They should master Marxism as their "home-grown skill" by reading the original works systematically. They should also unite reading, teaching and research around the same teaching priorities. The author presents these as the practical regularities behind well-run courses. Read the original if you want a detailed, officially aligned account of how Chinese theorists justify the content, method and teacher training of the ideological and political courses.
quoteEn: The essential requirement of ideological and political theory courses is to help students learn Marxist theory well.
quoteZh: 思政课的本质要求是帮助学生学好马克思主义理论。

glossary.explanation: Eight pairs of requirements for teaching the courses, set out by Xi Jinping at a 2019 symposium for teachers of these courses, such as political and academic character, and indoctrination and heuristic teaching.
An idiom for one's core, decisive competence. Xi Jinping applies it to mastering Marxism as the basic skill for Party cadres and teachers.

t: The leading role of universities in integrating ideological and political theory courses across university, secondary and primary schools
zh: 论高校在大中小学思政课一体化建设中的引领作用
source: Journal of Teaching and Research on Marxist Theory, 2025 no. 1
paras: Xu Ruifang and Wu Yutong ask how universities can best lead the integrated construction of ideological and political theory courses (sizheng ke) across university, secondary and primary schools. Their answer is that universities should act on the strategic importance the Party Central Committee attaches to this work, including the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), and use their strengths in disciplines, theory, teachers and resources to guide high-quality, content-based development of integration.

The article has three parts. The first defines four roles for universities: interpreter of policy and theory, solver of teaching-research problems, trainer of teachers, and developer of high-quality resources. The second identifies three difficulties: weak links between curriculum standards and textbooks, insufficient conversion of theoretical findings into classroom practice, and limited exchange between school stages. The third sets out a path of leadership through ideas, personnel, content and methods.

On the diagnosis, the authors report that university courses have no curriculum standards of their own, that primary-school goals are more detailed than those of later stages, and that textbooks repeat material or invert the order of difficulty. They give examples, such as a high-school textbook on the new development philosophy that is more detailed than its university counterpart. They also say that some research stays at the level of theoretical frameworks and that university teachers know little about what is taught in schools below them.

In response, the authors call for a unified curriculum standard across all stages that still respects the differences between them, with universities taking part in drafting it. They propose that universities support the move from disciplinary theory to textbooks and then to teaching, and that they train teachers through both pre-service and in-service programmes, with teacher-training universities in the lead. They also advocate practice-based teaching using local red-culture resources, together with digital platforms and regional databases shared among universities and schools. Throughout, they frame Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era as the core content of the courses. Read the original if you want a detailed Chinese-language account of how education researchers describe the policy problems and proposed institutional measures for integrating ideological and political courses across school stages.
quoteEn: Universities should truly play their leading role in advancing the integrated construction of ideological and political courses across university, secondary and primary schools by raising ideological awareness, strengthening teaching staff, coordinating course content and reinforcing technological empowerment.
quoteZh: 高校应通过提升思想认识、加强师资配备、统筹课程内容、强化技术赋能，切实发挥自身在推进大中小学思政课一体化建设中的引领作用。

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses on Marxism, Party theory and moral and political education taught at every level of Chinese schooling. The official name is 思想政治理论课, shortened to sizheng ke.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The official body of ideas associated with Xi Jinping, written into the Party and state constitutions and presented as the current stage of adapting Marxism to China.

t: On the deep integration of artificial intelligence and ideological and political education
zh: 人工智能与思想政治教育的深度融合论要
source: Marxist Theory Teaching and Research (马克思主义理论教学与研究), 2025 no. 1
paras: Ren Zhifeng and Liu Yang take up a problem they see in the current "AI+" research boom in education: an application-driven approach must decide which side leads. If education leads and AI is only an external tool, its potential is wasted; if AI leads, education risks technological domination and loss of its political and humanistic character. Following Xi Jinping's call to promote the deep integration of AI and education, the authors argue for moving from an "application orientation" to "deep integration", which they describe as a chemical rather than a physical reaction, and apply this to ideological and political education.

The article is organised in three parts. The first sets out the preconditions for integration; the second analyses its complex effects on ideological and political education; the third proposes possible paths. The authors draw on Marx's remarks on machinery, instruments of labour and technology, and on Horkheimer and Marcuse for the ideological character of technology.

On preconditions, the authors treat AI in three roles: as a technical means, as an infrastructure comparable to the steam engine, electricity and the internet, and as a marker of a new "intelligent civilisation". Each, they argue, matches a feature of ideological and political education: its technical logic, its changing forms, and its innovative development. On effects, they claim integration sharpens its essential ideological attribute, since AI carries implicit ideological functions and risks. It also brings out the meaning of human life, because the field must counter feelings of being replaced by machines. It makes practice more flexible through simulated and ubiquitous scenes, "strong interaction" between educator and learner, and quantified, precise evaluation.

For paths, the authors propose complementing strengths: big data to digitise, deep learning to make the field more intelligent, and computing power to make it more scientific. They propose linking functions across "what machines can do", "what humans and machines can do together" and "what humans can do". They also call for coordinated development that addresses legitimacy, effectiveness and innovation, keeping the cultivation of virtue and the human subject's leading role as the fixed value coordinates. Read the original if you want to see how Chinese scholars of ideological and political education justify and structure AI integration, and how they combine Marxist technology theory with practical proposals.
quoteEn: The deep integration of AI and ideological and political education is an intelligent turn in the latter's innovative development; it is not a wholesale deconstruction of ideological and political education, still less a wholesale subversion of its essence.
quoteZh: 人工智能与思想政治教育深度融合是思想政治教育创新发展的智能转向，既不是对思想政治教育的全面解构，更不是对思想政治教育本质的全面颠覆。

glossary.explanation: The system of teaching and guidance, in schools and beyond, through which the Party-state conveys its political ideas, values and morality. It is also an academic discipline in Chinese universities.
A fundamental educational aim in official Chinese policy: moral and character formation of students is the basic task of education.

t: The theoretical logic and pathways by which education digitalization promotes the development of new quality productive forces
zh: 教育数字化促进新质生产力发展的理论逻辑与路径探析
source: Journal of Guizhou University (Social Sciences Edition), 2025 no. 1
paras: Why, and how, can the digitalization of education advance new quality productive forces? Wang Tianping and Pan Qinqing argue that education digitalization is both a constituent part and an effective means of developing these forces, and that its main point of leverage is the training of "new quality talents". Writing in the context of Chinese modernization and high-quality development, they set out the internal logic of the link and propose practical paths.

The article has three parts. The first explains why education digitalization can promote new quality productive forces, drawing on the Marxist theory of productive forces, philosophy of technology and human-capital theory. The second describes four functions: promoting the turnover of emerging technologies, cultivating cutting-edge talent, creating a digital environment, and generating digital education industry clusters. The third identifies bottlenecks and proposes five paths, ending with a short conclusion.

The authors treat new quality productive forces as the third systemic revolution in productive forces, after the agricultural and industrial eras, marked by intelligent labour, digitalized factors of production and data as a new factor. Education belongs to the superstructure but also reproduces labour capacity and turns latent knowledge into actual productive power. Education digitalization therefore enlarges individuals' intellectual capital and spurs technological breakthroughs, through personalised learning, immersive environments, supportive policy and new industries such as online learning platforms. They also note risks: digital technology is a double-edged sword that may produce new inequalities, shallow thinking and privacy leaks.

The authors list current obstacles: weak technological foundations, unclear mechanisms linking technology and education, low digital literacy and an incomplete institutional framework. They propose five paths: advancing digital technology innovation, raising the level of digital education services, strengthening the educational function of digital education, building collaborative industry formats such as industry–university–research cooperation, and improving top-level design through strategic action plans, coordination mechanisms and ethical and privacy rules. They conclude that integrating education, science and technology, and talent is essential for developing new quality productive forces. Read the original if you want an example of how Chinese education scholars connect digitalization policy to new quality productive forces, with detailed policy suggestions.
quoteEn: Education digitalization promotes new quality productive forces by focusing on the cultivation of new quality talents: their development needs such talents, and by renewing the education system, education digitalization fosters them and supplies human resources to these forces.
quoteZh: 教育数字化推动新质生产力发展以培养新质人才为着力点，新质生产力发展需要新质人才推动，教育数字化通过革新教育系统，进而促进新质人才培养，为新质生产力提供人才资源。

glossary.explanation: A concept Xi Jinping first used in September 2023, referring to advanced productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs, innovative allocation of factors and industrial upgrading. It has since become central to official economic policy.
The official description of China's own path to modernization, which the Party presents as distinct from Western models.
An official goal, stressed since 2017, that prioritises innovation, efficiency and quality over speed of growth.
The deep integration of digital technologies into education systems, which official documents, including the 20th Party Congress report (2022), treat as a strategic task.

t: An analysis of the operating mechanisms of "Great Ideological and Political Course" practical teaching bases from an integrated perspective
zh: 一体化视域下“大思政课”实践教学基地运行机制探析
source: School Party Building and Ideological Education (学校党建与思想教育)
paras: How should the practical teaching bases of the "Great Ideological and Political Course" be run so that they work across primary school, secondary school and university? Yu and Chen treat these bases as venues and education platforms serving students of all three stages. They argue that the bases link the stages, join theory to practice, pool resources and support the fundamental task of fostering virtue through education. Their answer is a set of five operating mechanisms.

The article is a policy-oriented analysis of what it calls the integrated (一体化) approach to ideological and political courses across school stages. It is organised in five sections: a linked, coordinated mechanism; a regular interaction and communication mechanism; a stepped mechanism for education goals; a holistic evaluation and feedback mechanism; and a systematic support mechanism. Each section is broken into numbered sub-measures with concrete examples.

On coordination, the authors propose a joint leadership body of education authorities, schools and base managers. It would draw up shared plans, allocate resources, set common themes such as patriotism and red culture, and make content progress from intuitive experience in primary school to social investigation in secondary school and research-based practice at university. They also propose set communication rhythms: monthly online exchanges, a joint meeting each term and a site visit each year. Goals are tiered by age, moving from moral awareness to critical thinking to analysis of social hot-button issues, with teacher training and facilities tailored to each stage. Evaluation rests on five principles: political orientation, innovation, demonstration value, replicability and effectiveness. It also uses concrete checklists covering content, venue, staff, activities, rules and funding, and it combines process with outcome, quantitative with qualitative, and self with third-party assessment.

For support, the authors call for a special policy document, tax relief and subsidies for participating museums and enterprises, and coordination among education, finance and culture departments. They also propose awards for teachers, practice credits for students, honours for partner institutions and earmarked government funds supplemented by donations, with audit and public disclosure. In their view, these measures together can make the bases a lasting carrier of continuous, progressive ideological and political education. Read the original if you want a detailed, practice-level blueprint of how Chinese education officials and scholars envisage organising, evaluating and funding cross-stage practical teaching bases.
quoteEn: Political character is the core. It requires the bases to adhere to the guidance of Marxism in practical teaching and to disseminate the Party's theory, line, guidelines and policies.
quoteZh: 政治性是核心。它要求基地在实践教学中始终坚持马克思主义指导，传播党的理论和路线方针政策

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Chinese leaders in recent years that extends ideological and political teaching beyond the classroom into society and practice. It links the "small classroom" of the school with the "big classroom" of social life.
A stated fundamental task of Chinese education: shaping students' moral character and values alongside knowledge and skills.

glossary.literal: ideological and political course practical teaching base
glossary.explanation: Sites such as museums, memorials, enterprises or communities where students take part in practice-based ideological and political education outside the classroom.

t: Expanding the content of ideological and political education in the new era and building an autonomous knowledge system
zh: 新时代思想政治教育内容的拓展及自主知识体系建构
source: Studies on the Discipline of Marxist Theory (Marxism Theory Discipline Research)
paras: Dong Yahua asks how the content of ideological and political education should be innovated in the new era, on what basis, and what theoretical foundations the resulting expansion offers for an autonomous knowledge system of the discipline. The article, marking forty years since the discipline was founded, argues that content must develop in response to practice and under the guidance of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. It holds that the expanded content can be organised into ten "conceptions" and supported by a four-layer knowledge structure.

The article has three parts. The first sets out the grounds for innovation: social practice, illustrated by the shift from "legal system education" to "rule-of-law education" after the 15th Party Congress, and the guiding theory of the Party's latest Marxism. The second classifies the new content into six dimensions (ideals and convictions, core values, the Chinese spirit, cultural thought, ecological thinking, all-round human development) and ten conceptions, placed within the established five blocks of ideological, political, moral, cultural and psychological education. The third part builds the knowledge system.

Dong's core argument is that the ten conceptions, from worldview and ecology to political, national, ethnic, reform-and-innovation, moral, cultural and mental-health outlooks, extend the discipline's original framework in line with the principle of keeping to fundamental principles while innovating. For each, the article lists teaching priorities, such as whole-process people's democracy, rule-of-law education, common prosperity and forging a strong sense of community among the Chinese nation. The knowledge system then has four layers: Marxist fundamentals; Xi Jinping Thought as the core; Chinese and foreign disciplinary theories, including Western democratic theory, as a critical reference; and social practice and fine traditional Chinese culture. Drawing on Lakatos, Dong calls the first two the theoretical "hard core" and the last the "protective belt".

Dong concludes that these four layers should work together so that the aim of forging souls and nurturing people with Xi Jinping Thought takes root. The article is a programmatic outline of curriculum content rather than an empirical study. Read the original if you want a detailed map of how Chinese scholars of ideological and political education classify new-era teaching content and justify an autonomous disciplinary knowledge system.
quoteEn: Developmental character is a basic trait of the Chinese Communist Party's ideological and political education in each era, and keeping to fundamental principles while innovating is the basic principle for its development in the new era.
quoteZh: 发展性是中国共产党思想政治教育时代品质的基本特性，守正创新是新时代思想政治教育发展的基本原则。

glossary.explanation: The Party-state's system of teaching political ideas, values and morality, delivered in schools, universities and other institutions. It is also an academic discipline, founded in China in the mid-1980s.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The official guiding ideology of the Communist Party of China, written into the Party constitution in 2017.

A concept advanced by Xi Jinping to describe China's democratic system as covering all stages of political life, not only elections. Official sources present it as an alternative to Western electoral democracy.
An official goal of prosperity shared by all, which official texts describe as neither the wealth of a few nor egalitarian levelling.

glossary.en: sense of community among the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: consciousness of the Chinese nation as a community
glossary.explanation: An official policy slogan, stressed since 2014, that calls for a common national identity among all ethnic groups in China.

glossary.en: keeping to fundamental principles while innovating
glossary.explanation: An official formula for pursuing innovation without departing from the basic positions of Marxism and Party leadership.

t: Forty years of change in the undergraduate programme and academic discipline of ideological and political education: a multi-perspective reflection
zh: 40年来思想政治教育专业与学科变革实践的多域审思
paras: Marking the 40th anniversary of the establishment of the ideological and political education programme (zhuanye) in 2024, Huang Rongsheng asks what the programme and the academic discipline (xueke) of ideological and political education are, where they came from and where they should go. The author notes that scholars agree on the relation between practice and theory but disagree on how programme and discipline relate: which belongs to which, which came first, and which guides the other. Huang's answer is that the two are distinct but bound by a shared purpose and have developed in mutual support, and that their next stage should shift from scale to quality.

The article is organised in three perspectives. The first, conceptual, defines the programme as a category of study set up in universities to train specialists in ideological and political work, and the discipline as an academic classification that studies how people's ideological and political qualities form and how education shapes them. The second, historical, periodises each track using official catalogues and policy documents. The third looks ahead to goals and measures for the new journey.

Huang argues that the two share three commitments: training people for the Party and the country, training specialists in ideological and political work, and teaching through courses. On history, the programme is traced from 1984 through setting-up, stabilisation and improvement phases. The discipline is traced from 1987 through inception, initial establishment, merger and renewal, ending in its place as a second-level discipline under the first-level discipline of Marxist theory. Huang stresses that this path was unusual, since the programme came first and the discipline later. The author describes the programme as catalysing the discipline, the discipline then supporting the programme with textbooks, degree programmes and teaching staff, and both serving university courses in ideological and political theory.

For the programme, Huang proposes optimising training plans, building a systematic curriculum and compiling key textbooks. For the discipline, the proposals are building an autonomous knowledge system, raising the quality of its academic workforce and strengthening research. Three general measures follow: holding to the "lifeline" and "central link" role of ideological and political work, advancing reform and innovation, and strengthening bases and platforms. Read the original if you study how Chinese higher education institutionalised ideological and political education, or want a detailed chronology of the relevant catalogues, policies and textbooks.
quoteEn: The logical connection between the ideological and political education programme and discipline is concentrated in jointly serving and safeguarding universities' fundamental task of fostering virtue through education and training qualified builders and reliable successors for socialism.
quoteZh: 思想政治教育专业与学科的逻辑关联集中体现在共同为高校完成“立德树人”根本任务、培养社会主义合格建设者和可靠接班人提供服务和保障。

glossary.explanation: A Chinese concept covering the Party's and universities' work of shaping people's ideological, political and moral outlook. It is both a social practice and an academic field in China.
A category of study set up by a university to train people in a particular line of work, with its own courses and degrees.
An academic classification of a field of research, listed in the state catalogue for postgraduate education and degree awarding.
A phrase in Party discourse describing ideological and political work as the lifeline of economic work and all other work. The author cites Hu Jintao's formulation.
A Party formulation, used by Mao Zedong and later leaders, describing ideological education as the pivotal element in uniting the Party and people for their tasks.

t: Activating the outstanding elements of China's excellent traditional culture
zh: 激活中华优秀传统文化中的优秀因子
paras: This commentary, published in Guangming Daily on 3 March 2025, takes up Xi Jinping's instruction to use Marxism to activate the vital elements of China's excellent traditional culture and give them new meaning for the era. Han Qingxiang reads the instruction as setting out the agent, object, purpose and method of activation, and as a basic guide to building a strong socialist cultural power. Han argues that Marxism and traditional culture are highly compatible, so activation can bring out the contemporary value of tradition and serve national rejuvenation.

The piece has three parts. The first identifies which "outstanding elements" are to be activated; the second sets out how activation should proceed; the third lists the new contemporary meanings to be given to them. For the first part, Han draws on Chinese philosophy, ethics and morality, and the shared everyday values of ordinary people.

The core argument concerns method. Han says activation means making traditional culture "modern" and giving Chinese civilization modern strength, and it must resolve four questions: cognition, agent, method and purpose. On agent, Han holds that Marxism is inclusive, opposes dogmatism and shares with tradition the goals of national rejuvenation and peaceful development. The method is mutual empowerment through the Two Integrations: tradition supplies soil for adapting Marxism, and Marxism renews tradition. The purpose is to consolidate the cultural subjectivity of the Chinese nation, move beyond Western-centred narratives of modernity, and build an autonomous Chinese knowledge system. Han also proposes new contemporary meanings. Harmony between humans and nature is linked to ecological civilization, "the world belongs to all" to a community with a shared future for mankind, and "the people as the foundation" to putting the people first. Traditional ethics is linked to Party-building, loyalty to the Party, the Two Establishes and the Two Upholds, and official integrity, while everyday values are linked to family ethics, honest labour and the rule of law.

Han concludes that activation should release creative vitality in Chinese culture, assert its subjectivity, build an autonomous knowledge system and raise the global influence of Chinese civilization. It would also enrich people's spiritual world and strengthen Party leadership over culture. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned statement of how Party theorists frame the relation between Marxism and traditional culture, and which concepts they select for reinterpretation.
quoteEn: The essence of "activation" is to make China's excellent traditional culture modern, to create the cultural form of Chinese modernization, and to endow Chinese civilization with modern strength.
quoteZh: “激活”的实质，就是让中华优秀传统文化成为现代的，创造中国式现代化的文化形态，赋予中华文明以现代力量。

glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's formula for combining Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture. The second integration was added to Party theory in 2021–2023.
A formula from the 20th Party Congress period (2022) affirming Xi Jinping's position as the Party's core and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought.
A Party principle requiring members to uphold Xi Jinping's core position in the Party and the authority and centralised leadership of the Central Committee.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept for China's vision of international relations, stressing cooperation and shared development.
A term popularised in recent Party discourse for the Chinese nation's independent standing and self-awareness in cultural matters, as opposed to dependence on Western frameworks.

t: Using red resources to strengthen the fighting spirit of young cadres
zh: 运用红色资源增强年轻干部的斗争精神
paras: This commentary asks how "red resources" can be used to build the fighting spirit (douzheng jingshen) of young cadres. Wang takes up Xi Jinping's call to use such resources to strengthen ideals and convictions and raise the capacity to struggle. The article argues that the historical, cultural and contemporary value of these resources should be tapped so that young cadres learn to shoulder heavy responsibilities, work hard and confront problems.

Wang organises the piece around four types of red resource: historical events, revolutionary heroes, revolutionary spirit and revolutionary cultural relics. Each is linked to a distinct quality to be cultivated: struggle consciousness, will, strength and wisdom. Xi Jinping's statements are cited throughout as the guiding framework.

On historical events, Wang says they show that struggle is tied to individual survival and national strength. They should be studied through a connected view, on the basis of reliable sources, so that political education works through events. On heroes and spirit, Wang calls for learning loyalty, persistence and plainness, and for the Party's self-reform, a people-centred approach and tempering in strict inner-Party political life. On relics, Wang proposes a shift from rescue to preventive protection, protecting objects together with their surroundings, and using modern technology and immersive display.

Wang also proposes linking revolutionary culture education to anti-corruption education, including integrity education bases at red sites, and deeper research into the history behind relics. The aim is for Party members and cadres to take up the task of national rejuvenation through concrete action. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-school writing links heritage protection to cadre training.
quoteEn: Only by forming a correct understanding of historical events can one truly grasp the great choices the Party made at different historical stages.
quoteZh: 唯有对历史事件形成正确的认知，才能真正理解在不同历史阶段党作出的伟大抉择

glossary.explanation: A collective term for sites, relics, figures, events and spirit associated with the Communist Party's revolutionary history, used in patriotic and Party education.
A quality stressed in Xi Jinping-era Party discourse: readiness to confront risks, difficulties and problems. It is promoted among cadres through training and education.
An official concept for the Party's efforts to purify, improve and renew itself through internal discipline and rectification.

glossary.literal: great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's central goal of restoring China's strength and international standing by the mid-twenty-first century.

t: Research on building ideological positions: course, main achievements and future trends
zh: 意识形态阵地建设研究的历程回顾、主要成就与趋势展望
source: School Party Building and Ideological Education (学校党建与思想教育), 2024 no. 21
paras: This literature review surveys more than twenty years of Chinese scholarship on "ideological position building" (yishi xingtai zhendi jianshe), the effort to hold and expand the physical and virtual spaces where Marxist ideology is transmitted. The authors argue that the research has tracked national economic conditions, policy priorities and technological change. They conclude that it still lacks overall coherence, theoretical grounding and historical depth. The article was published in a 2024 journal on Party building and ideological education.

The review divides the research into four phases. The first, after reform and opening up, drew little attention. Attention then rose after Xi Jinping's 2014 holistic approach to national security, with universities as the main focus. The 19th Party Congress (2017) called for strengthening position building and management, and publications peaked in 2019. After the Party's third historical resolution (2021), output declined, with universities and the internet remaining central. The main body then sorts the literature into four themes: why position building is necessary, the key concepts, the main arenas, and response strategies.

On necessity, the authors report that scholars point to the Soviet collapse, which they attribute partly to the loss of control over public opinion. They also report the view that ideology has no vacuum, that socialist and capitalist ideologies are in irreconcilable contest, and that Western pressure on China persists. On concepts, scholars treat a "position" as both real and virtual space, and read "position consciousness" as both cognition and responsibility. The authors note that no clear definition of position building exists. The strategies they summarise are strengthening position consciousness, occupying positions with Marxism, upholding Party leadership, combining position building with the rule of law, and taking the initiative in struggle.

The authors identify three gaps. Research should treat position building as a system, covering its features, current problems, goals and evaluation mechanisms. It should draw more on Marxist theory, such as the views of contradiction and of time and space, rather than on Western theories of hegemony. It should also offer a systematic account of the Chinese Communist Party's century of experience in this field. Read the original if you want a map of how Chinese ideological-work scholarship is organised, including its main themes, representative studies and recommended directions.
quoteEn: Scholars hold that there is no vacuum in ideology.
quoteZh: 学者们认为，意识形态没有中空地带。

glossary.explanation: A term in Chinese Party discourse for establishing and managing the institutions and spaces (media, universities, the internet) through which the Party's dominant ideology is spread and defended.
A phrase Xi Jinping used at the 2013 national conference on propaganda and ideological work. It calls on cadres to recognise that ideological spaces not held by the Party will be taken by others.
A concept Xi Jinping put forward in 2014 that treats security broadly, including political, cultural and ideological fields alongside military security.
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched in China in 1978.

t: New progress in research on the methodology of ideological and political education in the new era
zh: 新时代思想政治教育方法论研究的新进展
source: School Party Building and Ideological Education (Xuexiao dangjian yu sixiang jiaoyu), 10 December 2024
paras: This is a literature review of scholarship on the methodology of ideological and political education (the body of theory about the methods used in such education) since the 18th Party Congress (2012). Liu treats this methodology as an important part of the discipline's knowledge system. The review argues that research has advanced by following three methodological principles: upholding fundamental principles while innovating, being problem-oriented, and thinking systemically.

The review is organised in three sections that match those principles. The first covers basic theory: core concepts, "meta-theory", theoretical sources and historical development. The second covers new problems: big-data methods, the teaching methods of ideological and political theory courses, and the use of specific methods. The third covers the construction of a knowledge system, meaning the structure of methodological systems and research methods. Liu names many scholars and works under each heading, including Luo Yuting, Xiang Jiuyu, Lou Shuhua, Zou Shaoqing and Zhang Yaocan.

On basic theory, Liu reports that definitions have come to stress interaction between educators and the people they educate, and that scholars separate "method" from "methodology", the latter being a systematic abstraction of methods. Theoretical support is drawn from Marxist classics, traditional Chinese culture, the educational practice of Chinese Communists such as Mao Zedong, and Xi Jinping's discussions. On new problems, the review describes work on integrating big data with the discipline, on diversified and technology-enabled teaching, and on borrowing from sociology, psychology, linguistics and cognitive neuroscience. On system-building, it traces successive frameworks (activity-process, epistemological, contradiction-based, strategic-guidance) and recent debates, such as whether the system can be made scientific or only disciplinary. It also covers research paradigms and methods, including theoretical, textual, historical, interest-analysis and oral-history approaches.

Liu presents the field as marked by growing methodological self-awareness, with a rich output of books and papers. Anniversaries such as the discipline's 30th and 40th have prompted retrospective summaries. The review does not set out a separate list of gaps, but it points to the continuing task of deepening theory, digital transformation and system-building. Read the original if you want a map of the main Chinese scholars, titles and subtopics in this subfield, for example when tracing how the discipline's teaching and research methods are being theorised.
quoteEn: The primary focus of methodological research on ideological and political education in the new era is to uphold fundamental principles while innovating, and to keep deepening understanding of its basic concepts, historical development, \"meta-theory\" construction, the theoretical support for methods, and the laws governing their development and innovation.
quoteZh: 新时代思想政治教育方法论研究的首要着力点是坚持守正创新，继续深化对思想政治教育方法论的基本概念、历史发展、“元理论”建构以及方法的理论支撑、发展创新规律等问题域的理解

glossary.explanation: A Chinese academic discipline and field of practice concerned with shaping people's ideas, values and political outlook, especially in schools and universities and within the Party.

glossary.literal: preserve what is correct and innovate
glossary.explanation: A guiding formula in Party discourse: keep to fundamental principles and orientation while developing new approaches.
Compulsory courses on Marxism and Party doctrine taught at Chinese schools and universities, which Party leaders have repeatedly urged be reformed and strengthened.
Reflection on a theory's own concepts, objects and assumptions. In this review it means scholars examining the methodology of the discipline itself.

t: The theoretical characteristics of the Party's propaganda, ideological and cultural work
zh: 党的宣传思想文化工作的理论特质
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 27 February 2025
paras: This short commentary asks what distinguishes the Communist Party of China's propaganda, ideological and cultural work as a body of theory and practice. The authors argue that since the 18th Party Congress (2012), Xi Jinping has systematically set out why the work matters, where it is headed, who does it and how. They contend that it displays three paired characteristics: unity of Party spirit and people's character, of principle and innovation, and of the national and the global.

The article is organised around these pairs, with a short framing introduction. It treats each pair in turn, first describing the two sides and then stating what the resulting characteristic enables. It draws throughout on Xi Jinping's statements on leadership, the goals of the work, new media, historical nihilism and cultural confidence. The authors present the work as a response to fundamental questions that Xi is said to have answered.

On the first pair, the authors say that upholding Party leadership over ideology and the principle of Party spirit goes together with a people-centred orientation that serves and educates the masses. They hold that the Party's aims coincide with the people's fundamental interests, so the pairing consolidates the Party's governing base and gathers strength for the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation through Chinese modernization. On the second pair, principle means firm adherence to Marxism's guiding position and treating ideological security as part of national political security. Innovation means new ideas, methods and grassroots practice, a "big propaganda" concept, and new formulations such as "cultural identity is the deepest level of identity". Together these amount to "upholding fundamental principles while breaking new ground". The authors add that the third pair, timeliness and practicality, is shown in the response to new media and to historical nihilism. The fourth, the national and the global, combines emphasis on Chinese cultural subjectivity and an autonomous knowledge system with learning from other civilizations, international communication and a community with a shared future for mankind.

The authors conclude that these characteristics let the Party keep its direction while moving with the times, turn grassroots experience into working principles, and build national cultural confidence. They also say the characteristics help China withstand the clash of ideas and culture and present itself as a self-reliant civilizational power. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how Party theorists summarise the logic of Xi-era ideological work.
quoteEn: To uphold the unity of principle and innovation in the Party's propaganda, ideological and cultural work is to uphold fundamental principles while breaking new ground in this field.
quoteZh: 党的宣传思想文化工作坚持原则性和创新性的统一，就是在宣传思想文化工作领域坚持守正创新。

glossary.explanation: The Party's portfolio covering propaganda, ideology, media, culture and public opinion. It is handled by the Party's propaganda system, which the Party itself describes with this term.
A formula holding that loyalty to the Party and service to the people are identical in the Party's work. It is often applied to the media and ideological work.
