glossary.en: upholding fundamental principles while breaking new ground
glossary.literal: preserve what is correct and innovate
glossary.explanation: A slogan in Xi-era Party discourse that pairs fidelity to core principles with innovation in methods and ideas.
The official name for the Party's path to modernization, presented as distinct from Western models. It has been prominent in Party discourse since the 20th Party Congress (2022).

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept for international relations, which the Party presents as an alternative framework of global cooperation.
In Party usage, a label for views seen as distorting or denigrating the Party's history, its leaders and the socialist record.

t: Building China's international image in the new era
zh: 建构新时代中国国际形象
source: Jiefang Daily, 18 February 2024 (as given in the source metadata)
paras: This short newspaper commentary asks how China's international image should be measured and built, and who should hold the authority to define it. Wang Zhen starts from the global attention drawn by DeepSeek and the film Ne Zha 2, and from the Global Times' report on China's international image, a survey of 51,000 people in 46 countries. The author argues that the survey marks a shift from an image shaped by others to one shaped by China itself, and that China must build its own discursive power.

The piece has three parts. The first reads the survey results and the significance of the report. The second sets out three academic approaches to assessing a national image and questions the claimed neutrality of Western polling bodies. The third makes proposals for building China's own discourse power, under two headings: strengthening self-awareness and confidence, and strengthening design and guidance.

Wang reads the survey as showing that 77 per cent of respondents see China's economy as strong, that over 90 per cent expect growth over the next decade, and that 69 per cent want China to take a larger part in international affairs. The author says this refutes Western claims of a Chinese economic collapse or a peak in China's rise. Wang also stresses that developing-country respondents, including those in the Global South, were given particular weight and were more favourable. The three approaches to assessment are communication studies (opinion polling), marketing (national brand indices) and international politics (soft power). Wang argues that Western pollsters present themselves as scientific but can shape results through agenda-setting, assumed positions and sampling. As evidence the author cites funding of US think tanks and media organisations by government bodies, including the US Agency for International Development.

Wang concludes that questions about China's image cannot be settled by a few Western institutions or politicians, nor by Western standards alone. The author calls for resisting what the piece describes as Western slander in international opinion contests, and for original theoretical frameworks acceptable abroad. Wang also urges adherence to the Four-sphere Confidence, support for Chinese media to "go global", and narratives that overseas audiences can understand and respond to. Read the original if you want a concise example of how a Chinese scholar frames image-building as a contest over discursive power and cites the Global Times survey in support of that view.
quoteEn: The construction and assessment of China's international image is moving from \"other-shaping\", led by Western institutions, to a more active and autonomous \"self-shaping\".
quoteZh: 中国国际形象建构与评估正在从以西方机构为主导的“他塑”跨向更加积极自主的“自塑”。

glossary.explanation: A formula in Party discourse, associated with Xi Jinping, calling for confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics.
A term for developing countries, widely used in Chinese official and academic discourse to place China among them.
The capacity to set the terms, concepts and narratives through which a country or issue is described internationally. Chinese writers often argue that Western states hold it and China should gain it.

t: Explaining principles, infusing love, putting into practice: continuously strengthening the guiding power of ideological and political work in universities
zh: 讲理、融爱、力行，不断提升高校思政引领力
paras: This short commentary starts from Xi Jinping's remarks at the 2024 National Education Conference. Xi listed six capacities of a leading education country, and Liu notes that the guiding power of ideological and political work comes first. Liu argues that universities can raise this guiding power along three paths: explaining principles (讲理), infusing love (融爱) and putting ideas into practice (力行).

The article is organised under three short headings, each unpacked into three sub-points. "Principles" covers Marxist fundamentals, the theory behind Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, and everyday guidance on how to live, study and act. "Love" covers care, passion and a larger patriotic love. "Practice" covers hands-on activity, learning that follows industry trends, and volunteering.

On principles, Liu calls for teaching why Marxism is scientific and suits China, and for guiding students to read original works and to "truly study, understand, believe and apply" it. Teaching must also reach students through the internet and forms they like. On love, Liu says educators should first understand students' needs, for example through "one-stop" community centres combining tutoring, counselling and talks. They should also awaken intrinsic motivation and nurture patriotic feeling through immersive experiences, alumni visits and red culture on campus. On practice, Liu proposes a broad ideological and political education system in which classes extend into society, internships, research placements and volunteering.

Liu concludes that students should unite knowledge and action, so that what they learn is applied, their capacity to innovate grows and their ideals come alive. The piece is a practical outline for university ideological and political educators. Read the original if you want a concise example of how current Party language on education is turned into suggestions for campus ideological and political work.
quoteEn: Ideological and political courses should be taught not only in the classroom but also in social life.
quoteZh: 思政课不仅应该在课堂上讲，也应该在社会生活中讲。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Communist Party of China's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017 and 2018.

glossary.en: guiding power of ideological and political work
glossary.explanation: One of the "six capacities" Xi Jinping named for a leading education country. It refers to the capacity of ideological and political education to shape students' beliefs and values.

t: The spread and transformation of the concept of "nihilism" in China
zh: “虚无主义”概念的传播与衍变
paras: This short piece, published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today on 26 February 2025, asks how the concept of "nihilism" (xuwu zhuyi) entered Chinese and why its meaning has been so unclear. Zhang argues that the term's introduction and evolution were highly complex: in the early twentieth century it referred at once to Western Nihilism, to anarchism, and to the Daoist ideas of "emptiness and non-action".

The article proceeds chronologically and by sources. It begins with the classical meaning of xuwu in Daoist texts, then traces the transliteration of Nihilist in late nineteenth-century Chinese newspapers and diplomats' diaries. It next follows the Japanese route through which "nihilist party" became the standard rendering, examines early English–Chinese dictionaries of 1908, 1913 and 1916, and ends with attempts by Liao Zhongkai and Zhou Zuoren to clarify the concept.

Zhang's central argument is that Chinese usage became confused as the term passed through Japan. In the 1880s Japanese translators rendered Nihilist as "nihilist party", and after 1903 Liang Qichao's essay and translations of Kayama Sentarō's work on modern anarchism, often retitled with "nihilist party", made nihilism, populism and anarchism "share one hat". The dictionaries reflect this: the 1916 dictionary Guanhua gave separate philosophical and political senses, the latter equated with anarchism. Zhang reports that Zhou Zuoren in 1907 tried to separate nihilism as a philosophical doctrine from terrorism, but that such efforts had little effect, and that Liao Zhongkai himself used the terms inconsistently.

Zhang concludes that in early twentieth-century Chinese, many intellectuals used such "new terms" in polemics without systematic understanding, leaving the meaning of "nihilism" ambiguous. The piece offers a conceptual history rather than a contemporary political argument. Read the original if you are interested in the translation history of Nihilism in China and the early dictionary and periodical sources behind it.
quoteEn: In sum, in the Chinese context of the early twentieth century, "nihilism" referred to Nihilism, to anarchism, and was also closely tied to the Daoist "emptiness and non-action", presenting a complex picture of unclear meaning.
quoteZh: 总而言之，在20世纪初的中文语境中，“虚无主义”既指Nihilism，又指Anarchist（无政府主义），还与道家的“虚无、无为”密切相关，呈现出语义不明的复杂图景。

glossary.explanation: Modern Chinese rendering of Nihilism, built on the older Daoist word xuwu. In early twentieth-century China it also overlapped with anarchism and populism.
Term, borrowed from Japanese, for Russian Nihilists and especially the populist Narodnaya Volya assassins. It later became a loose label for revolutionaries and anarchists.
Doctrine opposing state authority. In late Qing and early Republican China it was often conflated with the "nihilist party".
Relating to the school of thought associated with Laozi and Zhuangzi. Its texts use xuwu for the formless, empty nature of the Dao.

t: Always making the Party's innovative theory the primary task of forging souls and educating people
zh: 始终把党的创新理论武装作为铸魂育人的首要任务
paras: This commentary by Pu Duanhua, first published in the PLA Daily on 24 February 2024, takes up a requirement in a recent notice from the Political Work Department of the Central Military Commission on the army's annual education campaign. The notice calls for always making arming people with the Party's innovative theory the primary task of "forging souls and educating people" (铸魂育人) in the armed forces. Pu argues that this requirement correctly identifies the status and function of theoretical armament and gives the military a clear direction for this foundational work.

The piece has three numbered sections. The first explains why theoretical armament deserves priority, the second what role it plays in forging souls, and the third how to carry it out in practice. Pu draws on Lenin, early Party documents, Mao Zedong's principles for the Red Army and Xi Jinping's statements on talent and ideological unity.

In the first section, Pu gives three grounds for the priority. It follows a regularity of proletarian parties, which need to "instil" advanced theory from outside to produce successors for a long-term cause. It continues a tradition the Party and army have kept since the first Party Congress and the Red Army's early days. It is also required to train high-quality officers for building a strong military and a world-class army by the centenary goal of 2027. The second section assigns theory three functions: political guidance, value shaping and goal orientation. Under political guidance, officers and soldiers should grasp the Two Establishes, strengthen the Four-sphere Confidence, carry out the Two Upholds and implement the chairman responsibility system of the Central Military Commission. Under value shaping, theory should counter the effects of competing social currents. Under goal orientation, it should unite the force around the centenary goal.

In the third section Pu proposes three measures. The first is to study Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era and Xi Jinping Thought on Strengthening the Military in depth and persistently, with attention to original texts. The second is to promote a Marxist style of study that links theory to practice and opposes empty talk and a split between theory and practice. The third is to make leading cadres, the "critical few", set an example as the "lead geese", studying first and more deeply. Read the original if you want a concise example of how PLA political-work writing justifies and operationalises ideological education.
quoteEn: The more thorough the theoretical armament, the purer the thinking, the firmer the belief and the more conscious the action.
quoteZh: 理论武装越彻底，思想就越纯洁，信仰就越坚定，行动就越自觉。

glossary.literal: casting the soul and nurturing people
glossary.explanation: A phrase for ideological and moral education aimed at shaping the political loyalty and convictions of personnel. Here it is used for political education in the armed forces.
A formula from the Party's 2021 resolution on history, affirming Xi Jinping's position as core of the Central Committee and the Party as a whole and the guiding role of his thought.
A Party requirement to uphold Xi Jinping's core position in the Central Committee and the Party as a whole, and to uphold the Central Committee's authority and centralised, unified leadership.
Confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017 and 2018.
A term for leading cadres, whose conduct and study are held to set the example for the wider membership.

keywords: Xi Jinping Thought on Strengthening the Military

t: Cleaning up the online environment requires breaking the "information cocoon"
zh: 净化网络环境亟须破除“信息茧房”
paras: This newspaper commentary, published in Guangming Daily on 24 February 2025, takes up the "information cocoon" (xinxi canfang), the condition in which algorithms surround users with customised content. It was prompted by a joint notice from the Cyberspace Administration of China and other ministries launching a special "Qinglang" campaign against typical algorithm problems, including homogeneous content pushing. He argues that strict, law-based enforcement is needed to build a healthy, orderly and diverse information environment.

The piece first defines the phenomenon and lists its harms to individuals, society and the state. It then sets out five lines of action: government supervision and legislation, platform responsibility and transparency, cooperation between regulators and research institutions, public education, and punishment of false information.

He argues that cocoons narrow users' horizons, produce cognitive bias, stifle innovation, hinder communication between groups and may damage social harmony. The author also says wrongdoers exploit algorithmic recommendation for false advertising, traffic fraud and telecom scams, citing recruitment platforms that stoke job anxiety to sell expensive memberships. On the remedies, He proposes dedicated algorithm regulators, periodic algorithm audits and specific algorithm laws built on principles such as fairness and explainability. Platforms should disclose how their algorithms work and diversify recommendations. Regulators should use AI to monitor algorithms, "fighting magic with magic", and blockchain and digital watermarks should secure the traceability of content.

He concludes that law-based enforcement is a necessary step towards an open, inclusive and truthful digital society, and that it also needs the joint effort of all sectors. Public critical thinking and rumour punishment are treated as part of the same effort. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Chinese legal scholars and official media frame algorithm governance and the "information cocoon" in policy terms.
quoteEn: The "information cocoon" is a serious challenge of the information age; only strict, law-based crackdown and rectification can promote diversity and openness of information, create a safe platform environment and build a healthy, orderly and pluralistic information environment.
quoteZh: “信息茧房”是信息时代面临的一个严峻挑战，只有依法严厉打击整治，才能促进信息的多样性和开放性，创建安全的平台环境，构建一个健康、有序、多元的信息环境。

glossary.explanation: A state in which users, fed personalised content by algorithms, meet only information matching their existing preferences. The idea is similar to the Western notion of the filter bubble or echo chamber.
A series of special campaigns run by Chinese internet regulators, led by the Cyberspace Administration of China, to clean up online content and platform conduct.

t: How 5G technology can strengthen the guidance of mainstream ideology and public opinion
zh: 5G技术助力提升主流思想舆论引导力
paras: Writing in China Social Sciences Today (21 February 2025), Lin Minjian takes up the call of the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) to integrate the management of news publicity and online opinion. The commentary argues that applying 5G technology to strengthen the guidance of mainstream ideology and public opinion is both a necessary response to new challenges and an unavoidable result of new technologies spreading through society.

Lin organises the proposals under four headings: "5G+content" production, "5G+public opinion" governance, "5G+media" communication scenarios, and a "5G+talent" workforce. Each is tied to an image of mainstream opinion work: an "gravitational field", a "firewall", an "adhesive" and "concentric circles".

On content, Lin argues that robot writing, digital anchors and platforms such as Xinhua's "central kitchen" raise output, while CCTV's "5G+8K" and "5G+VR" broadcasts make mainstream content more attractive. On governance, Lin warns that 5G speeds the spread of negative opinion and false information. The author calls for upholding Marxism's guiding position, Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era and core socialist values, together with joint government–media prevention and control mechanisms and routine big-data monitoring of opinion. On communication, Lin urges wearables, smart homes, holographic formats and precise algorithmic delivery.

Lin concludes that mainstream media need a workforce with political awareness, media literacy and technical skill. Proposed measures include reformed incentive systems, training in new technologies, and cultivating politically firm, popular scholars as online opinion leaders. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Chinese ideological-work scholarship frames 5G and big data as tools for opinion guidance.
quoteEn: Whatever the environment, we should always uphold and consolidate Marxism's guiding position in the ideological sphere.
quoteZh: 无论环境如何变化,我们都应始终坚持和巩固马克思主义在意识形态领域的指导地位。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.
A set of 24 characters in three tiers (national, social, individual) promoted officially since 2012, including prosperity, democracy, harmony and patriotism.
Official term for the dominant, Party-endorsed ideas and public discourse, as distinct from "negative" or "erroneous" opinion.

t: Methods for building an international communication strategy system with Chinese characteristics
zh: 中国特色国际传播战略体系构建方法
paras: Responding to the call of the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) to build a "more effective international communication system", Chen Hong asks how an international communication strategy system with Chinese characteristics should be built. The author argues that it must rest on a value system, a structural system and an operating system, and that the aim is to strengthen global strategic cooperation against shared conflicts and challenges. The piece is a short newspaper commentary.

It is organised in three parts. The first concerns communication practice grounded in a community with a shared future for mankind. The second concerns deepening all-media, multidimensional discourse among government, media, enterprises and individuals. The third concerns an operating system for multiple audiences, with a focus on Generation Z.

Chen argues that the idea of a community with a shared future for mankind supplies the guiding value, and that the Belt and Road Initiative gives it a practical platform. Emotional resonance, in this account, can cross cultural and language barriers. The author assigns distinct roles to each actor: government as communicator and gatekeeper, media as guarantor of accurate reporting, enterprises as carriers of brand values, and individuals as spontaneous disseminators. These actors need a professional deliberative mechanism, and messages should fit local cultural contexts to avoid "communication without understanding". Chen cites the overseas spread of Chinese 5G technology as an example. Generation Z, described as the first "digital natives", is presented as key to building a communication system for all. The author notes that TikTok has over 1.1 billion daily active users worldwide, yet only seven central state-owned enterprises have official accounts.

Chen calls for a combined system in which government leads, media cooperate and enterprises support, so that young people can take part in cross-cultural exchange. The aim is shared cultural understanding worldwide and a higher-quality stage of international communication. Read the original if you want a brief statement of how Chinese communication scholars frame audience strategy, especially towards Generation Z.
quoteEn: International communication is in essence a process of uniting forces and winning hearts and minds.
quoteZh: 国际传播本质上是团结力量、争取人心的过程。

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping since the early 2010s, describing a vision of international relations based on shared interests and cooperation. It is presented as a guiding idea of Chinese foreign policy.
A Chinese initiative launched in 2013 to build infrastructure and economic links between China and other countries across Eurasia, Africa and beyond.
The Chinese term for external communication aimed at foreign audiences, covering media, diplomacy and cultural outreach. It is often discussed as a way to "tell China's story well".

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: Upholding fundamental principles and innovating to promote the intension-based development of ideological and political courses in universities
zh: 守正创新推动高校思政课建设内涵式发展
paras: This newspaper commentary, published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in February 2025, asks how university ideological and political courses (sizheng courses) can improve their quality and appeal. Mei argues that the answer lies in balancing two requirements, upholding fundamental principles (shouzheng) and innovating (chuangxin). Taking Xi Jinping's instruction on the subject as its starting point, the article treats this balance as the basis of what it calls intension-based development, meaning growth driven by internal elements and quality rather than expansion in scale.

The piece is organised in three parts. The first explains why both principles and innovation are needed. The second covers fulfilling the fundamental task of fostering virtue through education (lide shuren) through three internal elements: teaching content, teaching channels and teacher quality. The third sets out three innovative measures: integrating ideological and political courses across primary, secondary and university stages, aligning dedicated courses with ideological content in other subjects, and using digital and intelligent technology.

In Mei's account, upholding principles means keeping to Party leadership, Marxism as the guiding ideology, socialist conviction and Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, drawing on traditional, revolutionary and advanced socialist culture. Innovation means moving from rote instruction to student-centred teaching that links theory to current events and to students' majors. Mei proposes building high-quality classes through lively language and varied pacing, and extending learning through rural-revitalisation fieldwork, volunteer teaching and visits to red heritage sites. Teachers should be both scholars of classics and moral exemplars, which the author ties to study of Marxist classics, teaching competitions and professional ethics. On innovation, Mei describes stage-by-stage curricula, model courses with design guidelines, and smart platforms with VR and AR for "precise drip irrigation" of ideas.

Mei concludes that combining steadfastness on direction with innovation in methods will produce a new generation capable of carrying the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation and socialist modernization. The article is a practical, policy-oriented statement rather than a theoretical study. Read the original if you want a concise example of how a university Party official frames current guidance on ideological and political education, including its practical recommendations for classrooms, teachers and technology.
quoteEn: Only by upholding fundamental principles can we avoid losing our way or making subversive mistakes, distinguish right from wrong, and consolidate the foundation for the intension-based development of ideological and political courses.
quoteZh: 只有守正才能不迷失方向、不犯颠覆性错误，才能明辨是非，夯实思政课建设内涵式发展的根基

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses in Chinese schools and universities that teach Marxism, Party theory, history and morality. They are treated as the main channel of ideological education.
Development that relies on internal elements and quality improvement rather than expansion in scale or numbers.
The stated fundamental task of Chinese education, which stresses moral and ideological formation alongside knowledge.
The practice of weaving ideological and political content into non-political courses such as professional and general subjects. It is meant to work in step with dedicated sizheng courses.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng

glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology since 2017, written into the Party and state constitutions. It is the core content of current ideological and political teaching.

t: What the classical dispute over rhetoric and dialectic still teaches us
zh: 古典思想争论的当代启示
source: Chinese Social Sciences Today (中国社会科学报), 19 February 2025
paras: This is a Chinese translation, by Yang Xue, of a speech given by the classicist Michael Trapp at the first World Congress of Classics. Trapp takes up the second-century orations of Aelius Aristides, which answer Plato's critique of rhetoric in the Gorgias. He rejects the common view that these texts are stale pedantry and argues that they remain worth reading.

The talk reviews Aristides' attack on Plato in three parts: his defence of rhetoric against the charge of being non-scientific, his rebuttal of Plato's criticism of four great Athenian statesman-orators, and his portrayal of Plato's school as an aberration in Greek tradition. Trapp then looks at Aristides' own positive account of rhetoric, including his revised Prometheus myth.

Trapp concedes Aristides' exaggeration and uncritical assumption, inherited from Isocrates, that a true orator is virtuous. He nonetheless finds real force in the rebuttal. Plato calls rhetoric mere guesswork (stochastikê), and Aristides answers that aiming is a rational act. He adds that archery, navigation and medicine are genuine crafts despite relying on conjecture. In Trapp's reading, this challenges Plato's rationalism and his sharp opposition of reason and unreason. Trapp also notes that dialectic alone struggles to found a political community: the Republic confines dialectical exchange to an elite and leaves room for deception and coercion.

Trapp declines to name a winner, saying both sides have blind spots, and he does not endorse Aristides' idea that rhetoricians are automatically defenders of civilisation. He concludes that the quarrel keeps alive the question of how we communicate and engage with others, and that classical works supply models of both rhetoric and dialectic and make debate over them necessary. Read the original if you want a short classicist's defence of an ancient anti-Platonic text and its present-day relevance.
quoteEn: Continuing to reflect on ways of communicating, what they mean and how to apply them properly still has real value.
quoteZh: 不断思考交流方式、它们的含义以及如何恰当应用它们，仍具有真正的价值。

t: Taking Xi Jinping Thought on Culture as guidance to strengthen the leading power of ideological and political education
zh: 坚持习近平文化思想为指导提升思政引领力
paras: This short commentary, published in early 2025, takes up the concept of "leading power of ideological and political education" (sizheng yinlingli), which Xi Jinping first put forward at the National Education Conference and presented as the primary feature of a strong education nation with Chinese characteristics. Liu and Sun argue that this capacity must be built by integrating the Party's innovative theory into ideological and political courses, and that Xi Jinping Thought on Culture should serve as the guiding framework.

The authors tie their argument to the Outline Plan for Building a Strong Education Nation (2024–2035) and to the Study Outline of Xi Jinping Thought on Culture, which they say offers systematic guidance. The piece is organised around four tasks: upholding Marxism's guiding position in ideology, advancing the Two Integrations, forging a sense of community for the Chinese nation, and using revolutionary cultural relics in teaching.

On the first two tasks, Liu and Sun hold that Marxism-is-outdated claims and the idea that "modernization means Westernization" still reach young people through the internet. They call for popularising theory, listening to students' difficulties, and explaining Marxism's contemporary explanatory power. They present the "second integration" as having resolved the modern "dispute between ancient and modern, Chinese and Western", and urge building a Chinese independent knowledge system, coordinating textbooks across courses and developing a "great ideological and political education" paradigm. On the third and fourth, they call for refuting mistaken ethnic theories, teaching the course on the Chinese national community well, and making core socialist values part of daily life. They list weaknesses in red-culture practice, including student-centred visits with little teacher guidance, content detached from textbooks, perfunctory tours and museum displays lacking theoretical coherence. Their remedies are a Party-history narrative built around revolutionary relics, a bridging role for teachers, and oral-history methods that turn students into interpreters.

The authors conclude that ideological and political courses address students' ideals and convictions, which rest on cultural values. They describe strengthening this leading power as a task bearing on the Party's long-term rule and national stability, to be pursued persistently. Read the original if you want a compact example of how Party-school educators link Xi Jinping Thought on Culture to concrete teaching reforms in ideological and political courses.
quoteEn: Ideological and political courses must address students' ideals and convictions, and behind those ideals and convictions stands the strong support of cultural values and concepts.
quoteZh: 思政课要解决的是学生的理想信念问题，而理想信念的背后是文化价值理念的强力支撑。

glossary.explanation: A body of ideas on cultural work attributed to Xi Jinping and formally presented in 2023 as part of Xi Jinping Thought. It covers Party leadership of culture, cultural confidence and the integration of Marxism with traditional Chinese culture.

The formula of combining Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities (the first) and with China's fine traditional culture (the second). The second was added in 2021–2023 and is stressed in current Party theory.

glossary.en: leading power of ideological and political education
glossary.explanation: A concept Xi Jinping introduced at the 2024 National Education Conference, referring to the capacity of ideological and political education to guide students' values and orientation.

glossary.en: a sense of community for the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: consciousness of the Chinese national community
glossary.explanation: An official policy concept promoting a shared national identity across China's ethnic groups, emphasised in Party ethnic and education policy since 2014.

t: Upholding and consolidating the Party's cultural leadership from three dimensions
zh: 从三个维度坚持和巩固党的文化领导权
paras: Lin and Zhuang ask how the Communist Party of China can uphold and consolidate its cultural leadership (cultural hegemony) at a time when, in the authors' words, the world is undergoing changes unseen in a century and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation has entered a critical period. They argue that cultural leadership bears on ideological security, cultural security and the realisation of cultural modernisation, and propose three dimensions for strengthening it.

The short commentary treats cultural leadership as a question of a class's or party's discursive power in ideology, not only of culture. It moves through three headings: upholding and strengthening Party leadership, putting the people at the centre, and consolidating the cultural subjectivity of the Chinese nation.

On Party leadership, the authors say it keeps culture on the right course, resists foreign cultural erosion, secures Marxism's guiding position and lets the Party concentrate resources on cultural undertakings. They call for the Two Upholds, stronger strategic planning (citing the 14th Five-Year Plan for cultural development) and firm Party control of propaganda and ideological work. On the people-centred dimension, they hold that Party spirit and the people's character must be unified, and cite the television dramas Minning Town and The Age of Awakening as examples. On cultural subjectivity, they call for adherence to Marxism, creative transformation of traditional culture, socialist core values and an independent Chinese knowledge system.

The authors conclude that these three measures together provide the political, popular and cultural foundations of the Party's cultural leadership in the new era. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how Party-affiliated scholars frame cultural leadership in current ideological education.
quoteEn: Socialist culture with Chinese characteristics is in essence the culture of the people at large, a culture jointly built and shared by the people.
quoteZh: 中国特色社会主义文化本质上是人民大众的文化，是人民共建共享的文化。

glossary.explanation: A Chinese rendering of the Gramscian idea of cultural hegemony, used for the Party's authority over ideology, discourse and culture.
A Party formula, in use since 2018, calling on members to uphold General Secretary Xi Jinping's core position and the Central Committee's authority.
A term stressed by Xi Jinping in 2023 for a nation's distinctive values and cultural character, said to underpin cultural confidence and national identity.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's central national goal, associated with the Chinese Dream, of restoring China's strength and international standing.

t: Starting from "knowing, feeling, willing, acting": guiding university students towards a stronger identification with Chinese civilization
zh: 从“知情意行”入手，引导大学生更好认同中华文明
paras: This short commentary, published in Guangming Daily in February 2025, asks how universities can lead students to recognise and identify with Chinese civilization. Opening with Xi Jinping's call to strengthen young people's "ambition, backbone and confidence" as Chinese, the authors argue that education should follow the laws of students' thinking and of teaching, and work through four links: knowing, feeling, willing and acting.

The text takes each link in turn and gives two practical measures for each. Knowledge is addressed through courses and academic events; emotion through campus culture and festivals; will through role models and online outreach; action through cultural social practice and cultural entrepreneurship.

The authors treat identification as a progression from cognition to commitment. They propose integrating civilization education into the curriculum, with lectures, debates and expert dialogues, so that students understand its origins and contribution to human civilization. They suggest campus sculptures, murals and traditional festivals, opera and dance as ways of building emotional resonance. To build will, they call for carefully chosen exemplars, new-media content and AI-based monitoring of online opinion to help students resist harmful online culture. Finally, they propose site visits, intangible heritage work, craft learning and creative products as practice.

The authors conclude that this approach will lead students to take up responsibility for promoting excellent traditional Chinese culture and building a modern Chinese civilization, in service of the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want a concise example of how university leaders frame civilization education and ideological work with students.
quoteEn: We must follow the laws of students' cognition and of education and teaching, attend to key links such as knowing, feeling, willing and acting, and guide university students to identify more fully with Chinese civilization.
quoteZh: 要遵循学生思想认知规律和教育教学规律，抓好“知、情、意、行”等关键环节，教育引导大学生更好认同中华文明

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central goal of Chinese Communist Party discourse, associated especially with Xi Jinping's Chinese Dream, meaning national revival in strength and prosperity.
A framework from Chinese moral and ideological education describing four stages in forming belief and conduct: cognition, emotion, will and practice.

t: New trends in the evolution of international political thought
zh: 国际政治思潮演变新趋势
paras: Writing in a Party newspaper in February 2025, Liu Endong asks how international political currents are changing amid what the article calls "changes unseen in a century". Liu's thesis is that traditional Western mainstream currents are declining while new ones rise and intermingle, and that the direction of any current ultimately depends on its contribution to the interests of humanity as a whole.

The commentary surveys eight developments in turn. These are the decline of neoliberalism and conservatism; the retreat of "universal values"; the spread of anti-globalisation together with the return of statism; democratic socialism at the margins; the growing influence of ecologism; the rise of debate on technology and its ethics; the flourishing of currents that look to common human interests; and the stronger interaction among currents.

On the first group, Liu points to the 2008 financial crisis, Trumpism, Brexit and the Ukraine crisis as eroding the neoliberal consensus. Liu cites National Security Adviser Jake Sullivan's April 2023 Brookings speech, which called for a "new Washington consensus", as a sign that neoliberalism faces a fundamental crisis. Liu argues that anti-globalisation, which now carries elements of containment and bullying, is closely tied to a return of statism, and that governments may come to see its unsustainability. In the final sections, Liu holds that extreme and confrontational currents such as colonialism, militarism and fascism have largely left the stage, while hegemonism has limited and increasingly resisted influence. Liu names China's proposals as currents of the opposite kind: a community with a shared future for mankind, the Belt and Road Initiative, and the global development, security and civilisation initiatives. Liu says these are gaining acceptance worldwide. Liu also warns that ecologism, nationalism, populism, racism and statism are merging in ways that deepen polarisation and unsettle the international order.

Liu concludes that currents attending to the interests of humanity as a whole will win growing support, while narrow and confrontational ones will fade. The piece is a short overview from the Party School's perspective rather than a detailed empirical study. Read the original if you want a concise sample of how a Central Party School scholar maps global ideological trends and presents Chinese initiatives as a counter-current to Western thought.
quoteEn: Overall, the development trend of international political currents depends on their contribution to the interests of humanity as a whole.
quoteZh: 总体来看，国际政治思潮的发展趋势，取决于其对人类整体利益的贡献。

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept promoted by Xi Jinping since around 2012–13. It calls for shared interests and joint governance in international relations.
A Chinese infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative launched in 2013, linking China with countries across Eurasia, Africa and beyond.

glossary.literal: great changes not seen in a hundred years
glossary.explanation: A phrase used in Chinese official discourse to describe a period of major shifts in the global balance of power and the international order.

t: The functions of Marxist classics in integrating ideological and political education into courses
zh: 马克思主义经典著作的课程思政功能
paras: This short commentary, published in Guangming Daily in February 2025, asks how the Marxist classics can serve "ideological and political education in the curriculum" at universities. Zhou Xiaomao argues that the classics contain rich material for guiding students towards truth, firm belief and healthy growth, and should be mined in depth so that specialist courses and ideological-political teaching complement each other.

The article opens with Xi Jinping's remark that the most effective way to study theory is to read the original works. It then sets out five functions of the classics: educational, cognitive, discriminating, identification-building and cohesive.

On the educational function, Zhou points to Marx's The Civil War in France and its account of the Paris Commune's heroism, which the author says can still inspire students to work for communism. The cognitive function lies in the dialectical and historical materialist worldview, which Zhou treats as the "master switch" for students at a formative stage. The discriminating function rests on polemical works: Critique of the Gotha Programme, Anti-Dühring, What Is To Be Done? and Materialism and Empirio-Criticism, which Zhou says help students tell genuine from false Marxism. The identification function aims at political, intellectual and emotional identification with the Party's guiding theories, which Zhou sees as harder to achieve amid social transformation and diversifying values.

On the cohesive function, Zhou says the classics treat the individual as a social being, criticise individualism and uphold a society-centred value orientation. The author concludes that this helps align personal ideals with social ones and cultivates a new generation able to carry the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Chinese academics justify using Marxist classics in university ideological-political teaching.
quoteEn: The Marxist classics contain rich nourishment for guiding students to pursue truth, hold firm beliefs, temper their will and grow in a healthy way, and are vivid teaching material for ideological and political education in the curriculum.
quoteZh: 马克思主义经典著作中蕴含着引领学生追求真理、坚定信仰，磨炼意志、健康成长的丰富养料，是开展课程思政的生动教材。

glossary.en: ideological and political education in the curriculum
glossary.explanation: A policy approach promoted in Chinese higher education since the mid-2010s, which embeds ideological and moral-political content in all courses, not only dedicated political-theory classes.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: An official goal of national revival, closely associated with Xi Jinping and the Chinese Dream, usually dated to a target of 2049.

t: Popularising the Party's innovative theory in the new era: communication practice and future paths
zh: 新时代党的创新理论大众化的传播实践与未来进路
paras: This short commentary, published on Guangming Net in February 2025, asks how the Party's innovative theory can be made accessible to ordinary people in the internet age. Zhang Sen starts from Xi Jinping's instruction that Marxism must be spread in popular, plain language rather than by reciting texts. Zhang argues that the core of popularisation is the "masses", which means keeping to the people's standpoint so that theory reaches ordinary households.

The piece notes that 2024 marked thirty years since China's full connection to the global internet. It treats the internet as more than a new channel: in Zhang's account it is a "high-dimensional medium" that has changed how people receive information, connect with one another and form values. For this reason Zhang calls it the main front of propaganda, public opinion work and ideological struggle.

Zhang proposes a "combination of punches" built on three principles. Interactive communication replaces the one-way sender–audience model with comments, likes, shares and Q&A, so that audiences take part and come to accept the theory. Targeted communication uses data profiling to tailor content to different groups, for example young people who resist preaching and should be addressed in everyday, humorous and emotionally engaging language. Immersive communication uses VR, holographic imaging, 3D projection and interactive design to build situations in which ideas are absorbed gradually.

Zhang concludes that, whatever the format, "content is king" still holds. Because the theory comes from and serves the people, content must stay close to their most immediate interests and keep a strong problem-orientation, so that the theory shows its force by answering real concerns. Read the original if you want a brief example of how Chinese communication scholars link internet media features to the dissemination of Party theory.
quoteEn: However much the forms of communication change and the communication landscape shifts, the iron rule that "content is king" will not change.
quoteZh: 不论传播形态如何改变、传播格局如何转换，“内容为王”的铁律不会变。

glossary.explanation: An official term for the Party's latest theoretical achievements, in the new era chiefly Xi Jinping Thought and related theory. It is promoted through study and propaganda campaigns.
The effort to make Marxist and Party theory understandable and acceptable to ordinary people, often by using plain, familiar language. It is a long-standing theme in Chinese Marxist discourse.
Official term for the contest over ideas and public opinion, which Party documents say includes the internet as a major arena.

t: The value implications of building a socialist cultural powerhouse
zh: 建设社会主义文化强国的价值意蕴
paras: This commentary, published in Guangming Daily in February 2025, asks what is at stake in building a socialist cultural powerhouse, the cultural goal set out in the decision of the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024). Qin Xuan argues that implementing the plan requires first grasping its value implications. In Qin's view, these can be understood along five dimensions: the state, the nation, the Party, the individual and humanity.

The article is a short, programmatic piece organised under five numbered headings. It draws on speeches by Xi Jinping, Mao Zedong's 1940 essay On New Democracy, Deng Xiaoping's remarks at the start of reform and opening up, and Party congress documents from 2012 to 2024. It also cites Karl Jaspers, Qian Mu, Liang Qichao, and the Toynbee–Ikeda dialogue.

On the state dimension, Qin reads Chinese modernization as coordinating material and spiritual civilization, so that culture is a necessary component of a modernized socialist country. Culture is described as running through economic, political, social and ecological development and as a pivot for high-quality development. On the national dimension, the author holds that the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation is also a cultural revival. Qin stresses that this revival is not a return to the past but a creative transformation of traditional culture under Marxism, through the Two Integrations. On the Party dimension, Qin traces the Party's cultural goals from Mao and Deng to the 18th Party Congress (2012) and later documents, calling cultural strength a historic task for a long-governing Marxist party.

The individual dimension holds that, as the principal contradiction has shifted, people's demand for richer spiritual and cultural life grows with material prosperity. The humanity dimension treats culture as a response to a world of ideological competition and talk of a "clash of civilizations". Qin argues that Chinese modernization offers "Eastern wisdom" and a Chinese approach to civilizational progress. Qin concludes that stronger cultural soft power would let China play a leading role in mutual learning among civilizations and advance a community with a shared future for mankind. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how Party theorists justify the cultural powerhouse goal across five levels of argument.
quoteEn: The great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation is also a revival of culture and a revival of civilization.
quoteZh: 中华民族的伟大复兴，也是文化的复兴、文明的复兴。

glossary.explanation: The Party's official term for China's own path of modernization, introduced prominently at the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is described as socialist, led by the Party, and coordinating material and spiritual civilization.
Formula for combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture. The second integration was added in Xi Jinping's 2021–23 discourse.
An official goal, set out at the 18th Party Congress (2012) and given a 2035 target date in 2020, of building a country with strong cultural influence and soft power.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's formula for China's vision of international relations and global governance, stressing shared interests and cooperation among states.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: Core official goal of the Party, linked to the Chinese Dream, of restoring China's national strength and international standing by the mid-twenty-first century.
Official term for an economic approach prioritising quality, innovation and sustainability over speed of growth, prominent since the 19th Party Congress (2017).

t: Marxist research as the foundational project of ideological and theoretical construction
zh: 马克思主义研究是思想理论建设的基础工程
paras: This newspaper commentary (Chinese Social Sciences Today, 12 February 2025) takes up Xi Jinping's statement that the Marxist Theory Research and Construction Project is the "foundational" and "strategic" project of the Party's ideological and theoretical work. Gao argues that Marxist research is the basic task of that work, because political firmness depends on theoretical firmness.

The piece moves from the status of theory in Party documents to the project's mission and then to its current tasks. It touches on Marx's view of human development, the study of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, cultural subjectivity, ideological and political education as a discipline, and the building of an autonomous knowledge system.

Gao contends that Marxism still holds the high ground of truth and morality, and that the depth of one's grasp of theory determines political sensitivity and intellectual horizon. In the context of the "great changes unseen in a century" and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, Gao says theory must keep Marxism as its "soul" and fine traditional Chinese culture as its "root", since competition between major powers is at bottom a contest of values. The author holds that the Party's new ideas need scholarly interpretation and systematic construction, and that autonomy does not mean isolation but a synthesis of past, foreign and future resources.

Gao concludes that the project should turn Chinese experience into Chinese theory through the Two Integrations, and so build an autonomous knowledge system and philosophy and social sciences with Chinese characteristics. The author calls the project the core force of this unprecedented undertaking. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated scholars link Marxist theory research to cultural confidence and the autonomous knowledge system.
quoteEn: The autonomy we stress does not mean isolation or self-enclosure, but the arduous work of intellectual creation that synthesises remembering one's origins, absorbing what is foreign and looking to the future.
quoteZh: 我们强调的自主性并不是指孤立的隔绝的自我封闭，而是不忘本来、吸收外来、面向未来进行综汇的艰巨的思想创造。

t: Systematically grasping the value connotations of building a strong education country
zh: 系统把握建设教育强国的价值内涵
paras: Sun Xiuling's commentary in Guangming Daily (February 2025) interprets the Outline for Building a Strong Education Country (2024–2035), recently issued by the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China and the State Council. The author argues that implementing the Outline requires systems thinking and a firm grasp of the value connotations of building a strong education country with Chinese characteristics, so that education can play its leading, foundational and strategic supporting role in national rejuvenation.

The piece is organised under four headings: upholding the Party's overall leadership of education, upholding the fundamental task of fostering virtue through education, serving the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, and running education that satisfies the people. Each section links the Outline's provisions to concrete tasks.

Sun treats Party leadership as the core guarantee, calling for stronger organisational systems and Party building in the education sector. On moral education, the author calls for Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era to run through ideological and political education and for a stronger teaching force with strict standards of professional ethics. On national service, Sun calls for aligning higher education with national strategic needs, building an independent Chinese knowledge system, linking universities with industry to support new quality productive forces, and expanding international exchange.

Sun concludes that education for the people should stress equity, balanced compulsory education, lifelong learning, graduate employment, all-round development and digital education, with the Outline's targets set for 2027 and 2035. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned reading of how the Outline's priorities are framed for Chinese universities and schools.
quoteEn: Upholding the Party's overall leadership of education occupies the core position in building a strong education country with Chinese characteristics, and provides the fundamental guarantee for that effort.
quoteZh: 坚持党对教育事业的全面领导在建设中国特色社会主义教育强国中居于核心地位，为教育强国建设提供根本保证。

t: Building a new pattern of fostering virtue through education and cultivating new-era talents who can shoulder major responsibilities
zh: 构建立德树人新格局 培养堪当重任的时代新人
paras: This commentary, published in Guangming Daily in February 2025, responds to the Central Committee and State Council's Outline Plan for Building a Leading Education Country (2024–2035). Li Zhongjun argues that building a leading education country is a systems project. It should be organised around the questions of whom to train, how to train them and for whom, and driven by a new pattern of fostering virtue through education (lide shuren).

The piece is organised under three headings: using the Party's innovative theory to forge the soul and educate people; strengthening and improving ideological and political education in schools; and improving an all-round training system covering moral, intellectual, physical, aesthetic and labour education.

Li's first point is that Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era should be systematised and explained in academic terms, and carried into textbooks and teaching, especially the introductory course on that thought. Second, ideological and political theory courses should be developed in content, integrated across primary, secondary and university levels, and extended through practice-based education and a teaching force shaped by the spirit of educators. Third, Li places moral education first, calls for closing the gaps in physical and aesthetic education, and wants labour education tied to new quality productive forces and the new development philosophy.

Li concludes that this pattern is meant to produce new-era talents who are reliable for the Party, patriotic and ready to carry the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want a concise, official-style account of how a university Party leader translates the 2025 education plan into priorities for ideological and political education.
quoteEn: Ideological and political education is the lifeline of all work in schools.
quoteZh: 思想政治教育是学校各项工作的生命线。

glossary.explanation: A long-standing Confucian-derived phrase adopted as the 'fundamental task' of education in Party documents since the 18th Party Congress (2012). It stresses moral and political formation alongside knowledge.
A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2023, referring to productivity driven by technological innovation and emerging industries.

t: The essential meaning of making political supervision concrete, precise and routine
zh: 政治监督具体化精准化常态化的精髓要义
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in February 2025, Bai Xianliang takes up the Party's call to make political supervision concrete (具体化), precise (精准化) and routine (常态化). The author argues that these three requirements, stressed by Xi Jinping and at the second, third and fourth plenary sessions of the 20th Central Commission for Discipline Inspection, must be understood in their meaning and as a unified whole. Their purpose, in Bai's reading, is to uphold the authority and centralised, unified leadership of the Party Central Committee.

The short commentary has three parts. The first defines each requirement. The second sets out how to put them into practice at the levels of ideas, politics and action. The third looks at the three as an organic whole.

In Bai's definitions, concreteness means supervision must reach specific matters and work rather than stop at slogans and mobilisation. Precision means analysing each target specifically, for example by focusing on top leaders and leadership teams with a tailored approach to each. Routine means regular, institutionalised supervision, combining Party discipline organs with popular and democratic oversight, and daily with special-purpose supervision. In practice, Bai calls for study of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, strict political discipline built around the Two Upholds, and a rule of judging officials by deeds as well as words. Bai holds that the three requirements form a dialectical sequence: concreteness is the precondition for precision, precision for routine, and routine fixes both in institutions.

Bai concludes that supervision should have one aim, upholding the Central Committee's authority and the Two Establishes and Two Upholds. It should also have one foundation, the tasks of Chinese modernization and high-quality development, and it should be advanced as one whole. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how the Party's official discourse frames the logic and priorities of political supervision in 2025.
quoteEn: Concreteness is the precondition for precision and routinisation; if it is not achieved and supervision stays abstract and general, there can be no talk of precision or routinisation.
quoteZh: 具体化是精准化、常态化的前提，没有实现具体化，而是停留于抽象化和泛泛而论，是谈不上精准化和常态化的。

glossary.explanation: Party oversight of whether Party organisations and officials implement the Central Committee's decisions and observe political discipline. It is distinct from supervision of legal or financial compliance.
The Party's formula of upholding Xi Jinping's core position on the Central Committee and the whole Party, and upholding the Central Committee's authority and centralised, unified leadership.
A formula adopted in 2021–22 affirming Xi Jinping's core position in the Party and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought.

glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng

glossary.explanation: The Party's current official guiding ideology, written into the Party constitution in 2017.
The official term for China's path of modernization, presented by the Party as distinct from Western models.

t: Nourishing the core socialist values with excellent traditional Chinese culture
zh: 以中华优秀传统文化涵养社会主义核心价值观
paras: This commentary, published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in February 2025, asks how excellent traditional Chinese culture can nourish the core socialist values. Li Nan argues that traditional culture is the root of those values. In Li's account, its moral ideas, humanistic spirit and ideas of moral education give the values a cultural foundation and drive, and help them guide social norms and unify popular belief.

The piece has three parts. The first sets out the core requirements and the mission of the task: implementing Xi Jinping's thought on culture, serving Chinese modernization, and building a spiritual highland for the Chinese nation. The second looks at the meaning and value position of the link, through three pairings of traditional ideals and contemporary concepts. The third proposes practical paths.

The central move is to pair traditional concepts with Marxist and Party-theoretical ones. Li reads "when the great Way prevails" and "all under heaven is shared by all" as converging with the communist ideal of ending exploitation and class differences and achieving common prosperity. "Seeking truth from facts" is read as a dialectical-materialist epistemology consistent with the Two Integrations. The traditional outlook of "having the world in one's heart" is presented as an ideological basis for a community with a shared future for mankind. Li argues that holding to the communist ideal thereby achieves the modern transformation and innovative development of traditional culture.

On practice, Li calls for three things. The first is upholding Marxism's guiding position in the ideological sphere, through study of Marxist principles, integration of tradition with the values, firmer control of ideological positions, and arming the whole Party with Xi Jinping's thought on culture. The second is to carry out the Two Integrations by judging the timing, degree and effect of the "two creations" (creative transformation and innovative development). The third is to improve institutional mechanisms for fostering the values, combining law, education and culture, so that they become a lasting source of spiritual strength for Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official commentary on ideological and political education links traditional culture, the core socialist values and Xi Jinping's thought on culture.
quoteEn: \"Seeking truth from facts\" is not only a concrete expression of the Chinese nation's distinctive way of thinking and of the inner logic of contemporary China's development, but also a profound insight into the fundamental method by which humanity understands and transforms the world.
quoteZh: “实事求是”不仅是中华民族独特的思维方式与当代中国发展的内在逻辑的具体体现，更是对人类认识世界、改造世界的根本方法的深刻洞察。

glossary.explanation: A set of 24 characters in twelve values, promoted since the 18th Party Congress (2012). They operate at the national, social and individual levels.

Xi Jinping's formula, developed from 2021 and 2023, for combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's fine traditional culture. It sits alongside the earlier integration of Marxism with Chinese revolutionary and construction practice.
The official term for China's own path of modernization, set out by the Party since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.
The part of Xi's body of thought that deals with cultural work, formally put forward in October 2023. It covers ideology, cultural confidence and the cultural dimension of national rejuvenation.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept of international relations built on cooperation and shared interests. It is central to China's official foreign-policy discourse.
A goal of socialism in official discourse, stressing shared wealth for all. It has been emphasised in Party policy since the early 2020s.

t: Using Xi Jinping's Fujian experience to build a "grand ideological and political course"
st: Drawing on Fujian's distinctive strengths in teaching young students
zh: 发挥独特优势，善用习近平总书记在福建的探索实践成果建设“大思政课”
source: China Theory Net (中国理论网), February 2025
paras: This commentary, published on China Theory Net in February 2025, asks how the exploratory practice of General Secretary Xi Jinping during his years of work in Fujian can be used in the "grand ideological and political course" (da sizheng ke) for young students. Sun Qiaozhen argues that Fujian is an important place where Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era was nurtured and put into practice, and that telling these stories well helps students follow the leader's path and grasp the formation of the Thought.

The article is organised in five parts, each presenting one aspect of Xi's Fujian record and then drawing a lesson for students. These are his style of leadership, his working style, his methods of thinking, his sincere devotion to the people, and his concrete practical achievements. Each part moves from Xi's work in Xiamen, Ningde and Fuzhou to what Sun describes as the continuation of the same qualities after the 18th Party Congress (2012).

In Sun's account, Fujian examples show foresight, openness and innovation: lifting Ningde out of poverty, the Fuzhou "3820" strategic project, the Xiamen free-port-type special zone, and later the Belt and Road Initiative. They also show a pragmatic style of fieldwork, such as visiting all nine counties and cities of Ningde, and a systematic, dialectical way of thinking, including the idea that a "weak bird can fly first". Sun adds Xi's declared commitment to serve the people, the "Four Ten-Thousand Households" approach, and achievements such as "Digital Fujian", the ecological province concept and collective forest tenure reform.

Sun concludes that these results show a great leader's growth and give students material for sensing the power of the Thought. Students are urged to adopt Xi as a model: to link personal prospects with the nation's fate, practise investigation and perseverance, master scientific thinking methods, stand with the people, and contribute to the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want to see how Fujian-based material is framed for Party-led ideological and political education of university students.
quoteEn: General Secretary Xi Jinping's exploration and practice in Fujian vividly reflect the growth of a leader of a major country, open a window for young students to understand the leader's bearing, lay a path for them to follow his footsteps, and provide vivid material for them to appreciate the power of his thought.
quoteZh: 习近平总书记在福建的探索实践成果生动反映了大国领袖的成长历程，打开了广大青年学生了解领袖风范的窗口，铺设了广大青年学生追寻领袖足迹的道路，为青年学生感悟思想伟力提供了生动素材。

glossary.explanation: The Communist Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017 and 2018. It is presented officially as the latest stage in adapting Marxism to China.
An official education concept that extends ideological and political teaching beyond classrooms into society and practice. It was promoted by the Chinese education authorities from around 2021.
A foreign-policy and infrastructure initiative launched by Xi Jinping in 2013 to build trade and investment links across Eurasia, Africa and beyond.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A long-term national goal in official discourse, associated with the Chinese Dream and with achieving a modernised, strong China by the middle of the twenty-first century.

t: Ideological and political courses told in four narratives: teaching comprehensively deepening reform in depth, thoroughly and vividly
zh: 四重叙事的思政课：讲深讲透讲活全面深化改革
paras: This commentary, published in Guangming Daily in February 2025, asks how university ideological and political courses can teach the policy of comprehensively deepening reform more effectively. Liu Xingyun proposes the narrative teaching method, which the author describes as combining knowledge, emotion, will and action, and which is said to work through lived situations, carried meaning and multi-way interaction. The thesis is that teachers should use four kinds of narrative (image, emotion, history and innovation) to tell the reform story in depth, thoroughly and vividly, and so raise the practical effect of moulding students' ideals and character.

The piece has four numbered sections, one for each narrative. Image narrative covers the achievements of reform and opening up; emotional narrative covers the great spirit of reform and opening up; historical narrative covers the basic laws of comprehensively deepening reform; and innovation narrative covers the blueprint for further reform. Each section gives concrete classroom suggestions, drawing on the decision adopted at the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) and on remarks by Xi Jinping.

On image narrative, Liu urges using charts, paintings, documentaries, films and generative-AI animations so that reform results show "principle in the picture", beauty and moral character. For emotional narrative, the author draws on Xi's call for teachers to have feelings for family and country, for transmitting the Way, and for benevolence. Liu proposes telling stories of reformers, using role-play, and turning the reform spirit into both moral qualities and action. For historical narrative, the author asks teachers to adopt developmental, systemic and dialectical thinking: comparing reforms across history, linking course content in Marxist principles and Chinese modern history, and explaining both achievements and unresolved problems. For innovation narrative, Liu recommends telling stories of scientific teams, adopting the online and humorous speech style of young people, and using VR, AR and XR.

Liu concludes that these four narratives together can build an approach to education that moves from knowledge to practice and from emotion to deeper commitment. The author expects this to strengthen students' identification with reform, their confidence in theory, and their patriotism and innovative spirit. Read the original if you want a concrete example of how Chinese university teachers are being advised to turn Party policy on reform into classroom practice.
quoteEn: To teach the great spirit of reform and opening up in depth, thoroughly and vividly, one must carefully select reform stories that are moving and attractive, and tell vividly the world-renowned achievements of China's forty-odd years of reform and opening up, so as to arouse strong emotional resonance.
quoteZh: 讲深讲透讲活伟大改革开放精神，要精心遴选具有感染力与吸引力的改革故事，形象讲述中国改革开放40多年取得的举世瞩目成就，激发强烈的情感共鸣。

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses in Marxist theory, Party thought and modern Chinese history taught at Chinese schools and universities. They are meant to build students' political and moral outlook.
A phrase from Chinese educational policy naming moral cultivation as the fundamental task of education. It is used here for the aim of the ideological and political courses.

The Party's reform programme, launched at the Third Plenum of the 18th Central Committee in 2013, covering the economy, politics, culture, society and ecology. The Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) set out its latest phase.

glossary.en: the great spirit of reform and opening up
glossary.explanation: An official formulation for the values attributed to the reform era, such as daring to innovate, pragmatism and a sense of responsibility. It is used in Party education.

t: Deepening national defence education for all in the new era and gathering positive energy for loving the country and strengthening the military
zh: 深化新时代全民国防教育 汇聚爱国强军正能量
paras: Writing in the People's Daily on 6 February 2025, Lu Xiaoqing, head of the Jiangxi Provincial Party Committee's Publicity Department, asks how the province should put the newly revised National Defence Education Law into practice. The law was adopted by the Standing Committee of the 14th National People's Congress. Lu starts from Xi Jinping's statements that national defence belongs to the whole people and that education in it is a foundation for a strong defence and army. The article argues that Jiangxi should use its revolutionary heritage to apply the law and "gather positive energy" for loving the country and strengthening the military.

This is a short commentary by a provincial official, organised under three headings. The first covers a multi-level education system; the second, wider channels and vehicles for education; the third, a work structure with institutional guarantees. Each section opens by citing what the revised law now requires, then lists measures for Jiangxi, with references to local programmes, planning documents and sites.

On the education system, Lu calls for targeting three groups. These are leading cadres, who would be trained through Party study groups, Party schools and a graded training system that extends to state-enterprise executives, school principals and media heads. Young people, the group Lu calls the top priority, would be reached through the "big ideological and political course" reform, model defence schools, "red study tours" and military-skills experiences. The whole population would be reached through legal publicity and the integration of defence education into cultural and civilised-practice activities. On channels, Lu proposes telling defence stories through converged media, new films and television series and model figures. Lu also proposes immersive digital exhibitions at the province's roughly 2,900 revolutionary sites, and a red-heritage brand built on research into the Jinggangshan and Soviet-area spirit.

On organisation, Lu stresses Party leadership. Under the revised law, defence education duties formerly shared among the military and local governments are unified under the Party Central Committee and local Party committees. Lu proposes revising the Jiangxi Defence Education Regulations, strengthening military–civilian coordination through joint meetings and open-barracks events, and building an expert pool. Lu also proposes budget lines and donations for funding, and putting defence education into the 15th Five-Year Plan, performance assessments and ideological inspections. Lu's stated aim is for caring about, loving, building and defending national defence to become a common social practice in Jiangxi. Read the original if you want a worked example of how a provincial Party leader turns a national law on defence education into concrete local measures and institutional targets.
quoteEn: Mobilising the whole people and covering every domain is the most effective form of national defence education.
quoteZh: 全民动员、全域覆盖是最有效的国防教育。

glossary.explanation: A policy concept promoted since 2021 that extends ideological and political education beyond the classroom into society and practice. Jiangxi is described in the article as a pilot reform zone.
The national and provincial economic and social development plan for 2026–2030. The article proposes that defence education be written into it.

t: Telling the story of the Chinese national community to the world
zh: 对外讲好中华民族共同体故事
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 24 January 2025
paras: Li Tao takes up how China should communicate abroad the idea of forging a sense of community for the Chinese nation, which the Party since the 18th Party Congress (2012) has made the main thread of ethnic work. Li argues that some Western states and media use the language of human rights to weaken the cohesion of this community, and that China must build an external discourse system to answer what the author calls Western media's "discourse hegemony" on ethnic issues.

This short commentary has two parts. The first sets out three dimensions of external discourse: Chinese civilization, the Chinese political system, and human development. The second proposes practical routes: diversifying communicators, selecting discourse texts, and technological change.

On the three dimensions, Li calls for stories of exchanges and integration among peoples, from Zhao Wuling's adoption of nomad dress to Emperor Xiaowen's reforms of the Northern Wei. Li also calls for stories of ethnic unity and progress under China's institutions, to escape the "Western-centrism" trap, and for promoting a community with a shared future for mankind in terms foreign audiences can accept. On practice, Li finds that communication now relies mainly on official actors using declaratory, policy and combative language, which lacks warmth and depth. The author urges a larger role for civil and academic voices, agenda-setting on human rights instead of merely appealing to facts, and a shift from "borrowing a boat" to "building a boat" through Chinese-owned international platforms.

Li concludes that these measures would raise the effectiveness of external communication and help build a fairer global communication order. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Chinese ideological-education writing frames international communication on ethnic issues.
quoteEn: Through technological empowerment and overtaking on the curve, a powerful international opinion arena for the external communication of the sense of community of the Chinese nation can be built, promoting a fair and rational new global communication order and strengthening the effectiveness of that communication.
quoteZh: 通过技术赋能与弯道超车，切实构建起中华民族共同体意识对外传播的强大国际舆论场，从而推动建立公正合理的全球传播新秩序，增强中华民族共同体意识的对外传播效能。

glossary.zh: 铸牢中华民族共同体意识
glossary.en: forging a sense of community for the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: firmly forging the consciousness of the Chinese national community
