glossary.explanation: A formula made the main thread of the Party's ethnic work since the 18th Party Congress (2012). It stresses a shared national identity across China's ethnic groups.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A concept associated with Xi Jinping that presents China's approach to global governance and international relations as based on shared interests and cooperation.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: Accelerating the construction of a financial system for Chinese modernization
zh: 加快构建中国式现代化金融体系
paras: Chen argues that building a financial system suited to Chinese modernization is both the direction of China's financial development and a new requirement for finance to support the drive to build a strong country. Writing in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in January 2025, the author notes persistent problems: low quality and efficiency in serving the real economy, financial risks, weak regulation and governance, and a low level of financial opening.

The commentary sets out seven main areas of effort. These are Party leadership of financial work, legislation, regulatory reform, the supply of finance to the real economy, modern institutions and markets, institutional opening, and inclusive finance.

Chen presents Party leadership as the essential requirement, tracing it from the 1998 Party notice to the creation of the Central Financial Commission and Central Financial Work Commission in 2023. The author treats financial security as part of national security and says it depends on handling the dialectic between credit, leverage and risk. Serving the real economy is called the fundamental purpose, with more resources for infrastructure, advanced technology, strategic emerging industries and rural revitalisation. Chen contrasts Western finance, said to pursue self-expansion and profit maximisation, with a Chinese finance whose basis is serving the people.

Chen concludes that, as China now has the world's largest banking system, credit market and foreign-exchange reserves, a financial system of this kind is inevitable. The author also calls for moving from opening in capital and goods to opening in rules and standards, and for advancing renminbi internationalisation. Read the original if you want a concise statement of the policy priorities that Party-affiliated scholars link to Chinese modernization in finance.
quoteEn: Serving the real economy is the fundamental purpose of building a financial system for Chinese modernization, and its basic function and main task.
quoteZh: 服务实体经济是构建中国式现代化金融体系的根本宗旨，是中国式现代化金融体系的基本功能和主要任务。

glossary.explanation: The official Party concept of China's own path to modernization, which the leadership has stressed since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
A Party body set up in 2023 to provide centralised leadership over financial work, alongside the Central Financial Work Commission.
Opening up by aligning rules, regulations, management and standards with international practice, as distinct from opening in goods and capital flows.
Financial services aimed at widening access for ordinary people, small firms and rural areas.
A national strategy launched in 2017 to promote economic and social development in the countryside.

t: Making better use of the educational function of museums
zh: 更好发挥博物馆的教育功能
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in January 2025, Wang Xiaowen, director of the Liaoning Provincial Museum, asks how museums can better perform their educational function and meet the public's spiritual and cultural needs. The commentary takes its cue from Xi Jinping's call to strengthen museum building and to make full use of museums' educational role, and from the Party's goal of building a culturally strong country. Wang argues that education is a core mission of museums and that it should be advanced by upholding fundamental principles while innovating.

The piece opens with figures the author cites for 2023: 6,833 museums in China, more than 40,000 exhibitions, more than 380,000 educational activities and 1.29 billion visits. It has three parts. The first sets out why education is central to museums. The second reviews results achieved, through policy documents since the 2008 free-admission notice and through three practices: study tours, museum–school cooperation and technology-enabled experiences. The third offers four directions for the future.

In Wang's reading, museums teach through objects rather than texts, support self-directed and lifelong learning, and help turn fine traditional Chinese culture into forms the public can understand and identify with. The author illustrates this with examples: the Hebei Museum's study-tour programme, the Nanjing Museum's summer courses, Liaoning's cooperation with Shenyang education authorities on a 'museum–school–family–society' education community, and digital projects such as the Digital Library Cave and Dunhuang immersive exhibitions. Wang then argues that future work should be rooted in fine traditional Chinese culture and a people-centred approach, with digital tools used to match content to audience needs. The author also calls for wider partnerships with schools, research bodies and regions, for staff who understand both museums and education, and for digital transformation.

Wang concludes that museums should cultivate patriotism, public morality and 'new people of the era', build on socialist core values, and deliver inclusive, high-quality education both on site and online. The text is a short practitioner's commentary rather than a theoretical study, and it mainly reflects how a museum director frames the sector's tasks under current cultural policy. Read the original if you want a concise account of official priorities for museum education in China, together with examples from Chinese museums.
quoteEn: To bring the educational function of museums into play, we must put the people at the centre and take fine traditional Chinese culture as fertile soil, deepening feelings for family and country, lifting the national spirit and gathering China's strength, so that culture can shape and educate people.
quoteZh: 发挥博物馆教育功能，要坚持以人民为中心，以中华优秀传统文化为沃土，厚植家国情怀、振奋民族精神、凝聚中国力量，实现以文化人、以文育人的重要作用。

glossary.explanation: A strategic goal in Party documents, stressed by Xi Jinping in October 2024, of building China's cultural capacity and influence by around 2035.
A set of 24 characters of values promoted by the Party since the 18th Party Congress (2012), covering the national, social and individual levels.
The official term for the parts of China's traditional culture that the Party regards as worth inheriting and creatively developing.
Organised educational trips or courses combining travel with inquiry-based learning, widely promoted for young people in China.

t: Bringing the promotion of the educator's spirit into the international communication discourse system
zh: 将弘扬教育家精神纳入国际传播话语体系
paras: This short commentary, published in Guangming Daily in January 2025, takes up the call of the 2024 National Education Conference to raise the international influence and discourse power of Chinese education. Song argues that the distinctively Chinese 'educator's spirit' should be built into international communication, so that Chinese education stories and the stories of Chinese educators are told abroad.

The piece has three parts. It first explains why the educator's spirit matters for international communication, then discusses how to distil its content for foreign audiences, and finally sets out strategies for telling the stories systematically and continuously.

Song contends that education can act as a shared global language and that, according to 2024 data cited in the article, China's soft power index ranked third worldwide. Foreign interest in how China builds its teaching force is therefore expected. On content, the author proposes improving the system of honours for teachers, planning communication around positive messaging with comparison and borrowing, and sorting educators into types. Song draws these types from foreign educators who influenced China (Dewey, Sukhomlinsky, Rewi Alley). On strategy, the article stresses shaping an overall national education image, tailoring messages to audience age groups, and using foreign social platforms.

Song also calls for expanding both 'going out' and 'bringing in' in education: the Belt and Road Initiative education action, educational aid, Luban Workshops, study-in-China programmes and joint schools. The stated aim is to turn institutional, organisational, human, developmental and cultural advantages into communication advantages, supporting a strong education nation and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Chinese education authorities frame international communication and discourse power.
quoteEn: Bringing the promotion of the educator's spirit into the international communication discourse system, and telling good stories of Chinese education and Chinese educators, is a powerful measure for accelerating the building of a strong education nation and advancing the international communication of education.
quoteZh: 将弘扬教育家精神纳入国际传播话语体系，讲好中国教育故事、中国教育家故事，是我国加快教育强国建设、推进教育国际传播的有力举措。

glossary.explanation: A set of ideals for teachers promoted by Chinese leaders since 2023, covering belief, theory, social responsibility, dedication, moral sentiment and professional skill. The article treats it as a distinctively Chinese answer to how to build the teaching force.
The capacity to shape how issues are framed and understood in international debate. Chinese official writing often links it to national influence.
A national goal, stressed at the 2024 National Education Conference, of making China a leading country in education, tied to wider national development plans.
China's international cooperation framework launched in 2013, covering infrastructure, trade and people-to-people exchange, including education.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal of restoring China to national strength and prosperity, usually dated to 2049.

t: Understanding Xi Jinping's thought on culture to promote the integrated development of moral and aesthetic education in universities
zh: 深刻领会习近平文化思想 推动高校德育美育融合发展
paras: This short commentary in Guangming Daily asks how Chinese universities should combine moral education (deyu) with aesthetic education (meiyu). Chen argues that Xi Jinping Thought on Culture should guide the effort, and that the integration of the two is a key route to students' all-round development and to training young people of both virtue and talent.
The piece has three parts. It first explains why Xi's cultural thought supports integration, then draws three lessons from it, and finally sets out practical requirements for universities.

Chen says Xi's thought gives moral and aesthetic education a scientific orientation, a people-centred foundation in fostering virtue and cultivating people, and a cultural base in traditional Chinese culture. The lessons concern three pairings: historical and contemporary, theoretical and practical, and national and global. In practice, the author calls for building a theoretical framework alongside integrated courses, activities and home–school–community cooperation, and for drawing on both Chinese tradition and foreign educational ideas.

Chen concludes that universities must uphold Party leadership, put the people first and keep to fundamental principles while innovating. Concretely, this means Party leadership over moral and aesthetic work, fairer distribution of educational resources, and use of Confucian values, poetry and calligraphy alongside localised foreign methods. Read the original if you want a brief example of how a university Party official links Xi Jinping Thought on Culture to ideological and aesthetic education.
quoteEn: Moral education shapes the soul; aesthetic education nourishes the heart.
quoteZh: 德育塑造灵魂，美育滋养心灵。

glossary.explanation: A body of ideas on cultural work attributed to Xi Jinping and formally presented in October 2023. It treats culture as basic to national development and rejuvenation and emphasises adapting Marxism to Chinese cultural traditions.
A slogan for the fundamental task of education in official discourse: moral formation comes first in educating people.

t: Making the "Great Ideological and Political Course" knowledgeable, high-quality and smart
zh: 让“大思政课”有知、有质、更有智
paras: This commentary, published in Guangming Daily in January 2025, takes up the question of how to build the "Great Ideological and Political Course" (da sizheng ke). It responds to Xi Jinping's call at the National Education Conference (September 2024) for a strong education nation with "ideological and political leadership capacity". Liu argues that ideological and political courses are the main channel for that capacity, and that the "Great" course renews the idea of running them well by keeping them in step with the times and with practice.

The article is organised under three headings: consolidating the "root" and "soul", renewing content and methods in line with the times, and improving quality and effect by turning a static classroom into a dynamic one. Each section gives three practical requirements for universities.

On the first point, Liu holds that the course must stay anchored in Marxism and in fine traditional Chinese culture. It should be built around Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, around revolutionary and advanced socialist culture, and around the achievements of socialism with Chinese characteristics. On the second, the author calls for content close to students' lives, more varied teaching methods, plain contemporary language, and teachers who understand students and move from "mass output" to "personalised customisation". On the third, Liu proposes small-class core teaching, lessons held in campus museums and stadiums, mobile "walking" courses, and online classrooms using artificial intelligence and virtual reality.

Liu concludes that good teaching of these courses depends on schools and society working together, and that digital tools can remove limits of time and space. Read the original if you want a short example of how a university Party secretary translates central directives on ideological and political education into teaching practice.
quoteEn: We must innovate the discourse system, using popular, life-based and contemporary language to speak vividly and accessibly, so that "great principles" reach students' hearts, meaningful matters are made interesting, and lofty matters are given warmth.
quoteZh: 要创新话语体系，用通俗化、生活化、时代化的语言，生动活泼、深入浅出地把“大道理”讲到学生心坎上，把有意义的事情讲得有意思，把有高度的事情讲得有温度。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2021. It extends ideological and political teaching beyond the classroom into society, practice and online spaces.
A phrase from Xi Jinping's speech at the National Education Conference (September 2024). It names one of the attributes expected of China's education system.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The official Party guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018. It is taught as the core content of ideological and political courses.

t: A wholly new political system grown from Chinese soil
st: Understanding the universal, particular and distinctive attributes of China's people's congress system
zh: 从中国土壤中生长起来的全新政治制度
zhSub: 全面理解我国人大制度普遍性、特殊性和差异性的属性特征
paras: Writing in Beijing Daily in January 2025, Li Lin takes up Xi Jinping's description of the people's congress system as a "wholly new political system grown from Chinese soil". Li asks how this system should be understood in comparative political-philosophical terms. The commentary argues that it has three attributes at once: universality, particularity and difference. Together, Li says, these mark its historical position and its Chinese characteristics.

The piece is organised in three sections, one for each attribute. The first treats universality, drawing on Mao Zedong's 1954 speech on the draft constitution, on common human values, on the conceptual vocabulary of representative government, and on the National People's Congress's work in the Inter-Parliamentary Union since 1984. The second sets the system against Western capitalist democracies, citing Mao and Deng Xiaoping. The third compares it with other socialist states such as Vietnam, North Korea and Cuba.

On universality, Li argues that the system shares with world political civilisation concepts such as the constitution, elections, the rule of law, human rights and checks on power, and that Chinese institutions give these a "Chinese-style" content. Li holds that the system promotes shared human values and so serves as a fundamental political institution for building a community with a shared future for mankind. On particularity, Li states that China rejects presidential, parliamentary, constitutional-monarchy, "separation of three powers" and multiparty systems. In Li's account, the difference in state character and form of government sets it apart from Western capitalist systems. On difference, Li says the primary stage of socialism gives the system distinct features. These include Party leadership combined with people's mastery and law-based governance, whole-process people's democracy, regional ethnic autonomy and multiparty cooperation under Party leadership.

Li concludes, in the Marxist terms of the particular containing the general, that the three attributes exist together in dialectical unity. Universality, Li says, supplies a shared cultural basis for exchange with other countries. Particularity shows the socialist nature of the system and its claimed advantages. Difference shows its Chinese, contemporary and practical features. Li adds that this highlights the world significance of Chinese civilisation. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how a senior CASS scholar frames the people's congress system's relation to Western and other socialist models.
quoteEn: It is precisely this particularity that reveals the essential socialist-democratic character and political nature of China's people's congress system, and displays the marked advancement, people-centredness and superiority of the socialist democratic political system.
quoteZh: 正是这种特殊性，昭示了我国人大制度的社会主义民主本质特征和政治属性，展现出社会主义民主政治制度显著的先进性、人民性和优越性。

glossary.explanation: China's fundamental political system, under which people's congresses are elected at each level and the National People's Congress is the highest organ of state power. It was established in the 1954 Constitution.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept associated with Xi Jinping, stressing the interconnected fate of all countries and the pursuit of shared peace, security and prosperity.

A concept promoted by Xi Jinping since 2019. It holds that Chinese democracy covers every stage of political life, not only elections, and it presents people's congresses as a key institutional vehicle.
The official characterisation of China's present historical stage, used to explain why its system differs from other socialist models and from classical expectations.

t: Accelerating the intelligent transformation of political work in the armed forces
zh: 加快推进军队政治工作智能化建设
paras: This commentary, published in Guangming Daily in January 2025, asks how political work in the Chinese armed forces can be made "intelligent" through artificial intelligence, big data and cloud computing. Wang Yongchang argues that the process must follow the basic principles of military political work while adapting to the technical features of AI, so that "intelligence plus political work" develops through mutual shaping rather than technology simply replacing human work.

The article is organised in four sections: moving from informatization to intelligent political work; revitalising political work as the "lifeline" of the army; consolidating the distinctive advantages of the people's army under intelligent conditions; and making AI a trustworthy assistant. It covers technical building blocks (data, computing power, models, algorithms, infrastructure), organisational questions such as military–civilian coordination, and governance questions of ideology, ethics and regulation.

Wang's first central move is that intelligent political work is not unmanned political work and does not weaken the human subject. It combines revolutionary and humanistic spirit with technological rationality, inheriting the Party's command over the army, the mass line and leading by example, while building on the data and systems created by informatization. Second, Wang stresses demand-led application scenarios in ideological education, public opinion work and personnel management, and argues that political-work data, being data about people, requires specially designed datasets and algorithms and a "cloud–edge–end" computing layout. Third, the author calls for self-reliance in core technologies such as algorithms and domestic high-performance chips, and for governance of AI risks.

Wang concludes that the military should draw on late-mover advantages to turn technological strengths into soldiers' spiritual strength, Party committees' decision-making strength and units' operational strength. The author calls for vigilance against algorithmic ideological risks at the stages of training data, content production, recommendation and decision support, for human dominance in human–machine cooperation, explainable algorithms, and clear rules on rights, duties and oversight. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Chinese military academics frame AI in Party-led political work and its ideological and ethical safeguards.
quoteEn: But the intelligent transformation of military political work does not mean unmanned political work, still less a weakening of its human subjectivity; it is a union of revolutionary and humanistic spirit with technological and instrumental rationality.
quoteZh: 但军队政治工作智能化不是政治工作无人化，更不是对政治工作主体性的削弱，而是革命精神、人文精神与科技理性、工具理性的结合。

glossary.explanation: Official description of political work as essential to the army's nature and combat effectiveness; the formulation is long established in PLA discourse.

glossary.en: the Party's command over the army
glossary.explanation: The principle that the armed forces obey the Communist Party's leadership, the first of the stated requirements for the PLA.
A Party working method, associated with Mao Zedong, of drawing on the views of the people and then returning policies to them; here invoked as part of the army's traditional strengths.

t: "Walking" ideological and political courses: innovative and heartfelt
st: Yunnan Province's practical exploration of reform and innovation in ideological and political education
zh: “行走”的思政课，“走新”又“走心”
zhSub: 云南省积极推动思政教育改革创新的探索实践
paras: This field report from Guangming Daily (20 January 2025) asks how ideological and political courses (sizheng ke) can move students rather than merely instruct them. Its research team visited schools and universities across Yunnan and argues that the province has made these courses more attractive and influential by taking them out of the classroom, in what it calls "walking" courses. The report presents Yunnan's practice as a model worth drawing lessons from.

The report opens with scenes from the former site of the National Southwest Associated University, a border village and a Kunming primary school. It recalls Xi Jinping's 2020 visit to the Southwest Associated University site, where he stressed training builders and successors of socialism. Three sections follow: unity of knowledge and action, teaching through multiple channels on ethnic unity, and coverage of all school stages. A closing section sets out "experience and implications" in four points.

The team describes several examples. Visits to historic sites, the "Zhang Guimei Ideological and Political Lecture Hall" (15 recorded lectures and over 300 local sessions, according to the report) and the Puer oath-tablet site on ethnic unity are said to make the courses "visible" and "memorable". Yunnan is also said to be integrating teaching across primary, middle, secondary and university levels through a steering committee, local teaching materials, shared online resources and more than 25,000 full-time teachers. The team distils four lessons: Party leadership to build a "big ideological and political course" pattern; fuller use of resources and a "big classroom"; branded platforms; and a systematic teacher-training and recruitment framework.

The report concludes that Yunnan has grasped the needs of the times and acted on Xi Jinping's instructions, so that these courses become "golden courses" that students like and benefit from for life. It credits the gains to institutionalised Party leadership, links between classroom and social practice, and a stronger teaching force. Read the original if you want a detailed, officially framed picture of how ideological and political education is being implemented in a Chinese border province, including its practices on ethnic unity.
quoteEn: Yunnan Province attaches importance to moving from the "ideological and political course" to the "big ideological and political course", actively developing and using on- and off-campus practice bases, red-culture venues and other resources, and exploring a "classroom plus practice" model.
quoteZh: 云南省注重从“思政课”到“大思政课”的迭代，积极开发利用各类校内外实践基地、红色文化场馆等资源，探索“课堂+实践”模式

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses in Chinese schools and universities that teach Marxism, Party theory, history and morality as part of moral and civic education.
A concept promoted by Xi Jinping that extends ideological and political teaching beyond the classroom into society, social practice and everyday resources.

t: Algorithmic recommendation empowering core values education
zh: 算法推荐赋能核心价值观教育
source: Chinese Social Sciences Today (中国社会科学报), 17 January 2025
paras: Peng Xiaolan asks how algorithmic recommendation, a technology that profiles users' data and pushes content to match their inferred interests, can be used in education in the core socialist values. The commentary argues that, in the context of digital education, the technology can identify and track new ideological and behavioural trends and supply new methods for the models, settings and momentum of such education. It also holds that the technology produces specific tensions that must be managed through guiding principles.

The piece is built in three parts. The first describes three ways algorithmic recommendation empowers core values education: personalised, data-based and dynamic recommendation. The second sets out three contradictions between the technology and the aims of the education. The third offers three sets of measures, built around value orientation, ethics and law, and the laws of education.

On the benefits, Peng argues that personalised recommendation returns education to a one-to-one mode, big-data decision-making lets educators monitor learning and shape policy, and dynamic recommendation lets learners plan their own paths. Each is said to generate a "new quality" of teacher–student relations, learning materials and learners. The contradictions are algorithmic customisation versus all-round development, which risks distorted cognition and closed information circles. Algorithmic substitution versus creativity is the second, because black-box opacity and dependence weaken dialogue and human agency. Algorithmic bias versus educational fairness is the third, since small errors in data labelling, unclear accountability among designers and platforms, and privacy risks may distort outcomes.

Peng proposes that algorithms be guided by values. This means improving recommended content, building safeguards against "information cocoons", embedding Marxist theory and uplifting values, and following the national guidance on algorithm governance, with lawful training data and regular security assessments. Algorithms should also be bound by ethics and law, through data security, privacy and appropriate public disclosure of their purposes and workings. Finally, they should be developed in line with educational laws, through personalised yet selectable teaching plans and efficient feedback channels that track learners' creativity and curiosity. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Chinese ideological-education scholarship frames AI and recommender systems as both tools and risks for teaching core values.
quoteEn: Algorithmic customisation easily captures learners' attention, but this short-term comfort stands in inherent tension with the long-term nature of how values are formed.
quoteZh: 算法定制容易吸引受教育者的注意力，但这种短期的舒适感与价值观生成的长期性存在着内在张力。

glossary.explanation: Education in the core socialist values promoted by the Party-state, a central task of ideological and political education in schools and universities.
The idea that personalised feeds enclose users in a narrow range of content that reinforces their existing views, a concern widely discussed in Chinese media and policy.
The fact that the internal workings of an algorithm are not visible or understandable to its users or even its designers.

t: Experience and lessons from the popularisation of Marxism in the Yan'an period
zh: 延安时期马克思主义大众化传播的经验与启示
paras: This short commentary, first published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in January 2025, asks what the Communist Party's work of spreading Marxism among ordinary people in Yan'an (the Party's wartime base) can teach the present. Xi argues that the Yan'an period was a key stage in the popularisation of Marxism, and that its experience bears on adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, and on arming minds with Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era.

The article is organised around three headings: innovation in the discourse used to spread Marxism, a wider reach for its dissemination, and greater effectiveness of its communication. It draws on Party documents of 1941 and on Mao Zedong's 1942 speech "Oppose Stereotyped Party Writing".

Xi's core account is that Marxism had to be explained in the language of the Chinese people and of the masses, and that Party newspapers did this by taking up vivid popular speech. Dissemination ran through cadre schools, newspapers and radio, and also through folk forms such as yangge opera, New Year pictures, woodblock prints and drama. Xi stresses targeted communication: cadres, peasants and intellectuals were reached by different means, from cadre education and literacy campaigns to the Yan'an Rectification Movement and the Yan'an Forum on Literature and Art. Xi credits this with party unity, close Party–mass ties and national political mobilisation.

Xi concludes that practice-based innovation in discourse, targeted communication mechanisms and shared values pursued through persistent struggle underpinned the effectiveness of Yan'an-era communication. For today, Xi calls on mainstream media to uphold the Two Integrations, innovate their discourse and strategies, and use online media to draw "concentric circles" online and offline. Read the original if you want a brief, officially aligned overview of how Yan'an communication practice is being drawn on in current Chinese discussions of ideological work.
quoteEn: Practice-based innovation in discourse is the foundation for improving the effectiveness of Marxist communication; targeted and effective communication mechanisms are a necessary condition for raising it.
quoteZh: 立足实践的话语创新是提高马克思主义传播成效的基础；具有针对性的行之有效的传播机制，是提升马克思主义理论传播成效的必备条件。

glossary.explanation: A formula in Xi Jinping-era Party theory: combining the basic principles of Marxism with China's concrete realities, and with China's fine traditional culture.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The official body of ideas associated with Xi Jinping, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018 as the Party's guiding ideology.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for the continuing project of fitting Marxist theory to Chinese conditions and to the contemporary era.
A Party-wide campaign of 1942–1945 aimed at ideological education and discipline, which consolidated Mao Zedong's leadership and his approach to theory.

t: Creating an effective form of grassroots communication
st: Blackboard newspapers and worker-peasant correspondents in the War of Liberation period
zh: 创造基层传播的有效样态
zhSub: 解放战争时期的黑板报与工农通讯员
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 17 January 2025
paras: This short commentary from China Social Sciences Today asks how the Communist Party built effective grassroots communication during the War of Liberation (1945–49). Tian argues that the organic fusion of the village blackboard newspaper with worker-peasant correspondents was an effective form of grassroots communication in that period. Tian opens by noting that the Party is often described as the party that values the grassroots most, a commitment the author sees in its insistence on grassroots newspaper work.

The article first traces the background: wall newspapers and bulletins in the Soviet areas, the 1939 call for wall newspapers or 'mass blackboards', and the 1940s slogan of 'the whole Party and the masses run newspapers'. It then describes what a blackboard newspaper was: a chalk-written board carrying national news, local news, criticism, praise and cartoons, laid out like a paper. It draws on local examples from Shandong, the Shaanxi-Gansu-Ningxia Border Region, Hebei-Shanxi and the Huai-Hai and Yanfu areas.

Tian's central argument is a two-way relationship. Correspondents were the main contributors, and in many villages the management of correspondents merged with that of the blackboard. For the professional press they were 'amateur reporters', but for the blackboard they were its 'professional reporters'. In turn the blackboard was the 'main position' for developing correspondents. It offered illiterate or semi-literate villagers ways to take part, such as dictated 'messages'. It also gave far more chances to see their writing published, and it taught editing, organising and newspaper-reading. Tian cites figures such as 1,024 of 1,416 submissions published in one Funing village, and 10,038 of 17,541 items posted in Lianshui county during a two-month contest. Contemporary sources, quoted by the author, call the blackboard the peasants' own 'mouthpiece', the correspondent movement the 'crops' and the blackboard the 'soil'.

Tian concludes that peasants moved from 'silent' to 'speaking' subjects, and that the blackboard's reach, though limited, fostered their cultural agency. The author regrets that blackboards left almost no records, so later readers must rely on fragments. The historical lesson drawn is that, even as media change, new media should be built from grassroots conditions. Workers and peasants should get guidance, protection and new roles, so that people and media grow together and strengthen socialist ideology and culture. Read the original if you want a brief overview of Communist Party grassroots journalism in the late 1940s and the examples it cites.
quoteEn: Therefore, the organic fusion of blackboard newspapers and worker-peasant correspondents in the War of Liberation period was an effective form of grassroots communication at the time.
quoteZh: 因此，解放战争时期黑板报与工农通讯员的有机融合是当时基层传播的一种有效样态。

glossary.explanation: Ordinary workers and peasants who sent news items and letters to Party newspapers and local blackboards. They were mobilised in a mass 'correspondent movement' in the Party-led areas during the 1940s.
A chalk-written board in a village or workplace, laid out like a newspaper with news, criticism and cartoons. In the Party-led areas it served as the lowest-level medium.

glossary.pinyin: quándǎng bàn bào, qúnzhòng bàn bào
glossary.en: the whole Party and the masses run newspapers
glossary.explanation: A 1940s slogan calling on all Party organisations, and ordinary people as well, to take part in producing newspapers, not only professional journalists.
The Chinese term for the civil war between the Communist Party and the Nationalist government, 1945–49.

t: Artificial intelligence and the opinion-guiding capacity of mainstream media
zh: 人工智能助力主流媒体舆论引导力
source: China Social Sciences Today (Chinese Social Sciences Net), January 2025
paras: Following the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), which called for integrated management of news and publicity and online public opinion, Gong asks how mainstream media can strengthen their capacity to guide opinion. The commentary argues that artificial intelligence, especially generative AI, offers new means of doing so, though it carries risks.

The piece first lists three difficulties: a more plural and open set of opinion actors, with algorithmic "information cocoons" and platform-controlled visibility; online discourse that shifts quickly and is emotional, leaving official responses lagging in time and space; and cross-media and global opinion fields that overlap and sharpen confrontation. It then sets out three ways AI can be embedded in the work of mainstream media.

Gong's first point is that AI can build the scenario for news and opinion guidance: it can personalise delivery, help set the tone early in an event, filter rumours and vulgar content, and support international cooperation. Second, it can rebuild the discourse ecology by analysing public emotion and generating empathetic language, and by producing interactive content and cross-language texts for international communication. Third, it can run through the whole process of opinion monitoring: scanning sources, flagging crises, predicting trends, grading incidents and producing multimodal content.

Gong concludes that AI supports role change, new styles of expression and process re-engineering in news and publicity. The author also warns of homogenised content, path dependence, and challenges of technological ethics and transparency, and says that keeping information truthful and credible is a priority. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned view of how AI is expected to serve opinion guidance in Chinese state media.
quoteEn: How to preserve the truthfulness and credibility of information dissemination while using AI is a question that mainstream media will need to take very seriously in future.
quoteZh: 如何在使用AI技术的同时保持信息传播的真实性和公信力，是未来主流媒体需要高度重视的问题。

glossary.explanation: A long-standing Party-state concept of shaping public discourse through media and publicity so that it aligns with mainstream values and official priorities.
In Chinese usage, chiefly Party and state-run news organisations regarded as authoritative channels for official information and publicity.

glossary.zh: 新闻宣传和网络舆论一体化管理
glossary.pinyin: xīnwén xuānchuán hé wǎngluò yúlùn yītǐhuà guǎnlǐ
glossary.en: integrated management of news and publicity and online public opinion
glossary.explanation: A policy direction stressed at the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) to coordinate traditional publicity work with the governance of online discourse.

t: The "object" logic of communication in systematising Chinese stories
zh: 中国故事体系化的“物”理传播逻辑
source: Chinese Social Sciences Today (China Social Sciences Network), 2025
paras: This commentary, published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today, asks how to tell China's story well, as Xi Jinping has called for, when technology is changing the relation between people and things. Wang argues that things (wu) are gaining agency and that "everything is media", so China's international communication should build a system of communication through objects alongside narration by people. The author frames four practical questions: what to tell, with what, where, and how.

The piece is organised around those four questions. Wang first sets out the content of the stories, then classifies the objects that can carry them, then identifies the settings where they can be told, and finally proposes methods. Objects are grouped by the three kinds of story: Chinese stories, stories of the Communist Party, and stories of the new era.

On content, Wang says a story consists of teller, story, setting and audience, and that the core "principle" to convey is why the Communist Party "can", Marxism "works" and socialism with Chinese characteristics is "good". Drawing on Schramm's formula of selection probability, Wang holds that audiences need stories of use to them. On objects, Wang lists cultural heritage, revolutionary relics, and new-era items such as films, e-commerce and payment platforms, high-speed rail and artificial intelligence. Such objects are told in media platforms, everyday consumption and overseas tourism, where visitors' own experience lets objects speak.

On method, Wang proposes "observing things through things", citing Shao Yong and contrasting phenomenology's suspension of presuppositions, so that objective regularities show through objects. Wang also urges attention to objects' mobilising power (even idols and fans are described as reified media), giving each object a focused function, and building object-centred narrative platforms, which the author says do not yet exist. The aim is presented not as cultural domination but as mutual learning among civilisations and a communicable world. Read the original if you want an example of how Chinese communication scholars link the "object turn" in narrative theory to the official task of telling China's story well.
quoteEn: The aim of object narrative is to bring out the value and meaning of objects.
quoteZh: 物叙事的目标在于凸显物的价值和意义

glossary.explanation: A phrase from Xi Jinping, who has called for "telling China's story well and spreading China's voice well". It is the standard formula for guiding China's external communication.
The official name for the Chinese Communist Party's theory and system of socialism since the reform era.

t: The narrative code of "inspiring understanding of the Way" in ideological and political courses in the new era and new journey
zh: 新时代新征程思政课“启人悟道”的叙事密码
source: China Social Sciences Today (Chinese Social Sciences Net), 17 January 2025
paras: This short commentary, published in China Social Sciences Today in January 2025, asks how teachers of ideological and political courses (sizheng ke) in universities can make their teaching more persuasive. Chen Bo argues that they should build a habit of narrative thinking and teach through stories. Citing Xi Jinping's remark that deep truths must move and convince people through storytelling, the author holds that stories connect events to students' own situations and so carry value guidance indirectly.

The article sets out four kinds of story that teachers should draw on, each tied to a "way" (dao): Chinese history and culture, the Party's revolutionary success, reform and development, and human civilisation. It rests the approach on the achievements of socialism with Chinese characteristics and on traditional, revolutionary and advanced socialist culture.

On culture, Chen recommends using the structure of Chinese characters, ancient artefacts, the sayings of ancient thinkers and classical poetry to convey ideas such as benevolence, people-centredness and harmony. On revolution, teachers should tell the stories behind the Long March, Yan'an and Jinggangshan spirits, using local and campus resources and varied media such as images, museum visits, interviews and virtual experiences. On reform, Chen lists examples including the restoration of the college entrance examination, Xiaogang village's contract system, Zhongguancun, the "lucid waters and lush mountains" idea and the poverty reduction of nearly 100 million people. The author adds that teachers should present the Party's strategic wisdom in Chinese modernization.

The fourth strand asks teachers to promote exchange among civilisations through Dunhuang and Silk Road culture and cooperation stories from the Belt and Road Initiative. They should also treat peace, development, fairness, justice, democracy and freedom as shared human values and present the Global Civilization Initiative as a Chinese contribution. Chen concludes that such narrative work will make these courses more relevant and attractive. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Chinese pedagogical writing links storytelling methods to Party history and official political themes.
quoteEn: Teachers of ideological and political courses should continually improve their narrative thinking, taking the world-renowned achievements of socialism with Chinese characteristics as the content that supports it.
quoteZh: 思政课教师应不断提升叙事思维，以中国特色社会主义取得的举世瞩目成就为内容支撑

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses in Chinese schools and universities that teach Marxism, Party history and official political theory. They are a main channel of political education.
The official name for China's current political and economic path since reform and opening up, combining Party leadership with a market economy.
The official concept of China's own path to modernisation, set out by the Party especially since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
A Chinese international infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative launched by Xi Jinping in 2013.
A proposal put forward by Xi Jinping in 2023 that promotes respect for the diversity of civilisations and dialogue among them.

t: How new media can empower the building of red culture brands
zh: 新媒体赋能红色文化品牌建设
source: China Social Sciences Today (Chinese Social Sciences Net), 17 January 2025
paras: This short commentary in China Social Sciences Today asks how new media can be used to build brands around red culture, the spiritual legacy formed by the Party and the people in revolution, construction and reform. Liu Li argues that the interactive, data-driven and multi-channel features of new media give red culture fresh vitality, and takes the Sichuan–Chongqing region as the main case.

The article first outlines the characteristics of new media: immediacy, interactivity, multi-channel dissemination, personalisation and intelligence. It then explains why these suit the spread of regional culture, and turns to Sichuan–Chongqing red culture, discussing three routes of innovation and three communicative functions.

Liu contends that digital communication, creative product development and cross-sector integration are the main routes. Technologies such as 5G, holographic projection and VR can bring revolutionary sites and museums online; platform data can guide souvenirs, clothing, animation and other cultural products; and links with tourism, education and agriculture can support red study tours for young people. Liu then argues that new media serve empathetic communication, interactive exchange and value guidance, for example through live streaming, short-video contests and moderated discussion, so that audiences form what the article calls a community of expression.

Liu concludes that digital channels, innovative products and cross-field cooperation should continue to be used to meet diverse public needs and extend the reach and social influence of red culture. The piece is a brief, practice-oriented proposal rather than an empirical study. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Chinese ideological and political education scholars link new media strategy with regional red culture branding.
quoteEn: Taking digital communication as the channel, innovative product development as the vehicle and cross-field cooperation as the lever, [we should] keep meeting the public's diverse needs through new media communication and promote the development of the Sichuan–Chongqing red culture brand.
quoteZh: 以数字化传播为渠道，以创新产品开发为载体，以跨领域合作为抓手，不断在新媒体传播中满足大众的多元化需求，促进川渝红色文化品牌发展。

glossary.explanation: Cultural resources and spiritual traditions arising from the Chinese Communist Party's revolutionary, construction and reform history, including sites, memorials and the associated 'spirits'. It is treated officially as part of advanced socialist culture.
Educational trips, often for young people, to revolutionary sites that combine tourism with patriotic and ideological education.
The author's term for a group of audiences who share and express common interests and values through new media platforms.

t: Guiding the development of ethnology with a sense of community for the Chinese nation
zh: 用中华民族共同体意识引领民族学学科建设
source: China Social Sciences Today (via China Social Sciences Net), 2025
paras: Writing in the China Social Sciences Today after the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), Yang Zhengquan asks how ethnology, as a discipline, should respond to the call to build an autonomous Chinese system of philosophy and social science knowledge. The answer is that the discipline must be led by forging a strong sense of community for the Chinese nation. Yang calls this the primary political task of ethnology today and argues that the field must not drift from it.

The commentary is organised around three sources of guidance, each tied to a sub-discipline of ethnology. The first is contemporary Chinese Marxist theory of nationalities, linked to Marxist nationality theory and policy. The second is the idea of the 'Four-way Togetherness', linked to a discipline Yang calls Chinese nationality studies. The third is the idea of a community with a shared future for mankind, linked to anthropology and world ethnology. Yang draws on the Plenum's Decision and on statements by Xi Jinping.

Yang presents Xi Jinping's important thinking on strengthening and improving ethnic work as the contemporary Chinese Marxist theory of nationalities, and lists its twelve 'musts' from the 2021 Central Conference on Ethnic Work. The 'Four-way Togetherness' means sharing weal and woe, honour and disgrace, life and death, and destiny. Yang says it requires balancing commonality and diversity, and the Chinese national community consciousness and the consciousness of each ethnic group. Yang adds that Chinese history needs its own epistemology and methodology rather than imported Western nationality theory. The author repeatedly names Western theoretical and discursive influence as a problem in Chinese ethnology.

Yang concludes that ethnology should take forging this sense of community as its main thread. The discipline should build a complete theoretical system, and a disciplinary, academic and discourse system with Chinese characteristics. Yang also calls for textbooks such as the Introduction to the Chinese Nation Community, general histories of the Chinese nation, work on ancient texts and artefacts, and support for younger scholars. The aim is to train specialists who command this theory and have fieldwork skills. Read the original if you want to see how a senior academic administrator links Party nationality policy to the reorganisation of ethnology's sub-fields and training.
quoteEn: In studying the history of the development of the Chinese nation, one must use China's own epistemology and methodology, and cannot simply apply that set of Western theories of nationalities.
quoteZh: 研究中华民族发展史，要用中国自己的认识论和方法论，不能简单套用西方那一套民族理论。

glossary.zh: 铸牢中华民族共同体意识
glossary.en: a sense of community for the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: forging a firm consciousness of the Chinese national community
glossary.explanation: A slogan that Xi Jinping has made the central thread of the Party's ethnic work in the new era. It stresses a shared national identity that sits above the identities of individual ethnic groups.
Xi Jinping's formula that all ethnic groups should share weal and woe, honour and disgrace, life and death, and destiny. The article treats it as the ideological basis of the national community idea.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept for international relations, first put forward in the early 2010s. It stresses dialogue, win-win cooperation and mutual learning among civilisations.
A high-level Party meeting that sets policy on ethnic affairs. The 2021 meeting summarised the Party's experience in twelve 'musts'.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: How to present the "original theoretical image" of ideological and political education
zh: 怎样呈现思想政治教育的“理论原相”
source: China Social Sciences Net – Chinese Social Sciences Today, January 2025
paras: Marking forty years since ideological and political education was established as an academic discipline in 2024, this book review by Wu Hongzheng assesses a four-volume work by Li Zhongjun (Northeast Normal University) and colleagues, Research on the Ideological and Political Education Thought of Marx and Engels (the Research). Wu argues that the work presents the "original theoretical image" (lilun yuanxiang) of the field in a distinctive way, grounded closely in the classic texts. The review also contends that the work leaves the logical links among its parts underdeveloped.

The Research collects Marx's and Engels's direct and indirect remarks on the subject and organises them along four dimensions: concepts, categories, content and methods. Wu describes 11 concepts, nine pairs of categories (such as individual and society, thought and interest, theory and practice), ten kinds of educational content, and ten methods, including theoretical inculcation, critique and exposure, and self-reform. The review goes through each dimension and notes what the book contributes and what it omits.

Wu's main criticisms are logical. The book does not explain why these 11 concepts matter and others, such as freedom or species-essence, do not. It also does not state the dialectical principle that categories come in pairs, as in Hegel's logic, nor does it move from paired opposites to their synthesis. Its textual fidelity, Wu says, risks losing the "living soul" running through the texts. It also leaves open what "all-round" means in the all-round development of the person. On methods, Wu asks whether the defence of inculcation takes account of Marx's views on the people's subjecthood, and whether the stress on critique overlooks Marx's positive inheritance from German classical philosophy.

Wu concludes that the Research respects the classics, avoids forced interpretation, and offers a necessary "anatomical" analysis. Its four dimensions form a chain: analysis runs from front to back, and construction from back to front. Wu argues this supports the scientific and theoretical development of a young discipline whose concepts, categories and principles are still vague, and helps build an independent Chinese knowledge system of ideological and political education. Read the original if you want a short critical assessment of how Chinese scholars are recovering Marx and Engels as a foundation for the discipline of ideological and political education.
quoteEn: Yet research begins with "analysis" and ends in "synthesis", and this deserves to be affirmed.
quoteZh: 但是，“研究”工作首先起始于“分析”，终止于“综合”，这是需要肯定的。

glossary.explanation: A Chinese academic discipline and educational practice, established in 1984, that teaches political ideals, values and Marxist theory in schools, universities and the Party. It is also a field of research in Marxism departments.
The review's term for the field's theory as it first appears in the classic Marxist texts, before later interpretation.
A method, traced to Lenin's view that socialist consciousness is brought to workers from outside. It is controversial because critics see it as coercive.
Refers to the Party's self-revolution (self-reform), a theme in recent Party discourse that the book treats as a method of ideological education.

t: Inheriting and disseminating red culture in classic ethnic-minority literature
zh: 红色文化在民族文学经典中传承与传播
source: China Social Sciences Today (中国社会科学报), posted 17 January 2025
paras: This commentary, published in China Social Sciences Today in January 2025, asks how red culture embedded in the classics of ethnic-minority literature can be passed on within China and communicated abroad. Huang Xiaojuan argues that these classics carry red culture in distinctly ethnic forms while also giving it a universal, world-facing dimension. In the author's view, rereading them strengthens national identity and helps present the image of the Chinese nation as a single community to the world.

The piece opens by defining literary classics and red culture, which the author describes as a product of integrating Marxism with Chinese realities, formed from the New Democratic Revolution through reform and opening up. It then has two main sections: the ethnicized character of red culture and its contemporary inheritance, and its worldwide character and overseas dissemination. Examples include Manchu writers such as Shu Qun and Duanmu Hongliang in anti-Japanese war literature, and the Yan'an-trained arts troupe that went to Shenyang in 1945.

Huang contends that patriotism, ethnic unity and the Party's leadership recur as themes in minority literature, and that these works express red culture through ethnic lifeways, folk epic traditions, proverbs, songs and storytelling. The author then turns outward, citing the film script Sons and Daughters of China, which won an international festival prize, and Chinese troupes at the 1949 World Festival of Youth in Budapest. A lineage of heroes across revolution, construction and reform is presented as uniting ethnic and temporal character. Telling China's story well, Huang argues, lets these works evoke empathy across cultures and build Chinese cultural subjectivity.

Huang concludes that carrying forward red culture in minority classics is a mission of the new era, helping to forge a strong sense of community for the Chinese nation. The author proposes linking dissemination to international Chinese-language education through a "Chinese+" teaching model, and says such work can also help build a discipline system for literary studies with Chinese characteristics. Read the original if you want a short example of how Party-affiliated scholars link ethnic literature, red culture and external cultural communication.
quoteEn: The writing of red culture in the classics of ethnic literature is a vivid embodiment of the close union of ethnic character, the character of the times, and the people's character.
quoteZh: 民族文学经典中的红色文化书写是民族性、时代性、人民性紧密结合的生动体现

glossary.explanation: The revolutionary heritage associated with the Chinese Communist Party, including its history, heroes, spirit and cultural products, treated in official discourse as part of Chinese culture.

glossary.en: sense of community for the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: consciousness of the Chinese nation as a community
glossary.explanation: An official concept emphasising that all ethnic groups in China belong to one national community. It is central to Party ethnic policy, especially since the 2010s.
Mao Zedong's term for the Chinese revolution of roughly 1919–1949, led by the Communist Party, which was to precede the socialist stage.
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched in China in 1978.

t: Raising the discursive power of Marxist ideology in the new era
zh: 提升新时代马克思主义意识形态话语权
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), January 2025
paras: Writing in a newspaper commentary after Xi Jinping's recent instruction on the Marxist Theory Research and Construction Project (the "Marxism Project", launched by the Central Committee in 2004), Luo Yuting asks how the Project has strengthened the discursive power of Marxist ideology in the new era. Luo argues that over 21 years, and especially since the 18th Party Congress (2012), the Project has largely overcome a situation in which China's ideology "had reasons but could not state them, stated them but could not spread them, spread them but could not resonate". It is described as the key project for raising Marxist ideological discourse power.

The article is organised around three functions of the Project: promoting theoretical innovation, theoretical dissemination and the putting of theory into practice. Each is tied to one of the three problems in the formula above. The author draws on Xi Jinping's statements and on figures about the Project's research centres, textbooks, popular readings and digital outreach.

On innovation, Luo says the Project applies the Two Integrations and the "six musts", sets up research centres on socialist democracy, contemporary thought trends, international communication and Chinese civilisation, funds more than 700 key topics, and has set up 19 research centres on Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. On dissemination, it has produced unified textbooks for ideological and political theory courses and over 110 key textbooks for humanities disciplines. It also issues the popular series Theory Hotspots Face to Face, with total circulation in the tens of millions, uses digital platforms, and runs a Marxist literature collection project for international audiences. On practice, Luo contends that the Project turns theoretical, academic and ideological language into policy, popular and everyday language, and studies concepts such as people-centredness, Chinese modernization, the Belt and Road Initiative and a community with a shared future for mankind.

Luo concludes that through these three channels the Project has reversed Marxism's earlier "absence" in some disciplines, textbooks and forums. In the author's assessment, the ideological situation has undergone a fundamental, overall change, the guiding position of Marxism is consolidated, and the Project supplies strength for national rejuvenation through Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned account of how the Marxism Project's work is presented as building ideological discourse power.
quoteEn: The Marxism Project is the key project for raising the discursive power of Marxist ideology in the new era.
quoteZh: “马工程”是提升新时代马克思主义意识形态话语权的关键工程。

glossary.zh: 马克思主义理论研究和建设工程
glossary.pinyin: Mǎkèsīzhǔyì lǐlùn yánjiū hé jiànshè gōngchéng
glossary.en: Marxist Theory Research and Construction Project
glossary.explanation: A national programme launched by the Party Central Committee in 2004 to produce Marxist research and unified textbooks, usually abbreviated as the "Marxism Project" (马工程).
The capacity to set the terms of public debate and have one's ideological claims heard and accepted, domestically and internationally.
Formula associated with Xi Jinping: combining Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.
The official term for China's path of modernization, presented by the Party as distinct from Western models.
China's international infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative, launched in 2013.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept of international relations, stressing shared interests and cooperative global governance.

t: Universities should advance ideological and political theory courses in step with arming minds with the Party's innovative theory
zh: 高校要坚持思政课建设与党的创新理论武装同步推进
paras: This commentary, published in China Social Sciences Today in January 2025, responds to Xi Jinping's instruction that the building of ideological and political theory courses in schools should advance in step with arming teachers and students with the Party's innovative theory. Han Xu, a university Party secretary, argues that universities should treat high-quality, distinctive courses of this kind as the lever for raising the overall effectiveness of theoretical education and for the content-based development of ideological and political education.

The piece is organised in five sections. It sets out the theoretical basis for the dual task, the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, the practical effects required in the classroom, the need to raise the level of systematic and scholarly interpretation, and the building of a "big ideological and political course" framework. A final section on safeguards deals with the teaching staff.

Han first places the task in the Party's tradition of theoretical education, citing the Gutian Conference and the Yan'an rectification movement as precedents. In this account, the courses are the main venue for Marxist and ideological education, and their essence, following Xi, is "explaining principles". Han then argues that the courses must be targeted and probing: content detached from students' needs, such as employment, entrepreneurship and technological innovation, will not win their conviction. Teachers should therefore use lively cases, group discussion and simulation, and should work together to build a systematic, well-structured curriculum on Xi Jinping Thought so that they can teach theory rather than only tell stories.

Han calls for a "big ideological and political course" in which ideological content is carried by specialist teachers, counsellors and administrators, and in which classroom teaching is linked to visits to patriotic education bases and high-tech firms. The author also proposes stricter entry standards for ideological and political course teachers, training, incentives and an exit mechanism. The aim is a teaching force described as politically strong and broad in vision. Han concludes that advancing the two tasks together is a duty of the era and that universities should keep innovating their models in order to train socialist builders and successors. Read the original if you want an example of how a university Party leader translates a central directive into concrete institutional measures for ideological and political education.
quoteEn: Ideological and political theory courses are the main channel for disseminating the Party's innovative theory.
quoteZh: 思政课是党的创新理论传播的主渠道。

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses in Chinese schools and universities that teach Marxism, Party theory and political values. The abbreviation covers a defined set of national courses.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018. It is presented officially as the latest stage in adapting Marxism to China.
A policy concept promoted since 2021 that extends ideological education beyond the classroom, into society, practice and other subjects, involving many actors.
The effort to give Party theory a rigorous academic and logical grounding. It is often paired with systematization (体系化) in official discussions of ideological work.

t: Using the newly revised National Defence Education Law to build strong patriotic and military-strengthening forces
st: Shanghai's approach to implementing whole-people national defence education
zh: 以落实新修订国防教育法为契机 凝聚爱国强军的磅礴力量
paras: Zhao Jiaming, a senior Shanghai Party official, writes in the People's Daily on how to put the newly revised National Defence Education Law of the People's Republic of China into practice. The author argues that national defence is the foundation of national survival, and that a strong defence requires national defence education to reach the whole population. Zhao holds that the revised law, by clarifying the content, guiding ideology, coverage, methods and support mechanisms of such education, matters greatly for promoting patriotism and strengthening the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

The piece opens by citing a changing international environment, in which traditional and non-traditional security threats are said to intertwine. It gives Shanghai a special responsibility as an international metropolis and a front line of reform and opening up. It is then organised in three parts, each pairing what the revised law requires with what Shanghai has already done and what it will do next: ideological guidance, extending education from key groups to society as a whole, and coordination of institutions and resources.

On the first point, Zhao stresses that national defence education has a distinctly political character and must follow the Party's line. The revised law names Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era as its guiding ideology, and Zhao presents Xi Jinping's thinking on strengthening the armed forces as decisive for the work. On coverage, the author calls for combining universal education with attention to leading cadres, described as the key group, and young people, described as the foundation, so that progress with these groups pulls the rest of society along. Shanghai's measures include a curriculum system for cadres, youth brand activities, mass events, new-media channels, and the use of the city's red-heritage sites. On coordination, Zhao points to strengthened Party leadership, a dedicated working mechanism under the municipal publicity leadership group, designated education bases, and the involvement of social organisations, universities, veterans and volunteers.

Zhao concludes that these steps will make national defence education a genuinely society-wide undertaking, in which military and civilian sectors cooperate and the whole population takes part. The article offers a view of how a leading Party official describes local implementation of the law under the Party's guidance. Read the original if you want a concrete example of how Shanghai's leadership translates national defence legislation into institutions, programmes and propaganda work.
quoteEn: Our national defence is the defence of the whole people, and popularising and strengthening national defence education is a shared responsibility of the whole of society.
quoteZh: 我们的国防是全民国防，普及和加强国防教育是全社会共同的责任

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018. The revised law names it as the guiding ideology of national defence education.

glossary.en: Xi Jinping's thinking on strengthening the armed forces
glossary.literal: Xi Jinping Thought on Strengthening the Military
glossary.explanation: The official body of ideas on military building, presented as an important component of Xi Jinping Thought. The article treats it as the fundamental guide for national defence education.
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched in 1978. The article cites it in describing Shanghai as a front-line city.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's central national goal, associated with the Chinese Dream. Here national defence education is described as building its spiritual great wall.
Sites, relics and memorials linked to the Communist Party's revolutionary history. Shanghai, where the Party was founded, uses them as teaching resources for patriotic and defence education.

keywords: Xi Jinping's thinking on strengthening the armed forces

t: Finding the right focal points for building ideological and political theory courses in universities in the new era
zh: 找准新时代高校思政课建设着力点
paras: This newspaper commentary, published in China Social Sciences Today, asks how universities should build their ideological and political theory courses (sixheng ke) in the new era. Zhang Yuguang, a university Party official, argues that universities must study and implement Xi Jinping's speech at the National Education Conference (2024) and his May 2024 instructions on school ideological and political courses, and must identify the right points of leverage. The stated goal is to cultivate people of the new era who are reliable for the Party, patriotic and ready to shoulder national rejuvenation.

The article is organised around four areas of work: reforming and innovating the teaching of these key courses; planning a \"big ideological and political course\" with systems thinking; using digital technology to extend the courses' reach; and raising the professional level of the teachers. Each section opens with Xi Jinping's remarks and then sets out what universities should do.

On teaching reform, Zhang calls for a problem-oriented approach, which the author presents as a basic Marxist standpoint. Teachers should address the handful of questions that students are actually puzzled by and explain facts and principles one by one. The author asks for more student participation, content drawn from the achievements of socialism with Chinese characteristics, and language students find easy to accept. On systems thinking, Zhang urges coordination among many actors, collaborative mechanisms with funding and facilities, use of local red resources, and integrated courses across university, middle and primary schools. On digital technology, the article proposes immersive classrooms using generative AI, XR and VR, and a curriculum built around Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era.

On teachers, Zhang proposes building a team that is politically strong and broad in outlook. This means fostering professional pride, promoting the spirit of educators, and reforming evaluation and promotion so that teaching comes first. It also means that teachers should hold firm Marxist belief, give rigorous theoretical answers to students, and improve through recruitment, training, incentives and teaching competitions. Zhang concludes that these four measures together will push the courses to a new stage of high-quality, connotation-based development. Read the original if you want a concise example of how a Chinese university Party official translates central directives on ideological and political education into practical measures.
quoteEn: Ideological and political courses are not bookish learning or \"speculation in an ivory tower\", but a discipline widely applied in state governance, social development and everyday life.
quoteZh: 思政课不是书斋里的学问，不是“象牙塔中的玄想”，而是广泛应用于国家治理、社会发展、日常生活的学科

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018. The article says it should be the core of the curriculum and textbooks.
Compulsory courses in Marxist theory, Party doctrine and moral education taught at all levels of Chinese education. They are treated as the key vehicle for the Party's educational aims.
A concept promoted by Xi Jinping that extends ideological education beyond the classroom into society, practice and real-life settings.

t: Vigorously cultivating and promoting heroic culture
zh: 大力培育和弘扬英雄文化
paras: This commentary, first published in the PLA Daily on 15 January 2024, asks why and how the People's Liberation Army should cultivate heroic culture. Chen Zhen argues that heroic culture is an important part of the military's strong-army culture, a driver of morale and fighting spirit, and a support for the army's cohesion and combat capability. Preserving the army's heroic character, the author says, requires sustained effort to promote it.

The piece is organised in three parts. The first sets out three reasons why heroic culture is needed. The second describes its distinctive features and spiritual content. The third proposes concrete ways to cultivate and promote it. Chen draws throughout on Xi Jinping's remarks on heroes and heroic spirit, and on examples from Chinese history and the history of the Party and army.

On the reasons, Chen contends that heroic culture strengthens political loyalty, because it carries faith in Marxism, confidence in socialism with Chinese characteristics and in the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. It also raises moral standards and serves the goal of building a world-class military. On its features, the author argues that it combines an enduring core with change over time, affirms the people as makers of history while recognising the role of outstanding individuals, and values both great deeds and ordinary people doing ordinary work well. In this account, heroes include scientists and astronauts as well as ordinary workers and rank-and-file soldiers.

For practice, Chen proposes three lines of work. The first is better education and publicity: classroom teaching, ceremonies, and less abstract, formulaic and exaggerated portrayals of heroes. The second is more varied carriers, including original literary, film and music works, heroes' former residences and martyrs' cemeteries, and new technologies such as 5G and artificial intelligence. The third is stronger institutions: legal protection under the Heroes and Martyrs Protection Law, regular rather than episodic activity, and support for the families of those who died. Read the original if you want a short example of how PLA ideological work frames heroic culture and its practical measures.
quoteEn: Greatness comes from the ordinary, and the ordinary makes greatness; this is inherent in the heroic culture of the new era.
quoteZh: 伟大出自平凡，平凡造就伟大，这是新时代英雄文化的题中应有之义。

glossary.explanation: The body of values, stories, commemorations and symbols that honour heroes and martyrs. In Party and military discourse it is used for ideological education and morale-building.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The official goal of restoring China's national strength and international standing, closely associated with Xi Jinping's leadership.
The official name for the Chinese Communist Party's governing model and ideology since the reform era.
An official goal, set out under Xi Jinping, of building the PLA into a fully modern force by the middle of the twenty-first century.
A 2018 Chinese law that protects the names, reputations and honour of heroes and martyrs and penalises defaming or insulting them.

t: Strengthening the "six capacities" of a leading education country to support the building of a Healthy China
zh: 增强教育强国“六力” 支撑健康中国建设
paras: This commentary, published in Guangming Daily in January 2025, asks how medical education can serve the goal of building a leading education country with Chinese characteristics.
