Li and Huang take Xi Jinping's formulation at the second national education conference of the new era, which names six capacities, and argue that building national medical strength around them underpins both medical education quality and the Healthy China project.

The article goes through the six capacities in turn, each with a short list of tasks for medical schools: ideological and political guidance, talent competitiveness, scientific and technological support, capacity to safeguard people's wellbeing, social coordination, and international influence. It closes with a general statement on how medical schools should orient themselves.

Li and Huang call for moral education to be the first content of training, with ideals and professional ethics running through the whole process. They propose integrated curricula, "medicine plus X" and clinical medicine plus public health programmes, and AI in teaching. They want medical schools to target frontier science and national needs, with strategic fields such as precision and digital medicine, and to tackle "bottleneck" problems in translating basic research. On wellbeing, they urge new programmes in specialisms in short supply, standards and guidelines suited to China, and wider and more balanced distribution of quality medical resources. They also propose partnerships among schools, hospitals, firms and government, and international joint programmes and laboratories offering a "Chinese approach" to global medical education.

The authors conclude that medical schools must uphold the socialist orientation of education and put people's health first. They also call for balance between supporting national strategy and meeting livelihood needs, and between rooting in China and drawing on international experience. Read the original if you want a concise example of how a leading Zhejiang University medical school leadership translates Xi Jinping's education-power agenda into concrete tasks for medical education.
quoteEn: Medical schools must adhere to the socialist orientation of running schools and take improving the people's health and wellbeing as their own responsibility.
quoteZh: 医学院校要坚持社会主义办学方向，以增进人民健康福祉为己任

glossary.explanation: A national goal of building a world-leading education system, set out in official documents and Xi Jinping's speeches, with a target date of 2035 in the national plan.
A national strategy launched in 2016 to improve public health and healthcare services, aiming at a long-term set of health targets.

t: Building a system for transmitting traditional Chinese virtues
zh: 构建中华传统美德传承体系
paras: This newspaper commentary in Guangming Daily takes up a task set by the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024): building a system for transmitting traditional Chinese virtues. Zhang Hongxia describes these virtues as the essence of Chinese culture and an inexhaustible source for moral construction. The author argues that such a system requires sustained work in four areas: excavation and interpretation, communication, education, and institutional guarantees.

The article is organised under four numbered headings. It first deals with content, then with a three-dimensional communication matrix, then with joint educational effort by schools, families and society, and finally with institutional support. Each section lists concrete measures rather than historical or philosophical analysis of particular virtues.

On content, Zhang calls for using both traditional methods and digital and intelligent technologies to uncover virtues such as patriotic dedication, diligence and thrift, and filial piety. These should be explained accurately, comprehensively and in scholarly terms. Guided by Marxism, they should be given new meanings through creative transformation and innovative development, and be expressed in modern discourse. On communication, the author wants traditional and new media to work together, and domestic and overseas publicity to reinforce each other, for example through translating classics and holding international seminars. On education, Zhang proposes integrating virtue education across primary, secondary and university stages and treating the family as the first classroom. The author also proposes targeted approaches for officials, enterprises, communities and villages, with officials described as the "key minority".

Zhang's institutional proposals rest on Party leadership, a mix of "soft" social norms such as village and citizen codes and "hard" legal rules, and support in personnel, technology and funding. Incentives would include selecting moral models, local "traditional virtue lecture halls" and a system for evaluating citizens' moral quality. The stated aim is to make transmission routine and long-lasting. Read the original if you want a concise, policy-oriented account of how official discourse envisages operationalising the transmission of traditional virtue through media, schooling and governance.
quoteEn: Building a system for transmitting traditional Chinese virtues requires schools, families and society to work in concert, jointly build a three-dimensional pattern of education, and together create an educational force in which multiple actors resonate at the same frequency.
quoteZh: 构建中华传统美德传承体系，需要学校、家庭、社会协同发力，共建立体化育人格局，携手打造多主体同频共振的育人合力。

glossary.explanation: A Party formula for preserving core principles while renewing methods and content. Here it appears alongside the phrase 'creative transformation and innovative development' of traditional culture.

glossary.zh: 创造性转化、创新性发展
glossary.explanation: A formula in Party cultural policy for reworking traditional culture to fit contemporary society. It is used to justify reinterpreting inherited values under Marxist guidance.
A phrase Xi Jinping uses for leading cadres, whose conduct is said to set the example for wider society.

t: Three new forms of historical nihilism
zh: 历史虚无主义的三种新样态
paras: This short commentary in Study Times asks how historical nihilism is changing in the current environment. Chen argues that the trend will not leave the stage on its own. Instead it is shifting from open, blunt expression to oblique and concealed forms, and its themes are becoming more "academic". The author calls for attention to three new forms.
The article takes the forms in turn: networked, intelligent (AI-driven) and "academicised". It is a brief survey with a few examples, not a systematic study.

On the first, Chen says that since the 1990s, and especially after 2010, historical nihilism has moved onto social platforms, livestreaming and game apps. Open denials of historical materialism and attacks on heroes have, the author notes, decreased online. Chen reads this as concealment through fragmented narratives and everyday infiltration, not retreat, and cites a blogger whose account name "73I" is said to encourage forgetting Japanese wartime atrocities. On the second, Chen describes generative content tools producing material in bulk, deepfakes and "bot armies" posting and liking it, and recommendation algorithms targeting users with such content. On the third, the author says nihilists dress idealist history in scholarly language, citing partial sources. The leading example is the "New Qing History", which Chen says denies Manchu–Han integration, claims the Qing was not China and now extends to maritime claims, and which Chen calls false.

Chen concludes that these forms increase concealment and deception and that AI will create further room for spread, which needs high vigilance. Historians are urged to oppose "New Qing History" openly and to restore a true picture on the basis of historical materialism. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated writers characterise current forms of historical nihilism and the "New Qing History" debate.
quoteEn: With the help of artificial intelligence, historical nihilism has gained unprecedented room to grow in producing, publishing and spreading information; its concealment and deceptiveness have intensified further, and it carries the risk of diffusion and spread.
quoteZh: 借助人工智能技术，历史虚无主义在信息生产、发布与传播上获得了前所未有的滋长空间，隐匿性、欺骗性进一步加剧，潜藏着扩散、蔓延的风险。

glossary.explanation: In official Chinese usage, a label for views seen as denying or distorting the Party's revolutionary history, its leaders and socialism's historical path. Party writers treat it as an ideological threat.
The Marxist conception of history, which explains social change through material production and class relations. The article treats it as the correct basis for historical research.

A school of Western-based scholarship that stresses the Manchu and Inner Asian character of the Qing empire. Chinese official commentary often criticises it for questioning the continuity between the Qing and China.

t: Advancing the building of a leading country in education with strong ideological and political guidance
zh: 以强大的思政引领力推进教育强国建设
paras: Published in Study Times in January 2025, this commentary takes up Xi Jinping's statement at the National Education Conference that a leading country in education should have six strengths. Huang Siguang focuses on the first of them, the capacity for ideological and political guidance. The author argues that it is a continuation of the Party's tradition of ideological and political work and a basis for building an education system with Chinese characteristics.

The piece is organised in three parts. It first explains how this capacity defines the political character of the education drive, then how it steers the direction of that drive, and finally what universities can do to strengthen it in practice.

Huang contends that ideological and political guidance gives education its socialist foundation, reflects the Party's overall leadership of education, and expresses the fundamental task of fostering virtue through education. In the author's account, it builds cohesion around Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, stimulates creativity among staff and students, and links universities to the strategies for science, technology and talent. The proposed measures are to develop ideological and political courses in depth, using digital technology and red resources, to build a high-calibre teaching and counselling workforce, and to create a pattern of coordination across courses, research, practice, culture, online work and management.

Huang concludes that guidance should be turned into concrete results for high-quality development in higher education, so that all staff, throughout the whole process and in every respect, take part in fostering students. Read the original if you want to see how a university Party secretary presents the role of ideological and political education within the education-power agenda.
quoteEn: Among the "six strengths", ideological and political guidance holds first place.
quoteZh: 思政引领力在“六力”之中居于首位。

glossary.explanation: One of six capacities Xi Jinping said a leading country in education should have, named at the 2024 National Education Conference. It refers to the capacity of ideological and political education to steer the values and direction of schooling.
A long-standing Chinese educational concept, now officially described as the fundamental task of education. It stresses moral and political formation alongside knowledge.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017 and 2018.
The Party's official name for China's path, system and theory of socialism since the reform era.
Compulsory courses in Marxist theory, Party doctrine and moral education taught at all levels of Chinese schooling.

t: Making the Party's innovative theory take deeper root among the people
zh: 让党的创新理论更加深入人心
source: People's Forum Online (人民论坛网), January 2025
paras: This short commentary, published in January 2025, responds to a recent instruction from Xi Jinping on the Project for Marxist Theoretical Research and Development in the New Era. The instruction calls for systematic, scholarly study of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era and for more targeted, effective propaganda. Yang and Zhang argue that the Party's theoretical innovation contains new experience and wisdom whose full understanding strengthens theoretical consciousness and confidence and helps the theory reach ordinary people.

The article is organised around three tasks: publicising the historical experience of a century of struggle, upholding the original aspiration of putting the people first, and answering the latest demands of the era's questions.

On history, the authors say that Marxism gave China's people a direction after earlier searches for national salvation failed. In their account the nation moved from saving the country to building, enriching and strengthening it, guided by adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. On the people, they hold that people-centredness is Marxism's most distinctive character and that the Party's purpose is to serve the people wholeheartedly. On the era's demands, they argue that new risks make theoretical confidence more important, and that it requires deeper study of the Party's theory and a clear line against erroneous trends of thought.

The authors conclude that Party members should use Marxism to address China's concrete realities, act as doers in building Chinese modernization, and press on towards the second centenary goal. Read the original if you want a brief example of how Party-school commentary frames the task of popularising official theory after Xi's instruction.
quoteEn: Firm theoretical confidence means guarding against theoretical distortion and political disorientation.
quoteZh: 坚定理论自信就是要防止理论上的失真和政治立场上的迷困

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018. It is presented as the latest stage of adapting Marxism to China.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for the Party's project of combining Marxist theory with Chinese conditions and contemporary developments.
The Party's official term for China's own path of modernization, promoted since the 20th Party Congress (2022) as an alternative to Western models.
Confidence in the correctness of the Party's theoretical system, part of the official 'Four-sphere Confidence'.
The official goal of building a modern socialist country by 2049, the centenary of the People's Republic.

t: Upholding ideological and cultural foundation-building to consolidate absolute loyalty to the Party
zh: 坚持思想文化固本培元筑牢对党绝对忠诚
paras: This commentary, published in Study Times in January 2025, asks how ideological and cultural work can strengthen the absolute loyalty of state security personnel to the Party. Its author, identified as a Party committee member and head of the political department at the Ministry of State Security, argues that holding ideological leadership is the basis of all leadership. On that basis, Nie contends, the Party's absolute leadership over state security organs requires building a staff that is firm, pure and dedicated.

The piece is organised under three headings. The first says why ideological and cultural work must take a clear political stance. The second sets out how political guidance can forge loyalty. The third explains how the work should innovate with the times.

On the first point, Nie gives three reasons: the requirement of the Party's absolute leadership, the study and implementation of Xi Jinping's thought on culture, and the continuation of the 'red bloodline'. Nie asks state security organs to take political loyalty as the first task and to deepen Party history education, drawing on the history of the covert front. On the second, the author proposes four measures: consolidating the theoretical foundation through Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era and the holistic approach to national security; promoting the historical tradition of loyalty; holding up exemplary figures, including ordinary ones; and creating a cultural atmosphere through ceremonies such as flag-raising, oath-taking and awards, and through literary and artistic works on national security themes. On the third, Nie lists five kinds of awareness to be fostered: political, front-line (positions for propaganda and education), audience, quality-product and technological awareness. Audience awareness means tailoring content to leading cadres, young officers and the public. Technological awareness means using new technologies to empower ideological and cultural work.

Nie concludes that ideological and cultural work should be anchored in the Party's cultural leadership and be adjusted to changing conditions. It should also produce what the author calls an 'iron army' of state security personnel with reliable political loyalty. The text is a statement of institutional priorities and working methods rather than an analytical study. Read the original if you want a primary example of how a senior state security official describes ideological education, the 'red' tradition and cultural programmes inside China's security apparatus.
quoteEn: Holding ideological leadership is the basis of holding all leadership.
quoteZh: 掌握思想领导是掌握一切领导的基础。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018. It is presented as the latest stage in adapting Marxism to China.
A phrase for the revolutionary heritage and political character that the Party says it inherits from its history. It is used in Party education to stress continuity with the revolutionary past.
The established Chinese term for intelligence, counter-espionage and state security work. Its history and heroes are used in internal education.
A concept put forward by Xi Jinping in 2014. It treats security as covering many fields, including politics, economy, culture and technology.

t: Improving institutions and mechanisms for cultivating and practising core socialist values
zh: 完善制度机制，培育和践行社会主义核心价值观
paras: This commentary, published in Guangming Daily, takes up the call of the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) to improve the institutions and mechanisms for cultivating and practising core socialist values. Ma and Zhang argue that such values are indispensable to building a strong education nation and to advancing national rejuvenation through Chinese modernization. Their thesis is that the institutional advantage should be turned into a guarantee of value confidence and a driver of high-quality development in education.

The piece has three parts. The first explains why the values matter for building a strong education nation. The second sets out how to embed them in law, social development and daily life. The third proposes mechanisms to make the institutions work over the long term. It is a short policy-oriented essay, not a scholarly study, and draws on Party documents rather than empirical evidence.

On significance, the authors tie the values to three attributes of education. Its political attribute requires the Party's education policy and the fundamental task of fostering virtue through education, so as to produce capable successors. Its people-oriented attribute means education that satisfies the people and serves common prosperity, supported by the spirit of educators and by teachers' ethics. Its strategic attribute links education to science, technology and talent. On institutions, they trace the path from writing the values into the Constitution to the Fourth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2019) and the Third Plenum, and call for them to move from soft moral constraint to hard institutional provision. They also call for integration into public policy, social governance and moral systems, and for education that is lived and daily.

For long-term operation, the authors propose five mechanisms: Party-led organisation and accountability; coordination across departments, with integrated ideological and political education from primary school to university, and cooperation among family, school and society; incentives and sanctions, including negative lists; and an evaluation-and-feedback cycle. They present these as the means of making the institutions effective in practice. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated scholars link value education, law and educational governance in the official discourse after the Third Plenum.
quoteEn: The vitality of an institution lies in its implementation.
quoteZh: 制度的生命力在于执行。

glossary.explanation: A twelve-word official formula promoted since the 18th Party Congress (2012), covering national, social and individual-level values. It is used in education, law and public communication.
The Party's official concept of China's own path to modernization, prominent since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
An official goal of making China a leading country in education, which the Party links to science, technology and talent. It was set out in a plan for 2024–2035.
A Party-endorsed fundamental task of education: cultivating moral character and nurturing people. It is a central principle in official educational policy.
An official goal of prosperity shared by all, which Xi Jinping has stressed as a feature of socialism with Chinese characteristics.
The official guiding idea for development since 2017, emphasising quality and efficiency over growth rate.

t: Advancing the fundamental task of fostering virtue through moral education in the new era with the guiding power of ideological and political education
zh: 以思政引领力推进新时代立德树人工程
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in January 2025, Xia Zhilun, director of the Hunan Provincial Department of Education, takes up the idea of the "guiding power of ideological and political education" that Xi Jinping put forward at the national education conference in September 2024. Xia argues that this power heads the "six powers" of a strong education nation with Chinese characteristics, expresses its political character, and gives the basic guidance for the project of fostering virtue through moral education.

The short commentary has three parts. They treat the guiding power of ideological and political education as setting the direction, strengthening the intellectual engine, and clarifying the value pursuit of that project. Xia illustrates each part with measures taken in Hunan Province.

On direction, Xia holds that the education nation must keep to the socialist orientation of schooling and use Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era to shape students' beliefs. Universities are described as a front line in the ideological sphere, and talent training must produce people who support Party leadership and the socialist system. On ideas, Xia calls for integrating the latest results of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times into the whole training process, so that young people clear away confusion amid competing currents of thought. On values, Xia calls for promoting core socialist values and helping students balance personal and social value.

Xia cites Hunan's upgraded university ideological work programme, provincial leaders teaching ideological and political courses, eight innovation centres, an online "I Am a Successor" classroom, and integrated university-to-primary-school course communities in 14 cities and prefectures. Xia presents these as ways to strengthen young people's ambition, integrity and confidence. Read the original if you want a brief example of how a provincial education official applies the "guiding power" formula to moral education in practice.
quoteEn: We must fix the political character of talent training.
quoteZh: 要标定人才培养的政治属性。

glossary.explanation: The stated fundamental task of Chinese education, meaning that schools should cultivate moral character alongside knowledge and skills. It has been stressed in Party documents on education since the 18th Party Congress (2012).

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The official guiding ideology of the Communist Party of China, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for the Party's continuing effort to fit Marxism to China's conditions and to present-day developments.
A set of twelve values promoted officially since 2012, covering the national, social and individual levels.

glossary.en: guiding power of ideological and political education
glossary.explanation: A term from Xi Jinping's September 2024 speech, naming the first of six capacities of a strong education nation.

t: Core socialist values as a strong value support for advancing Chinese modernization
zh: 社会主义核心价值观为推进中国式现代化提供有力价值支撑
source: China Theory Network (中国理论网), reposted on marxism.cass.cn, 3 January 2025
paras: Taking its cue from the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), which described Chinese modernization as one that coordinates material and spiritual civilization, this commentary asks what role the core socialist values play in reaching the goal of basically realising socialist modernization by 2035. Wang argues that the values provide strong value support for Chinese modernization: they guide it, unite society behind it and express its distinctive value orientation to the world.

The piece is organised in three sections. The first treats the core values as both a product of and a guide for modernization. The second examines how they build consensus among individuals, in social life and in the legal system. The third considers how they reflect the value orientation of Chinese modernization and its claim to universal human significance.

Wang first contends that the values emerged from the Party's practice of modernization, guided by Marxist values and rooted in fine traditional Chinese culture, from the Party's first programme through reform and opening up. Since the new era, Wang says, they have been set as the fundamental value guide at the national, social and individual levels, and they keep modernization on a socialist course. Second, the author proposes that the values be internalised by individuals, embedded in digital space and cultural products, and written into law, citing the 2016 guideline on integrating them into the rule of law, their inclusion in the Constitution and the Civil Code, and Supreme People's Court documents on judicial reasoning.

Wang concludes that the core values are the value core of Chinese modernization and extend scientific socialism in twenty-first-century China. Citing Xi Jinping, the author argues that Chinese modernization breaks the equation of modernization with Westernization and offers a path that does not rely on exploiting or oppressing other nations. On this view both the path and its values surpass Western models and offer a new value direction for humankind. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official Party theory links the core socialist values to the Third Plenum's modernization agenda.”
quoteEn: The core socialist values clarify the value direction of Chinese modernization and ensure that it always advances along a socialist path.
quoteZh: 社会主义核心价值观明确了中国式现代化的价值方向，保证中国式现代化始终沿着社会主义方向前进。

glossary.explanation: The official Party formulation of China's own path to modernization, stressed since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.

A set of 24 characters promoted since the 18th Party Congress (2012): prosperity, democracy, civility and harmony at the national level; freedom, equality, justice and rule of law at the social level; patriotism, dedication, integrity and friendship at the individual level.

t: Consolidating the foundations of belief, conviction and confidence to strengthen the guiding power of ideological and political education
zh: 铸牢信仰信念信心根基 增强思政引领力
paras: This short commentary, published in Guangming Daily on 31 December 2024, asks how ideological and political education can build a strong guiding power as part of making China a leading country in education. Lan and Li argue that this power is an integral part of that goal and a requirement of Party leadership over it. They propose consolidating three foundations among young students: belief, conviction and confidence.

The piece is organised in three sections, each tied to one of these foundations. They are belief in Marxism, described as the soul of guiding power; conviction in socialism with Chinese characteristics, its basis; and confidence in the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, which keeps it on the right course. Each section describes the foundation and then sets out measures for education.

On belief, the authors call for Marxist theory education and Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era to shape students. They also want integrated ideological and political teaching from primary school to university and a "big ideological and political course" pattern. On conviction, they call for sound views of history, nation, state and culture, education in traditional Chinese culture, and stronger theoretical grounding. On confidence, they cite the scale and quality of China's education system. They urge integrated reform of education, science and technology, and talent, and the training of top talent at home, to support Chinese modernization.

Lan and Li conclude that China should keep to its own path of socialist education development. They want this path to deliver strong ideological, political and value guidance to students under the Party's overall leadership. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-aligned academics frame ideological and political education within the education-power agenda.
quoteEn: Building China into a leading country in education is a cherished aspiration of the Chinese nation since modern times.
quoteZh: 建成教育强国是近代以来中华民族梦寐以求的美好愿望

glossary.explanation: A national goal of building China into a world-leading education power, prominent in Party policy from 2023–24.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions, and taught in schools and universities.
The official name for China's path since reform and opening up, combining Party leadership, socialist institutions and a market economy.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal of restoring China's national strength and international standing, closely associated with Xi Jinping.
The Party's official description of China's own path to modernization, set out prominently at the 20th Party Congress (2022).

t: The reasoning and routes for telling China's story well in the era of "everything as media"
zh: “万物皆媒”时代讲好中国故事的理与路
paras: Wang Feng'e takes up a question raised by the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022): how to build Chinese discourse and narrative systems and tell China's story well. The commentary argues that in an era of deep digitalisation, networking and intelligence, when "everything is media", objects have acquired subjectivity, media function and narrative capacity. Wang proposes "object narrative", that is, using things as media to convey reasons, as a more scientific way to tell China's story.

The piece has three parts. The first sets out what should be told: the Chinese path, China's fine traditional culture and Chinese modernization. The second identifies which objects to use: those embodying Chinese civilisation, the Communist Party's spirit of struggle, and the outlook of the Chinese people. The third considers where to tell: on media platforms, in everyday life, and in the experience of foreign visitors.

Wang argues that telling the story of the Chinese path means explaining who development relies on and serves, and how it proceeds, through themes such as the Belt and Road Initiative and a community with a shared future for mankind. Cultural relics, intangible heritage, revolutionary relics, and newer objects such as high-speed rail, mobile payment and shared bicycles are presented as carriers of narrative, valued for their objectivity, immediacy and acceptability. Large models, consumer goods and inbound tourism are described as settings where objects act with people as narrators, so that the story is conveyed almost unnoticed.

Wang concludes that building platforms for object narrative would open routes for exchange between civilisations and create a shared context of mutual understanding. Read the original if you want a short example of how official discourse on international communication is being extended to media theory and material objects.
quoteEn: Let objects as media become part of people's everyday use, so that China's story is told subtly and unconsciously through daily life.
quoteZh: 让作为媒介的“物”，成为世人日常生活的“用”，在日用而不觉中潜移默化讲好中国故事。

glossary.explanation: The article's term for conveying stories and values through material or intangible objects rather than words alone.
The official term for China's path of modernization, which Party documents say differs from Western models and is peaceful and shared by all.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A concept in Xi Jinping's foreign policy discourse, calling for shared development and cooperation in international relations.
A Chinese international infrastructure and economic cooperation programme launched in 2013.

t: Offering the best spiritual nourishment to the people
zh: 把最好的精神食粮奉献给人民
paras: Li Yi, Party secretary and vice-chairman of the China Federation of Literary and Art Circles (CFLAC), writes in Study Times (Xuexi Shibao) that "putting the people first" runs through Xi Jinping Thought on Culture. The article argues that socialist literature and art are in essence the people's literature and art. Literary and art work, and the work of the federation, should therefore take a people-centred orientation and give the people the best spiritual nourishment.

The piece is organised under four headings, each opening with remarks by Xi Jinping. They concern strengthening the people's spiritual strength for national rejuvenation, writing about real life, using the people's evaluation as the highest standard, and cultivating artists who love the people. Li draws on recent works, including television dramas, films and dance dramas, as well as classical literature and world masterpieces. Li also describes CFLAC programmes and plans.

Li argues that culture and art are essential to the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation and to Chinese modernization, which Li describes as the coordination of material and spiritual civilisation. Artists are urged to tell the story of the Party and of the people's struggle. Li holds that good works come from deep immersion in the people's lives, citing CFLAC field trips to Tibetan, Inner Mongolian and Xinjiang areas. Li also holds that lasting classics are those that care about the people's fate. Li says the main contradiction in cultural supply has shifted from "whether there is any" to "whether it is excellent", so quality must be the lifeline of art. The standard is whether the people support, approve and are pleased by a work, with social benefit placed first and united with economic benefit. Artists must be of both moral and artistic merit, sharing the people's joys and worries, and the poet Ai Qing is offered as a model.

Li announces that the CFLAC will carry out the New Era Literary and Art Peak-building Action and the New Era Literary and Art Masterpiece Creation Project. It will also continue the "going deep into life, rooting among the people" practice, and improve talent mechanisms, with attention to young, grassroots and "new" arts workers. Li concludes that all innovation in literature and art ultimately comes from the people, and that artists should celebrate the era and build cultural peaks under Xi Jinping Thought on Culture. Read the original if you want to see how a senior official of the national arts federation presents the Party's people-centred cultural policy and the federation's planned measures.
quoteEn: Socialist literature and art are in essence the people's literature and art; the work of literary and art circles and federations should always keep a people-centred orientation, raise the banner of "the people", show the people as its underlying colour, and offer the best spiritual nourishment to the people.
quoteZh: 社会主义文艺本质上是人民的文艺，文艺文联工作应始终坚持以人民为中心的工作导向，高扬“人民”旗帜，彰显“人民”底色，把最好的精神食粮奉献给人民。

glossary.explanation: The part of Xi Jinping's thought dealing with culture and ideology, formally put forward in October 2023. A study outline for it was later published.
The official term for China's path of development, in which material and cultural-ethical advancement are meant to be coordinated. It has been prominent since the 20th Party Congress (2022).

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's long-term national goal of restoring China's strength and international standing, closely associated with Xi Jinping.

glossary.en: China Federation of Literary and Art Circles (CFLAC)
glossary.literal: China Federation of Literary and Art Circles
glossary.explanation: The national people's organisation of artists and writers' associations, led by the Party. It coordinates the arts sector and its programmes.

glossary.literal: fragrant in both virtue and art
glossary.explanation: A traditional ideal, now used in official cultural policy, that artists should combine moral integrity with artistic excellence.

t: Building a bridge from theory to the masses
zh: 架起理论通向群众的桥梁
paras: This commentary, first published in Study Times, asks how grassroots theory lectures can help ordinary people understand and master the Party's innovative theory and policies. Hu argues that, in the new era, such work must stay close to what the people need and concentrate on mass work. Opening with Xi Jinping's call to popularise and simplify the spread of Marxism, the article treats the people's standpoint as the key to propaganda and ideological work.

The article is organised around four practical areas: content, method, venues and personnel. It closes by urging story-telling about reform and development, linked to the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024).

On content, Hu calls for a "user mindset" and "demand orientation". Big theory should be presented through small topics and local stories, and skills-based talks should be tied to people's livelihoods and production. On method, political language should be turned into everyday speech, using forms such as poetry recitation and clapper talk. Lectures should be tailored to different groups, including farmers, workers, officials and young people, and audiences should take part instead of listening passively. On venues, Hu proposes using the New Era Civilization Practice Centres, streets and squares, Party newspapers and broadcasting, and platforms such as Weibo, WeChat and Douyin. On personnel, the author proposes recruiting ordinary people as lecturers, training them, and building local lecture brands under a "one place, one brand" scheme.

Hu concludes that lively stories from people's own lives make theory persuasive. The author wants lecturers to link such stories to Chinese modernization and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, so that popular strength and wisdom gather behind the Third Plenum's strategic plans. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party media describe practical methods for taking official theory to local communities.
quoteEn: Wherever the people are, the reach of theory lectures must extend there too.
quoteZh: 人民群众在哪里,理论宣讲的触角就要伸向哪里。

glossary.explanation: The Party's official description of China's own path to modernization. It is presented as distinct from Western models and is linked to the goal of national rejuvenation.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central official goal of the Party, associated especially with Xi Jinping. It refers to restoring China's strength and international standing by the mid-twenty-first century.
Local centres set up since 2018 to organise volunteer services and ideological and cultural activities at county, township and village level.

t: Ideological and political work with university students amid digital transformation
zh: 数字化转型中的高校学生思政工作
paras: This short commentary, published in Jiefang Daily on 30 December 2024, describes how Shanghai Jiao Tong University combines its traditional strengths in ideological and political work with information technology. Zhao Xin, the university's director of student affairs, argues that digital tools can make ideological and political education more targeted, more efficient and more attractive to students who grew up online.

The article is organised in four parts: understanding students as "internet natives", building the online skills of the teaching and counselling staff, equipping student work with a "digital toolbox", and returning to real-world campus settings. Each part is illustrated with initiatives at the university.

Zhao reports that the university monitors student opinion through key-stage surveys and analysis of online posts, and runs a studio that decodes internet slang ("meme guide"), which produced over 180 entries in 2024. A student development research institute founded in 2018 and a six-year counsellor training programme reaching over 1,200 trainees are presented as ways to strengthen online education skills. The university has also built self-developed systems, including a "student portrait" data warehouse, a digital "second classroom transcript" and an online service platform. Zhao stresses that digital work is complemented by a new student centre, a 24-hour service hotline, student-led think-tank projects and campus cultural events.

Zhao concludes that "digital ideological and political work" is part of the digital transformation of education and of fostering virtue through education (lì dé shù rén). The university will, in the author's account, apply the new development philosophy and new technologies to raise the Party's guiding capacity in the internet era. Read the original if you want a concrete, practitioner's account of how a leading Chinese university is operationalising digital ideological and political education.
quoteEn: Language is the outward expression of thought.
quoteZh: 语言是思想的外化。

glossary.explanation: The Party-led effort to shape students' values and political outlook, carried out in Chinese universities by counsellors, teachers and administrators alongside academic teaching.
The stated fundamental task of Chinese education: cultivating moral character and political commitment alongside knowledge and skills.
The official framework, introduced in 2015, of innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development.
University staff responsible for students' daily affairs and ideological guidance, a core part of the ideological and political work team.

t: Bringing the value of the "Two Roads" spirit to bear on forging a strong sense of community for the Chinese nation
zh: 发挥“两路”精神在铸牢中华民族共同体意识中的价值
paras: This short commentary asks how the "Two Roads" spirit, which arose in building the Sichuan–Tibet and Qinghai–Tibet highways, can serve the effort to forge a strong sense of community for the Chinese nation. Zhou and Chen argue that the spirit, formed through the shared struggle of People's Liberation Army soldiers and people of all ethnic groups, is a high-quality spiritual resource. In their view it makes the work of forging that sense of community vivid and close to ordinary people.

The authors first present the "Two Roads" spirit as a historical witness to the Party, the people and the army holding firm to revolutionary faith and revolutionary optimism under harsh conditions. They then set out three ways of putting it to use: spiritual guidance, education through cases, and widening the carriers and channels of dissemination.

On spiritual guidance, the article cites Xi Jinping's summary of the spirit and the figures it gives for the road-building: 110,000 Tibetan and Han builders, over 30 million cubic metres of earth and rock, more than 400 bridges and some 3,000 deaths. It argues that these deeds can deepen the content of ethnic unity. On cases, it points to sites left by the 18th Army along the Sichuan–Tibet route, such as cave dwellings, martyrs' tombs, slogans and songs, as teaching material. For wider channels, it proposes a case library, staged "Two Roads" stories, art and music, paper-cuts, pottery, songs and cultural-tourism products.

The authors conclude that fitting the spirit into this work strengthens ethnic identity, reinforces shared red memories and unites people of all ethnic groups. Their proposals are practical: collect and systematise case material, then spread it through varied cultural forms so that it takes hold in people's minds and hearts. Read the original if you want a brief example of how Chinese ethnic-unity education draws on revolutionary-era heritage and local historical sites.
quoteEn: Combining the "Two Roads" spirit with the work of forging a strong sense of community for the Chinese nation can better bring out the spirit's guiding role in that work.
quoteZh: 将“两路”精神与铸牢中华民族共同体意识相结合，可以更好地发挥“两路”精神在铸牢中华民族共同体意识中的精神引领作用

glossary.explanation: A spirit attributed to the builders of the Sichuan–Tibet and Qinghai–Tibet highways in the 1950s. Xi Jinping summarised it in 2014 as fearing neither hardship nor death, tenacity and willingness to be a paving stone, and unity between army and people and among ethnic groups.

t: Improving the Party's capacity and level in leading the building of a leading country in education
zh: 提高党领导教育强国建设的能力和水平
paras: Zhang Haishui and Guo Guoxiang take up the question of how Party members and officials can lead the building of a leading country in education more effectively. They argue that Party leadership is the fundamental guarantee for educational work. At this critical stage, in their view, cadres must continually raise their political awareness, strategic vision and professional competence, so that educational construction becomes a firm base for upholding Party leadership.

The short commentary, which opens with remarks by Xi Jinping on officials respecting and studying education, is organised around six requirements for cadres. These are holding the ideological and political guidance position, putting the people at the centre, grasping the laws of education, coordinating education with science and technology and talent strategies, applying systems thinking, and adapting measures to local conditions. Each section pairs a directive from Xi Jinping with practical tasks for officials.

The authors give first place to ideological and political guidance, the first of the "six forces" Xi Jinping set out at the national education conference. They present it as the political attribute of education and as the force that strengthens the other five: talent competitiveness, scientific support, livelihood security, social coordination and international influence. On the people-centred requirement, they call for a mass-line approach, for policy attention tilted towards disadvantaged groups, and for narrowing gaps between urban and rural areas and between schools. They also hold that the more accurately the Party understands educational laws, the more education prospers, and they say officials should learn through dialogue with teachers. The three-in-one layout of education, science and technology, and talent from the 20th Party Congress (2022) is described as resting on talent cultivation and serving new quality productive forces. Higher, vocational and basic education are each assigned specific tasks.

The authors call for systems thinking that combines school funding, teaching staff and facilities with the cooperation of families, communities and government departments. They also call for local adaptation, citing the large population scale of Chinese modernization as a reason to avoid uniform targets and to set separate paths for provinces, cities and counties. They further urge evaluation systems and law-based school governance, and policy that turns "public consensus" into public benefit. Read the original if you want a compact example of how Party-theory writing links Xi Jinping's education directives to concrete expectations of cadres.
quoteEn: Education is a science, and a scientific grasp and understanding of the laws of education, of teaching and of the growth of talent is one of the key factors determining how effectively education performs its functions.
quoteZh: 教育是一门科学，对教育规律、教学规律以及人才成长规律的科学把握与认识，是决定教育功能成效发挥的关键因素之一。

glossary.explanation: A national goal promoted in Party documents and by Xi Jinping, notably at the national education conference in September 2024. It envisages China becoming a world leader in education.
The official term for China's development path as presented by the Party since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It stresses features such as a huge population and common prosperity.
A concept introduced by Xi Jinping in 2023 for advanced productivity driven by technological innovation and emerging industries.

The first of the "six forces" of a leading education country in Xi Jinping's 2024 formulation. It refers to the capacity of ideological and political education to steer students' values and political orientation.

t: Integrating integrity culture and teachers' ideological and political work in universities in the new era: significance, principles and methods
zh: 新时代高校廉洁文化与教师思想政治工作一体化建设的意义、原则与方法
paras: Taking its cue from the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), which called for strengthening integrity culture in the new era, this short commentary asks how universities can fold ideological and political work with teachers into campus integrity-culture building. The authors argue that the two should be developed as one integrated effort, starting from teachers' own conduct, so that Party conduct, teachers' ethics and the study atmosphere reinforce one another.

The piece has three parts. It first sets out why teachers' ideological and political work matters for integrity culture, then states four principles for the integrated approach, and finally lists four working methods. It opens by citing Xi Jinping on putting teachers' ethics first and by invoking Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era as guidance.

On significance, the authors list five contributions: correct value orientation and firm communist ideals, better professional ethics, teachers as role models of academic integrity, stronger belonging to the university and its Party committee, and more exchange among teachers about integrity. The four principles are adherence to Party spirit, tailoring work to the individual, equal care, and thoroughness, with the last drawing on the Party's self-reform. The four methods are teaching by example, being serious yet patient, combining outside guidance with self-education, and uniting firmness with warmth.

The authors conclude that teachers are the foundation of education and so must be the starting point for integrity culture. They call for organic fusion of the two fields, which would enrich theory and practice and support high-quality development of university integrity culture. Read the original if you want a concise example of how university discipline-inspection and Party-education staff frame integrity education as part of teachers' ideological work.
quoteEn: Any outside preaching, if it is not accepted by its target, cannot be turned into an inner cognitive motivation.
quoteZh: 任何外在的说教，如果不为对象接受，就不能转化为内在的认知动力。

glossary.explanation: A phrase in Party discourse for the Party's continuous effort to correct its own errors and enforce discipline. It is often used to justify internal anti-corruption and education campaigns.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The official guiding ideology of the Communist Party of China, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.
An official term for a culture of probity and anti-corruption promoted in Party organs, schools and society, combining Party discipline with traditional Chinese ethical values.

t: A heart devoted to the nation: Wu Yuzhang's life in education
zh: 才为国寸心丹——吴玉章的教育人生
paras: This biographical essay, published in Guangming Daily on 30 December 2024, portrays Wu Yuzhang (1878–1966) as a revolutionary who treated education as part of revolution and national construction rather than as an abstract route to national salvation. The authors, Geng Huamin and Liu Gaoyuan, present him as a "red educator" whose work ran from the work-study movement in France to Yan'an and then to the founding of new higher education in the People's Republic.

The article follows Wu's career chronologically and thematically under four headings. It covers his role as a practical organiser of education, his ideas on training all-round new people, his insistence on linking teaching with practice, and his views on teachers and on family education. Evidence comes from his speeches, essays and school policies at Chengdu Higher Normal School, Yan'an University, North China University, Renmin University of China, the Chinese script reform committee and the Central Institute of Socialism.

The authors argue that Wu's educational thought rested on historical materialism and a people's standpoint. He backed study abroad, literacy campaigns and script reform, and, as the first president of Renmin University of China, aimed to train "tens of thousands of construction cadres". He required political theory courses to take 20–30 per cent of teaching hours, and held that political and professional training must go together. He opposed teaching cut off from practice and demanded that "educators must first be educated". He also supported free academic debate under the Hundred Flowers policy, citing his invitation to historians with differing views on periodizing ancient Chinese history. In family education he advocated "strictness combined with love", drawing on his grandmother's and father's example and on letters to his grandchildren.

The authors conclude that nurturing red educational traditions and training people for the Party and the country was Wu's greatest achievement, citing Mao Zedong's 1940 tribute to his lifelong service. They state that his educational ideas and his experience in building new higher education remain a valuable asset for the Party's leadership of education in the new era. Read the original if you want a detailed, officially framed account of Wu Yuzhang's educational practice, from Yan'an schooling to early Renmin University, and of how it is presented today.
quoteEn: Wu Yuzhang held that "the question of which road young people take is a major one bearing on the rise and fall of the nation and the success or failure of the revolution", and made firm ideals and convictions the first task of running schools and educating people.
quoteZh: 吴玉章认为，“青年人走什么道路的问题，是关系国家兴亡和革命成败的大问题”，将坚定理想信念作为办学育人的第一要务。

glossary.explanation: An early twentieth-century movement in which Chinese students, notably in France, combined paid labour with study. Many later leading Communists took part.
Efforts to simplify Chinese characters and introduce alphabetic writing, which led to the Scheme for Simplifying Chinese Characters and the Hanyu Pinyin scheme in the PRC.

glossary.literal: let a hundred flowers bloom, a hundred schools contend
glossary.explanation: A mid-1950s policy slogan promoted by Mao Zedong that encouraged open debate in the arts and sciences under Marxist guidance.

t: Building a new ecosystem for fostering virtue and cultivating talent in the digital-intelligence era
zh: 打造数智时代立德树人新生态
paras: This newspaper commentary, first published in Jiefang Daily in December 2024, asks how education can be rebuilt around the fundamental task of fostering virtue and cultivating talent now that artificial intelligence and big data have entered schooling. Zhu and Wang argue that digitalisation of education is more than a technical upgrade. In their view it requires deeper change in educational ideas and models, and a new educational ecosystem suited to the era.

The piece begins from Xi Jinping's statement that educational digitalisation is a key breakthrough for opening a new track in education. It then sets out three parts: the basic principles of the new ecosystem, the paths for implementing it, and the safeguards needed to sustain it.

On principles, the authors call for correct value orientation, since intelligent technology is a double-edged sword that can bring privacy leaks and ethical problems. They also call for the all-round development of students, with teaching shifting from a teacher–student pair to a teacher–machine–student pattern. Finally, they stress education's strategic character in supporting national competitiveness. On implementation, they propose smart learning environments, integrated digital resources, personalised teaching through learning analytics and adaptive systems, and evaluation that covers creativity, cooperation and moral qualities through peer, self and process-based assessment.

For safeguards, Zhu and Wang urge improved institutions, including quality monitoring and teacher development, and a high-calibre teaching force with ongoing training in digital and intelligent technologies. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how Chinese education officials frame AI-enabled teaching within the goal of fostering virtue and cultivating talent.
quoteEn: Only by placing students at the centre of the educational ecosystem can innovation in content, teaching methods and evaluation truly meet students' developmental needs, unlock their potential and cultivate the key abilities to adapt to future society.
quoteZh: 只有将学生置于教育生态系统的中心,才能确保教育内容、教学方法和评价体系的创新真正满足学生的成长需求,激发他们的潜能,培养他们适应未来社会的关键能力。

glossary.explanation: The fundamental task of Chinese education as stated in Party documents since the 18th Party Congress (2012): moral and ideological formation alongside academic training.

t: Practical exploration of an all-round online education system
zh: 全方位网络育人体系的实践探索
paras: Writing in Jiefang Daily on 27 December 2024, Zhang Yinshuang, a deputy head of the Party Committee's student affairs department at Shanghai Lixin University of Accounting and Finance, asks how universities can use digital technology for ideological and political education. Zhang argues that integrating digital tools with this work is both a task of the times and a key lever for building a new ecosystem of ideological and political education. The article presents the university's Yiban platform as a practical example.

The piece opens with Xi Jinping's call to raise online education capacity and with the Minister of Education's January 2024 pledge to promote AI-enabled education. It then describes Yiban, a national online community for Chinese universities, and the Lixin Yiban development centre set up in 2012. The case is organised under three headings: top-level design and institutions, content and brands, and personnel and organisational support.

Zhang reports that the university adopted a "1+X" institutional framework and a school-and-college co-building model. A leading group chaired by the Party secretary includes 18 units, and Yiban work is part of the assessment of colleges and counsellors. On content, Zhang cites nine Yiban spaces, an online pre-enrolment space for new students and an annual class competition. According to Zhang, new-student registration exceeds 98%, and the competition has run for 12 years and now draws about 800 classes from nearly 30 Shanghai universities. A four-tier management system, training programmes, 22 Yiban teacher studios and 56 online culture projects are said to involve nearly 10,000 teachers and students.

Zhang concludes that sustained institution-building and team development have produced an all-round online education system that has improved the relevance and effectiveness of ideological and political education. Read the original if you want a short, official-style example of how a Chinese university reports on implementing the "three-wide education" approach through an online platform.
quoteEn: Only a high-calibre, professional team of ideological and political workers can ensure that the goals of online education are achieved.
quoteZh: 只有高素质、专业化的思政工作队伍才能确保网络育人目标的落实。

glossary.literal: education by all personnel, throughout the whole process, in all respects
glossary.explanation: A policy framework in Chinese higher education that calls for all staff, all stages of study and all areas of university life to take part in moral and ideological education.

A national online interactive community for Chinese university students that combines teaching, campus services, culture and ideological education. It is promoted by the education authorities as a platform for online education.
The system of education in Chinese schools and universities that conveys Party-endorsed ideology, values and political stances to students.

t: Grasping the key links in using digital-intelligence technology to empower ideological and political theory courses in universities
zh: 把握数智技术赋能高校思政课建设的关键环节
paras: This short commentary, first published in Jiefang Daily on 27 December 2024, asks how universities should use digital-intelligence technology (big data, cloud computing, artificial intelligence) in their ideological and political theory courses. Liu Jingwei argues that the technology brings both opportunities and challenges, and that course development must seize four key links to raise quality.

The piece opens by citing Xi Jinping's call to fuse the traditional strengths of ideological and political work with information technology. It then sets out four numbered points: grasping the direction of technological development, guarding against technology-centrism, innovating the carriers of course delivery, and promoting collaborative education through the "big ideological and political course".

Liu holds that teachers should learn and apply new technologies, since algorithms, computing power and data analysis can support every stage of teaching. The author also warns against "technology-centrism": some students rely on AI to obtain answers, plagiarise or cheat, which Liu says turns AI into a stumbling block for independent thinking and leaves students in an "information cocoon". Over-reliance, Liu argues, neglects value formation, humanistic care and ethics. On the positive side, Liu proposes online resource libraries, micro-courses, MOOCs, blended teaching, virtual teaching assistants and smart classrooms, and says these make teacher–student relations more equal.

Liu concludes that the big ideological and political course should link real and virtual settings, classroom and extracurricular activity, and school and society, for example through online venues and bases. Students should use digital tools to record and share their practical experience, so that self-education extends the courses' social effect. Read the original if you want a brief example of how a Party-school-style university Marxism dean frames AI in political education.
quoteEn: Technology is not a "master key"; one must move beyond "technology-centrism", because over-reliance on technology leads to neglect of other important factors in ideological and political education, such as value formation, emotional and humanistic care, and morality and ethics.
quoteZh: 技术并不是把“万能钥匙”，要走出“唯技术论”，过度依赖技术会导致忽视思政教育的其他重要因素，如价值观塑造、情感人文关怀、道德伦理等。

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses in Marxism, Party theory and moral and legal education taught in all Chinese universities. They are often abbreviated as 思政课.
A term for the view that technology alone can solve problems, so that other factors are neglected. The author uses it as a mistake to be avoided.
A policy idea, promoted since about 2021, that political education should extend beyond the classroom to society, practice and online spaces, with many actors taking part.

t: Integrating digital and intelligent technology to open new paths for Communist Youth League online ideological and political work in universities
zh: 数智融合助推高校共青团网络思政新作为
paras: Writing in Jiefang Daily in December 2024, Luan asks how university Communist Youth League organisations can use digital and intelligent technologies in online ideological and political education. The commentary argues that integrating big data, cloud computing and AI lets the League profile young people accurately, target its education and services, and evaluate results more scientifically.

The piece opens by noting that cyberspace is now students' main channel for information and expression, and cites Xi Jinping's call at the National Education Conference to expand spaces for online education and to implement the national education digitalization strategy. It then sets out three areas of benefit: accurate profiling, service innovation and improved evaluation.

On profiling, Luan says analysis of students' behaviour, interests and social-media sentiment moves education from "flood irrigation" to "precision drip irrigation". It supports targeted activities, immersive VR and AR experiences and personalised content push. On services, the author describes "digital-intelligent" platforms that use machine learning to recommend career guidance and AI-based counselling offering 24-hour support. On evaluation, algorithms mine interaction records and feedback texts to monitor activities in real time and show which content works.

Luan concludes that these technologies make the League's work more precise, better matched to youth needs and more forward-looking. The article stays at the level of general examples and gives no data or case evidence. Read the original if you want a short example of how Youth League cadres frame AI and big data in university ideological education.
quoteEn: The deep integration of digital and intelligent technologies provides strong support for precision education.
quoteZh: 数智技术的深度融合为精准育人提供了强有力的支撑。

glossary.explanation: The Party's mass organisation for young people, roughly ages 14 to 28. Its university branches run political education and student services.
Ideological and political education carried out through internet platforms and social media, mainly aimed at university students.

t: How ideological and political large models innovate on traditional ideological and political education
zh: 思政大模型对传统思政教育的创新突破
paras: This short commentary, published in Jiefang Daily in December 2024, asks how large AI models built for ideological and political education can move beyond traditional methods. Meng argues that such models, as a university-level application of generative AI, change the settings of ideological and political education. In Meng's view they push it from networked to intelligent forms, and integrating AI with the field is both inevitable and necessary for high-quality development.

The article opens with the arrival of ChatGPT-style generative AI and the Ministry of Education's digital education strategy. It then treats the model under three headings. It is a mirror of offline space that builds a data engine, an extension of offline space that opens new forms, and an interactive presence that builds consensus. Throughout, it uses one example, the virtual assistant "AI Xiao Xin" at Shanghai Lixin University of Accounting and Finance.

Meng contends that the models turn data on students' learning, social ties and thinking into behavioural insight. In this account they rebuild the discourse logic of the field and move it away from one-way indoctrination. "AI Xiao Xin" is described as a virtual companion for study, daily life and emotional support. It offers course guidance, emotion sensing and early warning, and delivers digital products that carry mainstream values. Student-affairs staff can also configure quantified, multi-dimensional evaluations to spot problems in education management.

Meng concludes that digital and intelligent empowerment should make the service more experiential and intelligent, and its functions more valuable and timely. Its resources should become more interactive and effective, so that ideological and political education in universities gains depth and quality. The article offers no critical discussion of risks. Read the original if you want a concise, practice-based Chinese view of how AI tools are being introduced into university ideological and political education.
quoteEn: The integration of artificial intelligence with ideological and political education is already the general trend, and has become an inevitable requirement for the high-quality development of ideological and political education.
quoteZh: 人工智能与思想政治教育的融合已然是大势所趋，成为思想政治教育高质量发展的必然要求。

glossary.explanation: The system of teaching in Chinese schools and universities meant to shape students' political outlook, values and moral character in line with Party-state goals.
An official slogan, prominent since the late 2010s, that stresses quality, innovation and efficiency over speed of growth. Here it is applied to the education field.

t: Cultivating young people with a "Chinese heart" through education in ideals and convictions
zh: 以理想信念教育培养有“中国心”的时代青年
paras: Opening with Zhang Boling's three questions to Nankai University students in 1935 (are you Chinese, do you love China, do you want China to do well), the authors ask what it means for young people to have a "Chinese heart" today. They define it as identifying as Chinese, loving socialism and committing to the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Their thesis is that education in ideals and convictions is the way to cultivate such young people.

This short commentary rests on Xi Jinping's statement that patriotism must be united with love for the Party and socialism. It sets out three tasks of ideals-and-convictions education, each tied to one dimension of the "Chinese heart": identity, pride and action. It closes with a quotation from Li Dazhao and a statement about the task's national significance.

First, the authors call for systematic education in the "five histories" to pass on historical memory and the Party's revolutionary heritage. They argue that today's youth have not lived through national peril and so lack a lived sense of red beliefs, which calls for fresh material and vivid storytelling. Second, they propose strengthening the Four-sphere Confidence, describing Chinese youth as a generation that "looks at the world on equal terms". This education should use the "big ideological and political course" approach and a youth-oriented discourse. Third, they urge that personal and family dreams be merged into the Chinese Dream, with the unity of knowing, feeling, willing and acting. Marxist theory is to help young people judge social trends and career choices.

The authors conclude that cultivating young people with a "Chinese heart" is a fundamental task for building a strong education system and for the fate of the Party and country. They call it a matter of "great national importance". They place it against a background of what they call great changes unseen in a century. Read the original if you want a concise example of how current Party-school discourse frames patriotic and ideological education for youth.
quoteEn: To cultivate young people with a "Chinese heart", we must strengthen systematic education in the history of the Party, the history of New China, the history of reform and opening up, the history of socialist development and the history of the Chinese nation.
quoteZh: 培养有“中国心”的时代青年要加强党史、新中国史、改革开放史、社会主义发展史、中华民族发展史的系统教育

glossary.explanation: Official formula calling for confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics.
Education in the history of the Party, of New China, of reform and opening up, of socialist development and of the Chinese nation.
Slogan promoted by Xi Jinping from 2012, centred on national rejuvenation and national prosperity.
Official goal of restoring China's national strength and international standing, central to Party discourse.
Education policy approach that extends ideological and political teaching beyond the classroom into society and daily life.

t: Accelerating the construction of Chinese discourse and Chinese narrative systems
zh: 加快构建中国话语和中国叙事体系
paras: This commentary, first published in Guangming Daily on 29 November 2024, responds to the call of the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) to build Chinese discourse and narrative systems and raise the effectiveness of international communication. The authors argue that discourse (the tool that carries information) and narrative (the structure that engages audiences) are decisive for that effectiveness, which they define as persuasiveness, emotional appeal and cultural resonance as well as speed and reach.

The piece first defines discourse, narrative and "system", then sets out two construction tasks: innovating the discourse system and innovating the narrative system. It closes by describing the work as a long-term systematic project requiring coordination among many actors.

On discourse, the authors divide the system into three layers: ideological values at the core, theoretical knowledge as support, and forms of expression as the outward face. They call for drawing on the essence of Chinese culture, generating original theories and concepts, including an autonomous body of knowledge for Chinese journalism studies, and using accessible, targeted language. On narrative, they propose four dimensions: "development" (national-level stories, framed by a community with a shared future for mankind), "voicing" (authoritative responses to contested issues, moving from one-way output to interactive dialogue), "promotion" (traditional and regional culture, with strategies adapted to high- and low-context cultures) and "discovery" (everyday human stories that join individual and national narratives and, in their view, let emotion cross ideological divides).

The authors conclude that practice-based, focused innovation in both discourse and narrative should give Chinese voices lasting vitality in global opinion and open a new chapter for international communication. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how Chinese communication scholars translate the Plenum's directive into a framework for external messaging.
quoteEn: Building Chinese discourse and Chinese narrative systems is not a campaign in a single field, nor something achieved at one stroke, but a systematic project requiring multi-party coordination and sustained effort.
quoteZh: 构建中国话语和中国叙事体系，不是一域之役，也非一蹴而就，而是多方协同、久久为功的系统工程。

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept associated with Xi Jinping since the early 2010s, describing a vision of shared global development and governance. Here it serves as the core framework for China's global narrative.
The Third Plenum's term for how well China's external communication achieves its aims. The authors read it as covering persuasiveness and cultural resonance as well as reach.
A structured set of concepts, terms and modes of expression through which a country presents its ideas. Chinese policy writing treats it as tied to "discourse power" in international opinion.

t: Turning the educator's spirit into conscious thought and conscious action
zh: 将教育家精神转化为思想自觉、行动自觉
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in December 2024, Shi Xu asks how teachers can make the "educator's spirit" (jiaoyujia jingshen) their own. Shi argues that teachers should turn it into conscious thought and conscious action. The commentary takes its cue from Xi Jinping's call to implement an action plan that uses the educator's spirit to forge teachers' ideals and strengthen the teaching force.

Shi presents the educator's spirit as distinctively Chinese. In the author's account it draws on Marxist theory, the Party's spiritual lineage, traditional teacher-culture and a century of Chinese education. It has six elements: ideals and convictions, moral sentiment, wisdom in educating, a diligent working attitude, a loving heart, and the pursuit of the Way. The article is organised around four exhortations to teachers: keep the nation and the world in mind, hold fast to the lectern, pursue truth and wisdom, and cultivate benevolent love.

The first two exhortations tie teaching to national goals. Shi says students are the main force for the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, so teachers must raise a new generation who love the country and shoulder that task. Shi holds up the two "People's Educators" honoured in September 2024, Zhang Jinfan and Huang Danian, as examples of devotion to teaching. The remaining two exhortations concern conduct. Teachers should be lifelong learners, and Shi links diligent learning and putting it into practice to the Marxist view that truth is tested in practice. They should also care for each student, build trust, and attend to students' mental health.

Shi concludes that teachers must carry the educator's spirit into daily practice in order to take up the task of nurturing a new generation. The piece is a short, exhortatory statement in the register of Party-led education policy. Read the original if you want a concise example of how the educator's spirit is presented to Chinese teachers and school leaders.
quoteEn: The teacher's main duty is to impart knowledge and, beyond that, to "teach people to seek truth", which requires teachers to be truth-seeking and down-to-earth, and to become models in the pursuit of truth and wisdom.
quoteZh: 教师的主要职责是传授知识，进而“教人求真”，这就要求教师求真求实，成为追求真理智慧的榜样。

glossary.explanation: A formulation put forward by Xi Jinping in 2023 that sets out six qualities expected of teachers. Official texts present it as a guide for building the teaching force.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
