On content, they go through the seven focuses: a high-standard socialist market economy, whole-process people's democracy, a socialist cultural powerhouse, better living standards and a higher-level safe China, a beautiful China, and stronger Party leadership and governing capacity. Each is tied to a guiding body of thought, such as Xi Jinping's economic thought or his thought on culture, and to the aim of building students' confidence in China's path. On method, the authors propose four orientations: problem-oriented, hot-topic-oriented, discipline-oriented and technology-oriented integration. They suggest starting from students' doubts about China and the world, using current events, linking the plenum to students' majors, and using virtual practice platforms and digital teaching resources.

The authors conclude that sustained, targeted and innovative integration will let students grasp the plenum's theoretical and practical significance for Chinese modernization. They present this as part of raising the quality of ideological and political courses and of cultivating a generation able to build a strong country. Read the original if you want a concise example of how the Party's latest documents are translated into teaching content and methods in Chinese universities.
quoteEn: The plenum report is not only a political text but also an ideological and political education text, rich in the Marxist appeal of truth, of practice and of character.
quoteZh: 全会报告不仅是政治文本，也是思想政治教育文本，富有马克思主义的真理魅力、实践魅力和品格魅力。

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses in Marxist theory, Party doctrine and political education taught at Chinese schools and universities.

A concept put forward by Xi Jinping to describe China's democratic model as covering every stage of political and policy processes. Official sources present it as distinct from Western electoral democracy.
The official term for China's path of modernization under Party leadership, presented as having distinctive Chinese features.
An official goal of building China's cultural strength and influence under Marxist guidance, with emphasis on traditional, revolutionary and socialist culture.
An official slogan for ecological civilization, meaning environmental protection and harmony between humans and nature.

t: Advancing "green education" practice in universities through the ecological civilization concepts of the new era
zh: 新时代生态文明理念推进高校绿色育人实践
source: China Social Sciences Today (via marxism.cass.cn), 20 December 2024
paras: This short commentary in the China Social Sciences Today argues that universities should build the concepts of ecological civilization drawn from Xi Jinping's thought on ecological civilization into their "green education" (lüse yuren) practice. Nie holds that this is both a core part of the fundamental task of fostering virtue through education and a practical requirement of Chinese modernization, understood as the harmonious coexistence of humanity and nature.

The article first sets out four concepts it finds in Xi Jinping's ecological thought, then gives two reasons why green education matters, and ends with three institutional measures. It draws on official formulations such as the new development philosophy and the Fifth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee's call for coordinated education by schools, families and society.

Nie reads the concepts as a unity of four kinds of outlook: harmonious coexistence of humanity and nature as a value; \"lucid waters and lush mountains are invaluable assets\" as a mode of thinking that rejects opposing economic growth to ecological protection; respecting, accommodating and protecting nature as a view of nature; and green development as a view of development. Green education is presented as a strategic task of ecological civilization and as a response to the changed principal contradiction, in which people's needs now include a good ecological environment. University students are described as audience, communicators and practitioners of these ideas. The proposed mechanisms are an ecological civilization education system, a systematic working mechanism and a collaborative operating mechanism. The working mechanism covers teaching staff, a new curriculum and closer integration with ideological and political theory courses. The cited example is a student social practice project on ecological conditions led by college Youth League committees.

Nie concludes that Xi Jinping Thought should guide the whole process of green education, so that students internalise ecological values and act on them, and so that their sense of historic mission grows. Read the original if you want a brief example of how ideological and political education in Chinese universities is being linked to ecological civilization policy.
quoteEn: Green education practice in universities is a highly complex systematic undertaking.
quoteZh: 高校绿色育人实践是一项高度复杂的系统工程。

glossary.literal: green cultivation of people in universities
glossary.explanation: A term for incorporating ecological values and ecological civilization education into university teaching and student development.
The official name for China's path of modernization, which Party documents describe as including the harmonious coexistence of humanity and nature.
The stated fundamental task of Chinese education: moral and political formation alongside knowledge.

glossary.en: Xi Jinping's thought on ecological civilization
glossary.explanation: The body of ideas on environmental protection and development attributed to Xi Jinping, including the formula that lucid waters and lush mountains are invaluable assets.
An official framework, introduced in 2015, of innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development.

t: The fundamental guidance for making ideological and political courses "explain principles in depth, thoroughly and vividly"
zh: 思政课“把道理讲深讲透讲活”的根本遵循
source: China Social Sciences Network, posted 20 December 2024
paras: Wang Rangxin takes up Xi Jinping's instruction that ideological and political theory courses ("sizheng ke") in schools must "explain principles in depth, thoroughly and vividly" in the new era and on the new journey. The article asks how this can be done and answers that Xi's own instruction supplies the fundamental guidance. This has three parts: keep Marxism as the guiding ideology, use the achievements of socialism with Chinese characteristics as the substance of teaching, and use fine traditional Chinese culture, revolutionary culture and advanced socialist culture as the foundation of strength.

The piece is organised around these three requirements. Wang opens by arguing that the political character and ideological function of the courses are their essence. The article then treats the content of teaching: which achievements to cover, and how to teach them. The last section takes the three cultural sources in turn, with suggestions for classroom and extracurricular practice.

On Marxism, Wang argues that teachers need firm belief, so that conviction and affection reach students. Teachers must also apply the Marxist worldview and methodology, which Wang says lifts a \"principle\" to theory, philosophy and fundamental principle. The courses should show Marxism's scientific, popular, practical and developing character. On content, Wang says teachers must set out the Party's history of more than a century. This includes the successive \"great leaps\", the four solemn declarations to the world, and the historic achievements since the 18th Party Congress (2012). Methods proposed are using society as a \"big classroom\", immersive and technology-assisted experience, and inviting ordinary people, model Party members and descendants of martyrs into the classroom. On culture, Wang says fine traditional culture is the root, with its fit with Marxism. Revolutionary culture, carried by the Great Spirit of Party founding and later revolutionary spirits, is the \"source of strength\". Advanced socialist culture, centred on core socialist values, is said to be inclusive and forward-leading.

Wang concludes that grounding the courses in practice, as material force, and in culture, as spiritual force, will make their principles credible, respected and lovable. The article proposes teaching bases, supplementary materials, film archives, touring talks by model figures and exhibitions of achievements. It also proposes both explicit and subtle (\"moistening things silently\") ways of shaping students' emotional belief. Read the original if you want a Party-line account of how Xi's guidance on ideological and political courses is turned into teaching content and methods.
quoteEn: The principles taught in ideological and political courses are not preaching, nor a movement from concept to concept; they are rooted in living practice and have great vitality.
quoteZh: 思政课的道理不是说教，不是从概念到概念，而是扎根于活生生的实践，具有强大的生命力。

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses in Marxism, Party history and socialist values taught at all levels of Chinese schools and universities. Xi Jinping has repeatedly stressed their importance for educating younger generations.
The official name for China's path, system and theory of socialism since the reform era. It is presented by the Party as the application of Marxism to Chinese conditions.

The official term for the culture formed during the Party-led revolution, including the spirits of Jinggangshan, the Long March and Yan'an. It is one of three cultural sources, with fine traditional culture and advanced socialist culture, that Party discourse emphasises.
A twenty-four-character set of values, at national, social and individual levels, promoted by the Party since the 18th Party Congress (2012).

t: Advancing the development of ideological and political courses in step with arming minds with the Party's innovative theory
zh: 坚持思政课建设与党的创新理论武装同步推进
paras: Luo Xianyu and Liu Yuan take up Xi Jinping's instruction that the development of ideological and political courses (sizheng ke) in schools must advance in step with arming minds with the Party's innovative theory. They argue that this instruction shows why such courses need to unite political orientation with scholarly rigour. In their view it supplies theoretical guidance and a method for opening a new phase of ideological and political education in the new era.

The short commentary begins by noting what has changed since the 18th Party Congress (2012): the courses' higher standing in the Party's overall strategy, a larger teaching corps, new teaching methods and the use of information technology. It then points to new pressures, namely the impact of diverse social currents of thought and new problematic behaviour among young students in class. The main body is organised around five "connections": textbooks, curriculum, teaching, teaching staff and digital resources.

The authors' central move is to treat political and scholarly strength as inseparable. On textbooks, they call for a system centred on Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, with the latest theory brought in promptly and integrated across primary, secondary and university levels, plus supporting teaching guides and curriculum standards. On curriculum and teaching, they urge staged content that avoids "disconnection and inversion", closer alignment between ideological-political courses and "ideological and political education across all courses", and a shift from academic to teaching language. Teaching should answer the questions of whom to train, how and for whom, combining the teacher's leading role with the student's initiative.

On staff and technology, Luo and Liu propose a well-trained corps combining full-time and part-time teachers, including Party and university leaders, and a mechanism linking school, family and society into a "grand ideological and political education" pattern. They also call for digital resource platforms, online channels and immersive VR and AR teaching built on red cultural resources. The authors conclude that these five connections, advanced together, would raise the effectiveness of the courses and fulfil the fundamental task of fostering virtue through education. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-school scholars translate Xi Jinping's directives on ideological and political courses into practical measures for textbooks, curriculum, staffing and digital teaching.
quoteEn: The essence of ideological and political courses is reasoning, so attention must be paid to method, explaining the reasoning in depth, thoroughly and vividly.
quoteZh: 思政课的本质是讲道理，要注重方式方法，把道理讲深、讲透、讲活。

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses in Marxist theory, Party doctrine and moral-political education taught from primary school to university in China.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018 and made the core content of ideological and political teaching.

glossary.en: ideological and political education across all courses
glossary.explanation: The policy of embedding ideological and political content in all subjects, not only in dedicated ideological and political courses.
A concept promoted in recent years that extends ideological and political teaching beyond the classroom into society, practice and online spaces.
The stated fundamental task of Chinese education: cultivating moral character alongside knowledge.

t: Empowering the construction of the "Big Ideological and Political Course" in universities through digitalisation
zh: 以数字化赋能高校“大思政课”建设
paras: This short commentary asks how digital technology can strengthen the "Big Ideological and Political Course" (da sizheng ke) in Chinese universities. The authors, Yang Xiaoxia and Lai Hairong, take as their starting point the 2022 work plan issued by the Ministry of Education and nine other departments. They argue that artificial intelligence, big data and VR/AR will become an important route to high-quality development of the course, provided that obstacles in teacher outlook, skills, governance and infrastructure are addressed.

The article has two main parts. The first sets out three aspects of the "value logic" of digital empowerment. The second names the difficulties encountered and proposes three lines of action: raising digital literacy, reforming the "supply side" of the course, and building digital infrastructure. It closes with a brief appeal to university teachers to act on Xi Jinping's speech at the symposium for teachers of ideological and political theory courses.

On the value of digitalisation, the authors argue that data profiling of students makes teaching content more precise. They also hold that digital tools break down barriers between school stages and between spaces. VR/AR and online platforms extend teaching from the small classroom to the wider social classroom, and shared platforms ease the uneven distribution of teaching resources and permit more scientific evaluation. On the problems, they point to lagging attitudes or resistance among some teachers, insufficient digital literacy, limited application and governance shortcomings. They also see a risk of conflict between instrumental rationality and value rationality.

The authors call for systematic training of teachers and students in digital skills, including the ability to recognise erroneous trends and false information online. They also want reform of teaching subjects, content, space and resources using student data and platforms, and new networks and shared resource platforms. They further call for technical defences against what they describe as Western capitalist ideological intrusion, data theft and digital viruses. Their stated aim is a high-level course that cultivates the "four-have" new generation. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Chinese scholars of ideological and political education frame digital technology as a tool for ideological teaching.
quoteEn: Empowering the university "Big Ideological and Political Course" through digitalisation will enrich its teaching content, innovate teaching methods, and bring together all parties to build a powerful teaching platform for the course.
quoteZh: 以数字化赋能高校“大思政课”，将会丰富“大思政课”的教学内容、创新教学方式、凝聚各方主体协同建构强大的思政课教学大平台。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Chinese education authorities, notably in a 2022 work plan. It aims to extend ideological and political theory teaching beyond the classroom by drawing on society-wide resources, platforms and teachers.
Compulsory courses in Marxism, Party theory and moral education taught at all levels of Chinese education.
A formula for the kind of young person the education system is meant to cultivate: with ideals, moral integrity, knowledge and a strong sense of responsibility.

t: Continuing to advance the integrated development of ideological and political courses so that it takes deep root
zh: 持续推进思政课一体化建设走深走实
paras: Yao Guojian takes up Xi Jinping's May 2024 instruction on school ideological and political courses, which calls for deepening integrated ideological and political education across universities, secondary and primary schools. Yao argues that such integration is a systematic project, organised through theory, content and culture, for fostering a new generation able to shoulder the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

The commentary is organised in three parts. The first concerns the theoretical grounding of an integrated course system, the second the substance and practical content of teaching, and the third the transmission of three cultural sources: fine traditional Chinese culture, revolutionary culture and advanced socialist culture.

On theory, Yao says each stage of schooling should seek a common denominator in the truth of Marxism and use reasoned argument suited to the students' level, so as to build a graded, spiral-rising teaching system. On content, the author proposes moving from the near to the grand: from everyday progress around students, to national achievements such as high-speed rail, the C919 airliner and the Hong Kong–Zhuhai–Macao Bridge, to a resolve to serve the country. On culture, Yao assigns each stage a task: primary pupils cultivate virtues, middle schoolers learn to reason, high schoolers set aspirations, and university students engage with the Two Integrations. Revolutionary culture moves from enlightenment to knowledge to ideas, while students are asked to become creators of advanced socialist culture.

Yao concludes that, if teaching follows the pattern of student development and links personal ideals with the cause of the Party and state, integration will open a new phase of ideological and political education. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Chinese academics translate Xi Jinping's directives on course integration into stage-by-stage teaching principles.
quoteEn: The fundamental task of ideological and political courses is to foster virtue and cultivate talent, and advancing their integration across universities, secondary and primary schools is an important lever for carrying out that task.
quoteZh: 思政课的根本任务是立德树人，推进大中小学思政课一体化建设是落实立德树人根本任务的重要抓手。

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses in Marxism, Party theory, morality and the law taught at every level of Chinese schooling.
Xi Jinping's formula for combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's central national goal, presented as restoring China's strength and standing.

t: The livelihood attribute of ideological and political course teaching
zh: 思政课教育教学的民生属性
paras: This short commentary argues that teaching ideological and political courses (sizheng ke) in schools and universities has a "livelihood attribute" (minsheng shuxing), because education is a livelihood project. Li Hui contends that grasping this attribute helps explain why building these courses is a top priority in the Party's leadership of education.

The piece has three sections. The first defines livelihood as the unity of material and spiritual life. The second treats fostering virtue and nurturing talent (lide shuren) as a unity of public opinion and popular support. The third describes the kind of teacher the courses require.

Li starts from historical materialism: people must first be able to live before they can make history, so material needs are the premise of any livelihood orientation. Citing the 19th Party Congress report (2017) on the principal contradiction, Li adds that growing spiritual needs must be treated as a unity with material ones. On fostering virtue, Li says the task has a political and strategic side, producing successors to socialism, and also a livelihood side. Moral and political quality is, in Li's account, the core of an individual's growth, bears on family happiness, and supports public order. On teachers, Li calls for patriotic commitment and a caring attitude towards students. Drawing on Marx's concept of alienated labour, Li contrasts capitalist education, which in this reading trains labour-power for production, with socialist education aimed at all-round human development.

Li concludes that the courses have political and strategic attributes and also a livelihood attribute. Students' growth, parents' hopes and the Party and state's need for successors are said to rest on the same questions of whom to train, how and for whom. Read the original if you want a brief example of how Chinese Marxism-school scholars link ideological education to livelihood and moral formation.
quoteEn: Ideological and political courses have not only a political and strategic attribute, but, even more, a livelihood attribute.
quoteZh: 思政课不仅具有政治属性、战略属性，更具有民生属性。

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses in Marxism, Party theory, morality and law taught from primary school to university in China. They are treated as the main channel of ideological education.
The stated fundamental task of Chinese education, stressed in Party documents since the 18th Party Congress (2012). It combines moral formation with the training of capable people.
A traditional term for the material wellbeing of ordinary people, used in Party discourse for issues such as education, employment and healthcare.

t: Making the building of ideological and political theory courses the top priority of Party leadership over education
zh: 把思政课建设作为党领导教育工作的重中之重
paras: Writing in December 2024, Xue Weijiang takes up the place of school ideological and political theory courses (sizheng ke) within the Party's leadership of education. The commentary argues that these courses are the lifeline for implementing the Party's educational policy and must be treated as the top priority of educational work. Its thesis is that Party leadership is the defining feature and advantage of such courses, that experience of building them is an important lesson in leading education, and that handling a set of key relationships in reform is the route to strengthening that leadership.

The piece is organised in three parts. The first sets out how Party leadership shapes the courses in terms of educational direction, goals and methods. The second lists five regular patterns the author draws from experience since the 18th Party Congress (2012). The third turns to reform and innovation through the "eight unities" methodology associated with Xi Jinping.

In the first part, Xue says the courses serve the people and the modernization drive, aim at the all-round development of the person, and combine education with productive labour and social practice. The second part names five lessons: upholding Marxism as the guiding ideology and Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, upholding the socialist orientation and the fundamental task of fostering virtue through education, building a strong teaching force, rooting education in Chinese soil, and maintaining a work pattern of unified Party committee leadership with wide coordination. The third part walks through eight pairings, such as political and academic character, value and knowledge, constructive and critical approaches, theory and practice, indoctrination and inspiration, and explicit and implicit education. Xue presents these as ways to increase the courses' ideological quality, relevance and appeal.

Xue concludes that firmly grasping ideological and political education ensures the Party's banner flies in every sector of education, and that reform of the courses lays the ideological and political foundation for Party leadership of education. The text is a programmatic statement of official positions rather than an empirical study. Read the original if you want a concise account of how Party-school scholars frame the leadership, teaching staff and methodology of ideological and political courses in the new era.
quoteEn: Strengthening Party leadership is the fundamental guarantee for building ideological and political theory courses well.
quoteZh: 加强党的领导是做好思政课建设的根本保证。

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses in Marxist theory, Party ideology, morality and the rule of law taught at Chinese schools and universities. They are treated officially as the core channel of political education.
An official formula naming the fundamental task of education: cultivating moral character alongside knowledge. It is frequently cited in Xi Jinping-era education policy.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's current official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018. It forms the core content of the textbooks for these courses.
Eight paired principles for reforming ideological and political courses, set out by Xi Jinping in 2019, such as unifying political and academic character or explicit and implicit education.

t: Practical exploration of an education system for ideological and political education in courses
zh: 课程思政育人体系的实践探索
paras: Writing in late 2024, Huang Nansong, executive vice-president of Guangzhou Institute of Technology, asks how "ideological and political education in courses" (kecheng sizheng) can be made effective in Chinese universities. Citing Xi Jinping's remarks at the National Education Conference that building a strong education nation must centre on fostering virtue and cultivating people, Huang argues that the answer lies in a system with a sound theoretical basis, coordinated delivery and progressive stages, aimed at making the content take root in students' minds and be put into practice.

The short commentary has four parts. It first names three challenges facing universities: weak theoretical understanding, poor coordination, and a lack of progression in teaching content. It then offers a theoretical account of how such education works, a framework of five coordinated "actions" corresponding to the five educations, and a four-year staged path for student development. The examples come from practice that Huang presents as a model for other institutions.

Huang's central move is to ground the approach in two cycles. The "cognitive cycle" runs from perceptual to rational understanding; the "practice cycle" runs from first-classroom teaching through second-classroom activities such as clubs, speeches and volunteering, to social practice. Huang sums up the underlying principle as "seeking truth from facts, taking root in the mind and putting into practice". The five actions (moral education to forge the soul, intellectual education to strengthen the foundation, physical education, aesthetic education and labour education) combine in-class and out-of-class work and, in Huang's phrase, produce a "fifth-power effect". For progression, Huang proposes a ladder with five stages: initiation in the first year, accumulation in the second, practical transformation in the third, integration and career preparation in the fourth, and a final stage of aesthetic outlook at graduation.

Huang concludes that universities should carry out the national strategy on strengthening this form of education by building a system that is theoretically grounded, coordinated across processes and graded by level. The stated aim is the all-round development of students and the training of socialist builders and successors. Read the original if you want a concrete example of how a Chinese university frames and operationalises course-based ideological and political education, including its terminology and programme design.
quoteEn: The core theory of the education system for ideological and political education in courses can be summed up as "seeking truth from facts, taking root in the mind and putting into practice".
quoteZh: 课程思政育人体系的内核学理可概括为“实事求是，入心践行”

glossary.en: ideological and political education in courses
glossary.explanation: A policy approach that builds moral, ideological and political content into all university subjects, not only dedicated political courses. It has been promoted by the Ministry of Education since the mid-2010s.
The stated fundamental task of Chinese education: developing students' moral character alongside knowledge and skills. It is widely used in Party education policy.
The official aim of all-round development through moral, intellectual, physical, aesthetic and labour education (德智体美劳).

glossary.zh: 社会主义建设者和接班人
glossary.explanation: The official description of the goal of Chinese education: people who will carry forward the socialist cause.

t: Constructing the Party's ideological discourse system in the new era
zh: 新时代党的意识形态话语体系建构
paras: Wang Peizhou asks how the Chinese Communist Party's ideological discourse should be built in an era that combines profound global change, the national rejuvenation mission and Chinese modernization. The article argues that a "one-dimensional" approach is no longer adequate. Ideological discourse, in Wang's view, must be constructed as a system along three interlinked dimensions: politics, narrative and power.

The article is organised in three sections, one for each dimension, each with three sub-points. The political dimension covers value discourse, theoretical discourse and institutional discourse. The narrative dimension covers the narratives of goals, of development and of governance. The power dimension examines the power logic of discourse, hard power as the basis of soft power, and the interaction of the two. Wang draws on Party congress reports, Xi Jinping's statements and examples such as the "eight-point regulations", the Fengqiao experience and the word "taikonaut".

In the political dimension, Wang argues that discourse should turn "the discourse of politics" into "the politics of discourse", mobilising people through the founding mission, through theory that gives direction, and through Party regulations that secure execution. Wang adds that Western neoliberalism, "constitutional democracy" and historical nihilism set "either-or" traps that theory must clarify. In the narrative dimension, the rejuvenation story, the people-centred story of Chinese modernization and the community-based story of governance are said to generate attraction, because they rest on real achievements. In the power dimension, Wang holds that soft power becomes discourse power only because hard power underpins it. Hard power without soft power loses cohesion, and Wang cites the Soviet collapse as the example.

Wang concludes that building the ideological discourse system requires hard and soft power to interact and strengthen each other. The Party must also manage the pace and timing of propaganda and guard against ideological risk at key moments. Discourse gains force when values are matched by developmental facts. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese Party-theory scholar frames ideological work through the three lenses of politics, narrative and power, and how Party-state discourse and its priorities are justified.
quoteEn: One must see that \"soft power\" forms \"discourse power\" because it is in fact not soft: effective soft power is often backed by strong hard power.
quoteZh: 必须看到“软实力”之所以形成“话语权”,是因为其事实上并不软,有效的软实力背后往往都有强大的硬实力做支撑。

glossary.explanation: The official concept for China's path of modernization, set out in the 20th Party Congress report (2022). It is presented as having five features, including common prosperity and harmony between humanity and nature.
Rules on official conduct, aimed at curbing extravagance and bureaucratic formalism. The Politburo adopted them after the 18th Party Congress (2012).
A model of grassroots governance from Fengqiao, Zhejiang, in the 1960s. It stresses relying on the masses to resolve conflicts locally and is promoted in the new era.
The capacity to shape the terms of public and international discussion. Chinese ideological writing treats it as a form of power that the Party must hold.

t: Promoting the integration of the spirit of the 20th Party Congress into ideological and political courses from primary school to university, with high quality
zh: 高质量推进党的二十大精神融入大中小学思政课
source: China Theory Net (中国理论网), posted on marxism.cass.cn 18 December 2024
paras: Yang Qicai and Xu Yuehui take up a practical question in Party-led education: how the spirit of the 20th Party Congress (2022) can be built into ideological and political theory courses ('ideological and political courses') at primary, secondary and tertiary level. They hold that studying and implementing the Congress's spirit is the Party's primary political task and the top priority of these courses. Their answer is to teach eight defined topics and to introduce them in graduated stages.

The article, first published on China Theory Net, has two parts. The first sets out what to teach: eight areas drawn from the Congress report, Xi Jinping's statements and central requirements. The second sets out how to teach it, in three steps that the authors summarise as moving 'from low to high', 'from little to much' and 'from shallow to deep'.

The eight topics include the Congress's significance, its main outcomes and theme, its summing-up of a decade of change in the new era, and its account of a new stage in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. They also cover the Party's mission on the new journey, which centres on Chinese modernization, the twelve areas of strategic deployment, and the expectations placed on youth. On method, the authors assign each stage a task. Primary school plants seeds through stories, pictures and video ('enlightenment'). Junior secondary school relies on cases and lived experience ('experience'). Senior secondary school stresses 'common knowledge' through observation, analysis and reflection. University stresses systematic theory that links theory with practice and history with reality. Content likewise deepens from a first grasp of the Congress's significance to a thorough understanding of its framework and the mission it assigns.

Yang and Xu conclude that teachers should not simply wait, rely on documents or read them out, and should not copy mechanically. They call for goal-oriented teaching adapted to textbooks, students and available resources, with richer forms and innovative methods. The aim is for the Congress's spirit to be vivid, comprehensive and layered, so that it reaches students' minds and hearts. Read the original if you want a concrete example of how Party doctrine is mapped onto a staged curriculum from primary school to university in China's ideological and political education.
quoteEn: To promote the integration of the spirit of the 20th Party Congress into ideological and political courses at all levels with high quality, one should focus on getting the stages, content and methods right.
quoteZh: 高质量推进党的二十大精神融入大中小思政课，应重点把握好阶段、内容与方法

glossary.explanation: Compulsory ideological and political theory courses taught at all levels of Chinese education. They transmit Party theory and are described officially as the key course for 'fostering virtue through education'.
The official term for China's path to modernization, set out in the 20th Party Congress report (2022). The report names five essential features and five principles for it.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for the Party's continuing effort to fit Marxism to China's conditions and to contemporary circumstances. Party documents present Xi Jinping Thought as its latest outcome.

t: Why "the influence of culture is first of all the influence of values"
zh: 为何“文化的影响力首先是价值观的影响力”
paras: Taking up Xi Jinping's statement that the influence of culture is first of all the influence of values, Chen asks how the core socialist values (prosperity, democracy, civility, harmony, freedom, equality, justice, rule of law, patriotism, dedication, integrity and friendship) shape cultural influence. The author's answer is that these values play a pivotal role in every aspect of cultural life.

The short commentary examines four common states of culture: creation, charm, exchange and infiltration. Each is paired with a metaphor for the role of the core socialist values: a banner, a fixed star, a central axis and a line of defence.

Chen argues that the values answer the question of whom culture serves and which road it takes, so creators should uphold the people's standpoint and the socialist direction. Works such as the television drama The Age of Awakening and the film The Battle at Lake Changjin are cited as carrying such values, while cultural products that yield to capital logic are said to lose their way. In exchange, the values are presented as the standard for separating mainstream from tributary and essence from dross. The author portrays Western capitalist countries as using a vast cultural arsenal for infiltration and value dumping, which Chen calls a threat to China's cultural security.

Chen concludes that cultural construction begins with forging its soul, and that the soul of socialist culture is the core socialist values. Cultivating them is said to bear on national security, regime survival and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want a compact example of how Party-affiliated scholars link cultural influence, soft power and cultural security to core socialist values.
quoteEn: The core socialist values are the concentrated expression of the contemporary Chinese spirit, the greatest common denominator of the whole people's values and the essential embodiment of socialist ideology, and they determine the fundamental nature, basic temperament and deeper meaning of socialist cultural creation.
quoteZh: 社会主义核心价值观，是当代中国精神的集中呈现，是全国人民价值观念的最大公约数，是社会主义意识形态的本质体现，决定着社会主义文化创作的根本性质、基本气质与深层意义。

glossary.explanation: A twelve-word official formulation of values at national, social and individual levels, promoted by the Party since the 18th Party Congress (2012).

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central goal of Party discourse, referring to restoring China's national strength and international standing by the mid-twenty-first century.
Borrowed from Joseph Nye, the term is used in Party discourse for the attractiveness and cohesion of a country's culture and values, which Xi Jinping ties to core values.

t: Making good use of the textbook and preparing lessons well: advancing teaching of the Marxist view of journalism
st: Teaching experience based on "Twelve Lectures on the Marxist View of Journalism"
zh: 用好教材备好课 深入推进马克思主义新闻观教学
zhSub: 基于《马克思主义新闻观十二讲》的教学体验
paras: This is the edited text of a keynote talk by Zheng Baowei, chief editor of the national textbook Twelve Lectures on the Marxist View of Journalism, given at a collective lesson-preparation event on teaching the Marxist view of journalism at Xiamen University's School of Journalism and Communication. Zheng praises the school's collective approach and offers advice, drawn from the author's own editing and teaching experience, on how to use the textbook well. The central claim is that good teaching requires understanding why the subject matters, what the textbook is for, and how it is built.

Zheng's talk has six parts: the importance of Marxist journalism education; the textbook's positioning; its guiding principles of compilation; how it handles problems in teaching; its framework of twelve lectures; and the use of Xi Jinping's journalism work in Fujian as a teaching resource. Zheng traces the history of such education from 2000, through the Central Publicity Department's campaigns in 2001 and 2003, to the period after the 18th Party Congress (2012).

Zheng argues that Xi Jinping's speeches of 19 August 2013 and 19 February 2016 turned this education into what the author calls a "golden period". The 2016 speech called the view of journalism the "soul" of news and public-opinion work and demanded that Marxism run through journalism research and teaching. The textbook, compiled under a project commissioned by the Central Publicity Department and the Ministry of Education, is described as the first official standard text on the subject. Zheng lists five compilation principles, including applying the Marxist standpoint, summing up the Party's journalistic tradition, reflecting the latest results of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, and showing that the theory accords with the laws of journalism. The twelve lectures are grouped as introduction, basic principles, guiding principles (such as unifying Party spirit and people's character), professional norms and two practical topics.

Zheng proposes that Xiamen University draw on Xi Jinping's seventeen years in Fujian, including the revival of the Mindong Daily and a 1989 Ningde speech on journalism, as a distinctive teaching resource. Zheng also repeats a 2018 call to make the Marxist view of journalism the core of journalism education, covering all staff, the whole process and every student. Read the original if you want to see how the textbook's editor describes its design, its official rationale and the way it is meant to be taught in Chinese journalism schools.
quoteEn: The textbook organically integrates the Marxist view of journalism with the basic content of journalism theory.
quoteZh: 教材将马克思主义新闻观与新闻理论基本内容有机地融合在一起。

glossary.explanation: The official body of principles on the nature and role of news work, centred on the Party-led press. It is taught as a core subject in Chinese journalism schools.

glossary.en: unifying Party spirit and people's character
glossary.explanation: A guiding principle of Chinese journalism holding that the Party's leadership of the media and service to the people are consistent. It is one of the textbook's lectures.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for developing Marxist theory in line with Chinese conditions and contemporary demands. Zheng applies it to the Marxist view of journalism.

keywords: Twelve Lectures on the Marxist View of Journalism

t: Expanding and deepening the living use of red resources in the education of Party members and cadres in the new era
zh: 加大和深化红色资源在新时代党员干部教育中的活化利用
paras: Zhang Xingliang takes up how "red resources" can be put to more active use in educating Party members and cadres in the new era. The author argues that deeper use of these resources helps cadres perform their duties and carry out their mission. The piece opens with Xi Jinping's call to make good use of red resources and notes the regulations on Party history study and education issued on 5 February 2024.

Zhang defines red resources as the legacy formed as the Communist Party led revolution, construction and reform. They include revolutionary sites, memorial halls, relics and documents, and the deeds and spirit of martyrs and models. The commentary is organised around three functions: ideological and political education, practical training, and cultural transmission.

On the first function, Zhang holds that studying red resources lets cadres grasp the Party's lines and history, and understand why the Party "can", Marxism "works" and socialism with Chinese characteristics is "good". It is also said to temper Party spirit, reinforce the Party's purpose of serving the people and shape core socialist values. On practice, the author proposes site visits, scenario simulations, online courses and media, volunteer guiding, and red tourism routes and cultural brands, so that cadres learn by doing. On culture, Zhang argues that red resources enrich cadres' historical and cultural grounding, stimulate cultural innovation, and strengthen cultural confidence and China's international influence.

Zhang concludes that protecting, using and researching red resources will supply varied educational material for cadres and encourage them to model good conduct for society. The text is a short programmatic commentary, not an empirical study. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-education scholarship in China frames red culture, tourism and volunteering as tools for cadre training.
quoteEn: Red resources are a vivid vehicle for carrying out ideological and political education.
quoteZh: 红色资源是开展思想政治教育的生动载体。

glossary.explanation: Sites, relics, documents and stories of heroes and their spirit from the Communist Party's revolutionary, construction and reform history. They are used in Party education and in red tourism.
The ideological commitment, discipline and loyalty expected of Party members. Cadre education aims to cultivate it.
A twelve-word set of values promoted officially since 2012. It covers the national, social and individual levels.

t: Giving full play to the "four major platforms" role of Schools of Marxism
zh: 充分发挥马克思主义学院的“四大平台”作用
source: China Social Sciences Network (中国社会科学网), 2024
paras: Hu Daping, dean of the School of Marxism at Nanjing University, asks how Schools of Marxism can best serve as one of the "four major platforms" of ideological and theoretical work named by Xi Jinping at the symposium on philosophy and social sciences. The commentary argues that this platform function cannot be separated from the schools' core tasks of moral education and discipline building, and that it depends above all on the quality of teaching in ideological and political courses.

The piece first sets out what makes a School of Marxism distinctive: it differs from government departments, general academic bodies, Party schools, the Marxist theory research and construction project, and the media. It then lists the pressures the schools face and proposes several lines of work: organised research, coordination among the sub-disciplines, interdisciplinary expertise, institutional character, and a sustainable teaching force.

Hu contends that the schools' primary function is to educate people for the Party and the country, so theoretical research and propaganda must be integrated into the process of education. A research agenda that becomes "two layers of skin" with teaching would, in Hu's view, damage the main task. The schools must be strong in themselves, centring organised research on twenty-first-century Marxism and Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, and turning results into teaching. Hu also stresses the unity of the six second-level disciplines in Marxist theory, and the need for theorists to build real expertise in other fields to earn the respect of peers.

Hu concludes that the most important task is a sustainable corps of Marxist theorists, backed by institutions and material support. Hu also asks teachers to take Marx as a model of dedication despite scarce resources. Read the original if you want a short statement from a school dean of how a School of Marxism understands its roles and pressures.
quoteEn: If the theoretical research and interpretation of a School of Marxism are \"two layers of skin\" with the process of educating people, its main task of fostering virtue through education will be badly damaged, and it will often achieve little in propaganda either.
quoteZh: 马克思主义学院的理论研究与阐释如果和育人过程是“两张皮”，其立德树人的主任务必将受到重创，在宣传上往往也难有大作为。

glossary.zh: 思想理论工作“四大平台”
glossary.literal: four major platforms of ideological and theoretical work
glossary.explanation: Four institutional channels named by Xi Jinping in 2016 for Marxist theory research and publicity. They are the Marxist theory research and construction project, the research centres on the theoretical system of socialism with Chinese characteristics, Schools of Marxism, and the press and online media.
The official fundamental task of education in China. It stresses shaping students' moral character and political outlook alongside knowledge.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018. It is the main content of ideological and political teaching.
A formulation in official discourse for the latest stage of Marxism, which presents Xi Jinping's thought as its contemporary Chinese form.

t: Grasping the core meaning of "let those with faith teach faith"
zh: 把握“要让有信仰的人讲信仰”的核心要义
paras: Li Hui, a professor at the School of Marxism at Sun Yat-sen University, comments on Xi Jinping's remark at the symposium for teachers of ideological and political theory courses that such courses must resolve students' ideals and convictions, and that "those with faith should teach faith". Li reads the remark as defining what "strong politics" means for these teachers, as addressing a long-standing problem in building the teaching force, and as supplying a value orientation for that work.

The piece has three parts. The first argues that instilling scientific ideals and convictions is the core task of such courses. The second explains why conviction must take root in teachers before it can bear fruit in students. The third traces teachers' faith to self-confidence, which Li divides into the Four-sphere Confidence, confidence in the discipline, and confidence in students' need to grow and succeed.

Li argues that ideals and convictions are the fundamental task of ideological and political education, and that young people are at a critical stage because they form their self-awareness while facing a gap between ideal and reality. In Li's account, the United States and the West use ideological infiltration and talent strategies aimed at young people to contain the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, which makes the task more urgent. Teachers, Li says, are role models and guardians of social conscience, and political quality ranks first among their qualities. Marxist faith is described as scientific, because it rests on knowledge of laws of social development, and as morally grounded, because it rests on putting the people first. Only teachers who hold it can teach it convincingly.

Li holds that teachers' confidence rests on the Four-sphere Confidence, on a Marxist theory discipline that has made historic progress since reform and opening up, and especially since the 18th Party Congress (2012), and on the conviction that socialism with Chinese characteristics gives young people chances to succeed. Li concludes that having those with faith teach faith is a requirement of both ideological and political course building and education generally, and that it is the key to the fundamental task of fostering virtue through education. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how the Party's political education literature links teachers' personal belief to the aims of ideological and political courses.
quoteEn: Having those with faith teach faith is a requirement both for building ideological and political courses and for education itself.
quoteZh: 要让有信仰的人讲信仰既是对思政课建设的要求，也是教育的要求。

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses in Marxism, Party history and socialist values taught at all levels of Chinese education. Xi Jinping convened a symposium on their teachers in 2019.
Official formula calling for confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics.
The official name for China's development path and system since reform and opening up.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central official goal of national strength and prosperity, associated with the Chinese Dream and used as the Party's overarching mission.
Official term for the fundamental task of education: cultivating morally sound citizens who support the Party's course.
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched in 1978.

t: The lofty mission of ideological and political theory courses: guiding students to firmly believe in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
zh: “思政课”的崇高使命——引导学生牢固树立对马克思主义中国化时代化的坚定信仰
source: China Social Sciences Net, posted 17 December 2024
paras: Chen Binggong takes up the report of the 20th Party Congress (2022) and Xi Jinping's article on opening up new realms for adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. Chen argues that this is also a historic task for China's ideological and political theory courses ("sizheng ke"). The thesis is that these courses have the lofty mission of leading students to hold a firm, unshakeable belief in the latest results of that adaptation.

The commentary has two parts. The first explains why the mission is lofty, in three steps: the adaptation of Marxism is the living soul of a "new form of human civilisation", it is the "spiritual fulcrum" of China's future, and it is an important spiritual fulcrum for university students. The second part proposes five routes for carrying out the mission, covering teachers, teaching style, a new lecture course, the teacher corps and the training of Marxist theory students.

In the first part, Chen holds that the socialist market economy, which the author calls unprecedented in Chinese civilisation, underpins Chinese modernization and the new form of civilisation. Chen describes the latest theoretical results as a "spiritual steel" that unites socialism with the market economy and humanistic spirit with commodity consciousness. Chen defines a civilisation as a community held together by value belief, and argues that people build their inner world on a single spiritual fulcrum. For university students, whose worldview, outlook on life and values are still forming, a sound fulcrum shapes their choices and futures. In the second part, Chen asks teachers to take this belief as a lifelong goal and to develop four kinds of teaching appeal: theoretical, knowledge-based, artistic and personal. Chen also proposes a systematic lecture course on the new realms, taught by leading experts, and a "two-expert" model in which teachers are both Marxist theorists and education specialists.

Chen concludes that Marxist theory programmes should train their students on the "two-expert" model, since future teachers come from them. Chen attributes weak spots in current teaching, such as "failing to speak on hot topics" and low effectiveness, to a shortfall in these two kinds of competence. The text is a short programmatic statement on the aims and staffing of political theory teaching. Read the original if you want a concise example of how a Party-school theorist frames belief, curriculum design and teacher training in ideological and political education.
quoteEn: The lofty historic mission of the ideological and political theory courses must be, and can only be, to guide university students to establish a firm belief in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, and to make it an important "spiritual fulcrum" for their growth and success.
quoteZh: “思政课”的崇高历史使命必然是,也只能是,引导大学生树立对马克思主义中国化时代化的坚定信仰,并成为其成长成才的重要“精神支点”

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses in Marxism, Party theory and moral education taught at all levels of Chinese schools and universities.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: Official formula for the Party's ongoing effort to fit Marxism to Chinese conditions and to the present era. It was given prominence in the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022).
The Party's official term for China's own path to modernisation, set out prominently since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
The official description of China's economic system since the early 1990s, combining market mechanisms with public ownership and Party leadership.
The author's term for a core value belief on which a person's or a civilisation's inner world is said to rest.

t: Making practical teaching in university ideological and political theory courses take root and deliver results
zh: 推动高校思政课实践教学落地见效
paras: Wang Yongbin, a professor at Lanzhou Jiaotong University's School of Marxism, asks how practical teaching in university ideological and political theory courses (sizheng courses) can be made effective. The commentary argues that, although universities have developed varied models, the practical teaching system still needs improvement and should be built more systematically.

Drawing on surveys of several universities, the article first describes four models: a separate stand-alone practice course run by the School of Marxism; practice spread across individual courses; joint development with other schools and departments; and teaching bases on and off campus, described as 'walking' ideological and political courses. It then identifies common problems and sets out four proposals, citing the 2019 Opinions on deepening reform of these courses and the Ministry of Education's plan for the 'Great Ideological and Political Course'.

Wang finds three shared weaknesses. Goals are unclear, so universities lack a common understanding of what content to offer; the educational value is thin, with formalism, uniform action and a few students' practice standing in for all; and implementation is loose, marked by entertainment-style activities, 'forced' or superficial fusion with professional internships, and substitution of internships for course practice. In response, Wang calls for a university-wide system led by the Party committee and the School of Marxism with other departments, detailed implementation plans offering students menus of options by discipline, fuller use of campus and external resources, and a supervision and evaluation mechanism.

Wang concludes that practical teaching must unify knowing and doing and be run as a long-term systematic project, with clear responsibilities and assessment. Read the original if you want a concise account of how Chinese universities currently organise practice components of ideological and political courses and what official guidance expects of them.
quoteEn: Practical teaching in ideological and political theory courses is a systematic project and also a long-term task, which must be continuously advanced and strengthened.
quoteZh: 思政课实践教学是一项系统工程，也是一项长期任务，需要不断推进持续加强。

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses in Marxist theory, Party doctrine, history and morality taught in Chinese schools and universities, usually run by Schools of Marxism.
A policy idea that extends such teaching beyond the classroom into society, using social resources, practice bases and 'big platforms'. A 2022 plan by ten departments promoted it.

t: The mission and responsibility of universities in building a cyber power in the new era
zh: 高校在新时代网络强国建设中的使命担当
paras: Marking ten years since Xi Jinping put forward the strategic goal of building a cyber power (2024), this short commentary asks what universities should contribute to it. Chen and Wu argue that higher education should treat advancing the cyber power as a major political responsibility and a glorious mission, and that it can do so in three ways. They describe these as building a "talent pool", a "technology bank" and a store of "positive energy".

The authors begin by noting that, since the 18th Party Congress (2012), China has built the world's largest higher education system, which they say provides a solid base. The article then takes the three tasks in turn: self-reliant training of talent, self-reliance in science and technology, and guidance by core values. It closes with a short call to study Xi Jinping's thinking on the cyber power.

On talent, Chen and Wu hold that competition in cyberspace is ultimately competition for talent. They call for integrated training from primary school to university, closer ties between universities and network enterprises, and cooperation with cyberspace and public security authorities. On technology, they cite Xi's description of core internet technology as China's greatest "lifeline". They say core technologies and standards remain in developed countries' hands, and urge breakthroughs in AI, big data, 5G/6G and quantum communication. On values, they cite 1.099 billion internet users as of June 2024, nearly 50 million of them university students, and argue that socialist core values should shape online culture so that "positive energy" leads online traffic.

The authors conclude that talent training is the key, technological self-reliance the core and value guidance the goal of building a cyber power. They also call for high-quality development of higher education that produces well-rounded builders and successors of socialism with Chinese characteristics. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated university scholars link internet governance, science policy and ideological education.
quoteEn: Competition in cyberspace is, in the final analysis, competition for talent.
quoteZh: 网络空间的竞争，归根结底是人才的竞争。

glossary.explanation: A strategic goal, stated by Xi Jinping in 2014, of making China strong in internet technology, infrastructure, content and security. It is also often rendered "cyber superpower".

A set of 24 characters in twelve values, promoted by the Party since the 18th Party Congress (2012) and covering the national, social and individual levels. Schools and universities are expected to teach them.
A popular term, taken up in official discourse, for upbeat, constructive content and attitudes. In internet governance it means content that supports mainstream values.

t: Paths to improving the supply capacity of university ideological and political theory course teachers
zh: 提升高校思政课教师供给能力的路径
paras: Yu Haibo takes up a gap he sees in university ideological and political theory courses (sixheng ke): teachers' capacity to supply what the courses need does not match the drive to make these courses stronger. Citing Xi Jinping's remark that the key to running such courses well lies with teachers, Yu argues for a systematic approach that advances teaching, research and practice together.

The short commentary, published on Guangming Online, sets out four lines of action: goals, evaluation and support, theoretical content, and teaching method. Each is tied to a slogan about what teachers need: the will, the strength, the scholarship and the technique to become a "great teacher".

Yu first calls for stimulating teachers' inner motivation, countering burnout through career plans and "development communities" of senior, middle-aged and young teachers. Second, Yu proposes reforming evaluation: weighting teaching performance in promotion, avoiding counts of papers and projects, creating separate promotion tracks (teaching-research, teaching-focused, research-focused), and matching courses to teachers' academic backgrounds. Third, Yu argues that research should start from and return to teaching, so that teachers can "talk politics through scholarship" by reading original works and joining reading groups and seminars. Fourth, Yu observes that new teachers are highly qualified academically but lack systematic pedagogical training, and that short, often online certification courses have limited effect. Yu urges practical training in teaching internships, courses and competitions.

Yu concludes that improving teacher supply capacity will improve the content and methods of teaching and move these courses towards high-quality development in the new era. The text is a project output funded by the Ministry of Education. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Chinese university scholars frame teacher development, evaluation reform and training for ideological and political courses.
quoteEn: University ideological and political course teachers must be clear that the starting point and goal of academic research lie in teaching: when they engage in research, they should start from teaching and finally return to it.
quoteZh: 高校思政课教师要明确学术研究的出发点和落脚点在于教学，也就是说高校思政课教师从事学术研究活动，要从教学出发，最终回归教学。

glossary.explanation: An official policy slogan, prominent since 2017, that stresses quality and efficiency over growth in quantity. Here it is applied to the development of ideological and political courses.
Compulsory courses on Marxism, Party theory and political education taught in Chinese schools and universities. They are a central tool of the Party's ideological work with students.
An honorific for teachers who combine deep learning with moral example. It has been used in Xi Jinping's speeches on education.

t: Optimising the paths to emotional identification in political values education
zh: 政治价值观教育情感认同的路径优化
paras: Huang Jin takes up the question of how political values education for university students can win genuine emotional identification, meaning that students accept, endorse and are willing to put these values into practice. The short commentary, first published on Guangming Online's theory channel, argues that such identification is the necessary route to the goal of political values education and an urgent requirement of fostering virtue through education. Huang holds that current practice falls short and needs improved paths.

Huang defines students' political values as their overall views, evaluations, attitudes and behavioural tendencies towards the political world. The author describes universities as the main front for training reliable successors to the cause of socialism with Chinese characteristics. The article then names three shortcomings: educators lacking the competence to awaken emotion, incomplete content that fails to imprint emotion, and unscientific methods that prevent emotional interaction. Three groups of remedies follow, aimed at educators, content and methods.

On educators, Huang calls for stronger political literacy and theoretical grounding, together with positive emotions and emotional capacity, so that teachers can move students through real feeling. On content, the author argues that identification rests on meeting students' legitimate interests: reasonable needs should be recognised and met, unreasonable ones firmly stopped and guided. Scientific content should also be combined with humanistic content on relations between people, politics and society, and on emotion, will and belief. On methods, Huang proposes political rituals, which the author says shape national, political and emotional identification through shared emotional experience, and a blend of online and offline carriers.

Huang concludes that improving educators' abilities, content and methods together will let political values education reach students emotionally and not only cognitively. Students would then understand, take part in and practise these values. Read the original if you want a brief example of how Chinese ideological and political education scholarship frames emotional identification as a task for university teaching.
quoteEn: Emotional identification with political values among university students is in essence the process by which political values education is recognised, endorsed and willingly put into practice by students, and it is the necessary road to the ultimate goal of that education.
quoteZh: 大学生政治价值观情感认同实质上是政治价值观教育被大学生群体所认可、赞同并愿意践行的过程，是政治价值观教育实现终极旨归的必经之路。

glossary.explanation: A phrase presented in official documents as the fundamental task of education in China. It stresses moral and political formation alongside knowledge.
The official name for the Chinese Communist Party's path and theoretical system since the reform era.
The field and practice of teaching political ideas, values and morality in Chinese schools and universities.

t: Building strong ideological and political leadership for a fully built education powerhouse
zh: 为全面建成教育强国凝聚强大的思政引领力
paras: Han Shangfeng takes up one of the "six strengths" that Xi Jinping says a socialist education powerhouse with Chinese characteristics must possess: strong ideological and political leadership. Han notes that it is listed first, and argues that it expresses the Central Committee's requirement that ideological and political work run through Party building, state governance and the whole of education. The article's thesis is that this leadership is built by strengthening Party leadership over ideological and political courses, by raising the quality of teachers, and by reforming how ideological and political education is organised.

Published in Red Flag Manuscripts in 2024, the piece is a commentary by a university Party secretary, in three numbered sections. The first deals with Party leadership and the content of theory teaching. The second concerns the teaching force of ideological and political courses. The third covers institutional reform, integration of such education across university, middle and primary schools, and the "big ideological and political course". It draws heavily on Xi's remarks and on the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024).

In the first section, Han calls for firm political orientation, with Party leadership as the basic guarantee of the direction of education. Han also wants Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era to enter textbooks, classrooms and minds, and wants a framework of education involving all staff, the whole process and every aspect. The second section holds that teachers must be both teachers of knowledge and models of character, embodying the "spirit of educators". It also asks them to keep learning, including about digital technologies, so they can answer young people's questions. The third section calls for coordinated reform of educational methods, school-running models, management systems and support mechanisms. It also calls for integrated ideological and political education across school stages, and for extending the classroom into society using digital platforms, success stories of the new era and "red resources".

Han concludes that these measures would turn Party leadership and theory into practical educational strength. The measures would also bind individual growth to national development and cultivate young people who take the building of a modern socialist country as their mission. The article proposes accountability mechanisms, such as placing ideological work under Party responsibility systems and assessing teachers' political conduct. Read the original if you want to see how a Party-university leader translates Xi's "six strengths" formula into concrete tasks for ideological and political education.
quoteEn: To build strong ideological and political leadership, one must hold to the correct political direction and recognise that building an education powerhouse is a foundational project for the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, that the Party is the core force leading China's education, and that Party leadership is the fundamental guarantee of education's correct political direction.
quoteZh: 凝聚强大的思政引领力，必须坚持正确的政治方向，深刻认识到建设教育强国是中华民族伟大复兴的基础工程，党是领导中国教育事业发展的核心力量，党的领导是坚持教育正确政治方向的根本保障。

glossary.explanation: A goal set out in Party documents, including a 2024–2035 plan, of making China a leading country in education. Xi Jinping describes it as a basis for national rejuvenation.
The capacity of ideological and political work to guide values and direction. Xi lists it first among the six strengths of an education powerhouse.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017 and 2018.
A policy concept that extends ideological and political teaching beyond the classroom into society, practice and online resources.

t: Signature concepts of China's independent knowledge system of ecological civilization and their effects
zh: 中国自主的生态文明知识体系的标识性概念及其效应
paras: This commentary, published in Guangming Daily in November 2024, asks how China's practice of ecological civilization construction can be turned into an independent knowledge system. Cai Huajie argues that the task begins with extracting "signature concepts" (标识性概念), which the author treats as the cornerstone of such a system. In Cai's account, these concepts can be organised around one root concept, "Chinese Marxist ecology", and will have lasting methodological effects.

The piece opens by citing Xi Jinping's call to distil signature concepts and the achievements said to follow the 18th Party Congress (2012), when ecological civilization was placed within the "five-sphere integrated plan". It then has two parts: the first on how the concepts are extracted and analysed, the second on three effects they produce. Its examples include "Lucid waters and lush mountains are invaluable assets", "a community of life on Earth" and "Beautiful China".

Cai describes conceptualization as a way of grasping the relationship between humans and the world, which yields reflective, normative and constructive concepts. From the root concept "Chinese Marxist ecology", the author derives three groups. Reflective concepts respond to Western environmental disasters and mechanistic views of nature. Normative concepts include socialist ecological civilization and modernization in which humanity and nature coexist in harmony. Constructive concepts concern institutions and systems, such as integrated governance of mountains, rivers, forests, farmland, lakes, grassland and desert. Together they form a "reflection–norm–construction" framework. The three effects are adjustment and regulation of ways of production and life, revolution and innovation (a "revolution in terminology", in Engels's phrase), and communication and selection. On the last, Cai claims that Western approaches to climate change have institutional defects, which gives Chinese concepts a real chance of wider uptake.

Cai concludes that these concepts give China's ecological civilization knowledge system a firm foundation and a vehicle for narration. The author also holds that they offer countries wanting both development and environmental protection a new option, and that their spread demonstrates the scientific character and vitality of Marxism. Read the original if you want a short example of how Chinese scholars frame the building of an "independent knowledge system" in ecological thought, and which official slogans they treat as its core concepts.
quoteEn: Signature concepts are historicized concepts.
quoteZh: 标识性概念是历史化的概念。

glossary.explanation: A term in Chinese academic and Party discourse for new concepts that distinctively express China's experience and can be understood abroad. Xi Jinping has urged scholars to distil them as the basis of an independent knowledge system.

An official goal and framework in China that integrates environmental protection into economic, political, cultural and social development. It was written into the Party's overall plan at the 18th Party Congress (2012).
The Party's overall plan for advancing economic, political, cultural, social and ecological civilization construction together.

glossary.zh: 绿水青山就是金山银山
glossary.pinyin: lǜshuǐ qīngshān jiù shì jīnshān yínshān
glossary.en: Lucid waters and lush mountains are invaluable assets
glossary.explanation: A slogan attributed to Xi Jinping (2005) holding that environmental protection and economic development are mutually reinforcing, not opposed.

glossary.zh: 人与自然和谐共生的现代化
glossary.pinyin: rén yǔ zìrán héxié gòngshēng de xiàndàihuà
glossary.en: modernization in which humanity and nature coexist in harmony
glossary.explanation: One of the stated features of Chinese modernization, stressing a development path that does not set humans against nature.

t: Grasping the theoretical foundations of the "leading capacity of ideological and political education"
zh: 把握“思政引领力”的理论基础
paras: Xiong takes up a phrase from Xi Jinping's description of a strong education country: the capacity of ideological and political education to provide guidance (sizheng yinlingli). The article argues that this capacity expresses the socialist character of a "strong education country" with Chinese characteristics, and that strengthening it rests on a deep theoretical foundation in the Marxist classics.

The short commentary has three parts. It first reviews what Marx, Engels and Lenin said about the political character of education. It then sets out why the classics treated ideological and political guidance as a task of the proletarian party. It ends with practical proposals for the present.

Xiong draws on Lenin's 1920 rejection of "apolitical" education and on the Communist Manifesto to argue that politics shapes education, and that education in turn acts on politics, including in the Bolsheviks' mass education before the October Revolution. From this the author derives three requirements: consolidating socialist ideology, upholding Party leadership with a loyal teaching force, and encouraging learners' self-education, citing Engels's remarks on self-improvement among Russian revolutionary youth.

For practice, Xiong calls for improving the institutions through which the Party leads ideological and political work, and for building ideological and political theory courses around Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. The author also urges stronger teacher ethics and better incentives for teachers. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated scholars ground education policy in Lenin's writings on political education.
quoteEn: The leading capacity of ideological and political education is an important factor that embodies the socialist character of a strong education country.
quoteZh: 思政引领力是体现教育强国社会主义属性的重要因素。

glossary.explanation: A national goal of building a leading education system, stressed by Xi Jinping and described as socialist with Chinese characteristics.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology since 2017, now the core content of ideological and political courses.

t: Upholding fundamental principles and innovating in ideological and political courses in the new era
zh: 新时代思政课坚持守正创新
