paras: This short commentary asks how ideological and political courses (sizheng ke) in schools should combine continuity with change in the new era. Yin argues that "upholding fundamental principles and breaking new ground" means holding to the courses' basic task, educational essence and fundamental nature while innovating continually to open a new phase of political education. The author notes that since the 18th Party Congress (2012) the Party Central Committee has given these courses an important place in education work.

The piece is organised as seven prescriptions. The first three concern what must be kept: the task of fostering virtue and cultivating talent, the courses' essence as reasoned exposition of Marxist theory, and their political and educational nature. The remaining four concern a "big ideological and political course" framework, teaching methods, evaluation, and the teaching force.

Yin contends that the courses must be synchronised with the Party's innovative theory and must lead students to conclude that only socialism can save China and only Chinese modernization can develop it. Teachers are to explain Marxist theory in plain language, link it to everyday life, and draw on China's achievements and on traditional, revolutionary and advanced socialist culture. On innovation, Yin calls for a "big ideological and political course" that joins classroom, course-embedded political education and social practice, and for varied methods, including lecture, discussion and game-based teaching, that meet the challenge of digital technology.

Yin also proposes multi-party evaluation of teachers and process-based assessment of students. The author calls for teachers who are "politically strong, deeply committed, innovative in thinking, broad in vision, strictly self-disciplined and upright in character", so that the courses develop in depth. Read the original if you want a concise, official-register statement of how a university Marxism-school scholar frames the principles and practical priorities of ideological and political teaching.
quoteEn: The essence of ideological and political courses is to reason things through, and what they must explain well is the reasoning of Marxist theory.
quoteZh: 思政课的本质是讲道理，它要讲好的是关于马克思主义理论的道理。

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses in Marxism, Party theory and moral and political education taught in Chinese schools and universities.
A formulation, stressed since the 18th Party Congress, that defines the fundamental task of education as moral and political formation alongside knowledge.
A concept that extends political education beyond the classroom by linking it with society, other courses and practical activities.
The official term for China's path of development under Party leadership, promoted since the 20th Party Congress (2022).

t: Teaching well the value orientation of putting the people first
zh: 讲好坚持以人民为中心的价值取向
paras: Shi Wenrui takes up how ideological and political theory courses in universities should teach the principle of 'putting the people first' (adhering to a people-centred approach). The author notes that the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) listed this principle among the major principles for further deepening reform comprehensively. Shi argues that teaching it systematically helps students merge personal aspirations with those of the country and people and commit themselves to Chinese modernization.

This short commentary is organised around three justifications for the principle, followed by a section on teaching method. The justifications are theoretical (Marxism's people-oriented character), historical (the experience of reform and opening up) and practical (answering what Shi calls the 'people's questions' in the current period). The final part turns to pedagogy.

Shi argues that the people-centred orientation reflects the historical-materialist view that the people are the fundamental force creating history, and that students should learn from reform achievements across many fields how the masses create material and spiritual wealth. The author presents the orientation as an innovative development of Marxism and as a practical application of the mass line. Shi then argues that the Party's record since the 18th Party Congress (2012) shows reform serving and relying on the people. As people's demands now extend beyond material life to democracy, rule of law, fairness, justice, security and environment, courses should use successful cases to show how reform answers these needs.

Shi calls for 'Great Ideological and Political Courses' that link the classroom with society, bringing in exemplary figures and sending students out into practice, so the principle is felt as concrete rather than abstract. The aim is for students to serve the country and people in the cause of Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-state theory on people-centredness is translated into guidance for university ideological and political teaching.
quoteEn: Reform has meaning only when it is carried out for the people; reform has momentum only when it relies on the people.
quoteZh: 为了人民而改革，改革才有意义；依靠人民而改革，改革才有动力。

glossary.explanation: The official term for China's path of modernization, promoted by the Party since the 20th Party Congress (2022) as distinct from Western models.
Compulsory courses in Marxism, Party history and political education taught in Chinese schools and universities.
An initiative that extends ideological and political education beyond the classroom into society, practice and local resources.
A Party working method, associated with Mao Zedong, of drawing ideas from the masses and returning them as policy.
The policy of domestic economic reform and opening to the outside world launched in 1978.

t: Upholding fundamental principles and innovating to promote the intensive development of ideological and political courses
zh: 守正创新推动思政课建设内涵式发展
paras: Lin Xiaofang, writing in December 2024 in the theory channel of People's Daily Online, asks how ideological and political courses (sizheng ke) in Chinese schools can develop in depth rather than merely expand. The commentary answers that this requires "upholding fundamental principles and innovating" (shouzheng chuangxin). In practice, Lin argues, that means adhering to Marxist truth, reforming teaching, and building a wider, collaborative educational pattern.

The piece is organised in three parts. The first sets out the political foundations of the courses: political direction, Party leadership and the fundamental task of fostering virtue through education. The second concerns reform and innovation in content, teaching methods, the teacher–student relationship and the academic discipline. The third proposes a "big ideological and political course" that draws in many actors and settings.

On the first point, Lin holds that the courses must keep Marxism in its guiding position and use Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era to shape students' values. Party committees at all levels should treat the courses as a political responsibility. On reform, Lin calls for guidance by the "Eight Unifications", for fresh Party theory, including the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), to be integrated into teaching, and for AR, VR and MR technologies to create immersive classrooms. Teaching should move from one-way instruction to a model combining teacher guidance with student agency. The "big" course is to combine traditional classrooms, online classes and society as a classroom, integrate teaching from primary school through university, and draw on local history, other subjects and daily life as resources.

Lin concludes that teachers are the key. They should hold firm Marxist belief, be both "scholars of the classics" and moral exemplars, and be supported by evaluation systems that put teaching first, by training and by project funding. The aim is to cultivate a new generation who are loyal to the Party, patriotic and ready to take on national rejuvenation. Read the original if you want a concise statement of the official policy framework for ideological and political courses in Chinese schools and universities, and the measures now being promoted.
quoteEn: The essence of ideological and political courses is reasoning; the reasoning must be made deep, thorough and lively, and the scholarly exposition of the Party's innovative theory must be strengthened.
quoteZh: 思政课的本质是讲道理，要把道理讲深讲透讲活，加强对党的创新理论的学理阐释

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses in Chinese schools and universities that teach Marxism, Party theory and socialist values. Their content and role are set by Party and education authorities.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017 and 2018. It is now the core content of the ideological and political curriculum.
The officially stated fundamental task of education in China: moral formation of students alongside knowledge and skills.
A slogan promoted since 2021 for extending ideological and political education beyond the classroom to society, online platforms and practice.
Eight requirements for running ideological and political courses, set out by Xi Jinping in 2019. They include unifying political and academic orientation, and teacher guidance and student agency.

glossary.literal: great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's official goal of restoring China to national strength and prosperity, usually dated to 2049.

t: Integrating the spirit of labour into ideological and political education in universities
zh: 推动劳动精神融入高校思想政治教育
paras: This short commentary asks how universities can bring the spirit of labour into ideological and political education. Gao argues that the spirit of labour is an important part of the Chinese Communists' spiritual lineage and that embedding it is a key route to fulfilling the fundamental task of fostering virtue through education.

The article proposes three practical channels: ideological and political theory courses, a labour education curriculum and practice system, and social practice activities. It closes with a general call on universities to treat the relationship between knowledge learning and all-round development correctly.

Gao urges teachers of ideological and political courses to find points of fit between labour and course content, use modern information technology, run practice teaching on the theme, and invite model workers to speak in class. For labour education, universities should write it into training plans with compulsory credits, build teaching staff and materials, and set up practice bases with agricultural institutions so that students work in rural settings. For social practice, Gao points to summer study trips to revolutionary sites such as Yan'an, Jinggangshan and Xibaipo and to rural volunteer and survey programmes, through which students are meant to experience the value of labour directly.

Gao concludes that universities should make the ideas that labour is most glorious, noble, great and beautiful take root in teachers and students, so that labour cultivates virtue, intellect, physique and aesthetic sense and produces capable talent. Read the original if you want a brief example of how a university Party official describes concrete steps for linking labour education to ideological and political work.
quoteEn: Integrating the spirit of labour into ideological and political education in universities is an important way to keep strengthening and improving school ideological and political education in the new era and to perfect the system of all-round cultivation in moral, intellectual, physical, aesthetic and labour education.
quoteZh: 将劳动精神融入高校思想政治教育，是不断加强和改进新时代学校思想政治教育，健全德智体美劳全面培养体系的重要途径。

t: Building the "Great Ideological and Political Course" to improve the results of ideological and political education
zh: 以“大思政课”建设提升思政育人成效
paras: This short commentary, first published on People's Daily Online's theory channel, asks how universities can raise the effectiveness of ideological and political education through the "Great Ideological and Political Course" (da sizheng ke). Zhou Zifeng argues that building it is a key lever for fulfilling the fundamental task of fostering virtue through education and for training a new generation able to carry the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

The article rests on Xi Jinping's repeated emphasis on ideological and political education since the 18th Party Congress (2012). It is organised in four parts: Party leadership over ideological and political courses, the role of teachers, the integration of classroom teaching with wider social practice, and the use of digital technology.

Zhou first holds that Party leadership is the fundamental guarantee, so courses must serve the Party and the country and be grounded in Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. On teachers, the author proposes regular political study, including the Two Establishes and the Two Upholds. Zhou also proposes evaluation reform, more recruitment, and part-time teachers such as model workers, heroes and master craftsmen. The author then calls for linking the \"first classroom\" (course groups, interactive methods) to a \"second classroom\" of practice bases, surveys, labour and volunteering.

Finally, Zhou calls for digital means: big-data \"profiles\" of students' concerns, generative AI and recommendation tools for \"precise\" delivery of content, and virtual simulation, holographic imaging and the metaverse to recreate historical scenes. The author concludes that these measures together would widen the pattern of all-round education. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official commentary on ideological and political teaching sets out Party leadership, teacher management, practice teaching and digital tools.
quoteEn: Ideological and political courses should be taught not only in the classroom but also in social life.
quoteZh: 思政课不仅应该在课堂上讲，也应该在社会生活中来讲。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted since 2021 that extends ideological and political teaching beyond the classroom into social practice and society, involving many actors and resources.
The officially stated fundamental task of Chinese education: moral and political formation of students alongside knowledge.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017 and 2018, and a core content of ideological and political courses.
A formulation from the 2021 Party resolution affirming Xi Jinping's core position in the Party and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought.
The Party requirement to uphold General Secretary Xi Jinping's core position and the authority and centralised leadership of the Central Committee.

t: Guiding a new custom of respecting teachers and valuing education with the educator spirit
zh: 以教育家精神引领尊师重教新风尚
paras: This commentary, first published on the People's Daily Online theory channel, asks how the "educator spirit" (jiaoyujia jingshen) can be used to build a renewed social custom of respecting teachers and valuing education. Zheng Shipeng argues that such guidance would create a fair, respectful and harmonious environment for training high-quality teachers. In the author's view this would raise teachers' sense of professional honour, happiness and mission, and so supply the talent needed to build a strong education nation and advance the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. The piece takes its cue from the Central Committee and State Council Opinions on promoting the educator spirit and strengthening the teaching force in the new era.

The article has three parts. The first treats the traditional Chinese roots of respect for teachers, citing Xunzi and the Book of Rites, and the need for wider social recognition of the educator spirit. The second sets out three kinds of guidance the spirit provides: value-based, emotional and practical. The third proposes three ways of creating a good social atmosphere for educators. It includes one example, a Tibetan middle-school principal in Nyingchi, to illustrate emotional commitment.

Zheng contends that the educator spirit condenses the older tradition of honouring teachers into a modern form, covering ideals of serving the country, moral example, teaching according to aptitude, and a devotion to learning and innovation. Value guidance means putting the people first and treating education as a public-interest undertaking judged by popular satisfaction. Emotional guidance rests on the claim that education is essentially emotional labour. Practical guidance means unity of knowing and doing, with theory tested and revised in teaching practice, so that teachers become "great teachers" who combine skill in teaching with moral formation.

The author calls for three measures: running education that satisfies the people and meets demands for diverse, personalised schooling; strengthening teachers' ethics and conduct, including ethics assessment in qualification, recruitment and awards, model teachers as exemplars and practice bases for ethics education; and building platforms where teachers can display their abilities, with open talent policies and teachers volunteering in remote, border and rural areas. Zheng presents these as ways to restore the dignity of the teaching profession and build a strong education nation. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-state education policy links the educator spirit, teacher ethics and social respect for teachers.
quoteEn: The essence of education is emotional labour.
quoteZh: 教育的本质是情感劳动。

glossary.explanation: A set of ideals for teachers promoted by Xi Jinping in 2023. It covers patriotic commitment, moral example, teaching wisdom, diligent innovation, caring devotion and a broad cultural outlook.
A traditional Chinese social norm of honouring teachers and treating education as important. Official discourse presents it as a virtue to be revived.
A national goal stressed in recent Party documents, aiming to make China a leading country in education as a foundation for national rejuvenation.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's central long-term national goal, usually dated to 2049, of restoring China's strength and international standing.
An official principle that policy should serve the people's interests and be judged by their satisfaction. It is associated with Xi Jinping's leadership.
Official term for the moral standards and professional behaviour expected of teachers, which are assessed and promoted through regulations and campaigns.

t: Giving full play to higher education as the leading force
st: Building a leading country in education
zh: 发挥高等教育龙头引领作用
paras: Writing in the People's Daily on 23 October 2024, Hao Ping, identified as Party Secretary of Peking University, takes up the question of how universities should serve the drive to build a leading country in education. The commentary follows Xi Jinping's speech at the National Education Conference. Hao argues that higher education is the "leading force" of this effort and must be strengthened so that it supports Chinese modernization and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

The piece is organised under three headings. The first concerns fulfilling the fundamental task of fostering virtue through education, covering ideological and political education, discipline and talent-training reform, digital and intelligent education, and teacher development. The second concerns raising innovation capacity to serve national strategy and economic and social development. The third concerns deepening comprehensive reform of higher education in order to build world-class universities with Chinese characteristics.

Hao's core claim is that universities must combine political orientation with scientific and talent functions. They should teach with Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, expand the "大思政课" (broad ideological and political course) model, and adjust disciplines and training to the needs of new quality productive forces. Hao calls on research universities to join the new whole-nation system, link basic research to industry, and build an independent Chinese system of philosophy and social science knowledge. On reform, Hao stresses upholding the Party's overall leadership over universities, including the president responsibility system under Party committee leadership. Hao also calls for evaluation reform that ends the "five onlys" and puts the results of fostering virtue first, and for higher-level opening up in education.

Hao concludes that universities should aim for six strengths: ideological and political guidance, talent competitiveness, scientific and technological support, support for people's wellbeing, social coordination and international influence. The piece reads as a programmatic statement from a university leader on how to implement central policy. Read the original if you want to see how a senior university Party official translates the national education-strengthening agenda into concrete tasks for Chinese universities.
quoteEn: Universities must persistently use Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era to shape souls and nurture people, deepen reform and innovation in ideological and political courses, and forge them into the key courses for fulfilling the fundamental task of fostering virtue through education.
quoteZh: 高校要坚持不懈用习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想铸魂育人，深化思政课改革创新，锻造好落实立德树人根本任务的关键课程。

glossary.explanation: The official formulation of China's development path, promoted by the Party since the 20th Party Congress (2022) as distinct from Western models of modernization.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.
A concept introduced by Xi Jinping in 2023 for productive forces driven by technological innovation, notably in advanced industries and digital technology.
The official "fundamental task" of education: cultivating moral character alongside knowledge and skills.
An official term for mobilising state, research institutions and enterprises in a coordinated way to achieve key scientific and technological breakthroughs.

t: Accelerating the building of a socialist cultural powerhouse
zh: 加快建设社会主义文化强国
paras: Writing in the People's Daily on 27 September 2024, Liu Tongfang interprets the culture-related part of the decision of the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), which lists "building a socialist cultural powerhouse" among its seven areas of focus for further deepening reform. Liu argues that accelerating this task and reforming cultural institutions and mechanisms are essential to advancing Chinese modernization and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. The piece is a short newspaper commentary.

The article has three parts. The first sets out why a cultural powerhouse matters strategically. The second explains why cultural institutions and mechanisms must be reformed. The third lists practical measures under the guidance of Xi Jinping's thought on culture: ideological leadership, cultural undertakings and industries, cultural flourishing, the people's cultural life, and cultural soft power and international influence.

Liu's central claim is that national strength depends on cultural prosperity, citing Xi Jinping's line that without the flourishing of socialist culture there can be no socialist modernization. Chinese modernization, in this account, coordinates material and spiritual civilisation, and culture supports the market economy, high-quality development, people's livelihood and the Party's governing capacity. Reform is said to be necessary for three reasons: to strengthen cultural confidence through the Two Integrations, to foster a reformist and innovative spirit, and to liberate cultural productive forces in the face of market development and information technology.

On implementation, Liu calls for upholding Marxism's guiding position in ideology, with Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era at its core, along with the Two Establishes and the Two Upholds and a firm grip on ideological leadership. Liu also proposes balancing the ideological and industrial attributes of culture, putting social benefits first, expanding digital and public cultural services (especially in rural areas), and building Chinese discourse and international communication in support of a community with a shared future for mankind. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official commentary presents the cultural agenda of the 2024 Third Plenum and its main policy vocabulary.
quoteEn: Only by deepening the reform of cultural institutions and mechanisms and fully stimulating the whole nation's cultural creativity can we provide a continuous flow of spiritual impetus for Chinese modernization.
quoteZh: 只有深化文化体制机制改革，充分激发全民族文化创新创造活力，才能为中国式现代化提供源源不断的精神动力。

glossary.explanation: The official Party concept of a modernization path with Chinese characteristics, prominent since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It stresses coordinated material and spiritual civilisation, among other features.
Official formula for combining Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture. It is associated with Xi Jinping's discourse.
A formula from the 2022 Party resolution affirming Xi Jinping's core position in the Party and the guiding role of his thought.
A Party formula requiring members to uphold Xi Jinping's core position in the Central Committee and the Party as a whole, and the Central Committee's authority and centralised, unified leadership.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The official long-term national goal of restoring China to a strong, prosperous and influential position, central to Party discourse since the 18th Party Congress (2012).

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's foreign-policy concept of a world of shared interests and responsibilities, promoted in China's international discourse since the early 2010s.
The component of Xi Jinping's thought dealing with culture, formally put forward at a national conference on propaganda and ideological work in October 2023.

t: Firmly holding the Party's leadership over ideological work and improving the ideological work responsibility system
zh: 牢牢掌握党对意识形态工作领导权 完善意识形态工作责任制
paras: This commentary, first published in People's Daily on 22 October 2024, argues that ideological work is of extreme importance to the Party, and that the Party must keep leadership, management and discourse power over it firmly in its own hands. Liu Ronggang takes as his starting point the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), whose Decision lists "improving the ideological work responsibility system" as part of reforming cultural institutions and building a socialist cultural power.

The piece begins by stressing that ideological work bears on the Party's fate, long-term national stability and national cohesion. Liu says the ideological situation has changed fundamentally since the 18th Party Congress (2012) but remains complex and severe. He then sets out four areas for improvement, each introduced by a short heading.

First, Marxism must remain the guiding ideology, which Liu equates in the new era with Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era and Xi's thought on culture. He calls for regular theory study in Party committees and for building an independent Chinese system of philosophy and social science knowledge. Second, he calls for better mechanisms for cultivating core socialist values, through Party history education, patriotic education, moral and online ethics work, and opposition to money worship, hedonism and historical nihilism. Third, he proposes improved public-opinion guidance and response, including spokesperson systems, risk monitoring and all-media communication. Fourth, he urges open opposition to erroneous views, with Party committees taking political responsibility, managing media outlets closely and distinguishing political questions from academic ones.

Liu concludes that, as Chinese modernization advances, there is no room for compromise or retreat in ideological struggle, and that Party committees at every level must bear leadership responsibility. He calls for firm action against statements he describes as maliciously attacking Party leadership or the socialist system, distorting Party and national history or spreading rumours. Read the original if you want a concise, authoritative statement of how Party ideological responsibility is framed after the 2024 Third Plenum.
quoteEn: Whether ideological work is done well bears on the Party's future and destiny, on the country's long-term stability and on the cohesion and centripetal force of the nation.
quoteZh: 能否做好意识形态工作，事关党的前途命运、事关国家长治久安、事关民族凝聚力和向心力。

glossary.explanation: A Party arrangement, in place since 2015, that makes Party committees and leading groups at each level responsible for ideological work in their areas. The 2024 plenum Decision calls for improving it.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The official name for Xi Jinping's body of ideas, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018 as the Party's current guiding ideology.
A twelve-word official set of values (such as prosperity, democracy, harmony, patriotism and integrity) promoted nationally since the 18th Party Congress in 2012.
The official term for the Party's path of national development, set out prominently at the 20th Party Congress in 2022.
In official usage, a label for views that question or negate the Party's historical narrative, for example of the revolution and socialist period.

t: Firmly grasping the political, popular and strategic attributes of education
zh: 牢牢把握教育的政治属性人民属性战略属性
paras: This commentary, first published in the People's Daily on 14 October 2024, interprets Xi Jinping's speech at the National Education Conference. The authors, the Party Secretary and the President of Renmin University of China, argue that the speech reveals three attributes of education: political, popular and strategic. They contend that building a leading country in education requires grasping all three.

The piece is organised in four sections. Three sections take each attribute in turn, first explaining its meaning and then setting out what it requires in the new era. A final section turns to practice, with higher education as the "leading force" and Renmin University as the example.

On the political attribute, the authors hold that education reflects its social base and ideology, and that in class society it serves the ruling class's will. They say this attribute settles the question of whom to train, how and for whom. It must be turned into a socialist direction of schooling, a role for ideological and political guidance, and the fostering of moral character and cultivation of talent, so that students are loyal to the Party, the country, the people and socialism. On the popular attribute, they stress a people-centred approach, equity and public benefit. This means fuller development of the individual, quality-oriented education, adjusting resources to demographic change, and a national digital education strategy. On the strategic attribute, they present education as the foundation of national rejuvenation. It is forward-looking, foundational and supportive of science, talent and innovation, and should be planned within Chinese modernization.

The authors conclude that the "three attributes" are guiding principles for running schools and teaching. For Renmin University they pledge Party leadership, the training of "pillars of rejuvenation and pioneers of a strong nation", and an autonomous Chinese system of philosophy and social science knowledge. Read the original if you want an official university-leadership reading of the National Education Conference and of how Party ideology is tied to education policy.
quoteEn: The political attribute of education determines the fundamental questions of education: what kind of people to cultivate, how to cultivate them, and for whom.
quoteZh: 教育的政治属性决定着培养什么人、怎样培养人、为谁培养人这一教育的根本问题。

glossary.explanation: The official Party formulation of China's own path to modernization, promoted especially since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.
An official goal, set out in a 2024–2035 plan, of making China a world leader in education, closely tied to the aims of science, technology and talent.
The Party's central long-term goal of restoring China's strength and international standing, usually dated to 2049.
A major national meeting on education policy, held in September 2024. Xi Jinping gave a keynote speech there.

t: Giving full play to the leading role of higher education
zh: 充分发挥高等教育龙头作用
paras: Writing in the People's Daily on 9 September 2024, Qiu Yong, Party Secretary of Tsinghua University, argues that higher education is the "leading force" (longtou) in building China into a leading country in education. Drawing on the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) and on remarks by Xi Jinping, Qiu holds that the Party's and the state's need for scientific knowledge and talent is more urgent than ever. The article is a short commentary setting out what universities should do.

Qiu begins with the claim that every strong education country is a strong higher-education country. As evidence, the author cites the rise of Britain, France, Germany and the United States since the 15th century, which is attributed in part to leading education. The article then names four areas where higher education should lead: moral education and ideological and political courses; building world-class universities and disciplines; serving high-quality development; and international influence.

On moral education, Qiu calls for a curriculum and textbook system centred on Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, an independent evaluation system for ideological and political course teachers, online ideological education, and the "three-in-one" combination of value shaping, ability building and knowledge transmission. On university building, the author stresses Party leadership, converting the Four-sphere Confidence into confidence in education, and a shift to quality-focused, innovation-led development. On service to the nation, Qiu urges strengthening basic, emerging and interdisciplinary fields, tackling "bottleneck" technologies, expanding the Strong Foundation Plan, and deepening integration of science, education and industry.

On internationalisation, Qiu proposes both "bringing in" top talent and international students and "going out" through global education governance, university alliances, cooperation with Belt and Road Initiative countries and overseas campuses. The author also calls for building a China-centred independent knowledge system and telling China's story, contributing to a community with a shared future for mankind. The article ends by calling for the flourishing of world-class universities with Chinese characteristics to drive the wider building of an education powerhouse. Read the original if you want to see how a leading university Party secretary presents official priorities for higher education after the 2024 Third Plenum.
quoteEn: A university's outlook determines the outlook of the talent it trains; only by staying open and learning from the best achievements of human civilisation and the useful experience of higher education worldwide can universities truly achieve high-quality development.
quoteZh: 高校的办学视野决定着所培养的人才的视野，只有坚持开放，学习借鉴人类文明的优秀成果和世界高等教育的有益经验，大学才能真正实现高质量发展。

glossary.explanation: Official formula calling for confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics. It was elaborated under Xi Jinping.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.
China's international infrastructure and cooperation programme, launched by Xi Jinping in 2013.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's formula for China's vision of international relations, stressing common interests and joint development.
Official term for a development model that prioritises quality, innovation and efficiency over scale and speed.

t: Upholding fundamental principles and breaking new ground in ideological and political courses in the new era
zh: 新时代思政课坚持守正创新
source: People's Daily Online (reposted on marxism.cass.cn, 22 October 2024)
paras: This short commentary, originally published by People's Daily Online, asks how school ideological and political courses (sizheng ke) should combine fidelity to principle with innovation. Yin defines the Chinese formula "upholding fundamental principles and breaking new ground" as respecting correct direction, principles and laws while breaking through constraints to open new approaches. Applied to these courses, it means holding to their basic task, educational essence and fundamental character while innovating continuously.

The article moves through seven areas. The first three concern what must be upheld: the task of fostering virtue and cultivating talent, the courses' essence as reasoned argument, and their political and educational character. The remaining four concern innovation: a "big ideological and political course" pattern of education, teaching methods, evaluation systems and the teaching force.

Yin argues that the courses must keep pace with the Party's innovative theory and lead students to the conclusion that only socialism can save China and only Chinese modernization can develop it. Teachers should explain Marxist theory in plain language, tie it to everyday life, and draw on the achievements of socialism with Chinese characteristics and on traditional, revolutionary and socialist culture. Yin also calls for linking classroom teaching, course-based ideological education and social practice, for varied methods that respond to digital technology, and for multi-dimensional evaluation of teachers and students.

Yin concludes that teachers are the key actors and proposes building a corps that is politically strong, deeply committed, innovative in thinking, broad in outlook, self-disciplined and upright. This, Yin holds, would achieve the high-quality, content-focused development of these courses in the new era. Read the original if you want a concise, official-style statement of how Chinese academics frame the aims and methods of ideological and political education.
quoteEn: The essence of ideological and political courses is reasoned argument, and what they must explain well is the reasoning of Marxist theory.
quoteZh: 思政课的本质是讲道理，它要讲好的是关于马克思主义理论的道理。

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses in Marxism, Party theory and political education taught at all levels of Chinese schools and universities.
A long-standing educational slogan, designated in Party documents as the fundamental task of education.
A concept promoted since 2021 that extends political education beyond the classroom to society and social practice.
The official term for China's path of development under Party leadership, prominent in Party discourse since the 20th Party Congress (2022).

t: Nurturing young people's patriotic sentiment through fine traditional Chinese culture
zh: 以中华优秀传统文化涵育青少年爱国情怀
paras: Lan Xiaoxia asks how fine traditional Chinese culture can be used to cultivate patriotic sentiment among young people. Writing in Guangming Daily in October 2024, Lan takes as a starting point Xi Jinping's remarks in Baoji that Chinese civilisation should be studied and explained further, and the Patriotic Education Law, in force since 1 January 2024. Lan's thesis is that, in the new era, combining traditional culture with patriotic education matters both theoretically and practically, and that this requires a systematic training framework.

The short commentary has three parts. The first argues why traditional culture is the soil for patriotic feeling. The second sets out four core strands of content. The third proposes a three-part framework covering the education system, its content and its methods.

Lan argues that patriotism is the "bloodline gene" of Chinese civilisation and the essence of its fine traditional culture. Cultural identity, in this reading, underlies national and ethnic identity and cultural confidence, and the Party's stress on moral education is said to make traditional culture a means of raising a new generation for national rejuvenation and Chinese modernization. The four strands are: devotion to family and country (citing Mencius and the Book of Rites); unity and a strong sense of community of the Chinese nation, traced to the ancient idea of "great unification"; self-strengthening and innovation (citing the Book of Changes and the Doctrine of the Mean); and harmony, openness and inclusiveness, which Lan links to core socialist values.

Lan proposes improving the education system by building a "big ideological and political course" that joins classroom and extracurricular, school and society, and online and offline work. Patriotic content should be graded across primary, secondary and university stages, with supervision and evaluation. Content should stress history education, especially the "four histories", and bring heroes and model workers into schools. Methods should use museums and heritage sites, and also animation, musicals, short videos and other new-media forms that young people favour. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated scholars link traditional culture, the Patriotic Education Law and youth ideological education in practice.
quoteEn: Patriotism is the bloodline gene of Chinese civilisation's long history, and the essence of fine traditional Chinese culture.
quoteZh: 爱国主义是中华文明源远流长的血脉基因，是中华优秀传统文化的精华。

glossary.explanation: The official term for China's path to modernisation under Party leadership, promoted especially since the 20th Party Congress (2022).

glossary.en: sense of community of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: consciousness of the Chinese nation as a community
glossary.explanation: An official concept stressing that all ethnic groups belong to one national community. It is used in ethnic and ideological education.
An official education concept that extends ideological and political education beyond the classroom to society and online spaces.
The official set of histories taught in Party and school education: the history of the Party, of the People's Republic, of reform and opening up, and of socialist development.
The official term for those elements of China's traditional heritage that the Party endorses for inheritance and creative transformation.

t: On the "dao", "xue" and "shu" of teaching ideological and political theory courses
zh: 论思政课教学的“道”“学”“术”
source: Journal of Ideological and Theoretical Education (思想理论教育导刊), 2024 no. 9
paras: Liu Jianjun and Yin Li take up a formulation from Xi Jinping's speech of 18 March 2019 to teachers of ideological and political theory courses: that teaching these courses well involves not only technique (shu) but also scholarship (xue) and, above all, the Way (dao). The authors note that scholarly interpretation of this line is thin and inconsistent. They argue that it amounts to a theory of levels of teaching attainment, with technique as the lowest, scholarship as the middle and the Way as the highest.

The article opens by defining the three elements and their relations, then discusses the theoretical and practical value of Xi's formulation and the question of word order. Three main sections follow, one on each level: acquiring technique, building scholarly foundations, and raising one's intellectual and ideological standing. The authors draw on Xi's speeches of 2019, 2022 and 2024, on Ministry of Education regulations for these courses, and on Lenin and Dewey.

The authors read the three terms as a hierarchy that is also integrated: technique is the outward expression, scholarship the knowledge that supports it, and the Way its soul. They say this triad develops the traditional two-part Chinese notion of dao and shu into a new theory of teaching attainment. They also distinguish two orderings. Dao–xue–shu describes the overall logic of the theory and is used in the title, while shu–xue–dao describes the real process by which a teacher advances. Technique means observing teaching regulations, practising skills, learning from outstanding teachers and developing teaching artistry. Scholarship means systematic study of Marxist classics and of Marxism adapted to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, plus broad knowledge, research that supports teaching, and linking theory to practice. The Way means the political height and strategic thinking of a teacher who sees themselves as a political figure and spokesperson of the Party and state. It also means mastering Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, firm belief in Marxism, deep personal commitment, and following the laws of teaching, whose essence the authors, citing Xi, call "reasoning" (jiang daoli).

The authors conclude that a teacher who grasps the essence of these courses and follows their laws, applying the "eight unities" from Xi's 2019 speech, unites dao, xue and shu and reaches the highest level of teaching. They propose further theoretical research on the levels of attainment and call for teachers to treat self-improvement as a lifelong pursuit. Read the original if you want to see how Chinese scholars systematise Xi's remarks on ideological and political course teaching into a framework for training teachers, or if you study the language of Party-directed pedagogy.
quoteEn: Having technique is the elementary level of teaching ideological and political theory courses, having scholarship is a higher level, and having the Way is the highest level.
quoteZh: 有“术”是思政课教学的初级境界，有“学”是思政课教学的更高境界，有“道”是思政课教学的最高境界

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses in Marxism, Party theory and policy taught at all levels of Chinese education. The Party presents them as the key courses for fostering virtue and cultivating people.
A classical Chinese concept meaning path, principle or law. Here it denotes the essence of these courses and the laws of teaching.
Eight paired requirements for teaching ideological and political theory courses, set out in Xi Jinping's 2019 speech, such as combining political quality with academic rigour.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's current guiding ideology, written into its constitution in 2017 and presented as the latest stage of adapting Marxism to China.

t: How university ideological and political theory courses can teach the Party's innovative theory of the new era well
zh: 高校思政课如何讲好新时代党的创新理论
paras: Xiao Guiqing asks how university ideological and political theory courses (sizheng ke) can teach the Party's innovative theory of the new era effectively to young students. The article, published in Marxism and Reality in 2024, argues that this is a historic responsibility of higher education. In Xiao's view it follows from the need to train a new generation able to carry the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, and the task must be done by making the theory taught in depth, thoroughly and in a lively way.

The article has three parts. The first sets out why teaching this theory matters. The second sets out what the courses must convey: the theory's development, its scientific system, and its worldview and methodology. The third proposes methods under three headings: making the theory 'deep' (jiang shen), 'thorough' (jiang tou) and 'lively' (jiang huo). Xiao draws throughout on Xi Jinping's statements about ideological and political courses.

Xiao gives three reasons for the importance of the task. The theory is the latest result of the Two Integrations, especially integration with fine traditional Chinese culture. It is the guiding thought for building a modern socialist country and for Chinese modernization. And teaching it carries out the fundamental task of fostering virtue through education (lide shuren). On content, Xiao says teachers must present the theory as continuous with Mao Zedong Thought and later Party theories, and must combat erroneous views, notably on the relationship between the periods before and after reform and opening up. They must also explain the 'Ten Clarifications', 'Fourteen Commitments' and 'Thirteen Areas of Achievement', and the 'Six Musts' as a unified worldview and methodology. On method, Xiao calls for reading primary texts and building a coordinated matrix of courses from undergraduate to doctoral level, and for answering students' sharp questions through problem analysis. Xiao also calls for theoretical analysis that balances political and scholarly aims, and for everyday language. Xiao further favours student-centred teaching, new media, practical teaching outside the classroom and case studies.

Xiao concludes that students should not only learn the theory but also apply its standpoint and methods to real problems, since this is how the courses achieve their purpose of fostering virtue. The article warns against reciting documents, against replacing reasoning with preaching, and against reducing teaching to a pile of stories. Read the original if you want a detailed, Party-aligned account of how Chinese university theory courses are expected to teach Xi Jinping Thought, including course structure and teaching methods.
quoteEn: Teaching the Party's innovative theory of the new era thoroughly is the focus of university ideological and political theory courses.
quoteZh: 把新时代党的创新理论讲透是高校思政课的重点。

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses in Chinese schools and universities that teach Marxism, Party theory, Chinese history and moral education. They are treated as the main channel for the Party's theoretical education of students.

Formula for integrating the basic tenets of Marxism with China's specific realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture. The second integration was added in Xi Jinping's formulation of 2021–2023.

The official term for China's path to modernization, set out at the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is described as modernization of a huge population, common prosperity, material and cultural-ethical advancement, harmony with nature and peaceful development.
The stated fundamental task of Chinese education: cultivating moral character and political commitment alongside knowledge.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's central national goal, to restore China to a position of strength and prosperity by the middle of the twenty-first century.

glossary.literal: six things that must be upheld
glossary.explanation: Six principles in the 20th Party Congress report (2022) presented as the worldview and methodology of Xi Jinping Thought: put the people first, be self-confident and self-reliant, uphold fundamental principles while innovating, be problem-oriented, adopt a systems approach, and have a global vision.

t: The US "Summit for Democracy" and new challenges to China's ideological security
zh: 美国“民主峰会”与我国意识形态安全的新挑战
paras: The article asks what the Biden administration's "Summit for Democracy" is for and what it means for China. Writing after the third summit (March 2024, hosted by South Korea), the author argues that the summits are an instrument of ideological war against China and other states labelled "authoritarian". In the author's account they pose a set of new challenges to China's ideological security.

The text has four parts. It first explains why Washington revived the "democracy card", then analyses the summits' "normative" and "functional" attributes. It then identifies three inherent flaws, and finally turns to the threat to China and Chinese responses. The evidence comes from US strategy documents, summit declarations and initiatives, Freedom House reports and American scholars such as Fukuyama, Hal Brands and Robert Manning.

The author contends that the summits serve to shore up a relatively declining US hegemony and to repair the image of American democracy damaged by political polarisation and the Capitol riot of 2021. Their ideological aim, the author says, takes priority over their practical functions, which include technology export controls, a coalition over Ukraine and Taiwan, and funding for "democratic reformers" in ways the author compares to Cold War and "colour revolution" tactics. The author finds three flaws: a monolithic "American-style democracy" presented as plural, vague and instrumental criteria for invitations, and a false "democracy versus authoritarianism" story that ignores domestic causes of democratic decline.

For China, the author sees pressure on core values, set against the "common values of all mankind", and on the development model of Chinese modernization. The author proposes three responses. At the macro level, a holistic ideological security outlook under the overall national security concept. At the meso level, stronger international communication through combined official and non-official channels. At the micro level, tighter control of online platforms and foreign NGOs. The author also warns against being drawn into a comprehensive ideological contest like the one that exhausted the Soviet Union. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese Party-affiliated scholar frames the US democracy summits as an ideological security problem and what countermeasures are proposed.
quoteEn: The "Summit for Democracy" is a product of the US viewing strategic competition with China through a Cold War mindset, and an indispensable ideological link in the Biden administration's launch of an all-domain "new Cold War" against China.
quoteZh: “民主峰会”是美国以冷战思维审视对华战略竞争的产物，它是拜登政府开启对华全领域“新冷战”在意识形态领域不可或缺的重要一环。

glossary.explanation: The official concept for China's own path of development, promoted especially since the 20th Party Congress (2022) as an alternative to Western-style modernization.
The Party-state's concern with protecting Marxism's guiding position and the socialist value system from outside ideological influence. It is treated as part of political security.
A framework introduced by Xi Jinping in 2014 that treats security as covering political, economic, cultural, social, cyber and other fields, with political security as the priority.

A formula put forward by Xi Jinping naming peace, development, equity, justice, democracy and freedom as values shared by humanity. It is presented as an alternative to Western claims of universal values.
A term for the popular uprisings that toppled governments in post-Soviet and other states. Chinese official discourse describes them as externally engineered regime change.

t: Understanding how to promote the intensive, quality-oriented development of university ideological and political courses through upholding fundamental principles and innovation
zh: 对守正创新推动高校思政课建设内涵式发展的领悟
source: Journal of Ideological and Theoretical Education (思想理论教育导刊)
paras: Mei Rongzheng takes up Xi Jinping's call, made at the 2019 teachers' symposium and repeated in instructions of May 2024, to promote the "connotative development" (内涵式发展, quality-oriented development) of ideological and political theory courses (sizheng ke) in schools. Mei argues that this is an important part of the connotative development of higher education as a whole and could push wider teaching reform further. Mei proposes five areas in which it can be achieved, guided by combining problem-orientation with goal-orientation and uniting upholding fundamental principles with innovation.

The article first defines connotative development as growth driven by the internal essence and needs of a thing, as opposed to growth in scale. For the courses, this means that, once enrolment, staffing structure and funding are secured, teachers, curriculum and classroom teaching are to reform in concept, content, method, assessment, management, research and teacher quality. Mei then works through five points: one "fundamental" guide, one "key", one "focus", "three relationships" and one "historical summing-up".

The fundamental is Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, which Mei says must run through every course and be taught with depth in its theory, reasoning and philosophy. The key is the teaching force. Mei says many newly hired teachers come from non-Marxist disciplines and are weak in Marxist theory, Party history and the Four-sphere Confidence, so leaders should track their circumstances and guide them. The focus is textbooks, where Mei asks whether the key textbooks of the Marxist Theory Research and Construction Project are really used and used well. On the three relationships, Mei argues that the Marxist theory discipline must serve the courses; that teachers should not be overloaded with outside tasks; and that new undergraduate majors must not drain core teachers. Mei also warns against returning to the earlier practice of spreading these courses across other departments.

Mei reviews three curriculum schemes since reform and opening up (1985, 1998 and 2005) and says that a comprehensive, systematic assessment is needed of which experiences reflect teaching laws and which gaps remain. Mei proposes a large research group, led by the Ministry of Education's social sciences department, to produce a consultative report for decision-makers. Read the original if you want a Chinese academic's view of current staffing, textbook and institutional problems in university ideological and political courses and of the policy fixes he proposes.
quoteEn: It is not easy for teachers of ideological and political courses to explain principles deeply, thoroughly and vividly, and this cannot be done well if they read too little and spend too little time.
quoteZh: 思政课教师要把道理讲深、讲透、讲活很不容易，书读少了，时间花少了是做不到、做不好的。

glossary.explanation: Compulsory Marxist theory and political-education courses taught at all levels of Chinese schools and universities. They are overseen by the Party and the Ministry of Education.
A development model that stresses quality, internal structure and substance rather than expansion in scale. It is widely used in Chinese education policy.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018. It is the core content of current ideological and political teaching.
Official formula calling for confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义理论研究和建设工程
glossary.pinyin: Mǎkèsīzhǔyì lǐlùn yánjiū hé jiànshè gōngchéng
glossary.en: Marxist Theory Research and Construction Project
glossary.explanation: A national project launched in 2004 that compiles standard textbooks (马工程教材) for use in universities.

t: Grasping scientifically the major significance and practical requirements of deepening institutional reform in Party building
zh: 科学把握深化党的建设制度改革的重大意义和实践要求
paras: This commentary, published in Red Flag Manuscript in 2024, interprets the part of the Decision adopted at the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) that deals with institutional reform in Party building. Liu argues that the Decision answers what to reform, how to reform and what results to seek in this field. In Liu's reading, the Decision sets out the fundamental guidance for strengthening the Party's leadership and its capacity for long-term governance under the overall goal of further comprehensively deepening reform.

The article has three parts. The first explains why deepening Party-building reform matters. The second sets out the basic requirements for carrying it out. The third lists the concrete tasks for what Liu calls the critical stage of implementation: long-term learning mechanisms, cadre and personnel reform, Party organisations' political and organisational functions, management of Party members, and the authority of intra-Party regulations.

Liu gives three reasons for the significance of this reform. First, it is an integral part of modernizing the system and capacity of national governance, and it also guarantees that wider reform succeeds. Second, it is needed to mobilise Party members and officials to push reform and development, since deeper reform meets greater resistance. Third, it is required by the new great undertaking of Party building and by the need to deal with problems unique to a large party, such as slackness, incompetence, detachment from the people and corruption. On requirements, Liu calls for Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era as guidance. Liu also stresses three things that must not change: the Party's centralised and unified leadership of reform, the overall goal, and the people-centred value orientation. For implementation, Liu lists measures including the "first agenda item" system, the eight-point regulation, a correct view of performance, the "three distinctions", expanded Party coverage in new economic and social organisations, and an accountability system for implementing Party regulations.

Liu concludes that Party-building reform is "always in progress, never finished" and that the Party's own strength is the key to Chinese modernization and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. The article is a programmatic reading of the Decision, written from within the Party-state academic system. Read the original if you want a concise official-style account of how Party-building reform is framed after the Third Plenum, and of the practical measures it names for cadres, grassroots organisations and Party regulations.
quoteEn: Institutional reform in Party building is always in progress and never completed.
quoteZh: 党的建设制度改革只有进行时，没有完成时。

glossary.explanation: The official formula for China's path of modernization, promoted by the Party since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.
A set of rules adopted by the Central Committee in December 2012 to curb extravagance, bureaucratism and formalism among officials.

An official guideline asking disciplinary authorities to distinguish errors made in reform and exploration from deliberate violations, and similar cases, so that officials willing to take responsibility are protected.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's central national goal, which it links to achieving a strong, modernized socialist country by the middle of the century.

keywords: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party

t: Party leadership as the fundamental guarantee for further deepening reform comprehensively and advancing Chinese modernization
zh: 党的领导是进一步全面深化改革、推进中国式现代化的根本保证
paras: Writing in Red Flag Manuscripts (2024, no. 17), Shi Yubao interprets the Decision adopted by the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) on further deepening reform comprehensively and advancing Chinese modernization. The article takes the Decision's statement that Party leadership is the fundamental guarantee of reform and argues that carrying out its tasks depends above all on strengthening the Party's overall leadership.

The article has four sections. It first sets out why upholding the Party's overall leadership is the basis of reform. It then deals with the centralised and unified leadership of the Party Central Committee, followed by reform of Party-building institutions. It ends with a call to implement reform with a "nail-driving spirit". The author draws several examples from Guizhou Province on cadre selection, grassroots Party organisation and talent policy.

Shi presents the Party's overall leadership as a basic principle of scientific socialism, as the most valuable experience of revolution, construction and reform, and as a necessity given external pressure and domestic structural problems. The article then maintains that reform must proceed under the Central Committee's unified leadership. In practice this means firmly upholding the Two Establishes and the Two Upholds, arming Party members with Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, and raising the capacity of Party committees to plan and push reform.

On the institutional side, Shi proposes reforms in cadre personnel management, grassroots organisations, the education and management of Party members (cited as 99.185 million at the end of 2023) and talent development. The author ends by urging that reform be implemented through clear responsibilities, a systematic method and practical work, with formalism avoided and results tested by inspection and public satisfaction. Read the original if you want a clear example of how Party journals present the Party's leadership role in the 2024 reform agenda, including its Guizhou illustrations.
quoteEn: One part deployment, nine parts implementation.
quoteZh: 一分部署、九分落实。

glossary.explanation: A formulation from the 2021 Party resolution on history. It affirms Xi Jinping's position as the core of the Central Committee and the whole Party, and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought.
A Party requirement to uphold Xi Jinping's core position and the authority and centralised, unified leadership of the Central Committee.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party constitution in 2017.
The official name for the Party's path of national development, presented as distinct from Western models of modernization.

glossary.literal: the spirit of hammering in nails
glossary.explanation: A phrase used by Xi Jinping for persistent, step-by-step implementation of policy until it produces results.

t: The "way of becoming a person" in Fang Keli's educational thought
zh: 方克立教育思想中的“成人之道”
source: Chinese Social Sciences Today (中国社会科学报)
paras: Zhang Xiaoping and Liu Zihan present the educational thought of Fang Keli, the philosopher and educator who died more than four years before the piece was posted in 2024. They argue that Fang's principles for training graduate students form a coherent "way of becoming a person" (chengren zhi dao), meant to produce first-rate philosophy and social-science talent for the twenty-first century. The authors treat this as a legacy for later teachers and students.

The article, a short newspaper-style tribute, first introduces Fang: a member of the Academy's Divisions, former president of the CASS Graduate School and former chief expert of the Marxist Theory Research and Construction Project. He graduated from Renmin University in 1962 and taught for 58 years at Renmin, Nankai and CASS. It then sets out three clusters of ideas under separate headings: balancing learning and conduct, rigorous scholarship and noble character, and careful cultivation with strict management.

In the authors' account, Fang's first principle, put forward in 1982 at Nankai, was "balance learning and conduct, cultivate both virtue and vocation". It unites knowing with doing and scholarship with moral character, summed up in his remark "three parts learning, seven parts being a person". The second, announced in 1998 at the Graduate School's twentieth anniversary, was "rigorous scholarship, noble character". It calls for diligence, evidence-based work, study of historical materialism and a plain, unpretentious style. The third, "careful cultivation, strict management", rests on Fang's view that a strict teacher produces outstanding students. It requires teachers to lead by example and to teach according to each student's aptitude. It also encourages the "six first-rates" that students themselves proposed: character, cultivation, knowledge, vision, ability and physique.

The authors conclude that strengthening education requires strengthening teachers. They call for a highly skilled teaching corps with high ethical standards, for promoting the "spirit of educators" and for carrying out the fundamental task of fostering virtue through education (lide shuren). They propose that today's educators inherit Fang's approach to scholarship and conduct. Read the original if you want a concise, admiring portrait of a leading Chinese Marxist philosopher's views on graduate training and teacher ethics, as presented in an official Chinese academic setting.
quoteEn: Fang held that "it is not only a matter of doing scholarship well; above all one must first be a good person."
quoteZh: 方先生认为，“不仅学问做得好，首先做人得做得好”。

glossary.explanation: A phrase stressing moral formation as the fundamental task of education. It is prominent in Party and state education policy since the 18th Party Congress (2012).
A formulation promoted in official discourse, especially from 2023, that sets out ideals of teacher ethics and dedication.

glossary.pinyin: xué xíng bìngzhòng, dé yè shuāngxiū
glossary.en: balance learning and conduct, cultivate both virtue and vocation
glossary.literal: learning and conduct equally weighted; virtue and work both cultivated
glossary.explanation: Fang Keli's guiding principle for graduate students, first stated in 1982. It joins knowledge with practice and moral character with scholarship.

glossary.literal: strict in scholarship, lofty in conduct
glossary.explanation: An eight-character motto Fang proposed in 1998 for the CASS Graduate School. It is presented as the school's tradition and scholarly ethos.

t: Upholding the Party's cultural leadership and the cultural subjectivity of the Chinese nation
zh: 坚守党的文化领导权和中华民族的文化主体性
paras: Song Yuehong's commentary takes up Xi Jinping's statement at the symposium on cultural inheritance and development that "keeping to the fundamental principles" (守正) means upholding Marxism's guiding position in the ideological sphere, the Two Integrations, and the Communist Party's cultural leadership and the cultural subjectivity of the Chinese nation. Song presents this as a major innovative idea that gives the whole Party and people political assurance and spiritual strength for building a strong country and achieving national rejuvenation.

The article has three parts. The first argues that upholding the Party's cultural leadership bears on the fate of the Party and state. The second sets out how to sustain the Party's full leadership over propaganda, ideological and cultural work. The third lists concrete tasks for carrying out the "new cultural mission" of advancing cultural prosperity, building a strong socialist culture and building a modern Chinese civilisation.

In the first part, Song contends that cultural leadership is a political advantage of the Party. Citing Marx and Engels, the 1921 Party resolution on publications, Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping, Song says the Party has always treated it as strategic. Song also holds that it is required to protect Marxism as the "soul" and traditional Chinese culture as the "root", since the Two Integrations let Marxism renew Chinese civilisation while Chinese culture gives Marxism a Chinese style. In the second part Song argues that cultural subjectivity is consolidated through cultural confidence, core socialist values written into law and policy, and the principle that the Party manages propaganda and ideology. Song adds that the Party must keep firm control of positions in public opinion, including traditional and new media, and online ideological work.

Song's practical proposals include a fuller system of ideological responsibility, a Chinese autonomous knowledge system, stronger international communication, and a trained propaganda workforce. Further proposals are integrated management of traditional and new media, a "big propaganda" pattern under Party committees, and reform of cultural institutions and public cultural services. Song concludes that these steps will secure the Party's leadership and carry out the new cultural mission. Read the original if you want a compact, authoritative statement of the official line on cultural leadership and ideological work after Xi Jinping's 2023 cultural speech, including its institutional and media-management measures.
quoteEn: Upholding the Party's cultural leadership is a major political advantage that has enabled our Party to keep growing and strengthening.
quoteZh: 坚持党的文化领导权，是我们党不断发展壮大的一大政治优势。

glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's formula for combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with China's fine traditional culture.
The Party's authority to direct culture, ideology and public opinion, a concept with echoes of Gramscian hegemony. It is stressed in official texts since the 18th Party Congress (2012).
A term in Xi Jinping's 2023 cultural speeches for the Chinese nation's independent cultural identity and capacity to create culture on its own foundations.
Xi Jinping's formulation of 2023: advancing cultural prosperity, building a strong socialist culture and building a modern Chinese civilisation.
A set of twenty-four characters of values at the national, social and individual levels, promoted officially since the 18th Party Congress (2012).
The principle that the Party directs propaganda, media and ideological work; it is often paired with "the Party manages ideology".

t: Advancing Chinese modernization through further comprehensively deepening reform
zh: 在进一步全面深化改革中推进中国式现代化
paras: This is a study-and-interpretation commentary on the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), published in Red Flag Manuscripts. Wang Weiguang asks how the plenum's Decision on further comprehensively deepening reform should be understood and applied. The author's thesis is that deepening reform is the fundamental driving force of Chinese modernization, and that the new development philosophy and high-quality development supply its content and direction.

The article has three parts. The first sets out why reform must be placed at the centre of Chinese modernization and what characterises the new round of reform. The second explains the "Six Adherences" principles that the plenum laid down for reform. The third turns to high-quality development as the primary task, led by the new development philosophy. Wang draws throughout on the plenum Decision and on Xi Jinping's report and speech to it.

In the first part, Wang argues that reform now sits in a "deep-water zone" and must pay more attention to systems integration, to key priorities and to practical results, driven by problems. The "Six Adherences" are: the Party's overall leadership; a people-centred approach; upholding fundamental principles while breaking new ground; institution-building as the main thread; law-based governance; and a systems approach. Wang links the need for reform to shifts in the basic contradictions of society, which require continual adjustment of the relations of production and the superstructure. The third part presents new quality productive forces as an innovation-led advanced productivity, to be developed according to local conditions and not by uniform, bubble-prone campaigns. It also calls for innovation-driven development, with the state playing the leading role in key technology breakthroughs, and for institutional mechanisms that balance development with security.

Wang concludes that the path runs from the new development philosophy to high-quality development, then to Chinese modernization, and finally to the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. The author calls for unified thinking, firm resolve and thorough implementation of the plenum's measures. Read the original if you want an authoritative Party-theorist's reading of the Third Plenum's principles and of how reform, high-quality development and new quality productive forces are linked.
quoteEn: Comprehensively deepening reform is the fundamental driving force for advancing Chinese modernization.
quoteZh: 全面深化改革是推进中国式现代化的根本动力。

glossary.explanation: The Party's official formulation of China's path to modernization, prominent since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as having distinctive features, such as a huge population and common prosperity.

The six principles for further deepening reform set out by the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee in 2024: Party leadership, a people-centred approach, innovation, institution-building, rule of law and a systems approach.
The concept of innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development, put forward by Xi Jinping in 2015 as guidance for economic and social policy.
The official goal of shifting from rapid growth to development stressing quality, efficiency and innovation. The 20th Party Congress called it the primary task of building a modern socialist country.
A concept introduced by Xi Jinping in 2023 for advanced productivity driven by technological innovation. It is characterised as high-tech, high-efficiency and high-quality.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's central national goal of restoring China to national strength and prosperity, usually tied to a mid-century target.

t: Upholding, developing and improving China's new type of political party system
zh: 坚持好、发展好、完善好中国新型政党制度
paras: Ji Chunfang and Li Zhenghua present the multi-party cooperation and political consultation system led by the Communist Party of China as a "new type of political party system" and ask how it should be sustained and strengthened. Drawing on Xi Jinping's statements since the 18th Party Congress (2012), they argue that the system is a great political creation with distinctive advantages, and that the task now is to uphold, develop and improve it and to raise its effectiveness.

The article has three parts.
