The first traces the system's origins: the failure of constitutional monarchy and Western-style multi-party models after the Opium War, the Party's united front in the revolutionary period, the 1948 May Day call and the 1949 first plenary session of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference. It then follows later milestones, including the 1989 Central Committee document, the 1993 constitutional amendment, the 2021 white paper and the 20th Party Congress report (2022). The second part sets out the system's advantages, and the third its requirements for the present.

The core argument contrasts the new system with what the authors call "old-style" party systems. In their account, it represents the fundamental interests of the broadest public, because the Communist Party has no special interests of its own, and it channels the demands of different strata through consultation and democratic centralism. It avoids both the lack of oversight under single-party rule and the vicious competition of party rotation, since the democratic parties exercise consultative, cooperative supervision. It also promotes whole-process people's democracy by building consultation into decisions before and during implementation, which the authors say prevents social division.

The authors name three requirements: uphold the leadership of the Communist Party, which they call the prerequisite and fundamental guarantee; let the democratic parties and non-party figures play their role in democratic supervision and in building state power; and consolidate a common ideological and political foundation, now defined as socialism with Chinese characteristics and Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. They conclude that the system suits China's conditions and will gain vitality on the path to national rejuvenation. Read the original if you want a concise statement of the official Party narrative on the multi-party cooperation system, with its historical milestones and stated rationale.
quoteEn: China's new type of political party system has achieved a dialectical unity of democratic supervision and harmonious cooperation among parties, effectively avoiding the drawbacks of a single party lacking oversight or of multiple parties taking turns in power and competing viciously.
quoteZh: 中国新型政党制度实现了政党间民主监督与和谐合作的辩证统一，有效避免了一党缺乏监督或者多党轮流坐庄、恶性竞争的弊端。

glossary.en: new type of political party system
glossary.explanation: The official description of the system of multi-party cooperation and political consultation under Communist Party leadership. It is presented as distinct from both Western multi-party competition and one-party rule.
The eight non-Communist parties that take part in the Chinese political system. They accept the leadership of the Communist Party and take part in consultation and in government.

A concept promoted by Xi Jinping since 2019, describing democracy as covering every stage of political life, not only elections. Official sources present it as a distinctive Chinese form of democracy.
The official name for China's current path and system since reform and opening up. It is the stated common political foundation of the Party and the democratic parties.

t: Turning iron discipline into conscious action
zh: 把铁的纪律转化为自觉行动
paras: Writing in Red Flag Manuscript (2024, no. 13), Hu Yang asks how the Chinese Communist Party should understand and combine the coercive and the voluntary sides of Party discipline. The article argues that Party discipline is an inner unity of "iron discipline" and "conscious discipline": the first is the guarantee, the second the foundation. Hu presents this understanding as important for consolidating the effects of the Party discipline study and education campaign and for deepening full and rigorous self-governance of the Party.

The article has three parts. The first sets out why iron discipline is a defining trait of proletarian parties, citing Marx, Lenin, Mao Zedong, Deng Xiaoping and Xi Jinping on unity, victory over risks and challenges, and discipline as a "ruler" for cadres. The second explains why Party discipline must rest on conscious acceptance. The third turns to practical paths for strengthening discipline building.

In the second part Hu grounds conscious discipline in three bases: lofty ideals and convictions, given the Party's vanguard character; broad freedom and democracy, with discipline and freedom treated as a unity of opposites under democratic centralism; and a high degree of Party spirit. Hu uses Lenin's contrast between socialist discipline and the "discipline of the stick" and the "discipline of hunger". In the third part Hu proposes four measures: combining ideological Party-building with institutional governance, so that the "dare not, unable to, and not want to be corrupt" aims advance together; strictness across the whole chain, all levels, all elements and the whole cycle; handling Party spirit, Party style and Party discipline jointly, so as to cut the link from bad work style to corruption; and pairing incentives with constraints, strict management with care.

Hu concludes that discipline building should move officials from fear of punishment, to being unable to break rules, to not wanting to, until discipline becomes habit that is "used daily without being noticed". Hu also calls for protecting officials who take responsibility, so that strictness does not produce passivity. Read the original if you want to see how a Central Commission for Discipline Inspection researcher links Party discipline to the Marxist-Leninist canon and to current anti-corruption practice.
quoteEn: Conscious discipline and iron discipline complement each other: conscious discipline is the foundation, and iron discipline is the guarantee.
quoteZh: 自觉的纪律和铁的纪律相辅相成，自觉的纪律是基础，铁的纪律是保障。

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: A slogan associated with Xi Jinping since the 18th Party Congress (2012), covering discipline, anti-corruption and Party-building measures.
A phrase from Lenin's writings, used in Party rhetoric for strict, binding discipline within the Party.

glossary.pinyin: bù gǎn fǔ, bù néng fǔ, bù xiǎng fǔ
glossary.en: dare not, unable to, and not want to be corrupt
glossary.explanation: An official formula for anti-corruption work: deterrence by punishment, constraint by institutions, and ethical self-restraint.
The class character and Party loyalty expected of a member, emphasised in cadre education.
The Leninist organisational principle combining internal discussion with unified action once decisions are made.

t: The deep logic of how ideological and political education promotes the modernization of the human being
zh: 思想政治教育促进人的现代化的深层逻辑
paras: Starting from Xi Jinping's statement that the essence of modernization is the modernization of the human being, Wu Qiong and Lin Dongfang ask how ideological and political education can advance "the modernization of people". They treat this modernization as both the ultimate goal and a driving force of Chinese modernization. The authors argue that the education's essential attributes are closely tied to this process, and they organise the answer around three questions: why it can promote it (logical premise), by what means (logical unfolding), and how (logical aim).

The article has three sections. The first sets out the premise: the two are said to coincide in goal, share the same value content and interlock in practice. The second turns to four functions of ideological and political education: guiding direction, shaping the spirit, cultivating new people and coordinating relations. The third lists four paths that correspond to four dimensions of people's modernization: ideas, way of life, abilities and qualities, and social relations.

Wu and Lin argue that the education and human modernization point to the same end, the free and all-round development of the individual. They also hold that it serves Chinese modernization by passing on mainstream ideas and values, and that human modernization in turn pushes the education to modernize itself. In the unfolding section, the education guides people politically and in values with scientific theory and socialist core values. It builds the spiritual world, fosters hardiness, enterprise and responsibility, and promotes civilised interaction through conflict resolution, norms and consensus on shared human values. In the third section, theoretical armament is to be scientific, current and practical. Civilised social customs, including green living and a balance of material and spiritual life, are to modernize ways of life. Thinking, intellectual and labour potential are to be developed, and schools, social governance and individuals are to cooperate to modernize social relations.

The authors conclude that ideological and political education raises people's thinking, forms their character, builds their abilities and guides their behaviour, and that this is how it advances human modernization within Chinese modernization. They call for stronger theoretical education built around Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. They also call for attention to individual needs, and for the active involvement of schools, social bodies and individuals. Read the original if you want to see how Chinese scholars of ideological and political education link their discipline to Chinese modernization and to Marx's idea of all-round human development.
quoteEn: The modernization of the human being must emerge and develop in the field of serving Chinese modernization, which is inherently consistent with the value implications of ideological and political education.
quoteZh: 人的现代化需在服务于中国式现代化的场域中生成和发展，这与思想政治教育的价值意蕴内在一致。

glossary.explanation: The Party-state's system of teaching political ideas, values and morality, in schools and in society more widely. It is also an academic discipline within Marxist studies in China.

The idea that modernization covers changes in people's ideas, lifestyles, abilities and social relations, as well as in the economy and institutions. Chinese texts often cite Xi Jinping's remark that it is the essence of modernization.

The official term for China's path of modernization under Communist Party leadership, which the Party presents as distinct from Western models. It has been prominent in Party discourse since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
A set of twenty-four characters in twelve values, promoted officially since the 18th Party Congress (2012) at national, social and individual levels.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The official body of ideas associated with Xi Jinping, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017 and 2018. It is treated as the current guiding ideology.

t: Upholding and strengthening the Party's overall leadership over the reform and innovation of ideological and political theory courses
zh: 坚持和加强党对思政课改革创新的全面领导
paras: Following the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), which called for integrated reform of education and for the joint reform and innovation of ideological and political theory courses across universities, secondary and primary schools, Xu Tao asks how Party leadership should be maintained and strengthened in this work. The commentary argues that such courses are the top priority of the Party's leadership of education. It holds that since the 18th Party Congress (2012) the Central Committee has changed their environment and ecology fundamentally, and that political, ideological and organisational leadership must now be strengthened further.

The piece is organised in three parts, one for each form of leadership. The first covers political leadership and the correct direction of reform. The second covers ideological leadership and the "connotative" development of the courses. The third covers organisational leadership and a broad pattern of joint education. Xu draws throughout on Xi Jinping's remarks at the 2019 symposium for teachers of these courses and on other directives.

On political leadership, Xu argues that the Party's leadership is the fundamental experience and greatest advantage of these courses. It must keep them tied to the socialist orientation of schooling, build political identification among teachers and students, and supply institutional safeguards, with Party organisations ensuring that institutional strengths become governance effectiveness. On ideological leadership, the author calls for fostering virtue and cultivating people, with Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era at the core. This means a core course and a series of related courses, updated textbooks, and practical teaching that uses the achievements of Chinese modernization, including VR and AR technology and the "great ideological and political course".

On organisational leadership, Xu proposes that university Party secretaries and presidents personally take charge, and that university, faculty and branch Party bodies work together and are supervised through Party-building assessments. Xu also calls for strict standards in selecting, managing and assessing course teachers, and for evaluation reform and better status and pay. Finally, Xu urges coordination across school stages, between these courses and the integration of ethics education into other subjects, among staff, and with families, enterprises and society, all under unified Party leadership. The piece concludes that this will allow high-quality development of the courses within Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want an example of how a university Party secretary presents Party leadership of ideological education in official Party discourse in 2024.
quoteEn: Upholding and strengthening the Party's political leadership is the fundamental experience and greatest advantage in running ideological and political theory courses well.
quoteZh: 坚持和加强党的政治领导是办好思政课的根本经验和最大优势。

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses on Marxism, Party theory and moral education taught at all school levels in China. The Party treats them as a main channel for political education.
A long-standing educational ideal, adopted in Party documents as the fundamental task of education. It stresses moral and political formation alongside knowledge.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The official guiding ideology of the Communist Party of China, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.
The official concept for China's own path to modernisation, which the Party presents as distinct from Western models. It has been central to Party discourse since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
A policy concept that extends these courses beyond the classroom, using social practice, real-life settings and society-wide resources.

glossary.en: integration of ethics education into other subjects
glossary.explanation: The practice of building ideological and moral content into non-political courses, so that all subjects contribute to political education.

t: The threefold dimensions of ideological and political education from the perspective of the modernization of the human being
zh: 人的现代化视域下思想政治教育的三重向度
source: School Party Building and Ideological Education (学校党建与思想教育), 2024
paras: Cao and Zhang start from the claim that the essence of modernization is the modernization of the human being, meaning a shift in people's ideas, ways of thinking and ways of living from the traditional to the modern. They ask what this implies for ideological and political education. Their answer is that, seen from this angle, such education has three dimensions: individual, social and species-wide (the article's 'human' or 'generic' dimension), all oriented to the free and all-round development of the person.

The article first sets out the logical link between the two. It argues that ideological and political education carries the modernization of the human being within its values, supplies a method for achieving it through spiritual production, and must itself be modernized in response. Three sections then take each dimension in turn, drawing on Marx's three social formations, his account of world history and the 'real community', and Xi Jinping's statements on Chinese modernization.

In the individual dimension, the authors use Marx's contrast between dependence on persons and dependence on things to argue that modernization must move from an imbalance to a balance of material and spiritual life. Ideological and political education should therefore guide people towards spiritual richness, raising their spiritual needs and widening and deepening their spiritual interaction. In the social dimension, they contrast capital-driven Western modernization with Chinese modernization, which they describe as people-centred, and call on education to lead people to merge the 'small self' into the 'greater self' of nation and era. In the species dimension, they hold that individual liberation depends on the liberation of humanity, and they urge education to build global awareness and a community with a shared future for mankind on top of loyalty to the state.

The authors conclude that ideological and political education is always bound up with human activity and should keep renewing itself in order to advance the modernization of the human being. Their practical proposals include cross-cultural competence, participation in global governance and in the Belt and Road Initiative, and ecological ethics. Read the original if you want to see how Chinese scholars link Marx's theory of human development to the aims and curriculum of ideological and political education under Chinese modernization.
quoteEn: But loyalty to the state without a sense of humanity is narrow; only by guiding members of society to build a sense of humanity on the basis of loyalty to the state can it have social, historical and national justification.
quoteZh: 但是，没有人类情怀的国家忠诚是狭隘的，引导社会成员在对国家忠诚的基础上构筑人类情怀才具有社会的、历史的、民族的合理性。

glossary.explanation: The systematic education in political values, ideology and morality carried out in Chinese schools, universities and Party organisations. It is also an academic discipline within Chinese Marxist studies.
The official term for China's path of modernization under Party leadership, presented as distinct from the Western path. It stresses common prosperity and a people-centred approach.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy and theoretical concept associated with Xi Jinping. It calls for shared development, security and civilisational exchange among nations.
China's international infrastructure and economic cooperation programme, launched in 2013.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: The historical development and basic experience of building the discipline of ideological and political education
zh: 思想政治教育学科建设的历史发展与基本经验
source: Studies on the Marxist Theory Discipline (马克思主义理论学科研究), 2024 no. 7
paras: Marking the 40th anniversary of the undergraduate major in ideological and political education (established in 1984), Wu Qiantao and Du Sirui review how the discipline of the same name emerged and what its construction has taught. They argue that the discipline, which they describe as a key field positioned as the "lifeline" and "central link" of Party work, has moved from a major without a discipline to a mature discipline aligned with its major. They hold that its experience offers guidance for its "connotative development" in the new era.

The article has three parts. The first periodises the discipline's history: germination and cultivation (1984–1995), a start and exploration phase (1996–2004), and establishment and development (2005 to the present). The second sets out four areas of achievement: the core content of research, the teaching force, the training of students from bachelor's to doctoral level, and support for the university ideological and political theory courses ("Ideological and political theory courses"). The third distils three basic lessons.

The authors trace dated Party and state documents, such as the 1984 Ministry of Education notice, the 1996 doctoral programme, the 1997 listing as a second-level discipline, and the 2005 creation of Marxist theory as a first-level discipline. They then show content evolving in four strands: ideals and convictions, values, morality and the rule of law. Evidence includes staffing figures (5,650 full-time teachers in 2021, 28% of the Marxist theory total), degree-point numbers and graduate outcomes at selected institutions. The lessons are Party leadership with top-level design; building an autonomous knowledge system, drawing on traditional, revolutionary and socialist culture and distinguishing its treatment of ideals, values, morals and law from politics, philosophy, ethics and law; and joining theory to practice, by supporting the courses, talent training and practical work.

The authors conclude that the discipline's growth has depended on Party leadership, Party innovative theory and state policy support, and that its future lies in an autonomous knowledge system and in feeding research back into teaching and practice. They present this as an answer to the new tasks posed by the "two overall situations" and the goal of training new-era successors. Read the original if you want a detailed, policy-document-based institutional history of this discipline, with data on staffing and degree programmes, and the official account of its lessons.
quoteEn: Building a discipline's autonomous knowledge system is an important sign of its passing from newborn to mature.
quoteZh: 学科自主知识体系的构建是学科由新生走向成熟的重要标志。

glossary.explanation: The Party-state's system of instilling political ideals, values, morality and legal awareness, taught in schools and also carried out in workplaces and the military. It is both an area of practice and, as this article describes, an academic discipline with its own degrees.
The compulsory courses in Marxist theory, Party theory, morality and law taught at all levels of Chinese education. The article treats them as the main outlet of the discipline.
Xi Jinping's phrase for the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation and profound changes in the world unseen in a century, which are said to be unfolding together.

t: Teaching ideological and political theory courses well on the basis of the world-acclaimed achievements of socialism with Chinese characteristics
zh: 以举世瞩目成就为内容支撑讲好思政课
paras: Responding to Xi Jinping's recent instruction on school ideological and political theory courses (sizheng ke), Yan Lianfu asks how these courses can be taught well. The article argues that they must be anchored in the achievements of socialism with Chinese characteristics, which Yan says offer concrete evidence for the courses' claims. Doing so is presented as a way to strengthen students' faith, conviction and confidence and to encourage them to contribute to the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation and to Chinese modernization.

The piece has three parts. The first sets out why achievements should be the content support of these courses. The second identifies four kinds of achievement to teach: theoretical, material and technological, spiritual and cultural, and institutional. The third proposes practical paths. It was published in Qiushi's Red Flag Manuscript (Hongqi Wengao), 2024 no. 13, and Yan is dean of the School of Marxism at Xi'an Jiaotong University.

Yan argues that using achievements helps the courses explain principles in a deep, thorough and lively way. Achievements supply facts, data and cases to back theory. They enrich teaching content, widen teaching venues, and answer students' confusions about current events, including those arising online. Each type of achievement is linked to one form of confidence: theoretical achievements to theoretical confidence, material and technological ones to confidence in the path, cultural ones to cultural confidence, and institutional ones to institutional confidence. For institutions, Yan calls for explaining the 'institutional logic' behind the achievements.

For practice, Yan proposes four emphases: all courses at every level should teach achievements; teaching should keep up with new achievements; new technologies such as AI, VR and AR should be used; and teachers and students should present achievements together, with teachers leading and students acting as active participants. Yan concludes that this approach will raise the courses' relevance and appeal and ensure that the Party's cause has successors. Read the original if you want to see how a leading Marxist-college academic turns Xi Jinping's guidance into a method for teaching political theory in Chinese schools and universities.
quoteEn: To teach ideological and political courses well, one must make good use of 'spiritual and cultural achievements', cultivating people through culture and education and weaving the shaping of values into the transmission of knowledge.
quoteZh: 讲好思政课必须善用“精神文化成就”，要坚持以文化人、以文育人，寓价值观塑造于知识传授之中

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses in Marxist theory, Party history and political values taught at all levels of Chinese education. The Party treats them as a key vehicle for 'fostering virtue and cultivating talent'.
The official name for the Party's path of national development, set out prominently since the 20th Party Congress (2022).

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central goal of Party discourse since the 18th Party Congress (2012). It means restoring China to national strength and prosperity.
The Party's official name for China's socialist path since reform and opening up, covering its path, theory, system and culture.

t: Consciously shouldering the principal responsibility for building ideological and political theory courses
zh: 自觉担起思政课建设的主体责任
paras: This newspaper commentary, published in Guangming Daily on 29 July 2024, takes up Xi Jinping's May 2024 instruction that schools of all levels must consciously assume the principal responsibility for ideological and political theory courses (sizhengke). Ma argues that the changes in these courses since the 18th Party Congress (2012) owe much to schools carrying out that responsibility, and that it must be strengthened further.

The piece first explains why the responsibility is repeatedly stressed, citing Xi's March 2019 remarks and a joint General Office document of August 2019 naming Party secretaries and presidents as the "first responsible persons". It then sets out what the school's responsibility consists of, and closes with three practical measures.

Ma contends that the courses cannot be advanced by teaching departments and teachers alone. At the macro level they serve the fundamental task of fostering virtue and nurturing talent; at the micro level they demand much of teachers and so need institutional support for training, evaluation and promotion. Ma divides the duty into leadership, institution-building, and guarantee and supervision, and also into building the School of Marxism, the Marxist theory discipline, teaching quality and the teaching force.

Ma's three measures are: Party secretaries and presidents personally attend classes and direct the work; central policies are broken into indicators, responsibility lists, timetables and roadmaps; and a full system of assessment, accountability and sanctions is built. The aim is courses that students sincerely like and benefit from for life. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how the official line assigns duties for these courses to university leaders.
quoteEn: The principal responsibility for building ideological and political theory courses can only be shown through concrete measures and real results.
quoteZh: 思政课建设的主体责任只有在出实招、见真章中才能得到体现。

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses in Marxism, Party theory and moral and political education taught at Chinese schools and universities. The Party treats them as a key channel of ideological education.
An official formulation of the fundamental task of education: cultivating moral character alongside knowledge and skills.
The university unit responsible for teaching ideological and political theory courses and for the Marxist theory discipline.

t: The evolution, construction and development of the functions of ideological and political education over forty years
zh: 40年来思想政治教育功能的演进、建构与发展论析
source: Journal of Ideological and Theoretical Education (思想理论教育导刊), 2024 no. 7
paras: Marking forty years since ideological and political education was established as a university specialism in 1984, Huang Rongsheng and Liu Yunbin ask how its functions have evolved, how a functional system should now be built, and where it should go next. They argue that research moved from asking whether such education is needed to asking whether it is done well, and that the field now needs a systematic, structure-based account of its functions oriented towards high-quality development.

The article has three parts. The first traces three stages from 1984: early preparation, when the functions were discussed mainly as the "status and role" of ideological work; the proposal and creation of concepts as master's and doctoral programmes were set up from 1990 to 2004; and classification after the 2005 creation of Marxist theory as a first-level discipline. The second part builds a theoretical framework. The third sets out four orientations for the new era.

At the core, the authors criticise existing function lists, such as service, guarantee, coordination and education functions, as drawn from experience and leaving the origin of functions unclear. Drawing on systems science, they hold that structure determines function, following the logic of "elements–structure–function" and "system–whole–comprehensiveness". They sort functions into three kinds: those from a single structure (for example, the orientation function from the structure of educators, and the cognitive function from the structure of content), those from composite structures (education, shaping, regulation, motivation), and those from the whole system's place within society. For the new era, they call for four things: serving the Party and state's central tasks by explaining, rallying and securing support for Chinese modernization; optimising goals, educators and content to empower it; raising standards to promote all-round human development; and widening the field through international comparison.

The authors conclude that functions should be analysed through structure rather than listed case by case, and that the field should adopt this systemic approach while aligning its aims with the 20th Party Congress (2022) emphasis on high-quality development. They propose building international elements into curricula and improving the global communication of China's experience. Read the original if you study the disciplinary history of ideological and political education in China, or want to see how Chinese scholars apply systems theory to the field's core concepts.
quoteEn: The fundamental basis and criterion for judging whether a thing has a function, and what function it has, lies in the structure of that thing.
quoteZh: 判断一个事物是否具有功能、具有何种功能的根本性依据与标准在于该事物的结构。

glossary.explanation: The Party-state's system of moral, ideological and political instruction, taught as a university specialism and discipline and delivered in schools and elsewhere.
The official name for China's path to modernization, set out prominently in the 20th Party Congress report (2022).
An official development goal stressing quality, efficiency and innovation over speed of growth. The 20th Party Congress called it the first task of building a modern socialist country.

t: Teaching university ideological and political theory courses deeply, thoroughly and vividly on the basis of a scientific analysis of world, national, Party and popular conditions
zh: 在科学分析世情国情党情民情基础上，把高校思政课讲深讲透讲活
source: Journal of Ideological and Theoretical Education (思想理论教育导刊), 2024 no. 7
paras: He Wei takes up the question of how university ideological and political theory courses (sizheng ke) can answer student prejudices that they are unscientific, preachy or useless. Drawing on Xi Jinping's remarks at the 2019 symposium for teachers of these courses, the author argues that the basis of better teaching is a scientific analysis of the world situation, national conditions, Party conditions and popular conditions, which the article abbreviates as shiqing, guoqing, dangqing and minqing. Teaching theory within and in interaction with these four conditions, He contends, lets teachers make it deep, thorough and vivid.

The article has three main sections, each tied to one student misconception and one teaching aim. The first treats the charge that the courses are not scientific, the second the charge that they are mere preaching, and the third the charge that they are useless. Examples come from the Party-innovation theory courses on Mao Zedong Thought and Xi Jinping Thought, from the history courses (modern Chinese history, the history of the People's Republic, reform and opening up, the Party's history, the history of socialism), and from the course on ethics and the rule of law.

In the first section, He holds that the scientific character of these courses lies in their depth, legitimacy and effectiveness. Marxism, in this reading, ended speculative metaphysics by grounding theory in real conditions, so theory taught apart from the four conditions cannot be taught well. In the second, He recounts how Mao Zedong's thought emerged from the failed urban uprisings and the problems of building a Party and army in a semi-colonial, semi-feudal country, as a case of theory changing with conditions. In the third, He argues that theory is useful for understanding, for practice and for self-cultivation, and uses reform and opening up as the example. The author describes how Deng Xiaoping, Jiang Zemin, Hu Jintao and Xi Jinping responded to the changing conditions, and says that Western containment of China today differs from 1989 and exposes Western hypocrisy.

He concludes that the interplay between world conditions and China's own conditions, together with the Party's theoretical development, is the source of teachers' confidence and of courses that students both praise and attend. Teachers should therefore keep preparing and renewing content, as Xi urges. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese scholar of ideological education links course design to student attitudes and uses Party history as teaching material.
quoteEn: The vitality of theory lies in its constantly changing with changes in world, national, Party and popular conditions: reflecting change, responding to change and guiding change, so as to achieve a concrete, historical unity of theory and practice.
quoteZh: 理论的生命力，在于它始终依世情、国情、党情、民情的变化而变化，反映变化、因应变化、引导变化，实现理论与实践具体的历史的统一。

glossary.explanation: Compulsory Marxist theory and political-education courses taught in Chinese schools and universities. They include courses on Mao Zedong Thought, Xi Jinping Thought, Party history and ethics and law.

t: The value implications and practical paths of the guiding power of the patriotic spirit
zh: 爱国主义精神引领力的价值意蕴与实践路径
source: Renmin Luntan·Academic Frontiers (People's Tribune·Academic Frontiers), 2023 no. 21
paras: Starting from Xi Jinping's remark that a person without spirit cannot stand and a country without spirit cannot be strong, Zhang and Yang ask what the patriotic spirit contributes as a guiding force in the new journey of building a modern socialist country and achieving national rejuvenation. They argue that patriotism supplies spiritual inspiration, emotional cohesion and practical influence. On this basis, they say, the whole Party and people can unite as "a piece of hard steel" under the Party's banner and form a strong joint force for governing the country.

The article is in two parts. The first analyses the value implications of the patriotic spirit's guiding power under three headings: lifting morale (提振精气神), discerning major trends, and strengthening initiative. The second sets out practical paths, organised around two tasks: activating the patriotic "engine" in the spiritual lineage of Chinese Communists, and setting a patriotic orientation for young people in the new era. Each heading is divided into three sub-points, and the second part gives concrete measures for education, media and local resources.

In the first part, Zhang and Yang contend that patriotism steels political conviction, builds a self-confident and independent national character, and deepens cultural identity rooted in fine traditional culture. It also gives people a shared perspective for placing the nation's development in history. Through it, the authors link love of country with love of the Party and emotional identification with the path of socialism with Chinese characteristics. It further strengthens cultural subjectivity, moral feeling and the will to struggle. In the second part, the authors propose telling the Party's spiritual lineage in popular language, building ideological and political "gold courses" around the Outline course, and using drama series such as The Age of Awakening. They also propose developing local red tourism, offering tailored "lineage classrooms" and making short-video and other online products. For youth, they propose emotionally resonant storytelling of Party history, ritual activities such as constitutional oaths and martyrs' cemetery visits, and links between school education and social practice. They add "national-style" culture, "red gene bank" venues in physical and cloud form, and family-based education that treats loving one's family and loving one's country as one.

The authors conclude that patriotism, which Xi calls the deepest, most fundamental and most enduring part of the core socialist values, should be turned into practical drive for building a strong country and national rejuvenation. They call for a regular, long-term mechanism of patriotic education that is carried out frequently, woven into daily life and done as routine. Read the original if you want an example of how Chinese ideological and political education scholarship frames patriotism as a source of spiritual leadership, with specific proposals for the Party's spiritual lineage and for youth education.
quoteEn: The patriotic spirit is the most important spiritual asset for safeguarding national dignity and promoting national prosperity.
quoteZh: 爱国主义精神是维护民族尊严、推动国家繁荣最重要的精神财富

glossary.zh: 中国共产党人精神谱系
glossary.explanation: A series of named "spirits" (such as the Great Founding Spirit of the Party, the Long March spirit and the Yan'an spirit) that official discourse treats as the Party's inherited moral and ideological tradition. Its source is the Party's founding spirit.
A set of twelve values promoted since 2012 at the national, social and individual levels, with patriotism among the individual-level values.

t: Promoting cultural inheritance and development by strengthening history education for young people in the new era
zh: 在加强新时代青年的历史教育中推动文化传承发展
source: Renmin Luntan·Xueshu Qianyan (People's Tribune·Academic Frontiers), 2023 no. 15
paras: Xu Min and Zhu Kangyou take up Xi Jinping's call, made at the symposium on cultural inheritance and development, to build a modern civilization of the Chinese nation as a new cultural mission. They argue that young people in the new era are the vanguard and main force of this task, and that cultural inheritance and development should be advanced through stronger history education for them.

The article has two main parts. The first sets out the inner logic linking youth history education to cultural inheritance, in a theoretical and a practical strand. The second proposes concrete measures under three headings: building a knowledge system of history content, using historical and cultural heritage for practical education, and using digital technology to renew teaching methods. A short conclusion restates these three lines of work.

For the theoretical logic, the authors trace a Marxist view of youth from Marx, Engels and Lenin through Mao Zedong, Deng Xiaoping and Xi Jinping. In this account youth hold a historical position as vanguard, fresh force and successors, and that position determines their responsibility. For the practical logic, the authors point to the demanding task of the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation and to the traits of young people, who are eager to learn but open to confusion from competing currents of thought. On this basis they propose three things. Theoretical teaching should cover the history of Chinese civilization, modern Chinese history and the "four histories" (Party history, history of the People's Republic, history of reform and opening up, and history of socialist development). Practical education should draw on history museums, red education resources and volunteer work protecting heritage. Methods should use digital museums, cultural television programmes such as National Treasure and social media platforms, linking online and offline education.

The authors conclude that young people must acquire, through history education, the ability to shoulder their historical mission. They call for stronger historical theory education, wider practical education and new teaching methods, and they expect young people to take up the new cultural mission. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Chinese ideological and political education scholarship links youth, history teaching and the cultural mission set out by Xi Jinping.
quoteEn: History education for young people in the new era should fully tap the resources of historical and cultural heritage and broaden the content of practical education activities.
quoteZh: 新时代青年的历史教育，要充分挖掘历史文化遗产资源，拓展实践教育活动内容。

glossary.en: modern civilization of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: modern civilization of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A concept Xi Jinping put forward in his June 2023 speech at the symposium on cultural inheritance and development. It is presented as a new cultural mission, built on fine traditional Chinese culture and socialist cultural construction.

The history of the Communist Party of China, the history of the People's Republic of China, the history of reform and opening up, and the history of socialist development. Party education campaigns promote them as a combined subject of study.

glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The official national goal, closely tied to the Chinese Dream, of restoring China's strength and international standing by the mid-twenty-first century.

keywords: modern civilization of the Chinese nation

t: Understanding how to promote the connotative development of ideological and political theory courses in universities through upholding fundamental principles and innovating
zh: 对守正创新推动高校思政课建设内涵式发展的领悟
paras: Writing in August 2024, Mei Rongzheng takes up Xi Jinping's call to promote the "connotative development" (内涵式发展) of ideological and political theory courses in schools by combining upholding fundamental principles with innovation. Mei treats this as a key part of the connotative development of Chinese higher education. The article argues that it can pull up several aspects of the courses and push wider reform of university teaching. It sets out five areas of concern, based on problem-oriented and goal-oriented thinking.

Mei first defines connotative development as growth driven by the internal nature, laws and needs of a thing, as opposed to growth in scale. For the courses, this means that once scale, disciplinary structure and funding are secured, teachers, curricula and classroom teaching play their main roles. Reform then covers teaching philosophy, content, methods, assessment, management, research and teacher quality, so as to improve the quality of "forging souls and nurturing people". The five areas are one "fundamental" principle, one "key", one "focus", "three major relationships" and one "historical summary".

The first three areas are guidance, teachers and textbooks. Mei holds that Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era must run through every course. Teacher training is the key, because many newly hired teachers come from non-Marxist fields and have a weak grounding in Marxist theory and Party history. On textbooks, Mei asks whether the Marxist Theory Research and Construction Project textbooks are really used and used well, and calls for stronger leadership over course design and approval. Mei then considers three relationships: the Marxist theory discipline should supply academic support to the courses; publicity, student-affairs and Youth League offices should keep their separate roles; and new undergraduate majors should not drain core course teachers or hand the courses to teachers from other specialisms. Mei cites past experience of dispersing teaching across departments, which led to unstable staffing and poor quality.

Mei reviews three curriculum reforms since reform and opening up (the 1985 scheme, the 1998 scheme and the 2005 scheme) and asks which of their lessons reflect teaching laws worth upholding and which gaps need filling. The article recommends that the Ministry of Education's Department of Social Sciences set up a large research group to produce a comprehensive historical survey and a consultation report for decision-makers. It also suggests relieving teachers of non-essential duties so they have time to read and prepare. Read the original if you want an insider Chinese academic's view of current problems and policy proposals in teaching the Party's ideological and political theory courses.
quoteEn: It is not easy for teachers of ideological and political courses to explain the principles in depth, thoroughly and vividly; with too little reading and too little time spent, it cannot be done or done well.
quoteZh: 思政课教师要把道理讲深、讲透、讲活很不容易，书读少了，时间花少了是做不到、做不好的。

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses in Marxist theory, Party history and political morality taught at all levels of Chinese schools and universities.
A development model that stresses internal quality, structure and laws of a thing rather than expansion in scale; used in Chinese education policy.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义理论研究和建设工程
glossary.pinyin: Mǎkèsīzhǔyì lǐlùn yánjiū hé jiànshè gōngchéng
glossary.en: Marxist Theory Research and Construction Project
glossary.explanation: A state-sponsored project launched in 2004 that produces authoritative textbooks (often abbreviated 马工程) for social science and humanities teaching.
An official phrase describing the aim of education as shaping students' ideological convictions along with their knowledge.

t: How new quality productive forces empower the digital development of ideological and political education
st: A logical path
zh: 新质生产力赋能思想政治教育数字化发展的逻辑进路
source: Party Building and Ideological Education (学校党建与思想教育), 2024
paras: Lu Lan asks how new quality productive forces, with digital technology as their chief representative, can drive the digital transformation of ideological and political education. The article argues that borrowing concepts and methods from other disciplines is not enough and may even obscure the essence of the field. Lu contends that the field must instead grasp the characteristics of 'digital existence', where human life is increasingly rendered as data, and use this to optimise the structure and upgrade the functions of ideological and political education.

The article has three main sections, published in the journal Party Building and Ideological Education. The first describes the shift from experience-driven to data-driven education and the risks and opportunities this creates. The second examines changes in ways of thinking and the 'technological arming' of the field. The third turns to practice: how digital resources become educational value, how that value is placed in concrete scenarios and organised as an ecosystem, and where the limits of digital methods lie.

Lu's core argument rests on several moves. Internet thinking and ecological thinking, the author says, should reshape the discipline, with technology kept secondary to ideological and political education and anchored in fostering virtue and the all-round development of the person. Digital tools bring new subjects (human–machine relations), quantitative and algorithmic research, and virtual presence through VR and AR that widens the space of teaching. Lu then sets out a chain from digital resources to digital value, to scenario-based application, to an ecological scenario system. This system is described as moving data collection from static to dynamic, and as taking educational work down into people's everyday settings and grassroots grid organisations.

Lu cautions that algorithms driven by capital can crowd out mainstream values, and that over-reliance on technology risks alienating people and treating living individuals as objects of algorithmic control. The author calls for data security and shared access, and for a balance between humanistic values and technology. The article closes by invoking Weber's remark that the light of great problems still shines. Read the original if you want an example of how Chinese scholars of ideological and political education connect the concept of new quality productive forces to digitalisation, algorithms and educational practice.
quoteEn: Relative to ideological and political education, digital technology is secondary and must obey and serve ideological and political education.
quoteZh: 数字技术相对于思想政治教育是第二性的，必须服从和服务于思想政治教育。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2023 for advanced productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs and innovation. Chinese scholars present it as a development of Marxist productive-forces theory.
The Chinese discipline and practice of shaping students' and citizens' political outlook and moral values. It covers university courses and wider Party-led education work.

t: Teachers are the key to the high-quality development of ideological and political courses in universities in the new era
zh: 教师是新时代高校思政课高质量发展的关键
source: Marxist Theory Teaching and Research (马克思主义理论教学与研究), 2024 no. 3
paras: Duan Yan takes up Xi Jinping's 2019 statement that the key to running ideological and political theory courses well lies in teachers, and in drawing out their initiative, enthusiasm and creativity. Writing five years after the symposium of March 2019, the author argues that building a trustworthy, respected and capable teaching force is an inherent requirement for the high-quality development of these university courses. It is also presented as a necessary step in advancing education modernization and training talent suited to new quality productive forces.

The article has three sections. The first traces the Party's long attention to teachers, from revolutionary-era institutions such as the Anti-Japanese Military and Political University to Deng Xiaoping's 1978 remarks, and reports that the number of university ideological and political course teachers has risen to 145,000. The second explains why teachers' initiative matters, and the third sets out three proposals for strengthening the teaching force.

In Duan's account, the courses are 'essentially about reasoning', and this is hard to do well. The content spans Marxist philosophy, political economy, scientific socialism, the 'four histories' and domestic and international affairs. The students are active, curious and ready to raise sensitive questions, and the courses must constantly be renewed with modern teaching methods. Hence the 'six requirements' for teachers: strong politics, deep feeling, innovative thinking, broad vision, strict self-discipline and upright character.

Duan proposes three measures. Teachers should master the 'craft', 'scholarship' and 'way' of teaching, and teaching should follow the 'eight unities' set out by Xi. Party committees at all levels should lead, consolidate the 'great ideological and political education' pattern, expand case and material banks, run rotating training and reform evaluation and incentive systems. The author concludes that these courses should train more talent for building a strong nation and for national rejuvenation. Read the original if you want an example of how Party-aligned scholarship frames teacher development in ideological and political education under Xi Jinping.
quoteEn: The essence of ideological and political courses is reasoning.
quoteZh: 思政课的本质是讲道理

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses in Marxism and Party doctrine taught at all Chinese schools and universities, commonly shortened to 'sizheng ke'.
A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2023, referring to productive forces driven by technological innovation and high-tech sectors.
Xi Jinping's 2019 guidelines for running ideological and political courses, balancing pairs such as political and academic, and theory and practice.

t: Upholding fundamental principles and innovating to advance the content-based development of ideological and political courses
zh: 守正创新推动思政课建设内涵式发展
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily on 7 August 2024, Zhou Zhou takes up Xi Jinping's recent instruction on school ideological and political courses (sizheng ke). The commentary argues that these courses should advance "connotative" development by upholding fundamental principles while innovating, so as to raise their relevance and appeal.

The piece is organised around four commitments, each paired with a method of innovation: the socialist direction of education, the fundamental task of fostering virtue through education, a Chinese cultural standpoint, and the goal of cultivating new-era talent.

Zhou argues that the courses are above all about transmitting ideas and belief, so Marxist guidance and Party leadership are their political foundation. The Party's innovative theory, above all Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, should run through professional, compulsory and elective courses and become students' own convictions. Zhou also holds that students' confidence rests on Marxist truth, the achievements of socialism with Chinese characteristics, and the depth of Chinese civilisation, which should help them grasp the Two Integrations. Finally, Zhou calls for a "big ideological and political course" pattern in which classroom, professional, social and online teaching work together and other courses move in the same direction.

Zhou concludes that these measures serve the education of new-era talent who are reliable for the Party, patriotic and ready to take on national rejuvenation. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-state discourse on ideological education is framed for university teachers.
quoteEn: The Party's innovative theory is the most vivid theory, the weightiest thought and the most cutting-edge material for ideological and political courses.
quoteZh: 党的创新理论是思政课最鲜活的理论、最厚重的思想和最前沿的素材

glossary.explanation: Compulsory and elective courses in Chinese schools and universities that teach Marxism, Party theory and moral and political education.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.
The formula that Marxism should be integrated with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture.
An official term for the fundamental task of education: moral formation alongside knowledge.
An approach promoted by Xi Jinping that links these courses with real-life social practice and with other subjects and settings.

t: Forging souls and nurturing people with Xi Jinping Thought on Culture to strengthen students' cultural confidence
zh: 用习近平文化思想铸魂育人，增强学生文化自信
source: Teaching and Research in Marxist Theory, 2024 no. 3
paras: Wu Hongzheng asks how ideological and political education in universities should use Xi Jinping Thought on Culture, formally set out at the national conference on propaganda and ideological work in October 2023, to strengthen students' cultural confidence. Starting from Xi Jinping's "3.18" speech on ideological and political theory courses (2024), which names the Four-sphere Confidence as a direct goal of such teaching, Wu argues that this body of thought supplies the fundamental guidance for the task.

The article is a short essay in three parts, each linking Xi Jinping Thought on Culture to one educational task: fostering students' theoretical awareness of the cultural subjectivity of the Chinese nation, giving cultural confidence the support of an independent knowledge system, and guiding students to take up the mission of building a modern Chinese civilization. It was published in a journal on teaching and research in Marxist theory in 2024.

In the first move, Wu defines subjectivity as the capacity of an individual or community to make cognitive and practical judgements independently, and treats it as a condition of freedom. A nation shows cultural subjectivity when it holds to its own culture and is not penetrated by others. Wu reads China's unbroken civilisation of more than 5,000 years as proof of this, and holds that only Xi Jinping Thought on Culture has theorised it systematically. In the second move, Wu calls cultural confidence the subjective form of cultural subjectivity and says it must rest on theoretical understanding rather than blind pride. Xi Jinping Thought on Culture, with the Two Integrations (especially the "second integration" with traditional Chinese culture), supplies this understanding and counts as an independent knowledge system. Wu adds that who is educated depends on whose theory is used, and that students should be equipped to resist what the article calls Western cultural hegemonism and colonialism.

Wu concludes that educators should guide students to adopt a "grand view of history", use Marxist standpoint, viewpoint and method, creatively transform and innovatively develop traditional culture, and take part in building the modern Chinese civilization. The article describes that civilization as a new form created under Party leadership, which rejects "Western-centrism" and the "clash of civilizations" and offers a Chinese approach to the difficulties of capitalist civilization. Read the original if you want to see how Xi Jinping Thought on Culture is being set out as a teaching framework for ideological and political courses in Chinese universities.
quoteEn: Whom we train people for depends on whose theory we use to train them.
quoteZh: “为谁培养人”取决于“用谁的理论培养人”。

glossary.explanation: A body of ideas on culture presented as part of Xi Jinping's broader thought. It was formally put forward and systematically set out at the national conference on propaganda and ideological work in October 2023.
Confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics. It is a staple of Party ideological education.
The formula of combining Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture. The second element was stressed by Xi in 2021 and 2023.
A term used in Xi's 2023 culture discourse for a nation's capacity to maintain and consciously affirm its own culture while interacting with others.

glossary.literal: modern civilization of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A concept in Xi's 2023 culture discourse for a new civilizational form said to be created under Party leadership and Marxist guidance.

t: Building the foundation of strength for ideological and political theory courses on three cultures
zh: 以三种文化夯实思政课的力量根基
source: Journal of Ideological and Theoretical Education (Sixiang lilun jiaoyu daokan), 2024 no. 6
paras: Zhao Yiliang takes up Xi Jinping's recent instruction that ideological and political theory courses (sizheng courses) should treat excellent traditional Chinese culture, revolutionary culture and advanced socialist culture as their "foundation of strength". The article argues that these three cultures should underpin the courses' content, their value orientation and their teaching methods, and that doing so is a consistent requirement of the Party Central Committee for the courses' "connotative development".

The article is built around three "logics", each applied in turn to the three cultures. The first, a knowledge logic, treats the cultures as sources of cultural depth. The second, a value logic, treats them as the basis of students' beliefs and "confidence". The third, a method logic, treats them as a spur to innovation in teaching. Zhao draws heavily on Xi Jinping's speeches and writings, with occasional citations of Engels.

On the knowledge logic, Zhao argues that traditional culture supplies philosophical, moral and value resources, such as "all under heaven for the common good", the idea that rule should rest on virtue, and the people-centred idea of government. Revolutionary culture, including relics, heroes' stories and red sites, supplies teaching material and the "red bloodline". Advanced socialist culture, formed through the Two Integrations, supplies the spirit of patriotism and reform and the core socialist values. On the value logic, Zhao links traditional culture to historical and cultural confidence, revolutionary culture to confidence in the path and the system, and socialist culture to theoretical consciousness. Zhao adds that courses should uphold Marxism's guiding position and reject "non-Marxist", "pseudo-Marxist" and historically nihilist views. On method, Zhao proposes tracing origins and linking past and present when teaching traditional culture, and storytelling that joins knowledge with values, including virtual-reality and AI tools, for revolutionary culture. For socialist culture, Zhao proposes combining ideological guidance with scholarly explanation.

Zhao concludes that the three cultures should be treated as a foundational project for "fixing the root and forging the soul". They should run through the whole of ideological and political education and talent training, so as to raise the courses' relevance and appeal. Read the original if you want a detailed example of how Chinese scholars connect official cultural doctrine to the design and teaching of compulsory ideological and political courses.
quoteEn: To teach ideological and political courses well in the new era, these three cultures must be made the foundational project of fixing the root and forging the soul, running through the whole process of ideological and political education and talent training, so as to keep raising the courses' relevance and appeal and to keep advancing their connotative development.
quoteZh: 讲好新时代的思政课，必须把这三种文化作为固本铸魂的基础工程，将之贯穿于思想政治教育和人才培养全过程，不断提高思政课的针对性和吸引力，不断推动思政课建设内涵式发展。

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses on Marxism, Party history and Xi Jinping Thought taught at Chinese schools and universities. The Party treats them as the key means of moral and political education.
Formula for combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities (the first) and with its fine traditional culture (the second). The second integration was added in 2023.
Development that stresses quality, depth and substance over expansion in scale. It is widely used in Chinese education policy.

A set of twenty-four characters in twelve values, proclaimed at the 18th Party Congress (2012). They operate at national, social and individual levels, and include prosperity, democracy, patriotism and integrity.

t: Skilled at reasoning: the fundamental guideline for strengthening Marxist atheist education in university ideological and political theory courses
zh: 善讲道理：高校思政课加强马克思主义无神论教育的根本遵循
paras: Ren Baolong asks how university ideological and political theory courses (sizheng ke) can carry out the Marxist atheist education that a 2021 Party and State Council opinion on ideological and political work required. The article takes Xi Jinping's April 2022 statement that the essence of these courses is 'reasoning' (jiang daoli) as its guideline. Ren argues that 'being skilled at reasoning' means teachers must explain, in depth and thoroughly, the atheist principles embedded in each course. In Ren's view this bears on cultivating reliable successors and on securing Marxism's guiding position in the ideological sphere.

The article has three parts: why the approach is necessary, what is to be taught, and how to teach it. The first part contrasts what should be done with the actual situation. The second goes through six required courses in turn: Basic Principles of Marxism; the Introduction to Mao Zedong Thought and the Theoretical System of Socialism with Chinese Characteristics; the Introduction to Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era; the Outline of Modern and Contemporary Chinese History; Ethics and the Rule of Law; and Situation and Policy. The third part sets out teaching methods.

Ren holds that atheist education in these courses suffers from three absences: it is silent in the discipline of ideological and political education, missing from the unified textbooks, and unvoiced in teaching, because teachers are afraid to, unwilling to or unable to teach it. Drawing on Marx's remark that theory grips the masses when it is radical, Ren argues that a thorough theory still needs 'thoroughness of persuasion' to win over students. Each course is assigned its own atheist content. Examples are the people as makers of history in the principles course, atheism in the thought of Mao and later Party leaders, the Party's current religious work theory, missionaries and imperialism in the history course, and online fads such as burning incense in the ethics course. Ren also proposes lecture, practical and online teaching methods, teaching that is deep, thorough and lively, and teacher–student interaction.

Ren concludes that teachers must master and believe in Marxist atheism and set an example, while students must reflect on it actively. Teaching should use cases, everyday language and technology such as VR to answer students' sharp questions directly rather than avoid them. Ren argues that only this can resist the growing reach of theistic ideas among young people. Read the original if you want a detailed, course-by-course account of how Chinese university ideological and political courses are expected to integrate atheist education.
quoteEn: 'Thoroughness of persuasion' is also thoroughness in 'reasoning'.
quoteZh: “说服的彻底性”也即是“讲道理”的彻底性。

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses in Chinese universities that teach Marxism, Party theory, history and ethics. They are the main channel of ideological and political education.
Xi Jinping said in 2022 that the essence of ideological and political courses is to 'reason' with students. The article reads this as a method of persuasion.

The Party's official atheist position, rooted in dialectical and historical materialism. The Party promotes it in education and requires members to hold it, while policy also protects freedom of religious belief.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's guiding ideology since 2017, written into the Party and state constitutions. It has its own required university course.

t: Drawing fully on the treasure of fine traditional Chinese culture to advance the intensive development of ideological and political theory courses
zh: 充分挖掘中华优秀传统文化宝藏，推进思政课建设内涵式发展
source: Marxist Theory Teaching and Research (马克思主义理论教学与研究), 2024 no. 3
paras: Liu Shulin takes up Xi Jinping's instruction, conveyed at the 11 May 2024 conference on school ideological and political theory courses (sizhengke), that these courses should rest on Marxism and draw strength from fine traditional Chinese culture, revolutionary culture and advanced socialist culture. The author argues that, following the Second of the Two Integrations (Marxism with fine traditional Chinese culture), mining traditional culture is a major driver of what the article calls the intensive development of these courses. By this the author means real gains in guiding ideas, content, theoretical grounding and teaching method, rather than formalism.

The article is organised around five areas in which traditional culture can be put to use: experience of running schools and educating the people; ideals and beliefs; the people-based (minben) tradition; the historiographical heritage and the grand view of history; and China's tradition of proactive exchange with the outside world. Liu draws on the Book of Rites, the Book of Documents, Xunzi, the Records of the Grand Historian and other classics. These are set beside statements by Mao Zedong, Deng Xiaoping and Xi Jinping.

Liu's central claim is that classical ideas can be adopted selectively, with their feudal political content rejected, in line with Mao's call for critical use of the cultural heritage. The Book of Rites principle of mutual growth of teaching and learning is offered as a pedagogical lesson. Its contrast between the Great Unity and the moderately prosperous society (xiaokang) is read as showing that China has kept its highest ideal while setting achievable stage goals, which Liu links to Deng Xiaoping's use of xiaokang. The boat-and-water image of ruler and people, found from Xunzi to Wei Zheng, is presented as an ancestor of the Party's mass line and the people-centred approach. Historiography and the Party's two answers to the historical cycle are tied to the grand view of history, which Liu says supports opposing historical nihilism and teaching Party history. The Silk Road and Xuanzang are cited to show that Chinese civilisation was never closed.

Liu concludes that teachers should combine critical selection with absorption, using the past to serve the present and foreign learning to serve China. They should view the world through the grand view of history and support the Belt and Road Initiative and a community with a shared future for mankind. Doing so, the author holds, would improve the relevance and appeal of the courses and serve the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want to see how a Tsinghua Marxism scholar maps classical Chinese sources onto current Party doctrine for teaching ideology and politics.
quoteEn: Combining today's socialist and communist ideals and convictions with the pursuit of fine traditional Chinese culture over several millennia will open a new level for education in ideals and convictions.
quoteZh: 将今日的社会主义和共产主义理想信念与中华优秀传统文化的几千年追求相结合，便会获得理想信念教育的新境界。

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses in Marxism, Party history and political education taught in Chinese schools and universities. The Party treats them as the main channel of ideological and political education.
Formula associated with Xi Jinping: integrating Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities (the First Integration) and with fine traditional Chinese culture (the Second Integration).
Classical Chinese political idea that the people are the foundation of the state and that rulers must nurture them. Contemporary Party writers link it to the people-centred approach.
A term from the Book of Rites for a lesser ideal society. Deng Xiaoping revived it in 1979 as a development goal, and it later became an official Party target.
A viewpoint promoted by Xi Jinping that reads history across long time spans, linking past, present and future. The Party presents it as part of Xi Jinping Thought.
Official label for views that deny or denigrate the Party's revolutionary and socialist history. Party writers treat it as an ideological threat.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's foreign policy concept of a world of shared interests and responsibilities, promoted in Chinese diplomacy since the early 2010s.

t: Using scholarship to teach politics is the key to teaching ideological and political theory courses well
zh: 用学术讲政治是讲好思政课的关键
source: Journal of Ideological and Theoretical Education (思想理论教育导刊), 2024 no. 6
paras: How should university ideological and political theory courses (sizheng ke) persuade students rather than simply instruct them? Luo and Liu argue that the essence of these courses is to "explain the reasons" behind politics, and that the key is "using scholarship to teach politics": offering a Marxist, theory-based account of major historical and current political questions. In their view this strengthens the scientific and logical force of the courses and helps students build firm ideals and convictions.

The article has three parts. The first takes Xi Jinping's formula that political firmness comes from theoretical clarity and breaks firmness into political direction, the ability to judge right and wrong, and steady political resolve. The second traces theoretical clarity to three sources: the universal truth of Marxism, Marxism adapted to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, and the unity of Marxism's truthfulness and its value orientation. The third sets out what the authors call the key requirement for teaching the courses.

The authors hold that political character is the fundamental attribute of these courses and academic rigour their essential feature, so the two must be united. They propose three methods. Teachers should explain historical trends through the basic contradictions of capitalism and the claimed inevitability of socialism's victory. They should use international comparison, citing GDP and purchasing-power figures for China, the United States, India and Japan and contrasting China with Western political systems, to build political confidence. They should use the Party's century of struggle to deepen political identification. The authors also urge teachers to engage sensitive student questions and to criticise erroneous social trends, and they quote Mao Zedong that people must be persuaded, not coerced.

The authors conclude that teachers who themselves hold Marxist convictions and have real theoretical command can win students over by the force of truth. Students would then support Party leadership and socialism with Chinese characteristics and take part in Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want to see how Chinese ideological-education scholars justify and operationalise the link between academic argument and political education, including the comparative data and China–West contrasts they recommend using in class.
quoteEn: The essence of ideological and political theory courses is to explain the reasons, and using scholarship to teach politics is the key to teaching them well.
quoteZh: 思政课的本质是讲道理，用学术讲政治是讲好思政课的关键。

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses in Chinese schools and universities on Marxism, Party history and socialism with Chinese characteristics. They are presented officially as the main channel for moral and political education.

glossary.literal: use scholarship to speak about politics
glossary.explanation: The authors' formula for explaining political questions through Marxist theory and academic reasoning, rather than through slogans or assertion.
The Party's official description of China's own path to modernity, promoted since the 20th Party Congress (2022) as distinct from Western models.

keywords: Marxism adapted to the Chinese context

t: Practical guidelines for ideological and political education in the digital age
zh: 数字化时代思想政治教育的实践遵循
source: Research on Ideological Education (思想教育研究), 2024 no. 6
paras: How should ideological and political education respond to big data, algorithms and artificial intelligence? Wang Tianmin argues that it must accept the arrival of the digital age and adapt to it, but on a people-centred footing. Digital technology, in this view, is an objectification of human essence and so serves education, and the principle of 'putting people first' must remain the guide throughout.

The article has three parts. The first justifies digitalisation theoretically, drawing on Marx's thinking on humans as 'objectifying' beings, on needs, and on the human essence as the ensemble of social relations. The second asks how digital tools can deepen the people-centred educational idea. The third turns to practice: how digital technology enters research and educational work, and how its quality can be raised.

Wang's central move is that digital technology, like earlier technology, confirms human essence, since it turns people and their world into data that humans themselves invented. From this the author draws three advantages for educators. Aggregated data and big data give a holistic picture of the person, avoiding one-sided concepts. They track people as they develop, avoiding fixed and static definitions. And they present people together with their world, avoiding the separation of subject and object. In practice, Wang adapts a three-step model of AI-assisted research to education. The educator poses the problem, the system gathers data and generates plans, and the educator refines, tests and evaluates them against the goals set by the state and society.

Wang calls for educators to convert principles, policy documents, cases and methods into digital information and to build a growing digital resource base that reflects the will of the Party and state. The article calls cyberspace a frontline of ideological work and says digital positions must be strengthened to train a new generation for national rejuvenation. It holds that digital education is still at an early stage and cannot fully replace offline, embodied teaching. Technology remains an auxiliary means whose outputs must be checked against educational goals, so that people are not dominated by machines. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese scholar grounds the digitalisation of ideological and political education in Marxist philosophical anthropology and in practical workflows.
quoteEn: Putting people first is the basic principle that ideological and political education has always upheld.
quoteZh: 以人为本是思想政治教育始终坚持的基本原则

glossary.explanation: A field and practice in Chinese universities and society that aims to shape people's political views, ideals and moral character in line with Party and state goals.
A principle prominent in official discourse since the early 2000s, here applied to education as treating the person as its basis and aim.

t: Keeping the development of ideological and political courses in step with arming minds with the Party's innovative theory
zh: 坚持思政课建设与党的创新理论武装同步推进
paras: This newspaper commentary, published in Guangming Daily in July 2024, takes up an instruction Xi Jinping gave in May 2024: that the building of ideological and political courses (sizhengke) in schools should advance in step with arming people with the Party's innovative theory. Qin Fayue, a university vice-president, argues that the two tasks are inherently consistent.
