In Qin's account, the principle is a long-standing tradition of Party leadership, a requirement for opening a new phase of ideological education, and a safeguard for raising a new generation fit for the era.

The article is organised in three parts. The first traces the principle through four historical periods: the new-democratic revolution, socialist revolution and construction, reform and opening up, and the period since the 18th Party Congress (2012). The second sets out what the principle demands today, and the third explains how it supports the cultivation of "new people of the era". It closes with a section on the role of teachers.

For the historical part, Qin lists the courses offered at each stage, from Marxism and "political common sense" in revolutionary-era schools to the Marxism-Leninism and Mao Zedong Thought courses of the 1950s. Qin concludes that each step in curriculum building coincided with a step in theoretical education. For the present, Qin calls for a curriculum and textbook system centred on Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era and led by the course introducing that thought. Qin also proposes AI-enabled smart classrooms and a "big ideological and political course" that joins the classroom, society and online spaces, with examples such as lessons held in fields, venues and workshops.

Qin further argues that the achievements of socialism with Chinese characteristics since 2012 should serve as teaching content, so that students come to appreciate the system's advantages and strengthen their confidence in it. Qin calls for a teaching force that is politically strong and broad in vision, able to convey the substance of the Party's theory accurately. Read the original if you want a concise example of how the official line on ideological and political education is presented, including its historical narrative and practical measures.
quoteEn: Each time theoretical innovation advances a step, theoretical armament must follow a step behind.
quoteZh: 理论创新每前进一步，理论武装就要跟进一步。

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses in Chinese schools and universities that teach Marxism, Party theory and official values. They are treated as the main channel of political education for young people.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018. It is now the core content of the ideological and political curriculum.
A Party term for the young generation it aims to cultivate, described as loyal to the Party, patriotic and ready to take on national rejuvenation.
A concept promoted from 2021 that extends political education beyond the classroom into social practice, community resources and online platforms.

t: Integrating discourse into the classroom: methodological innovation in university ideological and political theory courses
zh: 话语融课：高校思政课的方法创新
paras: Dai Yuqi, writing in Study Times in July 2024, asks how university ideological and political theory courses can become more attractive and effective. The commentary argues that innovating the discourse system should lead the renewal of teaching methods. It identifies persistent classroom problems: grandiose talk, stiff talk, stale talk and monologue by the teacher.

The piece asks teachers to settle "for whom, what and how" they teach, while holding to fundamental principles and innovating. It is organised around four paired formulas for changing how things are said: big talk told small, hard talk told soft, old talk told anew, and talk shared by many.

Dai's central move is to treat contrasting registers as complementary rather than opposed. Grand theory and Party achievements should be taught with political firmness, but introduced through small, everyday cases that reveal larger themes. Dai likewise pairs "indoctrination" with "inspiration", citing Xi Jinping: firm language states political positions and keeps teaching accurate, while gentler language builds an open atmosphere, and teachers should switch between them as the situation requires. Old content should be refreshed with new vocabulary, internet language, differentiated teaching for different student groups, and integration of ideological and political education across school stages. Finally, the author calls for a "big ideological and political course" in which schools, families and society cooperate, and in which policymakers, grassroots workers, beneficiaries and students themselves also speak in class.

Dai concludes that discourse innovation makes these courses more targeted, approachable and effective. It is meant to unify students' knowledge, feeling, will and action, and to train new-era talents who take on the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want a short, practice-oriented example of how Party-affiliated academics frame teaching-method reform in ideological and political courses.
quoteEn: Innovation in the discourse system is an important means of keeping university ideological and political courses abreast of the times and of strengthening their relevance and effectiveness.
quoteZh: 话语体系的创新是推动高校思政课与时俱进、增强针对性和实效性的重要手段。

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses in Chinese schools and universities that teach Marxism, Party theory, history and morality. They are central to the Party's ideological education of students.
A policy concept that extends ideological and political education beyond the classroom to social practice and to cooperation among schools, families and society.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: An official goal of restoring China's strength and international standing, closely associated with the Chinese Dream and Xi Jinping's leadership.

t: Telling the ideological and political course well, with the world-noted achievements as its content support
zh: 以举世瞩目成就为内容支撑讲好思政课
paras: Writing in Red Flag Manuscripts (2024, no. 13), Yan Lianfu takes up Xi Jinping's recent instruction that schools' ideological and political courses (sizheng ke) should draw their content from the remarkable achievements of socialism with Chinese characteristics. Yan's thesis is that teaching these achievements is a requirement of the new period and the way to make such courses reason in a deep, thorough and lively manner, and to help students strengthen belief, conviction and confidence.

The article has three parts. The first sets out why achievements should anchor the courses. The second says which kinds of achievement teachers should draw on: theoretical, material and technological, spiritual and cultural, and institutional. The third proposes practical routes, each organised around one word: quan (all), xin (new), ji (technology) and gong (together).

Yan argues that achievements supply facts, data and cases that verify the theory taught, so that courses can answer students' questions and respond to confusion in a complicated online ideological environment. Each type of achievement is tied to a form of confidence. Theoretical achievements, including the Two Integrations and Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, support confidence in theory. Material achievements support confidence in the path, spiritual and cultural ones support confidence in culture, and institutional ones support confidence in the system. On method, Yan calls for every course at every level to teach achievements, for new achievements to enter teaching promptly, for AI and digital tools to enrich resources and identify student needs, and for students as well as teachers to tell the story of achievements.

Yan concludes that teachers should lead while students act as active subjects, so that students become communicators and practitioners of the achievements of socialism with Chinese characteristics. The piece shows how Party-line guidance on ideological and political education is turned into teaching practice. Read the original if you want a detailed, officially aligned account of how Chinese university ideological and political courses are told to use national achievements, digital technology and student participation in teaching.
quoteEn: To teach ideological and political courses well, one must rely on institution-building and make clear the "institutional logic" behind the great achievements. Students should fully recognise the "thirteen notable advantages" of China's state system and national governance, so that seeds of confidence in the system are sown in their minds and a surging, tireless drive to strive is aroused.
quoteZh: 讲好思政课必须依托制度建设，讲清楚伟大成就背后的“制度逻辑”，使学生充分认识我国国家制度和国家治理体系的“十三个显著优势”，把制度自信的种子播撒进学生心灵，激发其不懈奋斗的澎湃力量。

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses in Marxist theory, Party history and political values taught at every level of Chinese education. They are officially described as the key courses for fostering virtue and cultivating talent.
A formula for combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture. It is used in official discourse as the path of adapting Marxism to China.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's guiding ideology since the 19th Party Congress (2017), written into the Party and state constitutions. Officially it is presented as the Marxism of contemporary China.
The official name for China's path since reform and opening up. It combines Party leadership, a socialist system and a market economy under Chinese conditions.

t: Telling the story of the modern civilization of the Chinese nation well in university ideological and political courses: what should, must and can be done
zh: 高校思政课讲好中华民族现代文明的应然、必然与实然
source: School Party Building and Ideological Education
paras: Qi Weiping and Bai Jinyan ask how university ideological and political courses (sizheng courses) should incorporate the modern civilization of the Chinese nation, a concept the authors link to Chinese modernization. Their thesis is that teaching it well is something the courses ought to do (yingran), must do (biran) and can do through concrete methods (shiran).

The article is organised in three parts that follow this triad. The first argues that the concept enriches course content by connecting the Party's history, its present practice and its new mission. The second sets out why it is indispensable for moral education and the cultivation of talent (lide shuren). The third offers four practical approaches: political orientation, content, teaching formats and new media. A short conclusion draws on the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022).

In the authors' account, the modern civilization of the Chinese nation is the sum of the material and spiritual civilization created under the Communist Party's leadership in the course of modernization. It continues Chinese civilization and expresses the Chinese path to modernization and a new form of human civilization. The authors argue that teaching it deepens study of the Party's innovative theory, including the Two Integrations and Xi Jinping's thought on culture. They also say it builds a shared ideological basis for national rejuvenation and supports the all-round development of the person, which they contrast with Western modernization under the logic of capital. They further claim it strengthens students' cultural confidence against trends such as money worship, hedonism and historical nihilism.

On method, the authors call for adherence to the socialist orientation of education and for linking theory with practice through investigation and practical classes. They propose comparing Chinese modernization with world civilizational patterns, using Marxist social-formation theory to locate the present stage, and drawing on virtual and online teaching, social media and open online courses. They conclude that teachers should grasp all three dimensions in order to raise the effectiveness of the courses and build a youth base for national rejuvenation. Read the original if you want to see how Chinese scholars of Party education justify and operationalise new official concepts within the sizheng curriculum.
quoteEn: The modern civilization of the Chinese nation is important material for keeping university ideological and political courses abreast of the times.
quoteZh: 中华民族现代文明是高校思政课与时俱进的重要素材

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses in Marxism, Party history and national conditions taught in Chinese universities and schools to instil the official worldview and values.

glossary.en: modern civilization of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A concept introduced in Xi Jinping's 2023 speech on cultural inheritance and development. It denotes the civilization built under Party leadership in the course of modernization.
The official term for China's path to modernization, presented as distinct from Western models. It has been central to Party discourse since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
The Party formula of combining Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities and with China's fine traditional culture.

glossary.en: moral education and the cultivation of talent
glossary.explanation: The stated fundamental task of Chinese education: fostering moral character while training capable people.

keywords: modern civilization of the Chinese nation

t: Leading high-quality development of ideological and political education in the new era through integrated construction
zh: 以一体化建设引领推动新时代思政教育高质量发展
paras: Writing in the People's Daily on 22 July 2024, Weng Tiehui, a Vice Minister of Education, takes up the call from Xi Jinping to deepen the integration of ideological and political education across universities, secondary schools and primary schools. The piece appeared on the fifth anniversary of the 2019 symposium on school ideological and political theory teachers. Weng argues that integration bears on the basic educational questions of whom to train, how to train them and for whom, and that it should be pursued by following educational regularities and innovating in practice.

The commentary is organised in three parts. The first gives reasons why integration is of the utmost importance for ensuring the Party has successors. The second sets out how to overcome difficulties by focusing on pertinence and effectiveness. The third lists key links and priority areas: curriculum, practical teaching, evaluation, teaching staff and overall support. It is framed as a study of the spirit of the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) and as a contribution to building a leading education country.

Weng gives three grounds for integration: the political nature of education, which the Party has stressed through successive policy changes; the need to train talent for Chinese modernization; and the fundamental task of fostering virtue through education, which requires that courses, course-embedded ideological education and daily education not become isolated "islands". On method, Weng argues that stages should share one consistent direction while goals rise step by step. Patriotic education, for example, would start with emotional enlightenment in primary school and move to firm ideals and convictions at university. Weng also names unresolved problems, including weak links between knowledge and values, between theory and practice, and between teachers at different stages, and research on how students at each stage receive such education.

Weng proposes unified curriculum and textbook planning, more interactive teaching, and practical teaching outside the classroom that builds the Four-sphere Confidence. Weng warns against turning specialist courses into political courses and against "low-level red" and "high-level black" distortions. Other proposals are multi-dimensional evaluation that prioritises teaching, stronger teacher training, family–school–society cooperation, and leadership mechanisms with ideological education written into school planning and Party-building assessments. Read the original if you want an authoritative Ministry of Education statement of how integrated ideological and political education is to be organised and assessed in 2024.
quoteEn: School ideological and political work covers many areas, such as ideological and political courses, ideological and political education within other courses, and daily ideological education, and these cannot be isolated "islands".
quoteZh: 学校思政工作涉及思政课程、课程思政、日常思政教育等许多方面，不能是一座座“孤岛”。

glossary.explanation: The official Party formulation of China's own path to modernization, prominent since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.
Official slogan for confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics. It is a standard aim of ideological education.
The official fundamental task of education, stressing moral and political formation alongside knowledge. Xi Jinping has repeatedly called it the criterion for judging school work.
Dedicated ideological and political theory courses are distinguished from the integration of ideological and moral content into ordinary subject courses.

t: Key focal points for advancing ideological and political theory courses in the new era
zh: 推进新时代思想政治理论课建设的几个着力点
source: Marxist Theory Discipline Research (马克思主义理论学科研究), 2024 no. 6
paras: Writing after Xi Jinping's fresh instructions on ideological and political theory courses (known as sizheng courses) on the fifth anniversary of the 2019 symposium for their teachers, and after a national promotion meeting on 11 May 2024, Pang Jinju asks how these courses should be built in the new era. The article's answer is that they must be tied to the fundamental task of fostering virtue through education and cultivating successors to the socialist cause. Pang identifies five areas of emphasis.

The article proceeds in five numbered sections. It covers the mission of the courses and the responsibility for training a new generation; the reform of the curriculum and textbook systems; the updating of teaching content; the combination of classroom teaching with social practice; and Party leadership and teacher training. Pang draws heavily on Xi's remarks from 2019 to 2024 and on official data about achievements since 2012.

Pang argues that Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era should be the "soul" of moral education. The current curriculum rests on the 2005 "05 scheme", which Pang credits with a historic role but says must now be updated. Pang points to the new required course and textbook on the Thought as the direction of reform. Teaching content should bring in the Party's innovative theories and the achievements of the new era, citing poverty alleviation, GDP growth, reform and opening up, and improved livelihoods. Textbooks change slowly, so teachers must convert them into teaching. The "big ideological and political course" should join the classroom to social practice, covering past, present and future practice. Pang warns that practice must not replace classroom teaching, nor should teaching be confined to the classroom.

Pang concludes that Party committees at all levels must take political responsibility for these courses, building a coordinated working pattern. Teachers are the foundation and the key. Pang calls for them to meet Xi's requirements of strong politics, deep feeling, fresh thinking, broad vision, strict self-discipline and upright character. Pang also calls for a sound teacher evaluation system and better status and conditions for teachers. Read the original if you want a Party-line account of how senior figures in the field frame current priorities for political education in Chinese universities.
quoteEn: To keep the development of these courses in step with arming minds with the Party's innovative theory, one must both strengthen textbook development and revise textbooks in good time, and fully mobilise teachers' enthusiasm and creativity.
quoteZh: 坚持思政课建设与党的创新理论武装同步推进，既要加强教材建设，适时修订教材，又要充分调动教师的积极性和创造性

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses in Marxism and Party doctrine taught in Chinese schools and universities, usually abbreviated sizheng courses (思政课).
A stated fundamental task of Chinese education, meaning that moral formation comes first in cultivating talent.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.
A slogan from Xi Jinping meaning that political education should be taught in society and through practice as well as in classrooms.

t: Unwaveringly promoting the high-quality development of ideological and political theory courses in the new era
zh: 坚定不移推进新时代思想政治理论课高质量发展
source: Studies on the Marxist Theory Discipline (Marxism Theory Discipline Research), 2024 no. 6
paras: Jin Nuo takes up how ideological and political theory courses (sizheng ke) in Chinese schools and universities should develop in the new era. Writing after Xi Jinping's latest instructions on these courses, Jin argues that they are the key course for implementing the fundamental task of fostering virtue through education and the first front for teaching the Party's innovative theory. The article contends that high-quality development requires applying the worldview and methodology of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era.

The article is organised around four methodological principles drawn from that worldview: self-confidence and self-reliance, a problem-oriented approach, systems thinking, and staying true to fundamental principles while breaking new ground. Each section links the principle to concrete measures, including policy documents, textbooks, teacher training, practice bases, digital platforms and Ministry of Education programmes. It draws on Xi's speeches, including his 2019 symposium with teachers of these courses, and on citations from Marx.

In the first section, Jin argues that there are grounds for confidence in running the courses well. These are the Party Central Committee's attention to the work, the achievements of socialism with Chinese characteristics, China's traditional, revolutionary and socialist culture, and accumulated experience. The second section holds that the courses must answer students' real questions by explaining reasoning in depth, thoroughly and vividly. Jin criticises teaching that reads from scripts, favours form over substance, or fails to refute erroneous trends of thought. The third section presents the 'big ideological and political course' as extending teaching beyond the classroom through links between these courses and course-embedded ideological education, between teachers and students, and between schools and society.

In the fourth section, Jin calls for precise understanding of students' circumstances, content that joins theory, history and present reality, varied teaching methods, and digital tools such as cloud-based resource banks and smart classrooms. The conclusion calls on educators to be guided by Xi Jinping Thought and to do their utmost to run the courses well. Jin presents this as the way to raise the younger generation to meet the expectations of the Party, the state and the people. Read the original if you want a detailed, officially aligned account of current policy, institutions and teaching practice in China's ideological and political education.
quoteEn: The essence of ideological and political courses is to reason things out; attention must be paid to method, so that the reasoning is made deep, thorough and lively.
quoteZh: 思政课的本质是讲道理，要注重方式方法，把道理讲深、讲透、讲活

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses in Chinese schools and universities that teach Marxism, Party theory and official history and values. Usually abbreviated as sizheng ke.
A stated fundamental task of Chinese education: shaping students' moral and political character as well as their knowledge.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.
A concept promoted since 2021 that extends ideological and political education from the classroom into social practice, bases and society at large.

glossary.literal: ideology and politics in the curriculum
glossary.explanation: The practice of building ideological and political content into all subjects, not only the dedicated theory courses.

glossary.en: staying true to fundamental principles while breaking new ground
glossary.explanation: A methodological principle in Xi-era discourse that combines fidelity to basic principles with innovation.

t: Strengthening the building of the teaching force for ideological and political theory courses
zh: 加强思政课教师队伍建设
paras: This short commentary, published in Guangming Daily in July 2024, takes up Xi Jinping's recent instruction on school ideological and political theory courses. Zhang Jingmei explains how to build a teaching force that is, in Xi's formulation, strong in politics, deep in feeling, new in thinking, broad in vision, strict in self-discipline and upright in character. Zhang treats these six requirements as general guidance for raising the quality of the teaching force in the new era.
The article is organised as six sections, one for each requirement. Each section sets out three practical demands on teachers, and Zhang draws on Xi's earlier remarks on teachers and on the courses.

On political strength, Zhang calls on teachers to hold to the Party's leadership, grasp the significance of the Two Establishes, practise the Two Upholds and take the Four-sphere Confidence to students. They should also truly believe in Marxism themselves, since belief must first take root in teachers before it can bear fruit in students. The sections on feeling, thinking and vision ask teachers to cultivate love of country, of the people and of education, to keep pace with the information age and avoid reciting textbooks, and to broaden their knowledge and compare China with other countries without being closed or servile to the West. The sections on self-discipline and character stress ethical conduct, consistency of word and deed online and offline, and loyalty to the Party, country and people. Zhang also asks teachers to treat students with care and be their mentors and friends.

Zhang concludes that these six qualities together define what a high-quality teaching force requires. They are meant to produce a new generation committed to national rejuvenation. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official guidance on teacher conduct and the ideological and political courses is presented in the Party-state press.
quoteEn: Teachers of ideological and political courses should keep renewing their educational ideas, teaching content and methods, so as to make the courses more attractive.
quoteZh: 思政课教师应不断更新教育理念、教学内容和方式方法，增强思政课的吸引力。

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses in Marxism, Party theory, morality and law taught at all levels of Chinese schools and universities.
A formula from the Party's 2021 historical resolution, affirming Xi Jinping's position as the core of the Party and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought.
A Party requirement to uphold Xi Jinping's core position in the Party and the authority and centralised leadership of the Central Committee.
Confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics, a formula promoted since the 18th Party Congress.

t: The world dimension of innovative development in ideological and political education in the new era
zh: 论新时代思想政治教育创新发展的世界向度
source: Journal of Ideological Education Studies (Sixiang jiaoyu yanjiu), 2024 no. 6
paras: Zeng Linghui and Bu Luping ask how ideological and political education in China, forty years after it was established as an academic discipline, should develop beyond its domestic mission. They argue that, besides answering the questions of China and of the people, it must now answer "the questions of the world" against the backdrop of what official discourse calls changes unseen in a century. The authors propose four capacities that together form a new world-facing dimension: harmonious coexistence, narrative communication, discursive interpretation and self-confidence.

The article is organised as four sections, one for each capacity. It draws heavily on Xi Jinping's statements on civilisational diversity, telling China's story well and handling foreign theories critically. It gives examples from domestic practice, including implicit education, environmental education, ritual education and the "big ideological and political course", and lists channels such as Xinhua, CCTV international, social media, Confucius Institutes and academic exchange. It closes with a discussion of China's global governance proposals.

First, the authors argue that harmonious coexistence means critically borrowing from other countries' ideological education without replacing one model with another, while holding to the basic Marxist standpoint when dealing with Western thought. Second, they say narrative communication requires creative transformation of paradigms, so that traditional Chinese culture, Marxism adapted to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, and online narratives become intelligible to international audiences. This also needs new carriers (text, image, digital) and platforms, so that China's reasoning no longer "cannot be voiced or spread". Third, discursive interpretation is said to be weak because the field still describes experience rather than explaining it; the authors call for new theory and shared international discourse on a community with a shared future for mankind.

On self-confidence, Zeng and Bu hold that it rests on Marxist guidance, on active participation in international exchange and on communicating China's global governance proposals. They conclude that the field must "keep to principles and innovate", holding fast to the Marxist standpoint and to the stance of Chinese culture and modern civilisation, in order to build new discourse and narrative forms and to avoid falling silent in global exchanges. Read the original if you want to see how Chinese ideological education scholars frame the discipline's international communication tasks and the vocabulary they use for them.
quoteEn: Ideological and political education, in facing the world, must creatively transform its narrative and communication paradigm, connect effectively with international discourse and build platforms for exchange between Chinese and Western thought.
quoteZh: 思想政治教育面向世界既要创造性转化思想政治教育叙事传播范式，实现有效对接国际话语，搭建中西思想交流平台

glossary.explanation: A Chinese academic discipline and practice, established as a discipline in 1984, covering the teaching of Party ideology, political values and morality in schools and society.

glossary.zh: 世界百年未有之大变局
glossary.pinyin: shìjiè bǎinián wèi yǒu zhī dà biànjú
glossary.literal: great changes in the world not seen in a hundred years
glossary.explanation: A phrase used in Chinese official discourse, notably by Xi Jinping since 2017, to describe a shifting global order and the relative rise of emerging powers.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign policy and theoretical concept promoted by Xi Jinping since 2012–13, calling for cooperative global governance and shared development.
A teaching approach promoted by the Chinese authorities in which ideological education extends beyond the classroom into society and practical settings.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: On determining the principal contradiction of ideological and political education
zh: 论思想政治教育主要矛盾的判定
source: Research on Ideological Education (思想教育研究), 2024 no. 6
paras: Kuang Ning and Wang Xisheng take up a basic question in the theory of ideological and political education: what is its principal contradiction? They note that research on the topic is thin and that scholars disagree. Their thesis is that, in any given period, the principal contradiction is a single opposition-and-unity between ideological and political educators and the people educated, located at the level of their respective needs.

The article has three parts. It first surveys four representative views in the 40 years since the discipline was founded. These identify the contradiction from the constituent elements of the field, from conflicts within the educational process, from tensions in practical work (for example a single guiding ideology versus diverse social trends), and from the function of nurturing people. It then sets out criteria for judging a principal contradiction, and finally applies them to identify its two sides, its object and its nature. The authors say a later study will trace historical practice under the Communist Party.

The authors identify four disagreements: whether the contradiction is one or many, who its two sides are, at what level it operates, and whether it is mere difference or true opposition and unity. They answer by defining the concept, drawing on Mao Zedong's analysis of contradiction. A principal contradiction holds the dominant position, decides the nature and direction of the field and conditions the secondary contradictions. It changes between historical stages but is stable within one, and in any given period there can be only one. Two principal contradictions, they argue, would each be unable to dominate the other, which is incoherent.

Applying these criteria, the authors argue that the two sides must be educators and educated, the most basic elements in every scheme of the field's components, rather than content, methods or environment. The educators are a collective representing the will of the Party and state, and the educated include all members of society. The object of the contradiction is need, not ideas, since explaining behaviour by thought rather than need would repeat the old materialism Engels criticised. Educators must guide people according to the demands of Party and state, while the educated have varied needs and may bargain over ideas. Read the original if you want a systematic conceptual account of how Chinese theorists define and justify a principal contradiction in ideological and political education.
quoteEn: The principal contradiction of ideological and political education should be the relation of both opposition and unity, at the level of "needs", between "ideological and political educators" and "the educated" in a "specific period".
quoteZh: 思想政治教育主要矛盾应该是“特定时期”“思想政治教育者”与“教育对象”在“需要”层面的既相对立又相统一的关系

glossary.explanation: The Party-state's system of teaching political ideology, values and morality, in schools and in wider society. It is also an academic discipline in China, founded in the 1980s.
A concept from Mao Zedong's essay 'On Contradiction'. In a complex of contradictions, one is dominant and decides the nature and course of the others.
The people and institutions that carry out ideological and political education on behalf of the Party and state. The authors treat them as a collective, not individual teachers.
In this Marxist usage, needs are the underlying drives behind people's thoughts and actions. The authors place the principal contradiction at this level, not at the level of ideas.

t: An ideological and political education interpretation of "ideological reality" (sixiang shiji)
zh: “思想实际”的思想政治教育学阐释
source: Ideological and Political Education Research (Sixiang jiaoyu yanjiu), 2024 no. 6
paras: Marking the 40th anniversary of ideological and political education as an academic discipline, Ye Fangxing takes up "ideological reality" (sixiang shiji), a phrase that appears constantly in Party documents and everyday speech but is usually treated as self-explanatory. The article argues that it should be recognised as a core concept of the discipline. In Ye's account it denotes the actual state of people's thinking and spirit, and it supplies the factual premise on which ideological and political education must be built.

The article first defines the concept and distinguishes it from "work reality" (gongzuo shiji). It then sets out four features: its factual, structural, evaluative and typological character. Next it considers the concept's place in the discipline, and it ends with principles for investigating ideological reality. It draws on Marx and Engels (including The Condition of the Working Class in England), on Durkheim's Moral Education, and on Party documents and Chinese scholarship in the field.

Ye's central move is to hold together fact and norm. Ideological reality is an observable, measurable "ideological fact", centred on values, especially political values. Yet it is "what is", not "what ought to be": it must be assessed against the aims of ideological and political education, and observing it is only the starting point of that work. Ye also divides it into three types (overall, group and individual) and into cognitive, emotional and value layers. Ye further argues that it reflects people's social being, since what people think corresponds to how they live.

On this basis Ye treats ideological reality as a starting category of the discipline. Grounding work in it is described as a practical premise, a long-standing principle of the Party's ideological and political work, and a standard of effectiveness, because education that misses it becomes "ideological idling". Ye urges investigation that combines overall and differentiated views, fact and norm, and macro and micro approaches, with the individual and micro level needing the most strengthening through oral history, narrative and in-depth interviews. The article concludes that describing concepts of this kind gives theoretical research in the field an empirical footing. Read the original if you study the conceptual foundations of Chinese ideological and political education or the Party's tradition of investigation and research.
quoteEn: "Ideological reality" is what is the case, but it is not thereby what ought to be.
quoteZh: “思想实际”是“实然的”但并不是“当然的”。

glossary.explanation: The Chinese Party-state's system of value guidance and political education, practised in schools, workplaces and Party organisations. It is also an academic discipline, founded in 1984, studying that practice.
The actual state of people's thinking, attitudes and values at a given time. It is usually paired with "work reality" in Party methodology, which calls for work to be tailored to both.
The concrete conditions of the work in question, such as its methods, progress and results. It is the companion of "ideological reality" in the Party formula of combining thought and work conditions.

t: Upholding fundamental principles and breaking new ground to promote the connotative development of ideological and political theory courses
zh: 守正创新推动思政课建设内涵式发展
paras: Responding to a recent directive from Xi Jinping on school ideological and political theory courses (sizheng ke), Cai Wencheng argues that these courses should develop 'connotatively', that is, by improving quality rather than expanding scale. The article, a commentary in the Party journal Qiushi's sister publication Hongqi Wengao (2024, no. 12), holds that this requires upholding fundamental principles while innovating, so as to make the courses more targeted and more appealing. Cai presents this as a scientific guide to running such courses well in the new era.

The article has three parts. The first sets out the strategic significance of connotative development, the second its core meaning, and the third the practical requirements. It treats the courses as part of the wider course of the Party's cause, the building of a modern socialist country and national rejuvenation, and draws heavily on Xi's speeches and the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022).

In Cai's account, the courses matter for three reasons: they carry out the fundamental task of fostering virtue through education, they serve the Party's aim of educating people for the Party and talent for the country, and they are integral to building a leading country in education. The core meaning is that the courses must be political, strategic and bound up with people's wellbeing. Cai identifies four pillars: a high-standard curriculum and textbook system centred on Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era; a high-quality teaching system integrated across primary, secondary and tertiary levels; a high-level theoretical research system; and an effective talent-cultivation system that draws on all subjects through 'ideological and political education across the curriculum'.

Cai's practical requirements are to hold to the right political direction in an ideological field described as increasingly complex, and to apply Xi's 'eight unities' (for example, political and academic rigour, indoctrination and inspiration). Cai also calls for 'great ideological and political courses' that link classrooms to society, for new methods such as case-based and interactive teaching, and for teachers who are politically strong and ethically upright. Read the original if you want a concise statement of the official line on how ideological and political courses are to be organised and taught in Chinese schools and universities after Xi's 2024 directive.
quoteEn: Ideological and political courses are not the voice of a single school and cannot be developed behind closed doors; the small classroom must be joined to the large classroom of society, so that 'great ideological and political courses' open up a new pattern of all-round education.
quoteZh: 思政课不是“一家之言”，不能“闭门造车”，要把思政小课堂和社会大课堂结合起来，以“大思政课”拓展全面育人新格局。

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses in Marxism, Party theory, morality and law taught from primary school to university in China. They are a main channel of official ideological education.
A development path stressing quality, substance and efficiency over expansion in scale. It is used in official education discourse.
A stated fundamental task of Chinese education, emphasised in the report to the 20th Party Congress, that puts moral and political formation at the centre of schooling.

glossary.en: ideological and political education across the curriculum
glossary.explanation: The practice of building ideological and political content into all subjects, not only dedicated political courses.
A concept promoted by Xi Jinping that links classroom teaching with social practice and real-world resources.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology since 2017, written into the Party and state constitutions. It forms the core content of the curriculum described in the article.

t: Deepening basic theoretical research in ideological and political education in the new era
st: An interview with Professor Zhang Yaocan of Central China Normal University
zh: 《思想教育研究》记者：深化新时代思想政治教育基础理论研究 续写学科高质量发展新篇章
zhSub: 访华中师范大学张耀灿教授
source: Ideological and Political Education Research (思想教育研究), 2024 no. 6
paras: This is an interview, conducted by a reporter for the journal Ideological and Political Education Research, with Professor Zhang Yaocan of Central China Normal University. Zhang is introduced as one of the founders of the discipline of ideological and political education in China, with more than 60 years of teaching. Marking forty years since the discipline was established, the interview asks how it developed, what lessons it has produced, and how it should "uphold fundamental principles while breaking new ground" in the new era.

Zhang begins with a personal account. After studying political education at Central China Normal University, they worked in student affairs, taught a moral-cultivation course, and published a university moral-education text in 1986. Zhang then divides the discipline's history into three stages: exploration (1978–1983), systematic construction (1984–1996) and innovative development (1996 to the present). The interview then turns to the role of basic theory and to tasks for the future.

Zhang names three driving forces: the Party's adaptation of Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times through the Two Integrations, the practical experience of builders in many sectors, and the scholars and practitioners of the field. Five lessons follow: be guided by sinicised Marxist theory, combine theory with practice, combine history with theory, pursue cooperation alongside individual strengths, and treat the discipline, the undergraduate major and the ideological and political theory courses as mutually supporting. Zhang argues that basic theory is the first expression of the discipline's scientific character and also underpins its ideological character. Strengthening it requires "five adherences", including the unity of science and ideology, an interdisciplinary paradigm and cooperation among older, middle-aged and young scholars.

Looking ahead, Zhang calls for Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era to guide the discipline. Zhang also wants ideals-and-convictions education tied to Chinese modernization, the Belt and Road Initiative and a community with a shared future for mankind, and research kept oriented to practice. Zhang notes that metatheory has advanced, but that work on the discipline's basic categories is thin and lacks scholarly debate, which Zhang treats as a mark of a mature discipline. Read the original if you want a participant's periodisation of the field, with its policy milestones and course reforms, or an insider view of how the discipline defines its theoretical tasks.
quoteEn: Basic theory is the primary expression of a discipline's scientific character.
quoteZh: 基础理论则是学科科学性的首要体现。

glossary.explanation: A Chinese academic discipline and a field of Party and state work concerned with instilling Marxist theory, Party line and socialist values in students, workers and others. It is taught as a university major and sits under the first-level discipline of Marxist theory.

A formula in Party theory for combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's specific realities and with China's fine traditional culture. It is used to describe the adaptation of Marxism to China.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology since it was written into the Party constitution in 2017. It is presented as the current stage of adapting Marxism to China.
The official term for China's own path of modernization, promoted by the Party leadership especially since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
China's international infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative, launched in 2013.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy and theoretical concept promoted by Xi Jinping. It presents China's vision of international relations built on shared interests and cooperation.

t: Firmly grasping cultural discourse power in building school ideological and political courses in the new era
zh: 牢牢把握新时代学校思政课建设文化话语权
source: China Social Sciences Today (中国社会科学报), 9 July 2024
paras: This short commentary asks how schools' ideological and political courses (sizheng ke) can be developed in the new era, and answers that the key is to build and consolidate "cultural discourse power". Taking its cue from Xi Jinping's recent instruction that these courses must uphold Marxism's guiding position and draw strength from fine traditional Chinese culture, revolutionary culture and advanced socialist culture, Gu and Zhao argue that all ideological, moral and political education takes place in a cultural context and relies on cultural discourse as its vehicle.

The article moves through three sections. The first looks at what the authors call the ethical and character-forming nature of traditional Chinese culture. The second reviews the Chinese Communist Party's experience of cultivating virtue through culture, from Mao Zedong's policy of critically inheriting tradition to the present. The third turns to practical tasks for the new era.

Gu and Zhao contend that, historically, rulers and ordinary educators alike shaped and defended cultural discourse power, which they credit for the effectiveness of traditional moral education and the vitality of Chinese culture. In the new era, they say, global upheaval, cultural pluralism and online information have changed the cultural environment and posed unprecedented challenges. They propose three measures: heightening awareness of risk, including what they describe as cultural infiltration by some Western countries; building mainstream culture, explaining socialism with Chinese characteristics in Marxist political language while stressing Party leadership, the people's standpoint and patriotism; and guiding popular culture. On the last point, the authors acknowledge that popular culture enriches daily life but argue that its commercialism undermines recognition of core values, so courses should be down-to-earth in idiom yet pitched high in the values they convey.

The authors conclude that cultural discourse power determines whom the courses serve and how, and that it bears on carrying the Party's ideological and political work tradition into the future. They present securing it as a necessary choice for implementing Xi's instruction, fostering cultural confidence in socialism with Chinese characteristics, safeguarding ideological security and offering Chinese wisdom to global cultural governance. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Chinese scholars link Party ideological education to culture, tradition and ideological security.
quoteEn: Whether cultural discourse power can be grasped in building school ideological and political courses is a key factor determining the success or failure of the great cause of educating people for the Party and cultivating talent for the country.
quoteZh: 能否把握学校思政课建设实践中的文化话语权，是关乎为党育人、为国育才宏伟事业成败的关键要素。

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses in Marxist theory, Party history and political values taught in Chinese schools and universities.
The capacity to set the terms, concepts and narratives through which culture and values are understood and communicated. It is a common concept in Chinese discussions of ideology.
The official name for China's current path and system, developed since reform and opening up.

t: Collaborative innovation between specialist-course education and ideological and political theory course education from the perspective of curriculum-based ideological and political education
zh: 课程思政视域下专业课教育与思政课教育的协同创新
source: Teaching and Research on Marxist Theory (马克思主义理论教学与研究), 2024 no. 2
paras: Ren Menglei takes up a practical problem in Chinese university teaching: how specialist (professional) courses and the compulsory ideological and political theory courses can move 'in the same direction and together' under the policy of curriculum-based ideological and political education. Ren argues that some current practice wrongly treats the policy as 'specialist course plus political course', or tries to turn one type of course into the other. The thesis is that genuine coordination rests on the structural differences between the two kinds of course, aiming at 'harmony without uniformity' and at a combined force for fostering virtue and cultivating talent.

The article has three parts. The first examines the 'heterogeneity' of the two course types, reviewing scholarly definitions of curriculum-based ideological and political education and the misconceptions that Ren says have appeared in practice. The second turns to teachers as the main agents of reform. The third turns to teachers and students together, using Nankai University's 'four togethers' model, virtual-reality classrooms, case-sharing platforms and feedback mechanisms as examples.

Ren's core claim is that value is already embedded in knowledge, so bolting a few 'values' onto a specialist lesson is counterproductive. Reform therefore means drawing out the values inside each discipline's knowledge system, and building a Chinese independent knowledge system, while ideological and political theory courses build a complete scientific system of their own. Ren assigns the two types different strengths. Political theory courses are compulsory, reach all students and provide explicit, systematic Marxist education. Specialist courses reach fixed groups of students and offer implicit, tailored education. Teachers should share cases, borrow methods from each other (small-group seminars, a 'grand historical view', the chip-technology example) and keep value formation, knowledge transmission and ability building unified. Ren adds that students are active agents who internalise values, so their sense of gain should be a key measure of success.

Ren concludes that the two reforms must interlock in a spiral, not run as parallel lines, or the 'two skins' problem will persist. Course design should replace simple stacking of resources with sensible sequencing, and teacher–student feedback should be routine. Reform is not an end in itself: its purpose is to foster virtue and cultivate people. Read the original if you want a detailed Chinese-language account of how university teachers are urged to coordinate political theory courses and specialist courses, including Nankai's practices and the VR classroom debate.
quoteEn: In curriculum-based ideological and political education, specialist courses and political theory courses move in the same direction not by growing ever more alike in structure and function, but by arriving at the same goal by different routes under the aim of fostering virtue and cultivating talent.
quoteZh: 课程思政视域下专业课与思政课的同向同行，不在结构功能的日渐趋同，而在立德树人目标下的殊途同归

glossary.literal: ideology and politics in the curriculum
glossary.explanation: A policy promoted since 2016 that asks teachers of all university subjects, not only political courses, to build moral and political values into their teaching.
Compulsory courses for all Chinese university students that teach Marxism, Party history and Party theory, often shortened to 'sizheng ke'.
A stated fundamental task of Chinese education: shaping students' moral character alongside their knowledge and skills.
A common expression for two things that should be integrated but remain disconnected, here political education and specialist teaching.

t: Self-education as practical wisdom in ideological and political education
st: Three modes: knowledge, method and value
zh: 论作为思想政治教育实践智慧的自我教育样态
source: Teaching and Research on Marxist Theory (Mǎkèsīzhǔyì lǐlùn jiàoxué yǔ yánjiū), 2024 no. 2
paras: Yu Ying asks how self-education should be understood within ideological and political education, against a background of modernity in which people are drawn into other people's worlds and logics and lose sight of their own problems. Existing scholarship, the author says, treats self-education mainly as a methodological matter, either as a body of method knowledge or as an implementation technique. Yu argues instead that self-education is a form of practical wisdom that unites theoretical and practical reason, and that it has three practical modes: knowledge rooted in action, method that reproduces concrete situations, and value grounded in the subject's own reflection.

The article is a theoretical essay in four sections. The first three take each mode in turn, each time criticising two prevailing approaches. The fourth section is a conclusion that places the argument in the setting of globalisation and industrial modernity. Yu draws on Confucius, Mencius and Wang Yangming's unity of knowing and doing, on Marx and Engels's "real human beings", and on Gadamer's account of the humanities.

In the first move, Yu argues that empiricist and borrowing-oriented approaches both stress "a priori knowledge" of ideological and political education and overlook practical knowledge. Understanding the field is gained through lived experience in action, and self-education turns knowledge into wisdom through "unity of knowing and doing". In the second, Yu traces the "instrumental" and "technical" views of method to scientism. Drawing on Gadamer, the author holds that the meaning-world of human beings cannot be fully quantified, so self-education cannot be a standardised procedure. It is a method wisdom exercised according to time, person and circumstance, and it starts from the learner's own life world. In the third, Yu treats the value of ideological and political education as a relation to the needs of the educated subject. Needs vary, but Yu says they are social and share a common core, which is the improvement of political-ideological and moral quality. Classroom indicators such as attendance, the author suggests, do not capture this. Students must test and choose values themselves.

Yu concludes that political-ideological and moral quality cannot be produced by an "industrial logic" of efficiency and standardisation, which leaves people "one-dimensional". Self-education should therefore be seen as an integrated capacity of knowledge, method and value, not as a tool for educating oneself. It would preserve "self-awakening" and the drive to self-realisation, and an orientation towards the true, the good and the beautiful. Read the original if you work on the theory or pedagogy of ideological and political education in China and want to see how current scholarship draws on practical wisdom, hermeneutics and Marxist concepts of the person.
quoteEn: Self-education in the field of ideological and political education is not a tool or means of conducting such education on oneself. It is an integrated capacity of knowledge, method and value, stressing action, the reproduction of situations and the subject's own reflection.
quoteZh: 思想政治教育视域中的自我教育，并不是为了实现对自身进行思想政治教育的工具或手段，而是一种强调躬于行动、境遇再现、主体省思的集知识、方法、价值为一体的综合能力

glossary.explanation: The Chinese academic field and practice of shaping people's political outlook, ideology and moral character. It covers university courses on Marxist theory as well as wider work by the Party and schools.

Education that the learner carries out on themselves through reflection and practice, as distinct from being taught by others. The article treats it as a core topic in ideological and political education.
A concept close to Aristotle's phronesis: the capacity to judge and act well in concrete situations. The author uses it to join theoretical reason and practical reason.

A principle associated with the Ming-dynasty philosopher Wang Yangming, holding that moral knowledge and action are inseparable. The author cites it as a traditional Chinese precedent for self-education.
The view that the methods of natural science should govern all fields of knowledge. The author criticises its extension to ideological and political education.

t: Reflections on the development of part-time teachers of ideological and political theory courses in universities under the "Big Ideological and Political Course" initiative
st: From role identity, knowledge production and professional identity
zh: “大思政课”背景下高校思政课兼职教师发展现状的若干思考
zhSub: 从角色认同、知识生产和职业认同出发
source: Theory Teaching and Research of Marxism (马克思主义理论教学与研究), 2024 no. 2
paras: Zhang Nan asks how part-time teachers of university ideological and political theory courses ("sizheng ke") are coping with their new position as the "Big Ideological and Political Course" policy expands their ranks. The article is an empirical study based on educational narrative. It argues that these teachers face difficulties in three linked areas: role, knowledge and professional identity. Zhang proposes that these can be eased by recognising the value of "practical knowledge" and by building stronger organisational support.

The article opens with the policy background: Xi Jinping's 2021 remarks on the "Big Ideological and Political Course", the 2022 work plan issued by ten ministries, and Ministry of Education figures cited by the author, according to which part-time staff were 32.68 per cent of 106,411 such teachers in November 2021. The study draws on 20 valid interviewees from an initial 25. They are university counsellors, Party and administrative heads of departments, industry professionals and teaching staff from other subjects, drawn from four types of institution. Data came from semi-structured interviews, classroom observation and teaching documents. Three main sections follow: role, knowledge and professional identity.

On role, Zhang uses role theory (Mead, Merton's "role set") to describe overload from combining a main job with part-time teaching, and confusion over whether to teach as administrator or as educator. One interviewee uses "role reminders" to manage this. Zhang argues that unclear institutional expectations of part-time staff deepen this confusion, and that teachers' own convictions and supportive organisations help build role identity. On knowledge, Zhang draws on distinctions between essentialist and non-essentialist views of knowledge, and between theoretical and practical knowledge. In this reading, part-time teachers' experience can count as practical knowledge only if it is reflected on and turned into public teaching resources, through dialogue with full-time colleagues and critical reflection. On professional identity, Zhang finds that counsellors adapt more easily, while industry professionals feel isolated and under greater pressure to master theory.

Zhang concludes that universities should convert part-time teachers' practical experience into rational, teachable knowledge. They should also treat these teachers as an integral part of the "Big Ideological and Political Course" framework, not as a numerical supplement. The proposed measures are collaborative teaching models between full-time and part-time teachers, stronger group belonging and self-identity, and supporting platforms for training and exchange. Read the original if you want interview-based evidence on how part-time ideological and political teachers describe their work, or if you study teacher development in Chinese higher education.
quoteEn: Teachers' professional identity is a sense of value identification and meaning formed in the course of teaching practice and the work of nurturing students.
quoteZh: 教师的职业认同是教师在教学实践与育人过程中形成的一种价值认同和意义感。

glossary.explanation: A policy concept stressed by Xi Jinping in 2021. It calls for ideological and political education to extend beyond the classroom into social practice and to draw on wider teaching resources.
Compulsory courses in Chinese universities on Marxism, Party theory and official political values, usually shortened to sizheng ke.
Staff with other main jobs, such as counsellors, administrators, industry experts or teachers of other subjects, who are recruited to teach part of these courses.
In the article, knowledge teachers form by reflecting on and refining their own teaching and work experience, as distinct from systematic theoretical knowledge.
A qualitative research method in education that interprets teachers' own accounts of their experience.

t: Integrating the great founding spirit of the Party into university ideological and political courses: value, content design and practical strategies
zh: 伟大建党精神融入高校思政课教学的价值意蕴、内容设计与实践策略
source: Teaching and Research on Marxist Theory (Marxist Theory Teaching and Research), 2024 no. 2
paras: How should the great founding spirit of the Party be brought into university ideological and political theory courses? Ruan and Wu argue that this spirit embodies the Party's original aspiration and mission, and so is a rich ideological and teaching resource. Their thesis is that it should be integrated through precise content selection, systematic design and a coordinated set of practical measures, in order to raise its educational effect and meet the goal of cultivating new-era young people.

The article has three parts. The first sets out the value of integration: fulfilling the fundamental task of fostering virtue through education, safeguarding ideological security in universities, and deepening students' feelings for family and country. The second assigns content to each of the five core courses. The third proposes practical strategies, organised around systematic design, "three guarantees" and "six methods".

In the authors' design, each course highlights one "logic" of the spirit. The basic principles of Marxism course explains its theoretical logic. The two courses on Mao Zedong Thought, the theoretical system of socialism with Chinese characteristics and Xi Jinping Thought explain its practical logic, with stress on the Two Integrations. The modern Chinese history course covers its historical logic, and the ethics and rule of law course covers its value logic, following a progression from knowledge to emotion, will, belief and action. Practice is built on three guarantees: management, teaching staff and evaluation. The six methods are standard textbooks, digital technology, case teaching, practical teaching activities, new media and immersive teaching with red culture and art.

Ruan and Wu conclude that the spirit should be woven into the "big ideological and political course" pattern. This would link classroom, campus and society, relying on official policy documents, red educational resources, trained and part-time teachers, and clear evaluation standards. They present this as a way to strengthen students' political, ideological, theoretical and emotional identification with the Party. Read the original if you want a detailed example of how Party-history themes are mapped onto the five required university courses and the teaching methods proposed for them.
quoteEn: Integrating the great founding spirit of the Party into university ideological and political teaching is not a fragmented, one-directional matter, but a concrete and lively process of teaching practice.
quoteZh: 伟大建党精神融入高校思政课教学不是一个碎片化、单向度的，而是具体鲜活的教学实践过程

glossary.en: the great founding spirit of the Party
glossary.explanation: A formulation Xi Jinping set out in 2021 at the Party's centenary: upholding truth and ideals, practising the original aspiration and mission, fearless struggle, and loyalty to the Party and the people. It is presented as the source of the Party's "spiritual genealogy".
The stated fundamental task of education in official policy: forming students' moral character and political orientation alongside knowledge.
The principle of integrating the basic tenets of Marxism with China's specific realities and with its fine traditional culture. It is a core formula of Xi Jinping-era Party theory.
An official concept that extends ideological and political education beyond the classroom into society, practice and online spaces, using society-wide resources.

keywords: great founding spirit of the Party

t: Practical paths for integrating excellent traditional Chinese culture into ideological and political education
zh: 中华优秀传统文化融入思想政治教育的实践路径
source: Teaching and Research (教学与研究), 2024 no. 6
paras: Wang Zengfu asks how excellent traditional Chinese culture can be built into ideological and political education in practice. The article holds that the two share an inherent fit, since both aim to cultivate patriotic feeling, sound character and cultural confidence. Wang argues that integration is both an urgent requirement for passing on traditional culture and a means of making ideological and political education more effective. The article sets out to answer three questions: what to integrate, who integrates it, and how.

The article proposes five practical paths. These are systematically drawing out the educational resources in traditional culture; raising the traditional-culture literacy of those who carry out ideological and political education; building a graded chain of courses according to the principle of differentiated audiences; using digital technology to renew the technical and environmental carriers of integration; and establishing an evaluation mechanism. Wang places the whole programme under the Two Integrations and the fundamental task of fostering virtue through education.

On resources, Wang argues that selection must be guided by Marxism adapted to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. Ideas such as "the world belongs to all" and "the people as the foundation of the state" are said to fit the values of scientific socialism. They are to be transformed creatively and developed innovatively under the leadership of core socialist values, with the aim of cultivating mainstream values. On people and courses, Wang calls for teachers, responsible units, families, schools and society to work together. Wang also criticises "forced integration" that ignores audience differences and "loose links" between school stages, and proposes a sequence from primary school to university that links theory with practice and ideological-political courses with course-embedded ideological education. On digital technology, Wang points to storage, vivid presentation, shared resources and real-time feedback, plus immersive virtual and augmented reality, all within a secure campus culture.

Wang concludes that evaluation should involve many parties and combine top-down guidance with bottom-up participation. It should use indicators that are complete, dynamic and differentiated, cover the whole cycle before, during and after teaching, and be updated continuously. Wang says this would strengthen learners' cultural identity and confidence and advance the high-quality development of ideological and political education in the new era. Read the original if you work on ideological and political education in China and want a detailed, policy-oriented framework for curriculum design, digital carriers and evaluation.
quoteEn: Integrating excellent traditional Chinese culture into ideological and political education in all respects is both an urgent requirement for passing on and renewing it so as to reveal its value for our times, and the proper choice for strengthening the effectiveness of ideological and political education through the power of culture.
quoteZh: 中华优秀传统文化全方位融入思想政治教育，既是传承创新中华优秀传统文化以开显其时代价值的迫切要求，也是以文化之力增强思想政治教育实效性的应然之选。

glossary.explanation: A formula in Party theory: integrating the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with its excellent traditional culture. It is used to frame the adaptation of Marxism to China.
The system of teaching and guidance, in schools and elsewhere, meant to shape students' political convictions, values and morality in line with the Party's line.
A stated fundamental task of Chinese education: moral cultivation alongside knowledge and skills.

glossary.literal: ideology and politics in the curriculum
glossary.explanation: The practice of building ideological and moral content into non-political, specialist courses, to work alongside dedicated ideological-political courses.
A set of twenty-four characters in twelve values, promoted officially since the 18th Party Congress (2012), at national, social and individual levels.

t: Ideological and political education resources in excellent traditional Chinese culture
zh: 中华优秀传统文化蕴含的思想政治教育资源
source: Teaching and Research (Jiaoxue yu Yanjiu), 2024 no. 6
paras: Shan Wenpeng asks how excellent traditional Chinese culture can be systematically mined as a resource for ideological and political education, and how doing so can help build an autonomous Chinese knowledge system for the discipline. Writing in 2024, forty years after the discipline's founding, Shan argues that this culture is the 'root and lifeline' of the Party's theoretical innovation. The article holds that research should move from broad, general treatment to finer-grained discussion, guided by the Two Integrations.

The article has four main sections plus a conclusion. The first argues that traditional culture is already an important part of the discipline's content, and notes shortcomings in how it has been integrated. Three further sections then set out the resources the author identifies: ideas and concepts, humanistic spirit, and moral norms. Each section closes with a statement of what teaching should stress.

Shan's first move is to show that the culture serves the discipline's purposes: its goals of fostering virtue and cultivating people, the structure of its content, and its self-reliant knowledge system. The author criticises existing work for favouring grand narrative over systematic depth and quotation over logical interpretation. Second, Shan sorts the resources into three clusters. Ideas include the unity of heaven and humanity, governing by virtue, and the Great Harmony under heaven. Humanistic spirit covers self-strengthening, benevolence ('loving others') and harmony without uniformity. Moral norms cover righteousness over profit, filial piety extended into loyalty to the state, and self-cultivation. Shan presents each as the traditional answer to a basic relationship: humanity and nature, politics and governance, nation and world, person and person, family and state, self and others.

In the conclusion, Shan calls for deeper scholarly study of how traditional culture enters ideological and political education, under the guidance of the Two Integrations. Three tasks follow. The first is to strengthen the work of fostering virtue and cultivating people. The second is to consolidate cultural subjectivity. The third is to build an autonomous disciplinary knowledge system able to answer the questions of China, the world, the people and the times. Read the original if you study the theory of ideological and political education in China, or want to see which traditional concepts the discipline is now drawing on.
quoteEn: Excellent traditional Chinese culture is the 'root and lifeline' of the Party's theoretical innovation; it contains rich ideological and political education resources and richly nourishes the building of an autonomous Chinese knowledge system for the discipline.
quoteZh: 中华优秀传统文化是我们党理论创新的“根脉”，其中蕴含着丰富的思想政治教育资源，是建构中国自主的思想政治教育学科知识体系的丰厚滋养。

glossary.explanation: Formula associated with Xi Jinping: combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with its excellent traditional culture.
A Chinese academic discipline and practice, within the first-level discipline of Marxist theory, that teaches political ideology, values and morality, mainly in schools and universities.
The official fundamental task of Chinese education: cultivating moral character alongside knowledge and skills.

glossary.en: the unity of heaven and humanity
glossary.explanation: A traditional Chinese idea that humans and nature form one continuous whole and should live in harmony.
A traditional ideal of a world in which all things are shared and social harmony prevails, found in the Book of Rites.

t: The history and experience of integrating excellent traditional Chinese culture with ideological and political education
zh: 中华优秀传统文化与思想政治教育融合发展的历史与经验
source: Teaching and Research (教学与研究), 2024 no. 6
paras: Wang Yi asks how excellent traditional Chinese culture and ideological and political education have developed together over the forty years since ideological and political education became a formal academic discipline. The article argues that bringing traditional culture into the field's research agenda is a valuable experience of the discipline and a practical need for its continued development. Wang presents this as a way to build a Chinese-based body of disciplinary knowledge that serves Chinese modernization.

The article opens with three reasons why the two should be fused: they deepen the discipline's historical and cultural roots, they serve the Party's work of teaching traditional culture, and they drive innovation in the discipline. It then divides the fusion into three phases. The first is the institutional start from the early 1980s, with the creation of the specialty in 1984. The second is the deepening after 2005, when Marxist theory became a first-level discipline. The third is the comprehensive advance since the 18th Party Congress (2012). A final section looks ahead.

Wang describes the first phase as centred on socialist cultural-ethical progress, national spirit and histories of Chinese moral education, mainly Confucian. The author judges this work too focused on moral education to be clearly separated from the history of philosophy and ethics. In the second phase, research became more specialised and varied in perspective and moved towards practice, including work on the socialist core value system and on courses. Since 2012, guided by Xi Jinping's statements on traditional culture and the Two Integrations, studies have extended to cultural transmission, the core socialist values, family instructions, village rules and the reform of ideological and political theory courses, including guides for bringing traditional culture into textbooks.

Looking forward, Wang calls for work guided by Xi Jinping's thought on culture and the Two Integrations. The aim would be a Chinese-based knowledge system. Wang proposes using traditional humanistic values and methodological wisdom in teaching, and building the discipline, academic, discourse and textbook systems. Concrete proposals include deeper study of the history of ancient Chinese ideological and political education, telling stories drawn from the 'five histories', and writing textbook guides for all school levels. Read the original if you want a periodised, officially aligned account of how this discipline has treated traditional culture, or if you study how Chinese academics frame the construction of an autonomous knowledge system.
quoteEn: The integrated development of excellent traditional Chinese culture and ideological and political education is a practical need for driving innovative development of the ideological and political education discipline.
quoteZh: 中华优秀传统文化与思想政治教育融合发展是推动思想政治教育学科创新发展的现实需要。

glossary.explanation: A Chinese academic discipline and a field of practice covering political, ideological and moral education, especially in schools and universities. It became a formal specialty in 1984.
The official term for the parts of China's cultural heritage that Party discourse treats as worth inheriting and promoting.
Formula for combining the basic principles of Marxism with China's specific realities and with excellent traditional Chinese culture.
Official term for the Party's model of modernization, set out in Party documents from 2021 and 2022.
The label, formally adopted in 2023, for Xi Jinping's statements on culture and ideology, treated as a component of Party theory.
A set of 24 characters in twelve values, promoted since the 18th Party Congress (2012), at national, social and individual levels.
