t: Running school ideological and political courses to the "highest standard of the capital" to cultivate new-era talents who shoulder the task of national rejuvenation
zh: 以首善标准办好学校思政课 培养担当民族复兴重任的时代新人
authors: Education Work Committee of the CPC Beijing Municipal Committee
paras: This is an institutional report by the Education Work Committee of the CPC Beijing Municipal Committee, published in Red Flag Manuscripts (Hongqi Wengao) in 2024. It sets out how Beijing is implementing Xi Jinping's instructions on school ideological and political theory courses (sizheng ke). The Committee argues that such courses are the key course for ensuring the socialist orientation of education, and that Beijing is meeting the "highest standard of the capital" in building them.

The text follows five headings. These are: arming students with Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era; innovation in the content and quality of the courses; a capital-based "great ideological and political course" built around practical teaching; the "six requirements" for teachers; and Party leadership and social coordination. Each section opens with a quotation from Xi Jinping and then lists Beijing's measures, with figures and named programmes.

In the Committee's account, Beijing was the first in the country to make the compulsory course "Introduction to Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era" universal for new undergraduates (from autumn 2020). It also issued the first national guideline integrating ideological education across universities, secondary and primary schools, set up five pilot districts, and built digital teaching resources and a "Digital Marxism School" project. The Committee describes more than 200 immersive practice bases, student participation in events such as the 70th anniversary of the PRC, the Party's centenary and the Winter Olympics, and school-specific brands. It also describes teacher measures: a staff-student ratio of at least 1:350, Party membership for new recruits, separate promotion tracks, competitions, and dynamic removal of poorly rated teachers.

The Committee concludes that sustained Party leadership is decisive. It cites annual reports to the municipal Party standing committee, "first-in-charge" responsibility for school Party secretaries and presidents, and cooperation among families, schools, museums and the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei region. It presents these arrangements as the way to produce successors "whom the Party can rely on". Read the original if you want a detailed, official inventory of how a leading Chinese municipality organises ideological and political education, from curricula to teacher management.
quoteEn: School ideological and political courses most clearly embody the socialist orientation of education and most lastingly shape the convictions of a generation of a strong nation; they are the key course bearing on the Party's long-term governance, the country's lasting stability and the nation's great enterprise.
quoteZh: 学校思政课最鲜明地体现了社会主义办学方向，最持久地塑造着强国一代的信念信仰，是关乎我们党长期执政、国家长治久安和中华民族千秋伟业的关键课程。

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses in Marxist theory, Party doctrine and moral-political education taught at all school levels in China. The leadership treats them as the main channel of ideological education.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018. It is now taught as a compulsory subject in schools and universities.
A slogan associated with Xi Jinping in 2021. It calls for linking classroom teaching with social practice and real-world events.

t: Optimising the use of red historical and cultural resources in practical teaching of ideological and political theory courses in universities
st: An examination based on red venues
zh: 红色历史文化资源在高校思政课实践教学中的优化运用
zhSub: 基于红色场馆的考察
source: Journal of Party Building and Ideological Education in Schools (学校党建与思想教育)
paras: Xie Ruoyang and Song Jian ask how Chinese universities can make fuller and more effective use of red historical and cultural resources in the practical teaching of ideological and political theory courses. Starting from Xi Jinping's statements since the 18th Party Congress (2012) on using red resources and passing on the red gene, and from the current drive to build the "great ideological and political course", they argue that red venues such as memorials, museums and former revolutionary sites are an underused teaching platform. Their thesis is that a systematic, university–venue partnership is needed to resolve three identified problems.

The article has three parts. The first analyses the ideological and political education functions of red venues, physical and digital. The second reviews problems in how these venues are used in practical teaching. The third proposes ways to optimise their use. The authors place the discussion within the principle of unifying theory and practice and of linking the "small classroom" of the course with the "big classroom" of society.

The authors credit red venues with three functions: narrowing the temporal distance to history and building emotional identification; deepening historical understanding and theoretical thinking, strengthening confidence in Party history and helping students resist historical nihilism; and guiding young people's values so that they carry on the red gene. They then identify three problems. Universities, concentrated in cities, favour accessible urban venues, leaving rural and remote sites, where the authors say most revolutionary remains lie, neglected. Visits stay passive, and digital venues mainly display with little interaction. Evaluation also leans towards results and lacks feedback between venues and universities.

In response, Xie and Song call for a shared online and offline information platform linking venues and universities, and for joint research and interactive, participatory activities. They cite as an example the national research centre for revolutionary cultural relics that Wuhan University set up with the Xinhai Revolution Museum. They also propose a collaborative evaluation mechanism running through the whole teaching process, with several evaluating parties and a combination of process and outcome assessment, in place of reliance on practice reports alone. The aim, in their account, is to fulfil the fundamental task of fostering virtue and cultivating talent. Read the original if you work on ideological and political course pedagogy or museum–university cooperation in China and want a structured account of the officially stated problems and remedies.
quoteEn: Exhibition and education cannot simply be equated.
quoteZh: 展览与教育之间不能简单画等号。

glossary.explanation: A broad label for memorials, exhibition halls, former revolutionary sites and residences, and martyrs' cemeteries (physical or digital) that preserve the history of the Chinese Communist Party and the revolution.

A policy concept promoted in recent years that extends ideological and political education beyond the classroom by drawing on social practice and resources. It is often paired with the idea of the "social big classroom".
A phrase used in Party discourse for the revolutionary tradition and spirit that are to be inherited by later generations.
An official formulation of the fundamental task of education: moral formation of students alongside knowledge and skills.
In official Chinese usage, a label for views seen as denying or distorting the Party's history and the course of the revolution and socialist construction.

t: Making the resolution of problems unique to a large party the main line of attack
zh: 以解决大党独有难题为主攻方向
paras: This commentary, published in Red Flag Manuscripts (Hongqi Wengao) in 2024, interprets Xi Jinping's call at the Third Plenary Session of the 20th Central Commission for Discipline Inspection to take "resolving problems unique to a large party" as the main line of attack in advancing the Party's self-reform. The authors argue that this is both consistent with the Party's historical practice of tackling its principal problems and a strategic priority for the Party's long-term rule.

The article has three sections. The first traces how the Party identified key problems for self-reform in successive periods: the Land Revolution, the Yan'an rectification, the early People's Republic, the reform era under Deng Xiaoping, Jiang Zemin and Hu Jintao, and the period since the 18th Party Congress (2012). The second works through the "six questions of how to always..." that Xi set out as the content of these difficulties. The third explains the significance of the focus.

In the authors' account, the six questions concern keeping to the original aspiration and mission; unifying thinking, will and action; sustaining strong governing capacity; maintaining a drive to get things done; finding and solving the Party's own problems in good time; and keeping a clean political ecosystem. For each, they describe the risks of a Party with over 98 million members ruling the world's most populous country, citing Xi's remarks, and propose remedies such as the Two Upholds, theoretical study, discipline education, institution-based Party governance, popular supervision and anti-corruption work. They draw on the fall of the Soviet Communist Party after 74 years in power to argue that a ruling position is neither innate nor permanent.

The authors conclude that the focus shows deep awareness of risk, strategic vision and a methodology for self-reform. By "main line of attack" they mean concentrating forces and resources on deep-seated, complex problems rather than formal or superficial ones, while keeping systematic thinking and a problem-oriented approach. They present this as a way for the Party to avoid the historical cycle of rise and fall and open a new stage in its self-reform. Read the original if you want a concise, official-line account of how Party theorists frame the "unique difficulties of a large party" and the six questions attached to them.
quoteEn: The so-called main line of attack means concentrating the main forces, resources and attention on a particular direction and goal, so as to achieve the overall intention and task.
quoteZh: 所谓的主攻方向，就是要将主要的力量、资源和注意力集中在某个特定的方向和目标上，以此实现整体意图和任务。

glossary.explanation: A concept stressed under Xi Jinping referring to the Party's efforts to discipline, correct and renew itself, presented as the answer to the question of how to avoid the historical cycle of rise and decline.

glossary.en: problems unique to a large party
glossary.literal: difficult problems unique to a big party
glossary.explanation: A phrase introduced in the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022) for the special governance problems that arise from the Party's size, long rule and the scale of the country it governs.

The requirement to resolutely uphold Xi Jinping's core position on the Party Central Committee and in the whole Party, and to uphold the Central Committee's authority and centralised, unified leadership.

keywords: problems unique to a large party

t: Better shouldering the new cultural mission at a new historical starting point
zh: 在新的历史起点上更好担负起新的文化使命
paras: Fan Xichun's article, published in Red Flag Manuscript in 2024, expounds Xi Jinping's 2 June 2023 speech at the symposium on cultural inheritance and development. In that speech Xi called on the Party to continue promoting cultural prosperity, build a culturally strong country and build a modern Chinese civilization, which he termed the new cultural mission of the new era. Fan argues that Xi's three stressed requirements (firm cultural confidence, openness and inclusiveness, and upholding fundamental principles while innovating) provide scientific guidance and a guide to action for carrying out that mission.

The piece is organised in three parts, one for each requirement. Each part defines the concept, traces its historical and theoretical basis, and links it to the mission. Fan draws heavily on Xi's speeches and Party Congress reports (the 19th Party Congress in 2017 and the 20th in 2022), with one citation from Marx on people making history under inherited conditions.

In the first part, Fan argues that cultural confidence rests on cultural subjectivity. This subjectivity is formed by Marxism combined with China's concrete realities and its fine traditional culture, and by the creation of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. Cultural confidence, Fan says, underlies confidence in the path, theory and system, and is the precondition for national rejuvenation. The second part holds that openness and inclusiveness are traits of Chinese civilization that sustain its vitality through exchange and mutual learning. Fan says this means localising foreign culture and rejecting both Westernisation and revivalism. The third part defines upholding fundamental principles as maintaining Marxism's guiding position, the Two Integrations and the Party's cultural leadership. Innovation is described as new ideas, discourse, mechanisms and forms. Fan presents the combination of Marxism and fine traditional culture as the route to a new cultural organism, with Marxism as the 'soul' and tradition as the 'root'.

Fan concludes that the mission must be carried out under the guidance of Xi Jinping's thought on culture. In practice this means continuing the Chinese cultural lineage, fostering cultural undertakings and industries, strengthening shared ideological ground and raising national cultural soft power. Fan also claims that the three requirements enrich historical and dialectical materialism and develop Marxist methodology. Read the original if you want a representative example of how Party-theory journals present Xi's cultural thought and its three guiding principles.
quoteEn: Upholding fundamental principles while innovating is a cultural tradition of the Chinese nation over thousands of years, adhering to the right path while discarding the old for the new. It unites inheritance with development and principle with creativity, reflects a dialectical unity of steadfast adherence to truth and practical exploration, and is the methodology for promoting cultural prosperity.
quoteZh: 守正创新是中华民族几千年来恪守正道、革故鼎新的文化传统，是坚持继承与发展、原则性与创造性的统一，体现了真理性坚守与实践性探索的辩证统一，是推动文化繁荣发展的方法论。

glossary.explanation: A Party concept stressed by Xi Jinping, meaning affirmation of the value of China's own culture. It is presented as the foundation for confidence in the path, theory and system of socialism with Chinese characteristics.
A term Xi emphasised in 2023 for China's distinct cultural identity and independent standpoint. It is said to be built through combining Marxism with Chinese realities and traditional culture.

glossary.literal: guard what is correct, create anew
glossary.explanation: A Party formula for combining adherence to Marxist guidance and core principles with new ideas and forms. It is applied here to cultural work.
The Party's formula for combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture.

A body of ideas on cultural work attributed to Xi Jinping and formally set out in October 2023. Official sources describe it as part of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era.

glossary.literal: great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The official goal of restoring China to national strength and prosperity, central to Xi-era Party discourse.

t: Resolutely winning the tough and protracted battle against corruption
zh: 坚决打赢反腐败斗争攻坚战持久战
paras: Writing in Red Flag Manuscripts (2024, no. 8), Huang Rongsheng takes up Xi Jinping's speech at the Third Plenary Session of the 20th Central Commission for Discipline Inspection (2024). The article asks why the Party must treat the anti-corruption struggle as both a hard-fought assault and a protracted war. Huang's answer is that corruption threatens the Party's survival, that the situation remains severe and complex, and that the struggle must therefore be pursued to the end.

The article has three sections. The first presents anti-corruption as "the most thorough form of self-reform", citing Mao Zedong, Deng Xiaoping and Xi. The second describes the struggle as a major political fight that "cannot be lost". The third sets out how to carry it through: Party leadership, an integrated approach, and popular supervision.

Huang's central claim is that corruption is a political problem, not merely a disciplinary one. It damages the Party's vitality by cutting its ties to the people, and its combat capacity by hollowing out Party organisations and members. The article says the Party has gained the "overwhelming victory" since the 18th Party Congress (2012) but adds that this is not a thorough or fundamental victory. In Huang's account, the conditions that breed corruption persist, and new forms are emerging, such as shadow companies, shadow shareholders, revolving doors between officials and business, and "micro-corruption". Huang cites the collapse of the Soviet Union and Eastern Europe as a warning about privilege and corruption in a ruling party.

Huang proposes three measures. First, strengthen centralised Party leadership over the whole anti-corruption process, integrating political, ideological, organisational, conduct, discipline and institutional work. Second, advance "dare not, unable to, and not wanting to" be corrupt as one whole, combining deterrence, institutional constraint and moral education. Third, widen popular supervision through petitions, online platforms and open government, while guarding against false accusations. Read the original if you want a representative statement of the official Party-school line on anti-corruption and the Party's self-reform in 2024.
quoteEn: This major political struggle against corruption is long-term, arduous and complex; it is a political battle of assault and endurance that must never be lost.
quoteZh: 反腐败这一重大政治斗争具有长期性、艰巨性、复杂性，是一场绝不能输的政治攻坚战、持久战

glossary.explanation: A concept stressed by Xi Jinping since the 18th Party Congress. It means the Party rectifying itself, and it is used to frame discipline and anti-corruption work.
The official description of the anti-corruption results since 2012. The article stresses that it does not mean a thorough or final victory.

glossary.pinyin: bù gǎn fǔ, bù néng fǔ, bù xiǎng fǔ
glossary.en: dare not, unable to, and not wanting to be corrupt
glossary.literal: not daring to be corrupt, not able to be corrupt, not wanting to be corrupt
glossary.explanation: The official three-part anti-corruption approach. It combines deterrence by punishment, institutional constraint and moral education.
Official term for petty corruption at the grassroots, such as that of low-level officials who affect ordinary people directly.

t: Strengthening discipline building is the fundamental measure of full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
zh: 加强纪律建设是全面从严治党的治本之策
paras: Writing in 2024, as the Party launched a nationwide campaign of Party discipline study and education, Kan Daoyuan argues that strengthening discipline building is the fundamental measure (zhiben zhi ce) of full and rigorous self-governance of the Party. This commentary, published in Red Flag Manuscript, presents the campaign as an important step in deepening that governance and as a way to make members and cadres learn, understand and observe Party rules.

The article has three parts. The first treats strict discipline as a Marxist party's defining trait and as a Chinese Communist Party tradition, drawing on Marx, Engels, Lenin and Party history from the First Congress to the era since the 18th Party Congress (2012). The second sets out how discipline can address both symptoms and root causes. The third turns to the practical task of the education campaign.

Kan's core claim is that discipline-building rests on theoretical, historical and practical logic together. Citing Xi Jinping, the author holds that political discipline is the most fundamental discipline, and that if it is not upheld, other rules will collapse and the Party will become weak and slack. Discipline must therefore be a live "high-voltage line": rules are enforced without exception, leading cadres, especially Party-branch heads, set an example, and punishment, institutional constraint and raised awareness work together. The author also argues that Party spirit, Party style and Party discipline form an organic whole, with discipline as the safeguard of the other two, and that tackling bad work styles and corruption as sharing one root requires "whole-cycle management".

For the campaign itself, Kan calls on members to study the revised Regulations on Disciplinary Actions article by article, to learn both what is forbidden and what they may and should do, to internalise the rules, and to observe them unconditionally. The author further urges that the campaign become regular and long-term, that Party regulations keep being refined, that a zero-tolerance tone be maintained, and that study be tied to the Party Central Committee's key decisions and to local work. Read the original if you want a representative example of how official Party-building discourse in 2024 links the Marxist tradition of party discipline to the Party's self-governance.
quoteEn: Political discipline is the most important, most fundamental and most critical discipline, and observing it is an important foundation for observing all of the Party's discipline.
quoteZh: 政治纪律是最重要、最根本、最关键的纪律，遵守政治纪律是遵守党的全部纪律的重要基础。

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.literal: comprehensively and strictly govern the Party
glossary.explanation: A policy line associated with Xi Jinping since the 18th Party Congress (2012), covering ideological, organisational, stylistic and disciplinary discipline and the anti-corruption campaign.
A campaign run across the Party in 2024, centred on studying the revised Regulations on Disciplinary Actions of the Communist Party of China.
The rules governing members' political direction, stance, statements and conduct, in particular loyalty to the Party Central Committee. Official texts rank it first among the Party's disciplines.

keywords: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party

t: Keeping the development of ideological and political courses in step with arming minds with the Party's innovative theory
zh: 坚持思政课建设与党的创新理论武装同步推进
source: Journal of Ideological and Theoretical Education (Sixiang lilun jiaoyu daokan), 2024 no. 5
paras: Responding to a recent instruction from Xi Jinping on school ideological and political courses (sizhengke), Song Youwen asks how these courses should be built so that they advance in step with the Party's innovative theory. The author argues that this synchronisation is necessary because the courses now hold a prominent place in the Party Central Committee's overall strategy for governing the country, and that it requires deeper understanding of how Party theory develops and a content-led, high-quality development of the courses.

The article, published in a 2024 issue of a journal on ideological and political education, has three parts. The first sets out the strategic position of the courses. The second traces the pattern of theoretical innovation, using the sequence of Party theories and the revisions of the course curriculum since the 1980s. The third turns to practical measures for what the author calls connotative development.

In the first part, Song presents the courses as the key vehicle for four tasks: fostering virtue and cultivating people (the 'fundamental task' of education), building ideological consensus, forging a strong sense of community of the Chinese nation, and telling China's story to the world. In the second part, Song notes that curricula moved from the 1985, 1998 and 2005 schemes, and from courses on Mao Zedong Thought and Deng Xiaoping Theory to one on Xi Jinping Thought, and reads this as evidence that each theoretical advance is followed by theoretical arming and course reform. The author calls for systematisation and scholarly rigour (xitihua and xueli hua) in teaching, citing Engels's Anti-Dühring as a precedent, and insists that value education must rest on solid knowledge. The third part names three priorities: a curriculum and textbook system centred on Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, grounded in the relation between Marxism and traditional Chinese culture; teachers' close reading of original works; and equipping students with the Party theory's worldview and methodology, including its account of the 'three laws' of Party governance, socialist construction and human social development.

Song concludes that the courses should both absorb new theory into their content and use the achievements of the new era to enrich teaching and tell the story of the new era. Teaching should convey the truth, practical power and spiritual appeal of the theory, in plain language but with depth of research. Read the original if you want to see how a Renmin University scholar frames the official rationale and priorities for ideological and political courses in 2024.
quoteEn: Teaching in ideological and political courses must rest on in-depth research; the deeper the research, the more thorough and persuasive the teaching can be.
quoteZh: 思政课教学要以深入研究为基础，研究越是深入，思政课教学才能透彻、才能说服人。

glossary.explanation: The compulsory courses in Marxist theory and Party ideology taught at Chinese schools and universities. They are treated as the main channel for political education of students.
The officially declared fundamental task of education in China, combining moral and political formation with the transmission of knowledge.

glossary.zh: 铸牢中华民族共同体意识
glossary.en: forging a strong sense of community of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: cast firm the consciousness of the Chinese nation as a community
glossary.explanation: An official policy line, stressed since the late 2010s, on ethnic unity and a shared national identity among China's peoples.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's current official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.

glossary.literal: development in terms of internal content
glossary.explanation: Development that stresses quality, substance and internal improvement rather than expansion in scale; the author equates it with high-quality development.

t: Using the remarkable achievements of socialism with Chinese characteristics as content to teach ideological and political courses well
zh: 以中国特色社会主义取得的举世瞩目成就为内容支撑讲好思政课
paras: This short commentary, published in the People's Daily in June 2024, asks how the achievements of socialism with Chinese characteristics can be used to teach ideological and political courses (sizheng ke) in schools and universities. Taking its cue from Xi Jinping's instruction that these courses should rest on such achievements, Chen Jinlong argues that they should present facts as well as doctrine, grounding principles in facts and using principles to interpret them. Using the achievements of reform and opening up, and especially of the period since the 18th Party Congress (2012), is described as integral to the courses' task of fostering virtue and nurturing people.

The article has three parts. The first sets out how the achievements strengthen the courses' explanatory power, their emotional appeal and their approachability. The second identifies three kinds of content support the achievements supply: practical effectiveness, theoretical soundness and spiritual elevation. The third offers three practical focal points for teachers.

On the first part, Chen argues that theory alone cannot make arguments persuasive. Examples include high-speed rail, aerospace and the digital economy, which are said to illustrate new quality productive forces. Others are the 60.2 per cent gross enrolment rate in higher education in 2023 and the completion of poverty alleviation, which the article says met the UN 2030 poverty target ten years early. On the second, Chen contends that the achievements prove the success of the Party's path, confirm the scientific character of its innovative theory, and reflect the spirit of Chinese Communists. The three focal points are to apply a "big historical view" that places achievements in Party, national and world socialist history; to match specific achievements with specific teaching content, such as linking the principle of putting the people first to rising living standards and whole-process people's democracy; and to join the "small classroom" of the course with the "big classroom" of society through visits to fields, factories and development zones.

Chen concludes that firsthand contact with the achievements helps students understand course content and strengthens their conviction in Marxism, in socialism with Chinese characteristics and in the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. The text is a short normative piece on pedagogy rather than an empirical study. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official guidance frames the use of national achievements in Chinese ideological and political teaching.
quoteEn: Ideological and political courses must both present principles and set out facts, building principles on a foundation of facts, supporting principles with facts and interpreting facts through principles.
quoteZh: 思政课既要讲道理，也要摆事实，将道理建立在事实的基础上，以事实支撑道理，用道理诠释事实。

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses in Marxist theory, Party history and Party doctrine taught in Chinese schools and universities. They are meant to instil political convictions and moral values.
A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2023, referring to advanced productivity driven by technological innovation and emerging industries.
The official term for China's democratic model, which the Party presents as covering every stage of political and social life.
The Party's official designation for its own model of socialism, developed since the reform and opening up period.
An approach promoted in Party discourse that views a period within a long historical and wide spatial context in order to assess its significance.

t: Studying and grasping Xi Jinping's important statements on comprehensively deepening reform
zh: 深入学习领会习近平总书记关于全面深化改革的重要论述
paras: Writing in Qiushi in 2024, Mu Hong sets out to explain what Xi Jinping has said about comprehensively deepening reform since the Third Plenum of the 18th Central Committee (2013). The article argues that these statements answer why reform is needed in the new era and how to pursue it. In Mu's account, they form the richest and most creative part of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era and are the guiding thought and basic guideline for further reform and opening up.

The piece is a study-and-interpretation text organised into ten numbered principles, followed by a short conclusion. Each section quotes Xi, says what question the statement answers, and then lists what the Party Central Committee has done on that front since the 18th Party Congress (2012). The ten principles are Party leadership, the socialist path, innovation, a people-centred approach, problem orientation, emancipating the mind, rule of law, scientific methodology, opening up, and the Party's self-reform.

Mu's central claim is that reform is directed and bounded. It must follow the path of socialism with characteristics Chinese, avoiding both the 'old path of rigidity' and the 'evil path' of changing banners. The Party's centralised leadership, backed by the Two Establishes and the Two Upholds, is presented as the fundamental political guarantee. The author also treats reform as the application of the Marxist principle that relations of production must fit the productive forces. Mu links this to theoretical innovations such as high-quality development and new quality productive forces. Reform is to be advanced systematically, with the rule of law and with opening up, so that institutional strengths become governance capacity. Mu cites people's grassroots experiences, such as the Sanming health reform and the 'Fengqiao experience', as sources of reform practice.

Mu concludes that Xi's statements distil the historical experience of reform and opening up and the Party's understanding of the laws of socialist modernization, so they should be cherished and upheld over the long term. The author calls on Party members, especially leading cadres, to strengthen their political, intellectual and practical commitment to reform and to oppose formalism and bureaucratism. The text presents the Party's self-reform as leading a 'great social revolution', and sees reform as supplying momentum and institutional guarantees for national rejuvenation. Read the original if you want an authoritative example of how Party theorists summarise and organise Xi's reform discourse in the lead-up to the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024).
quoteEn: Comprehensively deepening reform is in essence the Party's application, adapted to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, of the basic Marxist principle that relations of production must suit the development of the productive forces and the superstructure must suit changes in the economic base, in light of new historical tasks and conditions.
quoteZh: 全面深化改革本质上是党根据新的历史任务和条件，推动生产关系适应生产力发展、上层建筑适应经济基础变化的马克思主义基本原理中国化时代化运用。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017 and 2018.
A formula from 2022 that affirms Xi Jinping's position as the Party's core and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought.
A Party requirement to uphold Xi Jinping's core position in the Central Committee and the Party's centralised, unified leadership.
A concept Xi put forward in 2023–24. It stresses innovation-driven, technology-led productive forces as the basis of high-quality development.
An official goal that replaces speed-focused growth with growth stressing quality, efficiency and innovation. It has been prominent since 2017.
The Party's term for its efforts to discipline and renew itself, linked to full and rigorous self-governance of the Party.

t: Striving to write a youth chapter of taking responsibility for Chinese modernization
zh: 奋力书写为中国式现代化挺膺担当的青春篇章
paras: This commentary responds to Xi Jinping's message to young people on Youth Day (4 May) 2024. Xi urged them to carry forward the May Fourth spirit, listen to the Party and follow the Party, and write a youth chapter of shouldering responsibility for Chinese modernization. Lin Jiang argues that the message sets the direction for the Party's youth work in the new era and should draw young people into building a strong country and achieving the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

The article is organised in three parts. The first asks how to inherit and develop the May Fourth spirit. The second sets out the trust and expectations the Party Central Committee places in youth since the 18th Party Congress (2012). The third turns to what young people should do in the race toward national rejuvenation. Lin draws throughout on Xi's speeches and on examples such as the winners of the 28th China Youth May Fourth Medal.

Lin's core argument is that the fate of youth has always been tied to the times, and that the history of national rejuvenation is also a history of youth struggle. The author reads the May Fourth Movement as the starting point of Marxism's spread in China and of the new-democratic revolution. Young people's most active period, Lin says, now coincides with the new journey of advancing the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation through Chinese modernization. Lin calls on them to take the lead in technological innovation, rural revitalisation, green development, social services and national defence, linking new quality productive forces to a demand for technical and applied talent. The author also asks them to hold ideals, accept hardship, reject pampered habits, and fold their personal efforts into the national cause. Lin adds that young officials, as the "key minority", should practise Xi's "five consciousnesses".

Lin concludes that young people should have confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics and unite with the people. Lin holds that the closer the nation comes to rejuvenation, the more youth must be mobilised and the less room there is for slackening. Read the original if you want to see how a Communist Youth League school official presents Xi's 2024 Youth Day message and the Party's current expectations of young people.
quoteEn: A history of national rejuvenation is also a history of youth struggle.
quoteZh: 一部民族复兴史,也是一部青年奋斗史。

glossary.explanation: The official term for China's path of modernization, which the Party presents as distinct from Western models. It was a central theme of the 20th Party Congress (2022).

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A long-term Party goal of restoring China's national strength and international standing, closely associated with Xi Jinping's idea of the Chinese Dream.
A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2023 that stresses technology-driven, innovation-led productive forces as the basis of high-quality development.
The official summary of the legacy of the 1919 May Fourth Movement, defined as patriotism, progress, democracy and science.
A national strategy launched in 2017 to develop agriculture, villages and rural livelihoods.
A Party phrase for leading cadres, whose conduct is said to set an example for the wider membership and society.

t: Upholding and developing the labour theory of value
zh: 坚持和发展劳动价值论
paras: Yang Jing and Liu Ying ask how the labour theory of value, a basic theory of Marxist political economy, can be upheld and developed in the age of digital and intelligent technology. They point to three new phenomena: the widening scope of productive labour, new forms of labour, and the participation of non-labour factors such as data in distribution. Their thesis is that understanding of Marx's theory must keep deepening, but its core must not change: living labour is the only source of value.

The article has three parts. It first restates the main tenets of Marx's theory: the two factors of the commodity, the dual character of labour, the magnitude of value, the value form and the law of value. It then sets out four areas where understanding needs to deepen: use value, productive labour, forms of labour, and the participation of production factors in distribution. Finally it proposes four distinctions as points of emphasis for further research.

The authors hold that in Marx's day consumption centred on material goods, whereas now spiritual products and services account for a growing share. They conclude that the concepts of use value and social product must be widened, and that productive labour now extends into non-material production. They also treat digital labour, such as social-media work, livestreaming and platform development, as a new form of human–machine interactive intellectual labour whose value-creating or value-transferring character needs study. The four distinctions are these. Living labour creates value, while all factors together create use values, and knowledge, technology, management and data create no value so long as they appear as objectified labour. Complex labour is multiplied simple labour and so creates more value. Productive labour must be told apart from unproductive labour such as commercial and financial work, which only shares in newly created value. Finally, every form of income originates in value created by labour, so "contribution" in distribution by factor means a role in producing use values.

The authors conclude that value creation and value distribution must be kept apart, and that distribution by factor according to contribution can be justified without abandoning Marx's thesis that only living labour creates value. They cite Xi Jinping on distribution according to work as the mainstay and on improving distribution by factor. They also cite the Digital China plan on data-based distribution. Read the original if you want a concise official-academic statement of how Chinese Marxist economists reconcile the labour theory of value with data as a factor of production and with digital labour.
quoteEn: However understanding is deepened, the essential core of Marx's labour theory of value must not change, and we should unwaveringly uphold Marx's scientific proposition that living labour is the sole source of value.
quoteZh: 但是不管如何深化认识，马克思劳动价值论的实质核心不能变，我们应毫不动摇地坚持马克思关于活劳动是创造价值的唯一源泉的科学论断。

glossary.explanation: In Marx, the physical and mental effort workers expend in production, as opposed to objectified (past) labour embodied in means of production. The article treats it as the sole source of new value.

A principle of China's income distribution system under which capital, technology, data and other production factors receive income according to their contribution. It operates alongside distribution according to work.
The socialist principle that individual income depends on the quantity and quality of labour contributed. Official Chinese policy treats it as the mainstay of the distribution system.

t: Improving the teaching system of university ideological and political theory courses by explaining principles "in depth, thoroughly and vividly"
zh: 在“讲深讲透讲活”道理中完善高校思政课教学体系
source: Journal of Ideological and Theoretical Education (思想理论教育导刊), 2024 no. 5
paras: Following the May 2024 conference on building school ideological and political courses, which relayed Xi Jinping's instruction to "explain principles in depth, thoroughly and vividly", Chen Xixi asks how university teachers can turn the unified textbook system into an effective teaching system. Chen argues that the answer lies in uniting the courses' ideological and theoretical substance with their approachability and relevance. In this reading, neither side may be pursued at the other's expense.

The article starts from Xi's 2019 speech to teachers of these courses and his 2022 remarks at Renmin University. It first explains why the courses must "go deep, thorough and vivid", citing their ideological nature and the training goals of socialist universities. It then devotes one section to each of the three requirements, offering concrete teaching proposals. These cover theoretical thinking, vertical links between school stages, reading original works, integrating the "seven histories" and the craft of classroom delivery.

Chen holds that the courses are the explicit, not implicit, vehicle of Marxist ideology. The textbooks' official wording therefore has to be converted into teaching content, since a teacher who stresses only conceptual analysis or only entertainment fails. "Depth" means training students' theoretical thinking, pairing constructive with critical teaching, and building the curriculum around Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. It also means avoiding repetition between high school, undergraduate and graduate courses. "Thoroughness" means guiding students to read original texts and placing principles within the seven histories. "Vividness" means starting from shallow, student-relevant cases that lead to deep theory, choosing what to treat in detail and what briefly, and following the textbook without reciting it. Chen also calls for plainer, more practical writing and speech, warning against formalism and stilted language.

Chen concludes that teaching should move from appealing to emotion to persuading by reason, from commenting on events to reasoning from them, from illustration to theoretical proof, and from covering everything to deepening step by step. Chen suggests this would raise both the courses' theoretical quality and their appeal to students. Read the original if you want a detailed, practice-oriented account of how Chinese university ideological and political courses are meant to be taught under current Party guidance.
quoteEn: In building the teaching system of ideological and political courses, we should as far as possible move from moving people by emotion to persuading them by reason, from commenting on events to reasoning from them, from illustration by example to theoretical proof, and from covering everything to deepening layer by layer.
quoteZh: 思政课教学体系的构建，要尽可能从以情动人提升为以理服人，从就事论事深化为就事论理，从举例说明转向理论证明，从面面俱到调整为层层深入

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party constitution in 2017. A dedicated university course and unified textbook now teach it.

Xi Jinping's extension of the "four histories" (Party, New China, reform and opening up, socialist development) to include 5,000 years of Chinese civilization, 170-plus years of national rejuvenation and the new era.

t: Ideological and political theory courses grounded in fine traditional Chinese culture, revolutionary culture and advanced socialist culture
zh: 思政课以中华优秀传统文化、革命文化和社会主义先进文化为力量根基
source: Research on Ideological Education (思想教育研究), 2024 no. 5
paras: Gao Guoxi takes up Xi Jinping's instruction that school ideological and political theory courses (sizhengke) should rest on three cultural sources: fine traditional Chinese culture, revolutionary culture and advanced socialist culture. The article asks how these resources can give the courses their "power base" in cultivating students as builders and successors of socialism. Gao argues that, used well, they turn knowledge transmission into value guidance and move students from spontaneous to conscious understanding, building cultural confidence.

The article, published in Research on Ideological Education (2024, no. 5), has three parts. The first explains what each of the three cultures contributes to understanding "why China is China". The second discusses how to make teaching more targeted and effective. The third sets out practical routes for putting the cultural resources to work in teaching.

In the first part, Gao reads traditional culture as showing the continuity and cultural subjectivity of Chinese civilisation, the tradition of unity, and a view of the person within social relations that Gao finds consistent with collectivism and common prosperity. Revolutionary culture, in Gao's account, explains the historical, theoretical and practical logic of Party leadership and provides ideals and convictions against historical nihilism. Advanced socialist culture is tied to the Two Integrations, which Gao says consolidate cultural subjectivity and let Marxism "speak Chinese". In the second part, Gao says the courses must respect the laws of education, students' physical and mental development and ideological work. They should move from knowledge to values to belief, and combine the teacher's leading role with the student's own agency.

For practice, Gao calls for integrated teaching across primary, secondary and university stages, coordination among the various ideological-political course types, and a family–school–community–government network. Gao also calls for making full use of the "great ideological and political course" (da sizhengke), which draws on social resources and practical teaching bases. Students should be drawn into volunteering and similar activity. Gao concludes that the three cultures give these courses a solid base for educating new people able to carry the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, and that this base needs further study. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese Marxism-school scholar links cultural resources to the design and pedagogy of ideological and political courses.
quoteEn: Ideological and political courses are not merely theoretical learning: they embody cultural genes in interpreting historical tradition, and apply and develop Marxist theory in the revolutionary practice led by the Party.
quoteZh: 思政课不只是理论之学，而是在阐释历史传统中体现文化基因，在党领导的革命实践中运用并发展马克思主义理论

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses in Chinese schools and universities that teach Marxism, Party theory, history and morality. Official documents describe them as the key courses for moral education.
Formula in which Marxism is combined with China's concrete realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture. The second integration was added to official discourse under Xi Jinping.
A concept in recent official discourse meaning that Chinese civilisation has its own continuous identity and capacity for independent development.
An approach that extends ideological and political education beyond the classroom, using social settings, practice bases and real-world experience.

t: Forty years of research on contradictions in ideological and political education: course, features and prospects
zh: 四十年来思想政治教育矛盾研究的历程、特征与展望
source: Journal of Party Building and Ideological Education in Schools (学校党建与思想教育)
paras: This review surveys four decades of scholarship (1984 to the present) on the contradictions that ideological and political education is meant to resolve. Hu and Bi start from the Marxist view that contradiction is the basic driver of development, so the discipline must say which contradictions it addresses and how. They argue that the research has moved from borrowing from pedagogy to building discipline-specific theory, and that it now needs more structural, concrete and forward-looking work.

The article is built in three parts. The first divides the research into four stages: initial construction (1984–1988), theoretical standardisation (1989–2003), gradual deepening (2004–2011) and innovative development (2012 to the present). The second identifies six features of the literature. The third sets out prospects under three headings.

On the history, Hu and Bi report that early work took over the moral-education theory of a basic contradiction between the educator's requirements and the educatee's actual moral level. Later scholars added layered and classified analyses, human-centred readings, and, after the shift in the principal social contradiction in the new era, contradictions linked to the need for a better life, online education and intelligent technology. The six features are Marxist guidance, grounding in the principal social contradiction, the laws of the discipline, the activity process, multidisciplinary borrowing and a focus on university students. For the future, they call for moving from multiplicity to structure by distinguishing basic from specific, principal from secondary, and inherent from new contradictions. They also call for linking abstract analysis to concrete goals, constraining factors and real problems, and for moving from adaptation to transcendence through traditional strengths, dialectical thinking and grassroots practical innovation.

Hu and Bi conclude that the field has produced rich results and more consensus than disagreement, but must change its thinking, widen its approaches and update its methods for the new era. They identify gaps: few studies of specific activities or tasks, thin analysis of the conditions under which influences operate, and a split between theoretical work on contradictions and descriptive work on problems. Read the original if you want a periodised map of Chinese scholarship on the basic contradiction of ideological and political education, with the main scholars and positions.
quoteEn: The practical soil for research on contradictions in ideological and political education is becoming ever thicker.
quoteZh: 思想政治教育矛盾研究的实践土壤也越来越厚实。

glossary.explanation: The Chinese discipline and practice of shaping people's political views, ideology and moral character, taught mainly in universities and Party organisations. It has been a recognised academic specialty since 1984.

The Party's official formulation of the main contradiction in Chinese society. Since the 19th Party Congress (2017) it has been the contradiction between people's growing need for a better life and unbalanced, inadequate development.

glossary.en: the need for a better life
glossary.explanation: The term used in the Party's post-2017 formulation of the principal social contradiction. Scholars use it to reframe the aims of ideological and political education.

t: Ideological and political education for university students in the perspective of social acceleration
zh: 社会加速视野下的大学生思想政治教育
source: Teaching and Research (教学与研究), 2024 no. 5
paras: Zhang Zhe asks how ideological and political education for university students should respond to what the article calls the era of social acceleration. The author argues that acceleration brings both opportunities and new challenges to this work, and that universities can meet them by guiding students in how they relate to the speed of others, to one another and to their own mental resilience.

The article has three parts. It first examines social acceleration through historical materialism, noting that Western acceleration theory grew out of left-wing debates on accelerationism and capitalism. It then analyses effects on students' learning, perception of time and psychology, on the media of ideological and political education, and on its environment. Finally it proposes three countermeasures, drawing on Hartmut Rosa's idea of resonance and on concepts from Hegel, Heidegger and Debord.

Zhang contends that, read through Marx, acceleration is not a single abstract process. It arises from the accelerating contradiction between the productive forces and the relations of production, and it unites positive and negative aspects, such as technological progress alongside faster economic crises and environmental pollution. For students, the author reports greater learning autonomy, a compressed sense of time and more psychological confusion. Digital media enrich teaching, but image-based 'spectacle' and technological logic risk weakening critical awareness and alienating students. A 'time lag' opens between the fast-changing external environment and the more stable internal environment of the education, producing what Zhang calls 'galloping standstill'.

Zhang proposes three responses. Students should be guided to coordinate with the 'social other's speed' by engaging dialectically with AI as a 'machine other' and by easing damaging competition over grades. They should be led to build wider 'relations of relations', with art as a bridge to resonance, since acceleration does not automatically mean a better life. Finally, a multi-layered support system should foster 'strong psychological traits', linking mental-health education and counselling with ideological and political education. Read the original if you want to see how contemporary social-acceleration theory is applied to Chinese university ideological and political education.
quoteEn: Social acceleration is not the same as an 'acceleration of the good'; it does not necessarily bring a good life, and many things it brings even reduce the experience of a good life.
quoteZh: 社会加速不等于“美好加速”，社会加速并不必然带来美好生活，很多由加速带来的东西甚至降低了对美好生活的体验。

glossary.explanation: The system of moral, political and ideological instruction in Chinese schools and universities, including compulsory 'ideological and political theory courses'. It aims to instil Marxism and Party-endorsed values.

A concept associated with Hartmut Rosa and with debates on accelerationism, describing the speeding up of technology, social change and the pace of life in modernity. The article adapts it to a historical-materialist framework.
Marx's theory that history develops through the contradictory movement of the productive forces and relations of production.
Rosa's term for a responsive, non-alienated relationship between people and the world. The article presents it as a way to counter alienation caused by acceleration.

t: Cultivating new-era youth with the core socialist values
zh: 用社会主义核心价值观培育时代新人
paras: Writing in Red Flag Manuscripts (2024, no. 9), Yang Xianjin, Party Secretary of Tianjin University, asks how universities should use the core socialist values to produce a new generation able to carry the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Taking its cue from Xi Jinping's message to young people for Youth Day 2024 and his October 2023 instruction on propaganda and ideological work, the article argues that universities must treat the cultivation and promotion of these values as a basic, strategic task. It describes the aim as young people who are idealistic, ready to take responsibility, able to endure hardship and willing to strive.

The piece has four parts. The first explains why universities must take up the task. The second sets out four directions for guiding young people. The third turns to methods, and the fourth to institutional guarantees. Throughout, Yang draws on Xi Jinping's speeches and the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022), and applies them to university governance and student life.

Yang gives three reasons for the university's role: young people's values are forming and will shape society's future values; universities are cultural centres with a mission of cultural leadership; and a "world-class university with Chinese characteristics" must rest on distinctive values and Chinese traditional culture. Moral education (lide shuren) is described as the university's fundamental task. It is to proceed by strengthening ideals and convictions, deepening patriotism, which Yang defines as the unity of loving the country, the Party and socialism, fostering a sense of responsibility, and building moral character. The core method is a movement from recognition to internalisation to action. Education and guidance cover theoretical study of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, ideals-and-convictions education and the use of "red resources". Cultural immersion works through campus culture, role models and traditional culture. Practice includes volunteering, academic integrity, online civility and encouraging graduates to take grassroots posts.

On guarantees, Yang calls for strengthened Party leadership, with the university Party committee as the leading core. He also calls for teacher training under the "educator spirit", integration of the values into every stage of talent cultivation and university rules, and cooperation among family, school, government and society. The work is described as "building a mansion in the mind", a gradual process that must be regularised and institutionalised. Read the original if you want to see how a university Party secretary translates the Party's values-education agenda into concrete campus measures and organisational mechanisms.
quoteEn: Building the core socialist values is, in the end, the construction of people's thinking and souls, and it focuses on producing socialist builders and successors with a correct worldview, outlook on life and values.
quoteZh: 社会主义核心价值观建设，说到底是人的思想建设、灵魂建设，聚焦的是造就具有正确世界观、人生观、价值观的社会主义建设者和接班人。

glossary.explanation: A set of twenty-four characters in twelve values, formulated at the 18th Party Congress (2012), at national, social and individual levels. They include prosperity, democracy, patriotism and integrity.
The stated fundamental task of Chinese education: cultivating moral character alongside knowledge. Xi Jinping has stressed it since the 18th Party Congress.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's current guiding ideology, written into the Party constitution in 2017 and into the state constitution in 2018.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The official national goal of restoring China to strength and prosperity, with milestones set for 2035 and the middle of the century.

t: The theoretical significance of accelerating the development of new quality productive forces
zh: 加快发展新质生产力的理论意义
paras: Zhou Wen asks what theoretical significance attaches to accelerating the development of new quality productive forces, a concept advanced by Xi Jinping. The article argues that the concept answers three questions: what these forces are, why they should be developed and how. In Zhou's account it innovates on Marxist productive-force theory, points to a new direction for productive-force development, and offers Chinese discourse and theory with world significance.

The piece, published in Red Flag Manuscript in 2024, has three sections. The first returns to Marx's treatment of productive forces: labourers, means of labour and objects of labour, together with cooperation, natural forces, management and science and technology. The second sets new quality productive forces within the history of industrial revolutions and in present-day international competition. The third links the concept to building China's own knowledge system and to the wider world.

Zhou contends that the concept continues Marx's view that science is itself a productive force and that productive forces and relations of production interact. It is described as the adapting of Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. In Zhou's reading it stresses innovation-led technology, information and data as core factors, counts green development as part of the concept, and looks to an optimised recombination of labourers, tools and materials. Zhou reads each industrial revolution as the product of scientific breakthroughs, so that new quality productive forces arise from key, disruptive technological breakthroughs. 'New' marks a break from resource-intensive growth, and 'quality' means innovation-driven leaps. The author says some developed countries use technology monopolies and decoupling to slow China, and presents the present as a convergence of challenges that is also a strategic opportunity.

Zhou concludes that the concept shows how to build Chinese discourse and theory from China's practice. Modernizing productive forces is described as the most fundamental task of Chinese modernization. Zhou holds that the concept will add momentum to world economic recovery, set an example for developing countries and become a Chinese theory leading world development. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated scholars in 2024 tied new quality productive forces to Marx's productive-force theory and to the project of a Chinese autonomous knowledge system.
quoteEn: New quality productive forces are productive forces in which scientific and technological innovation plays the leading role: high-tech, high-efficiency and high-quality, distinct from a mode of development that relies on heavy resource inputs and excessive consumption of resources and energy.
quoteZh: 新质生产力是科技创新在其中发挥主导作用的生产力，高科技、高效能、高质量，区别于依靠大量资源投入、过度消耗资源能源的生产力发展方式

glossary.explanation: A concept put forward by Xi Jinping in 2023–24 for advanced productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs and innovation rather than by heavy resource inputs. It has become a central slogan of China's economic policy.
The official name for China's path of modernization, presented by the Party as distinct from Western models. It has been prominent in Party discourse since the 20th Party Congress (2022).

t: Logical dimensions, technical foundations and forms of realisation of big data analysis in ideological and political education
zh: 思想政治教育大数据分析的逻辑向度、技术基础与实现形式
source: School Party Building and Ideological Education (Xuexiao dangjian yu sixiang jiaoyu)
paras: Liu Hongda and Liao Yinwei ask how big data analysis, which targets people's thoughts and behaviour, can be applied in ideological and political education. Citing Marx's remark that a science is truly developed only when it can use mathematics successfully, they argue that big data strengthens the discipline's capacity to capture, trace, describe, compute and predict people's behavioural, physiological, psychological and emotional states. Applying it, they say, requires clarifying its logical dimensions, mastering its technical basis and exploring its forms of realisation.

The article has three parts. The first sets out four logical shifts in how data are thought about. The second reviews technical foundations in four areas: network behaviour, physiological signals from wearables, facial-expression capture and emotion computing from audio and video. It draws on foreign studies of learning-platform logs, stress management, facial-expression recognition and speech analysis of depressed patients. The third proposes a four-dimensional analysis platform covering environmental variables, knowledge cognition, emotional identification and behavioural tendency.

On logic, the authors argue that analysis should move from social data to individual data, from known to unknown data, from logical data to computed data, and from quantitative to qualitative data. They stress that human thought is too complex to quantify fully, so qualitative analysis stays primary and quantitative analysis supplementary. Behavioural quantitative data can supply more objective support for qualitative judgements about thought. On realisation, each dimension yields analysis indices that support a practical scenario. Environmental data support a "dynamic environment" across home, school, community and internet. Cognitive data support a "dynamic teaching scenario" with personalised content, precise methods and intelligent procedures. Emotional data support a "smart psychological counselling scenario". Behavioural data support fuller, deeper and more accurate "student portraits" covering behaviour, thought and future tendencies.

The authors conclude that combining these logics, technologies and platforms can make ideological and political education more targeted, proactive, predictive and effective. They present big data as a means of moving from experience-based judgement to data-supported analysis of students' thoughts and behaviour. The text does not discuss privacy, ethics or the limits of such measurement. Read the original if you want a systematic Chinese-language account of how big data, wearables and affective computing are being proposed for use in ideological and political education.
quoteEn: The logical dimensions of big data analysis in ideological and political education
quoteZh: 思想政治教育大数据分析的逻辑向度

glossary.explanation: The system of teaching in schools, universities and Party organisations meant to shape students' political convictions, values and conduct in line with official ideology. It is also an academic discipline within Marxist theory studies in China.

t: Upholding fundamental principles and breaking new ground to promote the content-based development of ideological and political courses
zh: 守正创新推动思政课建设内涵式发展
source: Ideological and Educational Research (Sixiang jiaoyu yanjiu), 2024 no. 5
paras: Responding to Xi Jinping's recent instruction on school-level ideological and political courses (sizheng ke), Wang Yi asks how these courses can develop in depth under new conditions. The article argues that the answer lies in the method of "upholding fundamental principles and breaking new ground" (shouzheng chuangxin), which Wang presents as both a worldview and a methodology. Wang writes that the two elements are dialectically unified: upholding principles gives innovation its direction, and innovation supplies the source and momentum for upholding principles.

The piece is a commentary that opens with a general statement of the principle and then builds on four parts. The first concerns the core content of the courses, the second the achievements of socialism with Chinese characteristics as supporting material, the third the cultural foundations of the courses, and the fourth innovation as the driver of continuing improvement. It ties each part to quotations from Xi and to concrete measures, including course and textbook arrangements and teaching projects at Renmin University of China.

Wang's central move is to treat the "fundamental principles" as Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. The author calls for courses and textbooks built around it, such as the introductory course on that Thought, offered to undergraduates since autumn 2022. Other proposed modules cover Xi's thinking on the economy, the rule of law, ecological civilization, the military, diplomacy and culture. Wang also wants the courses to explain the achievements of socialism with Chinese characteristics and their root cause, so that students grasp the significance of the Two Establishes and strengthen the Four-sphere Confidence. The same section draws on traditional, revolutionary and advanced socialist culture, including core socialist values. On the innovation side, Wang proposes linking required and elective courses and combining the classroom with practice-based "big classrooms" in society. The article also proposes digital platforms with shared databases of problems, cases and teaching materials.

Wang concludes that this approach will fulfil the fundamental task of fostering virtue through education. It aims to train more young people of a new era who are reliable for the Party, patriotic and ready to take on the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. The article is a programmatic statement of how ideological and political courses are meant to be organised and taught. Read the original if you want to see how a Renmin University Party official translates Xi's 2024 instruction into specific curriculum, practice-teaching and digital measures.
quoteEn: Only by upholding fundamental principles does innovation have a clear stance and direction; only through continuous innovation can upholding principles gain its source and driving force.
quoteZh: 坚持守正，创新才有明确的立场和指向；不断创新，守正才能获得源泉和动力根基。

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses in Marxist theory, Party history and Party-state ideology taught from primary school to university in China.

glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.

glossary.literal: guard what is correct, create anew
glossary.explanation: A methodological formula stressed in recent Party discourse. It pairs fidelity to core political and theoretical positions with innovation in practice.
A 2021 Party formulation that affirms Xi Jinping's position as core of the Party and the guiding role of his Thought.
Confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics.
The official name for the Party's model of socialism since reform and opening up.

glossary.explanation: The Party's central national goal, tied to the Chinese Dream, of restoring China's strength and standing.

t: How to write the "big" article of the "Big Ideological and Political Course"
zh: “大思政课”如何做好“大”文章
paras: This commentary, published in Guangming Daily on 31 May 2024, asks how universities can realise the "big" in the "Big Ideological and Political Course" (大思政课). Zhang Ling argues that the shift from the ordinary ideological and political course to the "big" version is more than one word: it renews the concept, widens the vision and enlarges the pattern of teaching. In Zhang's reading, it joins the campus classroom to wider society and asks students to understand China and the world through history and reality.

The article follows Xi Jinping's recent instruction on school ideological and political courses and his earlier remarks on the subject. It then sets out six requirements, each beginning with "big": a large pattern, a large personality, great teachers, large resources, large combined strength and a large system.

Zhang's core argument is that each requirement ties teaching to Party leadership and to Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. Large personality means cultivating top talent in knowledge, ability and thought. Great teachers means strengthening the teaching corps, bringing in model workers, craftsmen and red-site guides, and exploring AI-era methods. Large resources means placing teaching within the long history of reform and opening up, New China, modern China, socialism and Chinese civilisation. Large combined strength and a large system mean opening the course to society, setting out responsibilities, and strengthening Party leadership through leading groups and accountability systems.

Zhang concludes that ideological and political education has entered a stage of quality improvement and substantive development. Universities should use "big" course construction to foster a new generation for Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want a concise example of how a university Party official presents the official agenda for ideological and political education in 2024.
quoteEn: The "Big Ideological and Political Course" is a large social course and a systematic project; relying on schools alone is far from enough, and it needs participation from all sectors of society and a course taught with open doors.
quoteZh: “大思政课”是一门社会大课，是系统工程，仅依靠学校远远不够，需要社会各方面的参与，需要开门办思政课。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted since 2021 that extends compulsory ideological and political courses beyond the classroom, using social practice, history and real-world resources. It was backed by a 2022 work plan from ten central departments.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017 and 2018.
The official term for China's own path of modernization, stressed by the Party since the 20th Party Congress (2022).

t: New developments in Xi Jinping's discourse on ideological and political theory courses in the five years since the "March 18" speech
zh: “3·18”重要讲话五年来习近平总书记关于思政课重要论述的新发展
source: Teaching and Research on Marxist Theory (马克思主义理论教学与研究), 2024 no. 2
paras: Marking five years since Xi Jinping's speech to a symposium of teachers of ideological and political theory courses on 18 March 2019, She asks how Xi's later remarks have extended his earlier statements. The article argues that these later remarks deepen the understanding of such courses in five respects and set higher requirements for their development.

The piece has two parts. The first sets out the five deepenings: the status of the courses, the conception of the curriculum, the essence of teaching, the teaching process and the evaluation of courses. The second draws six practical implications for teaching, and the article ends with a short summary.

In She's account, Xi has moved the courses from a "key course" for fostering virtue through education to a "top priority" of Party-led education work. The article says the "March 18" speech contained the outline of a "big ideological and political course" outlook, but that the concept was only named afterwards and extended to social practice and lived experience. It also says Xi later defined the essence of the courses as "explaining principles", described teaching as the teacher's "teaching" joined with the student's "comprehension", and proposed evaluation by whether the courses are taken seriously, suited to needs and done well.

She calls for teaching centred on Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, a wider conception of the curriculum, a renewed teacher–student relationship, continuous design across school stages and plural evaluation. The goal is the intensive, quality-focused development of the courses. Read the original if you want a concise account, from a Chinese education scholar, of how official guidance on political theory teaching has developed since 2019.
quoteEn: The statement that \"the essence of ideological and political theory courses is to explain principles\" raises the understanding of their teaching to the level of inherent laws.
quoteZh: “思政课的本质是讲道理”的论述，把对思政课教学的认识提升到内在规律层面

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses in Marxist theory, Party doctrine and moral-political education taught from primary school to university in China.
Concept stressing that political education should draw on society, practice and real life and not stay in the classroom.
Official fundamental task of education: cultivating moral character alongside knowledge.
