Zhang notes that Xi made the point at a special democratic life meeting of the Political Bureau held during the thematic education campaign on Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. Against a complex international and domestic situation, the article sets out three requirements: mastering Marxism, putting Party political building first, and guarding against risks.

First, Zhang argues that the depth of one's grasp of Marxist theory determines the degree of political sensitivity. Citing Mao Zedong's image of Marxism as a telescope and microscope, the author calls for thorough study of Xi Jinping Thought. Second, Zhang holds that political advancement distinguishes a Marxist party, so cadres must analyse problems politically, understand the decisive significance of the Two Establishes, strengthen the Four Consciousnesses, and carry out the Two Upholds. Third, the article urges bottom-line thinking and a sense of hardship, with particular vigilance towards political risks, sensitive factors and erroneous ideological trends.

Zhang concludes that these practices will keep all undertakings on the correct political course and improve cadres' ability to grasp direction, the overall situation and the general trend. Read the original if you want a compact example of how official Party-press commentary frames political sensitivity as a cadre competence.
quoteEn: Always maintaining a high degree of political sensitivity requires us to analyse problems politically so as to see their essence, and to solve problems politically so as to grasp their root.
quoteZh: 始终保持高度的政治敏锐性，要求我们从政治上分析问题进而看清本质，从政治上解决问题进而抓住根本。

glossary.explanation: A formula from the Party's 2021 resolution on history, affirming Xi Jinping's position as the core of the Central Committee and the Party as a whole, and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought.
The requirement to uphold the authority of General Secretary Xi Jinping as the core of the Party and the centralised, unified leadership of the Central Committee.
A Party requirement for members to maintain political awareness, a sense of the overall interest, a sense of the core, and a sense of alignment.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.
The capacity of officials to detect early signs of political problems and risks and to judge them from a political standpoint.

t: Cultivating a new generation for the new cultural mission
zh: 培养更好担负起新的文化使命的时代新人
paras: This short commentary, first published in the People's Daily on 10 April 2024, asks how universities can train students to take up the new cultural mission set out in Xi Jinping's thought on culture. That mission is to keep promoting cultural prosperity, build a strong cultural nation and build a modern Chinese civilization. He Xiuchao argues that universities should do so through three tasks: upholding cultural self-reliance, strengthening cultural confidence and achieving cultural self-strengthening.

The article takes each of the three tasks in turn, quoting Xi Jinping on each, and then sets out what the author thinks universities, ideological and political theory courses and teachers should do. It is addressed to higher-education leaders and teachers, and the author writes as a university Party secretary.

On cultural self-reliance, He holds that China's cultural subjectivity was built by the Party's combination of Marxism with the Chinese context and with fine traditional Chinese culture. In He's account, Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era is its strongest expression. On cultural confidence, He presents the Second Integration as evidence of the Party's confidence, and calls on universities to improve cultural curricula and teaching quality. He also wants ideological and political courses to teach Party theory and the histories of the Party, the People's Republic and socialism, so as to counter the pull of a more plural cultural environment. On cultural self-strengthening, He links culture to Chinese modernization and to the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

He concludes that universities should carry out the fundamental task of fostering virtue through education, keep Marxism as the guiding ideology and run Xi's cultural thought through the whole process of educating students. Teachers are urged to embody the spirit of educators and to bring Marxist views of the world, of life and of values into their teaching. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-state leaders frame university education around the new cultural mission.
quoteEn: Strengthening cultural confidence is a major question bearing on the rise and fall of the nation's fortunes, on cultural security and on the independence of the national spirit.
quoteZh: 坚定文化自信，是事关国运兴衰、事关文化安全、事关民族精神独立性的大问题。

glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's formulation, part of the Two Integrations, of combining the basic tenets of Marxism with fine traditional Chinese culture. It complements the First Integration, which combines Marxism with China's concrete realities.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.
Official term for confidence in China's own cultural tradition and in socialist culture. It is presented as a basis for the Four-sphere Confidence.
The officially stated fundamental task of education in China: moral and ideological formation alongside knowledge.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's central national goal, often tied to the centenary targets of 2049.
The Party's official term for its own path to modernization, stressing both material and cultural-ethical advancement.

t: The expansionist and exclusionary nature of the American road to modernization
zh: 美国现代化道路的扩张性、排他性
source: Renmin Luntan·Academic Frontiers (人民论坛·学术前沿), 2024 no. 5
paras: Liang Haoguang asks how the United States modernized and how that path underpins its present strategy of competing with China. The article argues that American modernization rests on expansion and exclusion: each sphere of development has been turned into an instrument of hegemony. Liang contends that Washington's policy towards China since the 18th Party Congress (2012) follows from this logic, and that China needs a differentiated response in each sphere.

The article first sets out the multiple senses of modernization: a world phenomenon, a civilizational shift and a development goal. It then reviews eight American "roads": agriculture and grain monopoly, industrialization and "re-industrialization", science and technology, culture, finance, military power, and global governance. For each, Liang pairs a historical account with the corresponding US policy towards China, supported by figures on trade, innovation, dollar share, voting rights and military bases. A second part proposes countermeasures in economics, technology, finance, security and governance, and a short conclusion returns to Chinese modernization.

Liang's central claim is that the US maintains its position through linked instruments. These include food-trade control, export controls and "democratic technology alliances", cultural and ideological infiltration, dollar dominance (supported by petrodollars, IMF veto power and currency swaps), a global base network, and alliance groupings such as the Quad. Liang says this makes the US the largest obstacle to reform of global governance. Liang adds that copying the American model has led most countries into development traps, and cites Daniel Bell and Cyril Black as rejecting the equation of modernization with Westernization.

Liang advises China to work "within the system" through incremental reform rather than challenge it from outside, and to avoid "extreme competition" and "hybrid confrontation". The proposals include building a modern industrial system and new quality productive forces, self-reliance in technology combined with greater openness, non-dollar payment systems and a multipolar currency order, a stronger Asia-Pacific position, and cooperation with Belt and Road and Global South countries. The article concludes that Chinese modernization offers developing countries a new paradigm. Read the original if you want a detailed example of how a Chinese Academy of Sciences scholar frames US–China rivalry as a contest between modernization paths, with data and policy recommendations.
quoteEn: The limits to promoting and replicating American modernization are plain: it is neither the endpoint of modernization nor its only path.
quoteZh: 美国现代化的推广、复制局限极为明显，其既不是现代化的终点，也不是唯一道路。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2023, referring to productivity driven by technological breakthroughs and innovation, especially in advanced industries.
The official term for China's path of modernization under Communist Party leadership, presented as distinct from the Western model.
A term for developing and emerging countries, increasingly used in Chinese foreign policy discourse to describe a group of states China identifies with.

t: Data-driven innovation in ideological and political education: trends, predicaments and supporting mechanisms
zh: 数据驱动思想政治教育创新发展的态势、困境及助推机制
source: School Party Building and Ideological Education (学校党建与思想教育)
paras: Yan Jie and Zhang Xiao ask how big-data technology can be used to renew ideological and political education, and what risks must be managed along the way. They argue that data-driven innovation expresses an internal unity of value rationality and instrumental rationality. In their view, the field should seize the opportunity, use big data reasonably, head off technological crises, and build an education mechanism guided by "technology for good", so as to improve educational results.

The article has three parts. The first describes three current trends: faster open sharing of data, continuing technological empowerment, and deepening cross-boundary integration. The second identifies three practical predicaments: data barriers, data risks and data anxiety. The third proposes three matching mechanisms, for data sharing, data security and data motivation. It opens with Xi Jinping's call to combine the traditional strengths of ideological and political work with information technology.

On the trends, the authors say that data technology enables precise identification, analysis, supply, evaluation and feedback about students. They add that VR, AR and MR create immersive scenes that turn abstract argument into something perceptible. They also say it shifts methods towards full-sample data and correlation analysis. The predicaments are set out in three groups. Data silos and monopolies obstruct the supply and circulation of educational data and leave room for social trends to exploit platforms. Leakage, misuse and theft threaten students' privacy. Over-reliance on figures, which neglects quality and causes anxiety, and over-rejection of data both undermine the work.

The proposed remedies run as follows. For sharing, the authors call for trust and identity recognition among educational actors, a defined list of shareable data with graded management, and agreed rules of conduct. For security, they propose data-processing, data-perception and encryption technologies, including node, link and end-to-end encryption. For motivation, they call for precise student profiling, an integrated intelligent data platform built with schools, government, enterprises and technical staff, and varied learning scenarios that move teaching from instrumental to human-centred. Read the original if you want a systematic Chinese-language account of how ideological and political education researchers frame digital technology, its risks and institutional safeguards.
quoteEn: Data-driven innovation in ideological and political education essentially embodies the internal unity of value rationality and instrumental rationality.
quoteZh: 数据驱动思想政治教育创新发展本质上体现了价值理性与工具理性的内在统一

glossary.explanation: The systematic work of Party, schools and other institutions to shape the political outlook, values and morals of students and citizens. It is also an academic discipline in China, closely tied to Marxist theory.

t: Why Western economic models no longer work
zh: 西方经济学模型为什么不灵了
paras: This short commentary, first published in Economic Daily on 24 February 2024, asks why Western economic models forecast so poorly. Ye argues that mainstream Western economics suffers from a severe "explanatory deficit" in reading both the world economy and China's, and that it needs to bring in humanistic factors.

The piece opens with recent criticism from within the West: the European Central Bank's president Christine Lagarde, AFP, and Nobel laureate Esther Duflo. It then cites central banks that have revised their forecasting systems after missing inflation, turns to Western reporting on China, and ends with a proposed remedy.

Ye contends that traditional Western economics starts from an abstract, homogeneous "economic man" and builds a logic driven purely by calculation. History, values and cultural and institutional influences are treated as "interference" and excluded. In Ye's account, this makes the models ill-suited to a more complex, non-linear world shaped by globalisation and technological revolution. Ye presents China as the typical case the models cannot explain, noting past predictions of collapse. Citing the Chinese economist Zhu Tian, Ye says China's growth owed much to institutions, policy and Confucian culture, especially its emphasis on saving and education.

Ye concludes that understanding China's economy requires adding more humanistic "parameters" and treating people as concrete social and cultural beings. Ye says this would explain why government can be a "necessary good" and why projects such as loss-making high-speed rail, rural revitalisation, the "dual carbon" policy and the Belt and Road Initiative go ahead. Read the original if you want a brief example of how a Chinese official newspaper frames the limits of Western economics.
quoteEn: To understand the Chinese economy, we need to introduce more humanistic "parameters".
quoteZh: 读懂中国经济，需引入更多人文“参数”。

glossary.explanation: A China-led international infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative announced by Xi Jinping in 2013.
A national strategy, launched in 2017, to develop agriculture, villages and rural incomes in China.
China's twin goals of peaking carbon emissions before 2030 and reaching carbon neutrality before 2060.

t: Scientific guidance for advancing theoretical innovation
zh: 推进理论创新的科学指引
paras: Liu Tongfang asks what Xi Jinping's statements on theoretical innovation tell the Party about how to renew its theory. Writing in Red Flag Manuscripts (2024), Liu argues that since the 18th Party Congress (2012) Xi has answered a series of major questions on the subject. In Liu's account, this has raised the Party's understanding of the laws of theoretical innovation to a new level and offers guidance for adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times.

The article is a short commentary in four sections. Each takes one pair of concepts from Xi's remarks: the "soul" and "root" of innovation; the age as the mother of ideas and practice as the source of theory; the people as the subject of innovation and their aspirations as its value; and systematization and doctrinal rigour (xueli).

Liu first holds that Marxism is the "soul-vein" and excellent traditional Chinese culture the "root-vein" of innovation, and that the two must interpenetrate. Marxism activates the living elements of traditional culture, while Chinese Marxists must draw on Chinese ways of thinking and living. Combining them is both a method and a result of innovation, and Liu ties it to the Two Integrations. Second, Liu says theory must respond to the age and to practice. It cites the "great changes unseen in a century", a community with a shared future for mankind and Chinese modernization as the practical ground for Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. Third, the people are the subject of innovation because their creative practice supplies fresh experience, and their aspiration for a better life is its value core, aimed at common prosperity. Liu also distinguishes system, which concerns links among parts, from doctrinal rigour, which concerns the passage from phenomena to essence. Without doctrinal rigour, innovation remains an accumulation of sensory experience and particular events.

Liu concludes that these four sets of ideas make up Xi's account of the laws of theoretical innovation. Following them, the author says, will open new horizons for adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times and will show the truth-power of Xi's thought. The piece is a Party-theory exposition rather than a critical study. Read the original if you want a compact statement of how current official theory frames the sources, subjects and methods of theoretical innovation.
quoteEn: The people are the subject of theoretical innovation, and meeting the people's aspiration for a better life is the value to which innovation belongs.
quoteZh: 人民是理论创新的主体，满足人民对美好生活的向往是理论创新的价值归属。

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: Official formula for the Party's project of fitting Marxist theory to China's conditions and to contemporary developments. It is the stated aim of theoretical innovation in Party discourse.
Formula stressing the integration of Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities and with excellent traditional Chinese culture. It is associated with Xi Jinping's 2021–2023 speeches.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.
Official term for China's own path of modernization, which the Party presents as distinct from Western models.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept for international relations and global governance, presented as an alternative to the existing international order.
Official goal of prosperity shared by all, stressed as a socialist objective in Party discourse, especially under Xi Jinping.

t: The basic functions and practical foundations of cultural inheritance and innovation in ideological and political education
zh: 思想政治教育文化传承创新的基本功能和现实根基
source: School Party Building and Ideological Education (学校党建与思想教育)
paras: Wang and Gong ask what role ideological and political education plays in the inheritance and innovation of culture, and how that role can be put on a firm footing. They argue that the two are fused in practice. In their account, ideological and political education carries out a mission of cultural inheritance and innovation, and that mission in turn gives it a deeper cultural root and distinctive strengths.

The article opens by defining cultural inheritance and innovation, drawing heavily on Xi Jinping's statements on 'keeping to fundamental principles while innovating', creative transformation of traditional culture and cultural confidence. It then sets out four basic functions of ideological and political education, and finally proposes four practical foundations for exercising them. It is a normative, policy-oriented discussion rather than an empirical study.

The authors present inheritance and innovation as mutually conditioning: inheritance supplies the basis for innovation, and innovation drives inheritance forward. The four functions are guiding (setting direction for mainstream culture and steering subcultures towards it), integrating (reconciling clashing cultures under mainstream values), innovating (supplying new content and methods) and disseminating (acting as a carrier for mainstream and traditional culture). The four foundations follow the same logic. These are Marxism as the guide, with Xi Jinping Thought on culture as core content; an integrative stance that upholds mainstream culture, draws on traditional culture and screens foreign culture; effective methods such as practice, healthy lifestyles, libraries and cultural exchange; and advanced channels of communication, including better-trained educators, new media and a healthy online environment.

Wang and Gong conclude that ideological and political education is an important support for cultural inheritance and innovation and a route to cultural confidence. They call for it to be guided by Marxism and Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, so that cultural development keeps its direction against rival currents of thought. Read the original if you want to see how Chinese scholars of ideological and political education link the discipline to cultural policy and to the official line on traditional culture.
quoteEn: The practical character of ideological and political education determines that its function of cultural innovation is realised through a continuous variety of rich practices.
quoteZh: 思想政治教育的实践性，决定了思想政治教育的文化创新功能是通过不断的丰富多彩的实践来实现的

glossary.explanation: The Chinese discipline and practice of teaching political theory, values and morality, from Party work to university courses. It is also an academic field in Chinese universities, housed in schools of Marxism.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.
Xi Jinping's term for confidence in China's cultural traditions and socialist culture. It was added to the earlier path, theory and system confidence.
The body of Xi's statements on cultural work, formally put forward in 2023. It stresses Marxism's guiding role and the Two Integrations.

t: Strengthening patriotic education in the new era to gather mighty strength for Chinese modernization
zh: 加强新时代爱国主义教育 凝聚中国式现代化建设磅礴伟力
paras: Hu Guodong, who is Youth League secretary at Peking University, asks how patriotic education should be carried out among young people in the new era. The article argues that the Patriotic Education Law of the People's Republic of China, in force from 1 January 2024, secures such education through law. In Hu's view this helps gather strength for building a modern socialist country and for the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

The short commentary has three parts. It first traces patriotism as an inherited spirit, from five thousand years of history through the Opium War, the May Fourth movement and the Party's leadership. It then explains why patriotic education matters now, citing Xi Jinping's statements since the 18th Party Congress (2012). Finally it sets out tasks for university Youth League organisations, with Peking University's practice as illustration.

Hu contends that the "two overall situations" (the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation and profound global change) bring confusion of thought and value conflicts, which makes building young people's spiritual world urgent. The author draws on Xi's formula that patriotism must be united with love of the Party and of socialism. Hu proposes three approaches: teaching Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era through combined teacher lectures and youth presentations; holding activities such as song concerts, poetry events and runs tied to national anniversaries; and linking ideals to practice, for example through volunteering during epidemic control and the Winter Olympics.

Hu concludes that patriotic education is a systematic project of consolidating foundations and forging the soul. Youth League bodies should follow Xi Jinping Thought, root patriotism in young people and cultivate a new generation able to carry the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation and Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party youth organisations describe the practical implementation of patriotic education in universities.
quoteEn: Patriotic education is a systematic project of consolidating the foundation and nurturing vitality, uniting hearts and forging the soul.
quoteZh: 爱国主义教育是一项固本培元、凝心铸魂的系统工程。

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal of restoring China to national strength and international standing after the "century of humiliation". It is closely tied to the Chinese Dream and the two centenary goals.
The official name for China's path to modernization under Party leadership, presented as distinct from Western models. It has been prominent in Party discourse since the 20th Party Congress (2022).

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018. It is taught as a core subject in schools and universities.

t: Grasping the foundations of cultural confidence
zh: 深入把握文化自信的根基所在
paras: This short commentary asks what cultural confidence rests on and how it should be strengthened. Zeng and Yin argue that it has three foundations: cultural subjectivity, Chinese civilisation, and Chinese modernization. They present cultural confidence as an important part of Xi Jinping's thought on culture and as an original contribution to Marxist cultural theory.

The piece is organised in three parts, one for each foundation. Each opens with a statement by Xi Jinping and ends with a task for the new era. The authors tie the discussion to building a culturally strong country and to the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

First, the authors hold that cultural subjectivity is the fundamental support of cultural confidence. They say it was built under Party leadership through the Two Integrations, and that Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era is its strongest expression. Second, they describe Chinese civilisation as continuous, innovative, unified, inclusive and peaceful. In their account, cultural confidence is therefore open and inclusive, not a matter of stagnation, simple restoration or blind exclusion of the foreign. Third, they argue that Chinese modernization supplies the practical ground for cultural confidence. They say it has rejected capital-centred, polarising, materialist and expansionist Western modernization and has broken the equation of modernization with Westernization.

The authors call for upholding the Party's cultural leadership, following the path of socialist culture with Chinese characteristics, and learning from other civilisations. They also call for turning Chinese experience into Chinese theory, so that cultural confidence and Chinese modernization reinforce each other. Read the original if you want a concise, official-style statement of how Party theorists currently ground cultural confidence.
quoteEn: Firm cultural confidence is not self-isolation or simple retro-restoration, nor is it self-importance and blind exclusion of the foreign, but rather an adherence to openness and inclusiveness.
quoteZh: 坚定文化自信不是故步自封、简单复古，也不是唯我独尊、盲目排外，而是秉持开放包容。

glossary.explanation: A concept stressed by Xi Jinping since the 2010s. It refers to confidence in the value and vitality of China's own culture, and is often listed alongside confidence in the path, theory and system of socialism with Chinese characteristics.
The idea that a culture must have its own independent identity and agency in order to lead, unite and shape society. Xi Jinping presented it as the source of cultural confidence.
The principle of combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture.
The official name for China's path of modernization. Party texts describe it as distinct from Western models.
A Party goal of raising China's cultural influence, creativity and cohesion, with the aim of building it by 2035.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's central national goal, associated with Xi Jinping's Chinese Dream and a target date of mid-century.

t: Promoting the building of a case bank for integrated ideological and political theory teaching across university, secondary and primary schools through quality evaluation
zh: 以质量评价推动大中小学思政课一体化教学课例库建设
paras: How should quality evaluation be used to build a bank of model teaching cases for the integrated teaching of ideological and political theory courses across universities, secondary schools and primary schools? Liu Jie argues that evaluation is a deep intervention in the case bank's construction and bears on the high-quality development of integrated ideological and political education. In the author's view, evaluation can produce "typical cases" only if it reflects the particular ecology and developmental regularities of this education.

The short commentary, written in 2024, is organised in three parts. The first sets out basic principles of quality evaluation, the second proposes a system of evaluation standards, and the third discusses relationships that must be handled correctly in integrated teaching. It draws on Xi Jinping's statements on ideological and political courses, the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022) and the project on big-data support for integrated teaching that funded the work.

On principles, Liu holds that ideological and political courses should be judged by whether they "explain principles in depth, thoroughly and vividly". This means building on the Party's established practice of mass ideological education, using Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, and strengthening ideals and convictions step by step from primary school to university. The proposed standards are a value standard that coordinates ideological and political courses with ideological and political education running through other courses; an effect standard that joins a grand historical perspective to political identification; and a standard that combines each school stage's comparative advantages with targeted measures and feedback. The relationships to be handled are those between textbook content and teaching content, between quantitative and qualitative indicators (including big-data monitoring of public opinion on cases), and between existing conditions and the teachers and students involved.

Liu concludes that principles, standards and the handling of these relationships should all be anchored in fostering virtue and nurturing talent and in improving students' core competencies. The author links this to the strategy of building a strong education system and to supplying talent for Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Chinese academics frame evaluation criteria for integrated ideological and political teaching, and how they tie them to Party-defined educational goals.
quoteEn: Quality evaluation can play a normative role in creating \"typical cases\" only when it fully reflects or presents their inherent connections and inner nature.
quoteZh: 质量评价只有在充分反映或呈现出它们之间的固有联系和内在本质时，才具备打造“典型课例”的规范作用。

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses on Marxism, Party theory and moral and political education taught at all levels of Chinese schooling.
A stated fundamental task of Chinese education, combining moral and ideological formation with the training of skilled people.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017 and 2018.
The official name for China's path of development, promoted by the Party since the 20th Party Congress in 2022.
A national goal of building China into a leading country in education, stressed in Party documents since the 20th Party Congress.

t: Youth ideological and political education in light of the evolution of educational digitalization
zh: 基于教育数字化演进之路的青年思想政治教育探究
source: Research on the Marxist Theory Discipline (《马克思主义理论学科研究》)
paras: Marking 40 years since the establishment of the ideological and political education discipline and 30 years since China's full internet connection, Feng Pei asks what the history of educational digitalization teaches about how to guide young people ideologically. The article argues that, although digital technologies keep changing, certain constants run through them, and that youth ideological and political education should use these constants to lead students' new needs as digital education moves from informatization to full digitalization.

The article first traces three stages of Chinese educational digitalization, seen from the perspective of ideological and cultural communication: a text-based 1.0 era around 2000 (desktop computers, BBS forums, blogs), an image-based 2.0 era after 2010 (mobile phones, MOOCs, Weibo, WeChat, short video), and an intelligent 3.0 era since 2013 (big data, virtual simulation, generative AI). It then draws three lessons from this history and three directions for guidance. Feng frames the discussion with Xi Jinping's remarks on the internet and AI and with the "seven focal points" of Xi Jinping's thought on culture.

Feng's central move is to distinguish the "constant within change" from the "new within the constant". The three constants are that content is king, that meeting individual needs is fundamental, and that connection and resonance are essential. Feng draws on Marx's account of needs as driving history to support the second. For each constant, Feng identifies a new feature of today's students and a matching task. Students born after 1995 and 2000 are said to be fragmented in their information intake, more emotionally expressive online, drawn to "shallow socializing", and inclined to conceal their real thinking in closed peer circles. Feng warns that algorithmic "information cocoons" and generative AI carry risks, including simulated empathy displacing real contact. The article also notes that ideological and political work suffers from weak sensitivity to student needs, staff turnover and costly, hard-to-scale virtual simulation.

Feng concludes that educators should keep the fundamental task of fostering virtue and cultivating talent as the guiding orientation, and renew it in three ways. They should respond sensitively to students' changing needs, supply precise and vivid content that is neither sensationalised nor pandering, and link the seven subsystems of university ideological and political work online and offline. Concrete proposals include "one-stop student communities", AI corpora for career, mental health and academic guidance, open feedback systems to evaluate staff performance, and regional university alliances to share simulation resources. The aim is to serve Chinese modernization by raising a new generation. Read the original if you want a Chinese academic account of how ideological and political educators propose to respond to generative AI, algorithms and youth online culture.
quoteEn: Education is not an amusement park or a catwalk.
quoteZh: 教育不是娱乐场和走秀台。

glossary.explanation: The system of teaching and guidance in schools and universities meant to instil the Party's ideology, political values and morality. It is also an academic discipline established in China in 1984.
The official term for China's path of modernization under Party leadership, promoted prominently since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
An official formulation of the fundamental task of education in China: moral formation alongside the training of capable people.

t: Forging strong organizations and building a sound contingent of cadres as an important focus
zh: 以锻造坚强组织、建设过硬队伍为重要着力点
paras: This commentary, published in Red Flag Manuscripts (Hongqi Wengao) in 2024, interprets one of the "nine requirements" that Xi Jinping set out at the Third Plenary Session of the 20th Central Commission for Discipline Inspection: advancing the Party's self-reform by forging strong organizations and building a sound contingent of cadres. Wang argues that a tightly knit organizational system is the source of a Marxist party's strength. Pursuing this focus, in the author's view, shows the Party's resolve to build such a system and to coordinate Party building at every level and in every field.

The article has three parts. The first explains why organization matters, drawing on Xi's statement that the Party's strength comes from its organization, and on the Party's record since its founding more than a century ago. The second sets out how to strengthen the political and organizational functions of Party organizations, as laid out at the 20th Party Congress (2022). The third turns to cadres, Party members and talent.

Wang's core claim is that the Party's central, local and primary-level organizations form a chain from the "first kilometre" to the "last kilometre" of carrying out the Central Committee's decisions. The author says the political and organizational functions reinforce each other, and proposes five areas of work. These are political building, theoretical education, tighter implementation, the mass line, and "immunity" through the Party's self-reform. On cadres, Wang calls for the principle that the Party manages cadres, with political reliability ranked first among the criteria for a "good cadre". The author also calls for strict entry and exit rules for membership, more recruitment from workers, farmers and young intellectuals, and the gathering of patriotic talent.

Wang concludes that comprehensive Party organization and a leadership that can command the whole Party to act together is an advantage no other party in the world has. Deepening the Party's self-reform through strong organizations and sound cadres, the author holds, will supply continuing momentum for high-quality development. Read the original if you want to see how Party-building discourse in 2024 linked organization, cadre selection and membership management to the Party's self-reform.
quoteEn: Political character is the fundamental attribute of Party organizations and political function is their basic function; the organizational function serves the political function, and is the foundation and guarantee for its exercise.
quoteZh: 政治属性是党组织的根本属性，政治功能是党组织的基本功能；组织功能服务于政治功能，是发挥党组织政治功能的基础和保证。

glossary.explanation: A concept central to Xi Jinping's thinking on Party building. It refers to the Party's efforts to discipline, purify and improve itself, and officials present it as the way the Party avoids the decay of other ruling parties.

A Party method, associated with Mao Zedong, of drawing ideas from the people and returning them as policy while staying in close contact with the people. It is treated as a core principle of Party work.
The official term, in use since about 2017, for a growth model that stresses quality, innovation and efficiency over speed alone.

t: Contributing the strength of higher education in the new era to accelerating the development of new quality productive forces
zh: 为推动新质生产力加快发展贡献新时代高等教育力量
paras: Written after Xi Jinping's speech at the 11th collective study session of the Political Bureau (31 January 2024), this article asks what role universities should play in speeding up new quality productive forces. Zhang argues that higher education is the key point where education, science and technology, and talent converge, and so a foundational link in developing productive forces. Universities should therefore study Xi's statements on the subject and carry out education reform, scientific innovation and talent training accordingly.

The article has three parts. The first treats accelerating new quality productive forces as an important mission of higher education. The second sets out the tasks this places on universities. The third proposes routes for the new era. Zhang draws heavily on Xi's remarks, especially on innovation, high-quality development and the 'Party's leadership of universities'.

In the first part, Zhang reasons that each major leap in productive forces has produced demand for new kinds of workers and changed education, from papermaking and printing to the three industrial revolutions. Three justifications follow: the modernization of education, the building of a major world centre for talent and an innovation highland, and the creation of world-class universities with Chinese characteristics, whose disciplines, teaching and governance new quality productive forces are said to restructure. The second part names three tasks: raising the quality of home-grown talent, advancing original and disruptive technological innovation toward high-level scientific and technological self-reliance, and speeding the conversion of research results into industry. The third part's routes are: strengthen Party leadership of universities, including the president responsibility system under the Party committee; pursue research at the world frontier and on national strategic needs; reshape talent-training goals, methods and evaluation; and let discipline building lead the modern industrial system through basic, emerging and interdisciplinary fields.

Zhang concludes that universities should build education, science and technology, and talent into a unified strategic base, innovation highland and stronghold. The article gives concrete measures: basic-discipline training bases, technology-transfer bodies, organised industry–education integration, and interdisciplinary teams and platforms for fields such as quantum and life sciences. Read the original if you want to see how a Party-theory journal translates Xi's new quality productive forces discourse into a programme for university governance, talent training and discipline planning.
quoteEn: Innovation relies on progress in science and technology, scientific and technological progress relies on talent training, and talent training relies on education.
quoteZh: 创新依靠科学与技术进步，科技进步依靠人才培养，人才培养依靠教育。

glossary.explanation: A concept Xi Jinping put forward in 2023–24. It refers to advanced productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs, innovative allocation of production factors and industrial upgrading.
An official goal of economic policy since about 2017, stressing quality, efficiency and innovation over speed of growth.

glossary.literal: science and technology standing on its own and strengthening itself
glossary.explanation: An official aim of reducing dependence on foreign core technologies and strengthening domestic innovation capacity.

glossary.zh: 党委领导下的校长负责制
glossary.pinyin: dǎngwěi lǐngdǎo xià de xiàozhǎng fùzé zhì
glossary.en: president responsibility system under the Party committee
glossary.literal: president-responsibility system under Party committee leadership
glossary.explanation: The governance arrangement in Chinese public universities in which the university Party committee holds the leading role and the president runs daily administration.
A policy of linking universities and vocational institutions closely with industry in training, research and technology transfer.

t: Upholding and strengthening the Party's overall leadership
zh: 坚持和加强党的全面领导
paras: Writing in Red Flag Manuscripts (2024, no. 6), Li Haiqing takes up the first of the "thirteen upholds" that the June 2023 national organisation work conference used to summarise Xi Jinping's thinking on Party building: upholding and strengthening the Party's overall leadership. Li argues that this is an inherent requirement of socialism with Chinese characteristics, that it must be put into practice in a comprehensive, systematic and holistic way, and that it depends on full and rigorous self-governance of the Party and on the Party's self-reform.

The piece is a short theoretical commentary in three numbered sections. The first explains why Party leadership is essential to socialism with Chinese characteristics and to Chinese modernization. The second unpacks the 20th Party Congress (2022) formula that Party leadership is "comprehensive, systematic and holistic". The third links leadership to the Party's self-reform, with a historical survey from the 1927 August 7 Meeting to the present.

Li builds on Xi Jinping's statements that Party leadership is the defining feature and greatest strength of socialism with Chinese characteristics. In Li's reading, a complex international and domestic environment raises the demands on the Party's capacity to set direction, manage risk and push reform. Li concludes that without Party leadership, national strength and rejuvenation would be illusory. Li then defines the three terms. "Comprehensive" covers the objects, content, process and methods of leadership, though the Party "oversees but does not take over" and must act within the constitution and law. "Systematic" means a complete system of leadership institutions. "Holistic" means every level of Party organisation, and the Party and state apparatus, functions in coordination. The first priority is upholding the authority and centralised, unified leadership of the Central Committee, through the Two Establishes and the Two Upholds.

In the third section Li holds that willingness to undertake self-reform distinguishes the Party from other parties and explains how it has escaped the historical cycle of rise and fall. Li presents the Party's history as both a social revolution and a self-reform, and credits the anti-corruption campaign since the 18th Party Congress (2012) with removing serious hidden dangers and reversing lax Party discipline. Li concludes that self-reform supplies the political guarantee for national strength and rejuvenation. Read the original if you want a concise, official-line account of how Party scholars justify the doctrine of overall Party leadership and link it to Party discipline.
quoteEn: The Chinese Communist Party's course of struggle is both a magnificent history of social revolution and a history of self-reform that sweeps away the foul and promotes the clean.
quoteZh: 中国共产党的奋斗征程，既是一部波澜壮阔的社会革命史，也是一部激浊扬清的自我革命史。

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.literal: comprehensively and strictly govern the Party
glossary.explanation: A policy line associated with Xi Jinping since 2012–14, covering Party discipline, anti-corruption and internal supervision.
Official term for the Party's efforts to correct its own faults and purify itself. It is presented as the counterpart of the "great social revolution" the Party leads.
A formula adopted in 2021–22 that affirms Xi Jinping's position as the core of the Party Central Committee and the Party as a whole, and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought.
A political requirement that Party members uphold Xi Jinping's core position and the authority and centralised, unified leadership of the Central Committee.
The official name for China's development path, set out especially at the 20th Party Congress in 2022.
The official name for China's political and economic system and its guiding ideology since the 1980s.

keywords: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party

t: Building the spiritual foundation and cultivating new people of the era
st: Ideological and political theory courses in the new era
zh: 铸牢精神之基 培育时代新人
paras: Han Hua's article, published in Qiushi's Red Flag Manuscripts (Hongqi Wengao) in 2024, asks how ideological and political theory courses (sizheng ke) in schools and universities can cultivate "new people of the era" (shidai xinren). Drawing throughout on Xi Jinping's remarks since the 18th Party Congress (2012), Han argues that these courses are the key vehicle for implementing the fundamental task of fostering virtue and cultivating talent. They are, in this account, central to ensuring that the Party's cause and the building of a modern socialist country have successors.

The article is organised in three parts. The first deals with education in ideals and convictions, which Han calls the red thread running through the courses. The second turns to teaching scientific ways of thinking. The third treats the cultivation of new people of the era as a systematic project in which the courses occupy a pivotal place across the stages of a young person's development. Each part is built around dated statements by Xi, from the 2016 national conference on ideological and political work in universities to the 2023 study campaign on Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era.

Han's central claims are that firm convictions come from scientific theory, and that teachers must therefore present Marxism and Xi's thought in a way that is deep, thorough and lively, rather than as empty preaching. The courses should explain why the Party, Marxism and socialism with Chinese characteristics are, in the author's words, effective and good, and help students merge personal ideals with the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Han adds that students need Marxist standpoints, viewpoints and methods, including historical, dialectical, systemic and innovative thinking, not just abstract concepts. The courses should also move progressively from primary school to university, address practical problems in study, careers and daily life, and put moral education first.

Han concludes that the courses must be reformed in teaching concepts, content, methods and means, so that students are willing to learn and can apply what they learn. The aim is talent who support Party leadership and the socialist system and commit their lives to socialism with Chinese characteristics. Read the original if you want a compact, Xi-quotation-based statement of how Party publications frame the purpose and method of ideological and political courses in the new era.
quoteEn: Ideological and political courses must explain the principles of belief in a way that is deep, thorough and lively, answering students with rigorous theoretical analysis, persuading them with thoroughgoing theory and guiding them by the power of truth, so that they know what is so, why it is so, and why it must be so.
quoteZh: 思政课要把信仰的道理讲深、讲透、讲活，以透彻的学理分析回应学生，以彻底的思想理论说服学生，用真理的强大力量引导学生，让学生“知其然、知其所以然、知其所以必然”。

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses (abbreviated sizheng ke) in Chinese schools and universities that teach Marxism, Party theory and moral and legal education.
A phrase used in Party discourse, notably since Xi Jinping's 2017 report to the 19th Party Congress, for young people expected to shoulder the task of national rejuvenation.
The stated fundamental task of Chinese education, giving priority to moral formation alongside the acquisition of knowledge and skills.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The official guiding ideology of the Chinese Communist Party, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's long-term national goal of restoring China's strength and international standing, closely linked to the Chinese Dream.

t: Consolidating and extending the results of the theme education campaign and advancing the modernization of grassroots governance
zh: 巩固拓展主题教育成果 奋力推进基层治理现代化
paras: This commentary by the Beijing Institute of Party Building takes up Xi Jinping's speech of 31 January 2024 on consolidating and extending the results of the Party's theme education campaign. It asks how those results can be turned into progress in modernizing grassroots governance. The authors argue that Party building must lead grassroots governance, and that doing so supports Chinese modernization.

The article is organised around four slogans from the campaign: learning to forge the soul, to increase wisdom, to correct work style and to promote action. Under each it sets out one task: building the ideological foundation, innovating ideas and measures, forging the governance workforce, and ensuring tasks are carried out. Each section draws heavily on Xi's remarks on grassroots work and pairs them with recommendations.

The first move is to justify the priority given to the grassroots. Citing Xi, the authors present grassroots governance as the base of the Party's rule, a way to meet people's aspirations for a better life, and a precondition for modernizing national governance. The second move is institutional. They call for fuller Party leadership, noting that Party-led governance risks becoming diluted or hollow. They also call for a streamlined grassroots management system, with resources, management and services moved down to the street and township level. Further proposals are wider participation by residents, social organisations and market actors, and combining self-governance, rule of law and moral governance. The third move concerns cadres and delivery. The authors call for the "Fengqiao experience" and the "four go-to-the-grassroots" practice. They also want sustained correction of formalism and bureaucratism to lighten the burden on grassroots officials, and training for village and community Party secretaries. They add a closed-loop, full-cycle management system with a performance evaluation in which residents' satisfaction carries weight, plus more funding and better community service facilities.

The authors conclude that grassroots governance works as a foundation for national governance, summed up in the phrase "good governance at the grassroots" underpinning "the governance of a great country". They propose that Party committees and governments at every level keep these tasks in view and take responsibility for results. Read the original if you want a compact example of how a Party research body translates Xi Jinping's speeches into a practical agenda for grassroots governance, including its stated problems and its remedies.
quoteEn: In grassroots governance, responsibility lies with the government, vitality with society, and potential with the market.
quoteZh: 基层治理，责任在政府、活力在社会、潜力在市场。

glossary.explanation: A Party-wide study and rectification campaign. This one, on Xi Jinping Thought, ran through 2023 and was formally summed up at the start of 2024.
The official term for China's path of modernization, promoted under Xi Jinping since 2021 as distinct from Western models.
A model from Fengqiao in Zhejiang, dating to the 1960s, in which disputes are resolved locally by relying on the masses. It has been recast as a "new era" approach under Xi.

glossary.literal: four goings down to the grassroots
glossary.explanation: A work method in which officials go down to the grassroots to investigate, handle petitions, promote policy and solve problems. Xi Jinping associates it with his earlier local posts.

t: Cultivating the course (yangke): the essential skill for ideological and political theory teachers who want more effective teaching
zh: 养课：思政课教师提高教学实效性必须练就的功夫
source: Journal of Ideological and Theoretical Education (思想理论教育导刊), 2024 no. 3
paras: Five years after Xi Jinping's 18 March 2019 speech at the symposium for teachers of ideological and political theory courses, Lu Binghui argues that teachers have become technically proficient at preparing and delivering lessons. Even so, the author holds that this is not enough to raise student attendance and attentiveness. The article proposes "yangke" (cultivating the course) as a further requirement: the teacher's own work on personal character, on abilities and qualities, and on the teaching environment.

The article is built around three headings that match the three dimensions of yangke. Part one reads the speech's "six requirements" for teachers as a path to moral cultivation. Part two takes the "eight unifications" as the key to building ability. Part three treats creating a good classroom atmosphere as the practical measure. Lu draws on classical Chinese sayings, Marx, Lenin and the speech itself, and cites an Anhui provincial policy from 2022 on appointing student ideological-political officers.

Lu groups the six requirements into three qualities: genuine feeling (strong politics and deep commitment), skill (new thinking and broad vision, combining specialist depth with breadth) and good character (strict self-discipline and upright personality). The eight unifications are applied to the teacher's professional stance, content and methods. Lu distinguishes facts, cases and materials as three ways of telling stories, and says methods should emphasise the constructive over the critical, diversity over uniformity, inspiration over indoctrination, and implicit over explicit education. The author's most distinctive move is an analogy with a pop star's concert. A teacher meets strangers with no build-up, so the first lesson is decisive, and the teacher must create a good "soft environment".

For university teaching, Lu urges teachers to relax their habitual absolute dominance of the classroom and move closer to students. Suggested steps include appointing class representatives and ideological-political officers and forming interest groups. Teachers should also join campus cultural activities and summer social practice, and show family-like concern for students' thinking and daily lives. Lu contends this will strengthen rather than weaken the teacher's guiding role. Read the original if you study ideological and political education in Chinese universities and want a detailed, practice-oriented reading of Xi Jinping's 2019 speech.
quoteEn: \"Yangke\" refers to the cultivating work that teachers do on themselves, in three areas, so as to teach ideological and political courses well: refining personal character, developing abilities and qualities, and nourishing the teaching environment.
quoteZh: 所谓“养课”，就是教师本人为讲好思政课在修养个体品德、培养能力素质、滋养教学环境三个方面所做的涵养工作。

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses in Marxism, Party theory and moral education taught at Chinese schools and universities. Their teaching is a central concern of Party education policy.
The author's own coinage for the teacher's preparatory self-cultivation, covering character, abilities and teaching environment, as distinct from lesson preparation and delivery.
Xi Jinping's 2019 criteria for ideological and political theory teachers: strong politics, deep feeling, new thinking, broad vision, strict self-discipline and upright personality.
Eight pairings set out in the same 2019 speech that teachers should hold together, such as political and academic content, or value and knowledge.

t: Advancing the integrated development of ideological and political courses across primary, secondary and tertiary schools: following the fundamental principles, strengthening practice, seeking innovation
zh: 推进大中小学思政课一体化建设：循根本、强实践、求创新
source: Journal of Ideological and Theoretical Education (Sixiang lilun jiaoyu daokan), 2024 no. 3
paras: Five years after Xi Jinping called in March 2019 for the integrated development of ideological and political courses (sizheng ke) from primary school to university to be treated as an important project, Xu Rong asks how that work can reach a new stage of high-quality development. The article argues that integration should rest on clearly understood fundamental principles, be driven by practice that confronts concrete bottlenecks, and be renewed through innovation suited to a changed educational and technological environment.

The article has three parts. The first sets out the guiding principles: serving national strategic needs, promoting students' growth, and improving teaching effectiveness. The second examines the practical logic of integration through a practice-oriented outlook, a strong problem awareness and effective coordination mechanisms. The third looks ahead to innovation under three headings: new qualities in the teaching ecosystem, new domains opened by digital and intelligent technology, and new strategies for cooperation between school stages. Xu reviews official documents issued since 2019, including guidance on teacher development and on building integration communities.

Xu identifies obstacles that persist despite the progress. Teachers tend to stay within their own stage, there is too little drive for communication between stages, and knowledge is sometimes repeated without deepening students' values. Costs and benefits of developing resources are also hard to share across institutions. The author warns against superficial or patchwork integration. They propose mutual supervision and feedback between stages, and argue that students' thinking does not develop linearly, so links between stages must be dynamic. On technology, Xu raises questions about data connectivity, digital twins and human–machine relations. Xu also argues that cooperation lacks a leading body and a cross-boundary governance mechanism, and calls for both so that stage boundaries become overlapping zones of shared knowledge.

Xu concludes that integration is fundamentally a collective undertaking that needs coordination, a lead organisation and cross-domain governance. It must also adapt to the digital and intelligent age. The article mostly poses questions and sets directions rather than reporting empirical results. Read the original if you study how Chinese educational policy conceives the coordination of ideological and political education across school stages, or want to see how the field is taking up digital technology.
quoteEn: Fundamentally, the integrated development of ideological and political courses across primary, secondary and tertiary schools is a collective action, so in practical work the emphasis lies on strengthening coordination.
quoteZh: 大中小学思政课一体化建设从根本上来说，是一项集体行动，因此，就实际工作推进而言，重在加强协同。

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses on Marxist theory, Party doctrine, morality and law taught at every school stage in China. They are central to the Party's aim of fostering moral character and political commitment in students.

glossary.zh: 大中小学思政课一体化建设
glossary.pinyin: dà zhōng xiǎo xué sīzhèngkè yītǐhuà jiànshè
glossary.en: integrated development of ideological and political courses
glossary.literal: integrated construction of university, secondary and primary school ideological-political courses
glossary.explanation: A policy push, stressed by Xi Jinping in 2019, to link the content, teaching and teacher training of these courses across school stages in a progressive, spiral sequence rather than treating each stage separately.

t: Building a spiral-ascending curriculum for teaching a sense of community of the Chinese nation across primary, secondary and university ideological and political courses
zh: 大中小学思政课中华民族共同体意识教学内容的螺旋上升式构建研究
source: School Party Building and Ideological Education (Xuexiao dangjian yu sixiang jiaoyu)
paras: Li Chunhui asks how teaching on the sense of community of the Chinese nation (Zhonghua minzu gongtongti yishi) should be organised across primary school, secondary school and university ideological and political courses. The article argues that content should be built in a "spiral-ascending" way, deepening stage by stage to match students' cognitive development. Li presents this as important for strengthening students' "five identifications" and for advancing the building of the Chinese national community.

The article has four parts. It first defines the concept and its scope, dividing it into political, economic, cultural and shared-destiny dimensions, drawing on Fei Xiaotong's "pluralism within unity" formula and on Xi Jinping's statements. It then sets out why a spiral structure matters, proposes three guiding principles, and finally gives concrete teaching paths for each of the four dimensions at primary, secondary and university level.

Li's core argument rests on three claims about significance: the spiral design moves from shallow to deep as students' cognition and values develop; it fills out the integrated construction of ideological and political courses from simple to complex; and students, as carriers of the idea, spread it from "points" to a wider "surface" of society. The three principles are to combine a top-level goal with stage goals, completeness with continuity, and gradual progression with continuity across stages. Concretely, primary teaching is activity-based (films, museum visits, ethnic food and costume exchanges, group projects); secondary teaching is theory- and case-based (national security cases, poverty alleviation, large-scale West-to-East resource projects, the Covid-19 response); university teaching is systematic and classics-based, using Marx and the Party's history. Li also proposes discussions that rebut Western criticism of China's ethnic affairs.

Li concludes that coordinated, step-by-step content design, with teachers drawing on Xi Jinping's thinking on ethnic work and enriching resources at each stage, is the route to embedding the sense of community in students. This is framed as serving the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want detailed examples of how Chinese educators propose to translate the official concept of forging a sense of community of the Chinese nation into stage-specific classroom content.
quoteEn: The spiral-ascending construction of teaching content on the sense of community of the Chinese nation in ideological and political courses from primary school to university is an important way of continuously shaping students' worldview, outlook on life and values.
quoteZh: 大中小学思政课中华民族共同体意识教学内容的螺旋上升式构建，是不断塑造小中大学生世界观、人生观、价值观的重要途径。

glossary.en: sense of community of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: consciousness of the Chinese nation as a community
glossary.explanation: An official concept since the 2010s, made the "main thread" of Party ethnic work under Xi Jinping. It stresses that all 56 ethnic groups belong to one national community; critics outside China see it as emphasising assimilation.
Compulsory courses in Chinese schools and universities that teach Marxism, Party history and official values. They are treated as the main channel of moral and political education.
The official requirement that all ethnic groups identify with the great motherland, the Chinese nation, Chinese culture, the Communist Party of China and socialism with Chinese characteristics.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal, closely tied to the Chinese Dream, of restoring China's national strength and international standing by mid-century.

keywords: sense of community of the Chinese nation

t: Three paths for building an autonomous knowledge system in the discipline of ideological and political education
zh: 思想政治教育学科自主知识体系建构的三重进路
source: Ideological and Theoretical Education Research (思想教育研究), 2024 no. 3
paras: Zhang Yixiang takes up a question for the discipline of ideological and political education, which the article says has developed for forty years into one of the most dynamic fields within the first-level discipline of Marxist theory. The question is how it should build its own autonomous knowledge system and pursue high-quality development in the new era. Zhang argues that this requires attention at three levels: scholarly self-awareness, the deepening of the discipline's internal content, and innovation through coordination. The article was published in 2024 in Ideological and Theoretical Education Research and opens with Xi Jinping's call to build philosophy and social sciences with Chinese characteristics.

The article has three main sections, each divided into three sub-points. The first concerns scholars' initiative and confidence, and distinguishes three levels of autonomy in the discipline's knowledge. The second works through the discipline's content along the dimensions of breadth, depth and boundary. The third turns to innovation: guidance by Marxism, grounding in Chinese modernization, and coordination of resources. Zhang draws on the three-part framing of discipline system, academic system and discourse system throughout.

Zhang holds that the discipline has not fully left its early 'apprentice' state of borrowing from pedagogy, ethics, management, psychology and political science. Some scholars, the author says, lack confidence and drift to other fields. Knowledge is classed as fully autonomous (core theory such as the nature, structure and laws of the field), predominantly autonomous (cross-disciplinary areas such as the psychology or management of ideological and political education) and jointly studied (such as Xi Jinping's thought on culture or social trends). Zhang sees meta-theory as lagging, the branch subjects as underdeveloped, and the discourse system as the weakest link, with little international influence. Contested points such as whether the process has a single or dual subject also need settling. The author proposes new fields, including work with new economic organisations, new social organisations and new employment groups, and judges that research on these is almost absent.

On innovation, Zhang calls for Marxism as the guide, with nourishment from the classics, the latest results of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, fine traditional Chinese culture, and critically absorbed foreign scholarship. The discipline should also study Chinese modernization, including its content, value and implementation paths. Zhang further urges coordination among academic resources (including artificial intelligence and engineering fields), researchers and practitioners, publishing platforms and policy support. Read the original if you want a view from within the discipline of its perceived weaknesses and agenda for building an autonomous knowledge system in ideological and political education.
quoteEn: The branch subjects of ideological and political education are an important component of the discipline system and a necessary supplement to the core knowledge of the main subjects, and they should continue to be explored and developed in depth.
quoteZh: 思想政治教育学科的分支科目是学科体系建设的重要构成，是主干科目核心知识内容的必要补充，应继续深入挖掘和建设。

glossary.explanation: The Chinese term for education aimed at forming political views, values and moral outlook in line with Party doctrine. It is both a practical field of work in schools and organisations and an academic discipline.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义理论一级学科
glossary.explanation: A top-level discipline category in China's university system, established in 2005. It contains second-level disciplines such as ideological and political education and the basic principles of Marxism.

glossary.zh: 学科体系、学术体系、话语体系
glossary.pinyin: xuékē tǐxì, xuéshù tǐxì, huàyǔ tǐxì
glossary.en: discipline system, academic system and discourse system
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's formula for the three parts of philosophy and social sciences with Chinese characteristics. The article calls them the 'three major systems'.
A body of concepts and theory developed on a country's or discipline's own basis rather than borrowed from outside. The idea is prominent in recent Chinese calls for self-reliant scholarship.
The official description of China's path of modernization, set out by the Party since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for the continuing process of fitting Marxism to China's conditions and to the present era.

t: Main achievements, key lessons and innovation directions in building university ideological and political theory courses in the new era
zh: 新时代高校思政课建设的主要成就、重要经验和创新向度
source: Journal of Ideological and Theoretical Education (思想理论教育导刊), 2024 no. 3
paras: Yang Xiaohui takes stock of how university ideological and political theory courses (sizheng ke) have developed since the 18th Party Congress (2012), and especially in the five years after the 2019 symposium for teachers of these courses. The article argues that guidance from Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era has produced a fundamental shift in the field. In Yang's account, this shift has delivered historic achievements, transferable lessons and clear directions for further innovation.

The article has three parts. The first lists five achievements: the courses' higher strategic standing, more developed guiding concepts, the progress of Party theory 'entering textbooks, classrooms and minds', a larger and better teaching force, and stronger safeguard mechanisms. The second distils six lessons from this record. The third sets out five directions for innovation, drawing on official figures such as growth in teacher numbers and degree-granting programmes, and on a 2017 national survey of student satisfaction.

Yang's argument rests on a few moves. The achievements are tied to concepts such as integrated course-building across primary school to university, the 'big ideological and political course', and the new Introduction to Xi Jinping Thought course and textbook. The lessons stress strengthening Party leadership, putting students at the centre, combining top-level planning with grassroots experiment, and balancing preserving fundamentals with innovation. Yang also pairs problem-orientation with goal-orientation and joins the 'big course' concept to mechanisms for cooperation. For the future, Yang calls for systematic study of Xi's statements on these courses, stronger conviction and creativity among teachers, and support from Marxism schools and the Marxist theory discipline. Yang also calls for clearer duties for Party and Communist Youth League organisations and for better coordination among university departments, which Yang says still sometimes work at cross purposes.

Yang concludes that building these courses should be treated as a systematic project under Party leadership, one that adapts to changing circumstances while keeping the courses' political nature. The article is written from within the official education system and relies on policy documents and official statistics rather than independent evaluation. Read the original if you want a detailed, officially aligned account of how Chinese higher-education authorities describe their achievements and priorities in ideological and political course reform.
quoteEn: Building university ideological and political theory courses is a complex systems project that requires joint effort from top to bottom.
quoteZh: 高校思政课建设是复杂的系统工程，需要上下形成合力。

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses on Marxism, Party theory and moral and political education taught at Chinese universities and schools. They are commonly abbreviated as sizheng ke.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The official ideological framework associated with Xi Jinping, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018. It is now the core content of Party theory education.
A concept promoted from 2021 that extends ideological education beyond the classroom into society, drawing on schools, families and social resources.
University units responsible for teaching ideological and political theory courses and for research in Marxist theory. Official policy since 2015 has stressed strengthening them.

t: The content of building an autonomous knowledge system for the discipline of ideological and political education
zh: 思想政治教育学科自主知识体系的建构内容
source: Research on Ideological Education (思想教育研究), 2024 no. 3
paras: After four decades of disciplinary development, ideological and political education has built a knowledge system centred on its principles and methods. Zhong Qidong asks what knowledge supports an autonomous version of that system, in what sense it is autonomous, and how knowledge about ideological and political education relates to the knowledge used to carry it out. The author argues that the two are closely interlinked and that the autonomous system must integrate both.

The article has three parts. The first sets out a historical-materialist basis, asking whether ideology is itself knowledge. The second examines the Chinese context for building autonomous knowledge through four relationships. The third lays out the content of the system, divided into constitutive knowledge (what ideological and political education is) and functional knowledge (how it operates). Zhong draws on Marx, Engels, Lenin, Xi Jinping and existing work by Chinese scholars in the field.

Zhong reads Marx and Engels as rejecting ideology as false consciousness while not denying that ideology is knowledge. Ideology generalises, so it counts as knowledge, but only a Marxism grounded in real individuals' material life is, in the author's reading, "genuine knowledge" and a "scientific ideology". On this basis the author describes a concentric knowledge spectrum around the discipline's own knowledge. Autonomous knowledge, in Zhong's definition, is new knowledge generated by applying existing knowledge, not self-certified knowledge. It requires handling four relationships: with Western knowledge, with traditional moral cultivation, with Chinese practice and experience, and with other disciplines. Constitutive knowledge is built from concepts (with ideology as the base concept), categories ("thought and reality"), propositions and ideas. Functional knowledge comprises laws (ideological laws), methods (with materialist dialectics as the master method) and a supporting body of substantive knowledge borrowed from other disciplines.

Zhong concludes that the main tasks are to reflect on and go beyond Western knowledge, inherit and sublate traditional moral education, interpret Chinese practice for the world, and clarify disciplinary boundaries. Autonomy is only relative, and knowledge borrowed from other fields should be recast as the discipline's own concepts and principles through creative transformation. The author also asks scholars to build a conceptual system around Xi Jinping's description of the Second Integration as a further liberation of thought. Read the original if you study the theoretical foundations of ideological and political education as a discipline, or how Chinese scholars link Marxist ideology theory to disciplinary autonomy.
quoteEn: Autonomous knowledge is the presence of the subject in the reproduction of knowledge, and the confirmation of that subject's right to it.
quoteZh: 自主知识是知识再生产的主体在场与确权。
