glossary.explanation: A field of Party-led education and a Chinese academic discipline, taught in schools and universities and used in wider public work. It aims to shape people's political outlook, values and ideology.
In this article, the core category of ideological and political education. Zhong treats it as a form of knowledge and a state-linked force, following Marx and Engels.

t: The logic of constructing an autonomous knowledge system for the discipline of ideological and political education
zh: 思想政治教育学科自主知识体系的建构逻辑
source: Research on Ideological Education (Sixiang jiaoyu yanjiu), 2024 no. 3
paras: Taking its cue from Xi Jinping's call to build an autonomous Chinese knowledge system in philosophy and the social sciences, this article asks how the discipline of ideological and political education should construct its own autonomous knowledge system. Li Hui argues that the task answers four questions: for whom and by whom the system is built, what it contains, and how it is built. In Li's account these correspond to five constructive logics, and Li holds that the effort has a dual effect: the discipline is to serve as a model for others, and the work marks a new stage in its own development.

The article is organised in five sections, each devoted to one logic: the logic of subjectivity, grounded in Communist Party leadership; the logic of guidance, grounded in Marxism; goal orientation centred on fostering virtue and cultivating talent; the holistic logic of systems thinking; and the logic of knowledge production through critical inheritance. Li draws mainly on Xi Jinping's speeches on philosophy and the social sciences and on Party documents, and refers to debates within the discipline.

On subjectivity, Li separates the "value subject" from the "building subject" and resolves a long-running dispute over whether the discipline serves scholars or the Party. Li concludes that it serves the Party and the people, and that its builders form a layered system of leadership, administrative and academic actors, with the Party holding leadership, management and discursive power. On guidance, Li holds that adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times is itself the process by which an autonomous knowledge system emerges. On goals, Li rejects value-neutrality and value-clarification positions, arguing that the discipline is both knowledge education and value education. Under systems thinking, Li treats the whole person, integrated education, socialist ideology and social development as the bases for constructing the system. Under critical inheritance, Li calls for drawing on Marxism, Party experience, traditional culture and foreign scholarship while criticising Western ideology.

Li concludes that the five logics support one another. Subjectivity and guidance secure autonomy, goal orientation makes them concrete in the educational process, holistic construction secures systematicity, and knowledge production secures scholarly rigour. Neglecting any one, Li warns, would damage the whole project. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese scholar of ideological and political education justifies Party leadership and Marxist guidance as the basis of disciplinary knowledge construction.
quoteEn: By upholding the logic of subjectivity and the logic of guidance, one upholds the autonomy of the knowledge system of the discipline of ideological and political education.
quoteZh: 坚持了主体性逻辑和主导性逻辑，就坚持了思想政治教育学科知识体系的自主性。

glossary.explanation: The Party-led work of shaping students' and citizens' worldview, values and political stance. It is also a university discipline under Marxist theory, taught at schools of Marxism.
A slogan stressing that Chinese philosophy and social sciences should build their own concepts and theories rather than rely on Western frameworks. It has been emphasised by Xi Jinping.
Officially defined as the fundamental mission of education, stressed since the 18th Party Congress (2012). It means moral and political formation alongside knowledge.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official name for the Party's project of developing Marxism in line with Chinese conditions and contemporary needs.

t: Reflections on how artificial intelligence can empower the precision development of ideological and political education in universities
zh: 人工智能赋能高校思想政治教育精准化发展的思考
source: School Party Building and Ideological Education (学校党建与思想教育)
paras: Tang Pingqiu and Liu Tingting take up a practical problem in Chinese higher education: how artificial intelligence (AI) can help make university ideological and political education more "precise". They start from the 2019 national education work conference, which called for "precision ideological and political education" to address weak targeting, poor fit between content and student needs, and low accuracy. The authors argue that AI has inherent strengths in precision, coordination and adaptation, so it can empower this approach and shape students' thinking gradually and unobtrusively. The condition they set is that it be steered by values and run by people.

The article has two parts. The first sets out three advantages of AI for precision education: timeliness, "intelligence" or wisdom, and targeted delivery. The second proposes three strategies: value guidance to set direction, human–machine collaboration, and platform construction. The authors give a short account of AI's technical layers (foundation, technology and application) and draw on technologies such as GPUs, face recognition, natural language processing, adaptive learning systems and virtual reality.

On the advantages, Tang and Liu argue that AI processes large volumes of student data quickly, frees teachers from routine tasks and builds cross-media "precise portraits" of students. Because its algorithms can optimise themselves, they say, AI can detect students' emotions and attention, mine patterns in unstructured data, and filter out "noise" from the infiltration of Western values. Unlike the earlier big-data stage, which stayed at the level of mass lectures and meetings, AI can adapt content to individuals and build immersive teaching scenes. On strategy, the authors insist that value rationality must direct instrumental rationality, and that shared values must anchor individualised education so that it does not simply cater to students' preferences. They hold that AI remains "weak AI", so teachers must lead, guard privacy and ideological security, and add emotional care.

On platforms, the authors call for a big-data collection platform with graded confidentiality and school–enterprise cooperation, a smart teaching platform with VR learning scenes and a knowledge graph of ideological and political education resources, and a management and service platform kept up to date by technical staff. They conclude that AI should serve the fundamental task of fostering virtue and cultivating talent, guided by Marxism and Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. Read the original if you want to see how Chinese university Party and ideological-education researchers frame the use of AI and student data in political education.
quoteEn: AI is like a "propeller" and must take value guidance as its "steering wheel", so as to keep a precise hold on the direction of education.
quoteZh: 人工智能好比“推进器”，必须以价值引领作为“方向盘”，精准把握育人方向。

glossary.explanation: The system of Party-led moral, ideological and political instruction in Chinese schools and universities, covering courses and extracurricular work.
An approach that uses data and technology to tailor political education to individual students. It was called for at the 2019 national education work conference.
A stated fundamental task of Chinese education: to build moral character while training people. It is often cited in Party documents on education.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology associated with Xi Jinping, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.

t: The rich connotations, methodological implications and practical requirements of "the essence of ideological and political theory courses is reasoning"
zh: “思政课的本质是讲道理”的丰富内涵、方法论意蕴和实践要求
source: Marxist Theory Discipline Studies (马克思主义理论学科研究), 2024 no. 3
paras: Ai Silin examines Xi Jinping's 2022 statement at Renmin University of China that "the essence of ideological and political theory courses is reasoning" (讲道理). Ai asks why this was raised to the level of the courses' essence and what it requires of teachers. The article argues that the statement deepens understanding of how such courses should be taught, and that it points to higher effectiveness for university courses in the new era.

The article has four parts. It first traces Xi's remarks on these courses since the 18th Party Congress (2012), including the 2019 teachers' symposium. It then sets out the meaning of "reasoning", the methodological guidance of "making arguments profound, thorough and lively", and three practical requirements. Ai draws on Marx, Engels, Lenin and Mao Zedong, and closes with a note on the discipline of Marxist theory.

Ai gives three reasons for the emphasis: the courses' theoretical and scientific character, the logic by which their goal of fostering conviction is reached, and the need to address teaching that "cannot reason well". Examples are reading from the textbook, stating conclusions without argument, superficial treatment and one-sided treatment. The reasoning taught is not ordinary reasoning. It unites truth with ethics and feeling, political principle with academic grounding, and general principles with concrete cases. Ai reads the methodological formula as follows. "Profound" means asking why, teaching standpoint and method, and moving from phenomena to essence. "Thorough" means teaching holistically, through students' questions, by comparison, and by criticising wrong ideas while affirming correct ones. "Lively" means accessible language and varied methods, including integrating artificial intelligence. Ai treats the three as mutually supporting.

Ai draws three practical requirements. Teachers should put heart and effort into every class and manage the tensions between teaching and learning. They should raise their scholarly level, because the courses are themselves scholarship and a lack of academic substance produces "filler courses". Finally, the discipline of Marxist theory should provide stronger support, including through the new first-level discipline of CPC history and Party building, more research funding and platforms, and teaching that explains Chinese modernization and builds the Four-sphere Confidence. Read the original if you want an authoritative-line account of how Party theorists in higher education justify and operationalise "reasoning" in ideological and political courses.
quoteEn: Without theoretical clarity, it is hard to have political firmness.
quoteZh: 没有理论的清醒，就难有政治上的坚定。

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses in Marxism, Party theory and moral-political education taught at all levels of Chinese schools and universities.
The official term for China's path of modernization under Party leadership, prominent in Party discourse since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
Official slogan calling for confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics.

t: Upholding the Party Central Committee's centralised and unified leadership as the fundamental guarantee for advancing the Party's self-reform
zh: 以坚持党中央集中统一领导为根本保证深入推进党的自我革命
paras: Writing in Red Flag Manuscripts (2024, no. 5), Wang Libing takes up one element of Xi Jinping's thinking on the Party's self-reform: that the work must be carried forward with \"upholding the centralised and unified leadership of the Party Central Committee as the fundamental guarantee\". Wang argues that this leadership is the highest principle of the Party's self-reform, and that the Party must firmly uphold the Central Committee's authority and keep fully in line with the Central Committee with Xi Jinping at its core.

The article has three sections. The first sets out why centralised and unified leadership is the highest principle, in theoretical, historical and practical terms. The second reviews what Wang describes as historic and pioneering achievements of the Party's self-reform since the 18th Party Congress (2012). The third turns to what it means in practice to take this leadership as the fundamental guarantee.

Wang's theoretical case cites Marx, Engels and Lenin on centralism and authority, and then Mao Zedong, Deng Xiaoping and Xi Jinping. The historical case runs from the Zunyi Meeting to the present and concludes that when the Party stresses self-reform and upholds central leadership, its cause advances, and that the reverse brings setbacks. The achievements are grouped under several heads: leading by example from the top, with the Central Committee and senior cadres setting the standard; strengthening the Party's overall leadership; the claimed decisive victory in the anti-corruption struggle; a more mature supervision system and body of Party regulations; and the Two Establishes, which Wang calls the most important political result.

For practice, Wang calls for three things. The Party should advance self-reform unwaveringly under central leadership, turning the Two Establishes into the Two Upholds. It should implement the Central Committee's decisions on self-reform to the letter. It should also use self-reform itself to defend central authority, by struggling against words and deeds that weaken Party leadership, tackling the \"seven haves\" problems, tightening political discipline and improving the institutional system of full and rigorous self-governance of the Party. Read the original if you want a compact statement of how the official line ties Party discipline, anti-corruption and institutional reform to central authority.
quoteEn: Whether in theoretical logic, historical logic or practical logic, upholding the centralised and unified leadership of the Party Central Committee is the highest principle that the Party's self-reform must adhere to.
quoteZh: 无论是在理论逻辑、历史逻辑，还是实践逻辑上，坚持党中央集中统一领导都是党的自我革命必须坚持的最高原则。

glossary.explanation: A term prominent under Xi Jinping for the Communist Party's continuing effort to discipline, purify and renew itself. It is presented as the Party's answer to how it can avoid decline while in power.
A formula from the 2021 Party history resolution and the 20th Party Congress. It affirms Xi Jinping's core status in the Central Committee and the Party, and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought.
The requirement to uphold Xi Jinping's core position in the Central Committee and the Party, and to uphold the Central Committee's authority and centralised, unified leadership.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: The official name for the campaign since 2012 to tighten Party discipline, conduct and anti-corruption work. It is one of the "Four Comprehensives".
A list Xi Jinping used in 2015 of seven political problems among officials. They include opposing the Central Committee's policies and engaging in cliques and factions.

keywords: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party

t: Carrying forward the Marxist style of study that links theory with practice
zh: 发扬理论联系实际的马克思主义学风
paras: Jiang Zexun takes up Xi Jinping's call, in his preface to the sixth batch of national cadre training textbooks, for officials to carry forward the Marxist style of study that links theory with practice and to act as resolute doers in building Chinese modernization. The article, published in Qiushi's Red Flag Manuscript (Hongqi Wengao) in 2024, argues that this style of study is a major political question bearing on the fortunes of the Party's cause. In Jiang's view, whether theory is tied to practice decides the quality of Party conduct and the success of national rejuvenation.

The piece has three parts. The first sets out why the style matters: it is a defining trait of Marxist theory, a requirement for adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, a practical necessity for Chinese modernization, and a continuation of the traditional Chinese unity of knowing and doing. The second says what cadres should link theory to: their own thinking, their work, and historical and cultural conditions. The third lists methods for doing so.

Jiang draws on Marx, Engels and Mao Zedong, and above all on Xi Jinping's statements, to argue that Marxism is a method and a guide to action rather than dogma. On the work side, cadres are told to tie study to Chinese modernization, high-quality development, the pressing concerns of the people, problems in Party building, and the domestic and international situation. The methods are mastering the theory, problem orientation, field investigation that avoids showy or superficial visits, the mass line (including online), a practical, results-oriented work style, and theoretical innovation drawn from practice. Jiang also invokes the traditional idea of the unity of knowing and doing as a cultural root of the approach.

Jiang concludes that the effectiveness of theory depends on how far it meets real needs and how deeply it enters practice. Cadres are urged to study Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era thoroughly, to curb formalism and bureaucratism, and to produce results that withstand scrutiny by history and the people. Jiang adds that practice must keep generating new concepts, so that the theoretical framework of Chinese modernization continues to develop. Read the original if you want a concise statement of the official Party-school line on study style and cadre work methods, with the key Xi Jinping formulations gathered in one place.
quoteEn: Upholding the link between theory and practice ultimately requires cadres at all levels to firmly establish a correct view of performance and to promote a spirit and style of seeking truth and getting things done.
quoteZh: 坚持理论联系实际，归根到底是要求各级干部牢固树立正确的政绩观，大力弘扬求真务实、真抓实干的精神和作风，务实功、出实招、求实效，以钉钉子精神，一件事情接着一件事情干

glossary.explanation: The Party's official formulation of China's own path to modernization, elaborated especially since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as the central task of national rejuvenation.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for fitting Marxist theory to China's conditions and to the present era. It is treated as an ongoing process of theoretical innovation.
The official goal of growth that stresses quality, innovation and efficiency over scale. Since the late 2010s it has been described as the first task of building a modern socialist country.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018. Cadres are required to study it systematically.
A Party working method from the Mao era, holding that leaders should gather views from the people and return them as policy. The article extends it to online spaces.

t: Scientific guidance for advancing theoretical innovation
zh: 推进理论创新的科学指引
paras: Writing in Red Flag Manuscripts (2024, no. 4), Liu Tongfang asks how the Communist Party of China should understand and carry out theoretical innovation. Liu argues that, since the 18th Party Congress (2012), Xi Jinping's remarks on the subject have raised the Party's grasp of the laws governing theoretical innovation to a new level. In Liu's reading, these remarks set out its basic principles and significance and its scientific method, and so give guidance for adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times.

The article is a commentary in four parts. Each part takes one pair of concepts from Xi's statements: the "soul" and "root" of theory; the times as "mother of thought" and practice as "source of theory"; the people as the subject of innovation and the value it serves; and the systematization and scholarly grounding of theory. It draws mainly on Xi's formulations and on the Party's experience of more than a century.

Liu's first claim is that Marxism is the "soul" and fine traditional Chinese culture the "root" of innovation, and that the two interpenetrate. Marxism gives scientific, people-centred, practical and open principles; traditional culture gives continuity and the Chinese character of theory. Liu treats the Two Integrations as both a method and a result of innovation. Second, Liu holds that the times and practice generate theory. Liu cites the world's "changes unseen in a century", Chinese modernization and a community with a shared future for mankind as practices that theorists must answer and guide. Third, Liu names the people as the subject of innovation and their aspiration for a better life as its value, aimed at common prosperity and human emancipation. Systematization links the different parts of theory, while scholarly grounding lifts it from perceptual experience to rational knowledge.

Liu concludes that continued innovation guided by these four sets of insights will open up new horizons for adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. It will also show the truth-power of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. The text is a Party-theory exposition rather than an empirical study. Read the original if you want a concise account of how current official discourse frames the logic, subject and method of theoretical innovation.
quoteEn: The people are the subject of theoretical innovation, and meeting the people's aspiration for a better life is the value to which it belongs.
quoteZh: 人民是理论创新的主体，满足人民对美好生活的向往是理论创新的价值归属。

glossary.explanation: Formula associated with Xi Jinping: combining the basic principles of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: Official phrase for the Party's ongoing effort to develop Marxism in line with Chinese conditions and the demands of each era.

glossary.pinyin: bǎi nián wèi yǒu zhī dà biànjú
glossary.literal: great changes not seen in a hundred years
glossary.explanation: Phrase used by Xi Jinping to describe a period of major global shifts in power, economy and order.
Official term for the Party's path of modernization, presented as distinct from Western models.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept for international relations and global governance, promoted since 2013.
Official goal of prosperity shared by all, linked to eliminating polarization between rich and poor.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.

t: Making good use of the "Great Ideological and Political Course": three narratives of connotation, value and practice
st: Characteristics, value orientation and practical path
zh: 善用“大思政课”三重叙事：内涵特征、价值旨归与实践理路
source: Marxist Theory Teaching and Research (马克思主义理论教学与研究), 2024 no. 1
paras: Since Xi Jinping told education-sector delegates in 2021 that the "Great Ideological and Political Course" (da sizheng ke) should be used well, scholars have debated what it means. Fu Hong and Cai Chen, writing in 2024, argue that the project has reached a "deep-water zone" in which unclear actors, weak results and even wrong direction have appeared. They hold that its basic questions must be clarified, and that the concept is best understood through three linked narratives: cognitive, value and practical.

The article first reviews existing scholarship on the concept's meaning, value and structure. It then sets out its own account in three parts: what "great" and "using well" mean and the course's basic features; the value of the approach for moral education and for fostering "new-era talents"; and the practical path for building it. Throughout, it draws on Xi Jinping's speeches on ideological and political courses and on the 2022 Ministry of Education work plan for promoting the course.

On connotation, the authors argue that the "great" course inherits the breadth already inherent in ideological and political courses, innovates on it, and builds a wider pattern of cooperation between school and society. They insist its emphasis remains on the "course", not on a loose "big ideology and politics", and that its test is effectiveness rather than size. "Using well" is read as using it truly, widely and flexibly, and as treating it as a system with holistic, structural, three-dimensional and dynamic features. Its characteristics are said to be problem orientation, practice orientation and cross-field coordination. On value, the authors present it as a way to carry out the fundamental task of fostering virtue and cultivating people, to resolve persistent difficulties in moral education, and to answer the questions of whom to train, how and for whom.

For practice, the authors call for three things. First, Party committees at all levels should give overall leadership by setting direction, planning and coordinating. Second, construction should rely on the ideological and political course itself, strengthening its theoretical depth, linking it to reality and using social resources, while course-embedded ideological education works alongside it. Third, three kinds of elements should be coordinated: people (educators, learners, outside participants), things (such as red resources and practice bases) and operational methods. Read the original if you study ideological and political education in Chinese universities and want a detailed, officially aligned account of how the "Great Ideological and Political Course" is conceptualised and what practical measures are proposed.
quoteEn: In the end, whether the "Great Ideological and Political Course" is well built depends not on its being "great" but on its effectiveness.
quoteZh: 说到底，“大思政课”建设得好不好，关键不在于“大”而在于“效”

glossary.explanation: A concept Xi Jinping put forward in 2021 for taking ideological and political theory teaching beyond the classroom into social life and practice. It is meant to link school classrooms with society and is distinct from a broader "big ideology and politics".
The compulsory Marxist theory and political education courses taught in Chinese schools and universities, commonly abbreviated as sizheng ke.
The stated fundamental task of Chinese education, giving priority to moral and political formation alongside knowledge and skills.
The practice of integrating ideological and political content into non-political subject courses so that all courses contribute to moral and political education.
A term used in Party documents, including the 20th Party Congress report, for the younger generation expected to carry the task of national rejuvenation.

t: Moral development of youth in the new era: current situation, problems and paths
zh: 新时代青年道德建设的现状、问题及路径分析
paras: Wang Jianmin asks how the moral development of young people aged 14 to 35 is faring in the new era and how it should be strengthened. Taking up the call of the 20th Party Congress (2022) to implement a citizen moral development project, Wang argues that the overall trend among youth is positive but that significant problems remain in how young people understand, feel, will and practise socialist morality. The author concludes that these problems can be addressed through seven coordinated paths.

The article first defines youth and socialist morality, which it describes as centred on serving the people, with collectivism as its principle and the core socialist values as its guide. It then assesses the current situation along four dimensions: moral cognition, moral emotion, moral will and moral conduct. A second section sets out problems in each dimension, and a third identifies causes and proposes paths. These paths are guidance by Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, Party leadership, family education, schools, the social environment, institutional mechanisms and young people's own moral cultivation.

On the situation, Wang cites patriotic sentiment, online expressions of national pride, acts of rescue and volunteering (over 90 million registered volunteers aged 14 to 35 by the end of 2021) as evidence of a healthy trend. On problems, Wang identifies shallow understanding of socialist morality, including belief that morality is useless or that it should wait for economic development. The author also points to uneven moral emotions, the downplaying of national history, uncritical admiration of Western moral culture, utilitarian motives, hesitation over helping others, online abuse, and indifference to wrongdoing. Wang attributes these to weak ideals and convictions, gaps in school and family education, negative social influences and limited self-cultivation.

For remedies, Wang calls for Party leadership over ideological work, stronger family education and family traditions, and school curricula on ideals, public and private morality and national security. Wang also proposes cleaner online spaces, community and red-culture education sites, combined rule-of-law and rule-of-virtue mechanisms, systems of reward and punishment, and several forms of oversight. The author ends by urging young people to be exemplary in public and private morality and to promote civic morality themselves. Read the original if you want to see how a Party-affiliated youth researcher frames youth moral problems and prescribes institutional and educational remedies in the language of ideological and political education.
quoteEn: Youth moral development is the top priority within the moral development of socialist citizens.
quoteZh: 青年道德建设是社会主义公民道德建设的重中之重

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018. It is presented as the latest stage in adapting Marxism to China.
A policy programme to raise public moral standards and civilised conduct, reaffirmed in the report to the 20th Party Congress in 2022.

glossary.pinyin: míng dàdé, shǒu gōngdé, yán sīdé
glossary.literal: understand great virtue, observe public virtue, be strict in private virtue
glossary.explanation: A formula from Xi Jinping asking citizens to grasp major virtue (loyalty to country and Party), observe public morality and keep strict private morality. The article uses it as the basic framework for youth moral education.
A set of twelve values promoted officially since the 18th Party Congress (2012), including prosperity, democracy, patriotism and integrity.

t: The distinctiveness of the development of the discipline of ideological and political education since reform and opening up
zh: 改革开放以来思想政治教育学科发展的特殊性
source: School Party Building and Ideological Education (学校党建与思想教育), 2024
paras: Why did the discipline of ideological and political education grow so quickly in the roughly forty years after reform and opening up? She Shuanghao and Lu Yuqiang answer that, among many lessons, the most fundamental cause is the discipline's distinctiveness. The article traces how the Chinese Communist Party moved ideological and political education from a social phenomenon to a practice, then to a science, and finally to an independent academic discipline with its own undergraduate programme.

The article is organised around five aspects of this distinctiveness: the discipline's Marxist, ideological nature; the practical base in the Party's own ideological and political work; the particular circumstances of its establishment; its position within the first-level discipline of Marxist theory; and its development model. It draws on Party and State Council documents from 2004–05, on the 1979–80 debate on making political work scientific, on textbook series from the 1980s and 1990s, and on statements by Deng Xiaoping, Hu Yaobang and Jiang Zemin.

The authors argue that, unlike the education that other ruling classes gave in their own interests, Marxist ideological and political education serves the fundamental interests of the proletariat and working people. In their account it works by reasoning, persuasion and consultation rather than coercion, and it rests on a century of Party practice that sometimes met difficulties when it borrowed from Soviet experience. They identify six factors behind the discipline's founding: objective need, the attention of the Party Central Committee, strong promotion by the education authorities, the efforts of theorists, academic societies and journals, and the results of talent training. Finally, they present the "programme first, discipline later" model as a source of strength. In their reading, it produced a textbook system, a conceptual vocabulary (notably the 1986 definition in Principles of Ideological and Political Education) and a body of specialist knowledge. They also describe the discipline as the point where all Marxist theory disciplines land in application, and say it helped bring about the first-level Marxist theory discipline.

The authors conclude that this distinctiveness explains past growth and should guide future development. They call on the discipline to clarify its nature, firm up its foundations, keep its distinctive features and original purpose, and follow its own laws of development. Read the original if you want a Chinese disciplinary insider's account of how ideological and political education became an academic field, including the documents, textbooks and institutions involved.
quoteEn: The discipline of ideological and political education has laws that are more complex and distinctive than those of the other disciplines within Marxist theory.
quoteZh: 思想政治教育学科比马克思主义理论中的其他学科具有更为复杂特殊的规律

glossary.explanation: The education, in schools and in society more broadly, through which the Party and state seek to shape people's political views, ideology and morality. It is also an academic discipline, set up in China in the 1980s.
The Party's long-standing practice of persuading, educating and mobilising people. It is described as a 'lifeline' of Party work and is the practical base from which the academic discipline emerged.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义理论一级学科
glossary.explanation: A top-level category in China's official academic classification, established in 2005. Ideological and political education is one of its second-level disciplines.

t: Clarifying the basic questions of ideological and political education in the curriculum
zh: 厘清课程思政的基本问题
source: Party Building and Ideological Education in Schools (学校党建与思想教育)
paras: Ideological and political education in the curriculum (kecheng sizheng) has become a buzzword in Chinese higher education, yet scholars disagree about what it is and how to strengthen it. Li Heliang argues that it is not a new discipline or a theoretical breakthrough but a logical return to the original purpose of education, which is to cultivate people morally as well as intellectually. The article was published in the journal Party Building and Ideological Education in Schools and posted on the Academy of Marxism site in 2024.

The article proceeds in six sections. It first places curriculum-based political education within the nature of education itself, then distinguishes it from dedicated ideological and political theory courses. It goes on to discuss how to draw out the ideological elements already inside each course, what the practice is for, what drives it forward, and how universities should plan it as a whole. Li draws on Vygotsky, Xi Jinping's remarks on education, and the Ministry of Education's May 2020 Guidelines for Ideological and Political Education in the Curriculum in Higher Education.

Li's central claim is that education is inseparable from society and from the free and all-round development of the person, so every course already carries a moral function. Long-standing instrumentalism has stressed knowledge and skills and let this moral element fade. Li distinguishes the dedicated theory courses, which are explicit and ideological, from curriculum-based education, which is mainly implicit and works through content and the teacher's conduct. The two are said to be in collaboration, not in a primary–supplementary relation. Li criticises teachers who bolt political content onto professional courses, or who create separate moral courses for students, arguing that such steps provoke resentment and weaken the effect. Poetry teaching is offered as an example of drawing out historical context and patriotic feeling.

Li concludes that the approach should not be applied uniformly: pure natural-science or highly technical courses need not carry it, and sometimes a few words from the teacher are enough. Universities should experiment, adapt to their own specialisms and students, and draw up common standards and even negative lists. Li calls for systematic coordination among Party committees, administrative departments, faculties, teachers and students, and for teachers to use methods from related disciplines. Read the original if you want a Chinese scholar's critique of mechanical practice in university ideological and political education and a view of how it should be managed.
quoteEn: Ideological and political education in the curriculum does not mean creating new courses; it means digging out and distilling, within all courses, the resources for ideological and political education that they already contain: convictions, moral norms, social responsibility, love of country and home, scientific literacy and humanistic spirit.
quoteZh: 课程思政不是新设课程，而是要在所有课程中深入挖掘、提炼课程本身所内含的信念追求、道德规范、社会责任、家国情怀、科学素养、人文精神等思想政治教育资源

glossary.en: ideological and political education in the curriculum
glossary.explanation: A policy approach, promoted since the mid-2010s, that asks teachers of all subjects to build moral and ideological education into their ordinary teaching, not only in dedicated political courses.
Compulsory courses in Marxist theory and Party ideology taught in Chinese schools and universities.

t: The internal structure, construction logic and advancement paths of an autonomous knowledge system for the discipline of ideological and political education
zh: 思想政治教育学科自主知识体系的内在结构、建构逻辑及推进路向
source: Journal of Ideological and Theoretical Education (思想理论教育导刊), 2024 no. 2
paras: Zheng Jingbin asks how the discipline of ideological and political education should build its own autonomous knowledge system, a task that Xi Jinping has placed at the centre of building a Chinese philosophy and social science. Citing Xi's 2016 and 2022 statements, Zheng argues that the knowledge system is the foundation of the "three systems" (discipline, academic and discourse systems), and that the discipline, as a basic part of the social sciences, must now construct one. The article was published in 2024 in a journal on ideological and theoretical education.

The article first gives four reasons the problem is pressing: the discipline's composite, multi-source character; its relatively recent founding (about forty years ago) and weak intensive growth; scholars' limited capacity for knowledge creation; and new practical questions that exceed existing explanations. It then reviews scholarly views on the system's components (two-, three- and four-element models), proposes its own structure, and surveys proposed features of an "autonomous" system, from which it selects four. It closes with five proposed routes for advancing construction.

Zheng divides the system into four blocks: theoretical knowledge (what is it), practical knowledge (what to do), methodological knowledge (how to do it) and institutional knowledge (what outcome to aim for), each an interdependent subsystem. From 28 keywords drawn from the literature, Zheng picks the four most frequent features as the logical thread of construction: localness in knowledge production, interconnectedness with other bodies of knowledge, systematicity of structure, and originality in application. Localness means drawing concepts from Chinese practice and traditional culture. Interconnection means integrating Marxist theory, technology, natural science and neighbouring social sciences. Originality means posing new propositions for Chinese problems and issues of wider human concern.

For advancement, Zheng calls for guidance by Marxist theory (the people's standpoint, Marxist worldview and method, and Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era). Further proposals are textbook-system reform with vertical coordination across school stages, a shift in research paradigms towards data-driven and interdisciplinary work, international dialogue that avoids mechanical borrowing from the West, and a problem-oriented approach. The aim is for knowledge to move from national to global significance and offer "Chinese wisdom" for a community with a shared future for mankind. Read the original if you want a detailed map of how scholars in this field conceptualise disciplinary knowledge-building under the current policy agenda.
quoteEn: The autonomous knowledge system of the ideological and political education discipline takes theoretical knowledge as its cornerstone, practical knowledge as its counterpart, methodological knowledge as its central axis, and institutional knowledge as its guide.
quoteZh: 思想政治教育学科自主知识体系以理论性知识为基石、以实践性知识为照应、以方法性知识为中轴、以制度性知识为引领

glossary.explanation: A Chinese academic discipline and educational practice concerned with cultivating political convictions, values and morality, notably in schools and universities and within Party work. It is taught within Marxist theory programmes.

Xi Jinping's formulation for a body of knowledge built on Chinese conditions, traditions and discourse rather than borrowed Western frameworks. It is presented as the core of building a Chinese philosophy and social science.

glossary.pinyin: xuékē tǐxì, xuéshù tǐxì, huàyǔ tǐxì
glossary.literal: discipline system, academic system, discourse system
glossary.explanation: The three components of a Chinese philosophy and social science that Xi Jinping called for at the 2016 symposium on philosophy and social sciences.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想

glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology since 2017, written into the Party and state constitutions.
