glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept for China's vision of international relations and global governance, promoted since 2012–13.

t: Digital ideological and political education and the reshaping of teachers' competence structure in ideological and political theory courses
zh: 数字思政与思政课教师能力结构再塑
source: School Party Building and Ideological Education, 2024
paras: Jiang Hong and Zhou Hongjiang ask how ideological and political theory courses ("sizheng ke") in Chinese universities can undergo digital transformation, and answer that the decisive factor is teachers. The article argues that "digital ideological and political education" is an important direction for such courses in the new era, and that its construction depends on reshaping teachers' competence structure around digital literacy.

The article opens from the call of the 20th Party Congress (2022) to advance the digitalisation of education, then proceeds in three steps. It first explains why digital ideological and political education matters, then argues that teachers are its key element, drawing on Xi Jinping's 2019 symposium on these courses (the "3·18" symposium). Finally it sets out four areas in which teachers' capacities should be rebuilt, before a short conclusion.

On the first point, the authors say that students' "networked existence" and the technological shifts of the age require the courses to adapt. They also warn against the "pan-entertainment" that excessive use of technology could bring to the classroom. For teachers, they stress personal charisma and professional ethics, based on Xi's "Six Requirements" and "four-have" good teacher standards. They also stress analysing students' interests and arming oneself with the Party's innovative theory. The four areas of capacity are improving network use (platform skills, training, shared digital resource banks); adopting a human–machine collaborative teaching philosophy; exploring digital teaching methods; and conducting immersive teaching with VR, AR and MR. In the authors' account, collaboration shifts communication from "person–person" to "person–machine–person", and teachers become guides and designers of resources, while technology lacks human value rationality and warmth. They link digital methods to Xi's "Eight Unities", for example combining explicit and implicit education through virtual scenes of revolutionary history.

The authors conclude that digital transformation must first settle whether teachers' competence structure is adequate, with digital literacy at its core. They add that digital ideological and political education is not merely a technical means but must carry educational ideals and values. Teachers should therefore keep to the Eight Unities, strengthen political conviction and cultural confidence, and act as guides to students' growth. Read the original if you want a representative example of how Chinese scholars in ideological and political education link digital technology, teacher training and Party guidance for classroom practice.
quoteEn: Digital ideological and political education is not merely a technical means; it should also be endowed with rich educational ideas and value connotations.
quoteZh: 数字思政不仅是一种技术手段，而且应当被赋予丰富的教育理念与价值内涵。

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses in Marxism, Party theory and moral education taught at Chinese schools and universities. The Party treats them as a key vehicle for value formation.
The use of big data, AI, VR and other digital technologies in ideological and political education. It is presented as a new research and reform theme following the 20th Party Congress.
Xi Jinping's 2019 requirements for ideological and political teachers: strong politics, deep feelings, innovative thinking, broad vision, strict self-discipline and upright character.
Eight principles for teaching ideological and political courses set out by Xi Jinping in 2019, such as unifying political stance with academic rigour and explicit with implicit education.

t: Integrating Party history study and education into university ideological and political theory courses
zh: 把党史学习教育融入高校思政课教学
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily, Gai Yixin, dean and professor at a school of Marxism, takes up the question of how Party history study and education can be built into university ideological and political theory courses. The commentary is prompted by the Regulations on Party History Study and Education issued by the CPC Central Committee in February 2024. Gai argues that Party history is the most vivid and persuasive textbook for these courses and that using it is necessary if they are to reach students' hearts, stimulate thinking and inspire commitment.

The piece is organised under three headings, each opening with a call from Xi Jinping: to form a broad view of history and of the times, to unite theory with practice, and to explain principles in depth, thoroughly and vividly. Gai sketches how the Party has used history-related courses since the new-democratic revolution, at Shaanbei Public School and North China United University, and after 1949. The commentary then gives teaching suggestions under each heading.

Gai's first move is that a broad historical outlook links the present-day classroom to Party history. It does so by showing students the Party's achievements and the significance of its century of struggle. The author adds that digital tools such as VR and AR can make red historical resources more engaging. Second, Gai calls for combining the "small classroom" of the course with the "big classroom" of society. This means building a "big ideological and political course" through reading, discussion, visits to red sites and fieldwork, so that students see the Party's material, institutional and spiritual strength and link personal goals to national rejuvenation. Third, Gai proposes three ways to "explain principles": telling small stories about ordinary people and local changes, breaking big principles into smaller ones close to student life, and learning through practice. One concrete proposal is to award course credit for students' vacation activities at home, such as volunteering at red exhibition halls, so that they move from passive listening to active explaining.

Gai concludes that Party history teaching should help students understand why the Party and socialism with Chinese characteristics have succeeded. It should also lead them to tie individual aims to national needs and to the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. The commentary is a practical, officially aligned account of teaching method, not a scholarly study. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party history education is being presented to university teachers of ideological and political courses after the 2024 Regulations.
quoteEn: To integrate Party history study and education into university ideological and political courses, the "two classrooms" must be linked and a "big ideological and political course" built.
quoteZh: 将党史学习教育融入高校思政课，就要融通“两个课堂”，构建“大思政课”。

glossary.explanation: A Party-wide campaign, launched in 2021 and made routine by the February 2024 Regulations, to study the history of the Communist Party of China. It aims to build political conviction and loyalty.
Compulsory courses on Marxism, Party history and Party theory taught in Chinese schools and universities. They are meant to shape students' political outlook.
A concept promoted under Xi Jinping that extends ideological and political education beyond the classroom into society and practice.

keywords: Regulations on Party History Study and Education

t: Advancing digital ideological and political education and strengthening online education capacity
zh: 推进数字思政建设 提高网络育人能力
paras: Sun Chuhang and Luo Liang, in a commentary first published in Guangming Daily on 12 October 2023, take up Xi Jinping's call to improve online education capacity and to carry out ideological work in schools well in the internet age. They argue that cyberspace has become the "first environment" of young students. In their view, "digital ideological and political education" (digital sizheng) is a paradigm shift for the field, not a simple addition to traditional teaching or a mere refinement of method.

The piece is built around four elements: the value of digital ideological and political education, its goals, its content, and the practical work needed to build it. It closes with a short note on top-level design and teacher capacity.

On value, the authors say the field should replace "inculcation" with interactive methods that draw out individual potential. It should also strengthen mainstream ideology in digital space and build a "firewall" against online infiltration. On goals, they name three: using value guidance to overcome technological alienation and addiction, easing the isolation and "information cocoons" of digital life, and using moral norms to reduce risks such as data leaks and algorithmic discrimination. On content, they stress digital thinking, digital ethics and digital skills. Practical measures include new methods such as virtual reality and immersive teaching, ideological and political data centres, algorithm governance across the student life cycle, and integrated monitoring and service platforms.

The authors conclude that progress requires stronger top-level design, innovation in concepts, content and methods, higher digital literacy among teachers, and a sustainable disciplinary theory and long-term working mechanism. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned account of how Chinese educators propose to use big data, algorithms and platforms in ideological and political education.
quoteEn: It is not a simple addition to traditional ideological and political education, nor merely a methodological improvement, but a transformation and upgrading of the inner workings of modern ideological and political education to suit digital time and space.
quoteZh: 它不是传统思政的简单增补，也不是单纯的方法改进，而是现代思想政治教育内在运行适应数字时空境遇的转型升级。

glossary.explanation: A term for ideological and political education adapted to digital technologies and online space. It extends the established practice of Party-led moral and political instruction in Chinese schools and universities.
The system of political, ideological and moral instruction in Chinese schools and universities, including dedicated courses. It aims to instil Party-endorsed values and worldviews.
The use of internet platforms and online space to shape students' values and character, as a complement to classroom teaching.

t: Understanding propaganda, ideological and cultural work as an extremely important task
zh: 深刻认识宣传思想文化工作是一项极端重要的工作
paras: This commentary, written by a vice president of the Central Party School, expounds Xi Jinping's directive on propaganda, ideological and cultural work. Xi called it "extremely important" work that bears on the Party's future and destiny, on the country's long-term stability and on the cohesion and centripetal force of the nation. Li Yi argues that these "three bearings" deepen the Party's understanding of the work's strategic and overall significance and show the way to shoulder the "new cultural mission".

The article is organised in three sections, one for each "bearing". The first traces the Party's treatment of propaganda work from the Communist League's 1847 rules and Lenin's writings through the Party's founding in 1921, the revolutionary, socialist-construction and reform-era periods, to the period since the 18th Party Congress (2012). The second turns to cultural security and ideological struggle, and the third to culture as the basis of national cohesion and to Xi Jinping Thought on culture.

Li's central argument is that in every historical period this work has supplied ideological guarantees for the Party's tasks, and has therefore been the Party's "lifeline". On national security, Li contends that Western hostile forces export "cultural hegemony" and promote liberalism, historical nihilism and "universal values" in order to push the Party to change its banner. The Soviet collapse and "colour revolutions" are cited as showing that socialism can be undone in the ideological sphere when it cannot be defeated by arms or economic pressure. Li holds that the Party can make no compromise there and must act from the standpoint of survival. On cohesion, Li presents the continuity and unity of Chinese civilisation as the source of national strength, and says the "second integration" of Marxism with fine traditional culture consolidates Chinese cultural subjectivity.

Li concludes that Xi Jinping's new ideas on culture are a theoretical summing-up of practice, form the cultural part of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, and constitute "Xi Jinping Thought on culture". Li calls for studying and applying them, strengthening the Party's overall leadership of this work, building a socialist ideology with strong cohesion, fostering core socialist values, improving news communication and international communication, and promoting Chinese traditional culture. Read the original if you want a representative statement of how a senior Party School official frames ideological work, cultural security and the "new cultural mission" at the end of 2023.
quoteEn: The collapse of a regime often begins in the realm of ideas; political turmoil and regime change may happen overnight, but the evolution of thought is a long process.
quoteZh: 一个政权的瓦解往往是从思想领域开始的，政治动荡、政权更迭可能在一夜之间发生，但思想演化是个长期过程。

glossary.explanation: The Party's term for its work on propaganda, ideology, media and culture, handled by the Propaganda Department. In Chinese usage "propaganda" (xuānchuán) is a neutral term for publicity and education.
A formulation Xi Jinping used in 2023, linking cultural prosperity, building a culturally strong country and creating a modern Chinese civilisation to the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.
A body of Xi's statements on cultural work, presented officially in October 2023 as the cultural component of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era.

t: Promoting patriotic education in the new era so that it is broad, in-depth, lasting and effective
zh: 推动新时代爱国主义教育广泛深入持久有效开展
paras: This short news report, originally carried in the People's Daily, covers a press conference on the Patriotic Education Law, which took effect on 1 January 2024. Jin Xin reports how officials presented the law as a legal guarantee for making patriotic education in the new era broad, in-depth, lasting and effective.

The press conference was jointly organised by the Legislative Affairs Commission and the General Office of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress. Officials from the Publicity Department of the Central Committee, the Cyberspace Administration, the Ministry of Culture and Tourism and the Ministry of Education answered reporters' questions.

Yang Heqing of the Legislative Affairs Commission lists four roles for the law: legal support for patriotic education, spiritual momentum for the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, support for traditional culture, and a basis for safeguarding national security, honour and interests. Tang Lei describes existing laws, regulations and rules on online content, including the Cybersecurity Law and the Regulations on the Online Protection of Minors. Zeng Jianli says that putting patriotic education into law reflects deeper understanding of its importance, the integration of core socialist values into the legal system, and the advance of law-based governance. Zhou Jiucai and Wang Daquan outline measures on cultural heritage, red tourism and intangible heritage, and on schools, where students are the key group.

The report concludes that the law is meant to consolidate shared values, strengthen national unity and gather strength for national rejuvenation. Education authorities say they will fulfil their statutory duties by integrating patriotic education into curricula, strengthening practical education, running signature activities and deepening cooperation between schools and families. Read the original if you want a brief official account of how Chinese state bodies describe the aims and implementation of the Patriotic Education Law.
quoteEn: Establishing, stressing, regulating and guiding patriotic education through legislation reflects a deepening understanding of the great significance and important role of the patriotic spirit, as the theory and practice of cultural development under Party leadership in the new era advance.
quoteZh: 以立法的形式对爱国主义教育进行确立、强调、规范、引导，体现了随着党领导新时代文化建设理论和实践的发展，我们对爱国主义精神重大意义和重要作用的认识不断深化

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal of restoring China to national strength and prosperity, closely associated with Xi Jinping's leadership since 2012.
A set of twelve values promoted officially since 2012, including prosperity, democracy, patriotism and the rule of law.

A law adopted by the National People's Congress Standing Committee in October 2023 and in force from 1 January 2024. It sets out requirements for patriotic education across schools, society, culture and the internet.

glossary.literal: comprehensively governing the country according to law
glossary.explanation: The official policy of comprehensively governing the country according to law, as framed by the Party. It has been a prominent slogan since the 18th Party Congress (2012).

t: Drawing vitality for ideological and political theory courses from reform and innovation
zh: 思政课建设要向改革创新要活力
paras: Marking five years since Xi Jinping's March 2019 symposium for teachers of ideological and political theory courses (sizhengke), this Guangming Daily commentary takes up how these courses can keep gaining vitality. Xi said then that their development must "draw vitality from reform and innovation". Wang argues that the five years have produced clear results, and that the next stage should rest on strengthened Party leadership, innovation, coordinated action and digital empowerment.

The piece has three parts. The first surveys results in four areas: guiding ideas, the overall pattern of work, the content system and teaching methods. The second extracts three basic lessons: upholding Party leadership, innovation as a driving force, and coordinated linkage. The third proposes how to deepen reform from "a new historical starting point".

In Wang's account, the guiding ideas are set by Xi's statements and by central policy documents, which supply top-level design. The pattern of work has changed through stronger Marxism schools, research funding for the courses, and a school–family–society effort. The content system is built around the course "Introduction to Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era", the "Great Ideological and Political Course" and integration across primary, secondary and university stages. Methods include case-based, inquiry-based and experiential teaching, as well as virtual classrooms. The lessons Wang draws stress that Party leadership "can only be strengthened, not weakened". They also cite university Party secretaries and presidents as first persons responsible, and a teacher–student ratio of no less than 1:350 for full-time teachers.

For the next stage Wang proposes three measures. The first links compulsory and elective courses, with the Xi Jinping Thought introduction as the core of a "gold course" system. The second joins the small classroom to the wider social classroom through practice bases, volunteering and fieldwork. The third uses digital platforms, resource banks and XR/VR simulation to move from using technology to being empowered by it, and from individual teachers to team effort. Read the original if you want an official-academic account of how Chinese universities describe their ideological and political course reforms, with concrete policy instruments and examples.
quoteEn: In promoting reform and innovation of ideological and political theory courses, Party leadership can only be strengthened, not weakened.
quoteZh: 推动思政课改革创新，党的领导只能加强、不能削弱。

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses in Marxist theory, Party ideology and moral education taught at Chinese schools and universities. They are treated as central to the task of fostering virtue and cultivating talent.
A concept from Xi Jinping that extends such teaching beyond the classroom into social practice and real-life settings, drawing on society as a whole.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology since 2017. It is written into the Party and state constitutions and is the core content of the courses described here.
University units that teach the ideological and political courses and carry out research in Marxist theory. Central policy has designated them key schools.

t: Strengthening political guidance for youth and cultivating new-era talents for the Party
zh: 加强青年政治引领 为党培育时代新人
paras: This commentary, by the secretary of Nanjing University's Communist Youth League committee, responds to Xi Jinping's remarks in a collective conversation with the new leadership of the League's Central Committee. Xi stressed strengthening political guidance for young people. Zhu argues that this is the League's fundamental task: it follows from the League's founding mission and from the Party's need for qualified builders and reliable successors.

The piece first explains why political guidance matters. It then sets out Xi's working path for the League: take a political perspective, start from ideology, and proceed from the characteristics of young people. The second half turns to four "logics" through which guidance is to be carried out: theoretical, historical, practical and one based on present-day reality.

Zhu holds that "listening to the Party and following the Party" is the League's political lifeblood and what distinguishes it from other youth organisations. On the theoretical side, young people should study Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era through regular thematic education. On the historical side, Party history and its "red genes" should be taught. Achievements since the 18th Party Congress (2012) are to serve as "achievement education" supporting the Four-sphere Confidence. The practical logic links practice to young people's specialist skills, to national priorities and to political commitment. Zhu also notes that today's "Z generation" requires new methods.

Zhu concludes that the League should unite, organise and mobilise young people to act as a vanguard and shock force for building a strong country and for the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation through Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated youth work is framed and operationalised after the 20th Party Congress (2022).
quoteEn: As a school in which young people learn socialism with Chinese characteristics and communism through practice, the Communist Youth League should lead young people to hone their professional skills in practice.
quoteZh: 共青团作为广大青年在实践中学习中国特色社会主义和共产主义的学校，应当引领青年在实践中锤炼专业本领

glossary.explanation: Confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics, a formula promoted under Xi Jinping.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.
The official term for China's own path to modernization, set out prominently at the 20th Party Congress (2022).

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal of restoring China's national strength and international standing, associated with the Chinese Dream.
The Party's mass organisation for young people, which the Party describes as its assistant and reserve force.

t: Linking citizen moral development and the raising of social civility in the new era
zh: 新时代公民道德建设与提升社会文明程度会通之径
source: Journal of Yangzhou University (Humanities & Social Sciences), 2020 no. 4
paras: Writing in 2020, Liang Haifeng takes up the Outline for Implementing Citizen Moral Development in the New Era, issued by the Central Committee and State Council in October 2019. The article asks how moral development among citizens relates to the level of civility (wenming chengdu) of Chinese society. Liang's thesis is that the two reinforce each other and cannot be separated: citizen morality is the foundation of social civility, and social civility in turn eases moral development.

The article first defines social civility, which Liang reads, following Party congress reports, mainly as spiritual and ideological-moral progress. It then discusses the limits of law, the "broken windows" theory and Gustave Le Bon's work on crowd psychology. Next it sets the Outline against China's economic growth, the change in the principal contradiction of society, and the drive to modernize state governance. The final sections take up the four key tasks the Outline sets out.

Liang argues from historical materialism that morality belongs to the superstructure and rises with the productive forces, citing Engels on civilization as a practical matter. Law is slow, cannot cover every uncivil act, and rests on a moral base, so Liang holds that rule by law and rule by virtue must work together. Citing the "broken windows" theory and Le Bon on conformity, the article claims that a clean, orderly environment encourages good conduct while a disordered one spreads bad conduct. Liang also contends that, with the principal contradiction now between people's growing need for a better life and unbalanced, inadequate development, spiritual needs depend on society's moral level.

Liang concludes that the Outline expresses cultural and path confidence and is part of modernizing the system and capacity of state governance. Its four tasks are firm ideals and convictions, the core socialist values, traditional Chinese virtues, and the national and contemporary spirit. Liang expects the Outline to raise moral standards and civility, and to prepare for building a modern socialist country. Read the original if you want an official-line account of how Chinese scholars in 2020 justified linking moral education, rule by virtue and social civility.
quoteEn: Citizen moral development is the cornerstone of raising social civility; conversely, a higher level of civility helps moral development proceed smoothly and effectively, and the two complement each other and cannot be separated.
quoteZh: 公民道德建设是提升社会文明程度的基石，反之，社会文明程度的提升又有助于公民道德建设的顺利有效开展，二者相辅相成，不可分割。

glossary.zh: 新时代公民道德建设实施纲要
glossary.pinyin: Xīn shídài gōngmín dàodé jiànshè shíshī gāngyào
glossary.en: Outline for Implementing Citizen Moral Development in the New Era
glossary.explanation: A policy document issued by the Central Committee and State Council in October 2019. It updates the 2001 Outline and sets tasks for moral education and conduct.
The level of civilizational progress of society. Party documents use it mainly for spiritual and ideological-moral progress and for citizens' civilized conduct.

A twenty-four-character formula promoted since the 18th Party Congress (2012). It names twelve values at the national, societal and individual levels, such as prosperity, democracy, patriotism and integrity.

glossary.zh: 依法治国和以德治国相结合
glossary.pinyin: yī fǎ zhìguó hé yǐ dé zhìguó xiāng jiéhé
glossary.en: rule by law and rule by virtue
glossary.literal: combining governing the country by law with governing it by virtue
glossary.explanation: A governance formula, stressed at the Fourth Plenum of the 18th Central Committee (2014), that combines legal governance with moral guidance.

glossary.zh: 国家治理体系和治理能力现代化
glossary.pinyin: guójiā zhìlǐ tǐxì hé zhìlǐ nénglì xiàndàihuà
glossary.en: modernizing the system and capacity of state governance
glossary.explanation: The overall goal of comprehensively deepening reform, set at the Third Plenum of the 18th Central Committee (2013). It refers to improving institutions and the Party-state's ability to govern.

A Marxist-Leninist category used by the Party to characterise the main tension of an era. The 19th Party Congress (2017) defined it as that between people's growing need for a better life and unbalanced, inadequate development.

t: Preventing disasters before they happen: building a popular line of defence for disaster prevention and reduction
zh: 防患未然，筑起防灾减灾的人民防线
paras: This short commentary, first published in Guangming Daily in October 2020, asks how China can strengthen its capacity for disaster risk governance. Yuan argues that disaster prevention, reduction and relief affect people's lives and property and social stability, and serve as a measure of the ruling party's leadership and the government's executive capacity. The author's answer is to place ordinary people and communities at the centre of disaster prevention.

Yuan notes that since the 18th Party Congress (2012) the Party Central Committee with Xi Jinping at its core has given disaster work greater prominence. The author nonetheless sees a still complex situation: weak sharing of disaster information, poorly coordinated resources, patchy public education, and a widespread habit of stressing relief over reduction. Four sets of proposals follow, each framed around a question: who takes charge, how, relying on whom, and where.

The first proposal is to train a group of knowledgeable people. Yuan wants grassroots cadres, volunteers and local notables trained in hazard knowledge, and grassroots information workers integrated to fix the "last mile" of warnings. The author cites the more than 700,000 grassroots disaster information officers active in the 2020 flood season. The second proposal is to build skills through education: popular books, games, films, household manuals and online classes. The third calls for relying on the masses through safety education, regular evacuation drills, hazard checks by residents and grid-based risk management.

The fourth proposal treats urban and rural communities as the front line, drawing on lessons from the fight against Covid-19. Yuan calls for emergency shelters, community hazard inspections, pooled reduction resources and model comprehensive disaster-reduction communities and counties. The author concludes that prevention and public self-help should replace the emphasis on relief. Read the original if you want a brief example of how a Party-aligned commentator in 2020 presented disaster governance as a mass-participation task grounded in communities.
quoteEn: To raise disaster risk governance capacity, Party member leaders and cadres must play their vanguard and exemplary role while fully mobilising and relying on the broad masses, so that the people can play their主体 role well.
quoteZh: 提高灾害风险治理能力，要在充分发挥党员领导干部先锋模范作用的同时，充分发动广大人民群众、充分依靠广大人民群众，发挥好人民群众的主体作用。

t: On the subject and object of ideological and political education
zh: 论思想政治教育的主体和客体
source: Studies on Ideological and Political Education (思想政治教育研究), 2020 no. 1
paras: Yu Bin takes up a basic question in the theory of ideological and political education: who is its subject and who is its object. The article challenges the influential view of "intersubjectivity", which holds that teachers and students are both subjects. Yu argues that students remain the object of education, even when they exercise some subjectivity, and that the subject is a wider group than teachers alone.

The article is a theoretical argument that proceeds mainly by close reading of Marx, Engels, Lenin and Xi Jinping. It first tests the premise of intersubjectivity, then lists who counts as a subject: teachers, the state, the ruling class and Party committees at all levels, and family members. It then turns to the object, to the ways objects can show initiative, and to practical consequences for university teaching staff.

Yu's central move is to deny that people can only be subjects. Citing Marx's uses of the word "subject" and "object", including value as the subject of a process, the author contends that the same entity can be both. Because the aim is for theory to "grip the masses", the students are objects. Yu reads Xi Jinping's call to "bring students' subjectivity into play" as the unity of guidance and subjectivity, not as a unity of teacher and student subjectivities. Citing Lenin's letter to the Capri school, Yu holds that teachers decide the real political direction of a course, so the teaching staff are the decisive subject. Ideological and political education works, Yu says, when the object recognises the content and when subject and object belong to the same class.

Yu concludes that universities must give priority to building the teaching force. Teachers who give "negative" ideological education should be removed or replaced, and others should be criticised, re-educated or more closely supervised. Teachers are described as "subjects with object-like qualities", who must follow the Party's education policy and accept supervision. Yu also endorses students' reports on classroom teaching they judge hostile, as an exercise of students' initiative, and favours combining indoctrination with heuristic teaching and social practice. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese Marxist scholar defends a hierarchical subject–object model against intersubjectivity theories, and what that implies for university teachers.
quoteEn: Therefore, bringing students' subjectivity into play is only to bring into play the subjectivity of an object that possesses subjectivity; students remain objects, even if objects that exercise their own subjectivity.
quoteZh: 因此，发挥学生主体性作用，只是发挥作为具有主体性的客体的主体性作用，学生仍然是客体，尽管是发挥了自身主体性作用的客体。

glossary.explanation: A concept, borrowed from Western philosophy, that treats teacher and student as equal subjects in a relationship. Yu Bin takes it as the main position he criticises.
The Chinese term for education in the Party's ideology, politics and moral outlook. It is carried out in schools, universities and the wider society.

t: Institutional strengths are the greatest strength of the Party and the state
st: Studying volume III of Xi Jinping: The Governance of China in depth
zh: 制度优势是党和国家的最大优势
zhSub: 深入学习《习近平谈治国理政》第三卷
paras: Writing in the People's Daily in August 2020, Qu Qingshan offers a study guide to the third volume of Xi Jinping: The Governance of China. The volume collects three texts by Xi on upholding and improving the system of socialism with Chinese characteristics and modernizing the system and capacity for national governance. Qu argues that these ideas are an important part of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. In Qu's reading, institutional strengths are, in Xi's phrase, the greatest strength of a party and a country.

The commentary is organised around five themes, each introduced as something that must be grasped. These are the overall goal of comprehensively deepening reform, the significance of institutional improvement, the relationship between the two halves of that goal, the relationship between governance system and governance capacity, and the distinctive features and strengths of China's system. It ends with the phased targets for modernizing governance. Qu relies mainly on extended quotations from Xi, with connecting commentary.

Qu first presents the goal set at the Third Plenum of the 18th Central Committee (2013), to improve socialism with Chinese characteristics and modernize national governance, as a major theoretical innovation. It was developed by the Fourth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2019). Qu then stresses that the goal has two inseparable parts: the first fixes the fundamental direction, the socialist path, while the second sets out how the system is to be improved. Likewise, governance system and governance capacity must be advanced together, since a good system does not automatically yield capacity. Qu lists thirteen areas of 'notable strength', including the Party's centralised leadership, the people as masters of the country, the ability to concentrate resources on major undertakings, public ownership as the mainstay, and 'one country, two systems'. Qu cites the response to COVID-19 and decades of rapid growth and social stability as practical proof.

Qu concludes by setting out the three-step target: more mature and settled institutions by the Party's centenary, basic modernization of governance by 2035, and full modernization by the centenary of the People's Republic. Qu holds that diligent study and implementation of Xi's thought will ensure these goals are met. Read the original if you want a concise, official-line summary of how Party commentary presented the governance-modernization agenda and the claimed advantages of China's system in 2020.
quoteEn: The national governance system and national governance capacity constrain and reinforce each other; governing a country cannot rely on either one alone.
quoteZh: 国家治理体系与国家治理能力两者相互制约、相互促进，单靠哪一个治理国家都不行。

glossary.explanation: The reform agenda launched at the Third Plenum of the 18th Central Committee in 2013, covering all major policy areas.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.
The official policy under which Hong Kong and Macao retain separate economic and administrative systems within China; the article presents it as a strength of the system.

t: The Communist Party of China: born for the people, flourishing through the people
zh: 中国共产党：为人民而生 因人民而兴
paras: Published in Guangming Daily on 4 September 2020, this commentary asks why the Communist Party of China has been able to lead China from semi-colonial status to national rejuvenation and to grow from a party of about 50 members into one of more than 91 million. Liu Hongling answers that the Party wins popular support through its basic stance and purpose and through concrete action and results on behalf of the people. The title echoes Xi Jinping's statement that the Party comes from the people, was born for the people and flourishes because of the people.

The article is organised around three themes, each traced from the Party's founding in 1921 through the revolutionary, socialist-construction and reform periods to the era after the 18th Party Congress (2012). The themes are a consistent people's standpoint and mass viewpoint, the safeguarding and advancement of the masses' interests, and the use of the people's approval as the highest standard for judging all Party work. Liu draws on statements by Mao Zedong, Deng Xiaoping and Xi Jinping, and on Party documents such as the 1990 decision on strengthening ties with the masses.

Liu argues that the Party's stance has been continuous. It adopted historical materialism and the people's standpoint from the start, wrote wholehearted service to the people into the Party constitution at the Seventh Congress (1945), and later elaborated a "six basic points" mass viewpoint and the people-centred development philosophy. This stance, the author says, was turned into practice through land reform, poverty reduction, disaster relief and epidemic response, and by treating development as the Party's first task in governing. Liu adds that the Party measures its work by whether the people support, approve of, are happy with and agree to it. In this account, that standard has driven rectification campaigns, anti-corruption work and historical resolutions in 1945 and 1981, which the author presents as evidence of the Party's courage in self-reform. Liu claims that no other party in the world has matched the Party's attention to conduct and its record of correcting errors.

Liu concludes that the Party has never had interests of its own and that its leading position was not self-proclaimed but chosen by history and the people. The author expects practice to continue to confirm the correctness of that choice. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated scholarship in 2020 explained the Party's legitimacy through the people's standpoint, and of which historical quotations and documents it used.
quoteEn: The leading position of the Communist Party of China was not self-proclaimed but chosen by history and the people, and practice has proved, and will further prove, that this choice is correct.
quoteZh: 中国共产党的领导地位不是自封的，而是历史与人民的选择，实践已经并将进一步证明这一选择的正确。

glossary.zh: 以人民为中心的发展思想
glossary.pinyin: yǐ rénmín wéi zhōngxīn de fāzhǎn sīxiǎng
glossary.literal: development thinking with the people at the centre
glossary.explanation: A formulation associated with Xi Jinping after 2012, holding that economic and social development should serve the people's interests and well-being.
A slogan associated with Mao Zedong from 1944 and written into the Party constitution at the Seventh Congress (1945) as the Party's fundamental purpose.
The Party doctrine that the masses are the makers of history and that Party work must rely on and serve them; it is closely tied to the "mass line".

t: Strengthen the study of history and firm up ideals and convictions
zh: 加强历史学习 坚定理想信念
paras: Writing in the People's Daily on 18 September 2020, Weng Tiehui argues that schools and universities should step up education in four histories: the history of the Communist Party of China, of the People's Republic, of reform and opening up, and of socialist development. The piece takes as its starting point Xi Jinping's reply earlier that year to young Party members at Fudan University, which urged them to study Marxist theory alongside these histories in order to strengthen their ideals and convictions. Weng presents this study as a way to consolidate the ideological foundations of teachers and students.

The commentary is organised in three parts. The first sets out why this learning matters, the second defines its goals and tasks, and the third proposes ways of carrying it out in the education system. Weng draws throughout on Xi Jinping's statements about history, and cites Marx on people making their own history under inherited conditions.

On significance, Weng gives three reasons. The study helps Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era take root in students' minds. It is also said to be inherent in firming up ideals and convictions, since these must rest on an understanding of Marxism and of historical laws. And it supplies material for ideological and political work in schools, for explaining why the Party "can", Marxism "works" and socialism with Chinese characteristics is "good". On goals, Weng names three aims: linking the distant and the near so that students learn to discern right from wrong and reject historical nihilism; centring on knowledge and belief, so that students understand both how things happened and why; and combining feeling with action, so that individual aspirations are tied to the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

For implementation, Weng calls for three measures. The first is to anchor the study in Xi Jinping Thought, bringing it into textbooks, classrooms and minds. The second is to use school education as the main channel, integrating the histories into ideological and political theory courses and into all teaching. The third is to treat the internet as the main front, with online courses, quizzes, virtual retracings of the Long March and new-media publicity. Weng describes the task as an important political task for the education system. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-state education policy in 2020 framed history study as a tool of ideological and political education.
quoteEn: We must grasp faith, conviction and confidence, and guide teachers and students to know how things came to be.
quoteZh: 要把握信仰、信念、信心，引导师生“知其然”

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018. It is presented officially as the latest stage in adapting Marxism to China.
In official usage, a label for views that question or negate the Party's revolutionary history and the path of socialism in China. Party texts present it as a harmful ideological trend.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal of restoring China's national strength and international standing, closely tied to the Chinese Dream and the "two centenary goals".
Compulsory courses in Chinese schools and universities that teach Marxism, Party history and official ideology.

t: The contemporary significance of Marxist philosophical methodology
zh: 马克思主义哲学方法论的时代意蕴
paras: This newspaper commentary, published in Guangming Daily in September 2020, argues that Marxist philosophy is both a scientific worldview and a scientific methodology. Han holds that Party members and cadres need to master the methodology in order to raise their philosophical competence and their ability to analyse and solve problems. The piece opens with Engels's remark that Marx's worldview is a method rather than a dogma.

The article is built in four short sections. It first stresses why method matters, citing Mao Zedong's image of the bridge needed to cross a river and Xi Jinping's description of the Marxist worldview as a "master key". It then sets out methods derived from dialectical materialism, methods derived from historical materialism, and finally a set of thinking methods and capacities.

Han ties each method to a branch of theory. Dialectical materialism yields seeking truth from facts, the materialist-dialectical method (comprehensive, interconnected, developmental and systemic observation, attention to principal contradictions) and testing ideas in practice. Historical materialism yields the method of social consciousness acting back on social being, analysis of the basic contradictions of society, and the mass line. The author presents the mass line as the Party's lifeline and calls for adherence to a people-centred approach in the new era. The final section defines six capacities that Xi Jinping asks leaders to improve: strategic, historical, dialectical, innovative, law-based and bottom-line thinking.

Han concludes that applying these methods and raising these thinking capacities is a basic requirement of studying Marxist philosophy, and that they serve Socialism with Chinese Characteristics in the new era and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. The text is largely a structured exposition of Xi Jinping's statements on method. Read the original if you want a compact example of how Party-oriented commentary organises Marxist methodology for cadre education.
quoteEn: The mass line is our Party's lifeline and fundamental working line, and an important family heirloom that keeps the Party forever youthful and combative.
quoteZh: 群众路线是我们党的生命线和根本工作路线，是我们党永葆青春活力和战斗力的重要传家宝。

glossary.explanation: A Party working method associated with Mao Zedong: policies are drawn from the masses' views and then taken back to them ("from the masses, to the masses"). It is described officially as the Party's lifeline.
A principle of basing policy on actual conditions, associated with Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping, and treated as the core of the Party's ideological line.
A mode of thought promoted by Xi Jinping: set the lowest acceptable outcome, prepare for the worst, and strive for the best result.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The official long-term national goal of restoring China's strength and international standing, central to Xi Jinping's idea of the Chinese Dream.

t: Strengthening study, reflection, practice and comprehension to achieve thorough mastery
zh: 强化学思践悟 做到融会贯通
paras: This short commentary, published in Economic Daily in September 2020, follows the release of the third volume of Xi Jinping: The Governance of China. Hao Yubin argues that the three volumes form one organic whole and are the authoritative work for studying Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. Reading the original texts as a unit, the author says, is the way to grasp the comprehensiveness and systematic structure of the theory and to reach thorough mastery.

The article is organised around four aspects of the Thought that readers are urged to study, reflect on and put into practice across all three volumes. These are the people-centred standpoint, the theoretical character of keeping pace with the times, scientific theoretical thinking, and a problem-oriented approach.

On the first, Hao traces the people-centred position from the opening piece of volume one through volume two to volume three, where it is said to deepen into a standard for understanding, action and judgement. On the second, the author cites the new development philosophy, supply-side structural reform and high-quality development as examples of theory continually enriched through practice. On the third, Hao points to dialectics, the call for strategic, innovative, dialectical, rule-of-law and bottom-line thinking, and grasping principal contradictions. On the fourth, the commentary describes the Thought as treating problems as the starting point of policy and as uniting Marxism's scientific and practical character.

Hao concludes that, as China completes a moderately prosperous society and enters a new journey toward the second centenary goal, deeper study should link theory with practice and unify knowing with doing. Doing so is said to strengthen theoretical confidence and the ability to identify and solve problems. Read the original if you want a brief example of how official commentary in 2020 framed the method of studying the three volumes of The Governance of China.
quoteEn: Only by treating volumes one, two and three as a whole, reading the original works and texts, grasping the principles and strengthening study, reflection, practice and comprehension, can one accurately grasp the comprehensiveness, richness, systematic structure and completeness of this theoretical system.
quoteZh: 把一卷、二卷、三卷作为一个整体，读原著、学原文、悟原理，强化学思践悟，才能准确掌握这个理论体系内容的全面性和丰富性、结构的系统性和完整性

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The official guiding ideology of the Chinese Communist Party, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017 and 2018.
A policy framework announced in 2015 stressing innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development.
An official economic goal emphasising quality and efficiency of growth rather than speed alone, prominent since 2017.
An economic policy programme launched around 2015 to adjust the structure of supply, for example by cutting excess capacity.

t: Continually tempering the political character of daring to take responsibility
st: Studying and implementing General Secretary Xi Jinping's series of important statements on courage to shoulder responsibility
zh: 不懈淬炼勇于担当的政治品格
zhSub: 深入学习贯彻习近平总书记关于勇于担当系列重要论述
paras: This commentary, published in the People's Daily in July 2020, takes up Xi Jinping's repeated statements that Party members and cadres must be willing to take responsibility. Zang Anmin argues that daring to shoulder responsibility is both a political quality and a basic duty of office. In the author's account, it is the clearest test of a cadre's Party spirit and work style, and cadres must keep tempering it as they face risks and challenges.

The piece opens by citing Xi's remarks during an inspection tour in Jilin on selecting cadres and protecting those who act. It is then organised in three parts. The first explains the significance of Xi's statements. The second sets out how responsibility is to be put into practice in each post and task. The third describes how Party members and their organisations can cultivate the quality, with examples ranging from revolutionary martyrs to Jiao Yulu, Liao Junbo, Huang Danian and cadres in the Covid-19 and flood responses.

Zang gives three reasons for the significance of Xi's statements. They enrich the Marxist standpoint of practice, they reveal how the Party has used a great revolutionary spirit to drive great social revolution, and they provide spiritual impetus for the Party's historical mission in the new era, including the Two Centenary Goals. The author then names four settings that call for responsibility: clarity on matters of principle, willingness to struggle against unhealthy tendencies, charging forward in urgent and difficult tasks, and tireless effort in routine work. On principle, Zang says cadres must strengthen the "Four Consciousnesses", the Four-sphere Confidence and the Two Upholds, and stay in line with the Party Central Committee with Xi at its core. Zang also traces failure to take responsibility to selfish thoughts, and says loyalty to the Party is shown through action.

For cultivation, Zang calls for three things. Cadres should unite knowledge and practice by studying Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. They should foster courage through selfless loyalty. Organisations should select, reward and protect cadres who act, and hold to account those who shirk, using role models to set the tone. Read the original if you want a compact example of how Party media in 2020 linked cadre responsibility to Xi's discourse on struggle and Party loyalty.
quoteEn: Taking responsibility is the "form"; political awareness is the "root".
quoteZh: 担当是“形”，觉悟是“本”。

glossary.explanation: A Party formulation, prominent since 2018, that calls on members to uphold General Secretary Xi Jinping's core position in the Party Central Committee and the Party's centralised, unified leadership.
Confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics, a slogan promoted under Xi Jinping.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.
A Party requirement, set out in 2016, that members maintain political awareness, awareness of the big picture, of the core, and of alignment.
Official targets of building a moderately prosperous society by the Party's centenary in 2021 and a modern socialist country by the People's Republic's centenary in 2049.

t: Grasping the dialectical relations in the pursuit of a better life in the new era
zh: 把握新时代追求美好生活的辩证关系
paras: This commentary, published in Guangming Daily in September 2020, takes up Xi Jinping's remarks on a "better life" in the third volume of Xi Jinping: The Governance of China. Ma Chunhong argues that the better life is both a practical and a theoretical question, and that pursuing it requires handling three dialectical relationships using the epistemology and methodology of the unity of opposites.

The article is organised in three sections. Each takes one pair: goal and means, efficiency and fairness, and individual and collective well-being. Each section sets out the logic of the pair and applies it to the new era.

On goals and means, Ma holds that the goal leads and the means depend on it, so the means for each stage of the Party's phased targets (2020, 2035, 2050) must be adjusted as people's needs change. On efficiency and fairness, Ma uses the image of making the cake bigger and dividing it well. Growth must continue, while distribution should reward ability and contribution and use secondary and tertiary distribution to build a fair pattern. On the individual and the collective, Ma treats the Chinese Dream as the organic unity of national, ethnic and personal dreams.

Ma concludes that individual and collective well-being promote each other and must not be set in opposition. Individual well-being, in Ma's view, must consciously be subordinated to and merged into collective well-being, under the strong leadership of the Communist Party. Read the original if you want a short example of how Party theorists present Xi's "better life" discourse through dialectical pairs.
quoteEn: Individual well-being must consciously submit to collective well-being, so that in the end the two promote each other and are realised together.
quoteZh: 个体美好必须自觉服从集体美好，最终实现个体美好和集体美好的相互促进和共同实现。

glossary.explanation: A slogan Xi Jinping introduced in 2012, centred on the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Official texts present it as joining national, ethnic and personal aspirations.

t: Resolutely advancing the building of a community with a shared future for mankind
zh: 更加坚定推动构建人类命运共同体
paras: Writing in People's Daily in September 2020, during the global spread of COVID-19, Leng Rong asks how China should respond to a world in what the article calls "changes unseen in a century". The commentary argues that the Party Central Committee with Xi Jinping at its core is right to hold to the path of peaceful development and to work for a community with a shared future for mankind. It presents this as a sign of the Party's steadiness and sense of responsibility.

The piece has three sections. The first traces China's commitment to peaceful development from the Five Principles of Peaceful Coexistence in the 1950s, through the independent foreign policy of peace after reform and opening up, to Xi Jinping's statements since the 18th Party Congress (2012). The second explains why the idea of a community with a shared future was put forward. The third turns to the pandemic and to China's future course.

Leng gives four reasons for peaceful development: it fits the global trend, it is a necessary choice for China, it is the shared wish of the world's peoples, and it requires opposition to hegemonism. The community with a shared future is tied to four developments: the changing balance of world forces (the article says emerging and developing countries contribute 80 per cent of global growth), new technologies that bind lives together, and global problems no state can handle alone. Leng cites the Belt and Road Initiative and the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank as practice, and says the idea has entered several UN documents. The pandemic is read as proof that humanity shares a common fate. Leng criticises those who politicise the virus, shift blame or cling to Cold War thinking and zero-sum games, and says the world order should be decided by all countries, not by one or a few.

Leng concludes that China will not waver in pursuing peaceful development and the community with a shared future, and will never seek hegemony or expansion. The article also calls for "bottom-line thinking" and preparation for a long period of external uncertainty, with the main task being to strengthen China's own capabilities. China is said to be set to make "new and greater contributions" to world peace on the path to the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want a concise, authoritative statement of how the Party press framed China's foreign policy and its global vision in the first year of the pandemic.
quoteEn: The idea of building a community with a shared future for mankind transcends differences in social systems, discards zero-sum thinking, and sketches for different countries, nations and civilizations the right direction for common effort.
quoteZh: 构建人类命运共同体理念，超越不同社会制度差异，摒弃零和博弈思维，为不同国家、不同民族、不同文明描绘了共同努力奋斗的正确方向。

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept associated with Xi Jinping since 2012–13. It says the interdependence of states calls for cooperation, shared development and a more consultative international order.
The official line that China pursues its development without war or expansion and seeks a peaceful international environment. The article traces it to the 1950s.
A Chinese initiative launched in 2013 to build infrastructure and economic links across Asia, Europe, Africa and beyond. The article treats it as practice of the shared-future idea.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal of restoring China's national strength and international standing, closely linked to the Chinese Dream.
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world begun in 1978 under Deng Xiaoping.

t: Striving for new breakthroughs in comprehensively deepening reform
st: Studying Xi Jinping's statements on comprehensively deepening reform in volume III of Xi Jinping: The Governance of China
zh: 奋力推动全面深化改革实现新突破
zhSub: 学习领会《习近平谈治国理政》第三卷关于全面深化改革的重要论述
paras: Mu Hong's commentary, first published in the People's Daily in August 2020, is a study-and-implementation piece on the newly published third volume of Xi Jinping: The Governance of China. It takes up how Party members and officials should understand and put into practice Xi Jinping's statements on comprehensively deepening reform. Mu's thesis is that these statements are an original part of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era and provide the fundamental guide for reform work, which must be pursued with greater resolve.

The text is organised around five themes: the historical position of reform in the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation; Party leadership; the strategic direction and goal of reform; reform's service to economic and social development; and the people-centred value orientation of reform. A final section calls for continued, practical implementation. It reviews achievements since the Third Plenum of the 18th Central Committee (2013) and sets out tasks for the year in which a moderately prosperous society is to be completed.

Mu argues that reform is the decisive move for realising the two centenary goals and that it is the fundamental driving force for meeting present risks. Reform must stay under the centralised leadership of the Party Central Committee, which Mu describes through the shift from a leading group to a Central Commission for Comprehensively Deepening Reform chaired by Xi, and through the Two Upholds. The overall aim, from the Third Plenum of the 18th Central Committee (2013) and the Fourth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2019), is to improve the socialist system with Chinese characteristics and modernise national governance. In Mu's account, reform serves high-quality development, including market, innovation, regional and opening-up measures. It also serves the people's sense of gain, happiness and security through employment, social security, health, education and poverty-reduction measures. Mu presents the response to COVID-19 as an example of combining reform with epidemic control.

Mu concludes that reform grows harder as it deepens and calls for courage, a practical work style, supervision and inspection, respect for grassroots initiative and tolerance of errors in pioneering reform. Officials are told to treat implementing the Central Committee's reform plans as a major political task and to guard against formalism and bureaucratism. Read the original if you want an official People's Daily framing of Xi-era reform, covering its Party-leadership logic, institutional goals and the practical requirements set for cadres in 2020.
quoteEn: The firm leadership of the Party Central Committee has always been the anchor of comprehensively deepening reform.
quoteZh: 党中央的坚强领导，始终是全面深化改革的定海神针。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017 and 2018.

A Party formula requiring members to uphold General Secretary Xi Jinping's core position in the Party Central Committee and the whole Party, and to uphold the authority and centralised, unified leadership of the Central Committee.

glossary.zh: 中央全面深化改革委员会
glossary.en: Central Commission for Comprehensively Deepening Reform
glossary.explanation: The Party body that designs and coordinates reform. It was set up as a leading group in 2013 and upgraded to a commission in 2018, with Xi Jinping as chair.

glossary.zh: 国家治理体系和治理能力现代化
glossary.pinyin: guójiā zhìlǐ tǐxì hé zhìlǐ nénglì xiàndàihuà
glossary.literal: modernisation of the national governance system and governance capacity
glossary.explanation: The stated overall goal of reform since the Third Plenum of the 18th Central Committee (2013): modernising the system and capacity of national governance.
An official formulation, prominent since 2017, that shifts the emphasis of economic policy from speed of growth to quality, efficiency and innovation.
The goals of completing a moderately prosperous society by the Party's centenary in 2021 and building a modern socialist country by the People's Republic's centenary in 2049.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The official overarching national goal associated with Xi Jinping's Chinese Dream.

t: The new position, new challenges and new opportunities of the new development stage
zh: 新发展阶段的新方位新挑战新机遇
paras: Writing in Economic Daily on 30 September 2020, Ding Maozhan takes up Xi Jinping's statements that the 14th Five-Year Plan period (2021–25) opens a "new development stage" for China. The article asks how to understand the stage's historical position and how to analyse, dialectically, the challenges and opportunities that deep changes at home and abroad bring. Ding argues that this understanding is important for planning economic work in the period.

The commentary opens by quoting Xi's remarks at the symposium of experts in the economic and social fields and at the 17 September meeting with grassroots representatives. It is then organised in three parts: the new position (历史方位, the historical position of the stage), the new challenges, and the new opportunities. Each part is divided into three or four sub-themes, with brief statistical and historical illustration.

On the position, Ding argues that China is completing the first centenary goal of a moderately prosperous society and setting out toward the second centenary goal of a modern socialist country. Ding adds that the economy has moved from high-speed growth to high-quality development, and that the principal contradiction is now between the people's growing needs for a better life and unbalanced, inadequate development. The article cites per capita GDP of 10,000 US dollars, urbanisation above 60 per cent, over 400 million middle-income earners and about 100 million people lifted out of poverty. On challenges, Ding points to a turbulent world (technological competition, protectionism, the pandemic, a reshaping of the global governance order) and to domestic pressures: an unsustainable factor-driven growth model, structural imbalances, and harder reforms. On opportunities, Ding stresses institutional advantages, a large market, resilience, and the Party's "strategic resolve" to pursue high-quality development.

Ding concludes that China remains in a period of important strategic opportunity, that long-term economic improvement will not change, and that challenges are problems of development. The article holds that, under the Party's leadership, China can create new opportunities out of crisis and achieve development that is higher in quality, efficiency, fairness, sustainability and security. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Chinese official economic commentary in 2020 framed the new development stage and the 14th Five-Year Plan.
quoteEn: China's development has ample resilience and enormous potential; the problems now faced are problems within development, and the trend of long-term economic improvement will not change.
quoteZh: 我国发展拥有足够的韧性、巨大的潜力,当前面临的是发展中的问题,经济长期向好的态势不会改变。

glossary.explanation: A phrase in official discourse for the period beginning with the 14th Five-Year Plan (2021–25), when China sets out to build a modern socialist country after completing the first centenary goal.

glossary.pinyin: liǎng gè yìbǎi nián fèndòu mùbiāo
glossary.explanation: Official targets: building a moderately prosperous society by the Party's centenary in 2021, and a modern socialist country by the centenary of the People's Republic in 2049.
An official formulation, adopted in late 2017, for a shift from rapid growth to growth emphasising quality, efficiency and innovation.

t: The basis for firming up the Four-sphere Confidence
st: The 13 notable advantages of China's national system and system of national governance
zh: 坚定“四个自信”的基本依据所在
paras: This short commentary, published in People's Daily in August 2020, asks why the 13 notable advantages of China's national system and system of national governance should be seen as the basis for the Four-sphere Confidence. Han Qingxiang notes that the Fourth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2019) was the first to summarise these advantages systematically. In Han's account they are the fundamental guarantee of the "two miracles" of rapid economic growth and long-term social stability, and the institutional "code" of "Chinese governance".

The article first treats the 13 advantages as an organic whole, then traces their source in socialism with Chinese characteristics, and finally sets out what is needed to bring them into full play. The areas Han lists include Party leadership, the people as masters of the country, rule of law, national unity, the economy, culture, people's livelihood, reform and innovation, defence, "one country, two systems", and foreign affairs.

Han argues that the advantages are layered and logically ordered. The advantage of upholding the Party's centralised and unified leadership, its scientific theory and political stability heads the list and runs through the other twelve. The system is described as scientific because the Party has combined Marxism's basic principles with China's realities and the features of the times, and has turned successful practice into institutions. Han presents Party leadership as the most essential feature and greatest strength of the system, resting on its capacity for ideological guidance, inspiration, mobilisation, consensus-building and implementation.

Han concludes that making full use of the 13 advantages requires upholding Party leadership and improving the institutional system through which the Party oversees the whole situation and coordinates all sides. Han holds that doing so will allow China to create new and greater miracles and strengthen the Four-sphere Confidence. Read the original if you want a compact example of how official commentary in 2020 linked the 13 advantages to Party leadership and to the Four-sphere Confidence.
quoteEn: Leadership by the Communist Party of China is the most essential feature of socialism with Chinese characteristics and the greatest strength of its system; the Party is the highest political leadership force.
quoteZh: 中国共产党领导是中国特色社会主义最本质的特征，是中国特色社会主义制度的最大优势，党是最高政治领导力量。

glossary.explanation: A formula, in full form since the 18th Party Congress (2012), calling for confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics.
The official name for the Party's model of socialism since the reform era, combining a socialist system with China-specific conditions and policies.
A list in the Decision of the Fourth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2019) of strengths claimed for China's national system and governance, from Party leadership to foreign affairs.
Official shorthand for China's rapid economic growth and long-term social stability.
The official policy framework for relations with Hong Kong and Macao, and proposed for Taiwan, under which socialist and capitalist systems coexist within one state.

t: The scientific methodology of building a moderately prosperous society in all respects
zh: 全面建成小康社会的科学方法论
paras: Writing in the People's Daily in July 2020, Chen Jinlong takes up the pledge to complete a moderately prosperous society in all respects by 2020, which he calls a solemn promise by the Party to the people and to history. Chen argues that since the 18th Party Congress (2012) the Central Committee with Xi Jinping at its core has developed a scientific methodology for this task. In Chen's reading, it embodies Marxist ways of thinking and working and serves as both ideological guidance and a practical guide for the final push.

The short commentary is organised under three headings. The first concerns viewing and planning the goal from a strategic height. The second concerns balanced planning that takes all factors into account (统筹兼顾), including how to balance epidemic control with development. The third concerns seizing the key points and achieving breakthroughs in the three critical battles: preventing major risks, targeted poverty alleviation and pollution control.

On strategy, Chen traces the goal from the "Two Centenary Goals" and notes the shift from "building" to "completing" a moderately prosperous society, which in his view raises the standard. He places it within the Four-pronged Comprehensive Strategy, where deepening reform, law-based governance and full and rigorous self-governance of the Party supply momentum, legal protection and political guarantees. On balance, Chen stresses that "comprehensive" matters more than "moderately prosperous": the society must cover all fields, all people and all regions, yet standards should not be raised blindly beyond national conditions. On the three battles, he describes risk-prevention mechanisms and "bottom-line thinking", precise poverty alleviation (551 million rural poor reduced to 5.51 million by end-2019, in the author's figure) and an ecological approach that rejects pollution first and treatment later.

Chen concludes that grasping the strategic opportunity, balancing epidemic control with economic and social development, and focusing on the weakest links are what will secure the goal despite the shock of COVID-19. He presents the methodology as a concrete application of dialectical thinking. Read the original if you want a concise official-line account, from mid-2020, of how Party theorists framed the final stage of the moderately prosperous society campaign.
quoteEn: What building a moderately prosperous society in all respects emphasises is not only "moderate prosperity" but, more importantly, being "all-round".
quoteZh: 全面建成小康社会强调的不仅是“小康”，更为重要的是“全面”。

glossary.explanation: A Chinese Communist Party development goal, first used by Deng Xiaoping, denoting a comfortable but not yet affluent standard of living. The 18th Party Congress set the aim of completing it in all respects by 2020.
The goals of building a moderately prosperous society by the Party's centenary in 2021 and a modern socialist country by the People's Republic's centenary in 2049.
A strategic framework put forward under Xi Jinping: building a moderately prosperous society in all respects, deepening reform, advancing law-based governance and strictly governing the Party.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: The official name for the Party's drive under Xi Jinping to tighten discipline, combat corruption and improve cadre conduct.
The policy, promoted by Xi Jinping, of tailoring poverty relief to specific households and villages rather than broad regional aid.

t: The leadership of the Communist Party of China is the correct choice made by history and the people
zh: 中国共产党的领导是历史和人民作出的正确选择
paras: Jiang Jinquan takes as his starting point Xi Jinping's statement that history and the people chose the Communist Party of China (CPC) to lead the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, and that this choice is correct and must be upheld permanently. Originally published in the People's Daily on 20 August 2020, the commentary argues that the claim rests on historical, theoretical and practical grounds. Jiang's thesis is that Party leadership is both a product of modern Chinese history and the essential guarantee for completing national rejuvenation.

The piece has three parts. The first traces how the Party's leading position was formed, from the Opium War of 1840 and the failed reform and revolutionary projects that followed, through the founding of the Party in 1921, the revolutionary wars, the founding of the People's Republic, the reform era after the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee, and the period since the 18th Party Congress (2012). The second explains why the Party was able to lead, and the third explains why its leadership remains indispensable.

In the second part Jiang identifies five features that he calls the Party's "genetic code": guidance by scientific theory, namely Marxism as adapted to Chinese conditions; a people-centred political stance; unremitting pursuit of its founding mission; a strong and tight organisational system built on democratic centralism, with, he says, over 4.68 million organisations and more than 91 million members; and a commitment to the Party's self-reform. He contends that no other party has these qualities, which is why history and the people chose it. The commentary cites a survey by a US public relations firm putting Chinese public trust in government at 95%. The third part, citing Xi, Deng Xiaoping and the classics, holds that leadership by the Party is the defining feature and greatest advantage of socialism with Chinese characteristics.

Jiang concludes that, with the world undergoing great changes and domestic development at a critical stage, the Party's leadership must be upheld without wavering. He calls for firm defence of the authority and centralised, unified leadership of the Central Committee with Xi Jinping at its core, applying the Four Consciousnesses, the Four-sphere Confidence and the Two Upholds, and for improving the institutional system of Party leadership and full and rigorous self-governance of the Party. Read the original if you want a compact example of the official People's Daily case for the legitimacy and necessity of Party leadership as it was framed in 2020.
quoteEn: Upholding the leadership of the Communist Party of China is an inevitable outcome of China's historical development in modern times and a rational choice by the Chinese people.
quoteZh: 坚持中国共产党的领导，是近代以来中国历史发展的必然，是中国人民的理性选择。

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central official goal of the Party, presenting China's modern history as a path from national humiliation to renewed national strength, with a target of a modern socialist country by mid-century.
