A Party requirement, formulated in 2018 to 2019, to uphold General Secretary Xi Jinping's core position in the Central Committee and the whole Party, and to uphold the authority and centralised, unified leadership of the Central Committee.
Official formula calling for confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: Slogan for the Party-building and anti-corruption drive carried out since the 18th Party Congress (2012), stressing discipline, ideological education and institutional rules.
The official name for the Party's model of socialism since the reform era, combining Party leadership and public ownership with market mechanisms.
The Leninist organisational principle of the Party, under which decisions are made after discussion, and lower levels obey higher levels and individuals obey the collective.

t: The Chinese people's choice of leadership by the Communist Party of China is entirely correct
zh: 中国人民选择中国共产党领导是完全正确的
paras: This commentary, first published in the People's Daily in August 2020, argues that the Communist Party of China's leadership is not self-proclaimed but the choice of history and of the people. Chen Li contends that history and present reality show this choice to be entirely correct, and that the Party will keep strengthening itself to lead the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

The piece opens with Xi Jinping's statement that Party leadership is the defining feature and greatest strength of socialism with Chinese characteristics. It has two main sections: why the people chose Party leadership, and why that choice will be sustained in future. It draws on the Party's growth from about 50 members to over 91 million, on revolutionary-era episodes and on the post-2012 period.

Chen's central claim is that the Party "comes from the people" and always represents their fundamental interests. Citing the Communist Manifesto, Chen treats representing the majority rather than a minority as what separates Marxist parties from others. Chen then points to the Party's struggles in the revolutionary, construction and new-era periods, to the moral example of figures such as Jiao Yulu, and to popular support in wartime as evidence. Looking ahead, Chen argues that growing international instability and the difficulty of the final stretch toward national rejuvenation make stronger Party leadership necessary.

Chen concludes that, since the 18th Party Congress (2012), the Central Committee with Xi Jinping at its core has upheld full and rigorous self-governance of the Party and the Party's self-reform, which the article says has increased the Party's cohesion and vitality. Chen expects the Party to keep earning popular support and to realise the Chinese Dream. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official Party commentary justifies one-party leadership by appeal to popular choice.
quoteEn: Popular support is the greatest politics, and the future of a political party depends on the people's choice.
quoteZh: 民心是最大的政治，一个政党的前途命运，取决于人民的选择。

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: A slogan associated with Xi Jinping's leadership since 2012, covering discipline, anti-corruption and Party-building measures.
An official formulation for the Party's efforts to correct its own problems and strengthen itself, presented as driving the broader social transformation it leads.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The official national goal of restoring China's strength and international standing, central to Party discourse since the 18th Party Congress.
A slogan Xi Jinping introduced in 2012 that links national rejuvenation with the well-being of the people.
The official name for China's current path and system, which the Party describes as Marxism adapted to Chinese conditions.

t: Striving for the happiness of the Chinese people and the cause of human progress
zh: 为中国人民幸福和人类进步事业而奋斗
paras: This commentary, first published in the People's Daily on 3 September 2020, takes up Xi Jinping's statement that the Communist Party of China is a party that seeks happiness for the Chinese people and also strives for the cause of human progress. Writing amid the global spread of Covid-19 and what it calls a world undergoing changes unseen in a century, Song argues that the Party stands on the right side of history. In the author's account, it does so by building a community with a shared future for mankind, rejecting Cold War thinking and power politics.

The article is organised around five roles it assigns to the Party: a firm practitioner of putting the people and their lives first; a defender of lasting peace and universal security; a practitioner of fairness, justice and responsibility; a promoter of mutual benefit and common development; and a leader in openness, inclusiveness and mutual learning among civilisations. Each section opens with a quotation from Xi Jinping and draws on domestic achievements, foreign policy statements and the reported views of foreign party figures.

Song's central move is to present the Party's domestic record as the basis of its international conduct. The article cites poverty alleviation, the Covid-19 response (including the share of Party members among medical staff sent to Hubei) and a survey reporting 95 per cent public trust in the government. It then describes a foreign policy of peaceful development, dialogue without confrontation, and no hegemony or expansion. It points to the Belt and Road Initiative, which it says is neither a sphere of influence nor a debt trap, and to the sharing of governance experience with foreign parties. It also says China will neither import nor export a model and will not draw lines by ideology. Throughout, Song attributes favourable assessments to foreign party leaders and organisations and contrasts the Party's conduct with that of unnamed states that shift blame or impose sanctions.

Song concludes that, as it approaches its centenary, the Party, guided by Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, will coordinate national rejuvenation with the global changes and work with other parties to build a community with a shared future for mankind. The piece is an official-style statement of how the Party presents its international role in 2020. Read the original if you want a representative example of the Party's own framing of its global responsibilities, including its language on the South China Sea, the pandemic and inter-party relations.
quoteEn: Adhering to a people-centred approach and doing everything for the people has always been the Chinese Communist Party's deepest imprint and most distinctive hallmark.
quoteZh: 坚持以人民为中心、一切为了人民，始终是中国共产党最深刻的烙印和最鲜明的底色。

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept promoted by Xi Jinping since the early 2010s, describing a vision of international cooperation and shared interests. Official texts present it as an alternative to Cold War thinking and power politics.

An infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative launched by Xi Jinping in 2013, linking China with countries across Asia, Africa and Europe. Critics abroad have raised concerns such as debt, which the article rejects.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: The historical turning point for the Chinese nation's march towards great rejuvenation
zh: 中华民族走向伟大复兴的历史转折点
paras: Writing in the People's Daily on 8 September 2020, Qu Qingshan takes up Xi Jinping's speech at the symposium marking the 75th anniversary of victory in the War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression and the World Anti-Fascist War. Qu asks why that war became the turning point from which the Chinese nation moved out of deep modern crisis towards the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. The answer is that the victory rested on four factors, and each offers a lesson for the present.

The piece is a study-and-interpretation commentary on Xi's speech, with one section per factor: spiritual, political, popular and external. Each section opens with a quotation from Xi, then names a reason why China lost earlier wars against foreign invaders, explains how the anti-Japanese war reversed that cause, and ends with a "historical enlightenment" for realising the Chinese Dream. Qu says that studying the speech should strengthen the Four Consciousnesses, the Four-sphere Confidence and the Two Upholds.

Qu argues that the national spirit centred on patriotism was the decisive factor. In Qu's account, earlier defeats came from lack of a unifying ideological force, a corrupt and incompetent ruling group, internal disunity and little international support. The Communist Party's "mainstay" role was the key: it was the first to mobilise against the invasion, and it promoted the anti-Japanese national united front. It also set out a comprehensive resistance line and the strategy of protracted war. Qu cites figures that Party-led forces fought 60 per cent of the Japanese troops and 95 per cent of the puppet troops. The whole nation's resistance, understood as people's war, is presented as the "magic weapon", with 35 million Chinese casualties. Aid from the Soviet Union, the Flying Tigers, Norman Bethune, Dwarkanath Kotnis and John Rabe is described as a necessary external condition, with internal causes primary.

Qu draws four lessons for the present. These are to promote the national spirit of patriotism and the spirit of reform and innovation, and to uphold the Party's overall leadership through the Party's self-reform. They also include keeping the people at the centre and strengthening unity at home and among overseas Chinese, and to follow peaceful development and opening up. The last lesson links this to a community with a shared future for mankind and the Belt and Road Initiative. Read the original if you want an example of how Party-state commentary in 2020 presented the anti-Japanese war's victory and tied its causes to current political tasks.
quoteEn: The reason the War of Resistance against Japan became a historical turning point is that the Communist Party of China played the role of the mainstay.
quoteZh: 抗日战争之所以成为历史转折，是因为中国共产党发挥了中流砥柱作用。

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal of restoring China's national strength and international standing after the "century of humiliation". It is closely tied to Xi Jinping's slogan of the Chinese Dream.
A metaphor for the force that stands firm amid turbulence. Mao Zedong used it of the Communist Party's role in the anti-Japanese war, and Xi Jinping's 2020 speech repeated it.
A Party slogan from 2016 calling on members to maintain political awareness, to think in terms of the big picture, to follow the core and to keep in line with the leadership.
Confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics.
The Party requirement to uphold General Secretary Xi Jinping's core position and to uphold the authority and centralised, unified leadership of the Central Committee.
A term in Xi-era Party discourse for the Party's continuing effort to correct its own problems through internal discipline and rectification.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept for a vision of international relations based on shared interests and cooperation.
China's international infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative, launched by Xi Jinping in 2013.

t: The Communist Party of China is forever heart to heart with the people
zh: 中国共产党永远与人民心连心
paras: This commentary, first published in the People's Daily on 4 September 2020, takes up Xi Jinping's call to uphold a people-centred philosophy of development. Zang argues that this idea is an important part of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. In Zang's account, it shows that the Party was born for the people and has prospered because of them, and that the Party must remain close to them. The article draws on Xi's recent inspection tour of Anhui and on the experience of the COVID-19 epidemic and flood-control work.

The text has three parts. The first treats the people-centred idea as a development of the Marxist view of the people as the subject of history, and as the expression of the Party's fundamental purpose of serving the people wholeheartedly. The second looks at how a tight Party organisational system puts the idea into practice, through the leader, the Party's overall leadership and the strength of Party organisations. The third sets out what each Party member and cadre should do.

In the first part, Zang argues from historical materialism that the masses are the decisive force in history. Citing Marx, Engels, Mao Zedong and Xi, the author holds that the Party's goal is to let all Chinese people live better lives. As evidence, Zang lists achievements since the 18th Party Congress (2012): poverty alleviation, environmental protection, the largest basic medical insurance network in the world, and the anti-corruption campaign against "tigers" and "flies". Zang also cites the epidemic response, including 39 million Party members and cadres on the front line and nearly 400 who died. In the second part, Zang invokes Engels's "On Authority" to argue that a leadership core is essential. Zang calls for the Four Consciousnesses, the Four-sphere Confidence and the Two Upholds, and for stronger Party institutions and grassroots organisations.

Zang concludes that every Party member and cadre must be a firm practitioner of the people-centred idea. The author proposes three requirements: study Xi Jinping Thought so that putting the people first becomes a settled conviction; solve practical problems in employment, education, social security, healthcare, housing, elderly care, food safety and public order; and combat formalism and bureaucratism through political awareness, better work procedures and cadre selection. Read the original if you want a clear example of how the Party press in 2020 linked the people-centred idea to Party organisation and cadre conduct.
quoteEn: The people-centred philosophy of development is an innovative development and a contemporary expression of the Marxist idea of the people as the subject.
quoteZh: 以人民为中心的发展思想，是马克思主义人民主体思想的创新发展、时代表达。

glossary.zh: 以人民为中心的发展思想
glossary.pinyin: yǐ rénmín wéi zhōngxīn de fāzhǎn sīxiǎng
glossary.literal: development thought with the people as the centre
glossary.explanation: A formulation associated with Xi Jinping, holding that development should be for the people, rely on the people and have its results shared by them. It is presented as part of Xi Jinping Thought.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017 and 2018.
The requirement to uphold Xi Jinping's position as the core of the Party Central Committee and the whole Party, and to uphold the Central Committee's authority and centralised, unified leadership.
Confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics.
A Party slogan calling on members to keep in mind political awareness, the big picture, the core and alignment with the leadership.

t: Deeply understanding the lofty pursuit and sense of mission of Communists
zh: 深入理解共产党人的崇高追求和使命担当
paras: This commentary, first published in the People's Daily on 25 August 2020, takes up the formula that Chinese Communists work "for the happiness of the people, the rejuvenation of the nation and the great harmony of the world", quoting Xi Jinping. Zhen Zhanmin argues that this formula sums up the Communists' lofty pursuit, directs the Party's development, shows the justice of its cause and expresses its sense of mission. In Zhen's account, the formula has grown clearer under the test of nearly a hundred years of history.

The piece has three parts. The first reads the Party's history of struggle through the formula. The second sets out why the formula is the source of the Party's drive. The third looks ahead to how the Party should contribute more to human progress in the new era.

In the historical part, Zhen says that, although tasks differed from period to period, the aim stayed constant. The author lists the new-democratic revolution, the socialist revolution, reform and opening up, and the new era since the 18th Party Congress (2012). Zhen also holds that linking China's progress to human progress is a distinctive feature of the Party's course, from the early claim that the Chinese revolution was part of a world revolution to the Belt and Road Initiative and a community with a shared future for mankind. On motivation, Zhen argues that the formula gives correct direction, bestows justice on the Party's struggle and supplies great strength. In this reading it sustains the Party's Four-sphere Confidence and wins support from the Chinese people and progressive forces worldwide.

Zhen calls for three things in the new era. The Party should keep its strategic resolve by grasping the broad trends of world development, despite hegemonism, protectionism and unilateralism. It should concentrate on managing its own affairs well, applying the new development philosophy and modernizing national governance. It should also keep "two overall situations" in view: national rejuvenation and the world's major changes of a kind not seen in a century. Zhen mentions the Covid-19 epidemic and states that the Party will not waver, because this course represents the "right path in the human world". Read the original if you want a compact example of how official Party discourse in 2020 tied the Party's domestic mission to its international claims.
quoteEn: Working for the people's happiness, the nation's rejuvenation and the world's great harmony is both the key to the Chinese Communists' success and experience, and the goal and source of strength for their struggle.
quoteZh: 为人民谋幸福、为民族谋复兴、为世界谋大同，是中国共产党人的成功之道和经验所在，也是中国共产党人拼搏奋斗的目标追求和力量源泉。

glossary.zh: 为人民谋幸福、为民族谋复兴、为世界谋大同
glossary.pinyin: wèi rénmín móu xìngfú, wèi mínzú móu fùxīng, wèi shìjiè móu dàtóng
glossary.en: the happiness of the people, the rejuvenation of the nation and the great harmony of the world
glossary.literal: seek happiness for the people, rejuvenation for the nation, great harmony for the world
glossary.explanation: A formula used by Xi Jinping to summarise the Communist Party's aims. "Great harmony" (datong) draws on a classical Confucian ideal of a harmonious world.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept promoted by Xi Jinping since around 2012. It calls for common development and shared responsibility among states.
An international infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative launched by Xi Jinping in 2013.
Confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics.
A policy framework announced in 2015 stressing innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: The irresistible trend of human historical development
zh: 人类历史发展大势不可阻挡
paras: Writing in People's Daily in August 2020, Zhao Zhouxian and Li Zhijun ask how the world should choose between deeper economic globalization and de-globalization, openness and closure, cooperation and confrontation, mutual benefit and zero-sum games. Their answer is that economic globalization is an irreversible historical trend, that win-win cooperation is the necessary choice for humankind, and that building a community with a shared future for mankind accords with the laws of historical development. The commentary treats the Covid-19 pandemic as accelerating the "great changes unseen in a century" and as sharpening these choices.

The piece has three sections, one for each claim. The first grounds globalization in the international division of labour and in Marx and Engels's thesis in The German Ideology of the shift from history to world history, and it recounts China's rise through opening up. The second takes up the pandemic, "decoupling" and the 1930s Smoot–Hawley tariff. The third sets out China's initiatives, its pandemic assistance and its domestic economic prospects.

The authors argue that the problems troubling some Western countries, such as debt crises, widening wealth gaps and social tensions, are not caused by globalization, so blaming it is both factually wrong and unhelpful. They hold that calls for "economic decoupling" and for relocating industrial chains go against economic law. In their account, global supply and value chains rest on long-accumulated human capital and industrial coordination, so breaking them brings high relocation, training and rebuilding costs and harms producers and consumers alike. They cite the Smoot–Hawley tariff as a historical warning that trade wars deepen depression and do not spare the country that starts them.

The authors present China as a beneficiary of and contributor to globalization. They cite its contribution of around 30% to world growth, a World Bank estimate of benefits from the Belt and Road Initiative, and its pandemic aid and information-sharing. They call for using the huge domestic market to build a new development pattern of "dual circulation", with the domestic cycle as the mainstay, so as to help world recovery and an open world economy. The pandemic response is said to show the advantages of the socialist system with Chinese characteristics. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official Chinese commentary in 2020 framed globalization, decoupling and the community with a shared future for mankind.
quoteEn: Economic globalization was not created artificially, and it will not be reversed by the will of certain people or certain countries.
quoteZh: 经济全球化不是人为造出来的，也不会因某些人、某些国家的意志而逆转。

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept promoted by Xi Jinping since around 2012–13. It stresses interdependence, shared security and development, and multilateral cooperation.
A Chinese initiative launched in 2013 to build infrastructure and trade links across Eurasia, Africa and beyond.

glossary.pinyin: bǎi nián wèi yǒu zhī dà biànjú
glossary.en: great changes unseen in a century
glossary.explanation: A phrase used by Xi Jinping to describe a period of shifting global power and rapid change, often tied to China's rise and Western relative decline.
A development strategy announced in 2020. It makes the domestic economic cycle the mainstay while domestic and international cycles reinforce each other.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: Using high-efficiency governance to advance high-quality development
zh: 以高效能治理助推高质量发展
paras: Writing in Economic Daily in June 2020, Gu Baoguo takes up Xi Jinping's remarks to the Inner Mongolia delegation at that year's National People's Congress session. In them Xi called for major plans, reforms and policies that "pull" high-quality development and high-efficiency governance forward. Gu's thesis is that the two are closely linked and that high-efficiency governance should be used to drive high-quality development. The piece is a short commentary, not a research article.

The article has two parts. The first sets out why high-quality development needs governance as its basis. It draws on the Fourth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2019) and on the gaps Gu sees in government capacity. The second part, written against the shock of the COVID-19 epidemic, describes how governance can be built into the whole process of development. It does so along four dimensions: governing goals, governing actors, governing methods and governing content.

Gu argues that the shift from high-speed growth to high-quality development requires turning institutional strengths into governance effectiveness. He lists problems he sees in government: blurred boundaries between government and market, excessive administrative intervention, weak regulation, and insufficient policy transparency and coordination. He calls for less direct government interference in resource allocation, pricing and market entry and exit, and for stronger public services and market supervision. On the four dimensions, he points to a timetable for modernizing the governance system by 2035 and by the centenary of the People's Republic. He describes interaction between central top-level design and local experimentation, and coordinated governance under Party leadership with government, enterprises, social organisations and individuals acting together. He also stresses systems thinking in which economic reform leads and other reforms follow.

Gu concludes that the epidemic has exposed weak points, such as public health emergency management, and that pressure should be turned into motivation. He says taking the initiative in deepening reform will make China's governance system more complete and its governance capacity stronger. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-state commentary in 2020 linked the governance modernization agenda to the economic goal of high-quality development.
quoteEn: High-efficiency governance is not only an effective guarantee of high-quality development but also its foundational support.
quoteZh: 高效能治理不仅是高质量发展的有效保障，也是高质量发展的基础支撑。

glossary.explanation: An official policy goal, prominent since 2017, that shifts emphasis from the speed of economic growth to its quality, efficiency and sustainability.

A phrase used by Xi Jinping in 2020 for governance that turns institutional advantages into practical results. It is closely tied to the idea of modernizing the national governance system and capacity.

t: The scientific form of Marx's philosophy
zh: 马克思哲学的科学形式
paras: Wang Shizhong asks how Marx's philosophy, read as a philosophy of practice, can be given a scientific form. Since the early 2000s, the article notes, some scholars have reinterpreted Marxist philosophy from a practice-philosophy standpoint, drawing on Chinese, Western and Marxist resources. Wang argues that practice can only escape the shadow of theoretical philosophy if it is expressed in the form of science.

The short piece, first published in a newspaper in 2020, moves through three steps: the case for scientific form, the relation between natural science, social science and economics, and a proposed structure. Along the way it draws on Hegel, Benedetto Croce, the Austrian economist Carl Menger and game-theoretic institutional economics.

Wang's central move is a method of 'reverse forcing' (fǎnxiàng dàobī). It examines the internal limits of natural science and then of social science, to find where a scientific form of Marx's philosophy must begin. Such a form must be refutable and correctable, and must point toward a 'community of free individuals'. In Wang's account, economics cannot supply it: economics without history faces a crisis of legitimacy, and economics with history faces a crisis of scientific standing. Hegel's dialectic is a further breakthrough, but Wang follows Croce in finding it flawed. Croce's own closed 'circuit' structure is judged too closed.

Wang proposes revising Croce's structure into an open 'double-layer, three-dimensional' one. The two layers are theoretical and practical activity. The practical layer has higher and lower levels. The openness leaves room for human freedom where theory falls short. Wang offers this as an interpretive framework and an operable scientific scheme for Marx's philosophy. Read the original if you want a compact sketch of one Chinese attempt to link practice philosophy, the philosophy of science and the dialectical tradition.
quoteEn: Hence "science" must serve as the theoretical form that represents "practice", rather than remaining within a "philosophical" interpretation of practice.
quoteZh: 故要以“科学”作为表征“实践”的理论形式，而不能停留在关于实践的“哲学”阐释之中。

t: The contemporary expression of the consciousness of hope in Marxist philosophy
zh: 马克思主义哲学希望意识的当代表达
paras: Writing in the Chinese Social Sciences Today (2020), Kuang Sanping asks how Marxist philosophy grounds its orientation towards the future. The author argues that, unlike earlier philosophies that only interpret the world, Marxism seeks to change it through practice. It therefore carries a strong future-oriented outlook and a consciousness of hope, which Kuang presents as a scientific expression of the future aspirations of the proletariat and of humanity.

The short piece has four parts: the dual existence of the human being, the unity of lawfulness and purposiveness, hope in practical activity, and the Chinese Dream as a contemporary expression of this consciousness. It draws on Marx's remarks on human beings, labour and history, and contrasts Marx with Hegel and Feuerbach.

Kuang's central claim is that humans exist both as natural beings bound by external measures and as self-conscious beings guided by internal measures of purpose and need. Practice, as the author describes it, affirms given reality while sublating it, moving people from what is to what ought to be. Marx's history is neither mechanical determinism nor mere spirit: it joins an account of objective laws with an account of human purposes. Speculative or merely intuitive approaches, in Kuang's reading, cannot form a clear concept of the future.

Kuang concludes that Xi Jinping, in proposing the Chinese Dream of the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, has given Marxist hope a contemporary expression. The author reads the Dream as historical, realistic and oriented to the future, and as enriching Marxism's scientific doctrine of the future. Read the original if you want a brief example of how Chinese commentary links Marxist philosophy of practice to official Party slogans.
quoteEn: From the day it was born, Marxist philosophy has consistently insisted on starting from real activity in order to examine history practically.
quoteZh: 马克思主义哲学从其诞生之日起，始终坚持从现实的活动出发去实践地考察历史

glossary.explanation: A slogan put forward by Xi Jinping in 2012 for national rejuvenation, prosperity and people's well-being.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A long-term Party goal of restoring China's national strength and standing after what it describes as a century of humiliation.

t: The strength of China's institutional advantages shown in the fight against the epidemic
zh: 我国制度优势在抗击疫情中的力量彰显
paras: Writing in the People's Daily on 19 June 2020, Qu Qingshan takes up what China's handling of COVID-19 reveals about its political system. Qu contrasts China's containment of the outbreak, which the article describes as a major strategic success within about three months in Wuhan and Hubei, with the continuing spread of the disease in some Western countries, above all the United States. The article's answer is that the epidemic response demonstrated the distinctive advantages of China's system and justifies the Four-sphere Confidence.

The piece is a short commentary organised around seven "forces" that Qu says the epidemic made visible, each tied to a role: leadership (the key role), ideas (the guiding role), the state (the foundational role), the people (the decisive role) and morality (the motivating role). It then adds the rule of law, which it says provides a safeguard, and science and technology, which it says provide support. It closes with a brief acknowledgement of weaknesses and a statement of confidence.

Qu's central claim is that the Party's centralised, unified leadership is the essence and greatest strength of socialism with Chinese characteristics. The article credits General Secretary Xi Jinping's directives, presented as a guiding body of ideas, with setting goals and strategy, including a "people's war" approach and the priority on Hubei and Wuhan. For the state's capacity to concentrate resources, Qu cites the Huoshenshan and Leishenshan hospitals built in 10 and 12 days, 346 medical teams with 42,600 personnel, 162.4 billion yuan in fiscal funds as of 31 May, and state payment of patients' treatment costs. The people's sacrifice, especially the more than two months of home isolation in Hubei, and the volunteer and moral mobilisation are presented as decisive. Qu repeatedly sets this against what the article calls confused decisions and ineffective measures in the United States and other Western countries.

Qu concedes that the epidemic exposed shortcomings in major-epidemic control mechanisms and public health emergency management. Qu calls for remedying them while advancing the modernization of the national governance system and capacity, so that institutional advantages become governance effectiveness. The article concludes that the Chinese system is the most promising, efficient, reliable and beneficial for its people in the world. Read the original if you want a representative official Party-press account, from mid-2020, of how the epidemic response was used to argue for institutional confidence.
quoteEn: A great epidemic brings a great examination, and a great examination prompts reflection.
quoteZh: 大疫带来大考，大考引发思考。

glossary.explanation: Official formula, associated with Xi Jinping, calling for confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics.
The official name of China's model of socialism since the reform era, combining Party leadership with a socialist market economy.
A concept from Mao Zedong's military thought, relying on mass mobilisation. Here it is applied to the epidemic response.

glossary.zh: 国家治理体系和治理能力现代化
glossary.pinyin: guójiā zhìlǐ tǐxì hé zhìlǐ nénglì xiàndàihuà
glossary.en: modernization of the national governance system and capacity
glossary.explanation: A goal set out at the Third Plenum of the 18th Central Committee (2013) to improve institutions and the ability to run the country.

t: How was the socialist system with Chinese characteristics arrived at?
zh: 中国特色社会主义制度是怎么得来的？
paras: Writing after the Fourth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2019), which for the first time in Party history devoted a session to upholding and improving the socialist system with Chinese characteristics and modernizing national governance, Li Junru asks where that system came from. The article's answer is that it is a scientific institutional system formed through more than a century of practical exploration and ideological struggle by the Party and the people. Li presents this as the necessary starting point for any effort to uphold and improve it.

The article has four parts. It first stresses how hard-won the system was, from failed attempts to copy Western constitutional monarchy, multiparty and presidential models to a series of doctrinal debates. It then describes the system's scientific character, traces its establishment, reform and improvement from 1949 to the Fourth Plenum's three-stage goals, and closes with lessons about its vitality. Li draws heavily on Xi Jinping's speeches and on Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping.

Li argues that the system is scientific in three senses. It applies Marxism, in particular historical materialism, to Chinese conditions. It is an interlocking set of institutions, which the plenum grouped into 13 areas, with Party leadership as the most essential feature. It is also rooted in Chinese soil and culture, so Li rejects judging or redesigning Chinese institutions by US or European 'models' and cites consultative democracy as drawing on Chinese political culture. Li's historical account runs from the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference and the people's congress system, through Deng Xiaoping's call for institutional reform and the socialist market economy, to the 18th Party Congress (2012) and its push for 'more mature and more defined' institutions.

Li concludes that the system has stayed robust because it renews itself, and names four sources of that vitality. These are Party leadership, the people as masters of the country, seeking truth from facts, and democratic centralism. Li says democratic centralism has produced a governance system that is neither liberal nor 'new authoritarian'. Read the original if you want an official Party-theorist account of how the institutional system is supposed to have been formed and why it is said to be durable.
quoteEn: The socialist system with Chinese characteristics is a system of institutions and governance rooted in Chinese soil, with deep foundations in Chinese culture and strong popular support. It is a scientific institutional system with historical roots, cultural depth and a social base.
quoteZh: 中国特色社会主义制度是植根中国大地、具有深厚中华文化根基、深得人民拥护的制度和治理体系，是有历史根基、文化底蕴和社会基础的科学的制度体系。

glossary.zh: 国家治理体系和治理能力现代化
glossary.pinyin: guójiā zhìlǐ tǐxì hé zhìlǐ nénglì xiàndàihuà
glossary.literal: modernization of the national governance system and governance capacity
glossary.explanation: A goal first formulated at the Third Plenum of the 18th Central Committee in 2013. It covers improving institutions and the Party-state's capacity to manage the economy, politics, society and culture.
The organisational principle of the Communist Party, combining discussion with unified decision and discipline. The article extends it to the state governance system.
A principle of the Party's ideological line, associated with Mao Zedong and revived under Deng Xiaoping. It calls for policy to start from practical reality.

t: Accelerating the construction of a philosophy and social science system with Chinese characteristics
zh: 加快构建中国特色哲学社会科学体系
paras: This short commentary, first published in People's Daily on 29 June 2020, asks how universities should help build a philosophy and social science system with Chinese characteristics. He argues that, since the 18th Party Congress (2012), the Party Central Committee has made this a strategic task. Universities, in He's view, should use their strengths and "uphold fundamental principles while innovating" to speed up building its three components: the disciplinary system, the academic system and the discourse system.

The piece is organised under three headings: setting the main tone, taking root in the main arena, and making the key moves. It draws heavily on Xi Jinping's statements about the Party's leadership of philosophy and social science, the field's role in governance, and its weak international voice.

He contends that the task is not only theoretical and educational but above all political and strategic. It therefore requires Party leadership, the guiding position of Marxism and Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. He says that research must be rooted in China's circumstances, serve the Party's governance, and draw on traditional Chinese culture. Three priorities follow: deeper study of Xi Jinping Thought, including its entry into textbooks, classrooms and minds; telling China's story so that Chinese scholarship "goes global"; and using philosophy and social science to educate students and give ideological and value guidance.

He concludes that universities must place this work within the "two overall situations" and the "Two Centenary Goals", and respond to the demands of the times. Read the original if you want a concise example of how the official line on universities' role in the Chinese philosophy and social science system was framed in 2020.
quoteEn: Universities must grasp the main tone and fight a proactive battle.
quoteZh: 要把握主基调、打好主动仗。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018. It is presented officially as the latest stage in adapting Marxism to China.
Official goals of building a moderately prosperous society by the Party's centenary (2021) and a modern socialist country by the People's Republic's centenary (2049).
A formula referring to the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation and to profound changes unseen in a century in the world.

t: Constructing a Chinese discourse of Marxist philosophy
zh: 构建马克思主义哲学的中国话语
paras: Ding Kuangyi takes up the question of how to build a Chinese discourse of contemporary Marxist philosophy, which the author treats as a matter of the locality and autonomy of Chinese philosophy and social science. The article argues that such a discourse is more than translating, interpreting or spreading Marxist philosophy in China. Its legitimacy rests on grasping China's developing reality from a basic Marxist standpoint, and it is marked by Chinese problem-awareness, home-grown concepts, explanatory propositions and systematic reflection.
Originally a short newspaper piece (Chinese Social Sciences Today, May 2020), the article organises its argument around three preconditions: the dimensions of text, space and time.

On text, Ding warns against both naive common-sense experience and over-conceptualisation, and holds that Western social science, built on Western conditions, cannot simply be applied to China. Classical Marxist texts should illuminate reality, with Western Marxism and critiques of modernity serving as reference points rather than analogies. On space, Ding rejects treating China as a case of some universal pattern, arguing that the "universal" is itself another local, Westernised extension. China's particularity is a primary resource for concepts, and its geopolitical position across land, sea and space must be considered. On time, Ding rejects linear time from pre-modern to modern in favour of concentric time, in which tradition permeates the present and the present contains anticipation of the future. Ding reads sublation as carrying the past within the present and into the future.

Ding concludes that working along these three dimensions, and forming problem-awareness, concepts and propositions that fit them, is the normative standard and necessary preparation for building this discourse. Read the original if you want a brief philosophical statement of how a Chinese Marxist philosopher frames the case for a locally grounded discourse.
quoteEn: China's particularity and locality are themselves the fundamental resource for generating problem-awareness and shaping concepts and propositions.
quoteZh: 中国的特殊性与地方性之本身即是生成问题意识、形塑概念与命题的根本资源。

glossary.explanation: The translation of Hegel's Aufhebung, adopted by Marx: a process that negates, preserves and lifts earlier elements into a higher stage. Ding reads it as carrying tradition into the present and future, not just critical inheritance.

t: Better coordinating Covid-19 prevention and control with economic and social development
zh: 更好统筹疫情防控和经济社会发展
paras: This commentary, first published in the People's Daily on 7 July 2020, asks how China should better coordinate epidemic prevention and control with economic and social development. Jia Lizheng argues that the Party's leadership has already produced major strategic results in the epidemic fight, and that consolidating them requires understanding several pairs of relationships through materialist dialectics. The stated aim is to secure the goals of finishing the building of a moderately prosperous society and winning the battle against poverty.

The article is organised around five relationships: contingency and necessity; internal and external factors; reform, development and stability; the immediate and the long term; and crisis and opportunity. Each section combines a philosophical principle with directives drawn from Xi Jinping's statements and current policy language. The closing section turns to lessons for national governance and to industrial upgrading.

Jia presents the epidemic as a contingent shock set against the necessary, pre-set goals of a moderately prosperous society and poverty alleviation, which no accidental factor should be allowed to block. Internal and external risks are said to reinforce one another, so that small risks can grow into systemic ones. In this context the author calls for the Two Upholds, a 'one national chessboard' outlook and a conversion of institutional strengths into governance effectiveness. On reform, development and stability, Jia endorses the general tone of seeking progress while maintaining stability, the 'six stabilities' and 'six guarantees', and the expansion of domestic demand. The author insists that the epidemic's impact is short-term and broadly controllable, and that China's long-term positive economic trend is unchanged.

Jia concludes that the epidemic is a major test of China's governance system and capacity. The author calls for closing gaps in public health emergency management, strengthening the legal safeguards for public health, reforming disease control and treatment systems, and improving medical insurance and emergency supplies. Jia also urges deeper reform to create a better institutional environment for new technologies and business models, and to nurture new growth points in areas such as smart manufacturing, online consumption and the contactless economy. Read the original if you want a compact example of how official commentary in mid-2020 framed pandemic response through dialectical categories and the language of the 'two overall situations'.
quoteEn: Crises can be overcome and turned into opportunities.
quoteZh: 危机就能够被克服并转化为机遇。

glossary.explanation: A Party formula, adopted in 2018–2019, calling on members to uphold Xi Jinping's position as the core of the Central Committee and the Party as a whole, and to uphold the Central Committee's authority and unified leadership.

glossary.literal: the whole country as one game of chess
glossary.explanation: A slogan stressing nationwide coordination under central direction, with all regions and sectors acting in concert towards common goals.
A set of economic policy priorities introduced in 2018: stable employment, finance, foreign trade, foreign investment, domestic investment and expectations.

Priorities set out in April 2020 in response to the epidemic: ensuring employment, basic living needs, market entities, food and energy security, stable industrial and supply chains, and grassroots operations.
The Party's goal, set for completion by 2020, of raising living standards across the country to a moderate level of well-being.

glossary.zh: 世界百年未有之大变局
glossary.pinyin: shìjiè bǎinián wèiyǒu zhī dà biànjú
glossary.literal: two big pictures (the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation and the great changes unseen in a century)
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's formula asking officials to keep in view both the strategic overall picture of national rejuvenation and the profound changes in the world order.

t: Why Marxism was able to take root in China
zh: 马克思主义为什么能在中国落地生根
paras: Why did Marxism, which arose in the West, take root in China rather than in the other countries where communist parties emerged after the First World War? Luo Pinghan, in a short historical commentary first published in Guangming Daily in 2020, argues that the answer lies in several factors. Marxism's own scientific rigour, the failure of earlier Western-inspired paths, the example of the October Revolution and China's particular cultural tradition all contributed.

The article proceeds chronologically in three parts. It first traces how Chinese reformers after 1840 moved from the Self-Strengthening Movement to constitutional monarchy and then to republicanism, and how each effort failed to achieve national independence. It then turns to the early, scattered introduction of Marxism and to the effect of the October Revolution, the Paris Peace Conference and Soviet renunciation of tsarist privileges. Finally, it describes how pioneers such as Li Dazhao and Chen Duxiu spread Marxism and founded study societies and early Communist organisations from 1920.

Luo's central claim is that the October Revolution turned Marxism from a theoretical design into a working social system. In Luo's account, this set it apart from other socialist doctrines that had reached China as armchair speculation. Testimony from Mao Zedong, Liu Shaoqi, Qu Qiubai and Lin Boqu is used to show that reformers disillusioned with capitalism turned to Russia and then to Marxism. Luo adds a cultural explanation, citing Ai Siqi and Wu Yuzhang: the ancient ideal of a 'great harmony' (datong) society made Marxism feel familiar to many Chinese and activated an existing aspiration. On this reading, Marxism became rooted in China as a result of both Chinese conditions and its scientific character.

Luo concludes that Marxism belongs to all humanity, not only to the West. Luo argues that successive generations' firm belief in it allowed it to take root and bear fruit. Luo credits it with leading the Communist Party in what the article calls an unprecedented development miracle, and quotes Xi Jinping on the Party's emergence. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned account of how Party historiography explains the early reception of Marxism in China, with period testimonies from founding figures.
quoteEn: The October Revolution turned Marxism from a theoretical conception into the building of an actual social system, opening a wholly new path of development for human society.
quoteZh: 十月革命把马克思主义从一种理论设想变成了现实社会制度构建，开创了人类社会崭新的发展道路。

glossary.explanation: An ideal of a world in which 'all under heaven is shared' (天下为公), drawn from classical Confucian texts. The article, following Ai Siqi, links it to the reception of communism in China.

t: Breaking through the worldwide problem of consolidating the socialist system
zh: 突破社会主义制度定型的世界性难题
paras: Writing after the Fourth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2019), Hou Huiqin argues that setting out the overall composition of the system of socialism with Chinese characteristics is a pioneering step in the history of the world socialist movement. In Hou's account, the October Revolution turned socialism from a movement into a state system but did not complete that transition, and after the Soviet and East European upheavals the task of consolidating and perfecting a socialist state system fell to the Communist Party of China. The article holds that the Party has achieved a historic breakthrough on this worldwide problem.

The short commentary is organised under two headings. The first concerns a bottom-line approach that sets untouchable red lines while actively tackling the difficulties of institutional consolidation. The second concerns grasping the trend of the times, advancing reform and opening up, and turning institutional strengths into effective governance.

Hou first argues that Mao Zedong's generation fixed two principles after the socialist transformations: contradictions persist but are non-antagonistic, and Party leadership is the core of the state system. These, Hou says, guard against subversive errors and "colour revolution". Second, Hou holds that the Party resolved the tension between lofty communist ideals and the realism of institutional interests by adhering to dialectical materialism, through three innovations and the Party's self-reform, summarised as "five ones". Third, Hou traces post-1978 consensus on the system's strengths and flaws, citing Deng Xiaoping on concentrating resources and on the plan–market relation.

Hou concludes that since the 18th Party Congress (2012) institution-building has been comprehensive innovation, whose soul is integrating Party leadership into the modern state system and governance, in contrast to Western multiparty models. Reform and opening up, in this view, is now internal to socialism with Chinese characteristics. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how a Party theorist framed institutional consolidation after the 2019 plenum.
quoteEn: The soul of this institutional innovation is to integrate adherence to Party leadership fully into the building of the modern state system and the system of national governance, constructing a governance model entirely different from Western multiparty systems.
quoteZh: 这一制度创新的灵魂，就是把坚持党的领导全面融入现代国家制度和国家治理体系建设之中，构建与西方多党制截然不同的国家治理模式。

glossary.explanation: The official name for the Chinese Communist Party's path, theory and system of socialism since the reform era, associated with Deng Xiaoping.
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched in 1978 under Deng Xiaoping.
An official formulation, stressed under Xi Jinping, for the Party's continuing efforts to discipline and renew itself, including anti-corruption work.
Official term for popular uprisings in post-Soviet and other states that Chinese authorities describe as externally encouraged attempts at regime change.

t: The scientific meaning and mutual relations of the disciplinary system, the academic system and the discourse system
zh: 学科体系、学术体系、话语体系的科学内涵与相互关系
paras: Tian Xinming addresses a question raised by Xi Jinping's call to build a philosophy and social science with Chinese characteristics: why this project is framed as three systems (disciplinary, academic and discourse), and how they relate. The article, first published in Guangming Daily in May 2020, argues that the three form a dialectical unity. The disciplinary system is a unity of many disciplines, while the academic and discourse systems are inseparable yet distinct aspects of each discipline.

The piece has three numbered sections. The first treats the disciplinary system and its basis in the objective world. The second takes up the academic and discourse systems and why they cannot be separated. The third explains why building each still needs to be set as its own task. Tian draws mainly on Mao Zedong's On Contradiction, Marx's 1859 Preface to A Contribution to the Critique of Political Economy, Engels on terminology in Capital, Lenin on "experience", and Xi Jinping's 2016 symposium remarks.

In Tian's account, disciplines are distinguished by the particularity of the contradictions in their objects, and linked by the universality those objects contain. This produces a layered system, with history as one example, containing Chinese history, world history and archaeology. Within each discipline, systematic theory forms the academic system and systematic concepts form the discourse system. Concepts are the "cell of thought" and the form of rational knowledge, so the discourse system is the linguistic carrier of the academic system. Tian then argues that the two are a unity of opposites. They develop at different speeds, as with Marx's materialist conception of history, which took shape in the 1840s but received its mature conceptual form only later. The same word can also carry different meanings in different schools. Struggle between theoretical systems therefore appears as a contest over discourse power as well as over content.

Tian concludes that building the academic system cannot stand in for building the discourse system, so the latter must be set as a separate task, and the two should advance together. Upholding Marxism as the guiding principle, Tian says, includes upholding its discourse system, clearing up terminological confusion, guarding against discourse infiltration and hegemony, and crafting distinctive concepts that international audiences can understand. Tian also notes that the disciplinary system is basically established but weak in emerging and interdisciplinary fields, and calls for stronger top-level design. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how Chinese theorists justify the "three systems" formula in Marxist philosophical terms.
quoteEn: The academic system is the systematic theory and knowledge that reveals the essence and laws of a discipline's object; the discourse system is the verbal expression of that theory and knowledge, the form in which the academic system appears and its linguistic vehicle.
quoteZh: 学术体系是揭示本学科对象的本质和规律的成体系的理论和知识；话语体系是理论和知识的语词表达，是学术体系的表现形式和语言载体。

glossary.explanation: The capacity to set the terms, concepts and narratives of debate. In Chinese official usage it is often tied to competition with Western academic and ideological influence.

glossary.zh: 中国特色哲学社会科学
glossary.en: philosophy and social science with Chinese characteristics
glossary.explanation: The project, promoted since Xi Jinping's May 2016 symposium, of building Chinese-grounded humanities and social sciences under Marxist guidance, drawing on Chinese tradition and foreign scholarship.
In this article, the system of concepts, categories and propositions through which a discipline expresses its theory.

keywords: philosophy and social science with Chinese characteristics

t: The internal tensions among the three forms of morality and their adjustment
zh: 道德三重样态的内在张力及其调适
source: Studies on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics, 2020 no. 2
paras: Liu Ailing asks how the conflicts inside morality can be resolved once morality is divided by the relation between subject and object. Working from historical materialism, the article distinguishes three "forms" (yangtai) of morality: the individual morality of persons, the political morality of administrative actors, and the public morality of the community. Liu argues that the three are relatively independent, fluid and internally determined, so they interact through contradiction and contest. Adjusting these tensions, in Liu's view, is the way to build a dynamic moral picture in which the three forms reorganise one another and reinforce each other.

The article has three parts. The first links the three social subjects (individual, social and political persons) to three moral forms: individual morality as self-respect, will and reason; political morality as justice, legality and altruism; public morality as publicness, responsibility and self-evident axioms. The second part identifies three tensions. The third proposes remedies at the level of subject and object, of moral fields, and of institutional mechanisms. Liu draws on Marx and Engels, Kant and other ethical writers, and uses examples such as epidemic quarantine, environmental protection, the Heinz dilemma and a Shandong criminal case.

Liu's central argument is that each tension arises from a mismatch of standards. Individual self-interest clashes with the "good of the community", for example when quarantine requires individuals to yield freedom, or when social responsibility is shifted onto individuals. Administrators' self-assessment diverges from the more idealistic public evaluation, and routine rules can conflict with emergency action, as in a Hubei city that locked down early during the COVID-19 outbreak. Individual free will meets the compulsion of law and political morality. Liu holds that these are resolved by "mutual construction": a cycle in which individual, political and social good support one another, and unity of moral consciousness, conduct and effect.

Liu proposes building a moral community in which individual, social and administrative responsibilities coexist, and in which individual values, public morality and political institutions reinforce one another. Concrete measures include legislation and evaluation standards for political morality, the exemplary role of moral models in the new era, and a reflective mechanism that adjusts policy by the test of whether the people are satisfied. Liu stresses attention to vulnerable groups and to special periods. Read the original if you are interested in how Chinese scholars of ideological and political education apply Marxist ethics to public morality, official conduct and epidemic-era governance.
quoteEn: Adjusting the internal tensions among the three forms of morality is an effective path to dissolving the contradictions among them and building a dynamic moral picture of mutual reorganisation, interaction and reinforcement.
quoteZh: 道德三重样态内在张力的调适，是消解三者间矛盾，构建交互重组、相互作用、彼此促进的道德动态图景的有效路径。

t: The responsibility logic and structural system of modernizing government governance
zh: 政府治理现代化的责任逻辑与结构体系
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in January 2020, Zhang Xianming takes up the task set by the Fourth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2019): to uphold and improve the administrative system with Chinese characteristics and build a government governance system with clear responsibilities and administration according to law. Zhang treats the modernization of government governance as a key link in modernizing national governance. The article argues that two things must be worked out together: the logic of responsibility, and the structural system of government.

The piece is a short newspaper commentary in two parts. The first part deals with how responsibility is assigned and how it is realized. The second part sets out three directions for optimizing the structure of the administrative system. It draws on Party documents, including the report to the 19th Party Congress (2017), rather than on case studies or foreign literature.

On responsibility, Zhang holds that whether a government is accountable to the people marks the difference between traditional and modern government. Responsibility should be assigned scientifically. It combines political, legal and moral responsibility. Powers should be fixed according to responsibilities (以责确权), with powers and responsibilities matched, and duties should be allocated vertically between central, local and grassroots levels and horizontally between departments. Realizing responsibility depends on supervision, meaning a network of oversight bodies and open, transparent politics, and on accountability mechanisms. Those mechanisms should cover the whole chain from decision to execution to result and be paired with a tolerance-for-error mechanism. On structure, Zhang calls for three steps: keep the direction of administrative reform under Party leadership while drawing on world experience; ease the tensions between vertical and horizontal lines of authority, and clarify the government's relations with society and the market; and activate the system's elements by giving local governments more autonomy and by integrating big data, the internet and artificial intelligence into administration.

Zhang concludes that a modern government system needs a complete structure, smooth operation and effective coordination. The author insists that national governance in China differs from "governance" in the Western sense, because it mobilizes plural actors under the overall arrangement of the Party and state. The stated aim is a situation in which national governance has strength, social governance has precision and grassroots governance has warmth. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how an official-academic voice in 2020 linked accountability, supervision and administrative restructuring to the Fourth Plenum's governance agenda.
quoteEn: Whether a government can be responsible to the people is the mark that distinguishes traditional government from modern government.
quoteZh: 政府能否对人民负责任是区分传统政府与现代政府的标志

glossary.explanation: A principle that a government's powers should be granted to match the responsibilities listed for it, so that responsibility comes before power. The article sets it against the older model of the regulatory (管制型) government.
A basic principle of Chinese public administration that an organ's authority should correspond to its duties, so that it neither fails to act nor oversteps.
A policy of tolerating certain mistakes made by officials in the course of reform, intended to encourage them to take initiative while accountability is still enforced.

glossary.en: vertical and horizontal lines of authority
glossary.explanation: The relationship between functional departments that run top-down through the levels of government (条) and the territorial governments at each level (块). The article says tensions here produce organizational conflict and bloat.

t: Study and promote the revolutionary spirit, and take a clear stand against historical nihilism
zh: 研究和弘扬革命精神 旗帜鲜明反对历史虚无主义
paras: This short commentary, first published in Guangming Daily on 5 February 2020, argues that studying, inheriting and promoting the revolutionary spirit of the Communist Party of China is an important part of the struggle against historical nihilism. Li Youxin holds that, besides exposing and refuting nihilist claims, this work must be supported by historical materialism and by concrete, vivid research results.

The article is organised around four forms of historical nihilism, each of which Li says calls for a response grounded in the revolutionary spirit: the nihilism that dismisses revolution, that dismisses heroes, that dismisses ideals, and that rejects the Party's leadership.

On the first, Li describes claims that the revolution was the product of radicalism, calls to "bid farewell to revolution", and the pitting of a "modernization perspective" against a "revolutionary perspective". The author argues that research into the historical detail of revolutionary spirit shows the necessity of China's revolutionary road. On heroes, Li points to online mockery, abuse of martyrs and pseudo-academic claims that heroes were "false models"; the answer, Li says, is legal protection plus study of heroes as embodiments of revolutionary spirit. On ideals, Li contends that denying the revolution amounts to denying the social ideal it pursued and the historical necessity of choosing Marxism and socialism. Li also maintains that hostile forces at home and abroad attack revolutionary history to undermine the Party's leadership.

Li concludes that revolutionary spirit is a lasting source of strength for the Party, and calls on readers to carry on the "red gene", strengthen ideals and convictions, and take up the task of the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want a compact example of how a 2020 Party-oriented commentary links the campaign against historical nihilism to the study of revolutionary spirit.
quoteEn: Studying, inheriting and promoting the revolutionary spirit of the Communist Party of China is not only an indispensable part of the struggle against historical nihilism, but also a powerful spiritual force for uniting people and overcoming difficulties in the new era.
quoteZh: 研究、继承和弘扬中国共产党革命精神，不仅是与历史虚无主义进行斗争不可或缺的重要内容，同时也是在新时代凝聚人心、战胜困难的强大精神力量。

glossary.explanation: In Chinese Party discourse, a label for views seen as denying or belittling the Party's revolutionary history, its leaders and heroes, and the socialist path. Official texts treat it as an ideological threat.
The set of ideals, virtues and fighting traditions the Party says were formed during the Chinese revolution. It is promoted as a source of continuing moral and political strength.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central official goal, presented as restoring China's national strength and standing. It is closely associated with the Chinese Dream.

t: Accelerating the construction of a discourse system of philosophy and social sciences with Chinese characteristics
zh: 加快构建中国特色哲学社会科学话语体系
paras: Writing in Red Flag Manuscripts in late 2019, on the 70th anniversary of the People's Republic, Jin Nuo argues that the weakness of China's international discourse power has become a pressing shortcoming as the country moves from 'standing up' and 'becoming rich' to 'becoming strong'. The article's thesis is that the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation requires a philosophy and social sciences discourse system with Chinese characteristics, and that raising China's international voice depends on building it quickly.

The article is organised in three parts. The first sets out why philosophy and social sciences must take on this responsibility. The second lists the basic principles to follow: Marxist guidance, the Four-sphere Confidence, and solid academic research. The third turns to the breakthroughs needed: grounding work in Chinese practice and pursuing original discourse. Each part is paired with a section on Renmin University of China, where the author writes from an institutional standpoint, presenting the university's history and duties.

Jin builds on Xi Jinping's remark that China has solved the problems of being beaten and starved but not yet of being 'abused', that is, of being misrepresented by Western powers using their own institutional models and value standards. On this reading, a flourishing philosophy and social sciences both marks national strength and carries international discourse power. The author holds that Marxism is what distinguishes contemporary Chinese scholarship, that confidence in China's achievements and culture is its spiritual pillar, and that real discourse power comes from depth of scholarship, not loud volume. Because Western discourse cannot explain Chinese practice, Jin calls for extracting Chinese concepts from reform-era and post-1949 experience and turning the Party's theoretical innovations into academic language. Jin also calls for originality and subjectivity, citing Xi's view that imitation cannot produce a Chinese-style scholarship.

Jin concludes that scholars, think tanks and universities must explain major theoretical and contemporary questions, so that Chinese theory interprets Chinese practice and Chinese practice in turn elevates theory, offering what the article calls Chinese solutions to the world. Renmin University is presented as bearing special responsibility, given its record in Marxist research and its stated aim of being 'satisfactory to the people and world-class'. Read the original if you want to see how a university leader frames discourse power, Marxist guidance and the tasks of Chinese social science in the period around 2019.
quoteEn: Genuine discourse power does not come from a loud voice but from depth of scholarship.
quoteZh: 真正的话语权，不是靠嗓门大，而是在学问深。

glossary.explanation: A formula in Party discourse calling for confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics. It was elaborated under Xi Jinping.

The capacity to set the terms in which a country, its system and its experience are described and judged internationally. Chinese official and academic writing treats it as a component of national strength and soft power.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal of restoring China to national strength and international standing, closely associated with the Chinese Dream.
The official Chinese category covering the humanities and social sciences. It is treated as both a body of knowledge and an ideological field.

t: The fundamental system of upholding Marxism's guiding role in the ideological field
zh: 坚持马克思主义在意识形态领域指导地位的根本制度
paras: Dong Xuewen's commentary, published in Red Flag Manuscripts in early 2020, reads one provision of the Fourth Plenum Decision of the 19th Central Committee (2019): the call to uphold Marxism's guiding role in the ideological field as a "fundamental system". Dong argues that this is a first in the history of Marxist thought and culture and in the Party's own documents. In Dong's account, it is a creative step that institutionalises Marxist guidance and advances the Chinese-adapted Marxist theory of culture.

The piece opens with the Decision as a whole, which Dong credits with setting out the "four pillars and eight beams" of the socialist system with Chinese characteristics and with a roadmap for the modernization of national governance. It then moves through three sections: the novelty of the provision, its institutional and practical force, and its place within governance modernization, with literature and art as the worked example. Dong draws on Xi Jinping's remarks on Marxism and on literature and art throughout.

Dong's central move is a conceptual reading of the terms. Since the Decision distinguishes "important", "basic" and "fundamental" systems, Dong defines a fundamental system as the most important rule of conduct that everyone must follow. Placing Marxist guidance at that level, Dong says, turns a theoretical appeal into an institutional and practical requirement tied to governance capacity. Such a system is rigid, allowing no bargaining or selective compliance, and it guides all other systems. Dong links it to ideological security, to keeping leadership, management and discourse power in Party hands, and to opposing historical nihilism and "two-faced" behaviour. Dong adds that because the system belongs to the category of "modernization", the view that Marxism is outdated is arbitrary and wrong.

Dong concludes that this system is the top priority and the key piece of top-level design in cultural institution-building, and that it must be implemented without lapses. In literature and art, Dong holds, adherence to Marxism is the first standard for telling good from bad and advanced from backward, and it must be a working "pointer" and "weapon" rather than a "mask" or "cosmetic". Read the original if you want an example of how a Party-affiliated theorist interpreted the 2019 Decision's ideological provisions and justified them as institutional design.
quoteEn: The establishment of a \"fundamental system\" raises theoretical formulations and declarations of principle to the level of fundamental institutional arrangements.
quoteZh: “根本制度”的确立，就是把理论表述和理念宣示提升到了根本性的制度安排层面。

glossary.explanation: In the 2019 Decision, the highest of three tiers of institutions (important, basic, fundamental). The author reads it as the most important rule of conduct that all must follow.

glossary.zh: 国家治理体系和治理能力现代化
glossary.pinyin: guójiā zhìlǐ tǐxì hé zhìlǐ nénglì xiàndàihuà
glossary.literal: modernization of the national governance system and governance capacity
glossary.explanation: A goal formulated by the Party in 2013 and elaborated in the 2019 Decision. It concerns improving institutions and the ability to run the state.

glossary.zh: 意识形态领域指导地位
glossary.en: guiding role in the ideological field
glossary.literal: guiding position in the ideological domain
glossary.explanation: The Party's long-standing principle that Marxism is the guiding thought in ideology, culture and academia. The 2019 Decision restated it as a fundamental system.
A term used in Party discourse for views that deny or belittle the official account of Chinese revolutionary and socialist history. Party writers treat it as an ideological threat.

t: Firmly mastering the Marxist way of thinking and way of working
zh: 切实掌握好马克思主义思想方法和工作方法
paras: Writing in Red Flag Manuscripts in 2019, Zhu Jianyi asks how Party members can truly master and apply the Marxist way of thinking and way of working. Starting from Xi Jinping's description of Marxism as a scientific, people-centred, practical and open theory, Zhu argues that this mastery is an important method for advancing the cause of socialism with Chinese characteristics in the new era and for realising the Chinese Dream of national rejuvenation.

The commentary is organised as a series of requirements, each opened by the phrase "always adhere to". They cover the study and use of Marxist philosophy, seeking truth from facts together with scientific thinking and a "nail-driving spirit", and a problem-oriented approach that relies on investigation, research and continuous learning. Zhu draws throughout on Xi Jinping's formulations and on the Party's own record of practice.

Zhu's first move is to make dialectical and historical materialism the cadre's "essential skill". Zhu grounds this in the nature of Marxist philosophy, which is said to unite class character with scientific character and knowing the world with changing it. Zhu calls for study of the classics and for upholding Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era as the Party's guiding ideology. The second move treats seeking truth from facts as the Party's basic method. It is tied to the mass line: the "facts" are those that come "from the masses", and the method must be carried back "to the masses". Zhu lists six modes of thinking to be cultivated: strategic, historical, dialectical, innovative, law-based and bottom-line. The "nail-driving spirit" means following one blueprint to the end and doing each task thoroughly, while stability-seeking progress and strategic resolve keep the course steady. The third move is a problem orientation. Cadres should treat the people's need for a better life as the main problem, investigate in a systematic way ("no investigation, no right to speak"), and study as a learning-oriented Party.

Zhu concludes that the Party should keep learning and practising, following the spiral of knowing, practising and knowing again, and should keep its attention on China's reality and the people's needs. In this way the theory and practice of socialism with Chinese characteristics in the new era would be steadily improved. The text is a hortatory piece of Party ideological education rather than an analytical study. Read the original if you want to see how the Party's official guidance of 2019 framed Marxist method for cadres, including its list of thinking methods and its stress on investigation and study.
quoteEn: Investigation and research have always been our Party's family heirloom, and also the basic skill for doing every kind of work well.
quoteZh: 调查研究一直以来都是我们党的传家宝，也是我们做好各项工作的基本功。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology associated with Xi Jinping, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017 and 2018.
A slogan associated with Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping, treated in Party doctrine as the core of its ideological line, meaning that policy should start from actual conditions.
A phrase popularised by Xi Jinping, urging officials to persist with a plan and carry out each task thoroughly, like driving one nail at a time.
The Party's working method, associated with Mao Zedong, of gathering the views of the people ("from the masses") and returning policy to them ("to the masses").
A slogan introduced by Xi Jinping in 2012 that stands for the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

t: Pushing propaganda and ideological work to grow ever stronger
zh: 推动宣传思想工作不断强起来
paras: This is a themed collection of short statements, published in the Party journal Dangjian in 2019, by heads of central propaganda and cultural institutions. Each reports how their body will study and implement the main points of Xi Jinping's speech at the national conference on propaganda and ideological work. The shared thesis is that the propaganda and ideological front must be guided by Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, reform and innovate, and so provide ideological guarantees and spiritual strength for the Party and the state.

Ten contributors write in turn.
