The piece is organised under three headings. The first presents courageous self-reform as a political gene of Chinese communists. The second treats it as the key to the Party's flesh-and-blood ties with the people. The third calls it the winning weapon for keeping the Party advanced and pure.

Li grounds self-reform in Marxism, described as a critical and revolutionary theory. Materialist dialectics holds that development involves internal contradictions, so a growing party must fight wrong ideas from within as well as from outside. Li adds that not every party applies this law consciously, whereas the Party is presented as a model. On the Party's relationship with the people, Li argues that forgetting the original aspiration would change the Party's nature and cost it popular support. Li therefore calls for tackling formalism, bureaucratism, inaction by officials and harm to the public interest, together with sustained pressure against corruption. Li also stresses accepting public supervision, since the masses judge whether officials have kept their aspiration.

Li concludes that since the 18th Party Congress (2012) full and rigorous self-governance of the Party has achieved notable results, but impurity in politics, thinking, organisation and conduct remains unresolved. Li calls on Party members to face problems squarely, to cut out harmful elements and to build their abilities for the new era. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-press commentary in 2019 linked the campaign to remember the original aspiration to the theme of self-reform.
quoteEn: Courageous self-reform is our Party's winning weapon for keeping its vanguard character and purity forever.
quoteZh: 勇于自我革命是我们党永葆先进性和纯洁性的制胜法宝。

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.literal: comprehensively and strictly governing the Party
glossary.explanation: A Party-building strategy emphasised since the 18th Party Congress (2012), covering political discipline, organisation, conduct and the fight against corruption.
The Party's claimed capacity to criticise, purify and renew itself. The term is also rendered as self-revolution.

t: Building ideological and political theory courses in the early years of the People's Republic
zh: 新中国成立初期的思想政治理论课建设
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in September 2019, Wu Xiaoni looks back at how universities in the early People's Republic established compulsory courses in ideological and political theory. The article argues that the Party and government's measures of that period (curriculum, leadership, teaching staff and teaching methods) were a useful exploration and offer lessons for current work on such courses. Wu links this to the instructions given by General Secretary Xi Jinping at the symposium for teachers of ideological and political theory courses in schools.

The article is organised around four themes. It begins with the construction of a course system centred on Marxist theory, then turns to a working mechanism in which Party and government leadership, university departments and all teachers share responsibility. It next covers the building of a politically reliable and theoretically competent teaching corps, and ends with methods that combine theory and practice. Wu draws on official regulations and directives from 1950 to 1955, and on remarks by educators and students of the time.

Wu describes the early curriculum as built on basic Marxist theory and Mao Zedong Thought. It started with dialectical and historical materialism, the theory of New Democracy and political economy, and was standardised by an instruction of October 1952. In 1953 it was adjusted after the general line for the transition period, and extended to postgraduates. Wu stresses that all teachers, not just political-course staff, were required to carry out ideological education within their own subjects, and calls this principle strategic and still relevant. To remedy a shortage of qualified instructors, a 1952 Central Committee directive led to selective recruitment, short-term training classes and research programmes, notably at Renmin University of China. Teaching combined theory with practice: the Korean War was used to counter pro-American attitudes, and students and staff took part in land reform, which Wu says helped them form a mass viewpoint and class standpoint.

Wu concludes that Party leadership, shared responsibility across the university, strong teaching staff and the link between theory and practice are experiences from this period that remain instructive for ideological and political theory courses in the new era. Student testimonies are cited as evidence that the courses raised political awareness. Read the original if you want a concise, officially framed account of how Marxist political courses were first built into Chinese higher education in the 1950s, and of the historical precedents that current policy invokes.
quoteEn: Leadership by the Party committee and government, joint management by all departments and the participation of everyone, forming an overall synergy to strengthen ideological and political theory courses for university students, was a major innovation in the early years of New China.
quoteZh: 党委政府领导、各部门齐抓共管、人人参与，形成加强大学生思想政治理论课工作的整体合力，是新中国成立初期在加强高校思政课方面的重大创举。

glossary.explanation: Compulsory Marxist theory and political education courses taught in Chinese schools and universities, often shortened to sizheng ke. They aim to shape students' political convictions as well as impart knowledge.

Mao Zedong's 1940 theory of a transitional stage of revolution led by the Communist Party before socialism. It was the basis of an early university course on this theory, later renamed History of the Chinese Revolution.

glossary.en: general line for the transition period
glossary.explanation: The Party line announced in 1953 for the period of transition from New Democracy to socialism, centred on gradual industrialisation and the socialist transformation of agriculture, handicrafts and private industry and commerce.
The early 1950s campaign to redistribute land from landlords to peasants. The article presents student and teacher participation in it as practical education.

t: The construction of national image over seventy years of New China
zh: 新中国70年国家形象的建构
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily on the eve of the People's Republic's 70th anniversary, Chen Jinlong asks how New China has built its national image and what that experience offers today. Chen defines national image as the impression and evaluation of a country's history, present and conduct held by the international community and its own people. The article argues that the seventy-year path from "standing up" to "becoming prosperous" to "becoming strong" was also a continuous process of constructing and refining that image.

The piece is organised under four headings. It sets out the dimensions of the image (economic, political, cultural, social and ecological), then the resources drawn on, the channels used, and finally the linkage between the images of the state, the Party and the people. Chen traces each theme from the Common Program of 1949 through Mao Zedong, Deng Xiaoping, Jiang Zemin and Hu Jintao to Xi Jinping.

Chen's central claim is that the image is multi-dimensional. The economy is its foundation, the political system its pillar, culture an important component, society its projection, and ecology a late-emerging but necessary element. The image draws on Chinese civilisation, on achievements publicised at national day and other anniversaries, and on national character. It is projected through commemorations, diplomacy (the Five Principles of Peaceful Coexistence, Belt and Road Initiative, a community with a shared future for mankind) and promotion of ethnic unity. Chen also stresses that the state's image cannot be separated from the ruling Party's image, which rests on its values, competence and integrity, including full and rigorous self-governance of the Party, or from the image of the people as the country's masters and creators of history.

Chen concludes that these results and experiences offer guidance for building national image in the new era. As the model, Chen quotes Xi Jinping's call to present four images: a civilised great country, an Eastern great country, a responsible great country and a socialist great country. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned account of how Chinese Party-state discourse in 2019 framed national image-building across the seventy years, with its standard citations from successive leaders.
quoteEn: The construction of New China's national image over seventy years has achieved major results and accumulated rich experience, and these results and experience offer important inspiration for building national image in the new era and for strengthening cultural confidence and cultural cohesion.
quoteZh: 新中国70年的国家形象建构，取得了重大成果、积累了丰富经验，这些成果与经验对于新时代国家形象建构、增强文化自信和文化凝聚力等都具有重要启迪意义。

glossary.explanation: A foreign-economic and infrastructure initiative proposed by Xi Jinping in 2013 to link China with Asia, Europe, Africa and beyond.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A concept in Xi Jinping's foreign policy discourse, presented as a vision of shared development and global governance.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: A slogan of the Xi Jinping era covering Party discipline, anti-corruption and internal supervision.
Principles of mutual respect for sovereignty, non-aggression, non-interference, equality and peaceful coexistence, first articulated by China and India in the 1950s.
The 1949 provisional programme adopted by the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference, which served as an interim constitution before 1954.

t: Seventy years of socialist cultural construction in New China and its lessons
zh: 新中国70年社会主义文化建设及其经验
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily on 10 July 2019, Ouyang Xuemei reviews how the Communist Party of China has led cultural work since 1949. The article argues that the Party, working from actual conditions, has built Chinese spirit and Chinese values, rallied the country and enriched people's cultural life. In Ouyang's account, this supported the passage from "standing up" to "becoming rich" to "becoming strong" and yielded a set of basic lessons.

The piece is organised chronologically in three stages, followed by a closing section of lessons. The first stage is the foundation of socialist culture after 1949, including mass literacy, public cultural facilities, script reform, minority-language policy and the promotion of Marxism. The second is the exploration of socialist culture with Chinese characteristics after the Cultural Revolution, running from the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee (1978) through the 12th to 17th Party Congresses. The third covers the period since the 18th Party Congress (2012).

Ouyang presents the early decades as establishing a new people's culture, while acknowledging that cultural questions were politicised and that the Cultural Revolution brought serious errors. The reform era is described as shifting emphasis from popularisation to raising standards, with spiritual civilisation, the distinction between public cultural undertakings and commercial cultural industries, and cultural-system reform as key advances. For the new era, the article stresses the Four-sphere Confidence, Marxist leadership in ideology, core socialist values, creative transformation of traditional culture, and a principle that social benefit comes first in literature and art. It also stresses telling China's story abroad and civilisational exchange.

Ouyang draws five lessons: Party leadership is the key; Marxism guides and keeps culture advanced; the people-centred character is the essence of socialist culture; core socialist values give culture its soul; and ancient and modern, Chinese and foreign cultures must be handled by preserving the roots, absorbing foreign achievements and facing the future. The author presents the record as a change from popularisation to improvement and from serving China's people to engaging the world. Read the original if you want a concise, officially framed periodisation of Party cultural policy from 1949 to 2019, with the key documents and slogans of each stage.
quoteEn: The people-centred character is the essential feature of socialist culture.
quoteZh: 人民性是社会主义文化的本质特征。

glossary.explanation: A formula associated with Xi Jinping: confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics. The article calls cultural confidence the most fundamental of the four.
A twelve-word set of values promoted since the 18th Party Congress, expressed at the national, social and individual levels.
Ideological, moral and cultural development, paired with material civilisation. The 12th Party Congress (1982) made it a strategic aim of modernization.

t: The Chinese path grows ever broader by upholding fundamental principles and breaking new ground
zh: 中国道路在守正创新中越走越宽广
paras: Writing in the People's Daily in July 2019, on the eve of the 70th anniversary of the People's Republic, Xin Ming argues that the path of socialism with Chinese characteristics (the "Chinese path") has widened because it combines faithfulness to fundamental principles (守正) with innovation (创新). The piece is a short commentary, not a research article. Xin presents the path as one opened by the Communist Party by upholding the basic principles of scientific socialism, grasping the laws of social development and drawing on the achievements of human civilisation.

The commentary has three sections. The first deals with scientific socialism and how the Chinese path both keeps and develops it. The second takes up modernization and the laws of social development. The third discusses the moral standing of the Chinese path and the push to build a community with a shared future for mankind, with the Belt and Road Initiative as its practical platform.

In the first section, Xin sets out what the author takes to be the core principles of scientific socialism: a historically necessary transition from capitalism, public ownership as a way to resolve the contradiction between socialised production and private appropriation, and leadership by a Marxist party. Xin holds that socialism with Chinese characteristics has kept these principles while innovating, citing the basic economic system, the decisive role of the market in allocating resources, and, since the 18th Party Congress (2012), the stress on Party leadership as its most essential feature. In the second section, Xin argues that modernization is not "Westernization". Western models built on colonial plunder and on opposing humanity to nature are, in Xin's account, exhausted, while China's emphasis on ecological civilisation and its answers to problems shared by developing countries offer an alternative. In the third, Xin contends that the path is peaceful and cooperative, rejects zero-sum thinking, and reflects a civilisation of harmony, citing Zheng He and Xi Jinping's image of a "peaceful, amiable and civilised lion".

Xin concludes that the success of the Chinese path is a victory for socialism itself and gives scientific socialism new vitality in twenty-first-century China. Xin also holds that the path offers developing countries a new option and contributes "Chinese wisdom" and a "Chinese approach" to global problems. Read the original if you want a concise example of how the Party press framed the Chinese path, modernization and the community with a shared future for mankind around the 70th anniversary in 2019.
quoteEn: Modernization is not "Westernization"; one must not simply parrot others, still less imitate them blindly.
quoteZh: 现代化不是“西方化”，不能人云亦云，更不能东施效颦。

glossary.explanation: The official name for the Chinese Communist Party's model of socialism since the reform era. It stresses adapting Marxism to China's conditions.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping since 2012–13 as China's vision for international relations based on cooperation and shared development.
An international infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative launched by Xi Jinping in 2013.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: How to uphold the eight "unities" in teaching ideological and political theory courses in universities
zh: 高校思政课教学怎样坚持八个“相统一”
paras: Lin Tai, a retired Tsinghua University professor who says he has taught ideological and political theory since 1959, reflects on the eight requirements ("unities") that Xi Jinping set out for reforming these courses. The piece is a personal commentary, published in Qiushi in 2019 after Lin attended the symposium of teachers of ideological and political theory courses on 18 March 2019. Lin argues that the eight pairings give teachers a concrete path to courses that are intellectually serious yet close to students' real concerns.

Lin opens with his own career, from political counsellor in 1954 to continued lecturing after retirement in 1999, and with what he says he has witnessed: the shift from Party history to an outline of modern Chinese history, the entry of the theoretical system of socialism with Chinese characteristics into the courses, and a stronger emphasis on core socialist values and moral and legal education. He then takes the eight unities in turn: political and academic; value and knowledge; constructive and critical; theoretical and practical; unity and diversity; the leading role of teachers and the agency of students; indoctrination and inspiration; explicit and implicit education.

The longest discussion concerns the first unity. Lin holds that a theory persuades only if it is thorough, that is, grasps the root of things. His examples are the claim that the Russian and Chinese revolutions came too early, which he answers by pointing to the shifting contradictions of the imperialist era, and the debate on human nature, which he treats through Marx's view that individuals must be understood within historical social relations. On the constructive and critical unity, he describes studying neoliberalism, Western constitutional democracy, historical nihilism and \"universal values\", and countering multiparty-competition ideas by comparing China with countries that adopted such systems. He also defends indoctrination as a principle, citing Lenin that socialist consciousness is brought to workers from outside, but says it must be carried out by inspiring students rather than by cramming.

Lin reports good practice among colleagues: field visits and social surveys, art students' exhibitions in the modern history course, and an engineering teacher who weaves ideological content into technical lectures. He calls for all courses and teachers to share responsibility for moral and political education. He ends by recalling a youth spent under the Japanese invasion and expresses confidence that, guided by Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, young people will fulfil their historic mission. Read the original if you want a veteran teacher's first-person account of how the official eight requirements are meant to work in the classroom.
quoteEn: Practice shows that, on the basis of upholding unity, ideological and political courses can fully be presented in a form where a hundred flowers bloom.
quoteZh: 实践表明，思政课在坚持统一性的基础上，完全可以以百花齐放的形式展现出来。

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses in Chinese universities on Marxism, Party history and socialism with Chinese characteristics, usually abbreviated as sizheng ke.

Eight paired requirements for teaching these courses, set out by Xi Jinping in his March 2019 speech to teachers, such as combining political and academic content, or constructive and critical approaches.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The official guiding ideology of the Communist Party of China, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.
The official name for the Chinese path of socialism since reform and opening up, combining Party leadership with a market-oriented economy.
In official usage, a label for views seen as denying or distorting the Party's history and the legitimacy of the revolution and socialist path.

t: A new breakthrough in the relationship between government and market in the new era
zh: 新时代政府和市场关系的新突破
paras: Writing in the China Social Sciences Today in July 2019, Liu Xuemei and Guo Guanqing take up the call for a Chinese philosophy and social science system, and ask how Chinese economics should understand the role of government and market. They argue that the Western ideal of 'small government, big market' does not fit late-developing countries, and that the reconstruction of the government–market relationship in Xi Jinping's economic thought is a new breakthrough.

The short piece moves from the history of economic thought to China's own record. It covers Adam Smith's context, the rival American School and German Historical School, Mises's 1920 critique of socialist economic calculation, the Soviet model, and China's decentralisation from 1958 onward. It ends with Xi Jinping's formulations on the market and Party leadership.

The authors contend that Smith's doctrine reflected Britain's position as a dominant industrial power, and that theorists overlook the pressures facing latecomers, whose governments must take on more functions. In their account, the Soviet model of vertical ministerial management could not solve information, incentive and soft budget constraint problems. China instead built a two-tier system based on regional decentralisation. There, local governments can shift state capital across sectors, and restructured state firms work with market price signals. The authors say this overcame the 'socialist economic calculation problem' and helped China become the world's second-largest economy in 2010.

Liu and Guo present Xi's twin principles as the theoretical expression of this experience: the market plays the decisive role in allocating resources, while the government plays its role better and the Party leads economic work in a centralised and unified way. They call on Chinese theoretical economics to build modernization theories, concepts and indicators from Chinese practice. Read the original if you want a brief statement of how Party-aligned economists in 2019 framed China's state-market model against Western and Soviet precedents.
quoteEn: Therefore, the laws behind the Chinese miracle need to be clarified from the standpoint of building an academic system.
quoteZh: 因此，需要从学术体系建设高度，阐明中国奇迹的规律。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义经济思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì jīngjì sīxiǎng
glossary.explanation: The body of economic theory attributed to Xi Jinping and promoted in Party theory since 2017. It is treated as part of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era.
A concept from János Kornai: loss-making enterprises are bailed out by the state, which weakens incentives for efficiency.
The article contrasts the 'tiao' (vertical lines of control from central ministries) with the 'kuai' (territorial management by local governments).

t: Promoting steadfast principles and innovation in ideological and political theory courses in the new era
zh: 推动新时代思政课守正创新
paras: This short commentary, published in People's Daily in August 2019, reports how Fudan University is putting into practice Xi Jinping's speech at a symposium for teachers of ideological and political theory courses. Jiao presents the speech as a programmatic document guiding such courses in the new era. The central claim is that Fudan is advancing these courses by holding to core principles while innovating in content, method and staffing.

The piece is organised under three headings: implementing Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era in teaching and research; reforming courses to raise quality; and building a trustworthy, capable teaching force. It draws on Fudan's own course system, textbooks and teacher-development practices.

On the first point, Jiao says Fudan insists that the courses be Marxist, socialist and Party-led, and offers a series of courses on Xi's thought. It seeks to bring this thought into scholarship, disciplines, courses, training, readers and students' minds. On the second, the university builds a "4+1+X" course system combining classroom and practical teaching, and plans to update supplementary textbooks, expand online courses and link ideological courses with "curriculum-based ideological education" in other subjects. Jiao reports that all four compulsory courses have become national or Shanghai model courses. On the third, the university sends teachers on study tours and practical postings, builds teaching teams through peer observation and mentoring, and coordinates university, college and branch Party organisations.

Jiao concludes that Fudan will continue reform along these lines so that students find the courses engaging and come to believe in what they study. The article is a Party-line account of institutional practice, not a theoretical study. Read the original if you want a concise example of how a leading Chinese university described its response to the 2019 directive on ideological and political courses.
quoteEn: We insist that people who have faith should be the ones to speak about faith.
quoteZh: 我们坚持让有信仰的人讲信仰

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018. It is taught as the latest stage of adapting Marxism to China.
Compulsory courses on Marxism, Party history and official ideology taught at Chinese schools and universities.

glossary.literal: ideology and politics in the curriculum
glossary.explanation: The policy of building ideological and moral education into all subjects, not only dedicated political courses.

t: Continuously deepening our understanding of the laws of socialist construction
zh: 不断深化对社会主义建设规律的认识
paras: Marking the 70th anniversary of the People's Republic in 2019, this commentary, first published in the People's Daily on 14 August 2019, asks what the Party has learned about the laws governing socialist construction. Tang Zhouyan argues that the 70 years were also seventy years of the Party leading the people in exploring those laws, and that continuing to summarise and deepen this understanding is necessary for advancing the cause of socialism with Chinese characteristics in the new era.

The piece is organised around five aspects that Tang calls especially important: the Party's role as the core of leadership; an accurate grasp of the historical stage of development and the principal contradiction in society; the scientific formulation of national development strategy; reform and opening up; and the continual meeting of the people's aspiration for a better life. Each section traces positions from Mao Zedong through successive Party congresses and plenums to Xi Jinping.

Tang's central move is to present each theme as a line of continuous refinement. On leadership, Tang cites Xi Jinping's claim that Party leadership is the defining feature and greatest strength of socialism with Chinese characteristics, and calls for upholding the Party Central Committee's authority and the core position of Xi. On the stage of development, Tang follows the formulation of the principal contradiction from 1956 through 1981 to the 19th Party Congress (2017), and stresses that its change leaves unaltered the judgment that China remains in the primary stage of socialism. On strategy and reform, Tang points to the Five-Year Plans, the three-step modernization plans, the 2020–2035–mid-century timetable, and the shift from the market's "basic" to "decisive" role in allocating resources.

Tang concludes that building a modern socialist country requires holding to the basic line of the primary stage, resolving unbalanced and inadequate development, deepening reform and opening up, and treating the people's longing for a better life as the goal. The commentary stresses the people-centred approach, poverty alleviation and the social security system as evidence. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party theorists in 2019 summarised the historical logic of seventy years of socialist construction.
quoteEn: Upholding the Party's leadership over all work is the foundation and lifeblood of the Party and the state, and the source of the interests and well-being of the people of all ethnic groups across the country.
quoteZh: 坚持党对一切工作的领导，是党和国家的根本所在、命脉所在，是全国各族人民的利益所在、幸福所在。

glossary.explanation: An official thesis, systematically set out at the 13th Party Congress in 1987, that China remains in an underdeveloped phase of socialism lasting a long historical period.

The Party's official judgment of the central tension in society, which guides policy. The 19th Party Congress (2017) restated it as that between the people's growing need for a better life and unbalanced, inadequate development.
The policy launched at the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee in 1978, shifting the Party's focus to economic construction and opening China to the outside world.

t: The intellectual content of the traditional view of past and present, and its sublation
zh: 传统古今观的思想内涵及其扬弃
source: Chinese Social Sciences Today (中国社会科学报), 30 July 2019
paras: Zhang Xiaoping asks how China's traditional understanding of "ancient" and "modern" (gu and jin) should be assessed and carried forward today. The commentary starts from Xi Jinping's repeated instruction that excellent traditional culture be inherited by making the past serve the present and using the past as a mirror, without privileging the ancient over the present or the reverse. Zhang argues that the traditional view contains both enduring essentials and dross, and that modern Chinese thought has sublated it, a process the author says should continue in the new era.

The piece is built in three parts. The first sets out the content of the traditional view: how "ancient" and "present" are conceived, how their relationship is understood, and what attitudes are taken towards each. The second separates what Zhang regards as valuable from what is not. The third traces the move from the late Qing and May Fourth periods, through Li Dazhao and Mao Zedong, to Xi Jinping's present-day guidance. Sources range from Shao Yong, Confucius and Sima Qian to Sima Guang, Gu Yanwu, Li Zhi and Wang Chong.

Zhang's central distinction is among three attitudes: favouring the ancient, favouring the present, and treating them as one. The author links each to a view of history as decline or progress, noting that Confucian reverence for the Three Dynasties, Daoist return to simplicity and Legalist reformism all fit this pattern, and that a comparable dispute existed in the West. On the positive side, Zhang credits the tradition with preserving texts, writing histories and drawing lessons for governance, including the people-centred reasoning of Sima Guang and the Confucian praise-and-blame ethic that restrained rulers. On the negative side, Zhang argues that Confucian moral norms hardened into absolute principle and narrowed thinking about past and present, a rigidity Li Zhi began to criticise.

In Zhang's account, Li Dazhao applied historical materialism to arrive at a "present-centred" view of history, and Mao Zedong held that history must not be severed and that the ancient should serve the present. Zhang calls for old content with lasting value to be given new forms through creative transformation and innovative development. The author also urges learning from the history of other countries, keeping historical materialism as the guide, and going beyond the productive-forces yardstick and a single Confucian moral standard. Read the original if you want a short, officially aligned overview of how Chinese scholars connect classical views of history to current cultural policy.
quoteEn: Between past and present there are both losses and gains, and change follows the times, yet within change there is an unchanging Way, and what is sought is the law of historical development.
quoteZh: 古今之间有损有益，因时而变，但变中又有不变的“道”，探寻的是历史的发展规律。

glossary.en: making the past serve the present
glossary.explanation: A principle associated with Mao Zedong for treating cultural heritage: drawing on past material for present needs. Xi Jinping has repeated it in discussing traditional culture.

glossary.zh: 创造性转化和创新性发展
glossary.explanation: A formula in official discourse on traditional culture, meaning that inherited cultural content should be reworked into new forms suited to contemporary conditions.
The Marxist theory that material production and social relations shape history. Chinese Marxists, including Li Dazhao, used it to explain social change.

t: Key focal points for running university ideological and political theory courses well
zh: 办好高校思想政治理论课的着力点
paras: Writing in 2019, Xu Rong takes up Xi Jinping's call, made at the 18 March symposium for teachers of school ideological and political theory courses, to run these courses well by answering the questions of whom to train, how to train them and for whom. Xu acknowledges that university courses have achieved notable results but sees unresolved problems in classroom effectiveness, the freshness of teaching materials and the make-up of the teaching staff. The article argues that success depends on three things: a clear mission, a workable path and a new overall pattern of course development.

The piece is organised in three parts. The first sets out the mission of 'forging souls and nurturing people'. The second treats 'upholding fundamental principles while innovating' as the necessary path, and walks through Xi's 'eight unities' for teaching reform. The third discusses how to build a new pattern for the courses, covering the social atmosphere around them, the course system, and institutions and mechanisms.

Xu holds that the courses should be grounded in the theoretical system of socialism with Chinese characteristics and in Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. They should answer students' real questions while taking a firm stand, and they need teachers who themselves hold firm convictions. Under the 'eight unities', Xu pairs the political with the academic, values with knowledge, and theory with practice. The pairings also include unity with diversity, teacher guidance with student agency, and explicit with implicit education. Xu defends 'indoctrination' (guànshū) as a necessary method, since scientific theory cannot arise spontaneously in students' minds, but says it must not become cramming and must be paired with inspiring methods. The article also calls for firm criticism of liberalism, individualism, historical nihilism, 'universal values' and 'constitutional democracy'.

On the new pattern, Xu contends that Party committees at every level must stop treating the courses as important in words but secondary in practice, and must end the squeezing of class hours and the disdain for teachers. Xu lists open questions about course systems, textbooks, staff, the relation between teaching and the discipline of Marxist theory, and evaluation. Xu notes uneven implementation of central rules, including places that cannot pay basic teaching fees, and calls for rule-of-law thinking and a 'ideological-political plus' approach that integrates the courses with all-round education. Read the original if you want to see how a 2019 Party-journal article translates Xi Jinping's instructions on ideological and political courses into a programme for university practice.
quoteEn: University ideological and political theory courses are the first lesson in forging souls and nurturing people in higher education, and they play an irreplaceable role in establishing young students' ideals and convictions, helping them make correct life choices, and training builders and successors of socialism.
quoteZh: 高校思想政治理论课是高等教育阶段铸魂育人的第一课，对于树立青年学生的理想信念、促进他们做出正确的人生选择，培养社会主义建设者和接班人，具有不可替代的重要作用。

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses on Marxism, Party theory and moral and political education taught in Chinese schools and universities, often abbreviated as 'sizheng' courses.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.
The official name for China's path since reform and opening up, combining Party leadership, a socialist system and a market economy.
A slogan for the aim of education as shaping students' ideals, convictions and values, not only transmitting knowledge.
Xi Jinping's 2019 requirements for reforming the courses, each pairing two aspects of teaching, such as politics and scholarship, or indoctrination and inspiration.

t: The fundamental guide to running ideological and political theory courses well in the new era
zh: 新时代办好思想政治理论课的根本指南
paras: This commentary, first published in Red Flag Manuscripts (Hongqi Wengao) in 2019, interprets Xi Jinping's speech at the symposium for teachers of school ideological and political theory courses. Sun Lanying argues that the speech sets out the basic guidance for running these courses well in the new era. The courses are presented as the key curriculum for carrying out the fundamental task of fostering virtue through education and for training a new generation able to shoulder national rejuvenation.

The article has three parts. The first explains why the courses are central to fostering virtue through education. The second takes up the claim that the key to the courses lies in teachers. The third deals with reform of the courses, which Sun grounds in Xi's requirements for teachers and in his "eight unities".

Sun describes universities as a front line of ideological work and the courses as the main battlefield for spreading Marxist theory and safeguarding national ideological security. In Sun's account, young students are a main target of Western hostile forces' efforts at "Westernisation" and division, so the courses must consolidate Marxism's guiding position, expose the nature of Western "universal values" and resist erroneous trends of thought. Teachers must meet Xi's "six requirements": strong politics, deep feelings for the country, innovative thinking, broad vision, strict self-discipline and upright character. For reform, Sun lists eight pairs to be unified: political and academic, value and knowledge, constructive and critical, theoretical and practical, unity and diversity, leading role and student agency, indoctrination and inspiration, explicit and implicit education. The first group is meant to make the courses persuasive through reasoned argument. The second is meant to make them engaging and substantive.

Sun concludes that reform needs strategic thinking and top-level design. The article also calls for mining ideological and political resources in other courses so that all teaching works in the same direction. It proposes using new media under an "Internet Plus" approach, and it cites online courses (MOOCs) and micro-courses as signs of reform momentum. Read the original if you want a compact example of how official commentary in 2019 explained the guiding principles for ideological and political education in universities, including the "six requirements" and "eight unities".
quoteEn: Teachers of ideological and political theory courses must study and master the fundamental method of materialist dialectics and continually strengthen their capacity for dialectical thinking.
quoteZh: 思想政治理论课教师要学习掌握唯物辩证法的根本方法，不断增强辩证思维能力。

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses in Chinese schools and universities that teach Marxism, Party theory and official political values. They are often shortened to sizheng ke.
A phrase presented in official documents as the fundamental task of education. It means moral and political character-building alongside the teaching of knowledge.
Xi Jinping's 2019 standards for teachers of these courses: strong politics, deep feelings, innovative thinking, broad vision, strict self-discipline and upright character.
Xi Jinping's eight paired principles for reforming the courses, such as combining indoctrination with inspiration and explicit with implicit education.

t: The historical significance and contemporary value of the May Fourth Movement
zh: 五四运动的历史意义和时代价值
paras: Writing for the 100th anniversary of the May Fourth Movement (1919), Dong Xuewen asks what the movement meant historically and what value it holds today. The author argues that its decisive achievement was to open the way for Marxism in China and so move the anti-imperialist, anti-feudal democratic revolution into a new stage. On this basis Dong presents the May Fourth spirit as one that young people in the new era should inherit in pursuing the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

The article is a commentary in six numbered sections, resting heavily on Mao Zedong's assessments in Selected Works vol. 2 and on speeches by Xi Jinping. It covers the movement's character and its link to the October Revolution, its place in modern Chinese intellectual history, the division between the periods before and after 1919 on the cultural front, the cultural debates of the time, and lessons for contemporary youth. Figures discussed include Li Dazhao, Chen Duxiu, Qu Qiubai, Hu Shih, Fu Sinian, Liang Qichao and Zhang Junmai.

Dong's central claim is that earlier movements, from the Sino-Japanese War of 1894–95 to the 1911 Revolution, failed because they lacked an advanced worldview. In this account the May Fourth Movement differed because young intellectuals turned to Marxism, took it to workers and prepared the ground for the founding of the Communist Party in 1921. Dong adds that cultural choices follow economic and social change, so wholesale Westernisation and eclectic schemes failed to fit China's conditions. Only the early communists, Dong says, offered a workable direction. The common description of the May Fourth spirit as 'science and democracy', the author holds, hides sharp differences: only Li Dazhao and others gave these ideas real substance through historical materialism and socialist democracy.

Dong concludes that the Party's founding in 1921, the People's Republic in 1949 and reform and opening up in 1978 all show the victory of Marxism in China and confirm that modern Chinese culture can be led only by proletarian, communist thought. Drawing on Xi Jinping, the author calls for strengthening Marxist belief and the ability to apply Marxism to current problems, and urges young people to carry on the tradition of 'permanent struggle' under Party leadership. Read the original if you want to see how a 2019 official-journal commentary ties the May Fourth legacy to Marxism, the Party's founding and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.
quoteEn: The basic core of the May Fourth spirit is patriotism.
quoteZh: 五四精神的基本核心是爱国主义。

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal, closely associated with Xi Jinping's Chinese Dream, of restoring China's national strength and international standing after the 'century of humiliation'.
The set of values attributed to the 1919 movement, usually patriotism, progress, democracy and science. Official accounts present it as a basis for the patriotic mission of Chinese youth.

t: How to teach ideological and political theory courses well in universities
zh: 怎样才能上好高校思想政治理论课
paras: Writing in Qiushi in 2019, after Xi Jinping chaired a symposium for teachers of school ideological and political theory courses on 18 March, Liu Jianjun asks three linked questions: why these courses matter, why they are hard to teach, and how they can be taught well. Liu argues that the courses are of special importance and special difficulty, but that the conditions now exist for teaching them well, provided teachers make efforts in several areas.

The commentary has three parts. The first sets out the importance of the courses in universities. The second lists the difficulties of teaching them. The third names the favourable conditions and then sets out four directions of effort for teachers, drawing throughout on Xi's speech at the symposium, including his principle of the "eight unifications".

On importance, Liu holds that the courses express the socialist character of Chinese universities, are the key courses for fulfilling the fundamental task of fostering virtue through education, and are the main channel and main battleground of students' ideological and political education. On difficulty, Liu points to the political character of the courses, which leaves a psychological distance from students, and to their theoretical depth. Liu adds the gap between theory and reality, the breadth of content and the speed at which it changes, and the aim of shaping values and ideals, which goes beyond imparting knowledge. Liu cautions that responsibility for students' ideals and convictions cannot be left to these courses alone.

Liu lists six favourable conditions, among them the Party and state's high priority, recent theoretical achievements in adapting Marxism to Chinese conditions, the achievements of socialism with Chinese characteristics, and a dependable teaching corps. Liu then calls on teachers to strengthen their convictions and teach with confidence, and to raise their theoretical level through research serving teaching. Liu also asks them to convert academic, political and everyday language into effective classroom discourse, and to try varied methods such as thematic, interactive and multimedia teaching. Read the original if you want a concise Party-journal statement of how the official case for ideological and political courses, and the expectations placed on their teachers, were presented after the 2019 symposium.
quoteEn: Teachers of ideological and political theory courses should take an active part in academic research and consciously use the results of disciplinary development to support and improve their teaching.
quoteZh: 思政课教师要积极参与学术研究，并自觉地以学科建设的成果来支撑和提升教学。

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses in Chinese schools and universities teaching Marxism, Party lines and policies, and moral and legal education. Often abbreviated as "sizheng ke" (思政课).
A formula for the fundamental task of Chinese education, stressing moral character alongside knowledge. It was given prominence in Party documents from the 18th Party Congress (2012).

Eight pairings of requirements for running ideological and political courses, announced by Xi Jinping at the March 2019 symposium, such as unifying political and academic orientation, and theory and practice.
The official name for China's path and system since reform and opening up, combining Party leadership, a socialist system and market-oriented reform.

t: Giving full play to ideological and political theory courses in forging souls and nurturing people
zh: 充分发挥思想政治理论课铸魂育人作用
paras: Writing in Red Flag Manuscripts in 2019, Yang Ming asks how universities can make their ideological and political theory courses (sizhengke) the "first classroom" for forging souls and nurturing people. The commentary argues that this requires studying and carrying out Xi Jinping's speech at the symposium for teachers of these courses, and strengthening the sense of responsibility for running them well.

The piece has three parts. The first sets out the content of Xi's speech, which Yang presents as answering why the courses must be run well, why they can be, and how. The second turns to teachers and the standards they are expected to meet. The third addresses the political responsibility of universities and sets out four practical tasks.

Yang reads the speech as grounded in Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. Yang stresses Xi's six requirements for teachers (strong politics, deep feeling, innovative thinking, broad vision, strict self-discipline, upright character) and the "eight unities". For teachers, Yang calls for reliable political positions, innovative methods that proceed step by step and in a rising spiral, and continuous study that keeps course content current with the latest results of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context. For institutions, Yang lists four tasks: coordination under Party committee leadership, strengthening the Marxist theory discipline, improving teaching with online and offline "golden courses", and building the teaching staff.

Yang concludes that a leadership structure involving the Party, administration, departments and society, together with strong teachers and academic support, will allow these courses to carry out the fundamental task of cultivating virtue and nurturing people. The text is a programmatic call rather than an empirical study. Read the original if you want a concise example of how the 2019 policy line on ideological and political courses was explained to university staff.
quoteEn: Teachers of ideological and political theory courses should grasp contemporary students' cognitive habits and ways of learning, work on the courses' ideological quality, theoretical quality, appeal and relevance, actively innovate teaching methods, and be good at making \"meaningful\" things \"interesting\".
quoteZh: 思想政治理论课教师要善于把握当代大学生的认知习惯和学习方式，在思想政治理论课的思想性、理论性、亲和力和针对性上下功夫，积极创新教学方法，善于把“有意义”的事情讲得“有意思”

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses in Marxism and Party theory taught at Chinese schools and universities, usually abbreviated sizhengke.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.
An official formulation of the fundamental task of education in China: moral formation of students alongside knowledge.
Eight paired requirements Xi Jinping set out in 2019 for reforming these courses, such as combining political and academic content, or indoctrination and inspiration.

glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context
glossary.explanation: The official idea that Marxism is applied to and developed within Chinese conditions, producing theories such as Mao Zedong Thought and Xi Jinping Thought.

t: Firmly holding the initiative in online ideological work
zh: 牢牢掌握网络意识形态工作主动权
paras: Writing in Red Flag Manuscripts in early 2019, Zheng Jie takes up Xi Jinping's remarks at the 12th collective study session of the Political Bureau (25 January 2019) on strengthening online content and running all-media communication within the rule of law. Zheng argues that, in the all-media era, holding leadership over ideological work depends largely on holding the initiative in online ideological work. The author maintains that the Party must keep its leadership over ideological work and create a clean online space, while explaining the Chinese path and safeguarding political and cultural security.

The article is organised in four parts, each with three sub-points: building initiative in online discourse power; improving that discourse as a whole; perfecting a set of mechanisms; and raising international influence. It is a policy-oriented commentary that draws heavily on Xi Jinping's statements, including those from the 2014 first meeting of the central leading group on cybersecurity and informatisation and the August 2018 national conference on propaganda and ideological work.

Zheng's core claim is that contests over online discourse are in essence contests of interests, in which a few developed Western countries use economic and technological advantages to exert infiltration under the cover of exchange. The author describes such contests as long-term, concealed, infiltrating, complex and varied. The response proposed is to build as well as rebut: strengthen mainstream media guidance and media convergence, set up dedicated Marxist theory websites, and replace abstruse language with plain, lively content and varied formats such as H5, AR and VR. Zheng also calls for legal, supervisory and responsive mechanisms: improved internet legislation, strict enforcement against content said to threaten national security or subvert the socialist system, early-warning systems for online opinion, technical means to detect and remove harmful information, and feedback channels with evaluation of communication effects.

Internationally, Zheng argues that Western states hold the discourse initiative through technological advantage, and calls for China to move from a large to a strong cyber power. Proposed steps include a global outlook combined with Chinese characteristics drawn from traditional culture, dialogue-based rather than one-way external messaging, online diplomacy, and a shift from advocate to leader in cyberspace governance. The author concludes that mainstream media should reach user terminals directly and form concentric circles online and offline. Read the original if you want a compact example of how official Party commentary in 2019 framed online ideological security, discourse power and internet governance.
quoteEn: The contest for online discourse power is in essence a contest of interests, behind which lie struggles over the space for online survival and development, over ideology, and over economic and political interests.
quoteZh: 网络话语权争夺实质是利益的争夺，其背后蕴含着网络生存发展空间、意识形态以及经济、政治等方面的利益之争。

glossary.explanation: A Party formulation holding that the Party must retain control over the ideological sphere, including media, education and culture. It is stressed in Xi Jinping-era documents.
The capacity to shape agendas, narratives and public opinion online. The term is used to frame competition between states and actors in cyberspace.
An official term for an integrated communication ecosystem combining print, broadcast, online and mobile media. Xi Jinping stressed it at the January 2019 study session.
A policy of merging traditional and new media so that official outlets can reach audiences across platforms.
A stated national goal of moving from having many internet users to leading in internet technology, industry and governance.

t: Upholding and continually enriching our understanding of the laws governing China's education
zh: 始终坚持并不断丰富发展对我国教育事业的规律性认识
paras: This commentary, published in Red Flag Manuscript in 2018, interprets Xi Jinping's speech at the National Education Conference of that year. In the article's account, the speech answered the fundamental questions of whom education should cultivate, how, and for whom, and set out a series of new ideas on education reform and development. Dai argues that these ideas deepen the Party's understanding of the laws of education in China, were hard won, and must be upheld and enriched. The article stresses four of them.

The piece is organised into four numbered sections: the importance of education as a matter of national and Party strategy; the fundamental task of education; Party leadership over education; and the teaching profession. Each section strings together remarks by Xi from 2013 to 2018, including letters, talks at Beijing Normal University and Peking University, the 2016 national conference on ideological and political work in universities, and the 2018 conference. Dai also cites Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping on the standing of intellectuals and education.

Dai's core claim is that education is "a major plan for the country and for the Party" and the foundation of the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Dai links this to competition in overall national strength, which the article calls ultimately a competition for talent. Because every country trains people according to its own political requirements, the author holds, the questions of whom to cultivate and how are political rather than technical. Education must therefore cultivate socialist builders and successors who support Party leadership and the socialist system. Dai presents the Party's comprehensive leadership as the fundamental guarantee, beginning with ideological and political leadership, Marxism's guiding position and the cultivation of core socialist values. Teachers are described as the foundation of education, and the article gives teachers' ethics and conduct as the first standard for judging them.

Dai concludes that educational authorities and school Party organisations should strengthen the Four Consciousnesses and the Four-sphere Confidence and uphold the authority of the Party Central Committee. Teachers are urged to unite teaching with moral education and to cultivate virtue, while society is urged to raise teachers' political, social and professional standing. Read the original if you want a compact example of how Party commentary in 2018 summarised Xi Jinping's education doctrine and its emphasis on Party leadership and teachers.
quoteEn: Only by insisting on making the priority development of education a key opening move in advancing all the work of the Party and the state can education keep pace with the demands of that work, meet the expectations of the people, and match China's overall national strength and international standing.
quoteZh: 只有坚持把优先发展教育事业作为推动党和国家各项事业发展的重要先手棋，才能不断使教育同党和国家事业发展要求相适应、同人民群众期待相契合、同我国综合国力和国际地位相匹配

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central official goal of the Party, associated especially with Xi Jinping's "Chinese Dream", of restoring China to national strength and international standing.
Official formula calling for confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics.
A Party discipline formula calling for political awareness, awareness of the big picture, of the core leader, and of alignment with the Party's line.
A set of twelve values promoted by the Party since the 18th Party Congress (2012), at national, social and individual levels.

t: Universities must show new achievements in taking up the era's mission of "fostering new people"
zh: 高校要在担当“育新人”时代使命中展现新作为
paras: Writing in Red Flag Manuscripts in 2018, after Xi Jinping's speeches at the National Education Conference and at Peking University, Xu Qinghong and Xu Peng ask how Chinese universities should carry out the task of cultivating "new people of the era" (shidai xinren) who can shoulder national rejuvenation. Their answer is that universities must be guided by Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, uphold the Party's overall leadership of education, and train socialist builders and successors with all-round moral, intellectual, physical, aesthetic and labour development.

The commentary is a policy-oriented exposition in three parts, each opening with Xi's statements and then setting out tasks for higher education. The first part concerns the socialist orientation of university education, the second the fundamental task of fostering virtue and nurturing talent, and the third the Party's leadership of universities. Each part is divided into three concrete measures.

On orientation, the authors hold that the question of whom universities serve and what kind of universities to build admits no ambiguity. They call for Marxism's guiding position to be maintained, for the "Four Services" requirement to be implemented, and for the "Double First-Class" initiative and comprehensive reform to be pursued with the correct political direction. On moral education, they argue that ideals and convictions, the core socialist values and a high-quality teaching staff with strong professional ethics must all be strengthened, so that students link personal dreams to the Chinese Dream. On Party leadership, they treat it as the basic feature and greatest strength of Chinese universities. They call for university Party committees to act as the leadership core, for grassroots Party branches to serve as "battle fortresses", and for an ideological and political work system that involves all staff, covers the whole process and extends in all directions.

The authors conclude that the success of universities in fostering new people depends on firm political direction, a moral education system built around virtue and talent, and strong Party organisation at every level. They present these as requirements of socialist universities and of educational modernization rather than as optional measures. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official Party discourse in 2018 set out the political tasks of higher education, with its main slogans and Xi Jinping citations gathered in one place.
quoteEn: Upholding and strengthening the Party's overall leadership of universities is an inevitable requirement for running socialist universities with Chinese characteristics well, and is also the basic feature and greatest strength of China's universities.
quoteZh: 坚持和加强党对高校的全面领导，是办好中国特色社会主义大学的必然要求，也是我国高校的基本特色和最大优势。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The official guiding ideology of the Communist Party of China, written into the Party constitution at the 19th Party Congress in 2017.
An official formulation naming the fundamental task of education: moral and ideological formation alongside the teaching of knowledge and skills.
Xi Jinping's 2016 requirement that higher education serve the people, the Party's governance, the consolidation of the socialist system, and reform, opening up and modernization.
A national initiative, launched in 2015, to build world-class universities and world-class disciplines.
A slogan popularised by Xi Jinping from 2012, referring to the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

t: New thinking on strengthening ideological work from the perspective of cultural technology
zh: 文化技术视阈下加强意识形态建设的新思考
paras: Writing in 2018, Ren Limei argues that research on online ideology has concentrated on content and on conflicts between internet culture and mainstream culture, and should instead start from the ideological character of network technology itself. The article holds that the internet has become the main battlefield of mainstream ideology and a key force for socialism with Chinese characteristics and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Its thesis is that ideological work must rely on developing and controlling network technology, as well as on managing content.

The article has four parts. It first examines the cultural features and ideological attributes of network technology, looking at technology from the standpoint of culture and at culture from the standpoint of technology. It then analyses the security problems facing online culture and ideology in what Ren calls the age of cultural technology. The third part sets out how to hold ideological leadership, management and discourse power through technology, and the fourth proposes building a "concentric circle" online and offline.

Ren's core argument is that technology has three layers: material artefacts, institutions and ideas, and that the last of these is technology's ideology. On this view, every platform carries the values of its operators, and the internet spreads and amplifies them faster than older media. Ren names several sources of risk. Chinese culture is said to be in a transitional stage, and some Western capitalist states are said to use networks to steer public sentiment and infiltrate ideologically. Niche online subcultures that mock mainstream culture, and market-driven pragmatic outlooks on life, are also listed. Ren's remedies are to promote the core socialist values in language suited to the internet, to deepen the integration of traditional and new media, and to master core technologies and train politically reliable technical personnel.

In the final part Ren calls for more investment in research and development, including blockchain, and for officials to follow the mass line online. Ren also proposes flatter, more flexible organisational structures for ideological work, and "Internet Plus" applications in services, rural development and poverty alleviation, so that people see practical benefits. The article concludes that China should use the internet era to draw a "concentric circle" and build a culture of mutual trust that secures mainstream ideology and the core socialist values. Read the original if you want an example of how Chinese ideological-work scholarship in 2018 linked internet governance, technology strategy and ideological security.
quoteEn: Rather than saying that the internet has set off a technological revolution, it is better to say that it has brought a cultural revolution and a clash of ideologies.
quoteZh: 与其说互联网引发了一场技术革命，不如说它带来一场文化革命和意识形态的交锋。

glossary.explanation: The capacity to shape public narratives and set the terms of debate. In Chinese Party writing it is paired with leadership and management power as the three components of ideological work.
A 24-character set of values (such as prosperity, democracy, harmony, freedom, equality, patriotism and integrity) promoted by the Party since the 18th Party Congress (2012).

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central official goal of restoring China's national strength and international standing, often linked to the Chinese Dream.
A metaphor from Xi Jinping's speeches for uniting people of all groups around the Party's leadership. The article extends it to online and offline spaces.
A traditional Party method of leadership that draws on the views of ordinary people and returns them as policy. Ren applies it to officials' engagement online.

t: The historic mission of university teachers of ideological and political theory courses
zh: 高校思政课教师的时代重任
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in June 2018, Lan Botao asks what role teachers of ideological and political theory courses in Chinese universities should play in the new era. The commentary argues that their central task is to equip students' minds with Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era and to strengthen students' faith in socialism with Chinese characteristics. Lan holds that teachers must see themselves in three roles: researcher, communicator and practitioner.

The piece opens from a Central Committee and State Council document on teacher-training reform, which says a strong nation first needs strong teachers. It then takes the three roles in turn. Each section draws on remarks by Xi Jinping, and one cites Marx's statement that every true philosophy is the spiritual quintessence of its time.

As researchers, Lan argues, teachers must follow the practice of socialism with Chinese characteristics closely and study its major theoretical achievements. Otherwise the courses lose their "source of living water", and the teachers cannot explain the Eight Clarifications and Fourteen Persistences. As communicators, they should turn theory into concrete cases, tie it to topical issues students care about, and attend to timing, degree and effect. As practitioners, they should start from students' daily lives and use lively language. They should also fit their methods to student type: reasoned argument for the humanities and social sciences, worked examples for science and engineering students.

Lan concludes that teachers must define their role clearly as researcher, communicator and practitioner in order to meet the responsibility the new era gives them. Read the original if you want a short example of how official discourse in 2018 described the duties and teaching methods expected of university political-theory teachers.
quoteEn: University ideological and political theory teachers must define their role clearly, recognising that they are at once researchers, communicators and practitioners, and must accomplish well the heavy task the new era has given them.
quoteZh: 高校思政课教师必须清晰地定位自己的角色，认识到自己既是研究者，又是传播者，还是实践者，出色地完成新时代赋予的重任。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The official guiding ideology of the Communist Party of China, written into the Party constitution in 2017 and the state constitution in 2018.
The official name for China's path of socialist development since reform and opening up began in the late 1970s.
A summary of the core theoretical propositions of Xi Jinping Thought, presented in the report to the 19th Party Congress (2017).
Fourteen basic principles for upholding and developing socialism with Chinese characteristics in the new era, set out at the 19th Party Congress (2017).
Compulsory courses in Marxism and Party ideology taught at all Chinese universities.

t: University ideological and political education should adapt to "three changes"
zh: 高校思政教育当顺应“三变”
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in July 2018, Zhang Zhenli asks how ideological and political education in universities should be done in the new era. The commentary opens with Xi Jinping's remarks of 2 May 2018 at Peking University that cultivating builders and successors of socialism is a common mission of all schools. Zhang's answer is that such education must adapt to three changes: in its audience, its purpose and its method.

The piece first notes that results are uneven. Programmes at Tsinghua, Peking University and Beihang University are praised by students, and some teachers have become popular figures. Other institutions, Zhang says, still rely on reading scripts, shouting slogans and declaring resolve, which leaves students dissatisfied and sometimes resistant.

On the audience, Zhang describes university students as the youth group with the strongest sense of subjectivity, rationality and questioning. They want to know whether a conclusion's premises hold, prefer historical detail to grand narrative, and seek practical rationality as well as appealing values. On purpose, Zhang argues that education should teach students to use the Marxist standpoint, viewpoint and method to observe and analyse the world. Patriotic enthusiasm alone, in Zhang's view, risks "good intentions doing harm". On method, Zhang calls for dialogue and discussion in place of the teacher's monologue, linking world affairs to students' own circumstances.

Zhang concludes, citing Gadamer, that each era must interpret inherited texts in its own way. It is therefore the right time, Zhang argues, to reconstruct how the classics of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context are interpreted in university teaching. Read the original if you want a short example of how a 2018 official-press commentary framed teaching reform in Chinese university ideological education.
quoteEn: Ideological and political education in universities should adapt to three changes.
quoteZh: 高校思想政治教育当顺应三个变化。

glossary.explanation: The system of Marxist theory teaching and value education in Chinese schools and universities, run under Party leadership. It includes compulsory courses and campus activities.

glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context
glossary.explanation: The official formula for applying Marxism to China's conditions and producing new theory, from Mao Zedong Thought to the present.

t: Promoting deep integration of Party building and ideological and political theory courses in universities
zh: 推动高校党建与思政课深度融合
paras: This short commentary, published in Guangming Daily in August 2018, asks how university Party building and ideological and political theory courses (sizhengke) can be deeply integrated. Zhang argues that the courses are an important vehicle and advantage channel for Party building. Integrating the two, in Zhang's view, would unify theoretical cultivation with practical guidance in the new era.

The article opens with remarks by Xi Jinping on higher education and moral education. It then has three parts: why Party building must provide ideological leadership, why folding Party building into the courses matters, and what practical routes to take.

Zhang presents the courses as the "bridge" for turning Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era into students' thinking and action. Three significances are given. The first is Marxist ideological education. The second is the fundamental task of cultivating people through moral education. The third is building a high-calibre team of Party-affairs cadres, since a long-standing split between Party building and teaching ("two layers of skin") is said to leave Party work formalistic.

For practice, Zhang calls for strengthening Marxist guidance, building Marxist schools and improving the political education of young teachers. Zhang also proposes new teaching vehicles such as Party-building salons, practical courses, red-culture visits and internet-based platforms. Zhang further urges coordination: course teachers giving Party lectures, Party workers teaching current-affairs courses, and mixed teacher–student Party branches. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official commentary in 2018 framed the link between campus Party organisation and ideological teaching.
quoteEn: Party building in universities is both a practical question and a theoretical one.
quoteZh: 高校党建既是实践问题,也是理论问题。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018. It is taught as core content in university ideological and political courses.
Compulsory courses in Chinese universities on Marxism, Party history and current policy. They are treated officially as the main channel of ideological education.
An official formula for the fundamental task of education: to cultivate virtue and nurture people. It is often cited by Xi Jinping.

t: Ideological work in the new era must strive to strengthen cohesion and guiding power
zh: 新时代意识形态工作要在增强凝聚力和引领力上下功夫
source: China Party and Government Cadres Forum (《中国党政干部论坛》), 2018 no. 9
paras: Writing in 2018, Jiang Hui takes up Xi Jinping's instruction at the National Conference on Propaganda and Ideological Work that unifying thinking and rallying strength must be the central task of ideological work in the new era. The article asks what problems stand in the way of building a socialist ideology with strong cohesion and guiding power, and how to address them. Jiang argues that this requires facing four sets of prominent problems squarely and then acting along five lines, with the Party firmly holding leadership over ideological work.

The article has two main parts. The first identifies four problem areas in the ideological sphere: Marxism's guiding position versus diverse currents of thought; core socialist values versus plural values; China's rising international standing versus attempts to contain it; and the challenge of new media to the way ideology is managed. The second part sets out five tasks: Marxist education, leadership over ideological work, discourse power, the quality of ideological personnel, and innovation in methods.

In Jiang's account, Marxism's unified guiding position is being tested by neo-liberalism, Western constitutional democracy, "universal values", historical nihilism and theories of the "end of ideology". Market-driven profit-seeking is said to feed utilitarianism and extreme individualism, which erode collectivism. Jiang also describes Western hostile forces as pushing "China threat" narratives and various "trap" theories, and as using mobile internet platforms for ideological infiltration, so that cyberspace is both the main battlefield and the front line of ideological work. In response, Jiang calls for studying Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, full implementation of the ideological work responsibility system under the principle that the Party manages propaganda, positions, opinion and media, and building Chinese-style discourse systems and international communication capacity.

Jiang concludes that ideological workers must be politically alert, distinguish questions of political principle from questions of understanding and academic views, and avoid both losing principle and arbitrarily escalating issues. Methods should combine indoctrination with reasoned persuasion, merge traditional and new media, and turn political and theoretical language into forms ordinary people welcome. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how a senior Academy of Marxism figure framed the ideological tasks of the new era, and how the threats and responses were described in 2018.
quoteEn: Ideological work is in essence political work, and it must take a clear-cut stand on politics.
quoteZh: 意识形态工作本质上是政治工作，必须旗帜鲜明讲政治。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018. It is presented as the latest achievement in adapting Marxism to China.
The Party's claim to control over ideology, propaganda, media and cultural fields, which it treats as essential to political security.
A set of twelve values promoted officially since 2012, covering the national, social and individual levels.
The capacity to set the terms of debate and have one's narrative accepted, domestically and internationally.
An official label for interpretations that question the Party's official historical narrative or revolutionary history.

t: Uncovering the meaning of life in Marxist philosophy
zh: 发掘马克思主义哲学生活意蕴
paras: This short commentary, published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in October 2018, argues that "life" and "real life" are the starting point and destination of all philosophical questions in the Marxist classics. On that basis Zhang proposes classifying Marxist philosophy as a "philosophy of life". The author holds that exploring its meaning would strengthen the philosophical foundation of the idea of "creating a better life for the people" and address the question of how people today should live.

The piece has two parts. The first sets out how Marx and Engels turned from speculative philosophy to a philosophy directed at real life. The second explains why this reading matters today. Zhang draws mainly on The German Ideology and the Theses on Feuerbach, and also cites Xi Jinping on the link between history and people's pursuit of a better life.

Zhang develops the first part in three steps.
