Liu argues that this task must be guided by Marxism and must keep to the forward direction of advanced socialist culture.

The piece has two parts. The first presents Marxism as the fundamental guide to cultural development. The second sets out how that guidance is to be applied to traditional, revolutionary and socialist culture and to foreign cultural achievements.

Liu holds that Marxist guidance must be concrete and not a slogan. It means using the latest results of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, and arming minds with Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. Cultural production, in Liu's account, should be rooted in life and aimed at the people's aspiration for a better life, given the principal contradiction identified for the new era. Liu then names four tasks: creative transformation of fine traditional Chinese culture, drawing on revolutionary culture, cultivating core socialist values, and absorbing useful foreign cultural achievements while bringing Chinese culture to the world.

Liu concludes that these efforts will strengthen cultural confidence, build a culturally strong socialist country and support the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Chinese civilisation is also expected to contribute to humankind's development. Read the original if you want a brief example of how official commentary in 2018 linked Marxist guidance to cultural policy after the 19th Party Congress.
quoteEn: Taking Marxism as the guide is not abstract but concrete, and must never be treated as a slogan.
quoteZh: 坚持以马克思主义为指导，不是抽象的而是具体的，决不能当作口号

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal, closely linked to the Chinese Dream, of restoring China's national strength and international standing.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party constitution in 2017 and the state constitution in 2018.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for combining Marxist theory with Chinese conditions. The article uses the shorter 2018 wording, 'Sinicization of Marxism'.
Confidence in China's own culture and cultural path, counted since 2016 as the fourth of the 'four confidences'.
A set of twelve values promoted officially since 2012, covering the national, social and individual levels.

t: Grasping the new era, understanding the new thought, studying the required course well
st: On the amended Party Constitution
zh: 把握新时代 领悟新思想 学好必修课
paras: This commentary, first published in Economic Daily on 29 March 2018, takes up the amendments made to the Party Constitution at the 19th Party Congress (2017). Zhang argues that writing the main content of the Congress report into the Constitution unifies thinking and builds consensus across the Party. The author presents this as having major practical and historical significance for advancing socialism with Chinese characteristics from a new historical starting point.

The article has two analytical parts and one practical part. The first explains why the amendments are required by the development of the Party and the state in the new era. The second treats them as a need to keep the Party's guiding ideology up to date. The third sets out how Party organisations and members should study, observe, implement and uphold the Constitution.

On the first point, Zhang says the Constitution now records the judgement that socialism with Chinese characteristics has entered a new era. It also records the revised statement of the principal contradiction in society, now between the people's ever-growing needs for a better life and unbalanced and inadequate development. The author adds the word "beautiful" to the Party's basic line and the shift from "country" to "great power", which Zhang links to the goal for the centenary of the People's Republic. On the second point, Zhang calls the writing of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era into the Constitution as the Party's guiding ideology the single biggest highlight of the revision. Zhang describes the thought as the latest result of adapting Marxism to Chinese conditions. The article adds that culture now sits alongside the path, theory and system as part of the basic content of socialism with Chinese characteristics, and that the amendments absorb the practice of full and rigorous self-governance of the Party.

Zhang concludes that Party members must establish awareness of the Constitution, treating it as the basic standard for Party conduct and the basis of work. The author calls for studying it together with Xi Jinping Thought and the spirit of the 19th Congress, and for holding to the Four Consciousnesses and the Four-sphere Confidence. Zhang also proposes more targeted education, stronger supervision of implementation, and better Party regulations. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official commentary in 2018 explained the rationale for the Party Constitution amendments and the duties they placed on members.
quoteEn: Establishing Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era as the Party's guiding ideology, and writing it on the Party's banner, is the biggest highlight and most outstanding historical contribution of this revision of the Party Constitution.
quoteZh: 把习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想确立为党的指导思想，写在党的旗帜上，是这次党章修改的最大亮点和最突出的历史贡献。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's current guiding ideology, written into the Party Constitution at the 19th Party Congress in 2017. Official texts present it as the latest stage in adapting Marxism to China.
The official name for China's path of development since reform and opening up. It is presented as combining a path, a body of theory, a system and, since 2017, a culture.

A Marxist-Maoist concept for the central tension that determines the Party's main tasks. The 19th Congress redefined it as the contradiction between the people's growing needs for a better life and unbalanced and inadequate development.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's formula for strengthening Party discipline and Party-building, closely tied to the anti-corruption campaign launched after 2012.
Official slogan calling for confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics.
A Party slogan demanding political awareness, awareness of the big picture, of the leadership core, and of alignment with the Party's line. Members are expected to cultivate these.

t: The Marxist philosophical implications of the "people-centred" thought
zh: “以人民为中心”思想的马克思主义哲学意蕴
source: Research on Ideological and Political Work, 2018 no. 8
paras: Writing in 2018, shortly after the 19th Party Congress (2017), Zou Xingping asks what the principle of "putting the people at the centre" means when read from the standpoint of Marxist philosophy. The article argues that the principle is an integral part of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era and that it follows directly from Marxist worldview, historical materialism and methodology.

The article is organised in three sections, treating the principle in turn as a worldview, as a conception of history and as a method. It traces the idea of "the people" from Marx and Engels, through Lenin and the October Revolution, to Mao Zedong, Deng Xiaoping and Xi Jinping.

Zou claims that Marx's "humanity" was abstract, whereas after the October Revolution it became the concrete "people" and a matter of political practice for a ruling proletarian party. Drawing on the historical-materialist thesis that the masses create history, the author contends that exploiting-class parties use "the people" as an ideological cover, while a proletarian party treats itself as the people's instrument. Methodologically, Zou describes the principle as the focal point of Marxist thinking, set against the bourgeois focus on "capital", and as a working method. It requires relying on the people, respecting their initiative and using their satisfaction as the test of comprehensively deepening reform.

Zou concludes that adhering to a people-centred approach is an essential requirement of the Chinese Communist Party's nature, since its Constitution sets the aim of serving the people wholeheartedly. The author links the principle to the new principal contradiction in Chinese society, between the people's growing needs for a better life and unbalanced, inadequate development. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party theorists in 2018 grounded the people-centred principle in the classical Marxist canon.
quoteEn: The bourgeois parties focus on "capital", whereas the proletarian party's thinking focuses on "the people".
quoteZh: 资产阶级政党的聚焦点是“资本”，无产阶级政党的思维聚焦点是“人民”

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The official guiding ideology of the Communist Party of China, written into the Party Constitution in 2017 at the 19th Party Congress.

glossary.en: putting the people at the centre
glossary.explanation: A principle of Xi Jinping's governing philosophy, holding that development and policy should start from and serve the people's interests.

t: How to do Marxist propaganda and education well and make it strong
zh: 马克思主义宣传教育何以做好做强
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in September 2018, Shang Zhixiao takes up Xi Jinping's speech at the National Conference on Propaganda and Ideological Work. The question is how to build a socialist ideology with strong cohesion and guiding power in the new era. Shang's answer is that Marxist propaganda and education must be done well (zuohao) and made strong (zuoqiang), above all by studying, understanding and applying Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era.

The commentary has two main parts. The first argues that Marxist education is the foundation for the mission Xi assigns to propaganda and ideological work: to hold high the banner, rally the people, nurture new people, promote culture and present China's image. The second sets out how the work itself should develop, through its content and system on one side and its forms and effects on the other.

In the first part, Shang holds that propaganda work is work on people, and that people need a scientific worldview, outlook on life and values before beliefs and confidence can take hold. Marxism, in Shang's account, gives thinking and method (historical materialism, the theory of surplus value, dialectics), practical wisdom about life, and a vision of free and all-round human development that includes the spiritual dimension. In the second part, "doing well" means setting direction and method, with content that is targeted and accepted by its audience. "Making strong" means shaping opinion, uniting propaganda forces across fields and building a multi-level structure. Content should be built on basic Marxist theory, stress the Party's innovative theory, be popularised and stay tied to the people's interests. Forms should keep pace with the times and avoid formalism and dogmatism.

Shang concludes that the work must answer why, what and how by drawing on Xi's remarks on Marxist guidance in philosophy and social sciences and on Marxism's historical standing at the 200th anniversary of Marx's birth. The commentary calls for sustained, constantly renewed effort. It cites Marx, Lenin and Deng Xiaoping to support the claim that Marxism is persuasive when it is thorough and plain. Read the original if you want a short example of how Party-affiliated scholars framed the tasks of ideological education after the 2018 propaganda conference.
quoteEn: Doing it well concerns direction and path; making it strong concerns intensity and effect.
quoteZh: 做好，管方向，管路径；做强，管力度，管效果。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's guiding ideology, written into the Party constitution in 2017 and the state constitution in 2018. It is presented officially as the latest result of adapting Marxism to China.

glossary.zh: 举旗帜、聚民心、育新人、兴文化、展形象
glossary.pinyin: jǔ qízhì, jù mínxīn, yù xīnrén, xīng wénhuà, zhǎn xíngxiàng
glossary.en: hold high the banner, rally the people, nurture new people, promote culture and present China's image
glossary.literal: raise the banner, gather popular support, cultivate new people, revitalise culture, display the image
glossary.explanation: The five-part mission of propaganda and ideological work set out by Xi Jinping at the 2018 national conference on the subject.
The Party's broad field of work covering ideology, media, education and culture. In Chinese usage "propaganda" (xuānchuán) is the standard term and is not pejorative.

t: The Marxist implications of comprehensively deepening reform
zh: 全面深化改革的马克思主义意蕴
paras: Writing in 2018, Yang Ming asks what Marxist worldview and methodology lie behind the policy of comprehensively deepening reform adopted since the 18th Party Congress (2012). The article argues that the Central Committee with Xi Jinping at its core has answered why, what and how to reform in a way that represents the concentrated application of Marxism's outlook on reform and development in the new era. For Yang, this shows a creative use of Marxist philosophy.

The article, published in Red Flag Manuscripts, is organised in three parts. Each takes one component of Marxist philosophy as the lens: the Marxist view of the people, the Marxist view of practice, and the Marxist view of contradiction. Each part is built mainly from Xi Jinping's statements on reform, which Yang arranges under numbered sub-headings and links to classical Marxist propositions.

On the view of the people, Yang argues that making 'happiness for the people' the mission of reform, treating the masses as its source of strength, and using the people's sense of gain (huodegan) as the test of results reflect historical materialism. Yang calls this the dividing line between materialist and idealist views of reform. The 'three whether' criteria echo Deng Xiaoping's 'three favourables'. On the view of practice, the article stresses the people as the subject of practice, a human-centred purpose, solid implementation ('hard work makes a nation flourish') and innovation as the first driving force of development. On the view of contradiction, Yang presents Xi's approach as a dialectical unity of the 'two-point' and 'key-point' theories. This means grasping principal contradictions, pursuing reform that is systematic, integrated and coordinated, and following laws of reform such as 'crossing the river by feeling the stones', which Yang describes as consistent with Marxist epistemology.

Yang concludes that these three dimensions make the reform programme an embodiment of Marxist methodology. The article also lists methodological principles it attributes to Xi: 'five relationships' in thinking and 'five relationships' in policy, such as top-level design and experimentation, and bold yet steady steps. The text is an exposition of official thought rather than a critical appraisal. Read the original if you want to see how Chinese Party theorists in 2018 tied Xi Jinping's reform discourse to Marxist categories of people, practice and contradiction.
quoteEn: These statements fundamentally settle whom comprehensively deepening reform should trust, rely on and serve. They are the dividing line between materialist and idealist conceptions of history on the question of reform, and the core test of whether reform adheres to Marxism.
quoteZh: 这一系列重要论述，从根本上解决了全面深化改革相信谁、依靠谁、为了谁的问题，是改革问题上唯物史观和唯心史观的分水岭，也是判断改革是否坚持马克思主义的核心体现。

glossary.explanation: The reform agenda announced at the Third Plenum of the 18th Central Committee (2013). It calls for coordinated reform across economic, political, cultural, social and ecological fields.
A term popularised under Xi Jinping from 2015. It refers to the tangible benefits people feel they receive from development and reform, and is used as a criterion for judging reform.
Deng Xiaoping's 1992 criteria for judging reform: whether it favours the growth of socialist productive forces, national strength and people's living standards.

glossary.en: crossing the river by feeling the stones
glossary.explanation: A saying associated with Deng Xiaoping and Chen Yun, describing gradual, experimental reform. The article treats it as consistent with Marxist epistemology.
A term for centrally planned, overall design of reform, often paired with local experimentation.

t: Reform and opening up demonstrates the powerful vitality of Marxism
zh: 改革开放彰显马克思主义强大生命力
paras: Writing in the People's Daily on 21 September 2018, in the year of Marx's 200th birthday and the 40th anniversary of reform and opening up, Li Jingzhi argues that China's reform record shows the strong vitality of Marxism. In Li's account, reform and opening up was carried out under Marxist guidance, and its achievements also prove the vitality of socialism with Chinese characteristics.

This short commentary has four steps. It first states that reform kept to Marxism and the Party's basic line, then traces how Marxism was combined with China's conditions in three historical periods. It next turns to theoretical innovation during reform, and ends by acknowledging setbacks while affirming socialism's prospects.

Li holds that Marxism's vitality lies in its universality, which allows it to be combined with each country's concrete conditions, and in its continued development with practice. The author describes three leaps: from the revolutionary era to "standing up", from reform to "becoming prosperous", and in the new era to "becoming strong". Li presents reform as avoiding both dogmatic understanding of Marxism and its rejection, and as avoiding both a closed, rigid old path and an "evil path" of changing the Party's banner. Li cites innovations such as the theories of the primary stage of socialism, the essence of socialism and the socialist market economy.

Li concedes that applying Marxism has not been smooth, but calls difficulties temporary and the outlook for socialism bright. Citing China's rise to the world's second-largest economy and rising living standards, Li concludes that socialism can perfect itself through reform and that Marxism still holds the high ground of truth and morality. Read the original if you want a brief example of the official People's Daily argument linking the 40 years of reform to Marxism's vitality.
quoteEn: The vitality of Marxism is concentrated in the fact that it develops continuously as practice develops, constantly achieving theoretical innovation.
quoteZh: 马克思主义的生命力集中体现在它随着实践发展而不断发展，不断实现理论创新。

glossary.explanation: The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched in China in late 1978 under Deng Xiaoping.
The official name for China's path of socialist development since reform began, combining Party leadership with market-oriented reform.
An official thesis, formalised in the 1980s, that China is in a long initial phase of socialism owing to its underdeveloped productive forces.
The official term, adopted in 1992, for China's economic system combining market mechanisms with public ownership and state guidance.

t: Grasping the laws of ideological work so that Party ideological development is truly put into practice
zh: 深入把握思想建设的规律 将思想建设真正落到实处
paras: This commentary, first published in the People's Daily in September 2018, asks how the Communist Party of China can make its ideological development (sixiang jianshe) effective in practice. Yang Deshan starts from Xi Jinping's remarks at the meeting marking the 200th anniversary of Marx's birth, which credit the Party's growth to its emphasis on building the Party ideologically and strengthening it through theory. Yang argues that ideological development is foundational and that it must follow several regularities.

The piece is a short, five-part argument. After an introduction, each section names one requirement: ideological work should be led by political development, grounded in theoretical study, secured by institutions, carried by effective vehicles, and supported by mechanisms for evaluating results. It draws on the 19th Party Congress (2017) report and on campaigns held since the 18th Party Congress (2012).

Yang contends that political development, placed first by the 19th Party Congress, gives ideological work its direction: members must align with the Central Committee in thought, and ideals and values must sustain a healthy political ecology in the Party. Firm conviction is said to rest on study of Marxism, of history and of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. Yang adds that institutionalising ideological measures, for example study and Party-spirit education systems, has been a mark of the period since 2012. Campaigns such as the mass line education campaign, the "Three Stricts and Three Honests" and "Two Studies, One Action" are presented as vehicles, with the "Remain true to the original aspiration" campaign as the next one.

On evaluation, Yang admits that results are hard to quantify but says assessment is still needed to stop ideological work becoming formalistic, marginal or entertainment-driven. Suggestions include checking meeting minutes and members' reading notes, and anonymous appraisal by people inside and outside the Party against criteria such as diligence, integrity and willingness to take responsibility. Read the original if you want a concise official statement of how Party ideological work was framed in 2018 and what practical measures were proposed.
quoteEn: Firmness in thought comes from clarity in theory.
quoteZh: 思想上的坚定源自理论上的清醒。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party constitution at the 19th Party Congress in 2017.
The Party's work of shaping members' beliefs, theoretical understanding and values, treated as one basic strand of Party building.
Party building in the political sphere, stressing loyalty to the Central Committee; the 19th Party Congress placed it first among Party-building tasks.

glossary.literal: study the Party constitution and speeches, and act as a qualified Party member
glossary.explanation: A Party education campaign launched in 2016 requiring members to study the Party constitution and Xi Jinping's speeches and to be qualified members.

glossary.zh: “不忘初心、牢记使命”主题教育
glossary.pinyin: “bú wàng chūxīn, láojì shǐmìng” zhǔtí jiàoyù
glossary.en: "Remain true to the original aspiration" campaign
glossary.literal: Do not forget the original aspiration, keep the mission firmly in mind thematic education
glossary.explanation: A Party-wide education campaign proposed in the 19th Party Congress report and later carried out in 2019.

t: Stiffen the spiritual backbone of Communists: firmly grasp the key to ideological building
zh: 挺起共产党人的精神脊梁 牢牢把握思想建设的关键
paras: Writing in the People's Daily in autumn 2018, Geng Hongbin argues that building the Party ideologically is the essential feature of a Marxist party and a long-standing strength of the Chinese Communist Party. In the new era, the author holds, the Party can be made strong only if ideological building keeps its foundational status.

The commentary opens with a short history. It recalls Mao Zedong's principle of building the Party first of all ideologically, so that members join in thought as well as in organisation. It then points to ideological campaigns in the reform period, such as the "Three Stresses" education and the Marxist learning-type party. Finally it credits the series of ideological education drives since the 18th Party Congress (2012) with strengthening the Party's creativity, cohesion and combat capacity.

Geng then names three priorities. The first is firm ideals and convictions, which the author calls the Party's spiritual pillar and which rest on morality, so members must be educated in public and private virtue. The second is stronger theoretical confidence, above all in contemporary Chinese Marxism, which Geng identifies with Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. The third is unified thinking, whose core is staying highly consistent with the Central Committee and upholding its authority.

Geng calls for combating individualism, decentralism, liberalism, departmentalism, factionalism, cliques and double-dealing, and treats consistency with the Central Committee as the basic test of how well ideological building works. Read the original if you want a short, official-register statement of how Party media framed ideological building in 2018.
quoteEn: Without clarity of mind there can hardly be political firmness.
quoteZh: 没有思想上的清醒，就难有政治上的坚定。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018. The article presents it as contemporary Chinese Marxism.
A Party education campaign launched around 1998 under Jiang Zemin. It stressed study, politics and integrity among officials.
One of the 'confidences' in official discourse, meaning confidence in the Party's guiding theory and in Marxism as adapted in China.
One strand of Party building, concerned with members' beliefs, theoretical education and ideals, and treated as its foundation.

t: Ideological development is the foundational work of Party building
zh: 思想建设是党的基础性建设
paras: Writing in the People's Daily in 2018, Song Jin takes up the 19th Party Congress (2017) statement that ideological development is the foundational work of Party building. The commentary argues that this is a scientific judgment grounded in the basic laws of Party building and is important for making the Party strong in the new era.

The piece explains what 'foundational' means, what ideological development should focus on, where communist ideals come from, and how they should be put into practice. It draws on remarks by Deng Xiaoping, Mao Zedong, Liu Shaoqi and Xi Jinping, and on the Communist Manifesto.

Song contends that ideas guide action: the guiding theory determines the Party's line and the conduct of its members, so other aspects of Party building cannot be consolidated without this base. The core task, in Song's reading, is to strengthen the ideals and convictions of Party members and officials, which rest on Marxism's account of social development and on its aim of serving the great majority. Members should therefore study Marxism, especially Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, which Song presents as the latest result of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context. Song adds that ideals must be both lofty and practical, illustrated by the story of Red Army women who cut their only quilt in half for a villager.

Song concludes that, if ideological development is treated as foundational, the Party can withstand the 'four tests' and overcome the 'four dangers'. It would then remain the leading core of socialism with Chinese characteristics. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official Party commentary justifies the priority given to ideals and theoretical study.
quoteEn: It can be said that if the foundation of ideological development is not firmly laid, the other aspects of Party building cannot be consolidated, and the Party's cause cannot develop smoothly.
quoteZh: 可以说，思想建设的基础没打牢，党的其他各方面建设就不可能巩固，党的事业就不可能顺利发展。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party constitution at the 19th Party Congress in 2017.
The official name for China's path, system and theory of socialism since the reform era.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context
glossary.explanation: The official idea that Marxism must be adapted to China's conditions, with each major Party theory presented as a new stage of this process.
Official formula for the challenges facing the Party: ruling, reform and opening up, the market economy, and the external environment.
Official formula for risks to the Party: lack of drive, inadequate ability, detachment from the people, and passivity and corruption.

t: The theoretical essence of the openness of Marxism
zh: 马克思主义开放性特征的理论真谛
paras: Taking up Xi Jinping's description of Marxism, at the 200th anniversary of Marx's birth, as scientific, people-centred, practical and open, this newspaper commentary asks what the openness of Marxism actually means. Kong and Chen argue that openness is a precondition of Marxism's scientific truth and a philosophical expression of dialectical negation. They say it also requires a scientific attitude towards the theory.

The piece has three parts. The first links openness to Marxism's truth and its ability to meet the problems of each era. The second traces its philosophical roots from Spinoza and Hegel to Marx's materialist dialectic. The third turns to attitudes towards Marxism today, citing Engels and Xi.

The authors contend that Marxism remains true because the basic contradictions of capitalism persist and the world is still in the epoch of transition from capitalism to socialism. Applying it, they say, requires the theory itself to stay open and to renew itself for each era. Openness rests on the dialectic of negation, which for Marx treats every existing form as transient and is therefore critical and revolutionary. As an example, Kong and Chen note that Marx and Engels drew no concrete socialist blueprint and did not say whether socialism could have a market economy. They present the political economy of socialism with Chinese characteristics as a case of Marxism's "self-negation".

The authors insist that guidance by Marxism and the basic principles of scientific socialism must never be abandoned, and that Marxism is not a fixed dogma. They present Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era as an original contribution made in this spirit. They also call for closer study of contemporary capitalism and for absorbing the beneficial achievements of human civilisation. Read the original if you want a short, official-line account of how Chinese commentators connect Marxism's openness to dialectics and to current theoretical innovation.
quoteEn: The openness of Marxism reflects its critical and revolutionary attitude towards all theories, ideas and isms, itself included.
quoteZh: 马克思主义开放性特征体现出马克思主义理论对包括自身在内的一切理论、思想和主义皆坚持批判的革命的态度

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018. It is presented officially as the latest adaptation of Marxism to China.
The official name for China's path and system since reform and opening up. It combines Party leadership, a socialist market economy and other features.

t: Contemporary lessons of the debate on the criterion of truth
st: Forty years after 1978
zh: 真理标准问题讨论的当代启示
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in May 2018, forty years after the debate on the criterion of truth, Ren Ping asks what that debate still teaches China. Ren argues that philosophical change leads epochal change, and that the debate's significance shows in the whole course of reform, not only at its start. In Ren's account, it broke the intellectual constraint of the "Two Whatevers", restored the authority of a practice-based, seeking-truth-from-facts Marxism, and opened reform and opening up and the path of socialism with Chinese characteristics.

This short commentary is organised as six lessons, introduced from the standpoint of what Ren calls socialism with Chinese characteristics entering a new era. The lessons concern the relation of philosophy to its age, the responsibility of philosophers, the people-centred value orientation of truth, confidence in the path and in theory, the developing character of truth, and the growth of Marxist philosophy itself. Each links the 1978 debate to present tasks.

Ren's central claim is that the debate joined two questions: how truth is tested and in whose interest. Ren holds that the more consistently practice is taken as the criterion, the more it accords with the people's fundamental interests, since the people are both the subject that tests truth and the beneficiary of its results. Ren also treats the debate as a political event as well as an academic one, which required political courage from philosophers. Ren then argues that truth develops with practice. In this view the "Two Whatevers" mindset must still be rejected, and so must the temporary, unreasonable ideas, institutions and interest structures formed during four decades of reform. Ren cites the shift from "crossing the river by feeling the stones" to modernising the system and capacity of national governance, and from extensive growth to the new development philosophy.

Ren concludes that, tested by forty years of practice, the debate strengthens confidence in the path, theory, system and culture, and that Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era must guide the new era. Ren calls on philosophers to engage with global governance, to build a community with a shared future for mankind, and to create original Chinese theory and discourse rather than retreat into pure scholarship. Ren also points to the flourishing of Marxist philosophy in China since 1978. Read the original if you want a concise, official-register Chinese reading of the 1978 truth-criterion debate and its use in legitimising the new era's tasks.
quoteEn: The debate on the criterion of truth not only opened the Chinese path in practice, but also, in theory, propelled Marxist philosophy into a new era of flourishing development.
quoteZh: 真理标准问题讨论不仅在实践上开辟中国道路，而且在理论上推动马克思主义哲学走向繁荣发展的新时代。

glossary.explanation: A 1977 editorial formula holding that whatever policy decisions Mao Zedong made and whatever instructions he gave must be upheld. Reformers later criticised it as dogmatic, and the 1978 truth-criterion debate challenged it.

glossary.en: debate on the criterion of truth
glossary.literal: discussion of the question of the criterion of truth
glossary.explanation: A 1978 nationwide debate, begun by the article "Practice is the sole criterion for testing truth", which became the ideological basis for ending the Mao-era dogmatism and launching reform.
The policy launched in 1978 under Deng Xiaoping, introducing market-oriented economic reform and opening to the outside world.
The official name for China's model of socialism since the reform era, combining Party leadership with a market economy.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept promoted by Xi Jinping, calling for cooperative global governance and shared development.

t: The philosophical implications of "lucid waters and lush mountains are invaluable assets"
zh: “绿水青山就是金山银山”的哲学意蕴
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in June 2018, Shan Tiping examines the philosophical meaning of Xi Jinping's formula that lucid waters and lush mountains are invaluable assets. The author argues that the formula is a practical guide for handling the relationship between humans and nature in the new era, and that it carries a deep historical dialectic.

The commentary is built around three historical stages: agricultural civilization, industrial civilization, and the present transition towards ecological civilization. It draws on classical Chinese poetry, Mao Zedong's poem "Farewell to the God of Plague", Engels's warning about nature's revenge and Rachel Carson's Silent Spring. It also lists the dates on which Xi developed the formula, from 2005 to the 19th Party Congress (2017).

Shan argues that in agricultural societies green mountains and material wealth were not yet linked, and that low productive forces left people at the mercy of natural disasters. Under capitalist-led industrial civilization, technology turned nature into a treasure house to be conquered. The author claims this system ignored the limits of nature's capacity, piling up wealth while the environment was ruined and humans and nature became mutually alienated. In the present transition, Shan says, the task is both to turn green mountains into material wealth and to turn the pursuit of wealth back towards preserving the mountains.

Shan concludes that the formula's essence is sustainable green development. It should meet people's aspiration for a better life with material security, while keeping the mountains green and the waters flowing in pursuit of a "Beautiful China" and harmony between humans and nature. Read the original if you want a short, officially aligned philosophical-historical reading of this slogan in Chinese ecological civilization discourse.
quoteEn: The scientific thesis that "lucid waters and lush mountains are invaluable assets" contains a profound historical dialectic, and its essence lies in sustainable green development.
quoteZh: “绿水青山就是金山银山”的科学论断，蕴含着深刻的历史辩证法，其本质在于可持续的绿色发展

glossary.explanation: A official Chinese concept for a model of development that places environmental protection alongside economic growth. It was written into Party documents from the 2007 Party Congress and elevated further in later years.

glossary.zh: 绿水青山就是金山银山
glossary.en: lucid waters and lush mountains are invaluable assets
glossary.literal: green waters and green mountains are mountains of gold and silver
glossary.explanation: A slogan Xi Jinping first put forward in 2005 while Party secretary of Zhejiang. It holds that a good environment is itself a form of wealth and that environmental protection and economic development can go together.
An official goal of building a country with a clean environment, promoted in Party documents from the 18th Party Congress (2012) as part of ecological civilization.

t: Leading and driving the revolution in social practice through a revolution in ideas and theory
st: Commemorating the great debate on the criterion of truth and celebrating the 40th anniversary of reform and opening up
zh: 以思想理论革命引领和推动社会实践革命
zhSub: 纪念真理标准大讨论和庆祝改革开放40周年
paras: Writing in 2018, Yan Xiaofeng marks two anniversaries: the 1978 debate on practice as the criterion of truth and forty years of reform and opening up. The article argues that the debate was an ideological revolution that supplied the intellectual starting point for reform, and that theoretical innovation and practical innovation have since advanced together. Yan concludes that a revolution in ideas and theory should keep leading and driving the revolution in social practice.

The piece has three sections. The first traces the path from the debate to the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee (1978). The second reviews how socialism with Chinese characteristics and its theoretical system developed from Deng Xiaoping Theory through the Three Represents and the Scientific Outlook on Development to Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. The third examines the practical and truth-bearing character of Xi's thought, and closes with the 2018 anniversaries of Marx's birth and the Communist Manifesto.

In Yan's account, philosophy can precede social revolution, and the Party's ideological line is at bottom a philosophical principle and a line of cognition. Yan sets the 'two whatevers' against the practice criterion, which he presents as the philosophical basis for correcting the Cultural Revolution's errors, shifting the Party's work to economic construction and launching reform. Yan then describes each generation of Party theory as a response to a problem raised by practice: what socialism is, what kind of Party to build, and what kind of development to pursue. Xi's thought, Yan argues, is tested in practice. Yan points to the changed principal contradiction of society, achievements since the 18th Party Congress (2012) in areas such as Party leadership and full and rigorous self-governance of the Party, and an overall framework built on the Four-sphere Confidence.

Yan concludes that the thought's fundamental principles are Party leadership, a people-centred approach and comprehensive deepening of reform, and that its historical mission is the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Yan presents the 2018 anniversaries as signalling a commitment to emancipating the mind, seeking truth from facts and carrying reform through to the end. Read the original if you want a representative Party-theorist account, from the time of the 40th anniversary, of how the 1978 truth-criterion debate is linked to Xi Jinping Thought and to the Party's own narrative of reform and opening up.
quoteEn: Recognising that the problem has changed already signals the beginning of theoretical innovation.
quoteZh: 发现问题的转化本身就意味着理论创新的开始。

glossary.explanation: A 1977 editorial formula holding that whatever policy decisions Mao Zedong made, and whatever instructions he gave, must be upheld. Deng Xiaoping and reformers opposed it.
The policy of economic reform and engagement with the outside world launched at the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee in December 1978.
Jiang Zemin's theory that the Party represents advanced productive forces, advanced culture and the fundamental interests of the overwhelming majority of the people.
Hu Jintao's guiding concept emphasising people-centred, comprehensive, coordinated and sustainable development.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.
Official formula of confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: Official term for the Party-discipline and anti-corruption drive promoted since the 18th Party Congress in 2012.

t: The contemporary value of China's fine traditional culture
zh: 中国优秀传统文化的当代价值
paras: Writing in Red Flag Manuscripts (2018, no. 12), Shi Huanxiang asks what China's fine traditional culture contributes today. The author argues that, as the only ancient civilisation to have continued without interruption, China holds cultural resources that should be given creative transformation and innovative development and be merged with contemporary Chinese culture. Shi presents this as a necessary requirement of the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

The article is organised in five sections. Each takes one field in which traditional culture is said to have contemporary value: the adaptation of Marxism to Chinese conditions, the socialist market economy, cultural confidence, the core socialist values, and the solution of global problems. Shi draws on Confucian and other classical sayings, on Mao Zedong, and on Xi Jinping's statements about the Party as the faithful heir of traditional culture.

Shi's central move is to treat tradition as a source from which modern theory and policy are continuously renewed. Marxism, described as a foreign-born body of thought, is said to have become Chinese by merging with concepts such as "seeking truth from facts", people-as-the-base thinking, "xiaokang" and "harmony", and Shi lists Party doctrines from the mass line to a community with a shared future for mankind as transformations of such ideas. For the market economy, the author argues that the traditional view of righteousness and profit can check money worship and that honesty and trustworthiness can support a contract and credit economy, while granting that the old righteousness-over-profit outlook had historical limits. Shi also claims that China's openness to Buddhism and to Arab and Persian culture shows an inclusive trait that sustains cultural confidence against Western cultural hegemony. The core socialist values at national, social and individual levels are said to correspond to the traditional sequence from rectifying the heart to bringing peace to the world.

Shi concludes that tradition and the core socialist values stand in a relationship of source and stream. The author further holds that ideas of harmony, good-neighbourliness, mutual benefit and harmony between humans and nature offer "Chinese wisdom" for global governance, and links the ancient Silk Road to the Belt and Road Initiative. Shi calls for an inclusive approach that respects other civilisations while promoting China's own cultural genes. Read the original if you want a compact example of how a 2018 Party journal framed traditional culture as a resource for Marxist theory, market ethics and foreign policy.
quoteEn: The vitality of a culture lies not in abandoning tradition but in the degree to which it absorbs tradition and recasts it.
quoteZh: 一种文化的活力不是抛弃传统，而是在何种程度上吸收传统、再铸传统。

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal, closely tied to the Chinese Dream, of restoring China's national strength and international standing by the mid-twenty-first century.
A concept promoted by Xi Jinping that calls for firm affirmation of China's own cultural values and vitality. It is listed alongside confidence in the path, theory and system.

A set of twelve values promoted officially since 2012: prosperity, democracy, civility and harmony at state level; freedom, equality, justice and rule of law at society level; patriotism, dedication, integrity and friendship at individual level.
A Chinese initiative launched in 2013 to build infrastructure, trade and cultural links across Eurasia, Africa and beyond.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept advanced by Xi Jinping that calls for shared responsibility and cooperation in addressing global challenges.

glossary.zh: 创造性转化、创新性发展
glossary.explanation: An official formula for how traditional culture should be treated: adapting it to present conditions and developing it further rather than simply preserving or discarding it.

t: Mao Zedong's poetry and the revolutionary spirit of Chinese Communists: Xi Jinping's quotations as an example
zh: 毛泽东诗词彰显中国共产党人的革命精神——以习近平引用毛泽东诗词为例
source: Studies on Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping Theories, 2018 no. 6
paras: Why does Xi Jinping so often quote Mao Zedong's poems and lyrics, and what do the quotations convey? Writing in 2018, Yuan Bingda argues that the quotations are neither ornamental nor mere aesthetic recitation. In the author's reading, they deliberately bring out the revolutionary spirit and the "Chinese spirit" that run through Mao's verse, and they offer that spirit as an inspiration for realising the Chinese Dream of national rejuvenation in the new era.

The article draws on Xi's speeches and writings since the 18th Party Congress (2012). Among them are his 2012 visit to *The Road to Rejuvenation* exhibition, the 2013 symposium marking the 120th anniversary of Mao's birth (where Xi cites Mao's poetry nine times), the 2016 speech marking the Party's 95th anniversary, and his 2014 visit to Peking University. It is organised in three sections: not forgetting the original aspiration and mission; sustaining the fighting spirit; and keeping the Party's youthfulness. Each section pairs Xi's quoted lines with the historical circumstances in which Mao wrote them.

Yuan's first move is a close reading of the two occurrences of "road" in Xi's 2012 remarks. The "mighty pass" line, written in 1935 after the Zunyi Conference, stands for the suffering and resilience of the Chinese nation. The "right path in the world" line, written in 1949, is read as showing that socialism with Chinese characteristics is the historically inevitable path. Second, the author draws out four qualities Xi attributes to Mao through selected lines: iron will (supported by Xi's frequent use of the image of iron), self-confidence, the Long March spirit and the "seize the day" urgency, and perseverance through struggle. Third, the author treats the 1925 poem on Changsha and Xi's remarks to students as a call for young people to carry the cause forward and for the Party to keep its youthfulness.

Yuan concludes that Mao's poetry artistically reproduces the ambition, revolutionary sentiment and spiritual character of the Communists who pursue national rejuvenation. The author holds that, as the Party leads a great social revolution through its own self-reform, it still needs this poeticised revolutionary spirit and the ideals it conveys. Read the original if you want a Chinese-language case study of how Xi's rhetoric uses Mao's poems, with the historical background to each quoted line.
quoteEn: Mao Zedong's poetry is a gem of Mao Zedong Thought, embodies the red cultural gene created by the Communist Party of China, and is an artistic reproduction of the great Chinese spirit.
quoteZh: 毛泽东诗词是毛泽东思想的瑰宝，蕴含中国共产党创造的红色文化基因，是伟大中国精神的艺术再现。

glossary.explanation: A slogan Xi Jinping popularised from late 2012, centred on the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. It was first stated prominently during his visit to the exhibition The Road to Rejuvenation.
The official name for the Party's path of socialist development since reform and opening up. It is presented as Marxism adapted to Chinese conditions.

t: New tasks for ideological and political education arising from the people's growing need for a better spiritual life
zh: 人民日益增长的美好精神生活需要对思想政治教育提出的新课题
source: Research on Ideological Education (Sixiang jiaoyu yanjiu), 2018 no. 3
paras: Writing in 2018, after the 19th Party Congress (2017) declared that the principal contradiction in Chinese society had changed, Yan Xiaofeng asks how ideological and political education should respond to the people's growing need for a better spiritual life. The contradiction is now between the people's ever-growing need for a better life and unbalanced and inadequate development. Yan's thesis is that a better spiritual life is an integral part of a better life, that ideological and political education is an effective route to meeting it, and that the field must be renewed to do so.

The article has four parts. The first defines the need for a better spiritual life and places it in the new era of socialism with Chinese characteristics. The second explains why ideological and political education is an important channel for meeting it. The third identifies where current practice falls short. The fourth sets out four directions for innovation.

Yan treats cultural life as the process and spiritual life as its purpose, and holds that spiritual life, like material life, has higher and lower levels. A better spiritual life involves a relaxed mind, a unified personality, ideals, sincerity, aesthetic pursuit and independence. Ideological and political education, Yan argues, supplies its content and models (the Lei Feng campaign is an example), helps people resolve conflicts such as that between survival pressures and the life of the mind, and offers practical paths grounded in Marxism's unity of practice and spiritual activity. Yan then names three weaknesses: the function is undervalued, with the aesthetic dimension neglected; research on it, both theoretical and empirical, is insufficient; and guidance is weak, shown in the author's account by people turning to religion, regarding the education as mere preaching, or by students who feel spiritually adrift.

Yan calls for four measures: firm ideals and convictions, including communist ideals and the common ideal of socialism with Chinese characteristics; making the core socialist values a conscious commitment; cultivation through the culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics, drawing on traditional, revolutionary and advanced socialist culture; and resistance to decadent and backward culture. Read the original if you want a Party-theory account of how ideological and political education is being repositioned around spiritual needs after the 19th Party Congress.
quoteEn: Without a better spiritual life, however abundant material life may be, that life is incomplete and can hardly be called a better life.
quoteZh: 没有美好精神生活，即使物质生活再丰裕，这种生活也是残缺不全的，也很难称得上是美好生活。

glossary.explanation: In Party theory, the central contradiction that shapes a stage of social development. The 19th Party Congress (2017) restated it as the contradiction between unbalanced and inadequate development and the people's growing need for a better life.
The Party-state's system of education in ideology, politics and morality, carried out in schools, the Party and society, and also a discipline in Chinese universities.
A set of 24 characters in 12 values promoted since the 18th Party Congress (2012) at national, social and individual levels.
The official name for China's path, theory and system of socialism since reform and opening up.

t: Reflection and reconstruction: thoughts on the predicament of modern moral development
zh: 反思与重构：基于现代道德发展困境的思考
source: Studies on Ideological Education (《思想教育研究》), 2018 no. 2
paras: Deng and Zhang take up the question of why morality in contemporary China has become superficial and marginal, and how it might be rebuilt. Writing in 2018 and opening with Xi Jinping's call to strengthen society-wide ideological and moral construction, they argue that the root of the predicament is a loss of moral belief among individuals, not a shortage of rules or of moral education. Their answer is a moral system that combines virtue and norms, and that follows the social development of human nature.

The article is in three parts. The first diagnoses three symptoms of the predicament: the instrumentalisation of morality for utility, moral nihilism and moral hypocrisy. The second looks for deeper causes in the over-expansion of normative ethics and in China's social modernization. The third proposes two paths of reconstruction, drawing on Aristotle, Kant, Habermas and Alasdair MacIntyre.

In the authors' account, market competition, materialism and imported Western individualism and liberalism have pushed traditional moral values aside. Scepticism and the liberal priority of rights over the good then supply nihilism with its intellectual support. The authors add that law can restrain outward wrongdoing but cannot reach conscience. Hypocrisy, they say, arises when moral aims are cut off from people's real needs. At a deeper level, rule-based ethics asks only what one should do and so sees "rules but not people". Rule systems have also detached from the lifeworld and, in Habermas's phrase, colonised it. Modernization has dissolved the kin-based order and dissolved faith in a transcendent moral authority. People now live as public citizens rather than natural persons, and virtue ethics loses its practical force.

The authors call for a moral system that keeps virtue and norms together, since each presupposes the other. Norms secure social order and a baseline ethics. Virtue is the ultimate aim of moral construction, which they link to the 19th Party Congress (2017) restatement of fostering virtue through education. They also hold that moral cultivation should follow the socialisation of human nature. Cognition, an innate potential for goodness and repeated internalisation and externalisation in the lifeworld would lead morality to become a person's "second nature". Read the original if you want a philosophical, virtue-ethics diagnosis of China's moral difficulties, written within the field of ideological and political education.)
quoteEn: Normative ethics in effect advocates a value standard of "seeing only rules and not people".
quoteZh: 规范伦理实则倡导了一种“只见规则而不见人”的价值标准。

t: Grasping the laws of development in hot-topic research on ideological and political education
zh: 把握思想政治教育热点研究的发展规律
source: Ideological and Political Education Research (思想教育研究), 2018 no. 2
paras: Feng Gang asks what defines a "research hotspot" in ideological and political education and how the field's hotspots develop. Drawing on his own compilation of an annual report on 2017 research hotspots, he argues that hotspots are not subjective inventions but the necessary result of theory and practice advancing together. Understanding their regularities, he holds, is required for deepening theory and advancing the discipline.

The article, published in 2018, has three parts. The first defines hotspot research, its features and its value. The second identifies seven characteristics of the previous year's research, set against the study of Xi Jinping's speech at the national conference on ideological and political work in universities, the 19th Party Congress (2017) and Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. The third draws out three laws of hotspot development.

On the definition, Feng says hotspots must fit their historical setting, the state of a still relatively young discipline (about thirty years old, with basic categories, boundaries and paradigms unsettled) and a clear practical orientation. The seven features of 2017 research are: firm adherence to the correct direction under Marxism; adaptation to the new era; fit with the stage of economic and social development; responsiveness to new demands of practice; greater depth; wider horizons; and varied methods. Examples include research on internal motivation, red culture, online education and the use of big data and the CIPP evaluation model. The three laws are that hotspots emerge from the deepening and extension of basic theory, from the development and needs of practice, and from a two-way interaction between hotspot research and the discipline that forms a closed loop.

Feng concludes that researchers must keep pace with the times, work from problems and plan within the context of educational modernization and the network age. He predicts that future hotspots may include interdisciplinary study of basic categories, process laws and policy; the characteristics of university students; online education models; carriers and methods; and collaborative education in universities. Read the original if you want a Chinese insider's overview of how the field of ideological and political education maps its own research priorities as of 2017–2018.
quoteEn: By driving hotspot research within the development of the discipline, and realising the discipline's development through hotspot research, in a repeating cycle, a benign interaction forms between hotspot research and disciplinary development, so that both advance together.
quoteZh: 在学科发展中推动热点研究，在热点研究中实现学科发展，往复循环，从而形成思想政治教育热点研究与思想政治教育学科发展的良性互动，实现二者的共同发展。

glossary.explanation: A Chinese academic discipline and a field of Party and school practice concerned with shaping the political outlook, ideals and values of citizens, especially students. It is taught in universities and studied as a subject in its own right.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's guiding ideology associated with Xi Jinping, written into the Party constitution at the 19th Party Congress in 2017.

t: The sociology of ideological and political education: aims, problems and ways beyond
zh: 思想政治教育社会学：目标、问题及超越
source: Research on Ideological Education (思想教育研究), 2018 no. 4
paras: Shen Dong and Sun Qi'ang take up the sociology of ideological and political education, a proposed sub-discipline that they say is still at an exploratory, early stage. The article asks what the sub-discipline is for, what obstacles it faces and how to overcome them. Their thesis is that it should not be read as a mere "marriage" of ideological and political education with sociology. In their view it is the product of the parent discipline differentiating and of a shift in research paradigm.

The article has four sections. The first sets the background: two historical transformations of ideological and political education, in 1949 and in 1978, and the discipline's reorganisation in 2005 when Marxist theory became a first-level discipline. The second diagnoses the sub-discipline's difficulties. The third sets out its tasks: empirical research, theory-building and policy advice. The fourth draws conclusions on the relation between sub-discipline and parent discipline.

The authors argue that ideological and political education succeeded in building an academic discipline but became marginal and weak in social practice, because its research paradigm remained tied to "work" and "experience". They identify three problems for the sub-discipline: scarce original knowledge, which is mostly borrowed from the parent discipline or sociology; insufficient theory of its own; and closed disciplinary boundaries, with sociologists showing little interest. They propose strengthening empirical study of what actually happens in society, building theory that can talk to other social sciences, and offering policy advice. They link the "what is", "why" and "how" questions about state and society, and say the sub-discipline supplies the "why" and adds a "state" and "ideological" perspective.

The authors conclude that the sub-discipline should draw out the "social attributes" of a field long confined to a state perspective. It should spur the growth of the parent discipline and its related branches, and carry out the applied research they say is still missing. They add that the field must meet the challenges of globalisation and plural social thought. Read the original if you study how Chinese scholars debate the disciplinary standing, methods and social relevance of ideological and political education.
quoteEn: The sociology of ideological and political education is not a simple repetition or mechanical superposition of ideological and political education and sociology.
quoteZh: 思想政治教育社会学不是思想政治教育与社会学的简单重复与机械叠加

glossary.explanation: The Party-state's system of ideological, moral and political instruction, taught in schools and run as an academic discipline under Marxist theory. The article treats it as both a social practice and a field of study.

glossary.en: sociology of ideological and political education
glossary.explanation: A proposed sub-discipline that applies sociological perspectives and methods to ideological and political education. The article assesses its aims and difficulties.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义理论一级学科
glossary.explanation: A top-tier category in China's official disciplinary catalogue. In 2005 Marxist theory became one, with ideological and political education as one of its six second-level disciplines.

t: New starting point, new positioning, new journey: building ideological and political education for the new era
zh: 新起点新定位新征程：迈向新时代的思想政治教育建设之路
source: Ideological Education Research (Sixiang jiaoyu yanjiu), 2018 no. 4
paras: Writing in 2018, shortly after the 19th Party Congress (2017), Zhang Kai and Zhang Shujun ask how ideological and political education should respond to the new era of socialism with Chinese characteristics. They argue that the field has a new starting point, a new positioning and a new journey. Each follows from the change in the principal social contradiction, from the task of national rejuvenation, and from Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era.

The article has three main sections. The first describes the changed environment and problems of ideological and political education. The second sets out its redefined goals and value as a spiritual driving force for national rejuvenation. The third turns to the guiding programme and practical mechanisms for the new journey, which the authors summarise as educating people through all aspects, the whole process and wholeheartedly.

In the first section, the authors say the principal contradiction is now between the people's growing need for a better life and unbalanced and inadequate development. They identify three consequences. Public spiritual needs have become more urgent and varied. Social contradictions have become fragmented, so the 'reality' that education must engage is now many realities. New technologies and 'time-space compression' (a term the authors take from David Harvey) have produced interwoven social interactions for which the field lacks analytical and response mechanisms. In the second section, they assign it three tasks: strengthening the Four-sphere Confidence and the Party's cohesion, raising citizens' cultural and moral quality through core socialist values, and building cultural soft power so as to tell China's story and guard ideological 'territory'. In the third, they make Xi Jinping Thought the basic content and theoretical foundation of the field. They also apply its methodology, which they list as people-centredness, practicality, innovation and scientific professionalism, and integrate Xi's specific directives on the work into the whole process.

The authors conclude that ideological and political education remains the Party's 'magic weapon' and is more important in the new era. Improving it, they say, must be rooted in propagating and implementing Xi Jinping Thought, both its content and its methods. They call on practitioners to study it thoroughly themselves, to reject formalism and detachment from the masses, and to pursue innovation and professionalisation. Read the original if you want an example of how Chinese scholars in 2018 tied ideological and political education to the new principal contradiction and to Xi Jinping Thought.
quoteEn: Ideological and political education work in the new era is an important spiritual driving force for national rejuvenation.
quoteZh: 新时代的思想政治教育工作是民族复兴的重要精神动力

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party constitution at the 19th Party Congress in 2017. It is presented as the latest stage in adapting Marxism to China.

A Marxist-Maoist concept for the central tension that shapes a period of development. The 19th Party Congress redefined it as the gap between people's need for a better life and unbalanced, inadequate development.
Official slogan calling for confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics.

glossary.literal: great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal of restoring China's strength and international standing, tied to the 'two centenary goals' of 2021 and 2049.
The system of education, in schools and the wider society, that conveys the Party's ideology, political stance and moral values.
A twelve-term official set of values promoted since 2012, covering the national, social and individual levels.

t: The Chinese people are a people with a great spirit of dreaming
zh: 中国人民是具有伟大梦想精神的人民
paras: Taking up Xi Jinping's statement that the Chinese people are a people with a great spirit of dreaming, Sun Laibin argues in this short commentary (published in Qiushi in 2018) that this spirit is embedded in the Chinese nation's cultural lineage. Sun contends that, if it is kept alive, it will carry the country to the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

The piece has three parts. The first treats the dreaming spirit as a cultural gene, the second as the support that sustained the nation through modern hardship, and the third as the driving force for what Sun calls the Long March of the new era.

Sun reads ancient myths such as Pangu, Kua Fu chasing the sun, Jingwei filling the sea and the Foolish Old Man moving mountains as expressions of a persistent will to realise dreams. Sun links them to modern achievements, including the Shenzhou and Tiangong space programmes, the South-to-North Water Diversion project and the Jiaolong deep-sea submersible. After the Opium War, Sun says, the nation did not lose its confidence but pursued the dream of rejuvenation for over 170 years. The Chinese Dream, in this account, joins family and country sentiment and is described as a dream of peace, development, cooperation and mutual benefit.

Sun concludes that, with socialism with Chinese characteristics in a new era, the Chinese people are closer than ever to rejuvenation, but the final stretch is hard. Sun calls for the spirit to be sustained through great struggle, hard work and a "nail-driving" perseverance, in order to finish building a moderately prosperous society and begin building a modern socialist country. Read the original if you want a compact example of how official Party commentary of 2018 tied national myth and history to the Chinese Dream.
quoteEn: The specific content of great dreams changes with historical conditions, but the spirit of great dreams has always been a powerful support driving the Chinese nation forward.
quoteZh: 伟大梦想的具体内容会随历史条件的改变而改变，但是伟大梦想精神却始终是推动中华民族砥砺前行的有力支撑。

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal of restoring China's national strength and international standing after the 'century of humiliation'. It has been closely tied to the Chinese Dream since 2012.
A slogan Xi Jinping put forward in 2012, defined as national prosperity, national rejuvenation and the people's well-being.
The official name for the Party's development path and system since reform and opening up.
A Confucian-derived term for a comfortable standard of living, used by the Party as a development target.

t: The Chinese people are a people with a great spirit of creativity
zh: 中国人民是具有伟大创造精神的人民
paras: Xin Ming's commentary in Qiushi (2018) argues that the spirit of innovation is the most distinctive endowment of the Chinese nation. In the author's account, this creative spirit has kept a civilisation of more than 5,000 years vital, brought the nation back from modern-era suffering to the threshold of the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, and now carries China towards a moderately prosperous society and a new journey of building a modern socialist country.

The piece moves through three periods: past civilisation, present achievements and future contribution. It cites classical thinkers, inventions, great works of engineering, literature and epics, then post-1978 growth figures and technological projects, and finally China's prospective role in global affairs.

Xin contends that the Chinese people created the country's splendid civilisation, and are now creating a magnificent reality. The article cites GDP of 82.7 trillion yuan, average growth above 8.5% over 40 years of reform and opening up, and scientific projects since the 18th Party Congress (2012). It holds that socialism with Chinese characteristics is the people's own invention under Party leadership, not a copy of any earlier template. It also points to everyday innovations such as high-speed rail, e-commerce and shared bicycles.

Xin concludes that the Chinese people will create a bright future, offering a "Chinese solution" and "alternative" path to modernization for other countries, achieved peacefully rather than through colonial expansion. Ideas such as a community with a shared future for mankind and the Belt and Road Initiative are presented as a new worldview, alongside traditional concepts like "harmony in diversity". Read the original if you want a compact example of how Qiushi framed national creativity and China's global contribution in 2018.
quoteEn: The Chinese people have created a distinctive path of socialism with Chinese characteristics.
quoteZh: 中国人民创造出一条独特的中国特色社会主义道路。

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal, prominent since Xi Jinping's "Chinese Dream" formulation, of restoring China to national strength and prosperity after the modern era of decline.
The official name for the Party's path since reform and opening up, combining one-party leadership and a socialist market economy.
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched in 1978.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept promoted by Xi Jinping that stresses interdependence and shared global governance.
A Chinese infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative launched in 2013, linking China with Eurasia, Africa and beyond.

t: Ideological security education in universities in the age of the mobile internet
zh: 移动互联网时代高校意识形态安全教育研究
paras: Zheng Jie and Xu Qiang ask how Chinese universities should carry out ideological security education now that, in the authors' words, the mobile internet has become the main battlefield of ideological struggle. Writing after the 19th Party Congress (2017), they argue that universities must treat this education as a major strategic task. Its aim is to win over young students and safeguard national ideological security, and the authors say it needs updated concepts, methods and mechanisms.

The article was published in Academic Forum in 2017. It has four parts: the practical reasons for strengthening this education, the opportunities the mobile internet offers, the challenges it poses, and a set of countermeasures. Throughout, the authors rely heavily on quotations from Xi Jinping and the 19th Party Congress report to frame the discussion.

The authors give four reasons for the education. It is a means of countering what they describe as Western ideological infiltration aimed at students. It ensures that students become qualified successors to the socialist cause. It serves the construction of a harmonious campus, and it supports students' healthy, all-round development. They then argue that mobile media strengthen students' role as active participants, extend education beyond classroom and campus, make it more effective than one-way "inculcation", and let schools, families and society work together. The challenges they list are outdated ideas and monotonous methods among some teachers, low media literacy, a complicated online environment, and weak oversight mechanisms.

For the response, Zheng and Xu propose the principle of "teacher-led, student-centred" education. They also call for classroom teaching as the main channel, campus culture and student societies as new fronts, and better media training for teachers and students. Government, universities and new media should work together, and universities should set up information-review bodies. They further propose that universities build coordinated management, evaluation, reward-and-accountability, monitoring and feedback mechanisms, and bring the spirit of the 19th Party Congress into textbooks, classrooms and minds. Read the original if you want a detailed example of how Chinese academic writing in 2017 framed ideological work in universities, and which practical measures it recommended.
quoteEn: Any technology is a double-edged sword.
quoteZh: 任何技术都是一把双刃剑。

glossary.explanation: A concept in Chinese official discourse that treats the dominance and stability of the Party's mainstream ideology as part of national security. It underlies much policy on education and media.

t: Guiding the development of economic globalization with the idea of a community with a shared future for mankind
zh: 以人类命运共同体理念引领经济全球化发展
paras: Writing in Qiushi in 2018, Zhao Kejin asks how economic globalization, whose drawbacks have become more visible since the start of the century, should be understood and steered. The short commentary argues that the idea of a community with a shared future for mankind, presented as China's proposal, can lead globalization in a more open, inclusive, balanced and win-win direction.

The piece opens by citing the 19th Party Congress (2017) report. It then moves through four steps: the irreversibility of globalization, the need for a new guiding idea, the theoretical content of the community idea, and three practical requirements.

Zhao holds that globalization follows from the development of productive forces and technological progress, and has bound national interests together. It is also a "double-edged sword": its problems are global and cannot be solved by one country. Western solutions, whether the neoliberal "Washington Consensus" or the "anti-globalization" current since the financial crisis, are said to serve capital while ignoring workers worldwide and the claims of developing countries. The community idea, in Zhao's account, replaces zero-sum thinking with win-win cooperation and promotes consultation, joint contribution and shared benefits. It requires common development for developing and developed countries, social justice, and sustainable, green development.

Zhao concludes that globalization guided by this idea goes beyond the Western-led globalization of the modern era. It is also described as a remedy for protectionism and populism, bringing innovation in path, theory and institutions toward a more prosperous and harmonious world. Read the original if you want a concise, official-style statement of how the community idea was presented in 2018 as an answer to globalization's problems.
quoteEn: The idea of a community with a shared future for mankind is a new idea of globalization that seeks lasting peace and common prosperity and pushes global governance in a fairer and more rational direction.
quoteZh: 人类命运共同体理念是谋求实现持久和平与共同繁荣、推动全球治理向着更加公正合理方向发展的新全球化理念。

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy and global-governance concept associated with Xi Jinping, promoted from around 2012–13. It stresses interdependence, shared interests and cooperation among states.
The Communist Party of China's national congress held in October 2017, which wrote the community with a shared future idea into Party documents.
A set of market-oriented policy prescriptions associated with neoliberalism and Washington-based institutions, here criticised by the author as favouring capital.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: The distinctive features of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想的鲜明特质
paras: Writing in Red Flag Manuscripts in 2018, Xia Jinwen asks what characterises Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era.
