Xia argues that the Thought sets out the theoretical and practical logic of Marxism and serves as a manifesto and a call to action for socialism with Chinese characteristics in a new era. Four distinctive features are identified.

The short commentary takes each feature in turn: the Thought's roots in its historical moment, its source in practice, its innovative character and its orientation towards the people. It draws on Xi Jinping's statements and on the report to the 19th Party Congress (2017).

On the first feature, Xia says the Thought was produced by the needs of the age. Xia points to changes in the Party's situation, including the "four tests" and "four risks", and in the national situation, where the two centenary goals meet, and in the world situation, described as one of great change. On the second, Xia holds that the Thought was neither devised in the study nor deduced from abstract concepts. It is drawn from practice since the 18th Party Congress (2012) and, in Xia's view, has been tested by results. Xia also presents it as innovative and open, continuing to develop with practice. On the fourth, Xia argues that the people-centred outlook runs through the 19th Party Congress report: development, democracy, the principal contradiction, common prosperity, people's livelihood and Party building.

Xia concludes that the Thought is the latest achievement in adapting Marxism to Chinese conditions and a source of strength for the new journey. Xia presents its people-centred orientation as an inheritance of the historical-materialist view that the people make history, and as already put into practice over the previous five years. Read the original if you want a concise, official-style statement of how Party theorists in 2018 characterised the Thought.
quoteEn: Originating in practice, guiding practice and advancing the development of practice is the most direct annotation of the practical character of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era.
quoteZh: 源于实践、指导实践、推动实践发展，是习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想对实践特性的最直接注解。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party constitution at the 19th Party Congress in 2017.
A goal of prosperity shared by all the people, presented in Party documents as an essential requirement of socialism.
Official goals of a moderately prosperous society by the Party's centenary (2021) and a modern socialist country by the People's Republic's centenary (2049).

glossary.pinyin: sì dà kǎoyàn hé sì dà fēngxiǎn
glossary.explanation: Official shorthand for challenges to the Party's rule. The tests are governing, reform and opening up, the market economy and the external environment. The risks are lack of drive, inadequate ability, detachment from the people, and corruption.

t: The freedom enslaved by neo-imperialism: a critique of neoliberalism
st: With a critique of Hayek's The Road to Serfdom
zh: 新帝国主义奴役的自由：评新自由主义
zhSub: 兼评哈耶克的《通向奴役的道路》
source: Journal of Hebei University of Economics and Business, 2017 no. 4
paras: Yu Bin's article, first published in the Journal of Hebei University of Economics and Business in 2017, offers a Marxist critique of neoliberalism. It argues that neoliberalism, including as set out in Hayek's The Road to Serfdom, stands for the freedom to exploit and enslave workers and serves as a policy and hegemonic tool of what the author calls neo-imperialism.

The text has three parts. The first takes up a professor's "steamed bun" parable about supply-side reform and reads it as an attempt to steer China's reform towards tax and fee cuts in the neoliberal supply-side tradition. The second examines Hayek's book and the position of workers under state capitalism and neoliberal capitalism. The third examines how neoliberal doctrine on markets, trade, globalisation and international institutions benefits neo-imperialist states.

Yu holds that the parable misdiagnoses the problem. Goods that are too dear to sell, in Yu's view, are not overcapacity, and tax cuts would not lower prices much or help the poor who buy cheap steamed buns. Yu also argues that China's reform is supply-side structural reform, which adjusts structure and relies on innovation, not tax-cutting. On Hayek, Yu argues that the "socialism" he attacks is Nazi state socialism and Second International revisionism, which Yu treats as forms of state capitalism and not Marxist scientific socialism. Yu reads his passages on unemployment, minimum wages and postwar austerity as defending the exploitation of workers. Yu also rejects the supposed "iron law" that wages must grow more slower than productivity, using a numerical example to argue that the law holds only where there is no surplus-value exploitation.

Yu contends that neoliberalism rose together with neo-imperialism in the 1970s, as Keynesian state intervention obstructed the plunder of other countries' resources. Equal opportunity, free trade, privatisation and international organisations such as the IMF, the World Bank and the WTO are described as instruments that open developing countries to transnational capital. Yu cites Latin America under the Washington Consensus, and criticises the privatisation of Chinese state enterprises and utilities as a departure from the principle of unwaveringly consolidating and developing the public sector. Read the original if you want an example of how a Chinese Marxist economist in 2017 linked the domestic supply-side reform debate to a critique of Hayek and neoliberal globalisation.
quoteEn: But the neoliberalism he advocates, that is, the liberalism of extreme individualism, is what represents the freedom to exploit and enslave.
quoteZh: 但是，他所鼓吹的新自由主义也就是极端个人主义的自由主义，才代表着剥削与奴役的自由。

glossary.explanation: An economic policy line announced by Xi Jinping in 2015 that aims to improve the quality and structure of supply, cutting overcapacity and promoting innovation. The article contrasts it with Western supply-side tax-cutting.

glossary.zh: 毫不动摇巩固和发展公有制经济
glossary.pinyin: háo bù dòngyáo gǒnggù hé fāzhǎn gōngyǒuzhì jīngjì
glossary.en: unwaveringly consolidating and developing the public sector
glossary.explanation: One half of the official principle known as the Two Unwaverings, which pairs support for the public sector with support for the non-public sector. The article invokes it against privatisation.
The article's term for the latest phase of imperialism, taking shape from the 1970s. It is marked, in Yu's account, by weakened state sovereignty and free plunder of other countries' resources.
Following Lenin, the article uses it for capitalism fused with state power, as in Nazi Germany. It treats this as a rival form of capitalism to neoliberalism.

t: Opening a new realm of governing the country in accordance with the Constitution
zh: 开创依宪治国新境界
paras: Writing shortly after the First Session of the 13th National People's Congress (2018) adopted amendments to the Constitution, Ma Yide offers a commentary on what the revision means. The author's thesis is that the amendments are a major historical contribution by the Party Central Committee with Xi Jinping at its core, and that they will let the Party lead the people to "a new realm" of governing the country in accordance with the Constitution. Ma frames the revision as the constitutional expression of the Party's governance experience since the 18th Party Congress (2012) and of the main ideas and policies set by the 19th Party Congress (2017).

The piece is organised around four main amendments, followed by a briefer survey of the rest. It takes in turn the inclusion of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era in the preamble, the new wording on Party leadership in Article 1, the removal of the two-term limit for the state president, and the creation of supervisory commissions. It closes with other changes: local legislative powers for cities divided into districts, the oath of allegiance to the Constitution, the new Constitution and Law Committee, socialist core values, and the united front.

Ma argues that each change brings the Constitution into line with the Party's established leadership arrangements. Writing "the leadership of the Communist Party of China is the defining feature of socialism with Chinese characteristics" into Article 1 gives Party leadership greater institutional and legal force and, in the author's view, helps the Party escape the historical cycle of rise and fall. On the presidency, Ma says the change makes the Constitution consistent with the "trinity" leadership system (Party general secretary, state president and military commission chairman), since Party rules and the military commission provisions already set no two-term limit. The author adds that this does not mean lifelong tenure, citing Party-constitution provisions on retirement. On supervision, Ma notes that 11 of the 21 amendments concern supervisory commissions, and argues that these commissions, working jointly with Party discipline inspection bodies, will give full coverage of public officials and unify Party oversight with state supervision.

Ma concludes that the amended Constitution is the legal elevation of Xi Jinping Thought and combines the Party's confidence in governing with its consciousness of the rule of law. The author also claims it widens the paths open to developing countries towards legal modernisation and offers "Chinese wisdom and a Chinese approach" to problems of the rule of law worldwide. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned account of how a Party-state legal scholar justified the 2018 constitutional amendments, especially the presidential term change and the supervisory system.
quoteEn: Writing \"the leadership of the Communist Party of China is the defining feature of socialism with Chinese characteristics\" into the Constitution makes the Party's leadership position in the state explicit at the level of the essential character of socialism.
quoteZh: 将“中国共产党领导是中国特色社会主义最本质的特征”写入宪法，从社会主义本质属性的高度明确党在国家中的领导地位

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party constitution in 2017 and into the state Constitution's preamble in 2018.
The Party's official name for its path, system and theory of socialism since the reform era.
New state anti-corruption bodies created from 2016 and given constitutional status in 2018. They cover all public officials and work jointly with Party discipline inspection organs.
The practice of one person holding the posts of Party general secretary, state president and chairman of the Central Military Commission.
The Party's system of alliance with non-Party groups and sectors, which the article says the amendments strengthen.

t: Understanding Marx's thought on freedom of the press accurately
zh: 准确理解马克思的新闻出版自由思想
source: Journalism and Communication Studies (新闻与传播研究), 2017 no. 10
paras: Yuan Xiuli takes issue with a reading that cites Marx's statements on press freedom (that it is a 'universal right' of everyone and a 'privilege of the human spirit') to argue that Marx and Engels defended a free press for all citizens. On this reading, the Soviet Union and China, by adopting centralised press systems, broke sharply with Marx. Yuan argues that this reading misreads Marx and Engels, and that quoting isolated phrases without their context produces distortion.

The article rests on three texts from Marx's Rheinische Zeitung period: 'Remarks on the Latest Prussian Censorship Instruction' (1843), the first article on the debates of the Sixth Rhine Province Assembly on press freedom, and the 'Trial of the Neue Rheinische Zeitung'. It proceeds in five sections: Marx's attack on Prussian censorship and support for bourgeois press freedom; his critical view of capitalist press freedom; the shift in his thinking from idealism to materialism; the absence of a press freedom common to all estates; and his views on press freedom and law.

Yuan's central claim is that Marx's early view was still shaped by Hegelian idealism, grounding freedom in reason and human nature, but that the Prussian reality pushed him towards material interests and class. In the Assembly debates, Yuan notes, the princely, knightly, urban and peasant estates held different positions, so no single demand could stand for 'everyone'. Yuan reads this as an early germ of historical materialism. Marx later saw that capital's control of publishing, and the legal system as an expression of ruling-class will, make press freedom class-bound under capitalism. Yuan also holds that Marx's early hope that the Prussian state would legislate press freedom was contradictory.

Yuan concludes that Marx never gave up the pursuit of press freedom, but came to place it on a scientific basis: in class society no press freedom exists above state and class, and universal freedom depends on the development of the productive forces and the resolution of class relations. Yuan therefore rejects the call to drop class analysis in favour of a 'citizens' freedom' framework. Read the original if you want a Chinese Marxist argument, built on the Rheinische Zeitung texts, that class analysis of press freedom is faithful to Marx.
quoteEn: Marx recognised that within the state, a press freedom that is independent of and transcends the state and class does not exist.
quoteZh: 马克思认识到，在国家中，独立的、超越国家、阶级的新闻出版自由并不存在。

t: Theoretical guidance for the shift to a stage of high-quality development
zh: 转向高质量发展阶段的理论指引
paras: Writing in early 2018, Hou Weimin takes up the Central Economic Work Conference's formal naming of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era in the economic field. Hou argues that this body of economic thought gives theoretical guidance for China's shift from a stage of high-speed growth to a stage of high-quality development.

The commentary, first published in Anhui Daily, is organised in four parts. They deal with the institutional basis and inherent advantages of high-quality development, its guiding concepts and methodology, its goals and requirements, and its ultimate purpose and criteria of judgement. Hou draws mainly on Xi Jinping's statements and the report to the 19th Party Congress (2017).

Hou's central move is to read the new development philosophy as the methodology of high-quality development and to link each of its five concepts to Marxian political economy. Innovation applies Marx's theory of productive forces, coordination reflects proportional allocation of production factors and social labour time, green development unites value and use-value production, opening up follows Marx's turn from national to world history, and sharing is the basic purpose of socialist production. Hou also argues that the modernized economic system must rest on the real economy, with finance and the virtual economy serving it in a subordinate role.

Hou concludes that the primary stage of socialism, the Two Unwaverings and Party leadership of economic work give high-quality development its institutional footing. Its end point is people's well-being, shown in priority for education, employment quality and income, and social security that is both done to the best of one's ability and within one's means. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official commentary in 2018 tied Xi's economic thought to Marxist political economy.
quoteEn: The modernized economic system must handle correctly the relationship between the real economy and financial development; modern finance is an important part of the socialist economy with Chinese characteristics for a new era and must serve the real economy.
quoteZh: 现代化经济体系需要正确处理好实体经济和金融发展之间的关系，现代金融是新时代中国特色社会主义经济的重要组成部分，需要发挥其服务实体经济的功能。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义经济思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì jīngjì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The official name of Xi's guiding ideology, adopted in 2017. The article concerns its economic component, named by the Central Economic Work Conference in December 2017.
Five concepts announced in 2015: innovation, coordination, green development, openness and sharing. They serve as official guidance for economic policy.
An official term for growth that stresses quality and efficiency over speed. It was declared the mark of the new stage of China's economy at the 19th Party Congress (2017).
The Party's official account of China's present historical position. It is used to justify a mixed economy with public ownership as the mainstay.
The formula of unwaveringly consolidating and developing the public sector and unwaveringly encouraging, supporting and guiding the non-public sector.

t: Correctly understanding the shift in the principal contradiction facing Chinese society
zh: 正确认识我国社会主要矛盾的转化
paras: Writing in the People's Daily on 30 March 2018, Lin Zhaomu takes up how the principal contradiction in Chinese society should be understood and formulated. Lin argues that the 19th Party Congress (2017) was right to hold that the contradiction is now one between people's ever-growing needs for a better life and unbalanced and inadequate development. In Lin's account, this judgement renews and innovates the Party's theory of the principal contradiction and sets new requirements for the work of the Party and state.

The commentary has five parts. It first traces two "leaps" in the Party's theory since the 1950s, then sets out four conditions behind the shift. It then discusses how the shift relates to the unchanged basic national condition, the primary stage of socialism. Finally it considers what the shift means for people-centred development and for the world economy.

Lin's central move is to separate a change of contradiction from a change of historical stage. The article describes the 8th Party Congress (1956) and the Sixth Plenum of the 11th Central Committee (1981) as the first leap, and the 19th Party Congress as the second. It presents the new formula as replacing "material and cultural needs" with a wider "better life" that includes democracy, rule of law, fairness, justice, security and environment. It also replaces "backward social production" with "unbalanced and inadequate development" across the five-sphere framework. As evidence the article cites GDP of 82.7 trillion yuan in 2017 and manufacturing output ranked first in the world for eight years. It adds a large middle-income group and the Party's new theory since the 18th Party Congress (2012). Lin says the shift happens inside the primary stage, which China remains in and will long remain in. The old formula fits its "first half" and the new one its "second half", so the basic task is still to liberate and develop the productive forces, and demands must not outrun them.

Lin concludes that a correct reading of the contradiction is what lets the Party serve people's immediate and long-term interests. The article links the new formula to targeted poverty alleviation, rural revitalisation, regional coordination, pollution control, high-quality development, education and health care, and employment. It also argues that the shift will benefit the world economy through new market and investment openings, a growing middle class that buys more abroad, and a continued commitment to peaceful development. Read the original if you want the official People's Daily account of how the 2017 reformulation of the principal contradiction was justified and tied to the primary stage of socialism.
quoteEn: It must be stressed that the shift in the principal contradiction in the new era is a change within the primary stage of socialism, not a change that goes beyond this historical stage.
quoteZh: 需要强调的是，新时代社会主要矛盾转化是在社会主义初级阶段内的变化，而不是超越这个历史阶段的变化

glossary.explanation: A concept from Mao Zedong's dialectics, used by the Party to define the central tension in society at a given time. It guides the Party's strategic priorities.

The official characterisation of China's basic national condition, developed in the 1980s and elaborated at the 13th and 15th Party Congresses. It holds that China remains in an underdeveloped phase of socialism that will last a long time.

glossary.zh: 以人民为中心的发展思想
glossary.pinyin: yǐ rénmín wéi zhōngxīn de fāzhǎn sīxiǎng
glossary.literal: development thought with the people at the centre
glossary.explanation: An official formulation associated with Xi Jinping, stating that development should aim at the people's well-being and be shared by them.

The official overall layout of the cause of socialism with Chinese characteristics, combining economic, political, cultural, social and ecological progress. It was set out at the 18th Party Congress (2012).
An official term, prominent since 2017, for a growth model that stresses quality, efficiency and innovation over speed.

t: The freedom of new imperialist enslavement: a critique of neoliberalism
zh: 新帝国主义奴役的自由：评新自由主义
source: Journal of Hebei University of Economics and Business, 2017 no. 4
paras: Yu Bin, writing in 2017, takes up the claim that neoliberalism stands for freedom and that socialism leads to serfdom. The article argues the opposite: neoliberalism is the freedom of capital to exploit and enslave workers, and it serves as the policy tool of what Yu calls new imperialism. It also warns that China's supply-side structural reform risks being steered onto a neoliberal path.

The article has two parts. The first answers a Chinese professor's "steamed bun" parable, in which tax cuts and lower fees are proposed to clear the obstacles between supply and demand. The second is a long critique of Friedrich Hayek's The Road to Serfdom. It moves from Hayek's account of Nazi "national socialism" and state capitalism to his views on unemployment, wages and competition, and then to neoliberalism's role in globalisation, international institutions and the Washington Consensus.

In the bun parable, Yu argues that the diagnosis is wrong: goods that do not sell because they are too dear are not overcapacity. Tax cuts would not necessarily lower prices, could merely shift overcapacity from buns to steamed bread, and would weaken the public finances that state action depends on. Yu says the reform needed is structural adjustment and innovation, not neoliberal supply-side tax cutting. Turning to Hayek, Yu reads the "socialism" he attacks as Nazi state capitalism and Bismarckian pseudo-socialism, not Marxist scientific socialism. Yu says Hayek's treatment of unemployment, minimum wages and "equality of opportunity" favours capital over labour. A numerical example is offered to show that the neoliberal "iron law" that wages must grow more slowly than productivity does not hold where surplus value is extracted. Yu then contends that neoliberalism became the hegemonic tool of new imperialism as Keynesianism declined in the 1970s. In Yu's account, free trade, privatisation, "human rights above sovereignty" and bodies such as the IMF, World Bank and WTO let transnational capital seize developing countries' economic lifelines. Yu cites Latin America's "lost decade" and Stiglitz as evidence.

Yu concludes that neoliberalism is the ideology of exploitation and imperialist plunder. Yu says China's reforms were hampered by neoliberal "market omnipotence" and the myth of private property, citing privatised state firms and foreign control of some urban utilities, and that China must hold to unwaveringly consolidating and developing the public sector. Read the original if you want a Marxist polemic against Hayek and neoliberal supply-side ideas, set in the debates over China's reform around 2017.
quoteEn: What we are carrying out at present is supply-side structural reform, not the supply-side reform of the neoliberal supply-side school.
quoteZh: 当前我们进行的是供给侧结构性改革,而不是新自由主义供给学派的供给侧改革

glossary.explanation: An economic policy line announced by Xi Jinping in 2015. It aims to adjust the structure of supply, cut overcapacity and promote innovation, and is presented officially as distinct from Western supply-side economics.

glossary.zh: 毫不动摇巩固和发展公有制经济
glossary.pinyin: háo bù dòngyáo gǒnggù hé fāzhǎn gōngyǒuzhì jīngjì
glossary.en: unwaveringly consolidating and developing the public sector
glossary.literal: unwaveringly consolidate and develop the public-ownership economy
glossary.explanation: Part of the official principle of the Two Unwaverings, which also covers unwaveringly supporting the non-public sector. It is the formula for the public sector's place in China's economy.

The author's term for a final stage of imperialism since the 1970s. It is marked by weakened state sovereignty and the free plunder of other countries' economic resources, with neoliberalism as its policy instrument.

A set of market-oriented policy prescriptions, including privatisation, liberalisation and fiscal discipline, promoted in the 1990s by Washington-based institutions. The article treats it as a vehicle of neoliberal reform in Latin America.

t: Understanding the new historical position of reform and opening up in the new era
zh: 深刻理解新时代改革开放的新方位
paras: Writing in 2018, as a series of reform measures drew wide public discussion, Ding Yuanzhu argues that they can only be understood from a historical and epochal standpoint, that is, from China's new historical position. The article's thesis is that this position must be read through great-power relations, above all the China–US relationship.

The short commentary first recalls that China's reform and opening up must be studied against its initial conditions and the global logic of the time, including US–China relations then. It then turns to the present: Trump's slogans of national revival and "making America great again", the competitive mentality behind them, and what they mean for China's choices.

Ding contends that US decline will be gradual. Citing an economy 1.5 times the size of China's and growth of 3 per cent, the author suggests that the rivalry could become a century-long contest. The US is described as facing challenges to its system and to its international standing, and as holding a competitive mindset formed by long prosperity. Chinese national rejuvenation, by contrast, rests on a century of humiliation and the search for a national path since the Opium War. Ding advises against over-interpreting American behaviour.

Ding concludes that China's most fundamental task is to do its own work well. The author calls for rethinking what to reform and open, and how, so as to reach the goal of a modern socialist great power while reducing friction with major powers. Improving people's livelihoods and national strength is presented as the common aim, and as the premise for the fortieth anniversary of reform and opening up and for modernizing national governance. Read the original if you want a brief example of how a Chinese scholar framed reform and opening up against US–China rivalry in 2018.
quoteEn: Therefore, our most fundamental task is to do our own work well.
quoteZh: 因此,我们最根本的任务是要把自己的事情做好。

glossary.explanation: The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched in China in 1978 under Deng Xiaoping. The year 2018 marked its fortieth anniversary.

t: Upholding the Four Cardinal Principles as the ideological and political foundation for advancing the "four greats"
zh: 坚持四项基本原则是推进“四个伟大”的思想政治基础
paras: Writing in Red Flag Manuscripts in 2018, Song Yuehong takes up the 19th Party Congress (2017) report's call to realise the great dream through the "four greats": great struggle, great project of Party building, great cause of socialism with Chinese characteristics, and the great dream itself. The article argues that upholding the Four Cardinal Principles, described as the foundation of the nation, is the fundamental political basis of the Party's historic mission of national rejuvenation. Song contends that the content of the "four greats" in turn gives the Principles new meaning for the new era.

The article is organised in three parts. The first traces why developing the path of socialism with Chinese characteristics requires the Principles, drawing on Deng Xiaoping, the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee (1978), the 1981 Resolution on Party history, the 1982 constitutional amendment and the 13th Party Congress. The second part treats socialist institutions and reform and opening up as conditions of national rejuvenation. The third part argues that the Principles are the essential requirement of each of the "four greats".

Song's central claim is that the Principles are historically grounded and internally linked to other elements of the Party line. In the author's account, the Principles were confirmed by revolution, construction and reform; they sit with economic construction and reform and opening up in the Party's basic line for the primary stage of socialism. Economic construction is called the key to national prosperity, reform and opening up the road to national strength, and the Principles the foundation of the state. Song holds that without the Principles and reform, economic construction would lose direction and momentum. Applied to the "four greats", upholding Party leadership and the socialist system is the core of the Principles: it requires full and rigorous self-governance of the Party, adherence to the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics, and deepened reform under the Party's unified leadership.

Song concludes that the Principles form a unified, systematic ideological and political system that cannot be shaken, departed from or reduced by dropping any one of them, or the whole cause of socialist modernization would be undermined. Reform and opening up, in turn, keeps giving the Principles new content for each era. Read the original if you want an example of how Party theorists in 2018 tied the Four Cardinal Principles to the 19th Party Congress framework of the \"four greats\".
quoteEn: Taking economic construction as the central task is the key to rejuvenating the country, persisting in reform and opening up is the road to national strength, and upholding the Four Cardinal Principles is the foundation of the nation.
quoteZh: 以经济建设为中心是兴国之要，坚持改革开放是强国之路，坚持四项基本原则是立国之本。

glossary.explanation: Formulated by Deng Xiaoping in 1979: keeping to the socialist road, the people's democratic dictatorship, the leadership of the Communist Party, and Marxism-Leninism and Mao Zedong Thought. They were written into the constitution in 1982.

A formula from Xi Jinping's report to the 19th Party Congress (2017): great struggle, great project, great cause and great dream. The report presents them as interconnected means of achieving national rejuvenation.
The official judgement that China is and will long remain at an early stage of socialist development, formally set out at the 13th Party Congress (1987). It underpins the Party's basic line.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: Party-building policy promoted under Xi Jinping since 2012, stressing discipline, anti-corruption and stricter internal management.
The policy launched at the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee in 1978, introducing economic reform and engagement with the outside world.

t: Why the "fire of truth" still shines: rereading the Communist Manifesto
zh: “真理之火”为何依然璀璨
paras: Writing in Jiefang Daily in February 2018, on the 170th anniversary of the Communist Manifesto, Zhou Wen asks why the "fire of truth" of scientific socialism still burns brightly. The commentary answers that the theory endures because it has developed through inheritance and innovated through practice.

Zhou first describes the Manifesto as a rich seam of ideas, translated into more than 200 languages and over 1,100 editions, and notes that it has attracted many misreadings and competing interpretations. The piece then ties the anniversary to the 200th anniversary of Marx's birth and the 40th anniversary of reform and opening up. It is organised around four "new realms" that the author says must keep being opened up.

The four realms are adapting Marxism to the Chinese context, socialism with Chinese characteristics, Party self-governance, and a twenty-first-century Marxism. Zhou cites the seven prefaces Marx and Engels wrote between 1872 and 1893 as evidence that they revised their views as practice developed. Zhou calls Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era a kind of "manifesto" for Communists in the new era. The author credits full and rigorous self-governance of the Party since the 18th Party Congress (2012) with strengthening the Party, and presents Party leadership as the greatest strength of the system. Zhou contrasts this with Western societies, which the author describes as lacking a real leading force and suffering division. The author also presents a community with a shared future for mankind as rooted in Marx's idea of an association and as a contemporary expression of the Manifesto.

Zhou concludes that rereading the Manifesto means keeping to the original aspiration and mission, carrying the responsibilities that the era and the people assign, and making China's voice strong in the new era. Read the original if you want a short example of how a 2018 official commentary links the Manifesto's anniversary to Party-building and to Xi Jinping's theory.
quoteEn: Only a theory that keeps pace with the times can remain forever vital; only thought that leads its era can show its mighty power.
quoteZh: 唯有与时俱进的理论，才能永葆生机；唯有引领时代的思想，方显磅礴伟力。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party constitution at the 19th Party Congress in 2017.

glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context
glossary.explanation: The official idea that Marxism must be combined with China's concrete conditions, giving rise to successive theoretical achievements such as Mao Zedong Thought.
The official name for China's path since reform and opening up, combining Party leadership and public ownership with market mechanisms.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: A slogan for the discipline and anti-corruption drive launched after the 18th Party Congress in 2012.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept for international relations, written into the report of the 19th Party Congress in 2017.
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched in 1978.

t: Using the Marxist materialist conception of history to identify erroneous social trends of thought scientifically
zh: 运用马克思主义唯物史观 科学辨识错误社会思潮
paras: Writing in early 2018, Jiang Yingchun asks how erroneous social trends of thought can be recognised and criticised. The article notes that since the 18th Party Congress (2012) the spread of such trends has been effectively checked, but argues that their presence and the struggle against them will be long-term. Its thesis is that these trends share a rejection of Marxist guidance, so the materialist conception of history should be used as the main tool for seeing through their theoretical surface.

The piece is a short theoretical commentary built on three "correct grasps" drawn from Engels's late letters, chiefly those to Mehring (1893) and Bloch (1890). The three are the inverted nature of false consciousness, the conditioned nature of history-making, and the directionality of historical development. Jiang applies each to liberalism, Western constitutional democracy and related currents in contemporary China, and ends with the Party's disciplinary stance.

First, Jiang reads Engels's account of ideology as showing that these trends separate consciousness from social being and treat ideas as self-generating. As examples, the article names Hayek's liberalism as a shared "spiritual weapon" and the claim that Western constitutional democracy is universal. Second, citing Engels's point that people make history under definite economic, political and traditional conditions, Jiang argues that these trends try to make history apart from the socialist mode of production, economic base and socialist spiritual-cultural tradition. The article gives as examples a scholar who reads 40 years of reform and opening up as a Western capitalist "modernity" project, and another who denies a distinctively Chinese social science. Third, Engels's "resultant force" of many wills must, Jiang says, be joined to the Marxist view of the masses. Otherwise it slides into voluntarism and individualism, which Jiang sees in the democracy proposals of these trends.

Jiang concludes that China's conditions for making history are objective and cannot be arbitrarily removed, and that the Four-sphere Confidence is itself a necessary condition for creating history. The article stresses that the people are the real masters of history and that struggle against erroneous trends is an important task of a Marxist party. It cites the guidelines on intra-Party political life adopted by the Sixth Plenum of the 18th Central Committee (2016), which require cadres to oppose such views openly. Read the original if you want a compact example of how Party theorists in 2018 used Engels's letters to frame the critique of liberalism and constitutionalism.
quoteEn: The basic approach of erroneous social trends of thought is to assert what is wrong by negating what is right; at their core they use liberalism to negate Marxism and socialism, and the flaw in their theoretical method is the denial of the conditioned nature of history-making.
quoteZh: 错误社会思潮的基本思路就是通过否定正确的东西来主张错误的东西，核心是用自由主义否定马克思主义和社会主义，其理论方法的错误就是否定历史创造的条件性。

glossary.explanation: Confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics. The formula was developed in Party discourse under Xi Jinping.

Official term for ideological currents such as liberalism, constitutional democracy and historical nihilism, which Party theorists regard as opposed to Marxism. It is used in discussions of ideological work.
A phrase from Engels's 1893 letter to Mehring. It describes thinking that treats ideas as self-generating and overlooks their material roots.

t: The inherent logic of achieving the "Two Centenary Goals"
zh: 实现“两个一百年”奋斗目标的内在逻辑
paras: Writing in Red Flag Manuscripts in 2018, Zhu Bingyuan asks what inner logic underlies the aim of achieving the "Two Centenary Goals" and building China into a modern socialist country. The article argues that this aim is both the historical trend of the Chinese nation since modern times and the internal logic of the development of socialism with Chinese characteristics. It presents the report to the 19th Party Congress (2017), which divided the second goal into two stages, as a mobilisation order issued at a decisive moment for building a moderately prosperous society.

The article is organised around four "logics": historical, theoretical, practical in the sense of the people's aspirations, and the practice of the Party's governance. Each section links a different dimension of the Two Centenary Goals to the Party's course. Zhu draws on Xi Jinping's statements, the earlier "three-step" strategy of the 1980s, the sequence of Party theories since Mao Zedong, and the 19th Party Congress report.

Zhu's central claims are as follows. Historically, socialism with Chinese characteristics is a unity of continuity and stages, and the goals refine the earlier "three-step" strategy into a timetable: a basically modernized country by 2035 and a strong, prosperous, democratic, culturally advanced, harmonious and beautiful country by the middle of the century. Theoretically, the Party's work has answered three questions, namely how to "stand up", "become rich" and "become strong", and Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era is presented as the theory for the third. In practical terms, the principal contradiction of the new era is between the people's growing needs for a better life and unbalanced, inadequate development, and a comprehensive moderately prosperous society must be comprehensive in fields, population and regions. As for governance, the author holds that long-term rule and avoiding the "historical cycle" require modernizing the system and capacity of national governance, which the author sees as built into the goals.

Zhu concludes that the goals follow necessarily from China's historical development, from theory, from popular needs and from the demands of governing, and that the strong modern socialist country is already clearly in view. The article closes by borrowing Mao Zedong's image of a rising sun. Read the original if you want a compact example of how Party theorists in 2018 explained the 19th Party Congress's timetable and tied it to the three-stage story of Chinese Marxism.
quoteEn: The Two Centenary Goals inherently include the modernization of the system and capacity of national governance.
quoteZh: 在“两个一百年”奋斗目标之中，内在地包含了国家治理体系和治理能力现代化。

glossary.explanation: Goals first set out at the 18th Party Congress (2012): a moderately prosperous society by the Party's centenary in 2021, and a modern socialist country by the centenary of the People's Republic in 2049.
A long-standing Chinese official goal of general, comfortable but not yet affluent living standards, used as the target of the first centenary goal.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party constitution at the 19th Party Congress in 2017.

t: Rethinking the connotation of ideological and political education
zh: 对思想政治教育内涵的再思考
source: Journal of the Graduate School of the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, 2017 no. 6
paras: Li Chunhua and Shangguan Miaomiao take up a basic question in the field of ideological and political education: what exactly is it? They note that research seldom addresses this "connotation" directly and usually approaches it through studies of its essence, content or value. The authors argue that a scientific definition is a precondition for the field to count as a science, and that it should rest on three principles: objectivity, universality and intrinsicality.

The article opens by explaining why the definition matters and then devotes one section to each principle, testing prevailing definitions in the Chinese literature against it. Along the way it draws on Engels's notion of a science of thought, the history of psychology, the Marxist theory of ruling ideas, and surveys of scholarly views on the essence of ideological and political education, including a ten-position summary published in 2016. It closes with the authors' own definition.

On objectivity, the authors hold that a definition must describe what has actually existed, not what is desired. In their view, common formulations that stress following the laws of how thought, character and psychology develop describe an ideal, scientific form available only to proletarian-party education, since the relevant sciences are barely a century old. On universality, they criticise three habits: treating the activity as coextensive with human society, when in their account it exists only in class societies; requiring it to be purposeful, planned and organised, when much influence was spontaneous; and attributing it only to ruling classes, when ruled classes and parties also conduct it. On intrinsicality, they argue the definition must capture the essence, which they describe as grasping people with ideas and theory, and must leave out derivative content such as the free and all-round development of the person or mental-health education.

The authors define ideological and political education as the social practice in which, in all societies since the emergence of classes, a given class, party or organisation influences and educates people with its own ideas or theory. They conclude that its essence is to win people over with ideological theory, and that in China this means winning people over with scientific Marxist theory. They hope the definition satisfies the three principles and helps clarify the field. Read the original if you work on the disciplinary foundations of ideological and political education in China and want to see how its definitions are criticised and reconstructed.
quoteEn: The essence of ideological and political education is to grasp people with ideological theory; in China, its essence is to grasp people with scientific Marxist theory.
quoteZh: 思想政治教育的本质是用思想理论掌握人，我国思想政治教育的本质就是用马克思主义科学理论掌握人。

glossary.explanation: A Chinese Party-state term for education and persuasion aimed at shaping people's political outlook, ideas and morality. It is also an academic discipline within Marxist theory studies in Chinese universities.
A term from Chinese logic for the set of essential attributes a concept reflects, as opposed to its extension (外延), the range of things it covers.

t: Paths to improving the affinity and relevance of ideological and political theory courses in universities
zh: 提升高校思想政治理论课亲和力与针对性的路径
paras: Writing in 2017, shortly before the 19th Party Congress, Zheng Jie asks how Chinese universities can make their ideological and political theory courses (sizheng ke) more engaging and better suited to students' needs. The article takes as its starting point Xi Jinping's call at the 2016 national conference on ideological and political work in universities to raise the "affinity and relevance" of these courses. Zheng's answer is that teachers must work on two sets of qualities, summarised as the "four degrees" and the "four airs".

The article is a short policy-oriented essay published in the journal Gaoxiao fudaoyuan (University Counsellors). After a brief introduction citing Xi Jinping's speeches and the 2017 "quality year" campaign of the Ministry of Education, it sets out the two frameworks in turn. The "four degrees" concern teaching objectives, content, process and methods. The "four airs" concern lecturing, classroom language, teaching formats and assessment.

On the "four degrees", Zheng argues that objectives need "height": courses should be tied to the task of cultivating reliable successors to the cause of socialism with Chinese characteristics. Content needs "depth", meaning teachers must master Marxist theory and the latest Party theory and explain it thoroughly but accessibly. The teaching process needs "warmth", and Zheng criticises teachers who read from scripts or slides in a flat tone. Methods need "effectiveness", combining lectures, case discussion, MOOCs, micro-films and social media. On the "four airs", teachers need confidence in their theory, grounded everyday and online-style language, lively practice-based formats, and varied assessment. Zheng's examples include micro-films for broadcasting students and performing revolutionary songs for music students.

Zheng concludes that teachers should follow the spirit of Xi Jinping's speeches and aim at higher course quality. The article proposes improving top-level design and making progress on four fronts: textbooks, teachers, teaching and methods. The stated goal is to strengthen the courses' attractiveness and persuasiveness and students' sense of benefit from them (huodegan). Read the original if you want a concrete picture of how Chinese university teachers are advised to put Party policy on ideological and political education into classroom practice around 2017.
quoteEn: Only such ideological and political theory teachers will come across as approachable, and only such teaching will have affinity and relevance.
quoteZh: 这样的思政课教师才有亲切感，这样的思政课教学才有亲和力与针对性。

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses on Marxism, Party theory and political education taught in Chinese universities, usually abbreviated sizheng ke.
Phrase used by Xi Jinping in 2016 for making political education more approachable and better matched to students' needs.
A term popular in Party discourse since about 2015, meaning people's felt experience of tangible benefit from policies or services.

t: Teachers of non-ideological-and-political courses should strengthen awareness of ideological and political education in their teaching
zh: 非思政课专业教师应特别增强授课中的思想政治教育意识
paras: Writing in Red Flag Manuscripts (Hongqi Wengao, 2017, no. 14), Tong Xiao takes up a problem raised by Xi Jinping's speech at the national conference on ideological and political work in universities: how teachers of ordinary subject courses can join the ideological and political education of students. Tong argues that a considerable number of such teachers lack this awareness, and that some even teach out of step with, or against, the ideological and political theory courses. The article calls for stronger awareness among them.

The commentary is a short, prescriptive piece organised around four requirements for subject teachers. It begins from the formula that every course should keep "its own section of the channel" and "tend its own responsibility field", moving in the same direction as the ideological and political theory courses.

Tong's first requirement is awareness of Marxism as a guiding ideology, in both course content and the teacher's own conduct. The second is to weave ideological and political content into subject teaching: drawing out the values already present in a subject, addressing students' questions inside and outside class, and not stressing skills at the expense of values. The third is to make "fostering virtue through education" the central task, coordinating with ideological and political teachers through staff exchange, shared content, joint case teaching and joint criticism of mistaken views. The fourth is to build ideological and political elements into course design, gently and without forcing them. Tong's examples are Marie Curie's patriotism in chemistry and Fei Xiaotong and the multiparty cooperation system in sociology. Tong warns against turning subject courses into ideological and political courses.

Tong concludes that the most effective education is received unconsciously, and that using subject teachers' influence is a political advantage of Chinese universities that must be pursued. Subject teachers should guide students' values while teaching their specialisms. Read the original if you want a concise statement of the 2017 official line on integrating ideological education into university subject teaching.
quoteEn: Ideological and political education must be clear in its banner and distinctive in character, yet also moisten things silently and work by imperceptible influence.
quoteZh: 思想政治教育既要旗帜鲜明、突出特点，也要润物无声、潜移默化。

glossary.explanation: Compulsory Marxist theory and political education courses in Chinese universities, often abbreviated as sizheng ke. They are treated as the main channel of ideological education.
A long-standing educational formula, stressed in Party documents, that moral character formation is the fundamental task of education.
A Party-affiliated journal on theory and ideology, published by the People's Daily group as the successor to the Red Flag magazine's manuscript series.

t: Institutional causes of Western disorder and Chinese governance
zh: 西方之乱与中国之治的制度原因
paras: Writing in 2017 (the piece appeared in Qiushi, issue 15), Zhang Weiwei asks why the West has fallen into turmoil while China has achieved good governance, although both exist under deepening globalization. Zhang opens with a list of Western troubles: the Trump presidency, the refugee influx into Europe, Brexit, populism, terrorist attacks and stagnating living standards. Against these, the author sets China's rise since the 18th Party Congress (2012). Zhang's answer is that the contrast comes from differing strategies toward globalization, differing institutional arrangements, and a different balance among three forces in governance.

The article has three numbered sections, each taking up one cause. The first compares Western and Chinese understandings of globalization. The second compares political, economic and social-governance institutions. The third sets out a framework of political, social and capital forces. Zhang uses figures such as Joseph Stiglitz's calculation on US median income, a 2016 Ipsos poll on satisfaction with national direction, and the 2010 and 2014 US Supreme Court rulings on campaign donations.

Zhang argues that Western-led globalization is essentially neoliberal globalization serving international monopoly capital. In this account it concentrates gains among a rich minority, hollows out domestic industry, and exports a political agenda whose consequences now return as refugees and terrorism. China, by contrast, treats globalization as economic only, not political or "Western", and uses socialist institutions to correct its defects. Zhang contrasts Western parties, called "partial-interest parties", with the Communist Party as a "whole-interest party". The author also contrasts neoliberal laissez-faire with China's socialist market economy and its model of Party-government leadership, social coordination and public participation. At the deepest level, Zhang says capital dominates in the United States and social forces dominate in parts of Europe. China's political force, in this reading, stays independent of both and can guide them.

Zhang concludes that Chinese governance rests on institutions oriented to the people's overall interests. In this account those institutions draw on Chinese civilizational heritage, the "red genes" of socialism with Chinese characteristics, and lessons from other civilizations. The author states that China's most lasting significance lies in offering experience and wisdom for building a better society, as well as in lifting a fifth of humanity toward prosperity. Zhang concedes that the Party faces challenges and calls for full and rigorous self-governance of the Party and deepened reform. Read the original if you want a representative statement of how a prominent Chinese commentator contrasted Western and Chinese systems in an official Party journal in 2017.
quoteEn: Behind Western disorder and Chinese governance lies a huge difference in the balance among three forces in state governance: political, social and capital.
quoteZh: 西方之乱和中国之治的背后是国家治理中三种力量——政治、社会、资本——对比关系的巨大差异。

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.literal: comprehensively and strictly govern the Party
glossary.explanation: A slogan associated with Xi Jinping's leadership since 2012, covering anti-corruption work and tighter Party discipline and internal supervision.
The official description of China's economic system since the 1990s, combining market allocation of resources with public ownership and state macro-control.
Zhang's term for the Communist Party as a force representing the people as a whole, contrasted with Western "partial-interest parties" that represent particular groups.

t: Raising high the ideological banner of twenty-first-century Marxism
zh: 高举21世纪马克思主义的思想旗帜
paras: Writing in Red Flag Manuscripts in 2017, Shuang Chuanxue takes up Xi Jinping's call, made at the symposium on philosophy and social sciences and in a letter marking the 40th anniversary of the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, to develop "twenty-first-century Marxism" and "contemporary Chinese Marxism". The article argues that this is a historical mission given to Chinese Communists by the age. It holds that Xi Jinping's thought on governing the country is the most concentrated expression of that Marxism.

The piece has three parts. The first explains why developing twenty-first-century Marxism is a historical task. The second presents Xi's ideas on state governance as the field's fullest embodiment. The third names the intellectual obstacles that must be cleared before the banner can be held high. Shuang draws on Marx and Engels, Lenin, and the record of the Communist Party of China since reform and opening up.

Shuang argues that Marxism is above all a method tied to changing practice, so it must renew itself with each age. Shuang points to Lenin's adaptation of Marxism to Russia and the Party's adaptation of it to China. The author holds that new problems in the course of socialism with Chinese characteristics cannot be solved from classic texts or by copying foreign experience. In this account, Xi's governance thought answers the people's new expectations, enriches the theoretical system of socialism with Chinese characteristics and has been tested in practice, with the Belt and Road Initiative forum of May 2017 cited as evidence. The third part rejects three versions of the claim that Marxism is outdated: that times have changed, that history has ended, and that Chinese practice has broken with Marx's vision. The author calls all three dogmatic. Shuang also opposes the "Westernization" and "Confucianization" of the guiding ideology. The author names historical nihilism, neoliberalism, "universal values", Western constitutional democracy, democratic socialism and cultural revivalism as erroneous currents to be criticised.

Shuang concludes that scholars should study and carry out Xi's speeches and his new ideas on governing the country, and should take up the task of upholding and developing twenty-first-century Marxism. The author says this opposition to Westernization and Confucianization is not hostility to Western civilization or to traditional Chinese culture, which should be creatively transformed. Read the original if you want a clear example of how a 2017 Party-theory journal linked Xi's governance thought to the idea of twenty-first-century Marxism and framed ideological threats to it.
quoteEn: Practice has proved that keeping pace with the times is the most important theoretical character of Marxism.
quoteZh: 实践证明，与时俱进是马克思主义最重要的理论品格。

glossary.explanation: A phrase used in Chinese official and academic discourse for the latest stage of Marxist theory, said to be developed through China's practice. It is often paired with "contemporary Chinese Marxism".

glossary.literal: thought on governing the country and managing state affairs
glossary.explanation: A label for Xi Jinping's speeches and ideas on state governance since the 18th Party Congress (2012). In 2017 it served as a main reference for his theoretical contribution.
A term used in Party discourse for views said to distort or negate the Party's and socialism's history. Official texts treat it as an ideological threat.

t: The dimensions of cultural confidence
zh: 文化自信的维度
paras: Writing in Qiushi in early 2017, Shen Zhuanghai asks what cultural confidence means for China and how it can be strengthened. Shen argues that, amid competition in cultural soft power, no culture or nation can stand at the forefront of civilisation without confidence in itself. The article proposes a comprehensive and rational view of cultural confidence, which Shen treats as a strategic task in building China into a strong socialist cultural power.

The piece has three parts. The first defines cultural confidence as the nation's conviction in its own cultural ideals, values, vitality and prospects, and explains why it is needed now. The second sets out three dimensions: confidence in cultural spirit, in cultural capacity and in the cultural path. The third lists practical ways to strengthen it.

Shen first places the question in modern history. Since the 19th century, the author says, China has had to handle the relations between past and present and between China and the world, and a sense of national weakness once left many people "lost in the Western tide, doubting tradition and unsure of the road ahead". Shen sees cultural confidence as rebuilt through national liberation and reform and opening up, but still needed given Western dominance in the global cultural order and what the author lists as unhealthy tendencies: blind worship of the West, rigid attachment to the past, self-contempt, arrogance and vulgar culture. The three dimensions then point to content, creative agents and development path. Confidence in cultural spirit means trust in values such as benevolence, people-centredness, good faith and harmony, and in the core socialist values as their contemporary transformation. Confidence in cultural capacity rests on the nation's creative record and its achievements under Party leadership. Confidence in the cultural path means the Marxist-guided cultural development path of socialism with Chinese characteristics.

To strengthen cultural confidence, Shen calls for keeping the Four-sphere Confidence in internal unity, building a real material and institutional foundation through reform, public cultural services and better international communication, and producing outstanding cultural works. Shen urges cultural workers to create works with China's own originality that tell its stories well. Read the original if you want a compact example of how a 2017 official Party journal framed the content and tasks of cultural confidence.
quoteEn: Cultural confidence is, in the final analysis, confidence in the ability of the creative agents of culture to create a new culture.
quoteZh: 文化自信，归根到底，是对文化创造主体创造新文化能力的自信。

glossary.explanation: A concept in Party discourse for confidence in China's own cultural traditions, revolutionary culture and socialist culture. It was later added by Xi Jinping to the "three confidences" to make the Four-sphere Confidence.
Confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics. Xi Jinping presented the full formula in 2016.
A set of 24 characters in twelve values at national, social and individual levels, promoted by the Party since the 18th Party Congress (2012).
The official name for the path, theory and system of socialism pursued in China since reform and opening up.
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world begun in 1978.

t: On authority
st: Why and how Party members should uphold the authority of the Party Central Committee
zh: 谈权威
paras: Writing in 2017, Wang Guancheng asks how Party members and cadres should uphold the authority of the Party Central Committee. The author starts from the Sixth Plenum of the 18th Central Committee (2016), which confirmed Xi Jinping's core position and made upholding the Central Committee's authority a key principle and a matter of political discipline. Wang's answer is that members must understand the significance of that authority in theory and must be clear-minded in thought, firm in politics and conscious in action.

The article has two parts. The first is a historical and theoretical survey, running from Marx and Engels through Lenin and the Soviet Communist Party to the Communist Party of China, arguing that upholding central authority is a constant principle of Marxist parties. The second sets out three practical requirements: clear-mindedness in thought, firmness in politics and consciousness in action, each divided into three sub-points.

Wang's core claim is that Marxist theory and Party history both show central authority to be a condition of success. The author cites Marx and Engels on the Paris Commune, which fell for lack of authority, and Lenin's democratic centralism, and reads the Chinese Party's two defeats and two victories as the absence and presence of a authoritative centre. The practical programme draws on this. Members should study Marxism and Xi Jinping's speeches and fight wrong ideas rather than act as "gentlemen". They should make political standards primary, keep the identity of Communist Party member first, and refuse to join in criticism of the Central Committee or distortion of Party history. They should follow the Party Constitution and discipline, and comply with the 2016 guidelines on intra-Party political life and the supervision regulations. The author adds that the authority of the Central Committee with Xi Jinping at its core continues and develops Marxist teaching on party leadership.

Wang concludes that upholding the Central Committee's authority is concrete rather than abstract. It should show in every member's thinking, speech and conduct, and it is a political requirement as well as discipline. The article ends by quoting Xi Jinping's demand for absolute loyalty, under which members do what the Party asks and refrain from what it forbids. Read the original if you want a compact example of how Party-school commentary in 2017 justified the "core" leadership and set out its expectations of members.
quoteEn: Upholding the authority of the Party Central Committee is therefore concrete, not abstract. It shows in every aspect of a member's thinking, speech and conduct, and it is not only a political requirement but also political discipline.
quoteZh: 所以说，维护党中央权威是具体的，不是抽象的，是体现在一个党员的思想、言论、行为方方面面的，这不仅是政治要求，更是政治纪律。

glossary.en: authority of the Party Central Committee
glossary.explanation: The principle that all Party organisations and members must accept the Central Committee's leadership and decisions. Since the 18th Party Congress (2012) it has been stressed as a core rule of Party political life.
The Leninist organisational principle in which decisions are reached through discussion and then binding on all members, with lower levels obeying higher levels.

t: Big data as an aid to cyber ideological governance and pathways for improving it
zh: 大数据助力网络意识形态治理及提升路径
paras: Writing in 2016, Fu Anling and Zhang Yaocan ask how big data can be used in the governance of ideology on the internet. They start from the Third Plenum of the 18th Central Committee (2013), which set the goal of modernizing the system and capacity of national governance. In the authors' view, ideological governance is an "extremely important" part of that task, and its modernization depends on seizing the national big data strategy. Their thesis is that big data fits the needs of cyber ideological governance closely, but brings security risks, and that a set of institutional and technical measures can capture the benefits and limit the risks.

The article has three parts. It first defines big data (the "4V" and "5V" characteristics, with definitions from Gartner, the US National Science Foundation and McKinsey) and defines cyber ideological governance and what big data "assisting" it means. It then matches the features of big data to governance needs, and sets out three risks. Finally it proposes five paths, with examples from Chinese social media and public-opinion incidents, such as the "Eastern Star" shipwreck and the 2015 Qing'an railway station shooting.

The central move pairs each big data feature with a governance requirement. Variety suits the plurality of governing actors, including government, enterprises and online communities. Velocity suits timeliness, volume suits holistic oversight of social currents, and veracity suits precise, targeted policy. The authors also note that low value density complicates governance. They name three risks: discourse power shifting to internet magnates and opinion leaders, decentralization of ideology, and weakening of authority. They say these risks erode the leading position of Marxism and of core socialist values online.

The five paths are: advancing a national big data strategy for ideological governance, including talent training and learning from the United States and France; building a big data early-warning mechanism; improving emergency handling of online public opinion; building a security guarantee system, with legal rules, a national "firewall" and limits on the abuse of state power; and using big data to renew Marxist discourse and appeal, including by shaping young people's learning and cultivating Marxist opinion leaders. The authors conclude that big data governance is a necessary route to modernizing ideological governance, and that its complexity must be recognized. Read the original if you want to see how a 2016 Chinese ideological-education journal framed big data, online opinion monitoring and ideological security.
quoteEn: In the big data era, whoever holds the initiative and discourse power over online information holds the initiative in ideological governance.
quoteZh: 大数据时代，谁掌握了网络信息主导权和话语权谁就掌握了意识形态治理的主动权。

glossary.explanation: The article defines it as governing actors aligned with the ruling class using formal and informal institutions to integrate resources in the ideological sphere. It is presented as part of the modernization of national governance.
A set of values promoted by the Party since the 18th Party Congress (2012), summarised in twenty-four characters. They are used as the guiding framework for public opinion and education.
Views, attitudes and opinions that internet users form about specific events and about governing bodies. Monitoring and guiding it is a task of Chinese internet governance.

t: Freedom in cyberspace and its limits
zh: 网络空间的自由及其限度
source: Marxist Digest (马克思主义文摘), 2017 no. 4
paras: This short commentary, published in Marxist Digest in 2017, asks how freedom of expression online should be understood and bounded. The author argues that freedom is the natural and defining feature of network society, but that it is necessarily relative and must operate within limits set by law, ethics and norms.

The piece opens with Xi Jinping's remarks at the third World Internet Conference on the opportunities and challenges of the internet, and with figures on Chinese internet users as of June 2016. It cites the proposals for the Thirteenth Five-Year Plan, which stress the strategy of building China into a cyber power, and notes problems of uneven development, weak rules and disorder online. It then treats the case for online freedom and the challenges to it in turn.

On the first side, the author holds that the internet has widened the framework of rights to expression. Technical change from Web 1.0 to Web 3.0 has expanded space for free, equal and shared exchange, turning every user into an information source and stirring a stronger desire for freedom. On the second side, the author argues that online individuals are bound to society and others, so online freedom needs the joint support of laws, regulations, ethics and values. Citing Rousseau, the author claims that absolute freedom brings its own negation, and that the over-extension of freedom narrows it.

The author concludes that freedom and norms are mutually conditioning, that real freedom is relative freedom within rules, and that users should respect others' freedom. The author notes that state authorities, legislators and network operators are building a regulatory system for online conduct. Read the original if you want a brief example of how Chinese ideological and political education writing frames online freedom as bounded by law and norms.
quoteEn: The essence of freedom is embodied in "relative freedom obtained under the constraint of certain norms."
quoteZh: 自由的本质体现在“一定规范束缚下获得的相对自由”。

t: The Communist Party of China's guidance of social trends of thought since the 18th Party Congress
st: An interview with Lin Tai on the revised edition of "Wendao"
zh: 十八大以来中国共产党对社会思潮的引领
source: Studies on Marxist Theory in Higher Education, 2017 no. 1
paras: This is an interview, published in 2017, in which Dai Hongkai, a postdoctoral researcher at Tsinghua University's School of Marxism, questions Professor Lin Tai. The occasion is the revised edition of Lin's edited volume Wendao (Seeking the Way): Social Trends of Thought since Reform and Opening Up and Ideological and Political Education for Youth. Lin argues that since the 18th Party Congress (2012) the Party has treated the question of path as decisive and has led social trends of thought by confronting what he calls erroneous currents directly.

The interview moves through three topics. First, it summarises how the 18th Congress and Xi Jinping assessed more than thirty years of reform and the evolution of social thought. Second, it reviews Xi's criticism of five currents: democratic socialism, neoliberalism, Western multiparty "universal values", historical nihilism, and nihilism toward traditional culture. Third, Lin looks ahead to how these trends may develop.

Lin's core argument is that the path decides a country's fate. He contrasts the Soviet Union and Russia, which he says followed neoliberal reform designs and collapsed or fell into crisis, with socialism with Chinese characteristics. He holds that every Party congress since the 1980s developed this path in struggle against both "leftist" rigidity and rightist bourgeois liberalization. In his account the recurring currents all turn on which road reform takes. He cites Xi on state-owned enterprises, mixed ownership and supply-side structural reform, which Xi distinguished from Western supply-side economics. He also cites Xi on the claim that Western political models are universally applicable, and on the dangers of negating the Party's history, including the Soviet case.

Lin predicts that these currents will persist in new forms. Debates over state-enterprise reform, industrial policy and the rule of law will increasingly be disputes over the direction of reform. International currents such as populism, nationalism and anti-globalization will become a new field of study. New media will transform how currents spread, so the Party must cultivate online opinion leaders and integrate old and new media around core socialist values. Read the original if you want a Party-theorist's account of how the Xi leadership framed ideological struggle in 2012–2017, with the specific currents and Xi statements he cites.
quoteEn: Every Party congress since reform and opening up has taken socialism with Chinese characteristics as its theme, consistently and without the slightest deviation.
quoteZh: 改革开放以来的历次党代会，一以贯之地都是以中国特色社会主义为主题，从未有丝毫偏离

glossary.explanation: Broad ideological tendencies circulating in society, such as neoliberalism or democratic socialism. In Chinese academic and Party discourse they are a field of study and of ideological management.
In Party usage, a label for views that negate the Party's history or the Marxist account of Chinese history. It is treated as a major ideological danger.
An economic policy slogan put forward by the central leadership from 2015 to address overcapacity and improve supply quality. Officials distinguish it from Western supply-side economics.

t: Strengthening theoretical confidence: we must unwaveringly uphold Marxism
zh: 坚定理论自信 必须毫不动摇坚持马克思主义
paras: This newspaper commentary, published in Chengdu Daily in 2017, asks what theoretical confidence means within the Four-sphere Confidence and why it requires holding firmly to Marxism. Li Chunhua argues that theoretical confidence is the soul of the other three confidences, and that it rests on Marxism's scientific character and truth, not on blind faith.

The piece is organised under three headings: treating Marxism with a scientific attitude, believing in Marxism's eventual victory, and advancing theoretical innovation. It moves from the nature of Marxism, through practical evidence from the international communist movement and China, to the system of theory known as socialism with Chinese characteristics.

Li holds that the essence of Marxism is its standpoint, viewpoint and method, and that it has the greatest explanatory power among theories of capitalism. The author calls for guarding against two errors: dogmatism that treats Marxism as sacred doctrine, and so-called innovation that departs from its basic principles. Practice is the final test of theory. Li cites the October Revolution and the achievements of reform and opening up as proof, and holds that world socialism's present low tide is temporary. Theory with Chinese characteristics, from Deng Xiaoping Theory to Xi Jinping's speeches, is said to follow in one line from Marxism-Leninism and Mao Zedong Thought. Li points to public ownership, distribution according to work, Party leadership and Marxist guidance as the socialist essence retained in the primary stage of socialism.

Li concludes that the fundamental way to strengthen confidence is to innovate theory by addressing major real-world problems, since a body of thought more than 160 years old needs updating as times change. Read the original if you want a concise example of how a CASS scholar presented theoretical confidence and the case for Marxist orthodoxy together with innovation in 2017.
quoteEn: Theoretical confidence is the rational recognition of a theory's value, together with faith in truth and a persistent pursuit of it.
quoteZh: 理论自信是理性地对理论价值的认可，对真理的信仰和执著的追求。

glossary.explanation: A formula in Party discourse, finalised under Xi Jinping, calling for confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics.
The official name for China's model of socialism, in use since the 1980s. It covers the path, theoretical system, institutions and culture of the Party's governance.
An official thesis that China is at an early stage of socialism and will remain there for a long period. It is used to explain features such as market mechanisms and diverse ownership.
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched in 1978 under Deng Xiaoping.

t: Challenges and countermeasures for ideological work in universities in the online environment
zh: 网络环境下高校意识形态工作的挑战与对策
paras: Writing in 2017, Zheng Jie and Mei Meng ask how universities can safeguard socialist ideology now that the internet has become a main channel of communication among students. They argue that universities are the main front of ideological work, and that networked communication has weakened the guiding, defensive, propaganda and control capacities of that work. The authors propose a set of measures to rebuild these capacities.

The article has three parts. The first sets out why ideological security in universities matters: for the Party's governing security and long-term national stability, for a harmonious campus, and for the all-round development of individual students. The second identifies four challenges, and the third offers four sets of countermeasures. It draws on speeches by Xi Jinping on ideological work and on official concepts such as the Chinese Dream and core socialist values.

In the authors' account, hostile Western forces use the internet to spread "universal values", individualism, money worship and historical nihilism. They target students, who are curious and still forming their worldview, and so erode students' identification with socialism. The authors add that some teachers of ideological and political theory courses are unfamiliar with or reluctant to use the internet, so the classroom is losing its position as the main channel. Weak internet legislation and supervision also let rumours, fraud and online abuse spread. The proposed responses are to strengthen the ideological formation of teachers and students around Marxism and a sense of vigilance. They also call for campus culture built on core socialist values, including "red" activities and campus social media.
