Drawing on Mao Zedong's call for a living Marxism and on Marx's point that principles must be studied in their historical conditions, Li proposes linking concepts to everyday life, basic principles to concrete cases, and the uncovering of laws to historical narrative. This is meant to equip students to resist erroneous currents of thought. For the online classroom, Li proposes three designs: bringing online stories into lectures, using mobile internet and multimedia as teaching tools, and setting up Weibo and WeChat groups through which teachers can guide opinion, counter rumours and monitor students' thinking. Li argues that fragmented, decentred online discourse has weakened the authority of classroom speech and the teacher's influence.

For teachers, Li calls for three kinds of planning. Layered planning would pair senior teachers' theoretical depth with younger teachers' ease with technology, through mentoring and exchange. Goal planning would align institutional management goals with teachers' own career and teaching goals. Quality planning would treat theoretical, cultural and new-media competence as the base of teachers' soft power. Li adds that the core requirement is conveying socialist ideology to students so that it becomes their own thinking and political awareness. Read the original if you want a concise example of how a 2016 Party journal framed practical teaching reform in ideological and political courses, including the use of social media.
quoteEn: In classroom teaching we do not lack factual support from practice; what we lack is the effort to dig into real life and the ability to use it in theory to explain principles well.
quoteZh: 我们在课堂教学上并不缺少实践事实的支撑，缺少的是挖掘生活实际的功夫以及将其运用到理论中讲好道理的能力。

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses in Marxism, Mao Zedong Thought and socialism with Chinese characteristics taught to all students in Chinese universities.
The Party's work of guiding public thought, education and media in line with Marxism and official policy.
The capacity to shape what is said and accepted in public debate; in Party usage it is one of the aspects of ideological leadership to be held firmly.

t: Targeted Party building: comprehensively raising the overall functions of primary-level Party organisations
zh: 精准党建：全面提升基层党组织整体功能
paras: Writing in 2016, Jiang Gang takes up a basic practical question in Party building: what to grasp and how to grasp it, under the slogan that doing Party building well is the greatest political achievement. The article presents the "targeted Party building" campaign of the Yibin municipal Party committee in Sichuan as a model for raising the overall functions of rural primary-level Party organisations. Jiang argues that the campaign unifies the political and service functions of these organisations and promotes interaction between Party building and economic and social development.

The article has three parts. The first describes the problems and background; the second sets out four mechanisms Yibin adopted; the third draws results and lessons. The campaign is framed by four goals (good cohesion, good interest linkages, good governance system, good operating model) and by a method of "six manys", which Jiang glosses as integrating plans, balancing industries, layering policies, diversifying investment, running multiple models and coordinating forces. Jiang draws on Xi Jinping's call for precision in reform and for solving problems at each specific point.

Jiang identifies four problems in rural Party organisations: pluralising values weaken their ideological leadership; the end of the agricultural tax and the lack of interest linkages loosen ties with villagers; diverse interests and the move from management to service and rule-based self-governance strain their governance role; and rough appraisal leaves cadres passive. Four mechanisms respond. A "1+X" education system of Party-spirit training bases targets cadres, villagers and business owners. A "one unified, four transformations" mechanism turns resources into assets and inputs into income, with 561 industry Party organisations and 606 collectively-poor villages removed from the list in the first half of 2016. A "base salary plus performance" appraisal scheme ties pay and promotion to service results. Legal affairs committees, piloted in 296 village branches, handle legal education, contract review, self-governance and mediation.

Jiang concludes that the campaign has moved beyond fragmented grassroots Party building and produced structural change. It uses Party building as the lever for overall development, enriches the objectives of rural Party organisations through the four goals, and replaces broad-brush spending with precisely targeted bundled resources. The article reports Yibin's figures without independent verification. Read the original if you want a Party-published case study of how a local Party committee in 2016 put grassroots Party building, rural industry, appraisal and village governance into one programme.
quoteEn: When Party building is done solidly it becomes productive force, when done meticulously it becomes cohesion, and when done forcefully it becomes fighting strength.
quoteZh: 党建工作抓实了就是生产力、抓细了就是凝聚力、抓强了就是战斗力。

glossary.explanation: The label Yibin gave its campaign, borrowing the idea of precision (as in targeted poverty alleviation) to direct Party-building work at specific problems and points.
The Party's lowest-level units, such as village and township branches and committees, which connect the Party to ordinary people.
Yibin's resource-coordination method: integrating plans, balancing industries, layering policies, diversifying investment, running multiple models and coordinating forces.

t: Basic lessons of the Party's ideological and theoretical development
zh: 党的思想理论建设的基本经验
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in 2016, shortly after Xi Jinping's speech marking the Party's 95th anniversary, Zhang Ruicai asks what the Communist Party of China has learned from its history about ideological and theoretical development. The commentary argues that the Party has always built itself first through ideas, and that its experience can be summed up in five pairings of tasks that must be pursued together.

The piece moves through these five pairings in turn. It draws on Mao Zedong, Lenin, Xi Jinping and the report of the 18th Party Congress (2012), and on a series of Party resolutions and congress summaries from the Yan'an rectification to the 17th Central Committee's fourth plenum.

Zhang's core claims are as follows. High priority on theory must go with solid practical work. Ideological and political work must go with active ideological struggle against anti-Marxist currents, and the author cites the Soviet and Eastern European collapse as a bitter lesson. Theoretical innovation must go with theoretical armament, so that study follows each theoretical advance. Ideological education must go with institutional governance, so that rules become a hard constraint rather than a rubber band. Theoretical study must go with summing up experience, as in the historical resolutions and the current Two Studies, One Doing campaign.

Zhang concludes that theoretical maturity underpins political firmness, keeping theory abreast of the times underpins bold action, and ideological unity ensures the whole Party moves in step. Read the original if you want a compact, official-style statement of how Party commentators in 2016 framed ideological work and Party-building.
quoteEn: The Party's 95 years of experience in ideological and theoretical development tell us that theoretical maturity is the foundation of political firmness, keeping theory abreast of the times is the precondition for bold action, and ideological unity is an important guarantee that the whole Party moves in step.
quoteZh: 中国共产党95年的思想理论建设经验告诉我们，理论上的成熟是政治上坚定的基础，理论上的与时俱进是行动上锐意进取的前提，思想上的统一是全党步调一致的重要保障。

glossary.explanation: A Party education campaign launched in 2016 for all members. It centres on studying the Party constitution and Xi Jinping's speeches and on becoming a qualified Party member.
The Party's work of education, propaganda and mobilisation among its members and the public, intended to secure adherence to its line and policies.

t: Cultivating belief among young people: establishing values amid cultural pluralism
zh: 青少年信仰培育：多元文化中的价值确立
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in September 2016, Zhang Hongxia takes up a problem the author considers serious: under the influence of diverse cultural currents, some young people, whose outlook is still forming, have lost their belief in Marxism. Zhang argues that this belief bears directly on the future of socialism with Chinese characteristics and of the Chinese nation, and proposes concrete ways to cultivate it.

The short commentary opens with Xi Jinping's remarks on youth and the formation of values, then describes the problem and sets out four remedies. It closes with practical measures in theory propaganda, tiered education, online work and practice-based education.

In Zhang's account, Western thought, while promoting "democracy" and "freedom", denies the inevitability of socialism, distorts the history of the Communist Party and claims Marxism is outdated. Zhang says this has three effects on young people: it erodes their pursuit of the lofty ideal of communism, shakes their confidence in socialist modernization, and disrupts their identification with core socialist values. The remedies are to clarify the scientific basis of Marxism and the historical necessity of China's choices; to tailor education to different groups, with communist ideals stressed for Party and Youth League members and simpler patriotic feeling for ordinary students; and to "seize" online ground through social media, dedicated websites and big-data "precision push". Zhang also calls for linking belief cultivation to film, volunteering, internships and everyday issues young people care about.

Zhang concludes that these measures can help young people form firm Marxist belief and correct values, so that they become qualified builders and reliable successors of socialism. Read the original if you want a compact example of how Party-aligned commentary in 2016 framed youth ideology work and its proposed methods.
quoteEn: Cultivating Marxist belief must teach students according to their aptitude, setting different goals according to their differing levels of ideological understanding and using different priorities, methods and means.
quoteZh: 马克思主义信仰培育要因材施教，根据学生的不同思想水平设定不同的培育目标，采用不同的培育重点、方法和手段。

glossary.explanation: A set of twelve values promoted by the Party since the 18th Party Congress (2012), covering the national, social and individual levels. They are used as a guide in education and public culture.
The official name for China's path since reform and opening up, combining Party leadership, a socialist system and a market-oriented economy.

t: The false and anti-democracy of the "model of democracy"
zh: “民主典范”的假民主和反民主
paras: Writing in 2016, He Wei takes aim at the United States' self-image as the world's most perfect democracy. The article argues that American democracy is not as flawless as Western thinkers and politicians claim: at home and abroad, in institutional design and in practice, it contains serious elements of what the author calls non-democracy, false democracy and anti-democracy.

The piece is organised in three parts. The first deals with how the American system treats forces hostile to it, citing the House Un-American Activities Committee, the Truman-era loyalty reviews and McCarthy's purge of embassy libraries. The second examines the domestic electoral and political system: presidential elections, the Supreme Court, money in politics, gun culture and parliamentary representation. The third turns to foreign policy, covering the use of democracy as an ideological tool, global resource inequality and humanitarian intervention.

He argues that US presidential elections are only apparently democratic. Candidates are filtered by economic elites, the Electoral College and winner-takes-all rule can elect a candidate with fewer votes nationally, and campaigns cost billions, tying officeholders to donors. The author also contends that the life-tenured Supreme Court, with its power of judicial review, amounts to a form of minority tyranny, citing the 2000 Bush–Gore case. Drawing on Marx and on Western writers such as Peter Eddy-Kler (as rendered in the Chinese source), Stephen Holmes, David Miller and Francis Fukuyama, He holds that where rights rest on private property, public power serves capital and cannot be above class. Abroad, the author says, Washington interferes in other states' affairs, justifies interventions as humanitarian while overriding rights at home (for instance through surveillance), and, citing a 2010 remark by Obama, does not want other peoples to reach American living standards.

He concludes that American democratic practice contradicts its professed values, and that behind its double standards lie self-centredness and egoism. The closing reference to Kissinger's call for credibility in diplomacy is presented as an idealistic statement that rings hollow against this reality. Read the original if you want to see how a 2016 Party-journal article frames a critique of US democracy, drawing on historical episodes, Western critics and Marxist arguments about class and property.
quoteEn: In a society where rights rest on private property, public power cannot rise above the limits of private property and must serve it; public power can therefore never stand above class, the state can never be a "universal state", and what truly dominates must be capital and the market.
quoteZh: 在一个权利建立在私有财产之上的社会里，公共权力无论如何非但不能超脱私有财产限制，而且必须为其服务，这就使得公共权力绝不可能是超阶级的，国家也不可能是“普遍性国家”，真正起支配作用的必然是资本和市场。

glossary.explanation: The doctrine that outside powers may use force in another state to prevent mass atrocities. The article treats it as a pretext for pursuing interests and for violating sovereignty.

t: The spiritual source of national rejuvenation
st: A brief discussion of the Long March spirit and the spirit of realizing the dream
zh: 民族复兴的精神动力之源
zhSub: 浅谈长征精神与圆梦精神
paras: Writing in 2016, the 80th anniversary of the Red Army's Long March, Gong Fangbin asks how the Long March spirit can be linked to the spirit needed to realize the Chinese Dream. The article treats the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation as a "new Long March". Gong argues that the Long March spirit is contained in, and further developed by, a "dream-realizing spirit" whose content is still being formulated.

The article has three parts. It first sets out the content of each spirit, then examines the logical relation between them, and finally proposes how the Long March spirit should be carried into the dream-realizing spirit.

Gong lists the Long March spirit's components, including firm ideals, courage, independence, unity and reliance on the masses. The dream-realizing spirit, in Gong's view, is strongly guided, broadly participatory, lofty in aim and persevering. Gong argues that it adds an element of creating human civilization, so that innovation becomes critical. Three elements of the Long March spirit are singled out for transmission: firm ideals and convictions, the courage to take untrodden paths through innovation, and willingness to sacrifice. On sacrifice, Gong cites China's growing role in setting international rules, Western "China threat" talk and island disputes with neighbours. Gong says China does not want war but must be prepared, and that the spirit should become values and conduct rather than only literal sacrifice.

Gong concludes that the goal of rejuvenation will be reached only if this spirit enters the nation's soul as values and behavioural norms. Read the original if you want a short example of how Party-affiliated writing in 2016 connected Long March commemoration to the Chinese Dream.
quoteEn: The dream-realizing spirit contains the Long March spirit and is a further development and sublimation of it.
quoteZh: 圆梦精神包含长征精神，并且是对长征精神的进一步发展与升华。

glossary.explanation: A set of values the Party attributes to the Red Army's Long March of 1934–36, such as firm ideals, courage and reliance on the masses. It is regularly invoked in Party education.
The author's term for the spiritual drive needed to realize the Chinese Dream. The author says its content is still being formulated.
Slogan introduced by Xi Jinping in November 2012, centred on the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: Official goal of restoring China to national strength and standing after what the Party describes as a century of humiliation.

t: On the Long March and the Long March spirit
zh: 论长征和长征精神
paras: Marking the 80th anniversary of the Long March's victory in 2016, Li Hongfeng asks what the march achieved, why it succeeded and how its spirit should be carried forward today. The article takes its cue from Xi Jinping's remarks of 23 September 2016 at the Military Museum, which called for remembering the Red Army's achievements and promoting the Long March spirit. Li's thesis is that the Long March was a victory of revolutionary spirit and of the people, made possible above all by a Party leadership core, and that its spirit remains necessary under present conditions.

The piece is organised in five sections. It first presents the Long March as unprecedented in history, drawing on Mao Zedong's 1935 report, foreign comparisons and Mao's Long March poems. It then treats the march as a triumph of revolutionary spirit and of the people, and identifies its most fundamental lesson. The final section sets out four requirements for promoting the Long March spirit now. Li cites figures on casualties, battles and distances, and the views of Edgar Snow, Harrison Salisbury, Philip Short and Zbigniew Brzezinski.

Li builds on Mao's description of the march as a manifesto, a propaganda team and a seeding machine. The author argues that the Red Army's survival and its work among ethnic minorities, through newspapers and through mobile schools show that victory came from mobilising and relying on the people. The decisive result, in Li's account, was the strategic turning point confirmed at the Zunyi Meeting of January 1935, which established Mao's leadership and ended four years of dogmatist rule. From this Li draws the central lesson: the Party found its leadership core, and leadership without a core cannot be relied upon.

Li calls for four things: holding high ideals and convictions, expressed in the Four-sphere Confidence; fighting complacency and slackening of spirit; keeping a sincere devotion to the people, since the author sees detachment from the masses as the ruling party's greatest danger; and strengthening Party leadership through discipline, democratic centralism, seeking truth from facts and loyalty to the Party Central Committee with Xi Jinping as General Secretary. Read the original if you want an example of how the Long March is used in 2016 Party-building discourse to link historical memory with calls for discipline, ideals and a leadership core.
quoteEn: The victory of the Long March was a victory of the spirit of the Chinese revolution.
quoteZh: 长征的胜利是中国革命精神的胜利。

glossary.explanation: A formulation, in its four-part form promoted under Xi Jinping from 2016, calling for confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics.
The set of values the Party attributes to the Red Army's 1934–36 Long March, including firm ideals, willingness to sacrifice, self-reliance, discipline and reliance on the masses.
An enlarged Politburo meeting held in January 1935 during the Long March. Party histories treat it as the point at which Mao Zedong's leadership was effectively established.

The Leninist organisational principle of the Communist Party, combining discussion with binding decisions. Li cites its four rules of subordination of individual to organisation, minority to majority, lower to higher level, and the whole Party to the Centre.
A Party principle of basing policy on actual conditions, associated with Mao Zedong and later Deng Xiaoping.

t: The significance of the Long March for the growth and maturing of our Party
zh: 长征对我们党成长、成熟的意义
paras: Writing in Party Building (Dangjian) in 2016, Liu Yazhou asks what the Long March meant for the Communist Party's development. Liu argues that it was one of the major turning points that pushed the Party towards maturity. With the Zunyi Conference as its marker, the Party began to lead the Chinese revolution independently and to evolve into a mature Marxist party.

The short piece has two sections: the Long March's role in advancing the adaptation of Marxism to Chinese conditions, and its role in producing a mature central leadership core. Liu draws on the Party's history before and after Zunyi, statements by Liu Bocheng and Deng Xiaoping, and figures on the Red Army's losses and its surviving cadres.

Liu holds that before the march, dogmatism of the "Left" line dominated the Party, and that, in Liu's account, it destroyed most Party organisations in the white areas and cost the Red Army and base areas ninety per cent of their strength. After the defeat at the Xiang River, many leaders came to support Mao Zedong. With the Comintern link cut, the Party chose its own central leaders for the first time, which Liu describes as the formation of a leadership core around Mao. Liu cites Deng Xiaoping that no mature central leadership existed before Zunyi, and notes that 222 of the 254 generals of rank lieutenant-general and above in 1955 had taken part in the march.

Liu concludes that the Long March shows the need to innovate in theory by combining Marxism's basic principles with Chinese realities, and that a mature party needs a firm leadership core. Linking this to the present, Liu calls on Party members to deepen the adaptation of Marxism to Chinese conditions, to strengthen core consciousness and to resolutely uphold the authority of Xi Jinping and the Central Committee. Read the original if you want an example of how Party-history writing in 2016 tied the Long March to the idea of a leadership core.
quoteEn: Any collective leadership needs a core; leadership without a core cannot be relied upon, and an important test of whether a party is mature is whether it has a strong and reliable leadership core.
quoteZh: 任何一个领导集体都要有一个核心，没有核心的领导是靠不住的，检验一个政党是不是成熟的一个重要标志，就是看有没有一个坚强可靠的领导核心。

glossary.explanation: An enlarged Politburo meeting held in January 1935 during the Long March. Official Party history treats it as the point at which Mao Zedong's leadership was effectively established and the Party began to decide its own course.

glossary.en: adaptation of Marxism to Chinese conditions
glossary.explanation: The Party's term for applying Marxism's basic principles to China's concrete circumstances and developing theory from that practice. It is usually traced to Mao Zedong in the 1930s and 1940s.
A term for the central figure around whom the collective leadership is organised. In Party discourse it is associated with Mao, Deng, Jiang and, since 2016, Xi Jinping.

t: The five strengths of the Communist Party of China
zh: 中国共产党的五大优势
paras: Writing in the People's Daily in June 2016, on the Party's 95th anniversary, Pang Xianzhi asks why the Communist Party of China grew from a small group of a few dozen people into a mature and powerful Marxist party leading a large Eastern country along the path of socialism with Chinese characteristics. Pang argues that this was no accident but follows from the Party's own nature and from five distinctive strengths.

The short commentary devotes one section to each strength. It draws on Mao Zedong's wartime and revolutionary judgements, on the Party's own documents, and on remarks by Xi Jinping, and it moves from the Party's founding to the period after the 18th Party Congress (2012).

In Pang's account, the Party holds a lofty ideal, communism, and links it to concrete programmes for each historical stage. Its fundamental purpose of serving the people wholeheartedly lets it find the "greatest common denominator" among the diverse interests that emerged after reform and opening up. Pang adds that centralised, unified leadership matters all the more now that the country is in what Xi calls a critical period of development, reform and emerging contradictions. The Party is also described as creative in adapting Marxism to Chinese conditions. Pang says it corrects its own mistakes, citing the two historical resolutions, and sets this against countries where parties rotate in office and long-term continuity is said to be impossible.

Pang concludes that these strengths explain the Party's victories and will secure the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation under its leadership. Read the original if you want a concise example of how a senior Party historian presented the sources of the Party's legitimacy in 2016.
quoteEn: Taking wholehearted service to the people as its fundamental purpose is the essential mark that distinguishes the Communist Party of China from all other parties, and is its greatest strength.
quoteZh: 把全心全意为人民服务作为根本宗旨，是中国共产党区别于其他一切政党的根本标志，是它最优胜的地方。

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal of restoring China's national strength and international standing, closely associated with Xi Jinping's leadership and the Chinese Dream.
The policy of economic reform and engagement with the world economy launched in 1978 under Deng Xiaoping.
A slogan from Mao Zedong's era, defined by the Party as its fundamental purpose.
Party resolutions on history, adopted in 1945 and 1981, that assess past leadership and errors; the article cites them as evidence of the Party's self-correction.

t: Shaping China's image with the new development philosophy
zh: 以新发展理念塑造中国形象
paras: Writing in 2016, Shen Haixiong asks how the five-part development philosophy of innovation, coordination, green development, openness and sharing can shape China's image at home and abroad. Shen argues that the new development philosophy is a concentrated expression of the Party Central Committee's new approach to governance under Xi Jinping. In this reading it will deeply influence China's national image, the image of the Party and China's international image, offering a "Chinese solution" and "Chinese wisdom" for global governance.

The short commentary is organised in three sections: the new national image, the good image of the Party, and the soft power of a major country. It draws mainly on Xi Jinping's speeches, including his remarks at the G20 Hangzhou summit, and refers to the Belt and Road Initiative and the goal of a moderately prosperous society in all respects. It ends with a brief summary and a call to be guided by the philosophy in practice.

On the national image, Shen treats the five concepts as a new lens on the Chinese path. Each is said to project a specific image: innovation signals a wise and sustainable country, coordination a balanced and harmonious one, green development a country that respects nature, openness a responsible and peaceful partner, and sharing a society of fairness and common prosperity. On the Party, Shen argues that the philosophy shows improved governing capacity, stresses the principle of governing for the people, and requires changes in the Party's way of governing, such as strategic and rule-of-law thinking and institutional reform. On international standing, Shen claims the philosophy offers a global development consensus, shows China as a responsible emerging power, and supplies a remedy for the world economy's difficulties since the 2008 financial crisis, with the G20 outcomes cited as evidence.

Shen concludes that the new development philosophy brings new opportunities, content and support for building the images of the country and the Party. Shen calls for conscious use of it to guide practice and to create a favourable environment for the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want a compact example of how Party media in 2016 linked the new development philosophy to national image-building and soft power.
quoteEn: The new development philosophy is both a direction of development and a philosophy of governance.
quoteZh: 新发展理念既是一种发展方向,也是一种执政理念

glossary.explanation: The five-part framework of innovation, coordination, green development, openness and sharing, set out by the Party leadership in 2015 as guidance for the 13th Five-Year Plan.
A long-standing socialist goal of prosperity shared by all members of society, stressed in Party discourse as a aim of development.
A Chinese initiative launched in 2013 to build infrastructure and economic cooperation links across Eurasia, Africa and beyond.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal of restoring China's national strength and international standing, associated with the Chinese Dream.

t: Ideological and political education should make full use of the power of truth in Marxism
zh: 思政教育要用好马克思主义的真理力量
source: Research on Ideological and Political Work, 2016 no. 8
paras: Liu Jianjun asks how ideological and political education can raise its level and reach, and answers that it must draw on the power of truth that Marxism possesses. In the author's view, whether this power is used well directly determines the influence, advanced character and scientific standing of such education. Citing Xi Jinping's remarks on ideals and convictions as the 'calcium' of the spirit, Liu says the choice of educational content, and the building of both rational and emotional force, should serve the establishment of Marxism's lofty ideal.

The article, published in 2016 in a journal on ideological and political work, has two main parts. The first sets out four sources of Marxism's truth-power: logical, truth-seeking, social and faith-based. The second explains how this power lifts the two forces of ideological and political education, the force of truth and the force of emotion. Liu draws on Lenin, Engels, Marx, the Communist Manifesto, Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping.

Liu links each source to a feature of Marxism. Its rigorous, self-consistent system gives logical force. Its disclosure of objective laws, summed up as seeking truth from facts, gives truth-seeking force. Its standpoint of the people gives social force. Its lofty communist ideal gives the force of faith. Liu then argues that this power gives education a logical model, true content, a value standpoint and a goal. It also turns emotion into love of truth, respect for the people and firm belief in the ideal. The author divides the mind into rational and non-rational elements, and treats truth as the object of the first and emotion as a key object of the second.

Liu concludes that, before Marxism, such education relied on authority, religion and superstition, so its truth-power was limited and its emotional power often blind. Marxist truth-power, in this account, offers a practical path from non-rational to rational dominance and so opens up a higher plane for the field. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how Chinese theorists of ideological and political education justify grounding their discipline in Marxism's claim to truth.
quoteEn: The power of truth that Marxism possesses gives the whole influence of ideological and political education a rational character.
quoteZh: 马克思主义具有的真理力量使整个思想政治教育的影响力具有理性气质。

glossary.explanation: The system of teaching in China's schools, universities and Party organisations meant to shape political views, values and conduct in line with Marxism and Party doctrine. It is also an academic discipline.
A principle associated with Mao Zedong, and later with Deng Xiaoping, that policy and theory should start from actual conditions rather than from doctrine alone.

t: Why the Communist Party of China has won the people's support and backing
zh: 中国共产党为什么能得到人民的拥护和支持
paras: Writing in Red Flag Manuscripts in 2016, the 95th year of the Party's history, Li Chunhua asks why the Communist Party of China has been able to grow from small and weak to large and strong. The article's answer is that the Party has consistently enjoyed the trust, support and backing of the broad masses, which Li treats as the material source and spiritual strength of China's revolution, construction and reform.

The commentary is a short, numbered argument in four parts. It runs through the revolutionary periods, the search for a path to national liberation, the post-1978 reform era, the development of people's democracy, and the Party's own internal building, ending with a brief reference to the Party leadership under Xi Jinping since the 18th Party Congress (2012).

Li gives four reasons. First, the Party stands for the fundamental interests of the great majority and serves the people wholeheartedly, which Li presents as the essential feature separating a proletarian party from others. Second, after other classes' attempts failed, it adopted Marxism and combined it with China's concrete conditions, producing Mao Zedong Thought. Third, since the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee (1978), it has liberated thinking and developed socialism with Chinese characteristics, which Li credits with raising living standards from inadequate subsistence to overall moderate prosperity and with advancing people's democracy and rule of law. Fourth, it practises strict self-governance, stresses ideological and work-style building, and corrects its mistakes, which Li says earns public respect.

Li concludes that all the Party's achievements result from popular support, and that it can overcome future difficulties and advance the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation only by continuing to share the people's fortunes and rely on their wisdom and strength. Read the original if you want a concise example of how the Party's official account of its popular legitimacy was framed on its 95th anniversary.
quoteEn: All the achievements won by the Communist Party of China in 95 years of struggle are the result of the people's strong support.
quoteZh: 中国共产党95年奋斗所取得的一切成就，都是人民群众大力支持的结果。

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal of restoring China's national strength and international standing, closely associated with the Chinese Dream.
The official name for the path and system developed since reform and opening up began in 1978.
The Party's policy of tightening discipline and internal management, stressed especially after the 18th Party Congress (2012).

t: Opening a new stage of flourishing for Chinese philosophy and social sciences
st: Studying General Secretary Xi Jinping's important speech at the symposium on philosophy and social sciences work
zh: 开创中国哲学社会科学繁荣发展新局面
zhSub: 学习习近平总书记在哲学社会科学工作座谈会上的重要讲话
paras: Ru Xin, who attended the symposium on philosophy and social sciences work chaired by Xi Jinping on 17 May 2016, offers his preliminary reflections on Xi's speech there. This short commentary, first published in the China Social Sciences Today in May 2016, argues that the speech clarifies the importance of the field and sets out how it should develop.

The piece is organised around four points Ru draws from the speech: the Party leadership's regard for philosophy and social sciences, the principle of Marxist guidance, the task of building philosophy and social sciences with Chinese characteristics, and the Party's expectations of intellectuals. It closes with a personal note from a long-serving scholar in the field.

Ru reports that the speech places the discipline in the broad sweep of world and Chinese history, holding that every major leap in civilisation has depended on intellectual change. Contemporary China's sweeping social change is said to make this an era that needs, and will produce, theory. Ru stresses that Marxist guidance is the fundamental mark distinguishing Chinese philosophy and social sciences, and that the speech explains how to uphold it: by advancing the adaptation of Marxism to the Chinese context, the needs of our times and the general public, and by treating upholding and developing Marxism as a dialectical unity. Ru also highlights the call to build original disciplinary, academic and discourse systems that draw on Marxist, traditional Chinese and foreign resources, under top-level design.

Ru concludes that the task is heavy and long, but is confident that implementing the speech will open a new stage and contribute to the Chinese Dream of national rejuvenation. Read the original if you want a brief, first-hand reaction from a senior Chinese scholar to the 2016 symposium and its guidelines for the field.
quoteEn: Upholding Marxism and developing Marxism are a dialectical unity.
quoteZh: 坚持马克思主义和发展马克思主义是辩证的统一。

glossary.explanation: A slogan associated with Xi Jinping since 2012, describing the goal of national rejuvenation and national prosperity.

glossary.zh: 中国特色哲学社会科学
glossary.en: philosophy and social sciences with Chinese characteristics
glossary.explanation: The aim, stressed in Xi's 2016 speech, of building Chinese-style disciplinary, academic and discourse systems guided by Marxism.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化大众化
glossary.en: the adaptation of Marxism to the Chinese context, the needs of our times and the general public
glossary.explanation: A formula for applying Marxism to Chinese conditions, to contemporary developments, and to ordinary people's understanding. The wording here is a close rendering of the 2016 phrasing.

t: Marxism has powerful vitality
zh: 马克思主义有着强大生命力
paras: Taking its cue from Xi Jinping's remark at a symposium on philosophy and social sciences (2016) that guidance by Marxism first requires solving the problem of truly understanding and truly believing it, this People's Daily commentary asks why some people, including a few Party members and officials, bear the Marxist name without believing in it. Liu and Liu argue that such people treat Marxism as empty preaching, and that this misconception must be overcome by grasping Marxism's significance for the present age.

The short piece is organised around three claims, each presented as a "commanding height" held by Marxism: truth, morality and methodology. It draws on Marx and Engels's own formulations and on two examples of Marxism's continuing influence abroad.

First, the authors hold that Marxism is a science with objective truth: it reveals general laws of nature, society and thought, criticises capitalism, and shows the historical inevitability of socialism replacing it. They cite the BBC's "thinker of the millennium" online poll, in which Marx came first, and renewed sales of Capital in Europe after the 2008 financial crisis. Second, Marxism's commitment to the proletariat's liberation coincides with human emancipation, giving it a popular character and a stance serving the great majority. Third, Marxism is practical: citing Engels, they present it as a method rather than a dogma, with theory arising from practice and returning to it.

The authors conclude that Party members and officials should believe in Marxism not merely out of political obligation but because of its truth, its popular character and its method. They add that it is the theoretical source of the Party's purpose of serving the people wholeheartedly. Read the original if you want a compact example of how the Party press framed the case for Marxist belief among cadres in 2016.
quoteEn: To date, no other theoretical doctrine has inspired people so continuously and influenced society so profoundly as Marxism.
quoteZh: 迄今为止，还没有哪一种理论学说能够像马克思主义这样持续地鼓舞人民、深远地影响社会。

t: People-oriented: the ultimate value of Marxism
zh: 以人为本：马克思主义终极价值
paras: Writing in 2016, as China entered the "deep water" of reform and ideology became more pluralistic under economic globalisation, Liang asks how Marxism's ultimate value and its discursive power can be upheld in China. The article's answer is that both must rest on the principle of putting people first, which Liang identifies as the practical form of Marxism's ultimate value: the all-round development of the human being.

The piece first defines the ultimate value and "discursive power" of Marxism, then identifies obstacles to realising each, and finally proposes a path of development in three dimensions: material base, political environment and rule of law. It is a short commentary in a Chinese political-theory journal.

Liang says that a people-first ultimate value must be universal, comprehensive, feasible and unlimited, an aim to be approached without end. Marxist discursive power is described as the people's most basic right, reflected in the Constitution, but also as relative and limited, since serving the majority will sometimes affect other strata. Obstacles include dogmatic or vulgarised readings of Marxism, Western discursive hegemony, competing social trends, and the blindness and self-interest of the market economy, which Liang says breeds moral lapses and distrust of the ruling party.

Liang calls for developing the productive forces and improving production relations, eliminating corruption during the transition period, and strengthening the rule of law so that the people's fundamental interests are protected. Read the original if you want a concise example of how a 2016 Chinese commentary links "people-oriented" governance to Marxist theory and discursive power.
quoteEn: The ultimate value of Marxism is to realise the all-round development of the human being.
quoteZh: 马克思主义终极价值是实现人的全面发展。

glossary.literal: taking the people as the foundation
glossary.explanation: A guiding principle of Party and government policy, prominent in the Scientific Outlook on Development of the 2000s, that development should serve the people's interests.
The capacity to shape public ideas and narratives. In Chinese ideological writing it is often framed as a contest between Marxism and rival ideologies.

t: Understanding shared development through the Marxist view of equality
zh: 从马克思主义平等观看共享发展
paras: Writing in Red Flag Manuscripts in 2016, Xie Weiguang asks how the Marxist conception of equality can guide the practice of shared development, the concept put forward at the Fifth Plenum of the 18th Central Committee (2015). The article argues that shared development, whose core is social justice, balances efficiency with fairness and presupposes equality, while equality in turn is expressed through shared results. In Xie's view, the Marxist view of equality has both theoretical and practical significance for carrying it out.

The piece has three sections. The first sets out the Marxist view of equality and its critique of bourgeois equality. The second argues that shared development and equality depend on each other. The third turns to what the author calls the application, upholding and development of Marxist equality in policy: equal basic rights and proportional non-basic rights.

Xie's core argument starts from Engels: equality is a historical product that reflects existing economic relations, so no equality exists beyond its historical conditions. Bourgeois slogans of equality before God, the law and the market are, on this reading, abstract and formal, because private ownership of the means of production produces real inequality. Xie cites Capital on the market as an appearance of equal exchange that hides exploitation in production, and cites the Critique of the Gotha Programme on distribution according to labour as still not full equality. Only the higher stage of communism, "from each according to his ability, to each according to his needs", would bring real equality, and its highest aim is the free and all-round development of the person.

From this Xie derives two tasks for the primary stage of socialism. Basic rights should be fully equal, mainly through government-led secondary distribution. This means upholding the dominant position of public ownership, equalising basic public services across regions and between town and country, strengthening transfer payments and poverty alleviation, and leaving no one behind on the road to a moderately prosperous society. Non-basic rights should be distributed in proportion to contribution, which Xie links to China's level of development and the continuing priority of growth. The author calls for institutions guaranteeing fairness of rights, opportunity and rules, moving steadily towards common prosperity. Read the original if you want a concise example of how a 2016 Party-journal article ties the shared development concept to classical Marxist texts on equality.
quoteEn: Shared development is development that balances efficiency and fairness, and development in which it and equality are each other's precondition.
quoteZh: 共享发展是兼顾效率与公平的发展，是与平等互为前提的发展。

glossary.explanation: One of the five concepts of the new development philosophy, put forward at the Fifth Plenum of the 18th Central Committee in 2015. It stresses that all people should share in the results of reform and development, with a focus on social justice.

Official thesis that China is still in an early, long-lasting phase of socialism with relatively underdeveloped productive forces. It is used to explain policies that fall short of full socialist or communist ideals.
A long-standing socialist goal of prosperity shared by all members of society, rather than a few becoming rich. It is repeatedly invoked in Party documents as a defining aim.
An official development goal of a society with a comfortable standard of living for all. In 2016 the Party aimed to complete its building by 2020.

t: Great practice requires a great development of philosophy and social sciences
zh: 伟大的实践需要哲学社会科学大发展
paras: Writing in Qiushi in 2016, Zhang Jiang takes up Xi Jinping's speech at the symposium on philosophy and social sciences work. The article argues that upholding and developing socialism with Chinese characteristics urgently requires a major development of philosophy and social sciences, and that scholars must shoulder the historical mission this implies.

The commentary is a short study of the speech in three parts. It first discusses the role of philosophy and social sciences in historical progress, then the new tasks set by the present situation, and finally the problems the field is said to have.

Zhang contends that philosophy and social sciences have driven social advance, citing Xi's remark that every great leap in human society has depended on intellectual change. Contemporary China, the author says, is undergoing the broadest social change in its history, which makes it an era that needs and will produce theory. Zhang links the new tasks to the new development philosophy, reform, the Party's full and rigorous self-governance, and China's international discourse power. The article then lists the weaknesses Xi identified: quantity without quality, experts without great masters, and weak discipline systems and evaluation mechanisms. It also names academic misconduct, from hasty compilation and detachment from reality to plagiarism and fabricated data.

Zhang concludes that facing these problems squarely will strengthen the sense of urgency and responsibility needed to improve the field. Scholars are urged to offer theoretical support and policy advice for the Party and people, and to help realise the Chinese Dream of national rejuvenation. Read the original if you want a concise example of how the 2016 official call for philosophy and social sciences was presented in Qiushi.
quoteEn: This is an era that needs theory and will certainly produce theory; it is an era that needs ideas and will certainly produce ideas.
quoteZh: 这是一个需要理论而且一定能够产生理论的时代，这是一个需要思想而且一定能够产生思想的时代。

glossary.explanation: A policy framework announced in 2015 stressing innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development.
A slogan associated with Xi Jinping since 2012, centred on national rejuvenation and national prosperity.

t: Strictly enforcing the political discipline that "Communist Party members may not believe in religion"
zh: 严明“共产党员不得信仰宗教”的政治纪律
paras: Writing in 2016, after the national conference on religious work held that April, Tian Xinming argues that the rule that Communist Party members may not hold religious beliefs is an important item of political discipline. In the author's account, it must be enforced strictly as part of full and rigorous self-governance of the Party. The piece, published in Red Flag Manuscripts, is a commentary that also rebuts a Party cadre who, in a magazine article, questioned the rule.

Tian first traces the rule's continuity, from Mao Zedong's wartime distinction between a united front with religious people and agreement with their doctrines, through the Central Committee's 1982 document on religious questions, to documents of 1991 and 2002. The article then gives three reasons for the rule and addresses the constitutional objection. Its second part answers two arguments for admitting believers to the Party: Lenin's remarks on priests and the practice of other communist parties, and the claim that political and religious belief can be separated.

The reasons given are that the Party's worldview is dialectical and historical materialism, which Tian calls incompatible with theism. Belief would also undermine socialism with Chinese characteristics, which rests on trust in the people and in objective laws of development. Finally, a believer would face a conflict of loyalties between Party and religious organisation, harming democratic centralism. To the constitutional objection, Tian replies that Party discipline is stricter than state law, joining is voluntary, and those unwilling to accept it may leave and keep their freedom of belief. On Lenin, the author says Lenin reasoned from Russian conditions, and that China is a secular country in which, according to the 1982 document, genuine believers are a small share of the population. Tian adds that other parties' policies are their own affair.

On the second argument, Tian holds that political stance and worldview are distinct, so patriotic religious figures can support the Party's cause within the united front, but Party members must unite the two. Admitting religious leaders to "show care" for religion would, in Tian's view, make society adapt to religion and let religion influence Party policy. The author concludes that the rule is necessary and workable, and that exceptions for minority areas with near-universal belief call for gradual, case-by-case handling. Read the original if you want an authoritative statement of the 2016 Party case against admitting religious believers, with its textual sources and its replies to critics inside the Party.
quoteEn: Party discipline is stricter than the law of the state.
quoteZh: 党纪严于国法。

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: A slogan associated with Xi Jinping's leadership since 2012, covering anti-corruption work, discipline and ideological education within the Communist Party.
The most basic category of Party discipline, requiring members to follow the Party's line and rules. The 2016 text treats the ban on religious belief as one such rule.
The Party's organisational principle combining discussion with binding unity of action, under which lower levels obey higher levels and the minority obeys the majority.
The Party's strategy of building alliances with non-Party groups, including religious circles, around shared political goals.
The official name for the Party's theory, path and system since the reform era.

t: Institutionalising Party ideological building as an important theoretical innovation of the Party
zh: 思想建设制度化是党的重要理论创新
paras: Writing in Qiushi's Red Flag Manuscripts in 2016, Liu Xinling and Lian Xiaolong take up the proposition of the "institutionalisation of the Party's ideological building", put forward by Xi Jinping after the 18th Party Congress (2012). The authors argue that it is an important theoretical innovation. In their account it extends ideological building beyond education, theoretical armament and theoretical innovation into the sphere of rules and regulations.

The article begins with a historical survey of how the content of Party ideological building has changed with the Party's central tasks. It moves from the early debates and the Gutian Conference, through the Zunyi Meeting, the Yan'an rectification campaign and the adoption of Mao Zedong Thought at the Seventh Congress. It then covers the rectification and anti-corruption campaigns of the early 1950s, the Eighth Congress (1956), and the "re-learning" stressed since the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee (1978). The second half examines recent Party regulations under three headings: theoretical work, Party spirit education and morality.

The authors argue that ideological building has two sides: struggle against non-Marxist ideas and the unification of the Party's thinking, and the innovation and propagation of Marxist theory. In their reading, the new proposition links ideological work to "governing the Party by institutions" and builds a complete system from institutional design to implementation. They cite the 2013–2017 five-year plan for Party regulations, the 2015 Disciplinary Regulations, the 2015 Regulations on Cadre Education and Training, and the 2015 Code of Integrity and Self-discipline. These set requirements for theory study, including training hours and assessment, rules on propaganda and Party management of the media, expulsion for opposing the Party's basic theory and line, and moral criteria in cadre selection and removal.

The authors conclude that institutionalisation answers the "four tests" and "four dangers" facing the Party. They hold that it lays an ideological foundation for the "two centenary goals" and gives institutional protection to ideological building under full and rigorous self-governance of the Party. Read the original if you want a Party-theory account of how ideological work was written into formal regulations in 2013–2016, with the specific documents and provisions cited.
quoteEn: This is an important theoretical innovation in the Party's ideological building: it extends ideological building from traditional ideological education, theoretical armament and theoretical innovation to the institutional level, and in practice builds a complete system running from institutional design to institutional implementation.
quoteZh: 这是对党的思想建设的重要理论创新，不仅把党的思想建设从传统的思想教育、理论武装、理论创新拓展到了制度化层面，而且在实践方面构建了党的思想建设从制度设计到制度执行的完整体系

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: A slogan associated with Xi Jinping since the 18th Party Congress (2012). It covers discipline, anti-corruption, ideological education and rule-building within the Party.
Formal rules issued by the Party's own bodies, such as the Disciplinary Regulations. They bind Party members and organisations and are distinct from state law.
Training meant to strengthen members' loyalty to the Party's character, aims and discipline, as set out in the Party Constitution.
Official targets: a moderately prosperous society by the Party's centenary in 2021, and a modern socialist country by the People's Republic's centenary in 2049.

t: Socialist core values are fundamentally different from Western values
st: Study notes on Xi Jinping's remarks on core values
zh: 社会主义核心价值观与西方价值观根本不同
paras: This short commentary, originally published in Qiushi in 2016 under the title "Upholding our core values", asks how China's socialist core values relate to the values promoted in Western countries. The author's answer is that they differ fundamentally, because each nation's core values grow out of its own history, struggles and problems.

The piece is a study note on General Secretary Xi Jinping's statements about core values. It first explains what the socialist core values express, then argues that they join state, society and citizen into one framework, and finally presents them as the broadest common ground among China's peoples.

Wen and Hua describe the socialist core values as the condensed core of the socialist core value system and as the value expression of the path, theory and institutions of socialism with Chinese characteristics. In their account, they uphold Party leadership, the guiding role of Marxism, a people-centred stance and the goal of communism. The authors claim that even terms shared with the West, such as democracy, freedom and justice, carry different meanings, since Western values, they say, reflect bourgeois interests. They also read the three-level formulation (national, social, individual) as continuous with the classical Chinese sequence from self-cultivation to governing the realm.

The authors conclude that the values were set out after repeated consultation and fit China's present stage of development, so they have won wide recognition as the "greatest common denominator" in the sphere of values. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official Party media framed the contrast between socialist core values and Western values in 2016.
quoteEn: Therefore, socialist core values are fundamentally different from the core values of Western countries.
quoteZh: 所以，社会主义核心价值观与西方国家的核心价值观根本不同。

glossary.explanation: A twelve-word formulation promoted by the Party since the 18th Party Congress (2012): prosperity, democracy, civility, harmony; freedom, equality, justice, rule of law; patriotism, dedication, integrity, friendliness.
A phrase used by Xi Jinping for the widest shared ground among different groups of Chinese people, here applied to values.
The official name for China's current system and path of development, associated with reform and opening up since 1978.

t: A look at the various ailments of Western rule of law
zh: 看看西方法治的种种病象
paras: Writing in Qiushi in 2016, Zhou Peiqing and Gao Wenjian respond to people who, in their account, admire Western rule of law and regard Western societies as genuinely law-governed. The authors argue that Western rule of law has always been accompanied by defects and still shows many 'symptoms' today.

The commentary sets out five of these symptoms in turn, each illustrated with recent cases drawn mainly from the United States and Japan. It closes with a short explanation of what the authors take to be their common cause.

The first symptom, the authors say, is legislation that ignores popular demands, citing Japan's Specially Designated Secrets Law and new security legislation, passed by the ruling party's majority despite opposition. The second is unequal justice: they point to the 2014 US cases in which white police officers who killed black men were not indicted, and to figures on police killings by race. The third is state bodies that break the law, for which they cite the PRISM surveillance programme. The fourth and fifth are interference in other sovereign states, including the 'Arab Spring' and Ukraine, and the violation of international law through wars such as Iraq in 2003 and Libya in 2011.

The authors conclude that these ailments stem fundamentally from the limits of the capitalist political system. In their view, that system serves bourgeois party politics and bourgeois interests, so legislation, justice and law enforcement uphold those interests whatever the language of 'democracy' and 'fairness', and disregard the majority at home and abroad. Read the original if you want a compact example of how official Chinese commentary criticised Western rule of law in the mid-2010s.
quoteEn: The various ailments of Western rule of law are, fundamentally, caused by the limitations of the capitalist political system.
quoteZh: 西方法治的种种病象，从根本上说，是资本主义政治制度的局限性所致。

glossary.explanation: The principle of governing according to law. In Chinese official discourse it is usually discussed as 'socialist rule of law', distinct from Western liberal models.

t: Four key points in building the current discourse system
zh: 当前话语体系建设的四个要点
paras: Writing in 2016 in the China Social Sciences Today, Zhuang Wencheng asks how Marxist discourse can be protected and made more persuasive, and holds that this requires clarifying the dialectical relations between several kinds of discourse. The short commentary argues that Marxist discourse should be adapted to specific contexts and audiences, and it identifies four pairs that deserve close attention.

The four pairs are core discourse and discourse of the times, collective and individual discourse, foreign and national discourse, and classical and plain discourse. Zhuang discusses each briefly and draws on Deng Xiaoping and Mao Zedong. The piece closes by recommending the Selected Works of Mao Zedong and Xi Jinping's speeches as models of discursive skill.

Zhuang argues that core discourse, which sets out the essential features of Marxism, must always be upheld and serves as the standard for judging other discourses. Discourse of the times, such as socialism with Chinese characteristics, the Chinese Dream and core socialist values, is presented as a renewal of that core, not a break with it. On collective and individual discourse, the author warns that each must not swallow the other, since individual discourse alone would produce liberal discursive hegemony. Their link lies in the unity of the particular and the universal, and the author proposes equal dialogue and agreed discursive rules.

On foreign and national discourse, Zhuang says Confucian, reformist and liberal thought failed in modern China. Marxism, in the author's view, is effective only when rooted in national tradition, and the author rejects both dismissing it as foreign and returning to Marx's own era. Classical expressions should be paired with plain, everyday language so that theory reaches people emotionally. Read the original if you want a brief Party-theory statement of how Marxist discourse construction was framed in 2016.
quoteEn: Discourse of the times describes the features of an era and expresses people's spirit and goals in a new historical period. It is the interpretation and application of core discourse in a new age, a "returning to the root to open the new" and not "breaking the old to establish the new".
quoteZh: “时代话语”述说着时代的特征，表达新历史时期人们的精神面貌和奋斗目标，是“核心话语”在新时代的阐释和运用，是对核心话语的“返本开新”，而不是“破旧立新”。

glossary.explanation: The official name for the Chinese Communist Party's model of socialism, in use since the 1980s. The article cites it as an example of discourse of the times.
A slogan promoted by Xi Jinping from 2012, centred on national rejuvenation and national prosperity.
An official set of twelve values promoted since 2012, including prosperity, democracy, freedom and equality.

t: Raising the soft power of red culture
st: Paths for red culture in the perspective of building a culturally strong nation
zh: 提升红色文化软实力
source: Journal of Jinggangshan University (Social Sciences Edition), 2016 no. 1
paras: Writing in 2016, Zhou Yanhong asks how the soft power of "red culture" can be raised after years of a nationwide "red culture craze". The author argues that the craze has produced distortions in how red culture is built and spread, and that a comprehensive and developmental perspective is needed to correct them.

The article identifies four tendencies: stressing publicity form over substance, short-term economic returns over long-term social benefit, isolated local efforts over wider integration, and domestic self-regard over international dialogue. Each tendency is answered by one proposal, and the article is organised around these four.

Zhou draws on the Marxist view that content and form are unified, with content decisive, to urge that red culture be distilled into core qualities such as patriotism, hard struggle and serving the people, rather than spread thinly across many "spirits". The author criticises TV dramas that distort revolutionary history for ratings, and calls for social benefit to take priority, with public-interest red culture and the red culture industry developed together. Zhou also cites the separate promotion of red tourism by Ruijin, Yudu, Ningdu and Xingguo in Ganzhou, Jiangxi, as a missed chance for scale and for presenting a continuous history.

On the international side, Zhou argues that red culture, as the first cultural form of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the result of its combination with traditional culture, is a distinctive asset for cultural outreach, citing performances abroad of the dance drama Hongmei zan and of Jiangxi folk songs. The author concludes that raising red culture's soft power will help realise the dream of a culturally strong nation and the Chinese Dream. Read the original if you want an example of how 2016 Chinese scholarship on ideological education framed red culture, red tourism and cultural outreach.
quoteEn: Red culture was formed in history, but it is inherited and developed to act on the future; it arose in China, but is increasingly accepted by the world and serves the world.
quoteZh: 红色文化形成于历史，但传承发展并作用于未来；红色文化产生于中国，但正日益为世界所接受并服务于世界

glossary.explanation: The culture arising from the revolutionary, wartime and socialist-construction experience of the Chinese Communist Party, including sites, songs, stories and "spirits" such as the Jinggangshan or Long March spirit.
The influence and appeal of a country's culture and values, a concept adapted in Chinese policy discourse from Joseph Nye.
Tourism to revolutionary historical sites, promoted by the state since the early 2000s as both an economic and an educational activity.
A slogan associated with Xi Jinping from 2012, referring to the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.
A policy goal of building China's cultural industries, influence and ideological cohesion.

t: A methodology for building ideological discourse power
zh: 意识形态话语权建设方法论研究
source: Journal of the Guizhou Provincial Party School of the CPC, 2016 no. 2
paras: Writing in 2016, as ideological work received growing attention in China, Hou Huiqin asks how ideological discourse power (yishi xingtai huayuquan) is acquired, built and used. Hou argues that ideology is in essence the power of intellectual domination required for class rule and the moral basis of state power, so it cannot be discussed in a non-ideological way. For China, the article holds, the core issue is upholding the leadership of the Communist Party and the guiding role of Marxism.

The article is organised in three parts: how discourse power is obtained and what it is in essence; how it is constructed and the laws governing this; and how it is used and what is decisive in its use. Hou draws on Marx and Engels on the ruling ideas of each age, on Sieyès and Saint-Simon as examples of the rising bourgeoisie, on Weber and Diderot in the discussion of human nature, and on Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping for the Chinese cases.

Hou's central claim is that a ruling class holds the means of mental production because it controls material production, and so occupies the moral high ground. The proletariat, lacking economic strength under capitalism, can overturn this only by occupying the high ground of history through scientific theory. Appeals to values alone, or to 'ethical socialism', are said to leave capitalism's core values unchallenged. Hou therefore says truth must be the foundation of values. Marxism is credited with recasting the debate from whether capitalism suits human nature to whether human nature can change, and with distinguishing 'real' from 'abstract' people. Hou describes abstract theories of human nature, 'conscience' and 'people-ness' detached from Party spirit and class character as weak points to be criticised.

In the third part Hou says discourse power is won by setting correct leading agendas and exposing false propositions. Examples of the former are Mao's people's democratic dictatorship and Deng's socialism with Chinese characteristics, which Hou links to the 'Four Comprehensives'. Examples of the latter are the opposition of 'revolution' to 'modernization', and slogans such as 'is the Party or the law greater'. Hou concludes that Party leadership is the focus of today's ideological struggle and that any proposition denying it is a false one. Read the original if you want a representative statement of how a leading Chinese Marxist theorist links discourse power, scientific theory and Party leadership in the mid-2010s.
quoteEn: It is not human nature that creates history, but history that changes human nature.
quoteZh: 不是人性创造历史，而是历史改变人性

glossary.explanation: The capacity to set the terms, agendas and standards of public ideas and to have one's account accepted as authoritative. The concept has been prominent in Chinese debates on ideological work since the early 2010s.

A strategic framework put forward by Xi Jinping in 2014–2015. It covers building a moderately prosperous society in all respects, deepening reform, governing the country according to law and strict Party self-governance.

Mao Zedong's formula (1949) for the state led by the working class and based on the worker-peasant alliance, democratic towards the people and coercive towards enemies. It remains a constitutional principle.
The official name for China's path since reform and opening up, introduced by Deng Xiaoping in 1982.

t: Guiding the great development of Chinese philosophy and social sciences with Marxism
zh: 用马克思主义指导中国哲学社会科学大发展
paras: Writing in 2016, Zhu Lingjun asks why Marxism must guide the development of Chinese philosophy and the social sciences, and how it should be studied and applied. Opening with the early-1920s debate between Hu Shi and Li Dazhao on "problems and isms", Zhu argues that every country needs an "ism" to guide it and that Marxism is China's. The article contends that a new leap in the adaptation of Marxism to China will bring a great flourishing of Chinese social science.

The article has four sections. The first gives four reasons for confidence in Marxism, drawing on modern Chinese history and on claimed affinities between Marxism and Chinese culture. The second discusses studying Marxism by linking theory to practice, using Lenin, Mao Zedong, Deng Xiaoping and other Party leaders as models. The third proposes studying Marxism through the method of "ancient and modern, Chinese and foreign". The fourth calls for taking the latest results of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context to the world.

Zhu argues that after Confucianism, Christian theology, social evolutionism, reformism and bourgeois democracy all failed to save China, Marxism succeeded because it matched demands for national independence and industrialisation and has parallels with traditional thought. Zhu also claims that Marx and Engels absorbed Chinese cultural elements through German philosophy. On method, Zhu holds that neither replacing Marxism with Confucianism nor the reverse is acceptable, and that imported Western social science, with its alleged Eurocentric assumptions and "technicism", cannot simply judge Chinese experience. Zhu proposes building macro-theory on Marxist philosophy, meso-theory on Chinese traditions and the socialist road, and micro-theory through comparison worldwide. Concretely, this means setting Chinese questions, shaping Chinese values and writing indigenous textbooks.

Zhu concludes that a strong system of knowledge would yield an interpretive system, discursive power and soft power, supporting the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Zhu presents three historical stages: Mao's generation made the Chinese people "stand up", Deng's made them "prosperous", and the present generation should make them "strong". Social scientists are urged to study the shift from governing a large country to governing a strong one and to tell China's story abroad. Read the original if you want a representative 2016 statement of the official case for Marxist guidance in Chinese social science, including its use of Chinese cultural continuity and indigenisation arguments.
quoteEn: A persuasive theoretical system is always formed through repeated comparison on a worldwide scale.
quoteZh: 一个有说服力的理论体系总是在世界范围内通过反复比较形成的。

glossary.explanation: A principle of Marxist study stressed by Mao Zedong, especially in his 1941 Yan'an speech. It opposes dogmatic reading of texts detached from conditions in China.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A Party slogan for restoring China's strength and international standing after the "century of humiliation". It is closely tied to Xi Jinping's Chinese Dream.

keywords: adaptation of Marxism to the Chinese context

t: Building philosophy and social sciences with Chinese characteristics, Chinese style and Chinese manner
zh: 构建中国特色中国风格中国气派的哲学社会科学
paras: Writing in Qiushi in 2016, Shen Zhuanghai asks how China's philosophy and social sciences can develop their own distinctive characteristics, style and manner. The article argues that this is a mark of maturity, strength and confidence, reached after a century of development alongside China's revolution, construction and reform. Shen presents Xi Jinping's speech at the symposium on philosophy and social sciences as the programme for this work.

The commentary follows four requirements drawn from that speech. They are to base research on China, to hold to innovation, to advance the discipline, academic and discourse systems together, and to treat the building of talent as the most fundamental task.

Shen's core claim is that distinctiveness comes from rooting scholarship in Chinese practice. This means focusing on Chinese problems, drawing on traditional culture, and building on the Marxist fundamentals and the theoretical results of adapting Marxism to China. Foreign scholarship is to be absorbed, not excluded. Shen insists that "Chinese style" does not mean antique flavour but contemporary ideas, produced by problem-oriented innovation under a Marxist worldview. The three systems are described as one whole: the academic system is the "way", the discipline system the "body" and the discourse system the "words". Shen says the discipline and discourse systems depend on the depth of the academic system.

Shen concludes that academic prosperity is measured by the people it produces as well as by its results. The author calls for talent strategies centred on cultivating people, making building projects "talent-nurturing" and not "formal" ones, and reforming research management to free scholarly creativity. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how official discourse in 2016 framed the aims and organisation of Chinese social science.
quoteEn: The fundamental sign of academic prosperity lies not only in producing results but, even more, in producing talent.
quoteZh: 学术繁荣的根本标志不仅在于出成果，更在于出人才。

t: On the fit between Marxism and present-day China
zh: 论马克思主义与当下中国的契合关系问题
source: Thought and Theory Education (思想理论教育), 2016 no. 6
paras: Writing in 2016, Huang Lizhi asks how well Marxism and China today fit each other (qihe guanxi), more than sixty years after the founding of the People's Republic. The article holds that the fit, which was clearly established in the revolutionary era, is now partial. In the author's reading, wide areas of agreement sit alongside real gaps between Marxist principles and the reality of a market-economy China. Huang argues that these gaps must be acknowledged and closed, or the Party's political legitimacy will suffer at its social base.

The article has three parts. It first surveys the present status of Marxism: its official ideological position, the Marxism research and construction project and the new first-level discipline, and the loss of faith that surveys and Xi Jinping's remarks describe among some Party members and officials. It then compares agreement and difference under the slogan "economic growth is the hard truth". Finally it proposes two ways of narrowing the gap, drawing on Marx, Engels, Mao Zedong, Deng Xiaoping, Daniel Bell and Chinese commentators.

Huang's core argument is that reform-era orthodoxy came to equate Marxism with developing the productive forces. In Huang's account this reading was historically justified, since it opened the way to rapid growth. The author argues that it is not Marxism's core, citing Marx and Lenin on capitalism's own drive to expand productive forces, and Engels's late letters rejecting economic reductionism. Huang says the costs have been ecological strain, polarisation, consumerism and damaged official credibility. The first remedy is a dialectical view of texts: balancing "what the founders said" against "what they never said", and recovering Marx's humanist concern with all-round human development, which Huang links to the Scientific Outlook on Development's "people-centred" principle. The second remedy is to move from "solving political problems through the economy" to "solving economic problems through politics". Huang criticises Li Zehou's sequence of economic growth, then individual freedom, then political democracy. The author argues that the state and superstructure must correct market outcomes, citing Bell's moral case for social minimums, Deng's remark about the "powerful state machinery" and recent redistribution, welfare and anti-corruption measures.

Huang concludes that these measures, introduced since the Scientific Outlook on Development and especially since the 18th Party Congress (2012), have already narrowed the gap between Marxism and Chinese reality, though the theory still has to be worked out consciously. The author expresses confidence that the relationship will become mutually reinforcing and calls on the Party to keep upholding and developing Marxism. Read the original if you want a Chinese scholar's critique of equating Marxism with productive-force development, and of the "economic solution to political problems" logic, in the early Xi Jinping period.
quoteEn: If Marxism is understood only as developing the productive forces, differences in the fit will arise, both textual differences and differences with reality.
quoteZh: 只把马克思主义理解为发展生产力，就会发生契合关系上的差异，包括文本的差异和现实的差异。

glossary.explanation: A guiding concept put forward under Hu Jintao from 2003 that stresses people-centred, coordinated and sustainable development rather than growth alone.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义理论研究和建设工程
glossary.pinyin: Mǎkèsī zhǔyì lǐlùn yánjiū hé jiànshè gōngchéng
glossary.en: the Marxism research and construction project
glossary.literal: Marxist theory research and construction project
glossary.explanation: A state-sponsored project launched in the early 2000s, abbreviated "Ma gongcheng", that organises research on Marxist theory and compiles standard textbooks and editions of the classics.
The core principle of the Scientific Outlook on Development, meaning that development should serve people's interests and all-round development.

t: Understanding more deeply the claim that "core values are a kind of virtue"
zh: 深入理解“核心价值观是一种德”
source: Research on Ideological and Political Education, 2015 no. 5
paras: The article interprets a remark Xi Jinping made in May 2014 in a discussion with students and teachers at Peking University: that core values are "in fact a kind of virtue" (de), at once personal virtue and a "great virtue" of the state and society. Li and Zhu argue that this formulation has real practical significance. In their reading it shows how the core socialist values link to traditional Chinese culture, reflects confidence in the socialist path, and indicates how the values should be cultivated.
